components.name: Accordion
components.summary: A stack of items whose content shows and hides under a title button: FAQs, settings groups, long forms split into sections.
components.guide:
# Accordion

A stack of items whose content shows and hides under a title button: FAQs, settings groups, long forms split into sections. One item open at a time by default, or several with `selectionMode="multiple"`.

**Also called:** collapsible, disclosure, expander, expandable section.

```jsx
import { Accordion, AccordionItem } from '@diki-stwn/serupa-ds';

<Accordion defaultValue={['shipping']}>
  <AccordionItem value="shipping" title="How long does shipping take?">Orders ship within 2 business days.</AccordionItem>
  <AccordionItem value="returns" title="Can I return an item?">Yes, within 30 days.</AccordionItem>
</Accordion>

<Accordion selectionMode="multiple" variant="card" headingLevel={2}>…</Accordion>

// Controlled
<Accordion value={open} onValueChange={setOpen}>…</Accordion>
```

## When to use

- Many sections where most people need only one or two, such as FAQs.
- Settings groups or a long form split into sections that people open as they need them.
- A narrow screen where showing every section at once would make the page very long.

## When not to use

- Content everyone needs to read, or compare across sections: show it on the page under [Heading] (npx serupa-docs Heading)s instead.
- Views of the same thing that people switch between: use [Tabs] (npx serupa-docs Tabs) instead.
- Steps people go through in order: use [Stepper] (npx serupa-docs Stepper) instead.
- One piece of content that shows and hides on its own: the native `<details>` and `<summary>` do that.

## Anatomy

Drawn from the `Playground` story.

1. **Item** (`.srp-accordion__item`): one section: its heading and its panel.
2. **Trigger** (`.srp-accordion__trigger`): the button in the heading that opens and closes the section.
3. **Title** (`.srp-accordion__title`): the section's name, inside the trigger.
4. **Chevron** (`.srp-accordion__icon`): turns to show whether the section is open.
5. **Panel** (`.srp-accordion__panel`): the section's content, shown when it's open.

## Usage

- Write titles that say what's inside, so people can pick one without opening the others.
- Use `selectionMode="multiple"` when people may want two sections open to compare them.
- Set `headingLevel` to fit the page's outline.
- Keep anything people must not miss out of a closed item: closed content is hidden from everyone.
- With many items and `selectionMode="multiple"`, add `showExpandAll` so people can open everything at once (to read or print the whole page) and close it again.
- The browser's find-in-page (Ctrl+F or ⌘F) searches closed items too, and opens the item a match is in.
- Closed items keep their content, and its state (a half-filled form, a playing video's position). Set `keepMounted={false}` on an item whose content is heavy and doesn't need to, such as a chart or a long table, so it renders only while open. Find-in-page can't find content that isn't there, so keep the default for text people may search.

### Do and don't

- **Do:** Write titles that say what's inside: "How long does shipping take?". (`DoSayWhatsInside`)
- **Don't:** Title items "Details", "More information" or "Other": people have to open each one to find what they need. (`DontVagueTitles`)

## Accessibility

- Follows the WAI-ARIA accordion pattern: each title is a button inside a heading, with `aria-expanded` and `aria-controls`; an open item's content is a region labeled by its title. Closed items aren't regions, so screen readers' landmark lists hold only what's showing, and with `selectionMode="multiple"` and more than six items no panel is a region (the APG's advice against crowding the landmarks); the content still follows its heading.
- Tab moves between titles, as it does between any buttons, and Enter and Space open and close. The pattern's optional arrow keys are left out: a title acts like every other button on the page, and Up and Down scroll it.
- Closed content is `hidden="until-found"`, so it's out of the tab order and screen readers skip it, but find-in-page still finds it: a match fires `beforematch`, which opens that item (in `single`, closing the open one). It's set once the closing animation ends. A disabled item's content stays `visibility: hidden` and isn't searchable. Before hydration, and in browsers without `until-found`, closed content is `visibility: hidden` as before.
- The Expand all button is a plain `<button>` that says "Expand all" or, once every enabled item is open, "Collapse all" (the `expandAll` and `collapseAll` labels in `SerupaProvider`). It has `aria-expanded`, true only once every item is open, since VoiceOver doesn't reliably say a label that changes on its own. Disabled items stay as they are.
- With `collapsible={false}` the open item's button has `aria-disabled`, since pressing it does nothing.
- Titles and content keep 4.5:1, the chevron 3:1, on `surface` in every theme (`Accordion.test.tsx`). Opening, the panel grows to its content's height while the content unfolds (a fade and an opening clip), so what's below slides down instead of jumping. Closing, it folds back while the height shrinks. A second press mid-way turns back from where it is. With reduced motion it only fades, and the height changes at once.

### Keyboard

| Key | Does |
| --- | --- |
| Tab | Through the titles and anything focusable in open items; closed content is skipped. With `showExpandAll`, its button comes first |
| Enter / Space | Opens or closes the focused item |

## Props

### Accordion

| Prop | Type | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | string | none | Goes to the root `<div>`. |
| `selectionMode` | `'single'` \| `'multiple'` | `'multiple'` | Any number open, so people can compare them, or one at a time |
| `value` | `string[]` | none | The open items (controlled) |
| `defaultValue` | `string[]` | `[]` | The items open at first. With `single`, only the first counts |
| `onValueChange` | `(value: string[]) => void` | none | Called when an item opens or closes |
| `collapsible` | boolean | `true` | With `single`: lets the open item close, leaving none open |
| `variant` | `'plain'` \| `'card'` | `'plain'` | Lines between items, or a bordered, rounded frame |
| `headingLevel` | `2`–`6` | `3` | The titles' heading level, to fit the page outline |
| `showExpandAll` | boolean | `false` | With `multiple`: an Expand all / Collapse all button above the items |

`className`, `style`, `ref` and everything else go to the wrapper, which has `data-component="accordion"`.

### AccordionItem

| Prop | Type | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `title` | node | required | What the title button says |
| `value` | string | its position (`"0"`, `"1"`…) | Identifies it in `value` |
| `disabled` | boolean | `false` | Can't be opened or closed |
| `children` | node | none | The content |
| `keepMounted` | boolean | `true` | `false` renders the content only while the item is open (and while it closes), for heavy content. Its state is lost on close, and find-in-page can't find it |

`className`, `ref` and everything else go to the item, which has `data-state="open"` or `"closed"`.

## Component tokens

Each is an optional override: set it on the page, a container or one accordion. The list lives in `src/components/Accordion/accordion.tokens.json` (also in `design-tokens/components/`).

<!-- token-table:start (made from accordion.tokens.json by npm run tokens: edit the descriptions there) -->
| Token | Default | Use |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--accordion-border` | `border` | The lines between items, and the frame of variant="card". |
| `--accordion-title-color` | `text` | An item's title. |
| `--accordion-content-color` | `text-muted` | An item's content (4.5:1 on surface). |
| `--accordion-icon-color` | `text-muted` | The chevron. |
| `--accordion-bg` | `surface` | The background of variant="card". |
| `--accordion-focus-ring` | `focus-ring` | The keyboard focus ring. |
| `--accordion-trigger-bg-pressed` | `pressed` | A title's fill while it's held down. |
| `--accordion-text-disabled` | `disabled-text` | Disabled: the text, icon or mark, in place of fading it (3:1 or more on its background, more with more contrast). |
| `--accordion-title-size` | `text-sm` | Title text (14px). |
| `--accordion-title-weight` | `font-medium` | Title weight (500). |
| `--accordion-content-size` | `text-sm` | Content text (14px). |
| `--accordion-padding-y` | `space-content` | Space above and below a title, and below the content: 16px, 12px in the compact density. |
| `--accordion-padding-x` | `spacing-4` | Side padding in variant="card" (16px). |
| `--accordion-icon-size` | `spacing-5` | The chevron (20px). |
| `--accordion-border-width` | `border-width-1` | Lines and frame (1px). |
| `--accordion-radius` | `radius-surface` | The corners of variant="card" (8px). |
| `--accordion-duration` | `motion-change-md` | Opening: the fade, unfold and height (200ms), and the chevron turning. Closing folds back and shrinks over motion-exit-md (150ms). |
<!-- token-table:end -->

components.name: Alert
components.summary: A message about the page or a task: something saved, something to know, something that went wrong.
components.guide:
# Alert

A message about the page or a task: something saved, something to know, something that went wrong. It's a tinted box with an icon, an optional title, a message, optional actions and an optional close button.

**Also called:** callout, banner, inline message.

```jsx
import { Alert, Button } from '@diki-stwn/serupa-ds';

<Alert>Your trial ends in 3 days.</Alert>

<Alert tone="danger" title="Payment failed" actions={<Button size="sm" variant="secondary">Update card</Button>}>
  We couldn't charge the card ending 4242.
</Alert>

// dismissible: hide it yourself in onDismiss
{show && <Alert tone="success" onDismiss={() => setShow(false)}>Changes saved.</Alert>}
```

## When to use

- Something about the page or a task that people should see and that stays until it's dealt with: a failed payment, an expiring trial.
- A form or a section couldn't be saved, and people need to know why and what to do.
- A warning before people act, such as "This project is shared with 12 people."

## When not to use

- A quick confirmation that something happened, such as "Link copied": use a [Toast] (npx serupa-docs Toast) instead.
- A decision people must make before they go on: use a [Dialog] (npx serupa-docs Dialog) with `alert` instead.
- An error on one field: use the error in [Field] (npx serupa-docs Field) instead.
- A short status label in a table or a card: use a [Badge] (npx serupa-docs Badge) instead.

## Anatomy

Drawn from the `LongText` story.

1. **Icon** (`.srp-alert__icon`): shows the tone (info, success, warning, danger) beside the words, never instead of them.
2. **Title** (`.srp-alert__title`): the short summary, read first.
3. **Message** (`.srp-alert__message`): what happened and what to do next.
4. **Dismiss** (`.srp-alert__dismiss`): closes the alert, when it can be closed.

## Usage

- Pick the `tone` from what happened: `danger` for something that failed, `warning` for a risk, `success` for a done task, `info` or `neutral` for something to know.
- Put the alert near what it's about: at the top of the form or section, not far from it.
- Keep the `title` to a few words and let the message say what happened and what to do. Put the way out in `actions`, such as "Update card".
- Add `onDismiss` only when the message can be safely ignored; leave it out for problems that still need fixing.

### Do and don't

- **Do:** Say what happened and what to do next, with the way out in `actions`. (`DoWhatAndNext`)
- **Don't:** Show a generic "Something went wrong": people can't tell what failed or how to fix it. (`DontGenericError`)
- **Do:** Pick the tone from what happened: `info` for news. (`DoMatchTone`)
- **Don't:** Use `danger` for something that isn't a problem: red loses its meaning, and real problems get missed. (`DontAlarmingTone`)

## Accessibility

- `role="alert"` (danger) is read out at once when the alert appears; `role="status"` (every other tone, warning too) waits for a pause. Danger interrupts and the rest wait, as in Toast and SaveStatus. Pass `role="alert"` for a warning that must stop people before they act. A screen reader only announces an alert that's added to the page, so render it when the event happens rather than toggling its text.
- The icon is decorative: the title or message must say what happened. Don't rely on the color alone.
- The close button is a real button with a name, 24×24px.
- In forced-colors mode the box gets a visible border and the icon a system color.
- The title and message keep 4.5:1 and the icon 3:1 on every tone, in every theme (`Alert.test.tsx`).
- **Keyboard:** Tab reaches the buttons and links in `actions`, then, with `onDismiss`, the ×, which Enter or Space presses. The alert itself isn't a Tab stop.
- **Focus after dismissing:** when the × had focus and `onDismiss` removes the alert, focus moves to the next element in the Tab order after where the alert was (the selected tab of a tab list, not the first), or the one before it at the end of the page, so keyboard and screen reader users keep their place. If `onDismiss` moves focus itself, or keeps the alert on screen, focus is left where it is.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | string | none | Goes to the root `<div>`. |
| `tone` | `'info'` \| `'success'` \| `'warning'` \| `'danger'` \| `'neutral'` | `'info'` | The background (each tone's `-subtle` color, `surface-muted` for neutral), the border tint and the icon |
| `title` | node | | A short first line in `font-semibold` |
| `children` | node | | The message |
| `icon` | icon name \| element \| `false` | the tone's | `info`, `check_circle`, `warning` or `error` by default; another name or element replaces it, `false` removes it |
| `actions` | node | | Buttons or links in a row under the message |
| `onDismiss` | function | | Shows a close button (a small ghost Button) that calls it |
| `dismissLabel` | string | `'Dismiss'` | The close button's name |

`role` is `"alert"` for danger and `"status"` for the others; pass `role` to change it. `className`, `style`, `ref` and everything else go to the box, which has `data-component="alert"` and `data-tone`.

## Component tokens

Each is an optional override: set it on the page, a container or one alert. The list lives in `src/components/Alert/alert.tokens.json` (also in `design-tokens/components/`).

<!-- token-table:start (made from alert.tokens.json by npm run tokens: edit the descriptions there) -->
| Token | Default | Use |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--alert-bg-info` | `info-subtle` | The background of a info alert. |
| `--alert-icon-info` | `info-text` | The icon and the border tint of a info alert (3:1 on its background). |
| `--alert-bg-success` | `success-subtle` | The background of a success alert. |
| `--alert-icon-success` | `success` | The icon and the border tint of a success alert (3:1 on its background). |
| `--alert-bg-warning` | `warning-subtle` | The background of a warning alert. |
| `--alert-icon-warning` | `warning` | The icon and the border tint of a warning alert (3:1 on its background). |
| `--alert-bg-danger` | `danger-subtle` | The background of a danger alert. |
| `--alert-icon-danger` | `danger` | The icon and the border tint of a danger alert (3:1 on its background). |
| `--alert-bg-neutral` | `surface-muted` | The background of a neutral alert. |
| `--alert-icon-neutral` | `text-muted` | The icon and the border tint of a neutral alert (3:1 on its background). |
| `--alert-title-color` | `text` | The title. |
| `--alert-text` | `text` | The message (4.5:1 on every tone's background). |
| `--alert-border-strength` | `opacity-30` | How strongly the border shows the tone's color (30%). |
| `--alert-radius` | `radius-surface` | The corner radius (8px). |
| `--alert-border-width` | `border-width-1` | The border width. |
| `--alert-padding-x` | `spacing-4` | Padding at the start and end (16px). |
| `--alert-padding-y` | `spacing-3` | Padding at the top and bottom (12px). |
| `--alert-gap` | `spacing-3` | Space between the icon, the content and the close button (12px). |
| `--alert-content-gap` | `spacing-1` | Space between the title, the message and the actions (4px). |
| `--alert-title-weight` | `font-semibold` | The title's weight (600). |
<!-- token-table:end -->

components.name: AppShell
components.summary: The frame around an app's pages: a skip link, the header, the sidebar, main, the footer and a bottom navigation, laid out and kept in place as the page scrolls.
components.guide:
# AppShell

The frame around an app's pages: a skip link, the header, the sidebar, main, the footer and a bottom navigation, laid out and kept in place as the page scrolls. Each page then only fills in main.

**Also called:** app layout, page shell, application frame.

```tsx
import { AppShell, Navbar, Sidebar, SidebarItem } from "@diki-stwn/serupa-ds";

<AppShell
  header={<Navbar sticky brand="Acme">…</Navbar>}
  sidebar={<Sidebar aria-label="Workspace">…</Sidebar>}
  footer="© 2026 Acme"
  background="muted"
>
  <Heading level={1}>Dashboard</Heading>
  …
</AppShell>
```

## When to use

- An app with several pages people move between, where the navigation stays put and only the content changes.
- A settings page, a dashboard, a list beside its detail: anything inside a signed-in app.

## When not to use

- A sign-in, sign-up or error page with no navigation: use [Center] (npx serupa-docs Center) as main instead.
- A marketing page of full-width bands: use a [Navbar] (npx serupa-docs Navbar), [PageSection] (npx serupa-docs PageSection)s and a Footer instead.
- Two columns inside a page, such as filters beside results: use [SidebarLayout] (npx serupa-docs SidebarLayout) inside main.

## Anatomy

Drawn from the `WithBottomNav` story.

1. **Skip link** (`.srp-skip-link`): "Skip to content", the first Tab stop, shown only while it has focus.
2. **Sidebar** (`.srp-app-shell__side`): the column beside main, from `sidebarFrom` up, holding your Sidebar.
3. **Main** (`.srp-app-shell__main`): the page's content, the skip link's target.
4. **Footer** (`.srp-app-shell__footer`): the footer landmark below main.
5. **Bottom navigation** (`.srp-app-shell__bottom`): the last thing in the page, holding a BottomNav for phones.

## Usage

- Pass a sticky [Navbar] (npx serupa-docs Navbar) as `header`: the sidebar then sticks below it and is the screen's height less the bar, with its own scroll. With a header that doesn't stick, the sidebar runs down beside main and the footer.
- Pass a [Sidebar] (npx serupa-docs Sidebar) as `sidebar`. It's gone below `sidebarFrom` (640px by default), so put its links in the Navbar's menu or a [BottomNav] (npx serupa-docs BottomNav) for phones, with `hideFrom` set to the same width.
- Set `background="muted"` when the page is built from Cards or panels: a dashboard, settings in Card sections, a board, a list beside its detail. Keep `plain` for a page people read or fill in (the Build a page guide, "The page's background").
- Pass the footer's content, not a `<footer>`: AppShell renders the footer landmark.
- `padded` gives main 16px of padding, 24px from 640px and 32px from 1024px. Set `padded={false}` for content that brings its own, such as a full-bleed map.

### Do and don't

- **Do:** Use the muted background behind a page built from Cards. (`DoMutedCards`)
- **Don't:** Put Cards on the plain background: their edges barely show. (`DontPlainCards`)

## Accessibility

- **Landmarks:** your header (a Navbar is a banner), the sidebar's `nav`, one `main` and one `footer` (contentinfo). Give the Sidebar a name of its own ("Workspace"), told apart from the Navbar's.
- **Keyboard:** Tab starts at the skip link; Enter on it moves focus into main. The rest is the header's, the sidebar's and the page's own controls, in the order they show.
- **Skip link:** "Skip to content" is the first Tab stop. It moves focus into main, past the header and the sidebar (WCAG 2.4.1); main has `tabindex="-1"` so focus lands there in every browser, with no outline of its own.
- **Focus not hidden:** a sticky Navbar sets the page's scroll padding, so a focused element in main is never under the bar (2.4.11).
- **Contrast:** text reads 4.5:1 on main's plain and muted backgrounds, and the footer's muted text on its own, in every theme (`AppShell.test.tsx`).
- **Reflow:** below `sidebarFrom` the sidebar gives its room to main, so nothing scrolls sideways at 320px (1.4.10). Keep its links reachable in the Navbar's menu or a BottomNav.
- **What's still yours:** the page's one h1 in main, the page's title, and moving focus after a route change with `announcePage()`.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | string | none | Goes to the outer `<div>`. main's own id is `mainId`. |
| `header` | ReactNode | none | The bar across the top: a Navbar |
| `sidebar` | ReactNode | none | Beside main, on the start side: a Sidebar |
| `sidebarFrom` | `'sm'` \| `'md'` \| `'lg'` | `'sm'` | The width the sidebar shows from: 640, 768 or 1024px |
| `children` | ReactNode | none | The page's content, in main |
| `footer` | ReactNode | none | The footer's content, below main |
| `bottomNav` | ReactNode | none | A BottomNav for phones, last in the page |
| `background` | `'plain'` \| `'muted'` | `'plain'` | main's background |
| `padded` | boolean | `true` | Padding around main's content |
| `skipLink` | boolean | `true` | A "Skip to content" link first in the page |
| `mainId` | string | `'main'` | main's id, the skip link's target |

A value that isn't on the list falls back to the default. `className`, `style`, `ref` and everything else go to the outer `<div>`, which has `data-component="app-shell"`.

## Component tokens

Each is an optional override: set it on the page, a container or one AppShell. The list lives in `src/components/AppShell/app-shell.tokens.json` (also in `design-tokens/components/`).

<!-- token-table:start (made from app-shell.tokens.json by npm run tokens: edit the descriptions there) -->
| Token | Default | Use |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--app-shell-bg` | `surface` | The page's background, and main's with background="plain". |
| `--app-shell-bg-muted` | `surface-muted` | main's background with background="muted". |
| `--app-shell-text` | `text` | The text (4.5:1 on bg and bg-muted). |
| `--app-shell-border` | `border` | The line above the footer. |
| `--app-shell-footer-text` | `text-muted` | The footer's text (4.5:1 on bg). |
| `--app-shell-padding` | `spacing-4` | Padding around main's content on small screens (16px). |
| `--app-shell-padding-sm` | `spacing-6` | Padding around main's content from 640px (24px). |
| `--app-shell-padding-lg` | `spacing-8` | Padding around main's content from 1024px (32px). |
| `--app-shell-footer-padding` | `spacing-6` | Padding inside the footer, on every side when set. Unset, it is 24px above and below, and its sides follow main's padding (16, 24 or 32px by width), so its text starts where main's content does. |
<!-- token-table:end -->

components.name: Attachment
components.summary: A file shown as one compact row: an icon for its kind, the name, the kind and size, and, while it uploads, a bar.
components.guide:
# Attachment A file shown as one compact row: an icon for its kind, the name, the kind and size, and, while it uploads, a bar. A failed upload shows why, with a retry button, and `onRemove` adds a remove button. Use it for files in a message, a comment, a record or a form. **Also called:** file, download link. ```tsx import { Attachment } from "@diki-stwn/serupa-ds"; cancel(file)} /> remove(file)} /> ``` ## When to use - Files attached to a message, a comment, a ticket or a record, which people open or download. - Files a person is adding, while they upload, with a way to remove each one. ## When not to use - Choosing files: [FileUpload] (npx serupa-docs FileUpload) has the drop area, the checks and the native input that submits with a form. - A picture people should see: show it with [Image] (npx serupa-docs Image), with the file name as its caption. - A list of many files with columns (owner, modified date): use a [Table] (npx serupa-docs Table). ## Anatomy Drawn from the `Upload` story. 1. **Icon** (`.srp-attachment__icon`): the kind of file, by shape. It's decorative: the kind is also written out. 2. **Name** (`.srp-attachment__name`): the file name, a link with `href`; a long one is cut in the middle so its ending stays. 3. **Kind and size** (`.srp-attachment__meta`): "PDF · 1.5 MB", in the locale's digits and units. 4. **Bar** (`.srp-attachment__progress`): the upload, while `progress` is set. 5. **Message** (`.srp-attachment__error`): why the upload failed, under the box as a Field's error is under its control. 6. **Try again** (`.srp-attachment__retry`): starts the upload again, after an error with `onRetry`. 7. **Remove** (`.srp-attachment__remove`): takes the file away, with `onRemove`. ## Usage - Pass `type` when you have it (a `File`'s `type`, or the server's content type): it picks the icon before the extension does. `kind` overrides both, for a file whose name says nothing ("scan-0042"). - `bytes` is shown in steps of 1000, as phones and macOS count: 1,482,000 is "1.5 MB". Leave it out when you don't know the size. - While uploading, set `progress` from 0 to 100, or `null` when you can't tell. Take it away when the upload is done, and set `done` to say "Complete" after the size. - A failed upload: set `error` to what went wrong ("Larger than 100 MB"), or `true` for "Couldn’t upload". The message shows under the box, which keeps its danger outline. Pass `onRetry` only when trying again can work. - Put several in a `
    ` with one per `
  • `, in a wrapping row or a column. Each grows to its content, up to 320px (`--attachment-max-width`), and never wider than its container. - `thumbnail` takes the icon's place, such as a 40px picture of an image file. FileUpload draws its files this way. - `attachmentKind(name, type)` returns the kind on its own, for a filter or your own icon. It runs in a Server Component too. ```tsx
      {files.map((f) => (
    • remove(f)} />
      • ))}
    ``` ## Behavior - A long name is cut in the middle, as Finder and Drive do: "Laporan keuangan tri…2026 final.xlsx". The last few characters and the extension stay, so files that differ only by year or version still look different. A cut name shows in full in a tooltip on hover and on keyboard focus: the link's focus, or, without a link, its own tab stop. It's laid out in its own direction. - The remove button calls `onRemove`; removing the file is yours. Move focus somewhere sensible afterwards, such as the next file's remove button, since the button goes away with the file. - `disabled` turns off the link and both buttons; the name and size stay readable. ### Do and don't - **Do:** Say what went wrong in `error`, and pass `onRetry` only when trying again can work. (`DoNoFutileRetry`) - **Don't:** Offer a retry for a file that will be refused again, such as one over the size limit. (`DontFutileRetry`) ## Accessibility - **Role and name:** a plain container, with no role of its own; put it in a list item when there are several. The name is read once, whole, even when it's cut on screen. A linked name is a link named by the file and described by its kind and size ("Q3.xlsx, link, Spreadsheet 88 kB"). - **Keyboard:** Tab reaches the link, "Try again" and the remove button, in that order. The link shows the focus ring. - **Progress:** the bar is a `progressbar` named by the file, with its value; with `null` it has no value, so it's read as busy. - **Error:** "Try again" is named with the file ("Try again Pitch.pptx") and described by the message. The message is shown, not announced: say a failure out loud from the code that uploads, with `announce()` or a [Toast] (npx serupa-docs Toast). - **Remove:** named "Remove Invoice.pdf", so several remove buttons in a row are told apart (WCAG 2.4.6). `removeLabel` changes the words. - **Color:** the kind is in the icon's shape and in words, and a failure in words, never in color alone (WCAG 1.4.1). - **Contrast:** the name, kind, size, link and message read 4.5:1, and the icon and the failed outline 3:1, in every theme (`Attachment.test.tsx`). - **What's still yours:** announcing when an upload finishes or fails, and where focus goes after a remove. ## Props | Prop | Type | Default | Notes | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `name` | `string` | | Required. The file name with its extension. | | `bytes` | `number` | | The size in bytes, shown in the locale's units. | | `type` | `string` | | The MIME type; picks the icon and kind before the extension. | | `kind` | `'pdf' \| 'image' \| 'sheet' \| 'doc' \| 'slides' \| 'archive' \| 'code' \| 'audio' \| 'video' \| 'other'` | from `type` and `name` | Overrides the icon and the word. | | `href` | `string` | | Makes the name a link. | | `download` | `boolean \| string` | | With `href`, the link's `download` attribute. | | `progress` | `number \| null` | | 0 to 100 while uploading; `null` when unknown. | | `done` | `boolean` | `false` | The upload finished: "Complete" with a check after the size. | | `thumbnail` | `ReactNode` | | Shown in place of the kind's icon. | | `error` | `ReactNode \| boolean` | | A failed upload's message; `true` says "Couldn’t upload". | | `onRetry` | `() => void` | | Adds "Try again" to a failed upload. | | `onRemove` | `() => void` | | Adds the remove button. | | `removeLabel` | `(name: string) => string` | `` `Remove ${name}` `` | The remove button's name. | | `disabled` | `boolean` | `false` | Turns the link and buttons off. | | `id` | `string` | | Goes to the root `
    `. | `className`, `ref` and other props go to the `
    `. ## Component tokens Each is an optional override: set it on the page, a container or one Attachment. The list lives in `src/components/Attachment/attachment.tokens.json` (also in `design-tokens/components/`). | Token | Default | Use | | --- | --- | --- | | `--attachment-bg` | `surface` | The background. | | `--attachment-text` | `text` | The file name (4.5:1 on bg). | | `--attachment-muted` | `text-muted` | The kind and size (4.5:1 on bg). | | `--attachment-icon` | `text-muted` | The kind icon (3:1 on bg). | | `--attachment-link` | `primary-text` | A linked name (4.5:1 on bg). | | `--attachment-link-hover` | `primary-text-hover` | A linked name under the pointer. | | `--attachment-border` | `border` | The outline. | | `--attachment-border-error` | `danger` | The outline of a failed upload (3:1 on the page). | | `--attachment-error-gap` | `spacing-1.5` | The space between a failed file's box and its message under it, a Field's gap between its control and its error (6px). | | `--attachment-error` | `danger-text` | A failed upload's message (4.5:1 on bg). | | `--attachment-focus-ring` | `focus-ring` | The ring around a focused link, or around a cut name that takes keyboard focus. | | `--attachment-done` | `success-text` | "Complete" and its check once an upload is done (4.5:1 on bg). | | `--attachment-radius` | `radius-control` | The corners (6px). | | `--attachment-padding` | `spacing-2` | Space inside (8px). | | `--attachment-padding-start` | `spacing-3` | Space before the icon (12px). | | `--attachment-gap` | `spacing-2` | Space between the icon, the name and the buttons (8px). | | `--attachment-max-width` | `spacing-80` | The widest it grows (320px); a narrower container makes it narrower. |

components.name: Avatar
components.summary: A small picture of a person (a circle) or of a team, project or organization (a square).
components.guide:
# Avatar A small picture of a person (a circle) or of a team, project or organization (a square). When there's no picture, or it fails to load (also one rendered on the server that failed before the page hydrated), it shows the initials, or a person icon when there's no name either. A picture that is slow to arrive (more than a quarter of a second) shows them too while it loads, then fades in over them, so a slow connection never shows an empty disc. **Also called:** profile picture, user image. ```jsx import { Avatar } from '@diki-stwn/serupa-ds'; // the name is already written next to it: hide the avatar from screen readers
{u.name}
``` ## When to use - Showing who someone is: next to a comment, in a list of members, for the signed-in user. - A team, project or organization's picture or initials, as a square. - Showing whether a person is online, busy, away or offline. ## When not to use - Any other picture, such as a photo, a screenshot or an upload: use [Image] (npx serupa-docs Image) instead. - A symbol for an action or a status: use [Icon] (npx serupa-docs Icon) instead. - A count, a status word or a tag: use [Badge] (npx serupa-docs Badge) instead. ## Anatomy Drawn from the `Status` story. 1. **Frame** (`.srp-avatar__frame`): the circle or square that clips the picture. 2. **Picture** (`.srp-avatar__img`): the person's photo; initials or an icon take its place when there is none. 3. **Status** (`.srp-avatar__status`): the presence dot: online, busy, away or offline, also given in words to screen readers. ## Usage - Pass `name` even when there's a `src`: it gives the accessible name, and the initials if the picture fails to load. - Next to the written name, pass `alt=""` so screen readers don't read it twice. - Use circles for people and squares for everything else. - Set `statusLabel` when the status means something more specific, such as "in a meeting". By default the status is read through the `avatarStatus` label, so it follows the provider's language ("daring" in `idLabels`). ### Do and don't - **Do:** Use circles for people and squares for teams, workspaces and apps. (`DoShapeByKind`) - **Don't:** Draw a workspace as a circle among people: it reads as one more person. (`DontMixShapes`) ## Accessibility - With a name, the avatar is one image (`role="img"`) named by it; the picture inside is decorative. Next to the written name, pass `alt=""` so it isn't read twice. - The status is part of the name, and each one has its own shape: online is a filled dot, busy a dot with a bar across, away a ring with a dot inside, and offline an empty ring. So it isn't told by color alone, and the four stay apart in forced-colors mode. - With `alt=""`, the picture is hidden from screen readers but the status isn't: the dot is read on its own ("online"). - Initials and the person icon keep 4.5:1 on their background in every theme (`Avatar.test.tsx`). - In forced-colors mode the frame gets a border. - **Keyboard:** none of its own: it isn't focusable. Inside a link or a Tooltip trigger, that element takes the focus. ## Props | Prop | Type | Default | What it does | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `id` | string | none | Goes to the root ``. | | `src` | string | | The picture, cropped to fill the shape | | `name` | string | | Gives the initials ("Grace Brewster Hopper" → "GH": the first letter, digit or emoji of the first and last words, one character each, so "ßen Müller" is "SM"; in a script whose letters join, such as Arabic, the two are kept apart so they don't read as a word) and the accessible name | | `alt` | string | the name | The accessible name; `alt=""` hides the avatar from screen readers | | `size` | `'xs'` \| `'sm'` \| `'md'` \| `'lg'` \| `'xl'` | `'md'` | 24, 32, 40, 48 or 64px | | `shape` | `'circle'` \| `'square'` | `'circle'` | Circles for people, squares (8px corners) for everything else | | `status` | `'online'` \| `'busy'` \| `'away'` \| `'offline'` | | A dot at the bottom end, with a shape per status, also added to the accessible name ("Grace Hopper, online") | | `statusLabel` | string | the status | What the status says to screen readers, such as "in a meeting" | | `imgProps` | `` props | `loading="lazy"`, `decoding="async"` | For the picture: `loading="eager"` for one above the fold, `referrerPolicy`, `crossOrigin` | `className`, `style`, `ref` and everything else go to the outer ``, which has `data-component="avatar"`, `data-size` and `data-shape`. `initials(name)` is exported too. ## Component tokens Each is an optional override: set it on the page, a container or one avatar. The list lives in `src/components/Avatar/avatar.tokens.json` (also in `design-tokens/components/`). | Token | Default | Use | | --- | --- | --- | | `--avatar-bg` | `secondary` | The background behind initials and the fallback icon. | | `--avatar-text` | `text` | The initials and the fallback icon (4.5:1 on the background). | | `--avatar-ring` | `surface` | The ring that separates the status dot from the picture. Unset, it takes the fill behind the avatar (--surface-behind, which the page and every surface set), else surface. | | `--avatar-status-online` | `success` | The status dot for status="online". | | `--avatar-status-busy` | `danger` | The status dot for status="busy". | | `--avatar-status-away` | `warning` | The status dot for status="away". | | `--avatar-status-offline` | `border-control` | The status dot for status="offline". | | `--avatar-edge` | `picture-edge` | The hairline just inside the photo's edge, so a face on white keeps its shape on a white page. | | `--avatar-size-xs` | `spacing-6` | size="xs" (24px). | | `--avatar-size-sm` | `spacing-8` | size="sm" (32px). | | `--avatar-size-md` | `spacing-10` | size="md", the default (40px). | | `--avatar-size-lg` | `spacing-12` | size="lg" (48px). | | `--avatar-size-xl` | `spacing-16` | size="xl" (64px). | | `--avatar-radius-square` | `radius-surface` | The corners of shape="square" (8px). | | `--avatar-ring-width` | `border-width-2` | The ring around the status dot (2px). | | `--avatar-weight` | `font-medium` | The initials' weight (500). |

components.name: AvatarGroup
components.summary: Avatars in an overlapping row, such as the people on a project or the assignees of a task.
components.guide:
# AvatarGroup

Avatars in an overlapping row, such as the people on a project or the assignees of a task. Avatars past `max` fold into a "+N" avatar at the end.

**Also called:** avatar stack, facepile.

```tsx
import { Avatar, AvatarGroup } from "@diki-stwn/serupa-ds";

<AvatarGroup aria-label="Assigned to" max={3}>
  <Avatar name="Ada Lovelace" src="/ada.jpg" />
  <Avatar name="Grace Hopper" />
  <Avatar name="Alan Turing" />
  <Avatar name="Katherine Johnson" />
</AvatarGroup>

<AvatarGroup aria-label="Members" size="sm" total={members.length}>
  {members.slice(0, 5).map((m) => <Avatar key={m.id} name={m.name} src={m.photo} />)}
</AvatarGroup>
```

## When to use

- Showing who's involved in something at a glance: a project's members, a task's assignees, who's viewing a document.
- A compact list of people where the faces matter more than the names, and the row has little room.

## When not to use

- One person: use [Avatar] (npx serupa-docs Avatar) on its own.
- When people need to read, compare or act on the names (remove a member, change a role): use [List] (npx serupa-docs List) with an Avatar in each row instead.
- A long, complete list of people, such as a team directory: use [Table] (npx serupa-docs Table) or List; "+N" hides who's there.

## Anatomy

Drawn from the `Overflow` story.

1. **Avatar** (`.srp-avatar-group__item`): one person, overlapping the next.
2. **More** (`.srp-avatar-group__more`): how many more there are, after the ones that fit.

## Usage

- Give the group a `label` that says what the people are to the thing ("Assigned to", "Members"), so a screen reader hears more than a run of names.
- Keep `max` small (3 to 5). Past that, the row reads as texture rather than people.
- When you only have some of the people loaded, pass `total` so "+N" counts everyone not shown.
- Use one `size` for the group; mixed sizes in one row look like a mistake.
- Put the names on hover by wrapping each Avatar in a [Tooltip] (npx serupa-docs Tooltip).
- Without `max`, a group too long for its box (ten reviewers on a phone) wraps onto more lines rather than widening the page. Set `max` to keep it on one line.
- To let people see who's behind "+N", pass `showMore`: "+N" becomes a button that opens a [Popover] (npx serupa-docs Popover) listing them by name. To show them your own way (a Dialog, a members page), pass `onMore` instead.
- On a background other than `surface`, set `--avatar-group-ring` to that color so the rings blend in.

## Behavior

- Each avatar overlaps the one before by 2px (sm), 4px (md), 8px (lg) or 12px (xl), and at xs they sit edge to edge, so the initials under the overlap stay whole; earlier ones sit on top, so every status dot shows. The overlap uses logical margins, so the row runs right to left in RTL.
- Each avatar has a 2px ring in `surface`. On another background, set `--avatar-group-ring` to that color.
- Past 99, "+N" reads "99+" (past 9 at `xs`, "9+") so it fits; its name keeps the exact count ("116 more").
- "+N" is written in the locale's digits, as Badge's count is: "+٣" in `ar-EG`.
- Wrap an avatar in a Tooltip to show the name on hover; it still lines up with the others.
- With `showMore`, "+N" opens a popover listing each hidden avatar with its name, then "N more" for the ones you didn't pass (`total`). With `onMore`, it calls your handler. Without either, "+N" is a picture, not a control.

### Do and don't

- **Do:** Keep `max` small (3 to 5), with "+N" for everyone else. (`DoSmallMax`)
- **Don't:** Show everyone in one row: past five or so, it reads as texture rather than people. (`DontShowEveryone`)

## Accessibility

- **Role and name:** `role="group"`, named by `label`. Each avatar keeps its own name (and status), so a screen reader reads every person shown, then "N more".
- **Keyboard:** with `showMore` or `onMore`, "+N" is a button that Tab reaches and Enter or Space opens, named like the picture ("2 more"). Otherwise nothing of its own; avatars inside links or Tooltips are reached by Tab as usual.
- **Contrast:** the "+N" text keeps 4.5:1 on its background in every theme (`AvatarGroup.test.tsx`).
- **What's still yours:** a `label` for the group, and a `name` on every Avatar.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | string | none | Goes to the root `<div>`. |
| `children` | `<Avatar>` elements | | The avatars, in order. Each can sit inside a Tooltip or a link, and fragments are opened up. |
| `max` | `number` | all | The most avatars to show; the rest become "+N". |
| `total` | `number` | the number of children | How many there are in all, when you pass only some. "+N" counts the ones not shown. |
| `size` | `'xs' \| 'sm' \| 'md' \| 'lg' \| 'xl'` | `'md'` | Every avatar's size, wrapped ones included. It wins over each avatar's own `size`. |
| `aria-label` | `string` | | The group's accessible name, such as "Assigned to". |
| `showMore` | `boolean` | `false` | Makes "+N" a button that opens a popover listing the people not shown. |
| `onMore` | `(event) => void` | | Makes "+N" a button that calls this, to show the rest your own way. Wins over `showMore`. |
| `moreLabel` | `(count, formatted) => string` | `"N more"` | What a screen reader hears for "+N", and the last line of the showMore list. `formatted` is the count in the locale's digits and grouping ("1,234", "١٬٢٣٤"); `count` is for plural rules. By default the `avatarMore` label ("N lainnya" in `idLabels`). |

`ref`, `className` and other props go to the outer `<div>`.

## Component tokens

Each is an optional override: set it on the page, a container or one group. The list lives in `src/components/AvatarGroup/avatar-group.tokens.json` (also in `design-tokens/components/`).

<!-- token-table:start (made from avatar-group.tokens.json by npm run tokens: edit the descriptions there) -->
| Token | Default | Use |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--avatar-group-ring` | `surface` | The ring around each avatar, which keeps the overlapping edges clear. Unset, it takes the fill behind the group (--surface-behind, which the page and every surface set), else surface. |
| `--avatar-group-more-bg` | `secondary` | The "+N" avatar's background. |
| `--avatar-group-more-color` | `text` | The "+N" text (4.5:1 on more-bg). |
| `--avatar-group-more-bg-hover` | `secondary-hover` | The "+N" button's background on hover, with `showMore` or `onMore`. |
| `--avatar-group-more-bg-pressed` | `secondary-pressed` | The "+N" button's background while it's held down, one step past hover. |
| `--avatar-group-focus-ring` | `focus-ring` | The focus ring round the "+N" button. |
| `--avatar-group-ring-width` | `border-width-2` | The ring's width (2px). |
| `--avatar-group-overlap-sm` | `spacing-0.5` | How far each avatar overlaps the one before at size sm (2px). At xs the avatars sit edge to edge, unless this is set. |
| `--avatar-group-overlap-md` | `spacing-1` | The overlap at size md, the default (4px), and lg (8px unless this is set). |
| `--avatar-group-overlap-lg` | `spacing-3` | The overlap at size xl (12px). |
<!-- token-table:end -->

components.name: Badge
components.summary: A short label for status, counts and categories, optionally clickable.
components.guide:
# Badge

A short label for status, counts and categories, optionally clickable. One size (20px tall, `text-xs`, 12px icons) in three styles (**subtle**, **solid**, **outline**), six tones built on the status colors and 17 palette tones for categories and tags. Every tone and style keeps 4.5:1 text in every theme. Extras: a status dot, a leading icon, a count and a remove button. States: hover, focus and active on clickable badges, and loading on any badge.

**Also called:** tag, chip, pill, label.

```jsx
import { Badge } from '@diki-stwn/serupa-ds';

<Badge>Draft</Badge>                                    // subtle, neutral
<Badge tone="success" dot>Online</Badge>
<Badge variant="solid" tone="danger" dot ping>Live</Badge>          // live states only
<Badge tone="warning" startIcon="schedule">Pending</Badge>
<Badge variant="solid" tone="primary">New</Badge>
<Badge variant="outline" tone="info">Beta</Badge>
<Badge tone="violet" onRemove={() => removeTag("Design")}>Design</Badge>

// "something new", no number: a lone indicator dot on the corner of the control
<button aria-label="Notifications, new" className="relative">
  <Icon name="notifications" />
  <Badge dot tone="danger" className="absolute top-0 right-0" />
</button>

// clickable: a button or a link, with hover, focus and active states
<Badge tone="success" dot onClick={openFilter}>Open</Badge>
<Badge tone="info" href="/docs">Docs</Badge>
<Badge variant="solid" tone="primary" loading={saving} onClick={retry}>Retry</Badge>

// a count on an icon button: name the button, hide the number
<button aria-label="Notifications, 5 unread">
  <Icon name="notifications" />
  <Badge variant="solid" tone="danger" count={5} aria-hidden="true" />
</button>
```

## When to use

- The status of an item in a table, a list or a card: "Draft", "Paid", "Failed".
- Tags and categories on an item, including filter chips people can remove.
- A count or a "something new" dot on an icon or a nav item, such as unread messages.

## When not to use

- An action: use [Button] (npx serupa-docs Button) instead. A badge is a label first. Make it clickable when the badge itself is the natural target (a status that opens its filter, a tag that links to its page).
- A message that needs a sentence, or that people must act on: use [Alert] (npx serupa-docs Alert) instead.
- Picking one option from a few: use [SegmentedControl] (npx serupa-docs SegmentedControl) instead.

## Anatomy

Drawn from the `Extras` story.

1. **Dot** (`.srp-badge__dot`): an optional mark of the tone before the label.
2. **Label** (`.srp-badge__label`): the word or number the badge says.
3. **Remove** (`.srp-badge__remove`): takes the badge away, when it can be removed (a filter, a tag).

## Usage

- Keep labels to one or two words; a badge is not a sentence. A badge is at most as wide as its container, and a longer label ends in an ellipsis; then the full label shows as the badge's `title` on hover (as on Button), unless you pass your own `title` or `aria-label`. Keyboard and touch users can't see a title, so keep labels short enough to fit.
- Use status tones for status and palette tones for categories. Don't make a category red or green: it reads as a status.
- Use `subtle` by default and `solid` sparingly: one strong badge per row or card.

### Do and don't

- **Do:** Keep the label to a word or two. (`DoShortLabel`)
- **Don't:** Put a sentence in a badge: it gets cut off, and the full text shows only on hover. (`DontSentence`)
- **Do:** Use palette tones for categories, such as teams or topics. (`DoPaletteForCategories`)
- **Don't:** Use status tones for categories: a red or green team reads as a problem or a success. (`DontStatusForCategories`)

### Styles

| Style | Light themes | Dark themes | Use for |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `subtle` (default) | 100 fill, 700 text, 1px outline in the text color at 20% | 950 fill, 300 text, outline at 20% | Most badges: statuses in tables, tags, categories |
| `solid` | 600 or 700 fill, white text | 400 fill, 950 text | Strong emphasis: "New", counts, one urgent status |
| `outline` | 700 text and 1px border | 300 text, 400 border | Quiet labels on busy or tinted surfaces (transparent fill) |

### Tones

- **`neutral`** (default): `secondary` fill and `text` (subtle, outlined in the text color at 20% like every subtle badge), `surface-inverse` and `text-inverse` (solid), `border-strong` and `text` (outline).
- **`primary`**: the theme's brand color, through the alias colors (`primary-subtle`, `primary`, `on-primary`), so it follows Blue, Violet and Emerald.
- **Statuses**: `success` (green), `warning` (amber), `danger` (red), `info` (sky), through the status roles (`success-subtle`, `success-text`, `success`, `on-success` and the same for the others), so a theme or page that sets `--success` or `--danger` moves its badges too.
- **Palette**: `red`, `orange`, `amber`, `yellow`, `lime`, `green`, `emerald`, `teal`, `cyan`, `sky`, `blue`, `indigo`, `violet`, `purple`, `fuchsia`, `pink`, `rose`, for categories and tags.

Palette tones use the fixed palette steps in the Styles table. Status tones use their roles: subtle is the status tint with its text color, solid the status fill with its `on-` color, outline the status text color on a border in the status fill. Solid uses 600 where white text keeps 4.5:1 on it (red, blue, indigo, violet, purple, fuchsia, pink, rose) and 700 for the lighter families. The steps follow the nearest theme: a badge in a dark area nested in a light page takes the dark steps.

### Extras

- **Dot**: `dot` adds a 6px dot before the label, centered in a box as tall as an icon and 2px narrower (10×12px), so a dot badge spaces like an icon badge with a little less room for the lighter dot. Use it for live states ("Online", "Away").
- **Indicator**: `dot` with no label, icon or count renders a lone dot that says "something new" without a number, for the corner of an icon or avatar. It's a solid circle in the tone's fill (any `variant` is ignored), 8px, with a 2px ring in the surface color so it stays apart from what it overlaps. You place it (for example `className="absolute top-0 right-0"` inside a `relative` parent). It can't be clicked or removed (too small to target): `onClick`, `href` and `onRemove` are dropped with a warning. Switch to `count` once you know how many.
- **Ping**: `ping` with `dot` adds the system's ping animation (the same `ping` keyframes and `--animate-ping` token as the `animate-ping` utility): a copy of the dot grows to twice its size and fades, every second, while the dot stays put. It works on a dot in a label and on the indicator. Use it for live states ("Live", "Recording", "In a call"), not for unread or ordinary statuses: several pinging dots on one screen compete for attention. Off under reduced motion and in forced-colors mode. Constant motion lasting more than 5 seconds should be stoppable (WCAG 2.2.2), so turn `ping` off when the state ends or after a while.
- **Icon**: `startIcon` adds a 12px icon before the label. It replaces the dot.
- **Count**: `count` makes a round pill, as wide as it is tall for one digit, with tabular digits. Past `max` (99) it shows "99+", while screen readers hear the real count and a tooltip (`title`) shows it, unless you pass your own `title`; at 0 it renders nothing unless `showZero`. The number is written in the digits of the locale from `SerupaProvider` (or the browser), as Calendar writes its days: ٩٩+ in Egyptian Arabic. A count badge has no label, dot, icon or remove button.
- **Optical balance**: like Button, an icon reads lighter than text, so a badge with an icon on one side only gets 2px more padding on the text side (`--badge-icon-offset`): a leading icon or dot pads the end (6 + 2px), a × pads the start. With an icon on both sides, or none, the padding is even. Logical sides, so right-to-left mirrors it.
- **Remove**: `onRemove` adds a × button at the end, for filter chips and tags. It's a real `<button type="button">` named "Remove" + the label, with a 2px focus ring. The × mirrors a leading icon: an icon-sized box (12px), `--badge-gap` from the label, and the same end padding as the start, so a badge with an icon, a label and a × is balanced. Because the × glyph sits further inside its box than most icons, the box is pulled in 2px on each side to even out what you see. The button still has a full 24×24 target (the WCAG 2.2 minimum, as on a small Button), reaching 2px past the badge's top and bottom, and its focus ring goes around all of it.

## States

Only a clickable badge (`onClick` or `href`) has hover, focus and active states, so a plain status badge never looks clickable.

| State | Look |
| --- | --- |
| Hover | A layer over the fill at 10%: the text color on subtle and outline (and the text moves 30% toward black in light themes, white in dark), black (light) or white (dark) on solid. The layer always moves away from the text, so every tone and style keeps 4.5:1 |
| Active (pressed) | The same layer at 15% |
| Focus | Keyboard focus only: a 2px `focus-ring` outline 2px out, like Button. The gap is transparent, and forced-colors mode draws it too |
| Loading | Any badge: a 12px ring in the text color, centered over the hidden content; the badge keeps its width and colors |
| Disabled | A disabled clickable badge: `disabled-surface` fill, `disabled-border` edge and `disabled-text` label at full opacity, `not-allowed` cursor, no layer |

## Behavior

### Micro-interactions

The same as Button's, each with a component token to tune it or turn it off. Only scale, opacity and the loading blur move, so nothing around the badge reflows.

- **Press** (clickable badges): the state layer goes from 10% to 15% while held by pointer, Space or Enter, so the badge darkens a step past hover. It doesn't shrink unless you ask (`--badge-press-scale: var(--scale-97)`): a shrink is hard to see under a finger on something this small.
- **Loading** (any badge): the content fades out while the ring fades and grows in, in 150ms; both blur a little (`blur-xs`) as they cross, so it reads as one change.
- Under reduced motion, a shrink you turned on is off and loading only fades (no blur); the held layer stays. Your `onPointerDown`, `onKeyDown`, `onKeyUp` and `onBlur` still run first.

## Accessibility

- Every tone and style keeps 4.5:1 text, and outline borders 3:1, in every theme; `Badge.test.tsx` checks all 69 combinations in each theme.
- Don't rely on color alone: say the status in the label ("Failed", not just a red badge). The dot and icons are decorative and hidden from screen readers.
- An indicator dot is hidden from screen readers. Say what it means on the control it sits on ("Notifications, new"), or give the dot an `aria-label` (it then becomes `role="img"`).
- A number alone means little to a screen reader. Name the control the count sits on ("Notifications, 5 unread") and hide the badge with `aria-hidden`, or give the badge an `aria-label`.
- A clickable badge is a real `<button>` or link, so Tab, Enter and Space work and screen readers announce it as one. Its label is its name; make it say what happens ("Filter: Open"), not just the status.
- While loading, the label stays in the accessibility tree (the badge keeps its name), `aria-busy` is set and `loadingLabel` is announced once.
- The remove button is reachable with Tab and pressed with Enter or Space. When `onRemove` takes the badge away and its × had focus, focus moves to the next tag's × in the same list, or the one before it after the last tag, so it isn't lost on the page. After the last tag, or to put focus somewhere else (such as the input that adds tags), move it in `onRemove`: the badge leaves focus alone then.
- In forced-colors (high-contrast) mode every badge gets a visible border.

### Keyboard

| Key | Does |
| --- | --- |
| Tab | To a clickable badge (a `<button>` or link), then to its remove button |
| Enter, Space | Press a clickable badge (Enter only, on a link), or the remove button |

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | string | none | Goes to the root `<span>`. |
| `variant` | `'subtle'` \| `'solid'` \| `'outline'` | `'subtle'` | The style |
| `tone` | `'neutral'` \| `'primary'` \| `'success'` \| `'warning'` \| `'danger'` \| `'info'` \| a palette family (`'red'` … `'rose'`) | `'neutral'` | The color |
| `dot` | boolean | `false` | A 6px status dot before the label, in the text color. With no label, icon or count, a lone indicator dot (see Extras) |
| `ping` | boolean | `false` | With `dot` (in a label or the indicator): the dot pings, growing and fading every second. For live states. Ignored without a dot |
| `startIcon` | icon name or element | | An icon before the label (Material Symbols or custom icon name); replaces the dot |
| `count` | number | | Makes it a count badge: a round pill with the number. 0 renders nothing |
| `max` | number | `99` | Past this, the count shows `99+` |
| `showZero` | boolean | `false` | Show a count of 0 |
| `onRemove` | function | | Adds a × button at the end that calls it |
| `removeLabel` | string | `'Remove'` | The × button's accessible name, before the label: "Remove Design" |
| `onClick` | function | | Renders a `<button type="button">` with hover, focus and active states. `onRemove` is ignored then (a button can't hold another button) |
| `href` | string | | Renders a link (the component set with `Serupa.configure({ link })`, `<a>` by default) with the same states; `target="_blank"` gets `rel="noopener noreferrer"` |
| `disabled` | boolean | `false` | With `onClick`: a native disabled button, in the neutral disabled colors with no states |
| `loading` | boolean | `false` | A ring at the icon size replaces the content and the badge keeps its width. Sets `aria-busy`; on a clickable badge also `aria-disabled`, and clicks, Enter and Space do nothing while focus stays. A remove button is disabled meanwhile. Once the ring shows, it stays at least 500ms, so loading that ends a moment later doesn't flash it |
| `loadingLabel` | string | `'Loading…'` | Said to screen readers when loading starts, not shown ("" says nothing) |

Any other attribute (`id`, `className`, `style`, `title`, `type`, `aria-*`, `data-*`, `ref`) goes to the outer element: a `<span>`, or the `<button>` or link when clickable. Every badge has `data-component="badge"`, `data-variant`, `data-tone` and `data-size` for tests, plus `data-interactive` when clickable and `data-loading` while loading.

components.name: BottomNav
components.summary: A bar of three to five main destinations fixed along the bottom of a phone screen, where a thumb reaches: each an icon over a short label, the current page marked.
components.guide:
# BottomNav

A bar of three to five main destinations fixed along the bottom of a phone screen, where a thumb reaches: each an icon over a short label, the current page marked. From 768px up it hides by default, where [Navbar] (npx serupa-docs Navbar) shows its links.

**Also called:** tab bar, bottom navigation bar.

```tsx
import { BottomNav, BottomNavLink } from "@diki-stwn/serupa-ds";

<BottomNav aria-label="Main">
  <BottomNavLink href="/" icon="home">Home</BottomNavLink>
  <BottomNavLink href="/inbox" icon="inbox" current>Inbox</BottomNavLink>
  <BottomNavLink as={RouterLink} to="/account" icon="person">Account</BottomNavLink>
</BottomNav>
```

## When to use

- An app people use on a phone with three to five top-level places they switch between often.

## When not to use

- Two places, or more than five: use [Tabs] (npx serupa-docs Tabs) for two, and [Navbar] (npx serupa-docs Navbar)'s menu or a [Sidebar] (npx serupa-docs Sidebar) for more.
- Actions, such as "New message": use a [Fab] (npx serupa-docs Fab) or a Button. Every item here goes somewhere.
- Steps in a flow, or filters on one page: use [Tabs] (npx serupa-docs Tabs) or [SegmentedControl] (npx serupa-docs SegmentedControl).

## Anatomy

Drawn from the `WithBadges` story.

1. **Bar** (`.srp-bottom-nav`): the navigation landmark, fixed along the bottom of a narrow screen, clear of a phone's home bar.
2. **List** (`.srp-bottom-nav__list`): the destinations, side by side in equal widths.
3. **Link** (`.srp-bottom-nav__link`): one destination; the current page is shaded and has `aria-current="page"`.
4. **Icon** (`.srp-bottom-nav__icon`): the destination's icon, in a pill that is shaded on the current page.
5. **Badge** (`.srp-bottom-nav__badge`): an optional count or dot on the icon's top-end corner, such as unread items.
6. **Label** (`.srp-bottom-nav__label`): the destination's name, always shown under its icon.
7. **Spacer** (`.srp-bottom-nav__spacer`): holds the bar's height at the end of the page, so the bar never covers the last content.

## Usage

- **Links:** BottomNavLink takes an `icon` and a label of one or two short words; `current` marks the current page, and `badge` puts a count on its icon (`badge={<Badge count={4} tone="danger" variant="solid" />}`, or a lone `<Badge dot />` for "something new"). `as` renders your router's link, typed with its props, or set it once with `configure({ link })`.
- **Widths:** `hideFrom` is the width from which it hides: `'md'` (768px, default), `'sm'` (640px), `'lg'` (1024px) or `false` to keep it at every width. Show the same destinations in the Navbar or Sidebar above that width.
- **Room on the page:** while it shows, a spacer before it takes its height at the end of the page, so the last content scrolls clear of it, and `scroll-padding-bottom` keeps anything focused or scrolled to from hiding under it.
- **Other things on the bottom edge:** a bottom [Toaster] (npx serupa-docs Toast), [OfflineBanner] (npx serupa-docs OfflineBanner) and [Fab] (npx serupa-docs Fab) move up above the bar while it shows.
- **Safe areas:** on phones with a home indicator it adds `env(safe-area-inset-bottom)` under the links (and the side insets in landscape). Pages need `viewport-fit=cover` in their viewport meta for the browser to report them.
- Keep the order the same on every page, and one BottomNav per page.

### Do and don't

- **Do:** Give each link an `icon` and one or two short words ("Home", "Inbox"). (`DoShortLabels`)
- **Don't:** Write long labels: they wrap and crowd the bar on a phone. (`DontLongLabels`)

## Accessibility

- **Role and name:** a `<nav>` landmark named by `label`, with a list of links, so screen readers say how many there are. The current one has `aria-current="page"`. Icons are hidden; the label is each link's name. A `badge` is read after the name, as its description ("Inbox, link, 4"), so a count needs no extra words; give a lone dot an `aria-label` ("New messages") or it says nothing.
- **Long labels:** a label passed as text that doesn't fit ends in an ellipsis and shows whole on hover and on the link's keyboard focus ([TruncatedText] (npx serupa-docs TruncatedText)); the link's name is always the whole label.
- **Keyboard:** each link is a Tab stop, in order; the focus ring is drawn inside the link so the bar doesn't cut it.
- **Target size:** each link fills its column and the bar's 64px height.
- **Contrast:** labels and the current page read 4.5:1 on the bar in every theme (`BottomNav.test.tsx`). In forced-colors mode the current page keeps an outline.
- **Print:** it and its spacer are hidden.
- **What's still yours:** short labels that make sense alone, `current` on the right link, and the same destinations reachable above `hideFrom`.

## Props

### BottomNav

| Prop | Type | Default | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `aria-label` | `string` | | The landmark's name ("Main") |
| `hideFrom` | `'sm'` \| `'md'` \| `'lg'` \| `false` | `'md'` | The width from which it hides |
| `children` | `ReactNode` | | Three to five BottomNavLink |
| `id` | string | none | Goes to the `<nav>`. |

`className`, `ref` and other props go to the `<nav>`.

### BottomNavLink

| Prop | Type | Default | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `icon` | icon name, icon or element | | Over the label |
| `current` | `boolean` | `false` | The current page |
| `badge` | `ReactNode` | none | A count or dot on the icon's top-end corner, such as `<Badge count={4} />`; read after the link's name |
| `as` | component | `configure({ link })` or `'a'` | Your router's link |
| `children` | `ReactNode` | | The label |

Other props, such as `href` or your router's `to`, go to the link.

## Component tokens

Each is an optional override: set it on the page, a container or one BottomNav. The list lives in `src/components/BottomNav/bottom-nav.tokens.json` (also in `design-tokens/components/`).

<!-- token-table:start (made from bottom-nav.tokens.json by npm run tokens: edit the descriptions there) -->
| Token | Default | Use |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--bottom-nav-bg` | `surface` | The bar's background. |
| `--bottom-nav-border` | `border` | The hairline along its top. |
| `--bottom-nav-text` | `text-muted` | A link's icon and label (4.5:1 on bg). |
| `--bottom-nav-text-hover` | `text` | A link under the pointer (not the current one, which keeps its own color). |
| `--bottom-nav-icon-bg-hover` | `secondary` | The pill behind the icon under the pointer (not on the current item, which keeps its own fill). |
| `--bottom-nav-icon-bg-pressed` | `secondary-hover` | The pill behind an item's icon while the item is held down, one step past hover (not on the current item, which keeps its own fill). |
| `--bottom-nav-text-active` | `primary-text` | The current page's icon and label (4.5:1 on bg). |
| `--bottom-nav-icon-bg-active` | `primary-subtle` | The pill behind the current page's icon. |
| `--bottom-nav-focus-ring` | `focus-ring` | The keyboard focus ring, inside the link. |
| `--bottom-nav-height` | `spacing-16` | The bar's height above the safe-area inset (64px); links fill it, so each is a 64px-tall target. |
| `--bottom-nav-badge-offset-x` | `spacing-8` | How far from the icon pill's start edge a badge starts: 4px past the middle, so it sits on the icon's top-end corner. |
| `--bottom-nav-badge-offset-y` | `spacing-0` | How far below the icon pill's top edge a badge sits. |
| `--bottom-nav-z-index` | `z-40` | Its stacking: with a sticky Navbar, under dialogs and toasts. |
<!-- token-table:end -->

components.name: Breadcrumb
components.summary: Shows where the current page sits: links to the pages above it, from the top level down, with chevrons between them.
components.guide:
# Breadcrumb

Shows where the current page sits: links to the pages above it, from the top level down, with chevrons between them. The last item is the current page. On a deep trail, `maxItems` collapses the middle into a "…" button that shows it again.

**Also called:** breadcrumbs, breadcrumb trail.

```jsx
import { Breadcrumb, BreadcrumbItem } from '@diki-stwn/serupa-ds';

<Breadcrumb>
  <BreadcrumbItem href="/" icon="home">Home</BreadcrumbItem>
  <BreadcrumbItem href="/projects">Projects</BreadcrumbItem>
  <BreadcrumbItem>Website redesign</BreadcrumbItem>
</Breadcrumb>

<Breadcrumb maxItems={3} separator="slash">…</Breadcrumb>

// With a router
<BreadcrumbItem as={RouterLink} to="/projects">Projects</BreadcrumbItem>
```

## When to use

- Pages two or more levels down a hierarchy, where people need to see where they are and go up a level.
- People who land deep in the product from a search or a shared link, and need a way to the pages above.

## When not to use

- The main way around the product: use a [Navbar] (npx serupa-docs Navbar) or a [Sidebar] (npx serupa-docs Sidebar) instead.
- Steps in a task done in order: use [Stepper] (npx serupa-docs Stepper) instead.
- A page at the top level, or a flat site: leave it out; the page's [Heading] (npx serupa-docs Heading) already says where people are.

## Anatomy

Drawn from the `Collapsed` story.

1. **List** (`.srp-breadcrumb__list`): the pages from the top level down to this one.
2. **Link** (`.srp-breadcrumb__link`): a page above this one.
3. **Separator** (`.srp-breadcrumb__separator`): the mark between pages; screen readers skip it.
4. **More** (`.srp-breadcrumb__more`): opens the pages hidden when the trail is too long.
5. **Current page** (`.srp-breadcrumb__item--current`): this page, last, not a link.

## Usage

- Go from the top level down to the current page, and make the current page the last item.
- Label each item with the title people see on that page, so the trail matches where it leads.
- On deep trails, set `maxItems` so it fits on one line; the first item and the last ones stay visible.
- Where the trail must stay on one line once "…" is pressed, such as a phone header, add `collapse="menu"`: "…" opens a [Menu] (npx serupa-docs Menu) of the hidden pages instead of putting them back in the trail.
- With a router, register its link component once with `configure({ link })`, or pass it as `as` so client-side navigation keeps working.

### Do and don't

- **Do:** Name each item with the title people see on that page, and end with the current page. (`DoPageTitles`)
- **Don't:** Make up names such as "Start", "List" or "Back": the trail no longer matches the pages it leads to. (`DontMadeUpNames`)

## Accessibility

- Each link, and the "…" button, takes a press over at least 24×24px (WCAG 2.5.8) without moving the trail. On a touch screen it's 44px high, as Apple and Material ask (the width stays, so links never overlap).
- A long unbroken label, such as a file name or a URL slug, wraps inside the trail rather than running past a 320px screen (WCAG 1.4.10).
- An item with only an `icon` needs an `aria-label`. Without one it's a link a screen reader can only call "link", and it warns once in the console.
- A Breadcrumb with no items renders nothing, so it doesn't leave an empty nav landmark.
- It's a `<nav>` landmark named "Breadcrumb" holding an ordered list, so screen readers say how many levels there are. Give it another name if the page has two.
- The current page has `aria-current="page"`. Separators sit inside the item after them and are hidden from screen readers, so the list has one item per page.
- With `collapse="menu"`, "…" is a menu button named "More pages" (`aria-haspopup="menu"`, `aria-expanded`), and the hidden pages are links in the menu. It follows Menu's keys: Enter, Space or ↓ opens it on the first page, ↑ ↓ move, Enter follows a link, and Escape closes it and returns to "…".
- Links, the current page and separators keep 4.5:1 on `surface` in every theme (`Breadcrumb.test.tsx`).
- Links are underlined on hover only: their place in the trail and the chevrons already say they're links.
- **Keyboard:** Tab moves through the links, and Enter follows one. The current page is text, not a Tab stop. With `maxItems`, the "…" button is a Tab stop too, and Enter or Space shows the hidden pages (or opens their menu with `collapse="menu"`).

## Props

### Breadcrumb

| Prop | Type | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | string | none | Goes to the root `<nav>`. |
| `children` | BreadcrumbItems | none | From the top level to the current page |
| `separator` | `'chevron'` \| `'slash'` | `'chevron'` | What goes between items. The chevron points left in right-to-left text, following the nearest `dir`, so a `dir="ltr"` block on a right-to-left page points right |
| `maxItems` | number (2 or more) | no limit | Shows the first item, "…", then the last `maxItems - 1`. Pressing "…" shows them all and moves focus to the first one it showed |
| `collapse` | `'inline'` \| `'menu'` | `'inline'` | What "…" does: shows the hidden items in the trail, or opens a Menu of them |
| `aria-label` | string | `"Breadcrumb"` | The nav's name |
| `expandLabel` | string | `"Show all pages"` (`"More pages"` with `collapse="menu"`) | The "…" button's name, and the menu's |

`className`, `style`, `ref` and everything else go to the `<nav>`, which has `data-component="breadcrumb"`.

### BreadcrumbItem

| Prop | Type | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `href` | string | none | Where it goes |
| `icon` | an icon name or element | none | A 16px icon before the label |
| `as` | a component | the `configure({ link })` link, else `'a'` | Your router's link component. Set it once for the app with `configure({ link })`; `as` wins for one link. Typed: the props and `ref` are those of the element `as` names, so `as={RouterLink} to="/x"` checks `to`, and without `as` they're an `<a>`'s. A link set only with `configure({ link })` is typed as an `<a>`, so pass it `href`. |

The last item is the current page (Breadcrumb sets its `current` prop; you don't pass it): text with `aria-current="page"`, not a link, even if it has an `href`. `className`, `ref` and everything else go to the link.

## Component tokens

Each is an optional override: set it on the page, a container or one breadcrumb. The list lives in `src/components/Breadcrumb/breadcrumb.tokens.json` (also in `design-tokens/components/`).

<!-- token-table:start (made from breadcrumb.tokens.json by npm run tokens: edit the descriptions there) -->
| Token | Default | Use |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--breadcrumb-text` | `text-muted` | A link to a parent page (4.5:1 on surface). |
| `--breadcrumb-text-hover` | `text` | A link on hover. |
| `--breadcrumb-text-current` | `text` | The current page. |
| `--breadcrumb-separator` | `text-muted` | The chevron or slash between items. |
| `--breadcrumb-focus-ring` | `focus-ring` | The keyboard focus ring. |
| `--breadcrumb-font-size` | `text-sm` | The text (14px). |
| `--breadcrumb-weight-current` | `font-medium` | The current page's weight (500). |
| `--breadcrumb-gap` | `spacing-1.5` | Space between an item and a separator (6px). |
| `--breadcrumb-separator-size` | `spacing-4` | The chevron's size (16px). |
| `--breadcrumb-icon-size` | `spacing-4` | An item's icon (16px). |
| `--breadcrumb-focus-radius` | `radius-inner` | The focus ring's corners (4px). |
<!-- token-table:end -->
