components.summary: Triggers an action: submitting a form, opening a dialog, confirming or canceling.
components.guide:
# Button

Triggers an action: submitting a form, opening a dialog, confirming or canceling. With `href` it becomes a link that looks like a button, for navigation. Every variant also has a destructive version; every value comes from this system's tokens.

**Also called:** call to action, CTA.

```jsx
import { Button, IconButton, buttonClass } from '@diki-stwn/serupa-ds';

<Button>Save changes</Button>
<Button variant="outline">Cancel</Button>
<Button destructive>Delete project</Button>
<Button variant="outline" destructive>Delete</Button>
<Button startIcon="add">New project</Button>
<Button variant="outline" endIcon="arrow_forward">Continue</Button>
<IconButton icon="settings" label="Settings" />
<Button loading={saving} startIcon="save">Save changes</Button>
<IconButton size="sm" destructive icon="delete" label="Remove" />
<Button href="/signup" endIcon="arrow_forward">Get started</Button>
<Button href="https://example.com" target="_blank" variant="link">Help</Button>
<label className={buttonClass({ variant: 'outline' })}>Upload <input type="file" hidden /></label>
```

## When to use

- Someone starts an action on the page: submitting a form, saving, opening a dialog, confirming or canceling.
- A call to action that goes to another page and should stand out more than a text link, such as "Get started" (give it an `href`).
- The confirming step of an action that deletes something or can't be undone (with `destructive`).

## When not to use

- A link inside a sentence, or a list of links: use [Link] (npx serupa-docs Link) instead.
- An icon on its own: use [IconButton] (npx serupa-docs IconButton), which makes the label required.
- A setting that stays on or off, such as bold or mute: use [ToggleButton] (npx serupa-docs ToggleButton).
- One choice out of a few options shown side by side: use [SegmentedControl] (npx serupa-docs SegmentedControl).
- A list of actions behind one button: use [Menu] (npx serupa-docs Menu).

## Anatomy

Drawn from the `States` story.

1. **Icon** (`.srp-btn__icon`): an optional picture before the label (`startIcon`) or after it (`endIcon`), or the whole of an icon-only button.
2. **Label** (`.srp-btn__label`): what the button does, in words.
3. **Loader** (`.srp-btn__loader`): the spinner while `loading`, over the label, which keeps the button's width.

When an action succeeds (`success`), a check takes the loader's place for a moment.

## Usage

- A button is never wider than its container. A text label that doesn't fit ends in an ellipsis and shows in full as the button's `title` on hover (the same words as its name, so screen readers don't hear it twice). Keyboard focus and touch don't show a title, so where a label may not fit (a narrow column, a long translation, 400% zoom) pass `wrap`: the label takes as many lines as it needs and the button grows from its size's height. Short labels are still best. In a flex row the long-labeled button is the one that gives way: it shrinks to its ellipsis rather than pushing the buttons next to it out of the row, and icon-only buttons keep their square. In a grid, give the column `minmax(0, 1fr)` rather than `auto`, or the row widens the column instead.
- One `primary` button per view or dialog; everything else is `secondary`, `outline` or `ghost`.
- Label with a verb: "Save changes", not "OK".
- Over a photo, a video or a brand-colored panel, set `surface="dark"` (white controls for dark media) or `surface="light"` (black for light media). They stay the same in every theme. Put a scrim on the media under the buttons, a dark or light wash, so they keep 4.5:1 at its lightest or darkest point. IconButton, Link and Divider take the same prop, and Loader's `tone="inverse"` is its white.
- Use `destructive` only for actions that delete or can't be undone, and only one solid (`primary`) destructive button per view, usually in the confirmation step.
- An icon on its own is an IconButton, whose `label` is required. Prefer a label with an icon unless the icon is universally understood (close, search, settings).
- Use a left icon to reinforce the action (`add` for create) and a right icon for direction (`arrow_forward` for next, `expand_more` for menus). Don't use both.
- Prefer `disabledReason` to a bare `disabled`: people can find out what to do instead of guessing.
- Use `loading` (or return a promise from `onClick`) for actions that take longer than about a second, and keep the label as it was ("Save changes", not "Saving…") so the width doesn't jump.
- Navigation is a link: give the Button an `href`, not an `onClick` that changes the URL.
- Icons come from Material Symbols Rounded (filled), drawn as SVG. The consumer provides the click handler.

### Do and don't

- **Do:** One `primary` button for the main action of a view or dialog, with the others `secondary`, `outline` or `ghost`. (`DoOnePrimary`)
- **Don't:** Several `primary` buttons side by side: none of them reads as the main action, and people stop to compare. (`DontManyPrimaries`)
- **Do:** Label with what happens: "Delete project", "Keep project". (`DoVerbLabels`)
- **Don't:** "Yes" and "No", which make people go back and read the question to know what each does. (`DontVagueLabels`)

### Variants

| `variant` | Looks | Use for |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `primary` *(default)* | Solid `primary`, `on-primary` text | The one main action in a view. |
| `secondary` | `primary` outline and text on `surface-raised`; `primary-subtle` tint on hover | Alternative actions beside a primary: on-brand, a step quieter. |
| `outline` | `surface-raised` with a `border` | Neutral actions, toolbars, "Cancel". |
| `ghost` | No fill until hover | Low-emphasis actions, icon buttons in dense UI. |
| `link` | `primary` text, underline on hover | Inline actions that read like a link. |

### Destructive

Add `destructive` to any variant to give it danger colors. Pick the variant by emphasis, exactly as for a normal action:

| `variant` + `destructive` | Looks | Use for |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `primary` | Solid `danger`, `on-danger` text | The confirming button in a delete dialog. |
| `secondary` | Solid `danger` outline, `danger-text`; `danger-subtle` tint on hover | A destructive action beside a primary one. |
| `outline` | Softer `danger-border`, `danger-text` | "Delete" in a toolbar or settings row. |
| `ghost` | `danger-text`, tint on hover | "Remove" on list rows and in dense UI. |
| `link` | `danger-text`, underline on hover | Inline "Remove" or "Revoke" links. |

Hover fills use `danger-hover`, `danger-subtle-hover` and `danger-subtle`; keyboard focus shows a `danger` ring.

### Sizes

| `size` | Height | Side padding | Text | Icon | Gap |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `sm` | 24px (`control-height-sm`) | 8px | `text-xs` (12px) | 14px | 4px |
| `md` *(default)* | 32px (`control-height-md`) | 12px | `text-sm` (14px) | 16px | 6px |
| `lg` | 44px (`control-height-lg`) | 20px | `text-base` (16px) | 20px | 8px |

All sizes use `font-medium` and `radius-control` (6px; a brand can change it). `primary`, `secondary` and `outline` buttons (and their destructive versions) carry `shadow-xs` (a 1px, 5% black shadow); `ghost` and `link` stay flat, and disabled buttons drop the shadow. A disabled button is drawn in muted colors (`surface-muted` with a `text-muted` label and a `border`; ghost and link keep no box), not faded: its label stays at least 3:1 in every theme, like a disabled field's, and 4.5:1 with more contrast, so a disabled button with a `disabledReason` can still be read. Use `lg` where touch matters: 44px is the minimum comfortable tap target. `sm` belongs in dense desktop UI like tables and toolbars. On a touch screen every size takes a press 44px across anyway, with nothing moving: an invisible box reaches past the button's edges. With other buttons in the same row it stops halfway into the gap (ButtonGroup and Toolbar tell it their gap; elsewhere it assumes 4px), so a press goes to the nearer button and never to a neighbor's face.

### Content

A button holds a label, an icon beside a label, or an icon alone:

| Content | Props | Looks |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Label only | `children` | Text |
| Start icon | `startIcon` + `children` | Icon, then text |
| End icon | `endIcon` + `children` | Text, then icon |
| Icon only | IconButton (`icon` + `label`) | A square: 24, 32 or 44px. Button has no `icon` of its own |

**Optical balance.** An icon reads lighter than text, so a button with one icon adds 4px of padding on the text side:

| `size` | Label only | Left icon (left / right) | Right icon (left / right) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `sm` | 8 / 8px | 8 / 12px | 12 / 8px |
| `md` | 12 / 12px | 12 / 16px | 16 / 12px |
| `lg` | 20 / 20px | 20 / 24px | 24 / 20px |

Button applies this automatically. With `buttonClass`, pass `iconPosition: 'start'` or `'end'`.

Pass any Material Symbols name (see the Icon guidelines) as a string (`startIcon="add"`), or an icon imported from `@diki-stwn/serupa-ds/icons` (`startIcon={Add}`), and Button renders it as an `Icon` in the Rounded, filled style at the right size. You can also pass an element. For an icon on its own, use IconButton: its `label` is required by the types.

### Links

A Button with `href` renders a link (`<a>`) with the button's look, because navigation belongs in a link: it opens in a new tab, shows its address and is listed among the page's links by screen readers.

- **Router links.** Register your router's link component once, at startup, and every Button with `href` uses it:

  ```jsx
  // Next.js
  import Link from 'next/link';
  Serupa.configure({ link: Link });

  // React Router: its Link takes `to`, so map href to it
  import { Link } from 'react-router-dom';
  Serupa.configure({ link: React.forwardRef(({ href, ...p }, ref) => <Link ref={ref} to={href} {...p} />) });
  ```

- **New tabs.** `target="_blank"` gets `rel="noopener noreferrer"` unless you pass `rel`.
- **Addresses from people.** Check any `href` that comes from people, such as a profile's website: allow only `https:`, `http:`, `mailto:` or your own paths. React still renders a `javascript:` link, which runs code when clicked.
- **Disabled.** Links have no disabled state in HTML, so a disabled link Button renders without `href`, with `role="link"` and `aria-disabled`: it can't be followed or focused and isn't listed as a link.
- **Loading** works as on a button: clicks do nothing until it ends.
- **Anything else** (a `<label>` for a file input, a `<summary>`): style it with `buttonClass({ variant, size, destructive })`.

### Forms and backend calls

The button is a plain `<button>`, so it works with any form library, router or data layer.

- **`type` defaults to `"button"`**, so a button inside a `<form>` never submits by accident. Pass `type="submit"` for the form's submit button; `name`, `value`, `form`, `formAction` and every other `<button>` attribute pass through.
- **Every native `<button>` attribute works**, checked in a browser: `autoFocus`, `disabled`, `form`, `formAction`, `formEncType`, `formMethod`, `formNoValidate`, `formTarget`, `name`, `value`, `type`, `popoverTarget` / `popoverTargetAction` (opens a `popover` element with no JavaScript) and `commandfor` / `command` (opens a `<dialog>` with `command="show-modal"`), plus global and event attributes. `name` and `value` are sent with the form when this button submits it, so one form can have Save and Publish buttons (`name="intent"`).
- **`loading` blocks repeat requests.** While it's true, clicks, Space and Enter on the button, and Enter in a form field (implicit submission) do nothing, so a slow request can't be sent twice. The click still bubbles, so a parent's handler hears it. The button keeps keyboard focus (unlike `disabled`, which would drop it mid-request) and sets `aria-busy` and `aria-disabled`.
- **`disabled`** is the native attribute: the button leaves the tab order and ignores clicks.
- **`disabledReason` says why.** With `disabled`, the button uses `aria-disabled` instead, so it stays in the tab order: keyboard and screen reader users can reach it and hear the reason as its description (`aria-describedby`), and it still looks disabled and ignores clicks, Enter and form submission. To show the reason on hover and focus as well, wrap it in a [Tooltip] (npx serupa-docs Tooltip) with the same words; the button then lets the tooltip describe it, so the reason is read once. A disabled link Button with a reason gets `tabIndex={0}`. Without `disabled`, `disabledReason` does nothing.
- **An `onClick` that returns a promise loads by itself.** The button shows `loading` until the promise settles, so a second click can't send the request twice, and you don't need your own loading state. A promise that settles within 300ms shows no spinner at all. Once the spinner shows, it stays at least 500ms, so one that ends just after 300ms doesn't flash it for a frame. With `successText` ("Saved"), a resolved promise shows a check (after the spinner, if one showed) in place of the label for 2 seconds (the button keeps its width and name) and announces the text politely. A rejected promise just ends the loading; show the error yourself. The rejection isn't swallowed: it still reaches `window`'s `unhandledrejection` (and Sentry or any other error reporting) once, as it would without Button.
- **A submit button in a form with an `action` loads by itself.** With `<form action={save}>` (React 19 form actions), a `type="submit"` Button shows `loading` while the form is being sent, from React's `useFormStatus`, so you don't need your own state. Set `loading` yourself to override it.
- **`ref`** reaches the DOM element (the `<button>`, or the `<a>` with `href`), for focusing after an error.

```jsx
function SaveForm() {
  const [saving, setSaving] = React.useState(false);
  async function onSubmit(e) {
    e.preventDefault();
    setSaving(true);
    try { await fetch('/api/projects', { method: 'POST', body: new FormData(e.currentTarget) }); }
    finally { setSaving(false); }
  }
  return (
    <form onSubmit={onSubmit}>
      <input name="title" />
      <Button type="submit" loading={saving} startIcon="save">Save changes</Button>
    </form>
  );
}
```

**Data attributes** for tests, analytics and styling: every button has `data-component="button"`, `data-variant` and `data-size`, plus `data-destructive`, `data-icon-only`, `data-loading`, `data-success` and `data-disabled` when they apply. Select with `[data-component="button"][data-loading]`, for example; don't select by the `srp-btn` class names.

### Micro-interactions

Small motion that confirms what happened, all built in:

| Interaction | What it does | Turn off or tune |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Press | While held (pointer, Space or Enter) the button takes its held fill, one step past hover: `primary-pressed`, `primary-subtle-pressed`, `secondary-hover` or `danger-pressed` and `danger-subtle-hover` when destructive. It never shrinks unless you ask: a shrink is hard to see under a finger and reads as a glitch on a small button | Fills: the `--button-…-bg-pressed` tokens. A shrink: `--button-press-scale: var(--scale-97)` |
| Icon nudge (off by default) | When turned on, a right icon slides in its direction on hover (on devices that hover), mirrored in right-to-left text. Left icons stay still. It suits forward arrows ("Continue →"), not chevrons or other icons, so it's off unless you turn it on | On: `--button-icon-nudge: var(--spacing-0\.5)` (2px) |
| Loading | The label and icons fade out while the spinner fades and grows in, in 150ms; both blur a little (`blur-xs`) as they cross, so it reads as one change; they fade back when done | `--button-loading-duration: 0ms` |

- They animate only `scale`, `translate`, `opacity` and the loading blur (`filter`), so nothing around the button reflows, and they never change its size, name or behavior: clicks, keys, forms and your own `onPointerDown`, `onKeyDown` and `onKeyUp` work as before.
- No press on disabled, loading or `link`-variant buttons (the link variant reads as text).
- Hover colors apply only on devices that hover (a mouse or trackpad). A phone keeps hover on the last button tapped, so on touch screens a tapped button goes straight back to its resting color, and the press is the feedback. This holds for every component's hover styles (`tools/test/touch-hover.mjs`).
- With reduced motion turned on (an operating-system setting), there's no shrink (if you turned one on) or nudge, and loading only fades (no blur). The held fill stays: it's a color, not motion.
- `buttonClass()` on another element gets the press, nudge and loading fade (they're all CSS).
- To turn the icon nudge on for a flow of "next" buttons:

  ```css
  .wizard-footer { --button-icon-nudge: var(--spacing-0\.5); }
  ```

- Set the tokens on the page, a container or one button, like any component token (see the Motion table below).

## States

| State | Looks | Cursor |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Default | Variant colors, `shadow-xs` on filled and outline buttons | `pointer` |
| Hover | `primary` darkens one step (`primary-hover`); secondary gains a `primary-subtle` tint and its text and border darken to `primary-hover`; outline and ghost gain a `secondary` fill; link underlines; a right icon slides 2px forward | `pointer` |
| Pressed | One step past hover: `primary-pressed`; secondary `primary-subtle-pressed`; outline and ghost `secondary-hover`; destructive `danger-pressed` (primary) or `danger-subtle-hover`. Full size | `pointer` |
| Focus (keyboard) | A 2px `focus-ring` outline 2px out (`danger` when destructive). The gap is transparent, so it reads on tinted backgrounds; forced-colors (high-contrast) mode draws it in the system color | `pointer` |
| Disabled | 50% opacity, no shadow, no hover change, ignores clicks | `not-allowed` |
| Loading | Full color, the content fades into a spinner, no hover change, no press, ignores clicks, keeps focus | `progress` |

**Loading details.** `loading` shows the [Loader] (npx serupa-docs Loader) (ring, decorative, at the button's icon size) while an action runs. The spinner sits in the center of every loading button (label only, with a left or right icon, or icon only), over the hidden content, so the button keeps its width and nothing around it shifts. The button sets `aria-busy` and `aria-disabled` so screen readers announce it as busy. Under reduced motion the ring's arc holds still and it turns slower.

## Accessibility

Button's behavior follows web standards; its look comes only from this design system's tokens.

| Behavior | Source |
| --- | --- |
| Renders a real `<button>` (Space and Enter press it, it's in the tab order, `disabled` works); `type` defaults to `"button"` because a `<button>` in a form otherwise submits it | [HTML Standard: the button element](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/form-elements.html#the-button-element), [MDN: `<button>`](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTML/Element/button) |
| Actions use `<button>`; navigation uses a real link (`href`), never an `onClick` that changes the URL | [WAI-ARIA APG: Button pattern](https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/button/), [MDN: button role](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/Accessibility/ARIA/Roles/button_role) |
| Loading blocks clicks and Enter-key implicit submission, but keeps focus (`aria-disabled`, not `disabled`), keeps the button's accessible name, and announces "Loading…" (`loadingLabel`) through a polite `role="status"` region | [HTML Standard: implicit submission](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/form-control-infrastructure.html#implicit-submission), [APG: focusability of disabled controls](https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/practices/keyboard-interface/#focusabilityofdisabledcontrols), [WCAG 4.1.3 Status Messages](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/status-messages.html) |
| A disabled link has no `href` (so it isn't a link, can't be focused or followed), with `role="link"` and `aria-disabled`; `target="_blank"` gets `rel="noopener noreferrer"` | [HTML Standard: the a element](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/text-level-semantics.html#the-a-element), [MDN: aria-disabled](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/Accessibility/ARIA/Attributes/aria-disabled), [MDN: rel=noopener](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTML/Attributes/rel/noopener) |
| Icon-only buttons need an `aria-label` (warns without one); icons are `aria-hidden` | [WCAG 4.1.2 Name, Role, Value](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/name-role-value.html), [WCAG 1.1.1 Non-text Content](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/non-text-content.html) |
| An `aria-label` on a button with visible text should start with that text ("Delete project", not "Remove") | [WCAG 2.5.3 Label in Name](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/label-in-name.html) |
| Visible keyboard focus, also in forced-colors (high-contrast) mode | [WCAG 2.4.7 Focus Visible](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/focus-visible.html), [WCAG 2.4.11 Focus Not Obscured](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/focus-not-obscured-minimum.html) |
| Every size is at least 24×24px; use `lg` (44px) on touch-first screens | [WCAG 2.5.8 Target Size (Minimum)](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/target-size-minimum.html), [WCAG 2.5.5 Target Size (Enhanced)](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/target-size-enhanced.html) |
| Under reduced motion the spinner turns slower with a steady arc, and press and nudge are off | [WCAG 2.3.3 Animation from Interactions](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/animation-from-interactions.html) |
| Toggle buttons pass `aria-pressed`; menu buttons pass `aria-haspopup`, `aria-expanded` and `aria-controls` | [APG: Button pattern (toggle)](https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/button/), [APG: Menu Button pattern](https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/menu-button/) |

### Keyboard

| Key | Does |
| --- | --- |
| Tab | To the button (also when it's loading or has a `disabledReason`; a plain `disabled` button is skipped) |
| Enter, Space | Press it; Enter shows the press as Space does. While loading, or disabled with a reason, nothing happens |
| Enter in a form field | Submits the form through a `type="submit"` button, unless that button is loading |

## Props

Button's own props are `variant` (`primary`), `destructive`, `surface` (`dark` or `light`: white or black over a photo, in every theme), `size` (`md`), `startIcon`, `endIcon`, `loading` (default: on while a `type="submit"` button's `<form action>` is being sent), `loadingLabel` (what screen readers hear when loading starts; default "Loading…", `""` for silence), `disabledReason` (why it's disabled: keeps it focusable and describes it), `successText` (shown with a check and announced after a promise from `onClick` resolves) and `wrap` (a long label takes more lines instead of an ellipsis; default `false`). With `href` it renders a link and takes link attributes (`target`, `rel`, `download`…); without, it's a `<button>` and takes button attributes (`type`, which defaults to `"button"`, `form`, `name`…). Everything else (`onClick`, `disabled`, `aria-label`…) passes straight through, and `id` goes to the `<button>` or `<a>` itself. That includes the native popover and invoker attributes, typed here because React's types don't list them yet: `popoverTarget` with `popoverTargetAction` (`show`, `hide` or `toggle`) works a `[popover]` element by id, and `commandfor` with `command` (such as `show-modal` for a `<dialog>`) sends it an invoker command.

`buttonClass({ variant, size, destructive, iconOnly, iconPosition, className })` returns the class names, to style any other element as a button. `Serupa.configure({ link })` sets the component that renders link Buttons.

## Component tokens

Button's colors, spacing, sizes, borders and micro-interactions go through its own tokens. Each is an optional override: set the CSS variable on the page, on a container or on one button, and every Button inside follows. Unset, it uses the shared token below, in the button's own theme, so themes (including nested ones) keep working. The list lives in `src/components/Button/button.tokens.json` (W3C Design Tokens format, also published in `design-tokens/components/`), and the tests check that the CSS uses exactly these defaults.


components.name: ButtonGroup
components.summary: Related buttons side by side, or stacked: joined into one control with shared borders (the default), or spaced apart.
components.guide:
# ButtonGroup

Related buttons side by side, or stacked: joined into one control with shared borders (the default), or spaced apart. Use it for two or three actions on the same thing (Copy, Paste), or a split button.

**Also called:** button bar, action group.

```jsx
import { ButtonGroup, Button, IconButton, ToggleButton } from '@diki-stwn/serupa-ds';

<ButtonGroup aria-label="Clipboard">
  <Button variant="outline" startIcon="content_copy">Copy</Button>
  <Button variant="outline" startIcon="content_paste">Paste</Button>
</ButtonGroup>

<ButtonGroup attached={false}>
  <Button variant="outline">Cancel</Button>
  <Button>Save</Button>
</ButtonGroup>

<ButtonGroup orientation="vertical" aria-label="Zoom">
  <IconButton variant="outline" icon="add" label="Zoom in" />
  <IconButton variant="outline" icon="remove" label="Zoom out" />
</ButtonGroup>
```

## When to use

- A few actions on the same thing, such as Copy and Paste, that read as one control.
- A pair of buttons that belong together but stay apart, such as Cancel and Save in a footer (`attached={false}`).

## When not to use

- One choice out of a few options: use [SegmentedControl] (npx serupa-docs SegmentedControl), which lets only one be on.
- [ToggleButton] (npx serupa-docs ToggleButton)s that share one value, such as alignment or text styles: use a [ToggleGroup] (npx serupa-docs ToggleGroup). Several groups of tools in a row, such as an editor's: put them in a [Toolbar] (npx serupa-docs Toolbar), which is one Tab stop with arrow keys between its buttons.
- Many actions, or ones people rarely use: put them in a [Menu] (npx serupa-docs Menu).

## Usage

Give the group a `size` and every button in it takes it (a button's own `size` still wins), so a large toolbar is one prop, not one per button. Variant stays on each button: give them all the same one. Two attached primary buttons get an edge between them in their text color (`--button-group-divider`), as a split button has.

An attached row that's wider than its container wraps as separate, spaced buttons (with `data-wrapped` on the group), so a narrow screen never scrolls sideways and no label is cut; it joins again once there's room. This holds in a CSS grid column or a flex row too. A vertical group doesn't wrap. The group is never wider than its container: a single label too long for a whole line (a long German compound at 320px) is cut with an ellipsis, with the whole label as the button's title, as a lone Button's is.

For a main action with a menu of variations, use [SplitButton] (npx serupa-docs SplitButton), which wires the menu and its names for you. A button can still be a Menu's trigger or sit in a Tooltip (`<Menu trigger={<IconButton … />}>` last): the outer corners go to the first and last buttons, whatever popup follows them.

### Do and don't

- **Do:** Give every button in an attached group the same variant. (`DoSameVariant`)
- **Don't:** Mix variants in one group: it breaks into pieces that don't look like one control. (`DontMixVariants`)

## Accessibility

- It's a `role="group"`: name it with `aria-label` when the buttons share a purpose ("Text formatting"), so screen readers announce it on the way in.
- A hovered, focused or pressed button comes to the front, so its border and focus ring are never hidden by its neighbor.
- Each button keeps its own colors and contrast; the group adds none.
- **Keyboard:** nothing of its own. Tab moves through its buttons one by one, as it would without the group.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | string | none | Goes to the root `<div>`. |
| `attached` | boolean | `true` | Joins them: shared borders, only the outer corners rounded |
| `orientation` | `'horizontal'` \| `'vertical'` | `'horizontal'` | A row or a column |
| `size` | `'sm'` \| `'md'` \| `'lg'` | none | The size of every Button, IconButton and ToggleButton in it that doesn't set its own (24, 32 or 44px) |
| `aria-label` | string | none | What the group is for |

`className`, `style`, `ref` and everything else go to the wrapper, which has `role="group"`, `data-component="button-group"` and `data-orientation`.

## Component tokens

Each is an optional override: set it on the page, a container or one group. The list lives in `src/components/ButtonGroup/button-group.tokens.json` (also in `design-tokens/components/`).

<!-- token-table:start (made from button-group.tokens.json by npm run tokens: edit the descriptions there) -->
| Token | Default | Use |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--button-group-gap` | `spacing-2` | Space between buttons when not attached (8px). |
| `--button-group-overlap` | `border-width-1` | How much attached buttons overlap, so their borders make one line (1px, the button border). |
| `--button-group-divider` | `opacity-40` | Strength of the edge between two attached primary buttons, in their text color (40%). Set `0%` for none. |
<!-- token-table:end -->

components.name: Calendar
components.summary: A month of days to pick one from, with full keyboard navigation.
components.guide:
# Calendar

A month of days to pick one from, with full keyboard navigation. DatePicker shows one in a popup; use Calendar on its own for an always-visible picker, such as in a booking page or a side panel.

**Also called:** date grid, month view.

```tsx
import { Calendar } from "@diki-stwn/serupa-ds";

const [day, setDay] = React.useState<Date | null>(null);
<Calendar value={day} onValueChange={setDay} min={new Date()} />
<Calendar defaultValue={new Date(2025, 2, 10)} isDateDisabled={(d) => d.getDay() === 0 || d.getDay() === 6} />
```

## When to use

- Picking a day is the main task on the page or panel, such as choosing a booking day.
- People should see which days are free or blocked before they choose.
- There's room to keep the month on screen while people look at other details beside it.

## When not to use

- A date field in a form: use [DatePicker] (npx serupa-docs DatePicker), which opens a Calendar only when needed.
- A start and an end date: use [DateRangePicker] (npx serupa-docs DateRangePicker); Calendar picks one day.
- A date people know by heart, such as a date of birth: use an [Input] (npx serupa-docs Input) with a format hint.

## Anatomy

Drawn from the `MonthYearPicker` story.

1. **Header** (`.srp-calendar__header`): the month shown and the ways to change it.
2. **Month and year** (`.srp-calendar__menus`): menus to jump to another month or year. Without them, the heading (`.srp-calendar__heading`) opens a grid of months (`.srp-calendar__periods`).
3. **Previous and next** (`.srp-calendar__nav`): move one month back or forward.
4. **Grid** (`.srp-calendar__grid`): the days of the month in weeks, with the weekday names above.
5. **Selected day** (`.srp-calendar__day--selected`): the chosen date.
6. **Day of another month** (`.srp-calendar__day--outside`): days before and after the month, to fill the weeks.

## Usage

- Put a heading or a line of text near it saying what the day is for ("Pick a delivery day"): the grid is named by its month title only.
- Block days with `min`, `max` and `isDateDisabled` so people see them before they pick, rather than refusing a day afterwards.
- Set `autoFocus` only when the Calendar appears because people asked for it, such as in a panel they just opened.
- Leave `locale` and `weekStartsOn` unset in most products so names and the first day follow the visitor's browser.
- Set `calendar` where people date things in another calendar: `"persian"` in Iran and Afghanistan, `"islamic-umalqura"` for Hijri dates in Saudi Arabia, `"buddhist"` in Thailand, `"japanese"` for era years. The grid then shows that calendar's months, with their own first and last days, and the title, the day names and the month and year grids follow it. Values stay `Date`s, and digits stay Latin. A locale's own calendar (`th`, `fa`, or a `-u-ca-` extension) isn't followed on its own: name it here.
- The weekday headers use the locale's short names, or its one-letter names where the short name is the full word or two words (Arabic, Persian, Hebrew, Vietnamese), so they fit their 32px columns. Screen readers always hear the full name.

## Behavior

- Always six weeks tall, so the layout doesn't jump between months. Days of the months before and after are muted and can be picked.
- Today is in primary with a dot under its number, in the same weight as the other days. The selected day is filled in primary. The weeks are 4px apart (`--calendar-row-gap`).
- In a range (RangeCalendar, DateRangePicker), the days between the ends are one square band per week, and each end is rounded only on its outer side, where it joins the band.
- With `presets`, a group of shortcut buttons named "Shortcuts" follows the days: beside them, or under them below 640px. The one the value matches is pressed (`aria-pressed`), and one whose day can't be picked is disabled.
- The heading ("March 2025") is a button: it opens the year's months, three by four, and their heading ("2025") opens twelve years. Pick a year for its months, and a month for its days: a date of birth in 1990 is four clicks from today. The previous and next buttons turn a year, or twelve years, there. Focus keeps its day of the month (the 17th in August to the 17th in the month picked). The months and years keep the days' size, so the calendar doesn't jump. Not in DateRangePicker's two months side by side, which turn together, nor with `monthYearPicker`.
- With `monthYearPicker`, the header shows a Month and a Year menu in place of the title, so people can jump years at once (a date of birth, an expiry). Years run from `min` to `max`, or from 100 years back to 10 ahead when unset; months outside `min` and `max` are disabled. Off by default.
- Today follows the clock: a calendar left open past midnight moves today to the new day without needing a re-render.
- Today is the visitor's day, not the server's. A server-rendered page marks it once it hydrates, since the server's date can differ (a UTC server and a visitor in Jakarta before 7am). Until then, the Tab stop is on the value or on the month's first day. With no value and no `defaultMonth`, the month shown at first is today's on each side. Around a month's turn that differs between the server and the visitor: the page hydrates on the month the server drew (the title carries it as `data-month`), and the visitor's month shows right after, with no mismatch; `onMonthChange` is called with it. A controlled `month` is left as it is.

### Do and don't

- **Do:** Put a heading or a line of text near it that says what the day is for ("Pick a delivery day"). (`DoSayWhatFor`)
- **Don't:** Show it on its own: the grid is named by its month only, so nobody knows what the day is for. (`DontUnexplained`)

## Accessibility

- A `role="grid"` table named by the month title, which is `aria-live` so screen readers hear the new month. The days have one Tab stop.
- The heading button is named by the month it shows and described by what it does ("Choose a month", in the month grid "Choose a year"). The month and year grids are `role="grid"` too, named by the hidden title, which says "2025" or "2016–2027" as the view changes. Months are shown short and read in full ("March 2025").
- Each day is named by its full date ("Monday, March 10, 2025"). The selected cell is `aria-selected`, today is `aria-current="date"`, and refused days are `aria-disabled` (in `disabled-text` and struck through).
- Weekday headers show the short name, and screen readers read the full one ("Monday", from visually hidden text, and in `abbr`), since "Mon" or "M" is read letter by letter or not at all by some.
- Text keeps 4.5:1 and the selected fill 3:1 in every theme (`Calendar.test.tsx`).
- In forced colors (Windows high contrast) the selected day is drawn in Highlight with HighlightText, exactly as set, so the browser's text backplate can't hide its number. The same goes for DatePicker's and DateRangePicker's pop-ups.

### Keyboard

| Key | Moves to |
| --- | --- |
| ← → | The day before or after (mirrored right to left). |
| ↑ ↓ | The same day a week before or after. |
| Home, End | The start or end of the week. |
| PageUp, PageDown | The same day a month before or after. With Shift, a year. |
| Enter, Space | Picks the focused day. |
| Escape | In the months or years: back a level (the years to the months, the months to the days, with focus on the heading). Inside DatePicker's popup it doesn't close the popup. |

In the months and years the same keys move by a month or a year: the arrows one, or a row of three up or down (mirrored right to left); Home and End to the row's ends; PageUp and PageDown a year, or twelve years; Enter or Space picks, a year opening its months and a month its days.

Moving past the shown month shows the next one. No key moves focus past `min` or `max`: a move that would, stops on that day.

A month arrow that reaches the month holding `min` or `max` turns disabled, so focus moves to the other arrow instead of falling back to the top of the page. DatePicker and DateRangePicker do the same.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | string | none | Goes to the root `<div>`. |
| `value` / `defaultValue` | `Date \| string \| null` | | The selected day, controlled or not: a Date (its time is ignored) or a plain `"yyyy-mm-dd"` string for that local day. |
| `onValueChange` | `(date: Date, details: { iso: string }) => void` | | Called with the picked day (local midnight) and details: `iso` is the same day as `"yyyy-mm-dd"`. |
| `month` / `defaultMonth` | `Date` | the selected day's month, or today's | The month shown: any day in it. |
| `onMonthChange` | `(month: Date) => void` | | Called with the first of the newly shown month. |
| `min`, `max` | `Date \| string` | | Days outside can't be picked, and the month buttons stop there. A Date or `"yyyy-mm-dd"`. |
| `presets` | `boolean \| DatePreset[]` | | Shortcuts in a list after the days: `true` for Today, Tomorrow and In a week, or your own `{ label, value }`. Picking one picks its day and shows its month. |
| `monthYearPicker` | `boolean` | `false` | Shows native Month and Year menus in the header instead of the title. The title stays for screen readers and still names the grid. |
| `isDateDisabled` | `(date: Date) => boolean` | | Days to refuse, such as weekends or holidays. |
| `headingLevel` | `2 \| 3 \| 4 \| 5 \| 6` | `2` | The month title's heading level, to fit the page's outline where the calendar sits inline (under an `h2`, say 3). |
| `locale` | `string` | the nearest `SerupaProvider`'s, else the browser's (en-US until a server-rendered page hydrates) | Month and weekday names, and the first day of the week. When it differs from the provider's, the month title and the grid carry `lang`, so screen readers read the names in that language; the nav buttons keep the page's. |
| `calendar` | `'gregory'` `'persian'` `'islamic-umalqura'` `'islamic-civil'` `'islamic-tbla'` `'indian'` `'buddhist'` `'japanese'` `'roc'` | `'gregory'` | The calendar system the months follow. Persian, Hijri and Indian have months of their own; Buddhist, Japanese and ROC share the Gregorian months and count years their way. Values stay `Date`s. |
| `weekStartsOn` | `0`–`6` | the locale's | 0 is Sunday. |
| `weekNumbers` | boolean | `false` | A narrow column of ISO 8601 week numbers before the days (the week holding each row's Thursday), for planning by week. Each number is its row's header, read as "Week 12" with the days; the days take its width off their share of a narrow screen. |
| `autoFocus` | `boolean` | `false` | Focus the selected day (or today) when it appears. |
| `previousLabel`, `nextLabel` | `string` | `"Previous month"`, `"Next month"` | The month buttons' names. |

`className`, `ref` and other props go to the outer `<div>`.

## Component tokens

Each is an optional override: set it on the page, a container or one calendar. The list lives in `src/components/Calendar/calendar.tokens.json` (also in `design-tokens/components/`).

<!-- token-table:start (made from calendar.tokens.json by npm run tokens: edit the descriptions there) -->
**Colors**

| Token | Default | Use |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--calendar-title-color` | `text` | The month and year. |

components.name: Card
components.summary: A surface that groups related content and its actions: a summary, a settings panel, an item in a grid.
components.guide:
# Card A surface that groups related content and its actions: a summary, a settings panel, an item in a grid. It's built from parts (`CardHeader`, `CardBody`, `CardFooter`) that you can mix with any content, and with `href` the whole card is clickable through one link on its title. **Also called:** tile. ```jsx import { Card, CardHeader, CardBody, CardFooter, Button, Badge } from '@diki-stwn/serupa-ds'; Active} /> Renews on 1 March. You're using 6 of 10 seats. // a whole card as a link: the title is the link, and its area covers the card; buttons inside still work // full-bleed media: no padding on the card, pad the parts yourself
``` ## When to use - A summary of one thing with its own actions: a plan, a project, a report. - A set of similar items in a grid, each opening its own page. - A panel that sets one group of settings or content apart from the rest of the page. ## When not to use - Rows of similar items people scan down: use [List] (npx serupa-docs List) instead, or [Table] (npx serupa-docs Table) when there are columns to compare. - Only separating two parts of a page: use space from [Stack] (npx serupa-docs Stack), or a [Divider] (npx serupa-docs Divider). - Content that sits over the page, such as a confirmation or a short form: use [Dialog] (npx serupa-docs Dialog) or [Popover] (npx serupa-docs Popover) instead. ## Anatomy Drawn from the `FooterLayouts` story. 1. **Header** (`.srp-card__header`): the title and description, with an optional action beside them. 2. **Title** (`.srp-card__title`): what the card is about. 3. **Description** (`.srp-card__description`): a line or two more about it. 4. **Body** (`.srp-card__body`): the card's content. 5. **Footer** (`.srp-card__footer`): actions or details at the end. ## Usage - Use `outline` for most cards, `elevated` for content over the page, and `filled` for a panel inside another surface. - Give a linked card a `CardHeader` with a `title`: the title is the link and names it ("Atlas"), so screen reader users don't hear the whole card read out as one link. - Buttons and other links can go inside a linked card. They sit above the card's link, so they work on their own and pressing them doesn't follow it. - Use `as="li"` for linked cards in a list. - For full-bleed media, set `padding="none"` and pad the parts yourself. ## States | State | Look | | --- | --- | | Rest | `surface` with a `border` border and `shadow-xs` (outline); `surface-raised` with `shadow-md` and a `border-raised` edge (elevated: the edge only shows in dark); `surface-muted` (filled), with a `border` edge in dark only, where that fill is the page's own | | Hover (a linked card) | A `border-strong` border | | Focus (a linked card) | From the keyboard: a 2px `focus-ring` outline, 2px outside the card | The hover border fades in 150ms (`duration-150`, `ease-move`), at once with `prefers-reduced-motion`. ### Do and don't - **Do:** Give a linked card a `CardHeader` with a `title`, so the title names the link ("Atlas"). (`DoTitleNamesLink`) - **Don't:** Leave a linked card without a title: screen readers read all of its text as the link's name. (`DontUntitledLink`) ## Accessibility - A card is a plain container: give it `as="section"` with a title when it's a landmark-worthy region, or `as="article"` for a self-contained item. - The title is a real heading, so screen reader users can jump between cards. Set `headingLevel` to fit the page. - A linked card has one link, around its `CardHeader` title (the "stretched link" pattern): it's named by the title, it's the card's first tab stop, and its clickable area covers the card. The card shows its focus ring. Without a direct `CardHeader` title, the link is empty, laid over the card and named by the card's text (or the card's `aria-label`). - The body text and the header's description sit above the link's area, so they can be selected and copied with the mouse. A plain click on them still follows the link. A click that ends a text selection doesn't. A Ctrl, Cmd or Shift click, or a middle click, on them opens the link in a new tab, as it would on the title. - The card itself stays a `
` (or `as`), so buttons and links inside are never nested in a link, which is invalid HTML. - In forced-colors mode every card gets a visible border. - The title, description and body text keep 4.5:1 on every variant, in every theme (`Card.test.tsx`). - In print, a card isn't split across two pages. - **Keyboard:** with `href`, the card is one Tab stop (its link), and Enter opens it. Buttons and links inside are Tab stops of their own. Without `href`, the card adds no Tab stop. ## Props ### Card | Prop | Type | Default | What it does | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `id` | string | none | Goes to the root element (`as`). | | `variant` | `'outline'` \| `'elevated'` \| `'filled'` | `'outline'` | A border and a hairline shadow; a raised shadow (for content over the page); or `surface-muted` and flat (a panel inside another surface; in dark it keeps a `border` edge, so it still shows on the page) | | `padding` | `'none'` \| `'sm'` \| `'md'` \| `'lg'` | `'md'` | 0, 12px, 20px or 24px inside, and the parts sit 16px apart | | `as` | `'div'` \| `'section'` \| `'article'` \| `'li'` | `'div'` | The element. Use `article` for a self-contained item, `li` inside a list | | `href` | string | | Makes the whole card clickable through one link around the `CardHeader` title (the link component set with `configure({ link })`, `` by default) | | `target`, `rel` | string | | Go to the link. `target="_blank"` adds `rel="noopener noreferrer"` | `className`, `style`, `ref` and everything else go to the card element (`aria-label` goes to the link of a linked card), which has `data-component="card"` and `data-variant`. ### CardHeader | Prop | Type | Default | What it does | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `title` | node | | The title, as a heading in `text-base`, `font-semibold` | | `description` | node | | A muted line under the title | | `action` | node | | Something at the end of the header, such as a Badge or a menu button. In a narrow card it drops under the title rather than squeezing it | | `headingLevel` | `2`–`6` | `3` | The title's heading level; pick the one that fits the page's outline | Children come after the description. ### CardBody and CardFooter `CardBody` holds the main content. `CardFooter` lays its children out in a wrapping row: `justify` is `'end'` (default), `'start'` or `'between'`. When the footer is narrower than 20rem (a card on a phone, or in a narrow column), each child takes the full row, one under the other, so each action gets a full-width tap target. ## Component tokens Each is an optional override: set it on the page, a container or one card. The list lives in `src/components/Card/card.tokens.json` (also in `design-tokens/components/`). **Colors** | Token | Default | Use | | --- | --- | --- | | `--card-row-bg-hover-elevated` | `surface-hover-raised` | A List or InlineEdit row on an elevated card, hovered or selected: a step up from the card in dark | | `--card-field-bg-elevated` | `field-raised` | The fill of a form field on an elevated card: a step up from the card in dark, so the field stands out from it | | `--card-bg` | `surface` | The background of an outline card | | `--card-bg-filled` | `surface-muted` | The background of a filled card | | `--card-border-filled` | `border` | A filled card's edge in dark, where its fill is the page's own; in light it has none. | | `--card-row-bg-hover` | `surface-hover` | A List or InlineEdit row on the card, hovered or selected | | `--card-row-bg-hover-filled` | `surface-raised` | A List or InlineEdit row on a filled card, hovered or selected: a step up, since surface-hover matches the filled card in light | | `--card-bg-elevated` | `surface-raised` | The background of an elevated card (one step up from the page in dark). | | `--card-border-elevated` | `border` | An elevated card's edge: the same `border` as an outline card's; the raised fill and shadow carry the lift | | `--card-border` | `border` | The border of an outline card | | `--card-title-color` | `text` | The title | | `--card-description-color` | `text-muted` | The description | | `--card-text` | `text` | Text in the body and footer | | `--card-border-hover` | `border-strong` | A linked card's border on hover | | `--card-wash-pressed` | `text` | The color washed over a card with `href` while it's held down, at layer-pressed strength: darker in light themes, lighter in dark. | | `--card-text-muted-pressed` | `text-muted-shaded` | Muted text on a card with `href` while it's held down (4.5:1 on the washed fill). | | `--card-focus-ring` | `focus-ring` | A linked card's keyboard focus ring | | `--card-divider-elevated` | `border-elevated` | What a divider or separator inside an elevated card reads as `border`: `border-elevated`, the line for the raised surface, since in dark `border` is that surface's own color and a line in it vanished | **Shadow** | Token | Default | Use | | --- | --- | --- | | `--card-shadow` | `elevation-rest` | An outline card's shadow | | `--card-shadow-elevated` | `elevation-raised` | An elevated card's shadow | **Border** | Token | Default | Use | | --- | --- | --- | | `--card-radius` | `radius-container` | The corners | | `--card-border-width` | `border-width-1` | The border | **Spacing** | Token | Default | Use | | --- | --- | --- | | `--card-padding-sm` | `spacing-3` | Padding, `sm` | | `--card-padding-md` | `space-card` | Padding, `md`: 20px, 12px in the compact density. | | `--card-padding-lg` | `space-surface` | Padding, `lg` | | `--card-gap` | `spacing-4` | The space between the parts | | `--card-header-gap` | `spacing-1` | The space between the title and the description | **Type** | Token | Default | Use | | --- | --- | --- | | `--card-title-weight` | `font-semibold` | The title's weight | **Motion** | Token | Default | Use | | --- | --- | --- | | `--card-press-scale` | `scale-100` | Size of a card with `href` while it's held down. 100%: off by default, since a press shows as the held wash (layer-pressed). Set it, e.g. to `var(--scale-97)`, to add a shrink. | | `--card-layer-pressed` | `opacity-10` | How strong the wash of the text color is on a card with `href` while it's held down (10%). | ## Related - [Grid] (npx serupa-docs Grid): lays out a set of cards in columns that fit the screen.

components.name: Carousel
components.summary: One slide at a time, with previous and next buttons, a dot per slide and swipe.
components.guide:
# Carousel

One slide at a time, with previous and next buttons, a dot per slide and swipe. Use it for a few related pictures or cards, such as product photos. It never moves on its own.

**Also called:** content slider, slideshow.

```tsx
import { Carousel, Image } from "@diki-stwn/serupa-ds";

<Carousel aria-label="Product photos">
  {photos.map((p) => <Image key={p.id} src={p.url} alt={p.alt} ratio="4:3" rounded={false} />)}
</Carousel>

<Carousel aria-label="Featured" index={i} onIndexChange={setI} loop dots={false}>
  <Card>…</Card>
  <Card>…</Card>
</Carousel>
```

## When to use

- A few related pictures or cards of equal weight, such as product photos or the screens of a feature tour, where showing one at a time saves room.
- Content people browse at their own pace and don't need to compare side by side.

## When not to use

- Content people must see, such as key messages, offers or anything that needs action: most people never get past the first slide. Show it on the page, in a [Card] (npx serupa-docs Card) or an [Alert] (npx serupa-docs Alert).
- Items people compare or scan: use a [Grid] (npx serupa-docs Grid) of Cards, or a [List] (npx serupa-docs List).
- Steps in a process: use [Stepper] (npx serupa-docs Stepper) or [Tabs] (npx serupa-docs Tabs), which show where people are and let them jump.
- A single picture: use [Image] (npx serupa-docs Image), with `viewable` to open it full size.

## Anatomy

Drawn from the `Controlled` story.

1. **Viewport** (`.srp-carousel__viewport`): the window the slides scroll through.
2. **Slide** (`.srp-carousel__slide`): one item; the ones out of view are hidden from screen readers.
3. **Previous and next** (`.srp-carousel__arrow`): move one slide (or one page of slides) at a time.
4. **Dots** (`.srp-carousel__dots`): one per slide: where you are, and a way to jump to any slide.

## Usage

- Keep it to a handful of slides (about 3 to 7). With more, people lose track and the dots get small to hit.
- Give every slide the same size and ratio (Image's `ratio` helps), so the controls don't jump.
- Put what matters most on the first slide; that's the one everyone sees.
- Write a `label` that says what the slides are ("Product photos"). Pass `slideLabel` when "2 of 5" isn't the best name, such as each photo's subject. The default comes from the `slideOf` label, so `SerupaProvider labels` translates it ("2 dari 5" with `idLabels`).
- Use `loop` for photos with no natural order, and leave it off when the slides have a start and an end.
- For a row of product cards or testimonials, show two or three at once with `perView`. Set it per screen width, such as `perView={{ base: 1, md: 2, lg: 3 }}`, so phones still get one at a time.
- On a phone, `peek` shows the edge of the next slide, which tells people they can swipe without them having to find the dots.
- Turn off `dots` for 2 slides or when the arrows are enough, and `arrows` only when swiping or your own controls (`index` and `onIndexChange`) replace them.
- The previous and next buttons sit over the slide's sides, 8px in and 32px wide. A picture can run under them, but give a slide with text at least 40px of inline padding while the arrows are on (`padding-inline: var(--spacing-10)`), or the buttons cover the ends of its lines on a phone. With `--carousel-arrow-offset` changed, that's the offset plus 32px.

## Behavior

- The previous and next buttons move one slide. A click on a dot goes to that slide. On the dots, the arrow keys move to the previous or next slide, and Home and End go to the first and last.
- The slides sit in the browser's own scroll container, which snaps to each slide. A touch swipe, a sideways two-finger swipe on a trackpad and Shift with the mouse wheel scroll it with the platform's momentum, and move one slide per gesture however hard the flick (`scroll-snap-stop`); the index and the dots follow where it settles. At an end it doesn't scroll the page sideways or go back a page. Up and down swipes still scroll the page. A mouse drag of 40px or more (or a flick) moves one slide too, and a shorter one, or one let go of while pulling back, springs back. Swiping works over pictures, and a drag that starts on a link doesn't follow it.
- Without `loop`, the button for the way you can't go hides; if it had focus, focus moves to the other button. With `loop`, next on the last slide scrolls back to the first, and previous on the first to the last; a swipe stops at the ends, as a scroll does.
- The buttons and dots scroll smoothly to the slide, and change it at once with reduced motion. With one slide there are no buttons or dots.
- With `perView`, the slides share the width, 16px apart (`--carousel-slide-gap`). `index` is the first slide shown, the buttons and a swipe still move one slide, and they stop once the last slide is in view. The dots count pages: with 3 per view and 7 slides, three dots for slides 1–3, 4–6 and 5–7, named "1–3 of 7" (the `slidesOf` label). `{ base, sm, md, lg }` follows the screen width (from 640, 768 and 1024px up) as it changes. With as many slides as fit, or fewer, there are no buttons or dots.
- In RTL (a `dir` attribute or CSS `direction`) the row runs right to left, and the buttons and arrow keys follow it.

### Do and don't

- **Do:** Give every slide the same size and ratio (Image's `ratio` helps), so the controls don't jump. (`DoSameRatio`)
- **Don't:** Mix ratios: the height changes and the arrows and dots jump as people move through. (`DontMixedRatios`)

## Accessibility

- **Role and name:** the `<section>` is a region named by `label`, with `aria-roledescription` "carousel" (the `carouselRole` label, "korsel" in Indonesian). Each slide is a group named "2 of 5" (`aria-roledescription` from `slideRole`). The slides not shown are `inert` and hidden, so Tab and screen readers only reach the current one (the ones in view, with `perView`). In server HTML, before JavaScript runs, none is: every slide can be scrolled to, read and used. The slides' scroll area is a keyboard stop of its own, a group named by the slides in view ("2 of 5"): focused, the arrow keys scroll it a slide at a time, and the index follows.
- **Keyboard:**

  | Key | Does |
  | --- | --- |
  | Tab | Reaches the current slide's content, the previous and next buttons, then the current dot. |
  | Enter, Space | Press a button or a dot. |
  | ←, → (on the dots) | The previous or next slide, following the reading direction. |
  | Home, End (on the dots) | The first or last slide. |

- **ARIA states:** the current dot has `aria-current="true"` and is the only one in the Tab order. The slides are in a polite live region, so a screen reader reads the new slide after a button press.
- **Motion:** it never moves on its own, so nothing needs pausing (WCAG 2.2.2), and slides change at once with reduced motion.
- **Contrast:** the dots and the buttons keep 3:1 in every theme (`Carousel.test.tsx`).
- **What's still yours:** a `label`, and alt text on every picture in the slides.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | string | none | Goes to the root `<section>`. |
| `children` | `ReactNode` | | One slide per child. |
| `aria-label` | `string` | | What the carousel shows; it names the region. Required unless you give `aria-labelledby` pointing at a visible heading. |
| `index` | `number` | | The slide shown (from 0), when you control it. |
| `defaultIndex` | `number` | `0` | The first slide shown when you don't. |
| `onIndexChange` | `(index) => void` | | Called with the new slide's index. |
| `loop` | `boolean` | `false` | Past the last slide comes the first. Without it, the buttons hide at the ends. |
| `arrows` | `boolean` | `true` | The previous and next buttons on the sides. |
| `dots` | `boolean` | `true` | A dot for each slide, under the carousel. |
| `previousLabel` | `string` | `"Previous slide"` | The previous button's name. |
| `nextLabel` | `string` | `"Next slide"` | The next button's name. |
| `slideLabel` | `(index, count) => string` | the `slideOf` label, `"2 of 5"` | Each slide's name, and its dot's. |
| `perView` | `number \| { base?, sm?, md?, lg? }` | `1` | How many slides show side by side, or one count per screen width (640, 768, 1024px up). |
| `peek` | `boolean` | `false` | Shows 48px of the next slide at the end (`--carousel-peek`), so people see there's more; on the last slide the previous one shows at the start. The slide that peeks stays out of the tab order. |

`ref`, `className`, `style` and other props go to the outer `<section>`.

## Component tokens

Each is an optional override: set it on the page, a container or one carousel. The list lives in `src/components/Carousel/carousel.tokens.json` (also in `design-tokens/components/`).

<!-- token-table:start (made from carousel.tokens.json by npm run tokens: edit the descriptions there) -->
| Token | Default | Use |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--carousel-dot` | `border-control` | The dots for the slides not shown (3:1 on surface). |
| `--carousel-dot-hover` | `border-control-hover` | A dot under the pointer, a step past dot, as a field's border darkens (text-muted is dot's own gray). |
| `--carousel-dot-pressed` | `text` | A dot while it's held down, a step past hover. |
| `--carousel-dot-active` | `primary` | The current slide's dot. |
| `--carousel-focus-ring` | `focus-ring` | A dot's keyboard focus ring. |
| `--carousel-dot-edge-active` | `primary-edge` | The current dot's 1px edge inside its fill (Yellow Light; transparent where the fill is 3:1 on the page) |
| `--carousel-radius` | `radius-container` | The slides' corners (12px). |
| `--carousel-dot-size` | `spacing-2` | A dot's size (8px). |
| `--carousel-dot-width-active` | `spacing-6` | The current dot's width (24px). |
| `--carousel-gap` | `spacing-3` | Space between the slides and the dots (12px). |
| `--carousel-slide-gap` | `spacing-4` | Space between slides shown side by side, with `perView` (16px). |
| `--carousel-peek` | `spacing-12` | How much of the next slide shows at the end with peek (48px). |
| `--carousel-arrow-offset` | `spacing-2` | The previous and next buttons' distance from the sides (8px). |
| `--carousel-arrow-shadow` | `elevation-part` | The previous and next buttons' shadow, so they stand out on any slide. |
<!-- token-table:end -->

components.name: CascadeSelect
components.summary: One choice made through a hierarchy, such as Provinsi › Kabupaten/Kota › Kecamatan or Category › Subcategory › Item.
components.guide:
# CascadeSelect

One choice made through a hierarchy, such as Provinsi › Kabupaten/Kota › Kecamatan or Category › Subcategory › Item. It looks like a [Select] (npx serupa-docs Select); it opens a panel of side-by-side columns, one per level, where picking in one shows its children in the next. The button shows the whole path, and a form gets the last value. Children can be loaded as an option is opened. On a phone it shows one column at a time, with a Back button.

**Also called:** cascader, cascading dropdown, nested select.

```jsx
import { CascadeSelect, Field } from '@diki-stwn/serupa-ds';

const regions = [
  { value: "jabar", label: "Jawa Barat", children: [
    { value: "bandung", label: "Kota Bandung", children: [{ value: "coblong", label: "Coblong" }, { value: "sukajadi", label: "Sukajadi" }] },
  ] },
  { value: "bali", label: "Bali", children: [/* … */] },
];

<Field label="Alamat">
  <CascadeSelect name="kecamatan" options={regions} levels={["Provinsi", "Kabupaten/Kota", "Kecamatan"]}
    value={path} onValueChange={(path, { options }) => setPath(path)} />
</Field>

// children loaded when an option is opened
<CascadeSelect aria-label="Kategori" options={topLevel} loadOptions={(path) => fetchChildren(path.at(-1)?.value)} />
```

## When to use

- One choice that only makes sense inside another: an area within a region, a subcategory within a category.
- A tree of options too big to show in one list, where people know the way down (they know their province before their district).

## When not to use

- A flat list: [Select] (npx serupa-docs Select), or a [Combobox] (npx serupa-docs Combobox) when people search it.
- People know the last step's name but not the path: a [Combobox] (npx serupa-docs Combobox) that searches every last step, showing the path as its description, is quicker.
- Choosing several items in a tree, or a tree people browse and edit: use a [TreeView] (npx serupa-docs TreeView).
- Two levels with a few options each: two Selects, the second filtered by the first, are simpler.

## Anatomy

Drawn from the `Open` story.

1. **Button** (`.srp-cascade-select__button`): the chosen path, joined with ›, or the placeholder; a chevron at the end.
2. **Panel** (`.srp-cascade-select__panel`): a dialog holding one column per level.
3. **Column** (`.srp-cascade-select__column`): its level's name (`levels`, or "Level 2") over a listbox of options, scrolling on its own past 288px.
4. **Option** (`.srp-cascade-select__option`): the highlighted one in each column is `primary-subtle`; one with children ends in a chevron, the chosen last step in a check.

## Usage

- Name each level with `levels`: it labels the columns, and people learn the order.
- Keep each column short enough to scan; sort options the way people look for them (alphabetically for places).
- `onValueChange` gets the path of values and the options themselves, so you have the labels without looking them up.
- Only a last step can be chosen unless `selectParents` is set; then Enter, or a second click, on a parent chooses it.
- With `loadOptions`, an option without `children` loads them when opened ("Loading…" meanwhile); a failure says so and how to try again: open that option again. Set `isLeaf` on options that have nothing under them, so they don't show a chevron or ask.
- A `value` or `defaultValue` with loaded levels (a saved one in an edit form) has its levels loaded right away, one at a time, so the button reads it in words without being opened. Until they arrive, or if a load fails, it shows the values themselves.

## States

| State | Look |
| --- | --- |
| Rest | `field` background, 1px `field-border`, the chevron in `text-muted` |
| Placeholder | "Choose…" (or `placeholder`) in the `placeholder` color |
| Hover | `field-border-hover` |
| Focus | Like the other fields: the border and a 1px ring hugging it take the `focus-ring` color (danger when invalid), and stay while the panel is open; inside the panel, an outline on the focused option or column |
| Open | The panel under the button (above it when there's no room), fading in |
| Invalid | `danger` border, and `aria-invalid` |
| Disabled | `field-readonly` background, `disabled-border` edge and `disabled-text` at full opacity, `not-allowed` cursor; it doesn't open |
| Loading | "Loading…" in the next column |

### Do and don't

- **Do:** Name each column with `levels`: it labels the columns, and people learn the order. (`Open`)
- **Don't:** Give every column the same name ("Pilih"): people have to guess what each one holds. (`DontGenericLevels`)

## Accessibility

- **Role and name:** the button is a `combobox` with `aria-haspopup="dialog"` and `aria-expanded`, named by a Field, a `<label>` or `aria-label`; the panel is a `dialog` named the same way. Each column is a `listbox` named by its level, and the highlighted option in each is `aria-selected`. An option with children is described as "More options: press Right arrow" (Left in right-to-left text).
- **Long paths:** a chosen path or placeholder that doesn't fit ends in an ellipsis and shows whole on hover and on the button's keyboard focus ([TruncatedText] (npx serupa-docs TruncatedText)); the button reads all of it.
- **Keyboard:** see the table. Focus moves into the panel when it opens, onto the chosen option, and back to the button when it closes.
- **Contrast:** text and placeholder keep 4.5:1 on `field`, the chevron 3:1; option text and level names 4.5:1 on the panel and the highlight; the check 3:1, in every theme (`CascadeSelect.test.tsx`). The resting border is soft on purpose (`field-border`: about 1.5:1 in light, 1.4:1 to 1.9:1 in dark), under the 3:1 WCAG 1.4.11 asks of a control's edge: a deliberate design exception. The label above the field, its fill in dark, the stronger border on hover and the 3:1 focus ring mark it, and more contrast (`data-contrast="more"` or the system setting) brings back a 3:1+ border.
- **What's still yours:** a name for it (Field, `<label>` or `aria-label`), `levels` that say what each column is, and the error text when a required choice is missing.

### Keyboard

| Key | Does |
| --- | --- |
| Enter, Space, ↓, ↑ (on the button) | Opens the panel |
| ↓ ↑ | The next or previous option in the column, skipping disabled ones |
| Home, End | The first or last option |
| → (← right to left) | Into the highlighted option's children |
| ← (→ right to left) | Back to the column before |
| Enter, Space | Chooses a last step and closes; on an option with children, goes into them (with `selectParents`, chooses it) |
| A letter | The next option that starts with it |
| Escape | Closes without a change |

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `options` | `CascadeOption[]` | | `{ value, label, children?, isLeaf?, disabled? }`: the first column, with the levels under it |
| `value` | `string[]` | | The chosen path, as values from the first column down (controlled) |
| `defaultValue` | `string[]` | `[]` | The path it starts with (uncontrolled) |
| `onValueChange` | `(value, { options }) => void` | | Called when a choice is made, with the path and its options |
| `loadOptions` | `(path: CascadeOption[]) => Promise<CascadeOption[]>` | | Loads the children of the path's last option when it has none |
| `levels` | `string[]` | "Level 1", "Level 2"… | Each column's name |
| `selectParents` | boolean | `false` | Lets an option with children be chosen too |
| `placeholder` | string | "Choose…" | Shown with nothing chosen |
| `size` | `'sm'` \| `'md'` \| `'lg'` | `'md'` | 24, 32 or 44px, like Select |
| `invalid` | boolean | `false` | A danger border and `aria-invalid`; set for you in a Field with an error |
| `required` | boolean | `false` | A path must be chosen: `aria-required` on the button, and the form isn't sent without one (the button is marked invalid and takes focus). A required Field sets only `aria-required`, as it does on an Input |
| `name` | string | | A form gets the path's last value under it, and a form reset brings back `defaultValue` |
| `open`, `defaultOpen`, `onOpenChange` | | | The panel's open state, controlled or not; `onOpenChange(open, { reason })` says why: `'trigger'`, `'select'`, `'escape'`, `'outside'` or `'reset'` |
| `disabled` | boolean | `false` | It can't open, and the form doesn't get its value |
| `readOnly` | boolean | `false` | Shows the path but can't open: focusable and read out (`aria-readonly`), and the form still gets its value, unlike `disabled` |

`ref`, `id`, `aria-*` and other props go to the `<button>`; `className` and `style` go to the wrapper (`data-component="cascade-select"`, `data-state`), full width by default.

## Component tokens

Each is an optional override: set it on the page, a container or one CascadeSelect. The list lives in `src/components/CascadeSelect/cascade-select.tokens.json` (also in `design-tokens/components/`).
