components.name: Center
components.summary: Keeps content to a maximum width in the middle of the space it's in, and with `vertical`, in the middle of the screen's height too.
components.guide:
# Center

Keeps content to a maximum width in the middle of the space it's in, and with `vertical`, in the middle of the screen's height too. Use it for a page with one short task, such as signing in, and for an error or empty page.

**Also called:** centered layout, auth layout.

```tsx
import { Center, Card } from "@diki-stwn/serupa-ds";

<Center as="main" vertical maxWidth="container-sm">
  <Card>…the sign-in form…</Card>
</Center>

<Center intrinsic centerText>…a heading, a line and a button…</Center>
```

## When to use

- A page with one short task: sign in, sign up, reset a password, accept an invite. With `vertical`, the form sits in the middle of the screen.
- An error page, an empty screen, or a short confirmation, with `intrinsic` and `centerText`.
- A narrow column inside something wider, such as a form in a wide Card.

## When not to use

- A page's whole content, header and footer, lined up on the same edges: use [Container] (npx serupa-docs Container) instead.
- A column of items with space between them: use [Stack] (npx serupa-docs Stack), inside the Center when you need both.
- A band of a long page with its own background: use [PageSection] (npx serupa-docs PageSection) instead.

## Usage

- Pick `maxWidth` from the sizing tokens: `container-sm` (384px) for a sign-in form, `container-md` (448px, the default) for a longer form, `container-2xl` (672px) for a short article.
- `vertical` makes it at least the screen's height. Use it once, around a page's content, not inside a scrolling page.
- Center only short text with `centerText`: a heading, one line, a button's row. Keep paragraphs aligned to the start.
- The side padding (16px) is outside the maximum width, so a 384px form stays 384px on a laptop and keeps off the edges on a phone. Set `padded={false}` inside something that already has padding.

### Do and don't

- **Do:** Center one short task, such as signing in, with a maximum width that suits a form. (`DoSingleTask`)
- **Don't:** Center paragraphs: each line starts at a different place, so it's harder to read. (`DontCenterLongText`)

## Accessibility

- **Role and name:** none of its own: a layout box. Use `as="main"` when it holds the page's main content, so people can jump to it.
- **Keyboard:** none: a layout box, not focusable. The reading and Tab order stay the order of its children.
- **Reflow:** the content takes the full width less the padding on a narrow screen, so nothing scrolls sideways at 320px (WCAG 1.4.10). With `vertical`, content taller than the screen grows the box and the page scrolls, so nothing is cut off at 400% zoom.
- **What's still yours:** the page's h1, its landmarks and its skip link (the Build a page guide).

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | string | none | Goes to the root element (`as`). |
| `maxWidth` | string | `'container-md'` (448px) | The widest the content gets: a sizing token name or a CSS length |
| `vertical` | boolean | `false` | Also centers it from top to bottom, in a box at least as tall as the screen |
| `intrinsic` | boolean | `false` | Each child at its own width, centered, instead of stretched across |
| `centerText` | boolean | `false` | Centers the lines of text too |
| `padded` | boolean | `true` | 16px of side padding outside the maximum width; with `vertical`, 32px above and below too |
| `as` | `'div'` \| `'main'` \| `'section'` \| `'article'` | `'div'` | The element |

A value that isn't on the list falls back to the default. `className`, `style`, `ref` and everything else go to the element, which has `data-component="center"`.

## Component tokens

Each is an optional override: set it on the page, a container or one Center. The list lives in `src/components/Center/center.tokens.json` (also in `design-tokens/components/`).

<!-- token-table:start (made from center.tokens.json by npm run tokens: edit the descriptions there) -->
| Token | Default | Use |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--center-max-width` | `container-md` | The widest the content gets when maxWidth isn't given (448px). |
| `--center-padding-x` | `spacing-4` | Side padding, outside the maximum width (16px). |
| `--center-padding-y` | `spacing-8` | Space above and below with vertical (32px). |
<!-- token-table:end -->

components.name: Chart
components.summary: A line, bar or area chart of a few series over the same categories, such as visitors per month or orders per region, a donut of one series' shares, such as traffic by source, or a heatmap of a grid of values, such as orders by weekday and hour.
components.guide:
# Chart

A line, bar or area chart of a few series over the same categories, such as visitors per month or orders per region, a donut of one series' shares, such as traffic by source, or a heatmap of a grid of values, such as orders by weekday and hour. It draws itself as SVG at its box's width, tells a screen reader what it shows, lets the keyboard reach every point, and shows the same numbers as a table at the press of a button.

**Also called:** graph, data visualization.

```tsx
import { Chart } from "@diki-stwn/serupa-ds";

<Chart
  title="Visitors and sign-ups"
  categories={["Jan", "Feb", "Mar", "Apr"]}
  series={[
    { name: "Visitors", values: [120, 132, 101, 134] },
    { name: "Sign-ups", values: [20, 42, 31, 54] },
  ]}
/>
```

## When to use

- A trend over time (`type="line"`, the default) or a comparison of amounts across a few categories (`type="bar"`).
- Amounts over time that add up to a total, such as orders by channel (`type="area"` with `stacked`), or one amount whose size over time matters (`type="area"`).
- The shares of one whole across a few categories, such as traffic by source (`type="donut"`). Keep it to a handful: past seven, the rest go into one "Other" slice.
- A pattern across two dimensions, such as orders by weekday and hour (`type="heatmap"`), or change from a baseline across regions and months (`type="heatmap"` with `scale="diverging"`).
- Up to eight series that share the same categories, where the shape of the numbers matters more than each one.

## When not to use

- One number against a known range, such as storage used: use [Meter] (npx serupa-docs Meter). A task's progress: [Progress] (npx serupa-docs Progress).
- When people need the exact numbers to act on, or more than a handful of series: use a [Table] (npx serupa-docs Table).
- Shares that are close to each other, or that people compare closely: bars show the difference better than slices.
- Maps, scatter plots or live streaming data: Chart draws lines, bars, areas, donuts and heatmaps only, for now.
- A heatmap where people need to compare two cells closely: shades show a pattern, not a difference of 5%. Use bars or the table.

## Anatomy

Drawn from the `Line` story.

1. **Title** (`.srp-chart__title`): what the chart shows, and its name.
2. **Table button** (`.srp-chart__toggle`): shows the same numbers as a table, and back.
3. **Plot** (`.srp-chart__plot`): the SVG, with grid lines and value labels (`.srp-chart__gridline`, `.srp-chart__label`) and the category axis (`.srp-chart__baseline`).
4. **Series** (`.srp-chart__series`): a line (`.srp-chart__line`) with a marker per point (`.srp-chart__marker`), or a bar per value (`.srp-chart__bar`). An area chart adds a filled shape under each line (`.srp-chart__area`). A donut has a slice per category (`.srp-chart__slice`) round the total (`.srp-chart__total`) in place of the grid, the axis and the series. A heatmap has a cell per value (`.srp-chart__cell`), a row per series named on its start side.
5. **Legend** (`.srp-chart__legend`): each series' marker or pattern and its name; in a donut, each slice's pattern, name and share (`.srp-chart__key-value`); in a heatmap, the scale: its lowest value, each step's shade from low to high, and its highest.

While the pointer is over a category or a point has focus, a tooltip beside it lists that category's values.

## Usage

- Give it a `title`, which shows above it and names it. Without one, give it an `aria-label`.
- Keep series to a few, and give each a short name: it's in the legend, the tooltip, the table and each point's name.
- Pass `null` for a value you don't have. The line breaks there and the bar is left out, rather than showing a zero that isn't true.
- Pass `formatValue` for money, percentages or units, so the axis, the tooltip, the table and what's read out all say "$1.2M" the same way.
- `stacked` stands each area on the one before it, so the top line is the total. A point still says its own value.
- A donut draws the first series only, and only its values above zero. Each slice is named with its value and its share ("Search: 4,200 (42%)").
- A heatmap shades each value in one of five steps of the sequential ramp (chart-seq-1 to 5), equal parts of the way from its lowest value to its highest. With `scale="diverging"` it uses seven steps of the diverging ramp (chart-div-1 to 7): the middle one is neutral around `midpoint` (0 by default), red below it and blue above, as far each way as the value furthest from it. Each row is a series, so it takes up to 64, and its height is 32px a row unless you set `height`. A missing value is an empty cell with a dashed edge.
- Bars and areas always start at zero. A line starts at zero too, unless its values sit so far from it that zero would flatten them.
- Put it in a [Card] (npx serupa-docs Card) for a dashboard tile. It takes its box's width and the `height` you give it (240px by default).

### Loading, empty and failed

- **Loading:** set `loading` and pass no categories yet. The plot is a placeholder block at its `height`, the table button is there but disabled, and the legend keeps its line, so nothing below the chart moves when the numbers arrive. Name the wait in `loadingLabel` ("Loading visitors"): a screen reader hears it once, after the loader's delay, so a quick load says nothing. When you refresh numbers already shown, keep them in and set `loading`: the chart stays as it is until the new ones arrive.
- **Empty:** in place of the Chart, an [EmptyState] (npx serupa-docs EmptyState) that says why there's nothing yet. A chart of zeros reads as a real result.
- **Failed:** in place of the Chart, a danger [Alert] (npx serupa-docs Alert) that says what didn't load and offers Retry in `actions`. It's `role="alert"`, so the failure is heard as it appears. On Retry, go back to loading.

```tsx
{state === 'failed' ? <Alert tone="danger" actions={<Button size="sm" onClick={load}>Retry</Button>}>Visitors didn't load.</Alert>
  : state === 'loaded' && !months.length ? <EmptyState size="sm" title="No visitors yet" />
  : <Chart title="Visitors" loading={state === 'loading'} loadingLabel="Loading visitors"
      categories={months} series={[{ name: "Visitors", values: visits }]} />}
```

### Do and don't

- **Do:** Pass `formatValue` for money, percentages or units, so the axis, tooltip, table and what's read out all say "$1.8M". (`DoFormatMoney`)
- **Don't:** Leave money as bare numbers: people count digits to tell a million from a hundred thousand. (`DontRawNumbers`)

## Accessibility

- **Role and name:** a `<figure>` named by its title (`figcaption`). The plot is a group named by its kind ("Line chart") and described by a summary: how many series and points, from which category to which, and each series' lowest and highest value.
- **Keyboard:** the plot is one tab stop, after the table button. Each point is named with its series, category and value ("Visitors, Feb: 132"), and shows its category's values beside it and a focus ring around it.

  | Key | Does |
  | --- | --- |
  | Tab | To the point focused last (or the first point), then out of the chart |
  | ArrowRight | The next category's point in the same series, skipping missing values; ArrowLeft in a right-to-left page |
  | ArrowLeft | The category before; ArrowRight in a right-to-left page |
  | ArrowDown, ArrowUp | The same category in the next or the previous series |
  | Home, End | The series' first or last point |

  In a heatmap, the arrows move along a row and between rows, as they do between series, and each cell is named with its row, column and value ("Mon, 12: 44").

  In a donut, ArrowRight and ArrowDown go to the next slice, clockwise, and ArrowLeft and ArrowUp to the one before (ArrowLeft and ArrowRight swap in a right-to-left page, where the slices go round the other way). Home and End go to the first and last slice. Its summary adds the total and the smallest and largest share.
- **A heatmap's shades:** the steps get darker (sequential) or stronger away from the middle (diverging), so their order reads in lightness, for every reader; the exact numbers are in each cell's name, the tooltip and the table, and the legend gives the scale's lowest and highest values. In forced colors the cells are the system text color, as strong as their step.
- **Not by color alone:** each series has its own marker shape on a line or an area, and its own pattern on a bar or a donut slice after the first, in the legend and tooltip too. A donut's legend also names each slice with its share, in words. The chart colors (chart-1 to chart-8) are 3:1 on the surface, with the chart-gap color between neighbors, in every theme.
- **The numbers as a table:** "Show as table" swaps the chart for a [Table] (npx serupa-docs Table) of the same numbers, sortable by any column, with "No value" where one is missing.
- **Motion:** the line draws in, the bars grow, and areas and slices fade in once, on the first paint; with reduced motion they're drawn at once.
- **Contrast:** labels and title read 4.5:1 on the surface in every theme (`Chart.test.tsx`). In forced colors the series take the system's colors and the markers and patterns tell them apart.
- **What's still yours:** say in the text around it what the chart shows that matters ("Sign-ups doubled since June"). The summary describes the numbers, not what they mean.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `categories` | `string[]` | | The labels along the bottom, in order. |
| `series` | `{ name: string; values: (number \| null)[] }[]` | | Up to eight (a heatmap's rows: 64), each with a value per category. |
| `type` | `'line' \| 'bar' \| 'area' \| 'donut' \| 'heatmap'` | `'line'` | A donut draws the first series as slices; a heatmap a row per series. |
| `stacked` | `boolean` | `false` | With `type="area"`: each series stands on the one before it. |
| `scale` | `'sequential' \| 'diverging'` | `'sequential'` | With `type="heatmap"`: light to dark, or two hues away from `midpoint`. |
| `midpoint` | `number` | `0` | With `scale="diverging"`: the neutral middle. |
| `title` | `ReactNode` | | Shown above, and names the chart. |
| `formatValue` | `(value: number) => string` | the locale's number | On the axis, the tooltip, the table and what's read out. |
| `height` | `number` | `240` | The plot's height in pixels; a heatmap's is 32 a row unless set. |
| `hideLegend` | `boolean` | `false` | With one series, or when the title names them. |
| `categoryLabel` | `string` | `"Category"` | The first column's heading in the table. |
| `view`, `defaultView`, `onViewChange` | `'chart' \| 'table'` | `'chart'` | Controlled or not. |
| `loading` | `boolean` | `false` | Sets `aria-busy`. With no categories yet, the plot is a placeholder at its height. |
| `loadingLabel` | `string` | `"Loading…"` | Said once as the placeholder appears. |
| `id` | string | none | Goes to the root `<figure>`. |

`className`, `ref` and other props go to the `<figure>`.

## Component tokens

Each is an optional override: set it on the page, a container or one Chart. The list lives in `src/components/Chart/chart.tokens.json` (also in `design-tokens/components/`).

<!-- token-table:start (made from chart.tokens.json by npm run tokens: edit the descriptions there) -->
**Colors**

| Token | Default | Use |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--chart-text` | `text` | The title and the table's text (4.5:1 on the surface). |
| `--chart-tip-bg` | `surface-overlay` | The tooltip's background. |
| `--chart-tip-text` | `text` | The tooltip's text (4.5:1 on tip-bg). |
| `--chart-series-1` | `chart-1` | Series 1's line, markers and bars. Unset, the page's chart-1. |
| `--chart-series-2` | `chart-2` | Series 2's line, markers and bars. Unset, the page's chart-2. |
| `--chart-series-3` | `chart-3` | Series 3's line, markers and bars. Unset, the page's chart-3. |

components.name: Chat
components.summary: A conversation: messages in a log that stays at the newest one while the reader is there, day dividers, and a composer where Enter sends.
components.guide:
# Chat A conversation: messages in a log that stays at the newest one while the reader is there, day dividers, and a composer where Enter sends. Use it for support chats, comments in real time and AI assistants. `Chat` is the scrolling list, `ChatMessage` one message, `ChatDivider` a day line and `ChatComposer` the field under it. **Also called:** chat window, assistant panel, message thread. ```tsx import { Chat, ChatMessage, ChatDivider, ChatComposer, Avatar, Attachment } from "@diki-stwn/serupa-ds";
} time={new Date()}> Hi! How can I help you today? My invoice shows the wrong address. send(text)} />
``` ## When to use - Two or more people, or a person and an assistant, writing back and forth, newest at the bottom. - A thread of messages that grows while it's open, where people need to read back without losing their place. ## When not to use - A list of notifications or events: use [NotificationCenter] (npx serupa-docs NotificationCenter) or a [Timeline] (npx serupa-docs Timeline). - Comments under a page that don't arrive live: a [List] (npx serupa-docs List) of comments with a [Textarea] (npx serupa-docs Textarea) and a button reads better, top to bottom. - One message to the person: use a [Toast] (npx serupa-docs Toast) or an [Alert] (npx serupa-docs Alert). ## Anatomy Drawn from the `Statuses` story. 1. **Log** (`.srp-chat__log`): the scrolling list of messages. 2. **Divider** (`.srp-chat-divider`): the day the next messages were sent. 3. **Message** (`.srp-chat-message`): avatar, then author and time, the bubble, files and status. 4. **Bubble** (`.srp-chat-message__bubble`): what the message says; own messages are tinted and sit at the end. 5. **Status** (`.srp-chat-message__status`): "Sending…", or "Not sent" with "Try again". 6. **Composer** (`.srp-chat-composer`): the field, any actions, and Send (or Stop while a reply streams). An assistant's reply (the `AgentReply` story) adds these parts: - **Reasoning** (`.srp-chat-message__reasoning`): "Thought for 12 seconds", closed until the reader opens it. - **Steps** (`.srp-chat-steps`): the tools it called, each in progress, done or failed. - **Thinking** (`.srp-chat-message__thinking`): "Thinking…" with a shine, until the first words arrive. - **Versions** (`.srp-chat-message__branches`): "2 / 3" between previous and next, under a regenerated reply. An assistant also asks before it acts with a `ChatApproval` card (`.srp-chat-approval`, the `Approval` story), offers Copy, Regenerate and a rating under a reply with `ChatReplyActions` (`.srp-chat-reply-actions`, the `ReplyActions` story), and names its sources with `ChatCitation` chips (`.srp-chat-citation`, the `Citations` story). While the reader is further up and new messages arrive, a "3 new messages" button (`.srp-chat__jump`) sits at the bottom of the log; it scrolls down and focuses the log. ## Usage - Give `Chat` a height (a flex child, or `style={{ height }}`): it scrolls inside it. Name it with `aria-label` ("Conversation with Support"). - Give every message and divider a stable `key`, oldest first. Chat tells a message added at the end from earlier ones added at the start by their keys. - Add new messages at the end. When the reader is at the bottom, the conversation follows them; when they've scrolled up, it stays put and offers "N new messages". - Earlier messages: set `hasOlder` and load them in `onLoadOlder`, with `loadingOlder` while they come. Put them at the start: the message the reader was on stays where it was. - A `ChatDivider` with a `date` says "Today" and "Yesterday" by the visitor's clock and moves on at their midnight. A server-rendered page shows the date until it hydrates, because the server's day can differ from the visitor's. - In a row of messages from the same person, set `hideAuthor` on the second and later ones. The name is still read out. - Own messages: `own`, with `status="sending"` until the server confirms and `status="failed"` plus `onRetry` when it doesn't. - Files: pass [Attachment] (npx serupa-docs Attachment) elements to `attachments`, on a message or on the composer. - A streaming reply: grow the last message's text, with `streaming` on it, and `streaming` plus `onStop` on the composer. Take both off when it's done. ### An assistant's reply - Before any words arrive, set `thinking` on the reply: it says "Thinking…" until its text comes, then the text takes its place. - The model's reasoning goes in `reasoning`, with `reasoningTime` in seconds: the reader sees "Thought for 12 seconds" and opens it when they want the why. Leave the time out and it says "Reasoning". - Tools it calls go in `steps`, in order, each `{ id, label, status, detail? }` with `status` `"running"`, `"done"` or `"failed"`. Give each a stable `id` and update its status as it ends. `ChatSteps` draws the same list on its own, outside a message. - Before it acts (a refund, an email, a command), put a `ChatApproval` in the reply's `attachments`: what it will do in words as its children, more in `detail`, and `onApprove` and `onDeny`. Set `status` to `"approved"` or `"denied"` once the person answers: the card becomes a one-line record ("Approved: Reverse refund 2"), said to screen readers, with focus on it. - Sources go in the text as ``: a real link that shows its number and host ("1 docs.example.com"), or your own words as children. Wrap one in a [HoverCard] (npx serupa-docs HoverCard) for a preview of the page. - Under a finished reply, a `ChatReplyActions` row in its `attachments`: `copyText` for Copy, `onRegenerate` for Regenerate, and `feedback` with `onFeedback` for Helpful and Not helpful. Each button shows only when given. A rating is optional, said back ("Thanks, noted") and taken back by pressing it again; act on it at once (a "Not helpful" can offer to regenerate) rather than asking why first. Leave the row off while the reply streams. - A reply the person regenerated keeps its versions: pass `branch` (from 1), `branches` and `onBranchChange`, and show that version's text. "2 / 3" sits under it between previous and next. - A model picker and how much context is used sit in the composer's `actions`: a small [Select] (npx serupa-docs Select) named "Model" and a small [Meter] (npx serupa-docs Meter) whose `formatValue` says it in words ("12,400 of 200,000 tokens used"). The `AgentReply` story shows both. ```tsx {replyText} ``` ## Behavior - Opens at the newest message. A message that grows (a streamed reply, a picture that loads) keeps the conversation at the bottom when the reader was there. - The jump button scrolls to the newest message and moves focus to the conversation, so the next arrow key reads on from there. - When "Load earlier messages" had focus and the load is done, focus moves to the conversation, which stays where the reader was. The button may be gone (nothing more to load) or above the messages that came in. - Enter sends, Shift+Enter starts a new line, and Enter that confirms an input method's text (Japanese, Chinese, Korean) doesn't send. A field that's empty or only spaces sends nothing. Uncontrolled, the field empties after sending and keeps focus. - While `streaming`, Send becomes Stop; the person can keep typing their next message, and Enter waits until it's done. - The field grows from one line to `maxRows` (6), then scrolls. ### Do and don't - **Do:** Put a `ChatDivider` with a `date` where the day changes, so people see when each message was sent. (`DoDateDividers`) - **Don't:** Run messages from different days together: a reply a day later reads as if it came at once. (`DontNoDividers`) ## Accessibility - **Role and name:** the conversation is a `log` named by `aria-label`, so screen readers read each new message politely as it's added. A streaming message is `aria-busy` until `streaming` comes off, so it's read once, whole, rather than word by word. - **Keyboard:** the conversation is a focusable scrolling region (Tab, then arrows or Page Up and Page Down), with a visible focus ring. Tab moves on through its buttons and links, then the composer's field and buttons. - **Who wrote it:** the author is read before each message, "You" for `own` ones, even with `hideAuthor`. The avatar is hidden from screen readers: the name says who it is. - **Status:** "Sending…" and "Not sent" are words under the message, not only a color; a failed message also has a danger outline. - **Send:** an icon button named "Send" (and "Stop"); with nothing to send it's `aria-disabled` rather than removed from the Tab order. - **Contrast:** message text reads 4.5:1 on both bubbles, and times, dividers and "Not sent" 4.5:1 on the page, in every theme (`Chat.test.tsx`). - **An assistant at work:** "Thinking…" is a progress bar with that name. Reasoning is a native disclosure (`details`), opened with Enter or Space. Each step says its state in words after its label ("Searched the help center, Done"), not only by its icon. Steps are read with the reply when the log adds it; a step that changes later isn't announced, so say the outcome in the reply. - **Approval and versions:** a pending `ChatApproval` is a group named by what it will do. The answer is said ("Approved: …"), and focus moves from the pressed button to the record, so it isn't lost. The version buttons are named "Previous response" and "Next response" inside a group named "Response 2 of 3"; a press says where it landed, and at either end the button stays focusable (`aria-disabled`). Each citation's name is its number and source. `ChatReplyActions` is a group named "Response actions"; Helpful and Not helpful are toggles (`aria-pressed`), and a rating given or taken back is said. - **What's still yours:** announcing a failure out loud if it matters right then (the log reads only additions), and moving focus after a send fails. ### Keyboard | Key | Does | | --- | --- | | Tab | To the log, then through its buttons and links, then the composer | | ↑ ↓, PageUp, PageDown, Home, End | Scroll the log while it has focus | | Enter (in the composer) | Sends the message | | Shift+Enter | A new line in the message | ## Props ### Chat | Prop | Type | Default | Notes | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `children` | `ReactNode` | | ChatMessage and ChatDivider elements, oldest first, each with a key. | | `hasOlder` | `boolean` | `false` | Shows "Load earlier messages" at the top. | | `onLoadOlder` | `() => void` | | Called by that button. | | `loadingOlder` | `boolean` | `false` | The button says it's loading. | `id`, `className`, `ref` and other props go to the outer `
`; `aria-label` and `aria-labelledby` name the log. ### ChatMessage | Prop | Type | Default | Notes | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `children` | `ReactNode` | | The text; line breaks are kept. | | `author` | `ReactNode` | | Who wrote it. | | `avatar` | `ReactNode` | | A picture beside it, such as ``. | | `time` | `Date \| number \| string` | | When it was sent: relative time today ("5 minutes ago"), the time of day after that ("9:41 AM"), since the day divider above says which day. The full date is on hover. | | `own` | `boolean` | `false` | The reader's own message. | | `hideAuthor` | `boolean` | `false` | For later messages in a row from the same person. | | `status` | `'sending' \| 'failed'` | | An own message on its way, or one that didn't go. | | `onRetry` | `() => void` | | Adds Retry to a failed message. | | `attachments` | `ReactNode` | | Attachment elements under the text. | | `streaming` | `boolean` | `false` | The text is still arriving. | | `thinking` | `boolean` | `false` | "Thinking…" while an assistant has no words yet; the text replaces it. | | `reasoning` | `ReactNode` | | The assistant's reasoning, in a section closed until it's opened. | | `reasoningTime` | `number` | | How long it thought, in seconds: "Thought for 12 seconds". | | `steps` | `ChatStep[]` | | Tools it called on the way, above the text (see ChatSteps). | | `branch` | `number` | | Which version of a regenerated reply shows, from 1. | | `branches` | `number` | | How many versions there are; 2 or more shows the switcher. | | `onBranchChange` | `(branch: number) => void` | | Called with the version to show. | ### ChatDivider | Prop | Type | Default | Notes | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `date` | `Date \| number \| string` | | "Today", "Yesterday", or the date in the locale's words. | | `children` | `ReactNode` | | Your own words in place of the date. | ### ChatSteps The steps an assistant takes on its way to a reply, as an ordered list. `ChatMessage` draws it from `steps`; use it alone outside a message. | Prop | Type | Default | Notes | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `steps` | `ChatStep[]` | | Each `{ id, label, status, detail? }`; `status` is `"running"`, `"done"` or `"failed"`. | ### ChatApproval An assistant asks before it acts. The children say what it will do and name the card. | Prop | Type | Default | Notes | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `children` | `ReactNode` | | What it will do, in words. Kept as the record. | | `detail` | `ReactNode` | | More about it, such as the command or what changes. | | `status` | `'pending' \| 'approved' \| 'denied'` | `'pending'` | Answered, it becomes a one-line record. | | `onApprove` / `onDeny` | `() => void` | | Called by Approve and Deny. | ### ChatReplyActions The row under an assistant's reply. Each button is there only when its prop is. Every other prop goes to the `div` (a group named "Response actions"). | Prop | Type | Default | Notes | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `copyText` | `string \| () => string \| Promise` | | The reply's text, for Copy. | | `onRegenerate` | `() => void` | | Called by Regenerate. | | `feedback` | `'good' \| 'bad' \| null` | | The rating given (controlled). | | `onFeedback` | `(feedback) => void` | | Called with `'good'`, `'bad'`, or `null` when the pressed one is pressed again. | ### ChatCitation A numbered source in a reply, as a link. Every other prop goes to the `a`. | Prop | Type | Default | Notes | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `href` | `string` | | Where the source is. | | `index` | `number` | | Its number in the reply, from 1. | | `children` | `ReactNode` | the host | The source's name, in place of its host. | ### ChatComposer | Prop | Type | Default | Notes | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `value` / `defaultValue` | `string` | | The text, controlled or not. | | `onValueChange` | `(value: string) => void` | | Called as the text changes. | | `onSend` | `(text: string) => void` | | Called with the text on Send or Enter. | | `streaming` | `boolean` | `false` | Send becomes Stop. | | `onStop` | `() => void` | | Called by Stop. | | `placeholder` | `string` | | The field's placeholder. | | `disabled` | `boolean` | `false` | Turns the field and buttons off. | | `attachments` | `ReactNode` | | Files about to be sent, above the field. | | `actions` | `ReactNode` | | More buttons before Send. | | `maxRows` | `number` | `6` | How far the field grows before it scrolls. | `aria-label` renames the field ("Message"); `className`, `ref` and other props go to the `
`. ## Component tokens Each is an optional override: set it on the page, a container or one Chat. The list lives in `src/components/Chat/chat.tokens.json` (also in `design-tokens/components/`). | Token | Default | Use | | --- | --- | --- | | `--chat-text` | `text` | Message text and authors (4.5:1 on both bubbles). | | `--chat-muted` | `text-muted` | Times, day dividers and "Sending…" (4.5:1 on the page). | | `--chat-bubble-bg` | `surface-hover` | Others' message bubbles: a step above the card or page they sit on, in light and dark. | | `--chat-own-bubble-bg` | `primary-subtle` | The reader's own message bubbles. | | `--chat-failed-border` | `danger` | The outline of a message that didn't go. | | `--chat-error` | `danger-text` | "Not sent" (4.5:1 on the page). | | `--chat-divider` | `border` | The day divider's lines. | | `--chat-focus-ring` | `focus-ring` | The ring around the focused conversation. | | `--chat-step-done` | `success-text` | ChatSteps: a done step's check (3:1 on the surface). | | `--chat-citation-bg` | `surface` | ChatCitation: a source chip's background, so it stands out on a bubble. | | `--chat-bubble-radius` | `radius-container` | A bubble's corners (12px). | | `--chat-padding` | `spacing-4` | Space around the conversation and the composer (16px). | | `--chat-gap` | `spacing-3` | Space between messages (12px). | | `--chat-bubble-padding-x` | `spacing-3` | Space at a bubble's sides (12px). | | `--chat-bubble-padding-y` | `spacing-2` | Space above and below a bubble's text (8px). | | `--chat-reasoning-indent` | `spacing-3` | ChatMessage: how far the reasoning text sits in from its rule. |

components.name: Checkbox
components.summary: A native checkbox with its label, for turning one option on or off, or picking any number from a list.
components.guide:
# Checkbox

A native checkbox with its label, for turning one option on or off, or picking any number from a list. The box is drawn from tokens (`appearance: none`) and sits centered on the label's first line; a click anywhere on the label toggles it. `indeterminate` shows a dash for a select-all box when only some items are picked.

**Also called:** check box, tick box.

```jsx
import { Checkbox, CheckboxGroup, Field } from '@diki-stwn/serupa-ds';

<Checkbox checked={agree} onCheckedChange={setAgree}>I accept the terms</Checkbox>

<Checkbox defaultChecked description="Get an email when someone mentions you.">Mentions</Checkbox>

// a set: Field group gives it a legend, a hint and an error
<Field group label="Notify me about" error={error}>
  <Checkbox name="notify" value="comments">Comments</Checkbox>
  <Checkbox name="notify" value="mentions">Mentions</Checkbox>
</Field>

// a group that holds the checked values, with a select-all box
const [tags, setTags] = React.useState(["news"]);
<Field group label="Topics">
  <CheckboxGroup name="topics" value={tags} onValueChange={setTags}>
    <Checkbox selectAll>All topics</Checkbox>
    <Checkbox value="news">News</Checkbox>
    <Checkbox value="tips">Tips</Checkbox>
  </CheckboxGroup>
</Field>

// select all by hand (a table)
<Checkbox checked={all} indeterminate={some && !all} onChange={toggleAll}>Select all</Checkbox>

// no visible label (a table row)
<Checkbox aria-label="Select row" />
```

## When to use

- Choices that take effect when the form is sent, such as accepting the terms.
- Picking any number of options from a list, including none.
- Selecting rows in a table, with a select-all box that shows `indeterminate` when only some are picked.

## When not to use

- A setting that applies at once: use a [Switch] (npx serupa-docs Switch).
- One choice from a list: use [radios] (npx serupa-docs Radio); checkboxes say "any number".

## Anatomy

Drawn from the `LongLabel` story.

1. **Box** (`.srp-checkbox__control`): the square that shows checked, unchecked or mixed, over the native checkbox.
2. **Check mark** (`.srp-checkbox__icon`): the mark inside the box when it's checked.
3. **Label** (`.srp-checkbox__text`): what checking it means; clicking it checks the box too.
4. **Description** (`.srp-checkbox__description`): optional detail under the label.

## Usage

- Write the label as a statement that's true when checked ("Email me about replies"), not a question.
- Stack sets vertically: they're quicker to scan than a row.
- For a set whose answer is a list of values, use `CheckboxGroup`. It holds the list, gives every box one `name`, and passes `size`, `invalid`, `disabled` and `required` down.
- Put a `selectAll` box first when people often want all or none. It needs no `value`.
- `variant="card"` makes each box a bordered card, pressed as a whole: for a few choices that each need a sentence or a price (add-ons, features, interests during onboarding). The boxes stay native, so Space, the form value and `selectAll` work as in a plain group. Keep cards to a handful; a long list scans faster as plain boxes.

```tsx
<Field label="Add-ons" group>
  <CheckboxGroup variant="card" orientation="horizontal" defaultValue={['wrap']}>
    <Checkbox value="wrap" description="Rp 15.000">Gift wrap</Checkbox>
    <Checkbox value="card" description="A printed note, free">Greeting card</Checkbox>
  </CheckboxGroup>
</Field>
```

### Do and don't

- **Do:** Say what a tick turns on: "Email me about orders". (`DoPositiveLabel`)
- **Don't:** A label in the negative, such as "Don't email me", where a tick means no and people have to read it twice. (`DontNegativeLabel`)
- **Do:** Cards for add-ons that each need a line to choose by, such as a price. (`DoCardsWithDetails`)
- **Don't:** Cards for options that explain themselves, such as colors to filter by: plain checkboxes read faster. (`DontCardsForShortOptions`)

## States

| State | Look |
| --- | --- |
| Unchecked | `field` background, 1px `field-border` |
| Checked | `primary` fill and border, a check in `on-primary` |
| Indeterminate | `primary` fill and border, a dash in `on-primary` |
| Hover | `field-border-hover`; a checked or indeterminate box turns `primary-hover` |
| Focus | From the keyboard: a 2px `focus-ring` outline 2px out (`focus-ring-width`, `focus-ring-offset`), like Button. The gap is transparent, so it reads on any background, and forced-colors mode draws it too |
| Invalid | `danger` border while unchecked, and a `danger` focus ring |
| Read-only | Looks as it is, with a default cursor and no hover change |
| Disabled | Neutral colors at full opacity: a `disabled-border` box, filled `disabled-surface` with a `disabled-text` tick when checked, and a `disabled-text` label; `not-allowed` cursor; also when a parent fieldset (`Field group disabled`) is disabled |
| Card | A `surface` card with a 1px `border` and 16px padding, the label in `font-medium`; `field-border-hover` under the pointer; checked, a 2px `primary` border drawn inside, so nothing moves (the tick shows it too); the focus ring goes around the whole card; invalid, a `danger` border while unchecked; in forced colors, a checked card's border is Highlight |

## Accessibility

- A press anywhere within 24px of the box or the row counts (WCAG 2.5.8): when the row is shorter, or the box stands alone, its hit area reaches past what is drawn, so nothing moves. On a touch screen it's 44px high, as Apple and Material ask; in a group it stops halfway into the gap, so neighbors never share a point.
- It's a real checkbox: Space toggles it, forms submit it, and screen readers announce checked, unchecked and mixed.
- The label names it. With a description, the checkbox is named by the label alone (`aria-labelledby`) and the description is read after it (`aria-describedby`).
- The check and dash are decorative (`aria-hidden`).
- `readOnly` keeps it focusable and read out with `aria-readonly`, but a click or Space doesn't change it, and `onChange` doesn't run (your `onClick` does). The browser's own `readonly` does nothing on a checkbox, so Checkbox cancels the click. A checked read-only box is still submitted, which `disabled` isn't.
- For a set, use `Field group`: a `<fieldset>` and `<legend>`, so the question is read with each option.
- `CheckboxGroup` is a `role="group"` with `aria-disabled` from its props. A group supports neither `aria-invalid` nor `aria-required`, so `invalid` puts `aria-invalid` on each box, and `required` is each box's native `required` (Field `group` also says "Required" in the legend). `required` means at least one: every box is `required` while none is checked, so the browser won't submit the form, and none is once one is. The browser says "Choose at least one option." (the `selectAtLeastOne` label, in English and Indonesian) rather than its one-box message, which reads as if every box were mandatory.
- Native constraints (`required`) show too: a box that fails them takes the `invalid` border once people have changed it or tried to send the form (`:user-invalid`), never on first paint. Inside a Field, the Field then says which constraint fails, in its error slot (in the provider's words), with `aria-invalid` and the description, so the border is never the only sign; an `error` you pass wins. On its own, the border is only a color: set `invalid` and say the problem in text when you check it yourself. To keep the browser out of it, leave out the attribute and check the value in your own code.
- A `selectAll` box is checked when every enabled box is, and indeterminate (announced as mixed) when only some are. A click checks every enabled box, or clears them when all are checked. Disabled boxes keep their state. It isn't submitted. Server-rendered, it already shows this state, counted from the Checkboxes among the group's children (a box inside a component of your own counts once it mounts).
- Server-rendered, an `indeterminate` box (or a `selectAll` box with some checked) already shows its dash: the markup carries `data-indeterminate` until the script sets the native state, which is what screen readers announce as mixed.
- The label and description keep 4.5:1, the checked fill, focus ring and invalid border 3:1, and the check 4.5:1 on its fill, in every theme (`Checkbox.test.tsx`). The resting border is soft on purpose (`field-border`: about 1.5:1 in light, 1.4:1 to 1.9:1 in dark), under the 3:1 WCAG 1.4.11 asks of a control's edge: a deliberate design exception. The label beside the box, its fill in dark, the stronger border on hover and the 3:1 focus ring mark it, and more contrast (`data-contrast="more"` or the system setting) brings back a 3:1+ border.

### Keyboard

| Key | Does |
| --- | --- |
| Tab | To the checkbox |
| Space | Check or uncheck it (an indeterminate one becomes checked) |

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | string | none | Goes to the native `<input type="checkbox">` (not the wrapper), so a `<label htmlFor>` or a Field can point at it. |
| `children` | node | | The label. Without one, give the checkbox an `aria-label` |
| `size` | `'sm'` \| `'md'` \| `'lg'` | `'md'` | A 14px box with `text-xs`, 16px with `text-sm`, 20px with `text-base` |
| `description` | node | | A muted second line under the label, linked with `aria-describedby` (and kept out of the name) |
| `indeterminate` | boolean | `false` | A dash, announced as "mixed". Set it from your state: a click clears it natively, and the next render puts it back if the prop is still true |
| `invalid` | boolean | `false` | A danger border (while unchecked) and focus ring, and `aria-invalid` |
| `variant` | `'plain'` \| `'card'` | the group's, or `'plain'` | `'card'`: the box, label and description in a bordered card pressed as a whole |
| `readOnly` | boolean | `false` | Focusable and read out (`aria-readonly`), but clicks and Space don't change it; a checked box is still submitted |

| `selectAll` | boolean | `false` | In a `CheckboxGroup`: checks or clears every other box; checked when all are, indeterminate when some are |

`onCheckedChange(checked, { event })` runs after `onChange` with the new state, the same shape as ToggleButton's `onPressedChange`, so you needn't read `event.target.checked`. Not on a read-only box.

Everything else (`checked`, `defaultChecked`, `onChange`, `name`, `value`, `disabled`, `required`, `id`, `aria-*`) and `ref` go to the `<input type="checkbox">`. In a `CheckboxGroup`, the group sets `name` and `checked` from each box's `value`. `className` and `style` go to the `<label>` around it, which has `data-component="checkbox"` and `data-size`.

### CheckboxGroup

| Prop | Type | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `value` | `(string \| number)[]` | | The checked boxes' values (controlled). Use with `onValueChange` |
| `defaultValue` | `(string \| number)[]` | `[]` | The values checked at first (uncontrolled). A form reset brings them back, also from outside the group: boxes with a `form` attribute reset with that form. |
| `onValueChange` | `(value, details: { event }) => void` | | Called with the new list, in the boxes' order. Numbers stay numbers |
| `name` | `string` | generated | Every box's name, so each checked one is submitted with its value |
| `orientation` | `'vertical'` \| `'horizontal'` | `'vertical'` | Stacked, or a wrapping row |
| `size` | `'sm'` \| `'md'` \| `'lg'` | | The boxes' size, unless a Checkbox sets its own |
| `variant` | `'plain'` \| `'card'` | `'plain'` | Every box's look, unless one sets its own. Cards fill the column, or share a wrapping row (each at least 192px) with `orientation="horizontal"`, 12px apart |
| `invalid` | boolean | `false` | A danger border on every unchecked box, and `aria-invalid` on each box. Field's `error` sets it |
| `disabled` | boolean | `false` | Disables every box |
| `required` | boolean | `false` | At least one box must be checked |
| `readOnly` | boolean | `false` | Every box shows its state without letting it change: focusable and read out (`aria-readonly`), and the form still sends the checked ones, unlike `disabled` |

Other props (`id`, `aria-label`, `aria-labelledby`, `className`…) and `ref` go to the `<div role="group">`, which has `data-component="checkbox-group"` and `data-orientation`.

## Component tokens

Each is an optional override: set it on the page, a container or one checkbox. The list lives in `src/components/Checkbox/checkbox.tokens.json` (also in `design-tokens/components/`).

<!-- token-table:start (made from checkbox.tokens.json by npm run tokens: edit the descriptions there) -->
**Colors**

| --- | --- | --- |
| `--checkbox-bg` | `field` | The box while unchecked |
| `--checkbox-bg-disabled` | `field-readonly` | The box when disabled and unchecked: a disabled field's fill, at or above the surface in dark rather than sunk below it |
| `--checkbox-bg-checked` | `primary` | Fill and border when checked or indeterminate |
| `--checkbox-bg-checked-hover` | `primary-hover` | The same, on hover |
| `--checkbox-bg-checked-pressed` | `primary-pressed` | The checked box's fill while held down, one step past bg-checked-hover. |
| `--checkbox-bg-pressed` | `secondary` | The unchecked box's background while held down. |

| `--checkbox-border-hover` | `field-border-hover` | Border on hover |
| `--checkbox-border-pressed` | `field-border-pressed` | The unchecked box's border while held down, one step past border-hover. |
| `--checkbox-icon-color` | `on-primary` | The check and the dash |
| `--checkbox-label-color` | `text` | The label |
| `--checkbox-description-color` | `text-muted` | The description |
| `--checkbox-focus-ring` | `focus-ring` | The focus ring |
| `--checkbox-invalid` | `field-border-invalid` | Border and focus ring when invalid |

| `--checkbox-edge-checked` | `primary-edge` | A checked box's edge (Yellow Light; transparent where the fill is 3:1 on the page) |

**Sizing**

components.name: CodeBlock
components.summary: Code for people to read and copy: an install command, a config file, an example.
components.guide:
# CodeBlock

Code for people to read and copy: an install command, a config file, an example. It shows the code in the mono font in a framed box, with an optional title, line numbers and marked lines, and a button that copies it all.

**Also called:** code snippet, syntax highlighter.

```tsx
import { CodeBlock } from "@diki-stwn/serupa-ds";

<CodeBlock title="SignIn.tsx" language="tsx" code={source} lineNumbers highlight={[3, [6, 7]]} />
```

## When to use

- A command or a file people will copy into their own work.
- An example longer than a line, where its layout matters.

## When not to use

- A word of code inside a sentence: use `<code>` in [Prose] (npx serupa-docs Prose).
- Text people type into: use [Textarea] (npx serupa-docs Textarea).
- A single value to copy, such as an API key: use [CopyButton] (npx serupa-docs CopyButton) beside it.

## Anatomy

Drawn from the `LineNumbers` story.

1. **Header** (`.srp-code-block__header`): the title, or the language when there's no title, and the copy button.
2. **Title** (`.srp-code-block__title`): the file name or what the code is.
3. **Copy button** (`.srp-code-block__copy`): copies the whole code and says "Copied".
4. **Code** (`.srp-code-block__pre`): the code, which scrolls sideways when it's wider than the box.
5. **Line** (`.srp-code-block__line`): one line, with its number before it; a marked line (`.srp-code-block__line--marked`) has a tint and a bar at its start.

## Usage

- Give it a `title` when the code is a file ("SignIn.tsx") or a step ("Install"). Without one, the `language` shows in the header.
- Mark the lines a step is about with `highlight`, rather than leaving people to find what changed.
- Use `lineNumbers` when the text around it points at lines; `startLine` when it shows part of a longer file.
- Long lines scroll sideways, which keeps code's layout. Use `wrap` for prose-like lines, such as a long message string.
- CodeBlock doesn't color the syntax. The `<code>` has a `language-*` class and the box a `data-language`, for a highlighter you add.

### Do and don't

- **Do:** Give it a `title` that names the file or step, and `highlight` the lines the step is about. (`DoTitleAndHighlight`)
- **Don't:** Leave out the title and the highlight: people have to hunt for what changed. (`DontBareCode`)

## Accessibility

- **Role and name:** a `<pre>` with the code as text, read as it is. When it's wider (or taller) than its box it becomes a region named by its title (or its language, or "Code") and a tab stop, so a keyboard can scroll it (WCAG 2.1.1); a box that fits is neither.
- **Keyboard:** Tab reaches the copy button, then the code when it scrolls. In the code, the arrow keys scroll it.

  | Key | Does |
  | --- | --- |
  | Tab | To the copy button, then to the code when it scrolls |
  | ArrowLeft, ArrowRight, ArrowUp, ArrowDown | Scroll the code, when it has focus |

- **Marked lines:** each is a `<mark>`, and has a bar at its start as well as the tint, so the mark isn't only a color. Line numbers are drawn by CSS, so they're neither selected, copied nor read.
- **Direction:** code reads left to right on every page, so `run();` never becomes `;()run` on a right-to-left page.
- **Contrast:** the code, the language and the line numbers read 4.5:1 on the box and on a marked line in every theme (`CodeBlock.test.tsx`).
- **What's still yours:** say before the block what the code does. Colors from a highlighter you add need 4.5:1 on `--code-block-bg` in each theme.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `code` | `string` | | The code, as text. |
| `title` | `ReactNode` | | In the header; names the scroll area. |
| `language` | `string` | | In the header without a title; a `language-*` class. |
| `lineNumbers` | `boolean` | `false` | |
| `startLine` | `number` | `1` | The first line's number. |
| `highlight` | `(number \| [number, number])[]` | | Lines and ranges to mark. |
| `wrap` | `boolean` | `false` | Wraps long lines instead of scrolling. |
| `copyable` | `boolean` | `true` | The copy button. |
| `id` | string | none | Goes to the root `<div>`. |

`className`, `ref` and other props go to the root `<div>`.

## Component tokens

Each is an optional override: set it on the page, a container or one CodeBlock. The list lives in `src/components/CodeBlock/code-block.tokens.json` (also in `design-tokens/components/`).

<!-- token-table:start (made from code-block.tokens.json by npm run tokens: edit the descriptions there) -->
| Token | Default | Use |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--code-block-bg` | `surface-muted` | The background. |
| `--code-block-text` | `text` | The code and title (4.5:1 on bg). |
| `--code-block-muted` | `text-muted` | The language and the line numbers (4.5:1 on bg). A marked line's number takes the text color. |
| `--code-block-border` | `border` | The frame and the line under the header. |
| `--code-block-mark-bg` | `primary-subtle` | A marked line's tint. |
| `--code-block-mark-bar` | `primary-text` | The bar at a marked line's start. |
| `--code-block-focus-ring` | `focus-ring` | The ring inside the frame when the code scrolls and has keyboard focus. |
| `--code-block-radius` | `radius-control` | The corners (6px). |
| `--code-block-padding` | `spacing-4` | Space around the code (16px). |
| `--code-block-font-size` | `text-sm` | The code's size (14px). |
<!-- token-table:end -->

components.name: ColorPicker
components.summary: Picks a color from a set of swatches, or any color by its hex code or with the browser's own picker.
components.guide:
# ColorPicker

Picks a color from a set of swatches, or any color by its hex code or with the browser's own picker. With `contrastWith`, it shows the contrast between the picked color and the one it goes on, and warns when text would be hard to read.

**Also called:** color input, swatch picker.

```tsx
import { ColorPicker } from "@diki-stwn/serupa-ds";

const SWATCHES = [{ value: "#1d4ed8", label: "Blue" }, { value: "#047857", label: "Emerald" }, { value: "#b91c1c", label: "Red" }];

<Field label="Label color">
  <ColorPicker swatches={SWATCHES} value={color} onValueChange={setColor} />
</Field>

<ColorPicker aria-label="Text color" swatches={SWATCHES} defaultValue="#1d4ed8" contrastWith="#ffffff" />  // "Contrast 6.7:1"
<ColorPicker aria-label="Tag" swatches={SWATCHES} custom={false} size="sm" />
```

## When to use

- Picking a color for something people make: a label, a tag, a calendar, a chart series, a brand color.
- A short set of colors that work in your product, with a way out for any other.

## When not to use

- Choosing between a few named options that happen to be colors ("Red", "Green" as statuses): use a [SegmentedControl] (npx serupa-docs SegmentedControl) or [Select] (npx serupa-docs Select) with the names.
- Theming the whole product: use the themes and tokens.

## Anatomy

Drawn from the `ContrastCheck` story.

1. **Swatches** (`.srp-color-picker__swatches`): the colors to choose from, each named for screen readers.
2. **Chosen swatch** (`.srp-color-picker__swatch--checked`): the color chosen now, with a check.
3. **Custom color** (`.srp-color-picker__custom`): any other color, from the system picker or as a hex code.
4. **Hex code** (`.srp-color-picker__hex`): the chosen color as a hex code, to read or type.
5. **Contrast** (`.srp-color-picker__contrast`): the contrast against the background it will sit on.
6. **Warning** (`.srp-color-picker__warning`): says when that contrast is too low to read.

## Usage

- Name every swatch in words with `label` ("Ocean", "Sunset"). Screen readers say the name. A bare hex string (or an empty `label`) gets a rough name from its color, such as "Dark blue" or "Light gray" (the `colorName` label, English and Indonesian built in), and its code as the tooltip; your own names are still better, since two blues both read as "Blue".
- Pick swatches that pass contrast where they'll be used, and set `contrastWith` to the background (or the text color) when people can pick freely, so they see the ratio. `minContrast` is 4.5 by default (body text); use 3 for large text and icons.
- Turn off `custom` when only the swatches are allowed.
- Colors come out as lowercase `#rrggbb`, whatever case or short form people type.

## States

| State | Look |
| --- | --- |
| Rest | Round swatches, each with a thin inset `border-control` edge (a soft line, 3:1 with more contrast), so white shows on white and black on black |
| Picked | A `primary` ring outside the swatch and a check in white or black, whichever stands out on it |
| Focus | A `focus-ring` outline around the swatch |
| Invalid | Every swatch's edge turns into a 2px `danger` one, as a field's border does |
| Read-only | As at rest, with a plain cursor; nothing can be picked |
| Disabled | The whole picker faded to `opacity-disabled`, with a `not-allowed` cursor |

## Behavior

- The swatches are one radio group: Tab reaches the picked swatch (or the first), the arrow keys move and pick (wrapping), and Home and End go to the ends.
- A form reset puts the first color (`defaultValue`) back, in the swatches, the hex field and the submitted value, also for a picker outside the form that `form` names, with or without `name`.
- The hex field picks the color as soon as six digits are typed, and a three-digit code (`f0a`) on Enter or blur. A code on its way to six digits isn't marked invalid; one that can't be a color (`1g`, seven digits) is marked at once, and a short one (`1d4e`) when Enter is pressed. A bad code goes back to the picked color on blur. The `#` is optional, and a pasted code is trimmed first, so ` #1d4ed8 ` copied with spaces works. Switching to another window or browser tab isn't leaving the field: the text waits until people come back.
- The browser's color picker (the square before the field) picks any color too; when the picked color isn't a swatch, no swatch is checked. With nothing picked, its square shows empty rather than black, and black chosen there is picked when it closes.
- The contrast ratio is rounded down to one decimal, so 4.49 shows as 4.4 and never looks like a pass. It's written in the locale's numbers ("4,5:1" in Indonesian).

### Do and don't

- **Do:** Set `contrastWith` to the background (or the text color) when people can pick freely, so they see the ratio. (`DoShowContrast`)
- **Don't:** Let people pick any color with no contrast shown: they choose colors that can't be read where they're used. (`DontPickBlind`)

## Accessibility

- `role="radiogroup"` named by `aria-label`, `aria-labelledby` or a surrounding [Field] (npx serupa-docs Field)'s label, with a `role="radio"` swatch for each color and `aria-checked` on the picked one. In a Field, the hint and error describe the radiogroup, and `aria-required` and `aria-invalid` sit on it. The hex field is its own field, named "Hex code".
- The picked swatch shows a ring (3:1 on the page in every theme) and a check in white or black, whichever stands out more on that color, so the choice doesn't rely on seeing the color.
- Every swatch, and the native color well, has a thin border in `border-control`, a soft line by design (3:1 with more contrast). So a white swatch shows on a white page and a black one on a dark page (WCAG 1.4.11). In forced-colors mode the swatches keep their real colors and the ring uses Highlight.
- The contrast line is a polite live region, so a change is read out. The warning has an icon and words, not just a color.
- With `contrastWith`, every swatch also says its ratio before it's picked, as its description ("Contrast 1.3:1, below 4.5:1, which can be hard to read"), and a swatch under `minContrast` is struck through with a diagonal line (`CanvasText` in forced-colors mode) and has `data-low-contrast`. The line goes away once it's picked, when the check and the contrast line take over.

### Keyboard

| Key | Does |
| --- | --- |
| Tab | To the chosen swatch (the swatches are one Tab stop), then the hex field and the browser's color picker, with `custom` |
| Right / Down | The next swatch, choosing it; Left and Right swap in right-to-left pages, and it wraps |
| Left / Up | The previous swatch, the same way |
| Home / End | The first or last swatch |
| Enter | In the hex field, chooses the color typed |

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | string | none | Goes to the root `<div>`. A `<label htmlFor>` can't name it; inside a Field, the Field's label names it through this id. A label click then focuses the picked swatch. |
| `swatches` | `Array<{ value, label } \| string>` | | The colors, as hex. A bare hex is named from its color ("Dark blue"). |
| `value` | `string \| null` | | Controlled, as hex. |
| `defaultValue` | `string \| null` | | Uncontrolled. |
| `onValueChange` | `(value: string) => void` | | With lowercase `#rrggbb`. |
| `onValueCommit` | `(value: string) => void` | | Called once a color is chosen: a swatch picked, the browser's picker closed, or the hex field left or Enter pressed. Not on every drag step or keystroke, unlike `onValueChange`. |
| `custom` | `boolean` | `true` | The browser's picker and a hex field. |
| `contrastWith` | `string` | | A hex color to check against: the picked one in the contrast line, and every swatch in its description and strike-through. |
| `minContrast` | `number` | `4.5` | Below this ratio it warns. |
| `size` | `'sm' \| 'md' \| 'lg'` | `'md'` | 24, 32 or 44px swatches. `lg` also has a large hex field and 16px text, to sit beside large fields and buttons and give touch-sized targets. |
| `disabled` | `boolean` | `false` | A `<fieldset disabled>` around it does the same |
| `readOnly` | `boolean` | `false` | Shows the color but can't change it: the swatches stay focusable and the group says it (`aria-readonly`), the hex field is read-only, the browser's picker doesn't open, and a form still sends the color, unlike `disabled` |
| `name` | `string` | | Submits the color with a form. |
| `form` | `string` | | The id of the form it submits with, when the picker sits outside it (like an input's `form`). |
| `required` | `boolean` | `false` | A color must be picked: `aria-required` on the swatches, and the form won't submit without one (the swatches are marked invalid and take focus). Set for you in a required Field. |
| `invalid` | `boolean` | `false` | Marks the swatches invalid: `aria-invalid` on the group, and each swatch's border turns the danger color (`--color-picker-invalid`). Set for you in a Field with an error. |

Every other prop, `className` and `ref` go to the outer `<div>`, which has `data-component="color-picker"`; `focus()` on it and `autoFocus` focus the picked swatch. `aria-label` and `aria-labelledby` name the radio group.

## Component tokens

Each is an optional override: set it on the page, a container or one picker. The hex field uses Input's tokens. The list lives in `src/components/ColorPicker/color-picker.tokens.json` (also in `design-tokens/components/`).

<!-- token-table:start (made from color-picker.tokens.json by npm run tokens: edit the descriptions there) -->
| Token | Default | Use |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--color-picker-text` | `text` | The picker's text. |
| `--color-picker-swatch-border` | `border-control` | The thin inset border on every swatch and round the native color well (3:1 on the page). |
| `--color-picker-ring` | `primary-text` | The ring around the picked swatch (3:1). |
| `--color-picker-ring-hover` | `border-control` | The ring round a swatch the pointer is on, before it is picked (3:1 on the page). |
| `--color-picker-invalid` | `danger` | The swatches' border while invalid (3:1), so the error shows on the swatches as well as in the Field's message. |
| `--color-picker-focus-ring` | `focus-ring` | The keyboard focus ring. |
