components.name: DateField
components.summary: A date people know or copy from a document, such as a date of birth or a passport's expiry, typed as day, month and year in three labeled boxes, in the locale's order.
components.guide:
# DateField

A date people know or copy from a document, such as a date of birth or a passport's expiry, typed as day, month and year in three labeled boxes, in the locale's order. The app gets `YYYY-MM-DD`, and is told what's wrong while it isn't a date, so it can word the error.

**Also called:** date input, segmented date input.

```tsx
import { DateField, Field } from "@diki-stwn/serupa-ds";

<Field label="Date of birth" hint="For example, 27 3 2007" error={error}>
  <DateField name="dob" autoComplete="bday" order="dmy" max={today} onValueChange={(value, { problem }) => setProblem(problem)} />
</Field>
```

## When to use

- A date of birth, or a date on a card, passport, ID or letter: one people type from memory or copy, often years from today.
- Forms filled in on a phone: the three boxes bring up the number keypad, and the browser can fill a date of birth.

## When not to use

- A date near today, or one picked by weekday ("next Tuesday", a booking, a deadline): use a [DatePicker] (npx serupa-docs DatePicker), whose calendar shows the days around it.
- A start and end date: use a [DateRangePicker] (npx serupa-docs DateRangePicker).
- A month and year only, such as a card's expiry: use an [Input] (npx serupa-docs Input) with `autoComplete="cc-exp"` and a hint ("MM/YY, like 08/27").

## Anatomy

Drawn from the `Playground` story.

1. **Group** (`.srp-date-field`): the three parts in a row, named by the Field's label. In a narrow column the parts wrap.
2. **Part** (`.srp-date-field__part`): a small label (`.srp-date-field__label`), Day, Month or Year, over its box.
3. **Box** (`.srp-date-field__input`): an [Input] (npx serupa-docs Input) sized for two digits, or four for the year.

## Usage

- Name it with a [Field] (npx serupa-docs Field) label ("Date of birth") or `aria-label`, and give an example in the hint, in the boxes' order ("For example, 27 3 2007" with `order="dmy"`, "3 27 2007" with `"mdy"`). Without `order` the boxes follow the locale, so set it whenever the hint is fixed text, and use a day over 12 so the example shows which box is which.
- The boxes take digits only, up to 2, 2 and 4: a letter typed or pasted is dropped, and digits in any script are read as 0–9. A wrong number isn't blocked or changed (a day of 55 stays), so a mistake can be read and fixed. A `/`, `.`, `-` or space after a number moves to the next box, and a whole date pasted into any box ("17/08/1945", "1945-08-17", "17 Agustus 1945") fills all three.
- `onValueChange(value, details)` gives `YYYY-MM-DD`, or `""` until the boxes make a real date. `details.problem` says what's wrong: `"empty"`, `"missing-day"`, `"missing-month"`, `"missing-year"` (also a year under 4 digits), `"not-a-date"` (31 April, month 13), `"before-min"` or `"after-max"`; `details.parts` says in which boxes. Word the error from it, GOV.UK style: "Date of birth must include a month", "Date of birth must be in the past".
- Once focus leaves the date, or the form is sent, it says what's wrong under the boxes and marks the box to fix: "Day must be between 1 and 31", "Month must be between 1 and 12", "Year must have 4 numbers", "Enter the month", "Enter a real date: February 2025 has 28 days", "Enter a date on or before 14 November 2026". It's about the first box that's wrong, and follows what's typed after that. A form isn't sent while the date is wrong: focus goes to the box instead. The message waits until a click that took focus away has landed, so it doesn't move the button from under the pointer. When the app marks it `invalid` (a Field with an error), the Field's words show instead, so nothing is said twice.
- `monthInput="select"` makes the month a menu of the locale's month names (Januari, Februari… in id-ID), for people who know the month by name. The value is the same.
- `min` and `max` don't stop anything being typed; a date outside them still comes as its value, with its problem, and its message names the date.
- With `invalid` (a Field with an error sets it), only the boxes the problem is in are marked, or all three when it's about the whole date.
- With `name`, a hidden input sends `YYYY-MM-DD` ("" while it isn't a date), and `form.reset()` goes back to `defaultValue`.
- Controlled, `value=""` empties the boxes only when they held a date, so a part typed so far stays.
- `autoComplete="bday"` for a date of birth lets the browser fill it.

### Do and don't

- **Do:** Give an example in the hint, in the boxes' order ("For example, 27 3 2007" with `order="dmy"`). (`DoExampleHint`)
- **Don't:** Leave out the example: people guess whether the day or the month comes first. (`DontNoExample`)

## Accessibility

- **Role and name:** a `group` named by its Field label or `aria-label`, and described by the Field's hint and error. Each box is a text field named by its own label, Day, Month or Year; `inputmode="numeric"` brings up a number keypad without `type="number"`'s spin buttons, its dropped leading zeros or its "e". The boxes the problem is in carry `aria-invalid` (the group can't); the error is read with the group, as its description, when focus enters it.
- **Keyboard:** Tab moves through the three boxes. Focus never jumps by itself when a box is full, which would surprise people who look at the keyboard while typing and those who use a screen reader; a typed separator moves on instead. Clicking the Field's label focuses the first box.

| Key | Does |
| --- | --- |
| Tab, Shift+Tab | Moves between the Day, Month and Year boxes, and out. |
| `/` `.` `-` Space | After a number, moves to the next box. In an empty box or the last one, does nothing. |
| Ctrl+V, ⌘V | A whole date fills all three boxes; a number alone goes in the box. |

- **Contrast:** the labels read 4.5:1 on the surface in every theme (`DateField.test.tsx`); the boxes are Inputs.
- **The message:** its line is the group's description and each marked box's, so it's read on entering the date and on the box to fix. It comes in all 20 languages, from the `dateFieldError` label.
- **What's still yours:** the label and example, and the error's words when you want your own (`details.problem` says which, and `invalid` on the DateField or an error on its Field takes the message's place).

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | `string` | | Goes to the root `<div role="group">`. A `<label htmlFor>` can't name a group; inside a Field, the Field's label names it through this id. |
| `value` | `string` | | The date (controlled), `YYYY-MM-DD`, or `""`. |
| `defaultValue` | `string` | | The date at first (uncontrolled), `YYYY-MM-DD`; `form.reset()` goes back to it. |
| `onValueChange` | `(value: string, details: DateFieldChangeDetails) => void` | | On every change. `details`: `{ day, month, year, problem, parts, reason }`, `reason` being `"type"`, `"paste"` or `"reset"`. |
| `min` | `string` | | The earliest right date, `YYYY-MM-DD`; earlier ones say `"before-min"`. |
| `max` | `string` | | The latest right date, `YYYY-MM-DD`; later ones say `"after-max"`. |
| `order` | `"dmy" \| "mdy" \| "ymd"` | the locale's | The boxes' order. |
| `autoComplete` | `"bday" \| "off"` | `"off"` | `"bday"` asks for `bday-day`, `bday-month` and `bday-year`. |
| `name` | `string` | | Sends `YYYY-MM-DD` with a form in a hidden input. |
| `form` | `string` | | The id of a form elsewhere on the page. |
| `size` | `"sm" \| "md" \| "lg"` | `"md"` | The boxes' size, as Input's. |
| `monthInput` | `"number" \| "select"` | `"number"` | The month as a number box, or a menu of the locale's month names. The value is the same either way. |
| `disabled` | `boolean` | `false` | Turns the boxes off; nothing is sent. |
| `readOnly` | `boolean` | `false` | The boxes stay focusable and read out as read-only, and the date is still sent, unlike `disabled`; typing and a pasted date change nothing. |
| `invalid` | `boolean` | `false` | Marks the boxes the problem is in. Field sets it from its error. |
| `required` | `boolean` | `false` | A date must be given: `aria-required` on the boxes, and the form isn't sent while they're empty (they're marked and the first takes focus; the Field's error says why). A required Field sets only `aria-required`, as it does on an Input. |

`className`, `ref` and other props go to the group's `<div>`; `ref.current.focus()` and `autoFocus` focus the first box.

## Component tokens

Each is an optional override: set it on the page, a container or one DateField. The list lives in `src/components/DateField/date-field.tokens.json` (also in `design-tokens/components/`).

<!-- token-table:start (made from date-field.tokens.json by npm run tokens: edit the descriptions there) -->
| Token | Default | Use |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--date-field-label` | `text` | The labels over the boxes (4.5:1 on the surface). |
| `--date-field-text-disabled` | `disabled-text` | Disabled: the text, icon or mark, in place of fading it (3:1 or more on its background, more with more contrast). |
| `--date-field-label-size` | `text-sm` | The labels' text (14px). |
| `--date-field-gap` | `spacing-4` | Space between the boxes (16px). |
| `--date-field-label-gap` | `spacing-1` | Space between a label and its box (4px). |
| `--date-field-short-width` | `spacing-16` | The day and month boxes' width, for two digits (64px). |
| `--date-field-year-width` | `spacing-24` | The year box's width, for four digits (96px). |
| `--date-field-error-icon-size` | `spacing-4` | The error icon beside the 14px message (16px). |
<!-- token-table:end -->

components.name: DatePicker
components.summary: A date field: people type a date, or pick one from a calendar that opens under the field.
components.guide:
# DatePicker A date field: people type a date, or pick one from a calendar that opens under the field. The calendar flips above the field when there's no room below; with no room on either side (a short window, a phone held sideways) it takes the roomier side and scrolls inside, so its last week can still be reached. **Also called:** date chooser, calendar input. ```tsx import { DatePicker, Field } from "@diki-stwn/serupa-ds"; const [due, setDue] = React.useState(null); ``` ## When to use - A single, specific day the person knows or can find on a calendar: a due date, a start date, an appointment day. - Dates near today, where seeing the month helps people choose (the next delivery day, a booking in the coming weeks). - When some days can't be chosen (past days, weekends, fully booked days) and people should see that before they pick. ## When not to use - A start and an end date: use [DateRangePicker] (npx serupa-docs DateRangePicker) instead. - A date people know by heart and that's far from today, such as a date of birth: a [DateField] (npx serupa-docs DateField) (day, month and year boxes) is quicker than paging back decades. DatePicker still accepts typing, so it works, but the calendar adds nothing. - Only a month or a year: use a [Select] (npx serupa-docs Select). - A calendar that's always on the page, such as a scheduling view: use [Calendar] (npx serupa-docs Calendar) on its own. ## Anatomy Drawn from the `Disabled` story. 1. **Field** (`.srp-input__field`): where the date is typed, in the format shown in the hint. 2. **Calendar button** (`.srp-date-picker__button`): opens a calendar to choose the date instead. ## Usage - Always wrap it in [Field] (npx serupa-docs Field) with a label, and put the expected format in the `hint` ("mm/dd/yyyy") for people who type. - Set `min`, `max` or `isDateDisabled` rather than rejecting a date after it's entered: blocked days show in `disabled-text` and struck through in the calendar and a blocked typed date puts back the last good value. - Leave `locale` unset in most products so the format follows the visitor's browser. Set it only when the whole product uses one locale. - Use `name` in a plain form: it sends `yyyy-mm-dd`, whatever the display format. - Keep a day from an API or database as the plain `"yyyy-mm-dd"` string and pass it as is: `value="2026-10-24"`, and store `iso` from `onValueChange`. `new Date("2026-10-24")` is UTC midnight, which is 23 October anywhere west of Greenwich; DatePicker warns once in the console when it's given such a Date there. - Match the `size` of the other fields in the same form. ## Date and time For "when" (a meeting, a scheduled post, a delivery slot), pair DatePicker with [TimePicker] (npx serupa-docs TimePicker) in one `Field group`. It reads as one question with one legend, one hint and one error, and each part keeps its own label for screen readers. ```tsx
setDay(iso)} min={today} invalid={!!error && !day} />
``` - **Check them together,** when the form is sent: one message for the pair, in the group's `error`, naming what's missing or wrong ("Choose a time", "Pick a time after now"). Set `invalid` only on the part that's at fault, so its border says where to look, and move focus to it: a screen reader then reads the legend and the error with it. - **Say whose time it is.** The legend's hint names the zone when it isn't obvious. When people in other zones use the form (a meeting across offices), add a [TimeZonePicker] (npx serupa-docs TimeZonePicker) as a third part, defaulting to the browser's zone (`Intl.DateTimeFormat().resolvedOptions().timeZone`). - **Store the parts, not a local Date.** Keep the day (`"yyyy-mm-dd"`), the time (`"HH:mm"`) and the zone's IANA name, and let the server turn them into an instant. A `Date` built in the browser takes the browser's zone, which is wrong when the zone was chosen. - **Keep the order of the locale's sentences:** date first, then time, then zone. On a narrow screen the parts wrap onto separate lines. ## States | State | Look | | --- | --- | | Rest | `field` background, 1px `field-border`, the calendar button in `text-muted` | | Hover | `field-border-hover`; the calendar button under the pointer takes a `field-hover` fill, `field-pressed` while pressed | | Focus | Like Input: the border and a 1px ring hugging it in `focus-ring` (2px in all), and a visible outline in forced-colors mode | | Invalid | `danger` border, and a `danger` focus ring | | Read-only | `field-readonly` background, no hover change; still focusable and selectable; the calendar button is off with a plain cursor, so the calendar doesn't open | | Disabled | `field-readonly` background, `disabled-border` edge and `disabled-text` at full opacity, `not-allowed` cursor; the calendar button is off and the calendar doesn't open | ## Behavior - With `presets`, a list of shortcuts sits beside the days in the popup, after them in reading order and under them on a narrow screen. Your own take a day or a function that returns one, so "Next Monday" follows today: `presets={[{ label: "Next Monday", value: nextMonday }]}`. A shortcut whose day can't be chosen is disabled. - People type in the locale's numeric order (11/22/2025 in en-US, 22.11.2025 in de-DE) or as `2025-11-22` anywhere. Digits alone work too, as typed on a number keypad: `11222025` or `112225` in en-US, `22112025` in de-DE, or `20251122`. A two-digit year is the one within 50 years of today: in 2026, `85` is 1985 and `30` is 2030, so birth dates and deadlines both read right. A date pasted with its month as a word reads too, in the locale or in English, in full or cut short: `12 Mei 2025`, `May 12, 2025`, `12. März 2025`. - The field always uses Gregorian years and Latin digits, so a date reads back as the same day in every locale: Thai shows 22/11/2025 rather than the Buddhist year 2568, and Persian shows 2025/11/22 rather than ۱۴۰۴/۰۹/۰۱. Digits typed in another script (٢٢/١١/٢٠٢٥) are read too. The calendar's month and weekday names stay in the locale. - The text is read on blur and on Enter. A date that can't be read, or one that can't be chosen, puts back the last good value. An empty field clears it. Switching to another window or browser tab isn't leaving the field: the text waits until people come back. - A press anywhere on the box, on its side padding or past the calendar button, focuses the field with the caret at the end, as the text cursor over the box promises. - The calendar opens from the button or Alt+↓ in the field, showing the typed or chosen month with focus on that day. Picking a day or Escape closes it and returns focus to the field. A click outside or Tab past the calendar closes it too, leaving focus where it went. On a touch screen, a finger that starts a scroll outside leaves it open; a tap outside closes it. ### Do and don't - **Do:** Wrap it in a [Field] (npx serupa-docs Field) with a label, and put the format in the `hint` for people who type. (`DoLabelAndFormat`) - **Don't:** Show it with no label or format: people can't tell what the date is for or how to type it. (`DontBareField`) ## Accessibility - The calendar fades and grows in out of the field over 150ms, and fades and shrinks back over 100ms when it closes; with `prefers-reduced-motion` it only fades. The motion is a transition, so closing it while it opens turns back from where it is. The calendar stays while it fades out, inert, and focus goes back to the field at once. Firefox and Safari can't keep a closing popup in the top layer yet, so there it closes at once. From the keyboard there is no motion: opened by Alt+ArrowDown or Enter on the calendar button it is there at once, and Escape takes it away at once. - **Role and name:** the field is a text input; label it with Field, `

components.name: DateRangePicker
components.summary: Two date fields for the start and end of a range (a stay, a report period, a filter), with a popup of two months to pick both.
components.guide:
# DateRangePicker

Two date fields for the start and end of a range (a stay, a report period, a filter), with a popup of two months to pick both.

**Also called:** range picker, date range input.

```tsx
import { DateRangePicker, Field, type DateRange } from "@diki-stwn/serupa-ds";

const [stay, setStay] = React.useState<DateRange>({ start: null, end: null });
<Field label="Stay" hint="mm/dd/yyyy">
  <DateRangePicker value={stay} onValueChange={setStay} min={new Date()} startName="check_in" endName="check_out" />
</Field>
```

## When to use

- A period with a start and an end day: a hotel stay, a leave request, a booking.
- Filtering a report or a list to the days between two dates.
- When people benefit from seeing the whole range on the calendar while they pick it.

## When not to use

- A single day: use [DatePicker] (npx serupa-docs DatePicker) instead.
- A fixed period such as "Last 7 days" or "This month": use a [Select] (npx serupa-docs Select) or a [SegmentedControl] (npx serupa-docs SegmentedControl) of presets instead.
- A time of day as well as the dates: pair the fields with [TimePicker] (npx serupa-docs TimePicker); DateRangePicker holds days only.

## Anatomy

Drawn from the `Disabled` story.

1. **Start date** (`.srp-date-range-picker__field`): the first day, typed or chosen.
2. **Dash** (`.srp-date-range-picker__dash`): between the two dates.
3. **Calendar button** (`.srp-date-range-picker__button`): opens two months to choose both days.

## Usage

- Wrap it in [Field] (npx serupa-docs Field) with one label for the range, and put the expected format in the `hint`. Field's `id` goes to the start field.
- Set `startLabel` and `endLabel` to fit the task ("Check-in", "Check-out") so each field has a clear name.
- Use `min`, `max` and `isDateDisabled` to block days rather than rejecting a range afterwards. Blocked days can't be an end but can sit inside a range, so check for them yourself if a range must not cross them.
- In narrow places, such as a side panel, set `months={1}`. Two months stack below 640px anyway, and the popup is then one month wide, 8px clear of both sides of the screen.
- In a plain form, use `startName` and `endName`: each end is sent as `yyyy-mm-dd`.

## States

| State | Look |
| --- | --- |
| Rest | `field` background, 1px `field-border`, the calendar button in `text-muted` |
| Hover | `field-border-hover`; the calendar button under the pointer takes a `field-hover` fill, `field-pressed` while pressed |
| Focus | Like Input: the border and a 1px ring hugging it in `focus-ring` (2px in all), and a visible outline in forced-colors mode |
| Invalid | `danger` border, and a `danger` focus ring |
| Read-only | `field-readonly` background, no hover change; still focusable and selectable; the calendar button is off with a plain cursor, so the calendar doesn't open |
| Disabled | `field-readonly` background, `disabled-border` edge and `disabled-text` at full opacity, `not-allowed` cursor; the calendar button is off and the calendar doesn't open |

## Behavior

- With `presets`, a list of shortcuts sits beside the months in the popup (under them on a narrow screen). Picking one sets both ends and shows the range in the months, and the popup stays open so people can see what they got or change an end. The one the range matches is pressed. "Last 7 days" and "Last 30 days" end today; "This month" and "Last month" run from the first day to the last. Your own take a range or a function that returns one: `{ label: "This quarter", value: () => quarterOf(new Date()) }`. A shortcut with an end that can't be chosen is disabled.
- In the popup, the first pick is the start and the second the end; a day before the start moves the start instead. Pointing at days previews the range. The popup closes once both ends are set, on Escape, on a click outside and when Tab moves focus past it. A finger that starts a scroll outside leaves it open.
- Opening it with only a start asks for the end.
- Each field reads typed text on blur and Enter, like DatePicker. Text that can't be used puts back the last good day, and a typed start after the end clears the end. Switching to another window or browser tab isn't leaving the field: the text waits until people come back.

### Do and don't

- **Do:** Wrap it in a [Field] (npx serupa-docs Field) with one label and the format in the `hint`, and name the ends for the task ("Check-in", "Check-out"). (`DoNameEnds`)
- **Don't:** Show a bare range: people can't tell what the dates are for or how to type them. (`DontBareRange`)

## Accessibility

- The calendar fades and grows in out of the field over 150ms, and fades and shrinks back over 100ms when it closes; with `prefers-reduced-motion` it only fades. The motion is a transition, so closing it while it opens turns back from where it is. The calendar stays while it fades out, inert, and focus goes back to the field at once. Firefox and Safari can't keep a closing popup in the top layer yet, so there it closes at once. From the keyboard there is no motion: opened by Alt+ArrowDown or Enter on the calendar button it is there at once, and Escape takes it away at once.
- The box is a `role="group"`; name it with `aria-label` when it has no Field. Each field has its own name.
- The popup is a `role="dialog"` holding one or two Calendars (see Calendar's keyboard table); a polite live line says which end to pick next.
- Each field's description ends with the format to type ("Format: mm/dd/yyyy"), after a Field hint, so it's heard once the placeholder is gone (the `formatHint` label).
- Days in a range, the status line and the dash keep 4.5:1 in every theme (`DateRangePicker.test.tsx`).

### Keyboard

| Key | Does |
| --- | --- |
| Tab | The start field, the end field, then the calendar button |
| Enter | In a field, reads the date typed |
| Alt+Down | In a field, opens the calendar |
| Enter / Space | On the calendar button, opens the calendar; in it, Calendar's keys pick the start, then the end |
| Arrow keys, PageUp, PageDown | In the calendar, Calendar's moves; with two months, crossing into the month the other grid shows moves focus there, and the months stay put |
| Escape | Closes the calendar and returns focus to the start field, as DatePicker returns it to its field |

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `value` / `defaultValue` | `{ start: Date \| string \| null; end: Date \| string \| null }` | | The range, controlled or not. Each end a Date or a plain `"yyyy-mm-dd"` string for that local day (`new Date("2026-10-24")` is UTC midnight, the day before west of Greenwich, and gets a console warning there). |
| `onValueChange` | `(range: DateRange, details: { iso: { start, end } }) => void` | | Called whenever either end changes, so also after the first pick (with `end: null`). `details.iso` is the same range as `"yyyy-mm-dd"` strings, to store or pass back as `value`. |
| `onInvalidInput` | `(text, reason) => void` | | Called when text typed in either field is put back: `"unreadable"` (not a date) or `"unavailable"` (outside `min`..`max`, disabled, or an end before the start). Screen readers also hear that it wasn't accepted (`inputNotAccepted`). The same words show under the field (`.srp-input-rejected`, read with it) until the text changes. |
| `min`, `max` | `Date \| string` | | Days outside can't be either end. A Date or `"yyyy-mm-dd"`. |
| `isDateDisabled` | `(date: Date) => boolean` | | Days that can't be an end. They can sit inside a range. |
| `months` | `1 \| 2` | `2` | Months side by side in the popup (stacked below 640px). |
| `locale`, `weekStartsOn`, `weekNumbers` | | the browser's | As in DatePicker. The calendars carry `lang` when it differs from the provider's; the two fields keep the page's, as their names do. |
| `calendar` | as Calendar's | `'gregory'` | The calendar system the popup's months follow, as in DatePicker. The typed dates stay Gregorian. |
| `size`, `invalid`, `disabled`, `readOnly` | | | Like Input. |
| `required` | `boolean` | `false` | Both fields are required (and `aria-required`), so a form won't submit until each end has a date. Field's `required` sets `aria-required` on both. |
| `id` | `string` | | The start field's id, so Field or `<label htmlFor>` focuses it. |
| `startLabel`, `endLabel` | `string` | `"Start date"`, `"End date"` | The fields' names. |
| `startName`, `endName` | `string` | | Hidden inputs that send each end as `yyyy-mm-dd`. |
| `form` | `string` | | The id of a form it sits outside of: both fields and both hidden inputs belong to that form, and reset with it. |
| `buttonLabel` | `string` | `"Choose dates"` | The calendar button's name, and the popup's. |
| `presets` | `boolean \| DateRangePreset[]` | | Shortcuts beside the months: `true` for Today, Yesterday, Last 7 days, Last 30 days, This month and Last month (with a `max` inside this month, This month ends at `max`, the month so far), or your own `{ label, value: { start, end } }`. |
| `open` | `boolean` | | Whether the calendar popup shows (controlled), with `onOpenChange`. Opened this way, focus stays where it is. |
| `defaultOpen` | `boolean` | `false` | Shows the popup at first, without moving focus into it. |
| `onOpenChange` | `(open, { reason }) => void` | | Called when the popup asks to open or close, and why. |

`className`, `ref`, `aria-label` and other props go to the box (`role="group"`); `aria-describedby` and `aria-required` (which Field passes) go to both fields. Its `focus()` and `autoFocus` move focus to the start field, so a form library that focuses the first invalid field after a failed submit lands on it.

## Component tokens

Each is an optional override: set it on the page, a container or one picker. The list lives in `src/components/DateRangePicker/date-range-picker.tokens.json` (also in `design-tokens/components/`).

<!-- token-table:start (made from date-range-picker.tokens.json by npm run tokens: edit the descriptions there) -->
| Token | Default | Use |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--date-range-picker-dash` | `placeholder` | The dash between the two fields. |
| `--date-range-picker-status-color` | `text-muted` | "Choose the start date" under the months (4.5:1 on surface). |
| `--date-range-picker-months-gap` | `spacing-6` | Space between the two months (24px). |
| `--date-range-picker-field-width` | `spacing-24` | Each field's width (96px), enough for a full date. |
<!-- token-table:end -->

It uses Input's box, DatePicker's button and popup (`--date-picker-*` tokens), and Calendar's days (`--calendar-*`, with `--calendar-range-bg` and `--calendar-range-color` for the days between).

components.name: DescriptionList
components.summary: A list of terms and their details: a record's fields on a detail page, an order's subtotal and total, a dialog of keyboard shortcuts.
components.guide:
# DescriptionList

A list of terms and their details: a record's fields on a detail page, an order's subtotal and total, a dialog of keyboard shortcuts. It is a real `<dl>`, so screen readers announce a list and pair each term with its details, and it lays them out three ways, with long values wrapping and every side mirrored in right-to-left.

**Also called:** key-value list, definition list, property list.

```tsx
import { DescriptionList, DescriptionItem } from "@diki-stwn/serupa-ds";

<DescriptionList>
  <DescriptionItem term="Owner">Ayu Lestari</DescriptionItem>
  <DescriptionItem term="Created"><time dateTime="2026-03-14">14 March 2026</time></DescriptionItem>
</DescriptionList>

<DescriptionList layout="split" dividers>
  <DescriptionItem term="Subtotal">Rp 240.000</DescriptionItem>
  <DescriptionItem term="Total" emphasis>Rp 240.000</DescriptionItem>
</DescriptionList>
```

## When to use

- Read-only fields of one thing: a project's owner and dates, a customer's contact details, an invoice's terms.
- Label and value pairs in a summary: totals in a cart or checkout, the settings a plan includes.
- Inline editing inside a value: put [InlineEdit] (npx serupa-docs InlineEdit) in the details.

## When not to use

- Many records with the same fields, to compare: use [Table] (npx serupa-docs Table).
- Fields a person fills in: use [Field] (npx serupa-docs Field) with its inputs.

## Anatomy

Drawn from the `Default` story.

1. **List** (`.srp-description-list`): the `<dl>`, a term beside its details from 480px wide, under it when narrower.
2. **Item** (`.srp-description-list__item`): one term and its details, in a `<div>`.
3. **Term** (`.srp-description-list__term`): the `<dt>`, what the value is, muted and medium weight.
4. **Details** (`.srp-description-list__details`): the `<dd>`, the value itself.

## Usage

- **Layouts:** `inline` (default) puts the term in a column a third of the list wide, beside its details, and stacks them when the list is under 480px wide (a container query, so a list in a narrow card stacks on a wide screen too). `stacked` always puts the term above. `split` puts the details at the end of the term's row, in tabular figures, and moves them under it when both don't fit: totals, settings, shortcuts.
- **Dividers:** `dividers` draws a hairline between items, with the item gap above and below each.
- **Emphasis:** `emphasis` on an item makes it larger and semibold: the total under the subtotals.
- **Long values** wrap anywhere, so a long URL or a long word doesn't widen the list or the page.
- **Text size** follows the surrounding text: put the list in `text-sm` for a compact summary.
- Write terms as short nouns ("Owner", not "The owner of this project is"). Show an empty value as a dash or "Not set", never as nothing, so the term isn't left alone.

### Loading and failed

- **Loading:** show the terms, which you already know, and a [Skeleton] (npx serupa-docs Skeleton) in each item's details, with `aria-busy` on the list. Pick the Skeleton's `size` by the list's text size (`sm` for `text-xs`, `md` for `text-sm`, `lg` for `text-base`): each skeleton line is as tall as a line of that text, so the rows don't move when the details arrive. Give the first Skeleton a `label` ("Loading order") and the others `label=""`: a screen reader hears the wait once, after the skeleton's delay, and a quick load says nothing.
- **Failed:** in place of the list, a danger [Alert] (npx serupa-docs Alert) that says what didn't load and offers Retry in `actions`. It's `role="alert"`, so the failure is heard as it appears. On Retry, go back to loading.

```tsx
{state === 'failed' ? <Alert tone="danger" actions={<Button size="sm" onClick={load}>Retry</Button>}>The order didn't load.</Alert>
  : <DescriptionList aria-busy={state === 'loading' || undefined}>
      {FIELDS.map((f, i) => (
        <DescriptionItem key={f.key} term={f.term}>
          {state === 'loading' ? <Skeleton size="md" label={i === 0 ? 'Loading order' : ''} /> : order[f.key]}
        </DescriptionItem>
      ))}
    </DescriptionList>}
```

### Do and don't

- **Do:** Use `emphasis` on the one item people look for, such as the total. (`DoEmphasizeOne`)
- **Don't:** Emphasize every item: nothing stands out. (`DontEmphasizeAll`)

## Accessibility

- **Role and name:** a `<dl>` with `<dt>` terms and `<dd>` details; each pair is wrapped in a `<div>`, which HTML allows in a `<dl>`. Give the list a heading before it, or `aria-label`, when the page has several.
- **Keyboard:** nothing of its own to focus; links and controls in the details are in the Tab order as usual.
- **Contrast:** terms and details read 4.5:1 on the page in every theme (`DescriptionList.test.tsx`).
- **Right to left:** every side is logical, so the term column and the split details mirror.
- **What's still yours:** terms that make sense on their own, and a text value for anything shown only as an icon or color.

## Props

### DescriptionList

| Prop | Type | Default | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `layout` | `'inline'` \| `'stacked'` \| `'split'` | `'inline'` | How a term sits beside its details |
| `dividers` | `boolean` | `false` | A hairline between items |
| `children` | `ReactNode` | | DescriptionItem elements |
| `id` | string | none | Goes to the `<dl>`. |

`className`, `ref` and other props go to the `<dl>`.

### DescriptionItem

| Prop | Type | Default | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `term` | `ReactNode` | | The term, in the `<dt>` |
| `children` | `ReactNode` | | The details, in the `<dd>` |
| `emphasis` | `boolean` | `false` | A larger, semibold row, such as a total |

`className`, `ref` and other props go to the item's `<div>`.

## Component tokens

Each is an optional override: set it on the page, a container or one DescriptionList. The list lives in `src/components/DescriptionList/description-list.tokens.json` (also in `design-tokens/components/`).

<!-- token-table:start (made from description-list.tokens.json by npm run tokens: edit the descriptions there) -->
| Token | Default | Use |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--description-list-text` | `text` | The list's text. |
| `--description-list-term` | `text` | The terms (4.5:1 on surface). |
| `--description-list-details` | `text` | The details (4.5:1 on surface). |
| `--description-list-divider` | `border` | The hairline between items with dividers. |
| `--description-list-term-weight` | `font-medium` | The terms' weight in inline and stacked (500). |
| `--description-list-gap` | `spacing-3` | Space between items, and above and below each with dividers (12px). |
| `--description-list-term-gap` | `spacing-1` | Space between a term and its details when stacked (4px). |
| `--description-list-column-gap` | `spacing-6` | Space between the term and details columns in inline and split (24px). |
<!-- token-table:end -->

components.name: Dialog
components.summary: A modal window over a dimmed page, for a task or a decision that needs attention before people go on: inviting someone, confirming a delete, editing a few fields.
components.guide:
# Dialog

A modal window over a dimmed page, for a task or a decision that needs attention before people go on: inviting someone, confirming a delete, editing a few fields. It's built on the native `<dialog>`, so the browser keeps focus inside it, makes the page behind unreachable, and puts it above everything.

**Also called:** modal, modal window, popup.

```jsx
import { Dialog, Button, Input, Field } from '@diki-stwn/serupa-ds';

const [open, setOpen] = React.useState(false);

<Button onClick={() => setOpen(true)}>Invite people</Button>
<Dialog open={open} onOpenChange={setOpen} title="Invite people" description="They'll get an email with a link."
  footer={<><Button variant="secondary" onClick={() => setOpen(false)}>Cancel</Button><Button onClick={send}>Send invite</Button></>}>
  <Field label="Email"><Input type="email" /></Field>
</Dialog>

// a confirmation
<Dialog alert size="sm" open={confirm} onOpenChange={setConfirm} title="Delete Atlas?" description="This can't be undone."
  footer={<><Button variant="secondary" onClick={() => setConfirm(false)}>Keep</Button><Button destructive onClick={remove}>Delete</Button></>} />
```

## When to use

- A short task that needs people's full attention before they go back to the page: inviting someone, renaming an item, editing a few fields.
- Confirming an action that can't be undone, such as a delete (with `alert`).
- A decision the product can't go on without.

## When not to use

- A long form, filters, or details people check while looking at the page: use a [Drawer] (npx serupa-docs Drawer) instead.
- A few controls or details next to the button that opens them, where the page should stay usable: use a [Popover] (npx serupa-docs Popover) instead.
- A confirmation that something happened: use a [Toast] (npx serupa-docs Toast) instead.
- A message about the page that doesn't need an answer: use an [Alert] (npx serupa-docs Alert) instead.

## Anatomy

Drawn from the `FullScreen` story.

1. **Panel** (`.srp-dialog__panel`): the box over the dimmed page; focus stays inside while it's open.
2. **Title** (`.srp-dialog__title`): what the dialog is for; it names the dialog for screen readers.
3. **Description** (`.srp-dialog__description`): an optional line under the title.
4. **Close** (`.srp-dialog__close`): closes it, as Escape does.
5. **Body** (`.srp-dialog__body`): the content; it scrolls when it's taller than the screen.
6. **Footer** (`.srp-dialog__footer`): the actions, the main one last.

## Usage

- Use a `title` that says what the dialog is for; for a confirmation, ask the question: "Delete Atlas?".
- Name the buttons in `footer` after what they do ("Delete", "Keep"), not "OK" and "Cancel" alone, and put the main action last.
- Use `alert` only for decisions people must make. It hides the × and stops a backdrop click from closing it.
- Keep the body short. Pick `size="sm"` for a confirmation and `lg` only when the content needs the width.
- For a long form on a phone, use `fullScreen="mobile"`. Under 640px the panel fills the screen with square corners, and the footer sits at the bottom, clear of the home bar.
- For a form in the dialog, give the form an `id` and make the main button in `footer` its submit button with `form`, so Enter in a field submits it as it would on a page. The footer sits outside the form, and without it, Enter in a dialog with more than one field does nothing. On a failed submit, move focus to the first field with an error (or an ErrorSummary for a long form), as a page does:

```tsx
<Dialog open={open} onOpenChange={setOpen} title="New project"
  footer={<><Button variant="secondary" onClick={() => setOpen(false)}>Cancel</Button><Button type="submit" form="new-project">Create project</Button></>}>
  <form id="new-project" onSubmit={(e) => { e.preventDefault(); if (!name.trim()) { setError("Enter a project name"); nameRef.current?.focus(); return; } create(name); }}>
    <Field label="Project name" required error={error}><Input ref={nameRef} value={name} onChange={(e) => setName(e.target.value)} /></Field>
  </form>
</Dialog>
```

- Keep it outside any `<form>`. The panel renders where it's placed, so inside a form its own form nests in the page's (Enter reloads the page) and Enter in its field submits the page's form. Place it after the form; a field that belongs to the page's form can say so with the `form` attribute. In development it warns (`overlay-in-form`).

### Do and don't

- **Do:** Ask the question in the title, and name the buttons for what they do: "Delete Atlas?", with Keep project and Delete project. (`DoAskTheQuestion`)
- **Don't:** Ask "Are you sure?" with OK and Cancel: people have to read the rest to learn what OK does. (`DontAreYouSure`)
- **Do:** Put the main action last in `footer`, where reading ends. (`DoMainActionLast`)
- **Don't:** Put it first: people pass it on the way to Cancel, and the order differs from every other dialog. (`DontMainActionFirst`)

## Behavior

- Opening moves focus to the first thing in it that takes focus. To choose another, pass its ref as `initialFocus` (Cancel in a confirmation, so Enter doesn't delete), or put `data-autofocus` on it (React's `autoFocus` runs while the dialog is still hidden, so it can't). Closing moves focus back to where it was. When closing takes that away (a confirmation that deletes the row it was opened from), pass `finalFocus`, such as the next row or the list's heading, so focus doesn't fall to the top of the page.
- A body taller than the screen takes Tab focus (with a focus ring) when it scrolls, so the arrow keys and Page Down scroll it in every browser, even with nothing focusable inside. It's a region named by the title.
- On a screen under 480px tall, such as a laptop at 400% zoom, the whole panel scrolls instead of the body, so the header and footer can't squeeze the body away or push the buttons off screen. Focusing a button scrolls it into view (WCAG 1.4.10 and 2.4.11).
- Tab and Shift+Tab stay inside. The page behind can't be clicked or reached, and doesn't scroll. It doesn't shift either: with classic scrollbars (Windows, Linux) the page keeps the scrollbar's space while it's hidden (`tools/test/scroll-lock.mjs`).
- It enters as a sequence: the backdrop fades in, and 50ms later (`motion-sequence`) the panel fades and grows in over 200ms. It fades and shrinks out over 150ms with the backdrop, both in place at the center; with `prefers-reduced-motion` it only fades. The motion is a transition, so closing it while it opens turns back from where it is. Focus goes back to what opened it at once, not after the fade, and presses reach the page while it fades. One open on arrival (`defaultOpen`, or `open` on the first render) is there from the first frame. Firefox and Safari can't keep a closing dialog in the top layer yet, so there it closes at once.
- On Android, the system back gesture asks to close it, the same as Escape. The browser sends it as the native `<dialog>`'s `cancel` event, so the page doesn't navigate away.
- Without `open`, it keeps its own state: `defaultOpen` shows it on arrival, and Escape, the × or the backdrop close it by themselves (`onOpenChange(false)` still comes).
- With `unsaved`, Escape, the ×, the backdrop or the browser closing it first ask "Discard changes?" in a small alert dialog on top, with Keep editing focused. Keep editing (or Escape) goes back to the form as it was; Discard closes both, and only then does `onOpenChange(false)` come, with the reason of the first request. Leaving or reloading the page while it's open asks too (the browser's own `beforeunload` question). Set it from your form's state (`unsaved={name !== saved.name}`), and back to `false` once saved. Your own Cancel button sets `open` itself, so it closes without asking.
- To keep it open for some other reason, leave `open` true when `onOpenChange(false)` comes. Chromium closes a modal dialog itself on a second Escape with no click in between; the component shows it again, so `open` stays the truth.
- Under `<React.StrictMode>`, a Dialog that is open on its first render stays the innermost modal, so toasts and announcements still move into it.

## Accessibility

- `aria-modal`, named by the title (`aria-labelledby`) and described by the description. Without a title, give it an `aria-label`.
- Use `alert` only for decisions people must make; Escape still cancels.
- Stacked: a Dialog or Drawer opened from inside another takes focus, and Escape, its × and its backdrop close only it. The next Escape closes the one underneath.
- A press on the backdrop while a Menu, Popover or other popup is open inside only closes the popup. The next one closes the dialog.
- The title and description keep 4.5:1 on the panel in every theme (`Dialog.test.tsx`). In forced-colors mode the panel gets a border.

### Keyboard

| Key | Does |
| --- | --- |
| Tab / Shift+Tab | Between the controls in the dialog; the page behind is inert, so focus stays inside |
| Escape | Asks to close it (`onOpenChange(false)`), in an `alert` dialog too; in stacked dialogs, only the top one. With `unsaved`, it asks "Discard changes?" first, and Escape there keeps editing |
| Enter / Space | On the ×, the same as Escape |

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | string | none | Goes to the root `<dialog>`. Point a Button's `commandfor` at it. |
| `open` | boolean | | Whether it's open (controlled) |
| `defaultOpen` | boolean | `false` | Open at first, then it closes itself (uncontrolled), for a dialog shown on arrival |
| `onOpenChange` | `(open, { reason }) => void` | | Called with `false` on Escape, the ×, or a click on the backdrop. Close it by setting `open`. `reason` says which: `'escape'`, `'close'` (the ×), `'outside'` (the backdrop) or `'api'` (the browser closed it, as `dialog.close()` or a `method="dialog"` form do) |
| `title` | node | | The heading (`text-lg`, `font-semibold`), which also names the dialog |
| `description` | node | | A muted line under the title, read when it opens |
| `footer` | node | | Buttons at the end, the main action last |
| `size` | `'sm'` \| `'md'` \| `'lg'` | `'md'` | 384, 512 or 672px wide; never more than the screen less 16px a side |
| `alert` | boolean | `false` | `role="alertdialog"` for a decision: no ×, and the backdrop doesn't close it |
| `closeButton` | boolean | `true` (`false` for alert) | The × in the corner |
| `closeLabel` | string | `'Close'` | The ×'s name |
| `closeOnBackdrop` | boolean | `true` (`false` for alert) | Whether a click on the dimmed page closes it |
| `fullScreen` | boolean \| `'mobile'` | `false` | Fills the screen: `true` always, or `'mobile'` under 640px wide. Square corners, no shadow, the body takes the free height, and the padding clears the notch and home bar |
| `initialFocus` | `RefObject<HTMLElement>` | | The element that takes focus when it opens, instead of the first that can. A ref to something outside the dialog is ignored |
| `finalFocus` | `RefObject<HTMLElement>` | | Where focus goes when it closes, instead of back to the opener. Used when it's on the page then; otherwise focus goes back to the opener |
| `unsaved` | boolean | `false` | There are changes that would be lost: closing asks "Discard changes?" first (Keep editing or Discard), and leaving the page asks too. `onOpenChange(false)` comes after Discard |

`children` is the body, which scrolls when it's taller than the screen. `className`, `style`, `ref` and everything else go to the `<dialog>`, which has `data-component="dialog"` and `data-size`.

## useUnsavedChanges(unsaved)

The same "Discard changes?" question, for a form or a page that isn't in a Dialog: a settings page, an editor.

```tsx
import { useUnsavedChanges } from "@diki-stwn/serupa-ds";

const guard = useUnsavedChanges(name !== saved.name);
// before moving away inside the app (a Cancel button, your router's blocker):
if (await guard.confirm()) navigate("/projects");
// …and somewhere in the form:
{guard.dialog}
```

- While `unsaved` is true, leaving or reloading the page asks the browser's own question (`beforeunload`), as an unsaved Dialog does.
- Moving away inside the app goes through your router, so ask first: `await confirm()` is `true` at once when nothing is unsaved. Otherwise it asks "Discard changes?" in a small alert dialog, with Keep editing focused. It's `true` on Discard, and `false` on Keep editing or Escape, and focus goes back to where it was. With React Router, call it when `useBlocker` blocks: `confirm().then((ok) => (ok ? blocker.proceed() : blocker.reset()))`.
- Render `dialog` inside the form's tree, so it's there while there are changes.
- A newer `confirm()` answers the one before it with `false`. Saving while the question shows (`unsaved` back to `false`) answers it with `true`, and unmounting answers it with `false`.

| Returns | Type | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `confirm` | `() => Promise<boolean>` | Asks "Discard changes?" when there are changes, and says whether to go on. |
| `dialog` | `ReactElement \| null` | The question; render it in the form. |

## Component tokens

Each is an optional override: set it on the page, a container or one dialog. The list lives in `src/components/Dialog/dialog.tokens.json` (also in `design-tokens/components/`).

<!-- token-table:start (made from dialog.tokens.json by npm run tokens: edit the descriptions there) -->
| Token | Default | Use |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--dialog-row-bg-hover` | `surface-hover-raised` | A List or InlineEdit row in the dialog, hovered or selected: a step up from its surface in dark |
| `--dialog-field-bg` | `field-raised` | The fill of a form field in the dialog: a step up from its surface in dark, so the field stands out from it |
| `--dialog-bg` | `surface-overlay` | The panel's background. |

components.name: Divider
components.summary: A 1px line between content, horizontal or vertical, with an optional label in the middle such as "or".
components.guide:
# Divider A 1px line between content, horizontal or vertical, with an optional label in the middle such as "or". **Also called:** separator, horizontal rule, vertical rule. ```jsx import { Divider, Stack } from '@diki-stwn/serupa-ds'; EditShare ``` ## When to use - Separating groups of content where space alone doesn't make the break clear. - Two ways to do the same thing, with "or" between them, such as signing in with a password or with a provider. - Separating items in a row, such as links or actions, with a vertical line. ## When not to use - When space between groups is enough: use the gap of a [Stack] (npx serupa-docs Stack) instead. - Lines between the rows of a list: use [List] (npx serupa-docs List), which has them (`divided`). - Setting a group of content apart in a box: use [Card] (npx serupa-docs Card) instead. ## Anatomy Drawn from the `LongLabel` story. 1. **Line** (`.srp-divider`): separates two groups of content. 2. **Label** (`.srp-divider__label`): optional words in the line that name the group after it. ## Usage - It has no margins: put it in a [Stack] (npx serupa-docs Stack) or give the space around it with the layout. - Keep a label to a word or two, such as "or". - A vertical divider takes the height of the row it's in, so put it in a row, such as ``. - Use `decorative` when the groups are already clear without it. ### Do and don't - **Do:** Keep a label to a word or two, such as "or". (`WithLabel`) - **Don't:** Write a sentence as the label: it reads as a heading squeezed into a line. (`DontSentenceLabel`) ## Accessibility - It's a separator to screen readers (an `
`, or `role="separator"` with `aria-orientation`). When it only decorates, such as between items that are already grouped, use `decorative`. - A separator's content isn't read, so a text `label` becomes its `aria-label` (your own `aria-label` wins). A label that isn't text, such as a heading, stays ordinary content and the divider drops the separator role, leaving the lines as decoration. - The label keeps 4.5:1 on `surface` in every theme (`Divider.test.tsx`). The line itself is decoration, so it doesn't need 3:1. - In Windows high-contrast mode the line uses the text color. - **Keyboard:** none: it isn't focusable. ## Props | Prop | Type | Default | What it does | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `id` | string | none | Goes to the root `
`. | | `orientation` | `'horizontal'` \| `'vertical'` | `'horizontal'` | Across the full width, or the height of the row it's in | | `label` | node | none | Text in the middle of a horizontal line. A vertical divider has no label | | `decorative` | boolean | `false` | Leaves it out of the accessibility tree | | `surface` | `'dark'` \| `'light'` | none | Over a photo or a colored panel: a white line and label for dark media, black for light | Without a label, a horizontal divider is an `
`; otherwise a `
`. It has no margins: space it with the layout around it. `className`, `style`, `ref` and everything else go to the element, which has `data-component="divider"`. ## Component tokens Each is an optional override: set it on the page, a container or one element. The list lives in `src/components/Divider/divider.tokens.json` (also in `design-tokens/components/`). | Token | Default | Use | | --- | --- | --- | | `--divider-color` | `border` | The line. | | `--divider-label-color` | `text-muted` | A label in the line (4.5:1 on surface). | | `--divider-on-dark` | `white` | surface="dark": the label, and the line at half strength, over dark media. | | `--divider-on-light` | `black` | surface="light": the label, and the line at half strength, over light media. | | `--divider-width` | `border-width-1` | The line's thickness (1px). | | `--divider-label-gap` | `spacing-3` | Space on each side of a label (12px). |

components.name: Drawer
components.summary: A modal panel that slides in from an edge of the screen: navigation on small screens, filters, or details and edits without leaving the page.
components.guide:
# Drawer

A modal panel that slides in from an edge of the screen: navigation on small screens, filters, or details and edits without leaving the page. For a short question or form, use Dialog; for something people keep open while they work, put it in the page.

**Also called:** sheet, tray, flyout, side panel.

```tsx
import { Drawer, Button } from "@diki-stwn/serupa-ds";

const [open, setOpen] = React.useState(false);
<Button onClick={() => setOpen(true)}>Filters</Button>
<Drawer open={open} onOpenChange={setOpen} title="Filters" description="Narrow the list."
  footer={<><Button variant="secondary" onClick={() => setOpen(false)}>Reset</Button><Button onClick={() => setOpen(false)}>Apply</Button></>}>
  …
</Drawer>
```

## When to use

- Navigation on small screens, where a [Sidebar] (npx serupa-docs Sidebar) doesn't fit.
- Filters for a list or a table, which people set and then apply.
- Viewing or editing one item's details without leaving the page, such as a row in a table.

## When not to use

- A short question or form: use a [Dialog] (npx serupa-docs Dialog) instead.
- Something people keep open while they work: put it in the page instead, such as a [Sidebar] (npx serupa-docs Sidebar), or use `modal={false}` for a side panel that leaves the page usable.
- A few controls next to the button that opens them: use a [Popover] (npx serupa-docs Popover) instead.

## Anatomy

Drawn from the `Bottom` story.

1. **Panel** (`.srp-drawer__panel`): slides in from an edge over the dimmed page; focus stays inside while it's open.
2. **Title** (`.srp-drawer__title`): what the drawer is for; it names it for screen readers.
3. **Description** (`.srp-drawer__description`): an optional line under the title.
4. **Close** (`.srp-drawer__close`): closes it, as Escape does.
5. **Body** (`.srp-drawer__body`): the content; it scrolls on its own.
6. **Footer** (`.srp-drawer__footer`): the actions, kept in view.

## Usage

- Use `placement="end"` (the default) for details and filters, and `placement="start"` for navigation; both follow the reading direction, so a right-to-left page gets them mirrored. Use `bottom` for short sheets on small screens.
- Give it a `title` that names what's inside ("Filters", "Order #1042").
- Put the actions in `footer` so they stay in view, with the main action last.
- Set `closeOnBackdrop={false}` when closing would lose work, such as unsaved edits.
- For a sheet people pull up for more, as on a map or a music player, give a bottom drawer `snapPoints`: the heights it stops at, as shares of the screen from the shortest (`[0.4, 0.9]`). It opens at the shortest (or `defaultSnap`); `snap` and `onSnapChange` control it.
- Set `modal={false}` for a panel people use alongside the page, such as an item's details next to a list they keep clicking through.
- Keep it outside any `<form>`. The panel renders where it's placed, so inside a form its own form nests in the page's (Enter reloads the page) and Enter in its field submits the page's form. Place it after the form; a field that belongs to the page's form can say so with the `form` attribute. In development it warns (`overlay-in-form`).

## Behavior

- It's a native `<dialog>` opened with `showModal()`, like Dialog. Focus moves inside and stays there, the page behind can't be reached and doesn't scroll (or shift sideways when a classic scrollbar goes away), and closing moves focus back to where it was. Focus goes to the first thing that takes it; pass another's ref as `initialFocus`, or put `data-autofocus` on it, to choose. When closing takes away what opened it (a panel that deletes its row), pass `finalFocus`, such as the next row, so focus doesn't fall to the top of the page. A backdrop press while a popup is open inside closes only the popup.
- On a touch screen, dragging it toward its edge closes it (`reason: 'swipe'`): past a third of its size, or where it's heading with the speed it's let go at (it carries on as a scroll would, so a slow drag still moving toward the edge counts), or with a flick (as little as 0.2px per ms over the last 100ms, so a gentle one counts); a shorter drag that has stopped springs back. Dragged the other way, away from its edge, it gives a little (24px at most) against growing resistance and springs back, with its background filling the edge behind it. Left and right drawers can be dragged anywhere outside a field, and top and bottom ones by the header or footer, so the body still scrolls. `swipeToClose={false}` turns it off; a sheet with `snapPoints` can still be dragged between its stops.
- With `snapPoints`, a handle sits at the top of the sheet. A press on it goes to the next stop, and from the tallest back to the shortest; its name says which ("Expand", "Collapse"), so it works from the keyboard and for people who can't drag. A touch drag on the handle or the header follows the finger by the sheet's height, past the tallest stop with growing resistance, and let go it carries on to the stop nearest where its speed would take it. Dragged below the shortest stop, it slides down instead, and a flick or a third of its height closes it; a fast drag down from a taller stop stops at the shortest. The sheet's height is its stop's share of the screen, so it follows the screen as it turns. Reduced motion: it changes height at once.
- With `modal={false}` it's opened with `show()` instead: no backdrop, the page stays usable and scrolls, focus moves inside but can leave it, and it isn't on the modal stack. Escape with focus inside it and the × close it; closing, or taking it off the page, moves focus back only if focus was still inside.
- Start and end drawers are full height. Top and bottom drawers are full width, as tall as their content up to the screen less 64px, and rounded on the open side.
- The body scrolls on its own, so the header and footer stay in view. While it scrolls it takes Tab focus (with a focus ring), so the arrow keys and Page Down scroll it in every browser, even with nothing focusable inside. It's a region named by the title.
- On a screen under 480px tall, such as a laptop at 400% zoom, the whole panel scrolls instead of the body, so the header and footer can't squeeze the body away or push the buttons off screen. Focusing a button scrolls it into view (WCAG 1.4.10 and 2.4.11).
- It enters as a sequence: a modal drawer's backdrop starts fading in, and 50ms later (`motion-sequence`) the panel slides in over 300ms. It slides back out to its edge over 200ms, together with the backdrop, both in a straight line along that edge; focusing a control as it opens never scrolls it into view early. With `prefers-reduced-motion` it fades instead of sliding. The motion is a transition, so closing it while it slides in turns back from where it is. Focus goes back to what opened it at once, not after the slide, and presses reach the page while it leaves. A swipe moves the panel with the finger; let go short and it slides back, far enough and it slides out from where it is. One open on arrival (`defaultOpen`, or `open` on the first render) is there from the first frame. Firefox and Safari can't keep a closing modal drawer in the top layer yet, so there it closes at once; a non-modal one slides out everywhere.

- On a phone with a notch or a home bar, the panel's padding and the footer clear them. This needs `<meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1, viewport-fit=cover">`; without `viewport-fit=cover` the browser keeps the page out of those areas itself.
- Scrolling to the end of the body doesn't scroll the page behind it (`overscroll-behavior: contain`).

### Do and don't

- **Do:** Put the actions in `footer` so they stay in view, with the main action last. (`DoFooterActions`)
- **Don't:** Put the actions at the end of the body: they scroll away with the content. (`DontBodyActions`)

## Accessibility

- `aria-modal` (left out with `modal={false}`), named by the title (`aria-labelledby`) and described by the description.
- The title, description and body text keep 4.5:1 on the panel in every theme (`Drawer.test.tsx`). In forced-colors mode the panel gets a border.
- A Dialog opened from inside it closes on its own: Escape closes the Dialog first, and the next Escape the Drawer.
- On Android, the system back gesture asks to close it, like Escape, with `modal={false}` too (Escape on the page still leaves a non-modal one open). Under `<React.StrictMode>`, a Drawer that is open on its first render stays the innermost modal, so toasts and announcements still move into it.
- With `unsaved`, Escape, the ×, the backdrop, a swipe or the browser closing it first ask "Discard changes?" in a small alert dialog on top, with Keep editing focused, as Dialog does. Keep editing (or Escape) goes back to the form as it was; Discard closes both, and only then does `onOpenChange(false)` come, with the reason of the first request. Leaving or reloading the page while it's open asks too (the browser's own `beforeunload` question). Your own Cancel button sets `open` itself, so it closes without asking.
- To keep it open for another reason, leave `open` true when `onOpenChange(false)` comes. Chromium closes a modal dialog itself on a second Escape with no click in between; the component shows it again, so `open` stays the truth.

### Keyboard

| Key | Does |
| --- | --- |
| Tab / Shift+Tab | Between the controls in the drawer; the page behind is inert, so focus stays inside |
| Escape | Asks to close it (`onOpenChange(false)`); with a Dialog open from it, the Dialog first. With `unsaved`, it asks "Discard changes?" first, and Escape there keeps editing |
| Enter / Space | On the ×, the same as Escape. On a sheet's handle, the next stop |

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | string | none | Goes to the root `<dialog>`. Point a Button's `commandfor` at it. |
| `open` | `boolean` | | Controlled: close it yourself in `onOpenChange`. |
| `defaultOpen` | `boolean` | `false` | Open at first, then it closes itself (uncontrolled). Escape, the × or the backdrop close it, and `onOpenChange(false)` still comes. |
| `onOpenChange` | `(open, { reason }) => void` | | Called with `false` on Escape, the ×, or a click on the backdrop. `reason` says which: `'escape'`, `'close'` (the ×), `'outside'` (the backdrop) or `'api'` (the browser closed it, as `dialog.close()` or a `method="dialog"` form do) |
| `placement` | `'start' \| 'end' \| 'top' \| 'bottom'` | `'end'` | The edge it slides in from. `start` and `end` are the edges the reading starts and ends at: `end` is the right in a left-to-right page and the left in a right-to-left one. |
| `size` | `'sm' \| 'md' \| 'lg'` | `'md'` | The width of a left or right drawer: 320, 384 or 512px, never wider than the screen. |
| `title` | `ReactNode` | | The heading; it also names the drawer. Without one, give it an `aria-label`. |
| `description` | `ReactNode` | | A muted line under the title. |
| `footer` | `ReactNode` | | Buttons pinned to the bottom under a line, with the main action last. |
| `closeButton` | `boolean` | `true` | The × in the corner. |
| `closeLabel` | `string` | `'Close'` | The ×'s name. |
| `closeOnBackdrop` | `boolean` | `true` | Whether a click on the backdrop closes it. Turn it off when closing would lose work. |
| `swipeToClose` | `boolean` | `true` | A touch drag toward its edge closes it, with `reason: 'swipe'`. |
| `snapPoints` | `number[]` | | Bottom only: the heights a sheet stops at, as shares of the screen from the shortest (`[0.4, 0.9]`). With two or more, it has a handle. |
| `snap` | `number` | | Which stop it's at, from 0 (controlled). |
| `defaultSnap` | `number` | `0` | Which stop it opens at (uncontrolled). |
| `onSnapChange` | `(snap: number) => void` | | Called with the stop a drag or the handle moves it to. |
| `initialFocus` | `RefObject<HTMLElement>` | | The element that takes focus when it opens, instead of the first that can. A ref to something outside the drawer is ignored. |
| `finalFocus` | `RefObject<HTMLElement>` | | Where focus goes when it closes, instead of back to the opener. Used when it's on the page then; otherwise focus goes back to the opener. |
| `modal` | `boolean` | `true` | `false`: a side panel beside a usable page, with no backdrop, opened with `show()`. |
| `unsaved` | `boolean` | `false` | There are changes that would be lost: closing asks "Discard changes?" first (Keep editing or Discard), and leaving the page asks too. `onOpenChange(false)` comes after Discard. |

Every other prop, `className` and `ref` go to the native `<dialog>`.

## Component tokens

Each is an optional override: set it on the page, a container or one drawer. The list lives in `src/components/Drawer/drawer.tokens.json` (also in `design-tokens/components/`).

components.name: Duration
components.summary: How long something takes or took, written the way the reader's locale writes it: "1 hr, 30 min", "1 jam, 30 menit", "1 hour, 30 minutes", "1h 30m" or "1:30:00".
components.guide:
# Duration How long something takes or took, written the way the reader's locale writes it: "1 hr, 30 min", "1 jam, 30 menit", "1 hour, 30 minutes", "1h 30m" or "1:30:00". It's a `` with the duration for machines in `datetime` ("PT1H30M"). **Also called:** formatted duration, time span, elapsed time. ```tsx import { Duration, formatDuration } from "@diki-stwn/serupa-ds";

Prep

// "Prep 1 hr, 15 min" // "12:04"… read as "12 minutes, 4 seconds" // "38 hours, 30 minutes" formatDuration(5400, "id", { display: "long" }) // "1 jam, 30 menit", for a title or a chart label ``` ## When to use - A length of time on its own: a recipe's prep, a lesson, a video, a flight, a timesheet's total, how long a job ran. - Anywhere you'd otherwise build "1 h 30 min" by hand: it gets every locale's words, plurals and order right. ## When not to use - Time left until a moment, ticking: use [Countdown] (npx serupa-docs Countdown). - How long ago or until a date ("3 days ago", "in 2 hours"): use [RelativeTime] (npx serupa-docs RelativeTime). - A time of day or a date: use `Intl.DateTimeFormat`, or the date components. ## Usage - Give `value` and its `unit` (`'second'` by default; `'millisecond'`, `'minute'`, `'hour'` or `'day'`). It's rounded to `smallest`, which defaults to that unit (minutes for hours and days, so 1.5 hours is "1 hr, 30 min"), so minutes never grow seconds. - `display`: `'short'` (default, "1 hr, 30 min"), `'long'` ("1 hour, 30 minutes"), `'narrow'` ("1h 30m"), or `'digital'` ("1:30:00", for media and stopwatches). A clock under an hour starts at the minutes ("0:45", "12:04"); `largest="hour"` keeps the hours ("0:00:45") so a column of clocks has the same parts. - `largest` stops the units there and lets it keep counting: `largest="hour"` writes 36 hours rather than "1 day, 12 hours", as a timesheet does. A clock counts hours by default. - Units that are 0 are left out ("2 hr", not "2 hr, 0 min"); a duration of 0 is "0 min" in the smallest unit. - `formatDuration(value, locale, options)` gives the same text outside React, and `isoDuration(value, options)` the `datetime`. ### Do and don't - **Do:** Give the unit you have and let it write the words: `` is "1 hr, 15 min" in English and "1 j, 15 mnt" in Indonesian. (`Displays`) - **Don't:** A clock where it could be read as a time of day: "1:30" beside a date. Use the words there. (`Digital`) ## Accessibility - **Role and name:** a `` with `datetime`, read as its text. A clock is hidden from screen readers and carries the long words in its place ("1 hour, 30 minutes"), so "1:30:00" is never read as half past one. - **Keyboard:** none: inline text, not focusable. - Each unit's number and word stay together, so a narrow column wraps only between units. - With a `locale` of its own it carries that locale's direction (`dir`) with its `lang`, so English words in a right-to-left page keep their order ("1 hr, 15 min", not "hr, 15 min 1"). - **What's still yours:** saying what the duration is of, in the words around it ("Prep", "Running time"). ## Props | Prop | Type | Default | Notes | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `id` | string | none | Goes to the root ``. | | `value` | `number` | | How long, in `unit`. A negative one is written as its size; NaN renders an empty element. | | `unit` | `'millisecond' \| 'second' \| 'minute' \| 'hour' \| 'day'` | `'second'` | The unit `value` is in. | | `display` | `'long' \| 'short' \| 'narrow' \| 'digital'` | `'short'` | How it's written. | | `smallest` | `'second' \| 'minute' \| 'hour' \| 'day'` | the unit given (`'minute'` for hours and days) | The finest unit shown; the rest is rounded to it. | | `largest` | `'second' \| 'minute' \| 'hour' \| 'day'` | `'day'` (`'hour'` with `'digital'`, left out under an hour) | The biggest unit shown; more of it keeps counting. | | `locale` | `string` | the provider's, else the browser's | When it differs from the provider's, the element carries `lang`. | Every other prop, `className` and `ref` go to the ``, which has `data-component="duration"`, and `srp-duration--digital` for a clock. ## Component tokens None: it uses the surrounding text's font and color, with tabular digits for a clock.

components.name: EmptyState
components.summary: What a page or a panel shows when there's nothing in it yet, or nothing matches: an icon, a few words saying what's empty, what it means, and the action that fills it.
components.guide:
# EmptyState

What a page or a panel shows when there's nothing in it yet, or nothing matches: an icon, a few words saying what's empty, what it means, and the action that fills it.

**Also called:** blank slate, zero state.

```jsx
import { EmptyState, Button } from '@diki-stwn/serupa-ds';

<EmptyState
  icon="folder_open"
  title="No projects yet"
  description="Create a project to start tracking your work."
  actions={<Button startIcon="add">New project</Button>}
/>

// Inside a table or a card, after a search: announce says it to screen readers as it appears
<EmptyState announce size="sm" icon="search_off" title="No results" description={`Nothing matches "${query}".`}
  actions={<Button variant="outline" onClick={clear}>Clear the search</Button>} />

// No results, with a spelling fix and a way out: "Did you mean: quarterly" and a "Clear filters" button
<EmptyState size="sm" icon="search_off" title={`No results for “${query}”`} suggestions={["quarterly"]}
  onSuggestion={setQuery} onClearFilters={clearFilters} />

// A slot to fill
<EmptyState variant="dashed" icon="upload" title="Drop files here" />
```

## When to use

- A list, a table or a page has nothing in it yet, such as a new account with no projects.
- A search or a filter matches nothing.
- A slot people fill themselves, such as an area waiting for its first item.

## When not to use

- Content that's still loading: use [Loader] (npx serupa-docs Loader) (a skeleton or a ring) instead, and show the empty state only once you know it's empty.
- Content that couldn't load because something failed: use an [Alert] (npx serupa-docs Alert) with a way to retry instead.
- A place to drop or choose files: use [FileUpload] (npx serupa-docs FileUpload), which checks and lists the files, instead.

## Anatomy

Drawn from the `LongText` story.

1. **Icon** (`.srp-empty-state__icon`): a picture of what would be here.
2. **Title** (`.srp-empty-state__title`): says what's empty, or why.
3. **Description** (`.srp-empty-state__description`): what to do about it.
4. **Suggestions** (`.srp-empty-state__suggestions`): optional other things to try, such as a search that would find something.
5. **Actions** (`.srp-empty-state__actions`): the next step, such as creating the first item.

## Usage

- Say what's empty and why, then what to do: "No invoices yet. Invoices you send show up here." with a "New invoice" button.
- After a search or a filter, say nothing matches and offer to clear it, rather than suggesting to create something. `onClearFilters` adds a "Clear filters" button, and `suggestions` offers other searches, such as the word spelled right.
- Keep it to one primary action.
- Use `size="sm"` inside a card, a table or a menu, and the default size for a whole page or panel.

### Do and don't

- **Do:** Say what's empty and what to do next: "No invoices yet", with a "New invoice" button. (`DoSayWhatNext`)
- **Don't:** Say only "No data": it doesn't say whether something broke or how to fill the page. (`DontNoData`)

## Accessibility

- The title is a heading (`h3` by default), so people can find it; set `headingLevel` to fit the page.
- The icon is decorative and hidden from screen readers.
- When the empty state appears after an action (a search, a filter), set `announce`: as it appears, its title and description are said politely through the same live region as Toast and Loader ("No results. Nothing matches "mars"."), which moves into an open Dialog or Drawer so it's heard there too. It's said once; give it a new `key` to say it again for a new query. Leave it off for a page that's empty on arrival, which people find by reading.
- The title and description keep 4.5:1 on `surface`, and the icon 3:1 on its circle, in every theme (`EmptyState.test.tsx`).
- Suggestions are link-style buttons at least 24px tall after "Did you mean:"; with `announce` they're said with the title and description. Without `onSuggestion` they're plain bold text.
- **Keyboard:** none of its own. Tab reaches the suggestions, then the buttons and links in its actions, then Clear filters.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | string | none | Goes to the root `<div>`. |
| `icon` | an icon name or element | none | An icon in a circle, or your own illustration at its own size |
| `title` | node | required | What's empty, in a few words |
| `description` | node | none | What it means or what to do next |
| `actions` | node | none | One or two Buttons |
| `size` | `'sm'` \| `'md'` | `'md'` | `sm` fits inside a card, a table or a menu |
| `variant` | `'plain'` \| `'dashed'` | `'plain'` | A dashed frame, for a drop zone or a slot to fill |
| `headingLevel` | `2`–`6` | `3` | The title's heading level |
| `suggestions` | string[] | none | Searches to try instead, after "Did you mean:" |
| `onSuggestion` | `(suggestion: string) => void` | none | Called with the suggestion picked; without it suggestions are plain text |
| `onClearFilters` | `() => void` | none | Adds a "Clear filters" button after the actions, which calls it |
| `announce` | boolean | `false` | Says the title and description to screen readers, politely, as it appears: for a result after a search or a filter |

The words "Did you mean:" and "Clear filters" are the labels `didYouMean` and `clearFilters`; change them with `<SerupaProvider labels>`.

`className`, `style`, `ref` and everything else go to the wrapper, which has `data-component="empty-state"`.

## Component tokens

Each is an optional override: set it on the page, a container or one empty state. The list lives in `src/components/EmptyState/empty-state.tokens.json` (also in `design-tokens/components/`).

| Token | Default | Use |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--empty-state-icon-color` | `text-muted` | The icon (3:1 on icon-bg). |
| `--empty-state-icon-bg` | `secondary` | The circle behind the icon. |
| `--empty-state-title-color` | `text` | The title. |
| `--empty-state-description-color` | `text-muted` | The description (4.5:1 on surface). |
| `--empty-state-border` | `border` | The dashed frame of variant="dashed". |
| `--empty-state-title-size` | `text-base` | The title (16px; sm: 14px). |
| `--empty-state-title-weight` | `font-semibold` | The title's weight (600). |
| `--empty-state-description-size` | `text-sm` | The description (14px). |
| `--empty-state-icon-size` | `spacing-6` | The icon (24px). |
| `--empty-state-icon-box` | `spacing-12` | The circle behind it (48px; sm: 40px). |
| `--empty-state-icon-box-sm` | `spacing-10` | The circle at size sm (40px). |
| `--empty-state-max-width` | `container-sm` | The widest the text gets (384px). |
