components.name: ErrorBoundary
components.summary: Catches an error thrown while rendering anything inside it and shows a message with "Try again" in its place, so one broken widget doesn't blank the whole page.
components.guide:
# ErrorBoundary

Catches an error thrown while rendering anything inside it and shows a message with "Try again" in its place, so one broken widget doesn't blank the whole page.

**Also called:** error fallback, crash screen.

```tsx
import { ErrorBoundary } from "@diki-stwn/serupa-ds";

<ErrorBoundary onError={(error, info) => report(error, info.componentStack)}>
  <SalesChart />
</ErrorBoundary>

// a whole page: the server error page from the Error pages pattern, with "Try again" as its reset
<ErrorBoundary fallback={({ reset }) => <ErrorPage kind="server" onRetry={reset} />} onError={report}>
  <Page />
</ErrorBoundary>

// your own words
<ErrorBoundary title="Couldn't load the chart" description="The rest of the page still works.">…</ErrorBoundary>

// your own fallback, and a reset when the route changes
<ErrorBoundary resetKeys={[pathname]} fallback={({ reset }) => <EmptyState title="Unavailable" actions={<Button onClick={reset}>Retry</Button>} />}>
  <Outlet />
</ErrorBoundary>
```

## When to use

- Around a whole page, with the server error page from the Error pages pattern as its `fallback` (above): one heading that says what happened, a description, "Try again" and a way home. The default Alert is for a part of a page, not a whole one.
- Around a part of the page that can fail on its own (a chart, a feed, a third-party widget), so the rest keeps working. The default Alert fits here.
- Around each route's content in a single-page app, with `resetKeys` set to the route, so moving on clears the error.

## When not to use

- For an error you expect, such as a failed request: show it where it happens, with an [Alert] (npx serupa-docs Alert), a [Toast] (npx serupa-docs Toast) or an [EmptyState] (npx serupa-docs EmptyState).
- For errors in event handlers, timers or promises: React doesn't send those to boundaries. Catch them in the handler.
- Around the whole app only: a single top-level boundary takes the whole page down for one widget. Use several, close to what can fail.

## Usage

- Pass `onError` to log or report the error; the boundary itself doesn't send it anywhere.
- Say what failed and what still works in `title` and `description` when you know ("Couldn't load the chart"), instead of the general default.
- "Try again" renders the children again. If they fail the same way, the fallback comes back.
- `resetKeys` clears the error when any value in it changes, such as a route or the id being shown.
- `fallback` replaces the default Alert, such as with the error page for a whole page: an element, or a function of `{ error, reset }`. Don't show `error.message` to people: it's written for developers.

### Do and don't

- **Do:** Say what failed and what still works in `title` and `description` ("Couldn't load the chart"). (`DoSayWhatFailed`)
- **Don't:** Show `error.message` to people: it's written for developers. (`DontShowErrorMessage`)

## Accessibility

- The default fallback is a danger [Alert] (npx serupa-docs Alert) (`role="alert"`), so screen readers read it as soon as it appears, with a "Try again" button.
- When the crash took focus with it (focus fell to `<body>`), focus moves to the fallback, so keyboard users aren't sent back to the top of the page. Focus elsewhere on the page is left alone. The box shows the focus ring when focus came from the keyboard.
- When the error is cleared from inside the fallback (Try again, a custom fallback's `reset()`, or a `resetKeys` change while focus is in it), focus moves to the first part of the content that came back that is shown and in the Tab order (the selected tab of a tab list, not a hidden button), rather than falling to the top of the page. If that content has nothing focusable, its first element takes focus for that one move (`tabIndex=-1`, removed when focus leaves).
- The words come from the `errorTitle`, `errorDescription` and `tryAgain` labels in `SerupaProvider` (English and Indonesian built in).
- A fallback of your own should do the same: say what happened in words and offer a way on.
- **Keyboard:** when a crash leaves focus nowhere, focus moves to the fallback, which isn't a Tab stop, so the next Tab reaches its Try again button. Enter or Space on that button renders the children again, and focus moves into them.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `children` | `ReactNode` | | The part of the page to guard. |
| `fallback` | `ReactNode \| ({ error, reset }) => ReactNode` | a danger Alert with Try again | What to show instead. |
| `title` | `ReactNode` | "Something went wrong" | The default fallback's title. |
| `description` | `ReactNode` | "This part of the page couldn’t load." | The default fallback's message. |
| `onError` | `(error, info) => void` | | Called with the error and React's `componentStack`. |
| `onReset` | `() => void` | | Called when the error is cleared (Try again, `reset()` or `resetKeys`). |
| `resetKeys` | `unknown[]` | | When a value changes, the error clears. |
| `className` | `string` | | On the default fallback's box, which has `data-component="error-boundary"`. |

`id` isn't a prop. Put an id on what you pass as `fallback`, or on an element inside.

A function `fallback` gets `ErrorBoundaryFallbackProps`: `error`, the value that was thrown, and `reset`, which clears it and renders the children again.

## Component tokens

Each is an optional override: set it on the page, a container or one boundary. The fallback is an Alert, so its colors follow the `--alert-*` tokens. The list lives in `src/components/ErrorBoundary/error-boundary.tokens.json` (also in `design-tokens/components/`).

<!-- token-table:start (made from error-boundary.tokens.json by npm run tokens: edit the descriptions there) -->
| Token | Default | Use |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--error-boundary-focus-ring` | `focus-ring` | The ring when the fallback takes focus. |
| `--error-boundary-radius` | `radius-surface` | The fallback box's corners, matching the Alert (8px). |
<!-- token-table:end -->

components.name: ErrorSummary
components.summary: After a form fails to submit, a box at the top of the form that says what's wrong, with each error a link to its field.
components.guide:
# ErrorSummary

After a form fails to submit, a box at the top of the form that says what's wrong, with each error a link to its field. It takes focus when it appears, so everyone, including people using a screen reader, learns the submit failed and can go straight to each problem.

**Also called:** error list, form error summary.

```tsx
import { ErrorSummary } from "@diki-stwn/serupa-ds";

<ErrorSummary errors={[
  { field: "email", message: "Enter an email address in the right format, like name@example.com" },
  { field: "start", message: "Start date must be today or in the future" },
]} />
```

## When to use

- A form with more than a couple of fields fails validation on submit: show the summary above the form, and the same messages on each field ([Field] (npx serupa-docs Field) `error`).

## When not to use

- One field checked as the person types or leaves it: its own error under the field is enough ([Field] (npx serupa-docs Field) `error`).
- A message about the page or a task, not about fields: use [Alert] (npx serupa-docs Alert).

## Anatomy

Drawn from the `WithDescription` story.

1. **Title** (`.srp-error-summary__title`): how many problems there are; focus moves here when the form is sent.
2. **Description** (`.srp-error-summary__description`): optional words on what to do.
3. **List** (`.srp-error-summary__list`): one line per problem.
4. **Link** (`.srp-error-summary__link`): takes you to the field to fix.

## Usage

- Render it only after a submit fails, at the top of the form (or the page's main content), with the errors in the order of the fields.
- Use the same words as each field's own error, so the link and the field say the same thing. Say what's wrong and how to fix it ("Enter your full name"), not just "Invalid".
- Each error's `field` is the id of the control to fix: an `<input>`, `<select>` or `<textarea>`, or a group's first radio or checkbox. A RadioGroup's or Rating's own id works too: the link focuses its checked radio, or else its first one that can be picked.
- Clear `errors` (or stop rendering it) once the form is sent. Leave it as it is while the person fixes fields: it updates on the next submit.
- For errors the server sends by field name, put it inside `FormErrors` (from Field) and leave `errors` out: it lists the messages the form's Fields still show, each linking to its control, in the order the server sent them. It takes focus for each new set of errors, not when fixing a field takes one away.
- Prefix the page's `<title>` with "Error: " while it shows, so the problem is also said when the page reloads.
- When it takes focus, the Fields in the same form don't also announce their new errors, so the list is read once.

## Behavior

- With no errors it renders nothing.
- It takes focus when it appears, and again when its errors change (another failed submit: a field added or gone, or a message that says something new), so the page scrolls to it and a screen reader reads its heading. `autoFocus={false}` turns this off.
- Clicking an error moves focus to its field and scrolls the field's label to the top, so the question shows above the answer. For a radio or checkbox in a fieldset, the group's legend shows, also when the error names a RadioGroup by its id. A modified click (new tab) or a field that isn't on the page follows the link as usual.

### Do and don't

- **Do:** Say what's wrong and how to fix it, in the field's own words: "Enter your full name". (`Default`)
- **Don't:** Write "Invalid" or "Error": people know something is wrong but not what to do. (`DontJustInvalid`)

## Accessibility

- **Role and name:** a `<div>` named by its heading (`aria-labelledby`), an `<h2>` by default (`headingLevel`), then a list of links. It takes focus (`tabIndex={-1}`) rather than being a live region, so it's read once, in full, when it appears.
- **Keyboard:** each error is a Tab stop. Enter follows it to its field.
- **Contrast:** its text reads 4.5:1 on its background in every theme (`ErrorSummary.test.tsx`), and so do its links.
- **What's still yours:** keep each field's own error (Field `error`) so the problem shows next to it too, and write messages that say how to fix it.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | string | none | Goes to the root `<div>`. |
| `errors` | `{ field, message }[]` | | The errors, in the fields' order: `field` is the control's id, `message` what's wrong. With none, nothing renders. Inside `FormErrors`, leave it out to list the form's messages. |
| `title` | `ReactNode` | `"There is a problem"`, or `"There are N problems"` | The heading. |
| `headingLevel` | `2 \| 3 \| 4 \| 5 \| 6` | `2` | The heading's level, to fit the page's outline. |
| `description` | `ReactNode` | | Text under the heading, before the list. |
| `autoFocus` | `boolean` | `true` | Moves focus to it when it appears and when its errors change. |

`className`, `ref` and other props go to the `<div>`.

## Component tokens

Each is an optional override: set it on the page, a container or one ErrorSummary. The list lives in `src/components/ErrorSummary/error-summary.tokens.json` (also in `design-tokens/components/`).

<!-- token-table:start (made from error-summary.tokens.json by npm run tokens: edit the descriptions there) -->
| Token | Default | Use |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--error-summary-bg` | `danger-subtle` | The background: the danger tint a danger Alert has. |
| `--error-summary-text` | `text` | The heading and description (4.5:1 on bg). |
| `--error-summary-border` | `danger` | The border, which marks it as errors. |
| `--error-summary-link` | `danger-text` | Each error's link (4.5:1 on bg). |
| `--error-summary-focus-ring` | `focus-ring` | The focus ring, on the box when it takes focus and on each link. |
| `--error-summary-border-width` | `border-width-2` | The border's width (2px). |
| `--error-summary-radius` | `radius-control` | The corners (6px). |
| `--error-summary-padding` | `spacing-4` | Space inside, on every side (16px). |
| `--error-summary-gap` | `spacing-2` | Space between the heading, the description and the list (8px). |
| `--error-summary-title-weight` | `font-semibold` | The heading's weight. |
<!-- token-table:end -->

components.name: EventCalendar
components.summary: A month of events: meetings, deadlines, bookings.
components.guide:
# EventCalendar

A month of events: meetings, deadlines, bookings. People see what's on each day, move through the month by keyboard, open an event, and, where your app allows it, add one at a time they pick and move it to another. A week or a day shows the hours, with each event at its time. On a phone, or by choice, the month shows as an agenda: a list of the days that have events.

**Also called:** scheduler, agenda.

```tsx
import { EventCalendar } from "@diki-stwn/serupa-ds";

<EventCalendar
  events={[
    { id: "1", title: "Team standup", start: "2025-03-03T09:30", end: "2025-03-03T09:45", repeating: true },
    { id: "2", title: "Launch day", start: "2025-03-12", allDay: true, tone: "success" },
  ]}
  onEventClick={(event) => openDetails(event.id)}
/>
```

## When to use

- A schedule people scan by date: team events, bookings, content going out, deadlines.
- When where an event falls in the month matters, not only what comes next.

## When not to use

- To pick a date or a range: use [DatePicker] (npx serupa-docs DatePicker), [DateRangePicker] (npx serupa-docs DateRangePicker) or [Calendar] (npx serupa-docs Calendar).
- For a few upcoming items with no need for the month around them: a list or a [Timeline] (npx serupa-docs Timeline) says it in less space.

## Anatomy

Drawn from the `Month` story.

1. **Toolbar** (`.srp-event-calendar__toolbar`): Today, Previous and Next, the title and the Month, Week, Day and Agenda switch.
2. **Title** (`.srp-event-calendar__heading`): the month, week or day shown, said when it changes.
3. **Grid** (`.srp-event-calendar__grid`): the weeks of the month, with the weekday names above.
4. **Day** (`.srp-event-calendar__day`): one date and its events; today's date is marked by color and weight, and in the agenda by color and an underline, so it never rests on color alone.
5. **Event** (`.srp-event-calendar__event`): a button with the event's time and title, and a bar of its tone at its start.
6. **More** (`.srp-event-calendar__more`): "+N more", which opens the rest of the day's events.

## Usage

- Pass the events of the shown month (more is fine: the rest aren't drawn, and the days of the months before and after show only their dates). Use `onMonthChange` to load each month as people move.
- `start` and `end` take a Date or an ISO string. A plain `"2025-03-12"` is that whole day, wherever the browser is. An event that runs over several days shows on each of them.
- Repeating events are your app's to expand: pass each occurrence, with `repeating: true`, and it's said and marked as repeating.
- `tone` colors an event (`primary`, `info`, `success`, `warning`, `danger`). Say what it means in the title too: color alone doesn't reach everyone.
- Open details from `onEventClick`, in a [Dialog] (npx serupa-docs Dialog) or [Drawer] (npx serupa-docs Drawer), and give focus back to the event when it closes.
- `maxPerDay` (default 3) is the most a day shows. Past it, the last place shows "+N more", which opens all of the day's events in a Popover.
- The week and day views show the hours in a box that scrolls, opened at 8 AM or the first event if it's earlier. Each event sits at its time, as tall as it lasts (half an hour at least, so it's still a target with its title showing). Events that overlap share the day's width side by side. All-day events are in a row on top, which stays with the weekday names as the hours scroll. Today has a line at the time now, and the time zone shows over the hour scale.
- Previous and Next move a week or a day in those views. `onMonthChange` still gets the month whenever the shown week or day moves into another one, so pass the events of the weeks that cross into the next month too.
- Below 640px wide, the week shows as the agenda, as the month does: seven columns don't fit a phone. The day view stays. A day in the week is never narrower than 96px at the default text size and grows with larger text, so with large text the week scrolls sideways in its box rather than cutting off an event's time.
- **Adding events:** with `onSlotSelect`, a press on a day's empty space chooses it for a new event. In the month that's the whole day; in the hours it's the hour from the half hour pressed. A drag down a day's hours chooses the span, by quarter hours, outlined as it goes. Enter or Space on a day chooses the whole day. Open your form from there, with the slot's times filled in.
- **Moving events:** with `onEventMove`, events move. Drag one to another day (it keeps its time) or, in the hours, to another time by quarter hours. Drag its end to change how long it lasts. Shift and an arrow key move the focused event: a day to either side, and up or down a week in the month or a quarter hour in the hours. The calendar doesn't move the event itself: update `events` with the new times, or it goes back. Each move is said in words ("Design review, now Thursday, March 6, 2:00 PM to 3:00 PM").
- Dragging is for a mouse or a pen. On a touch screen a drag scrolls the page. A tap on an event is still `onEventClick`, so your event form is the way to change its times there, and for anyone who can't drag (WCAG 2.5.7). Escape during a drag puts the event back.

### Do and don't

- **Do:** Say what a `tone` means in the title too ("Due: tax filing"). (`DoSayWhatToneMeans`)
- **Don't:** Rely on color alone: it doesn't reach everyone, and red can mean many things. (`DontToneAlone`)

## Accessibility

- **Role and name:** the month is a `role="grid"` named by its title ("March 2025"). The week and day views are a grid with a single row, named by their title ("March 2 – 8, 2025"). Each day in that row is a cell, so the names, keys and Tab stop work as in the month. The hour scale, the time zone and the line at the time now are hidden from screen readers, since each event already says its time. Each day is a cell that starts with its full date and how many events it has ("Tuesday, March 4, 2025, 1 event"), as hidden text so the name never hides the events. Today has `aria-current="date"`. Each event is a button named by what it shows (its time and title), then its day, its whole time and "Repeats" ("2:00 PM Design review, Tuesday, March 4, 2:00 PM to 3:00 PM").
- **Long titles:** an event's title that doesn't fit ends in an ellipsis and shows whole on hover and on the event's keyboard focus ([TruncatedText] (npx serupa-docs TruncatedText)); the event's name always holds the whole title.
- **Direction:** with a `locale` of its own, its times, hours and heading carry that locale's direction (`dir`), so "9:00 AM" in a right-to-left page keeps its order (not "AM 9:00"). The grid stays in the page's direction, with the buttons around it.
- **Keyboard:** one Tab stop on the days. Arrow keys move a day or a week, Home and End go to the week's start and end, and PageUp and PageDown go a month (a week or a day in those views). Moving past the month shows the next one. Tab from a day goes to its events and "+N more", and Escape on an event goes back to its day. Previous, Next and Today are buttons before the grid.
- **Changes are said:** the month's title is a polite live region, so Previous, Next, Today and paging say the new month. A moved event's new day and time are said through the shared polite region.
- **Dragging has an alternative (2.5.7):** every move a drag makes, Shift and the arrow keys make too. A press without a drag opens the event, where your form changes its times. A movable event lists its keys in `aria-keyshortcuts`.
- **Reading order:** the agenda is an ordered list of days, each with a heading one level below the title, so a screen reader can jump by day.
- **Contrast:** dates, weekday names and event text read 4.5:1 in every theme (`EventCalendar.test.tsx`).
- **What's still yours:** the event details, and returning focus to the event when they close.

### Keyboard

| Key | Does |
| --- | --- |
| Tab | Into the grid at the focused day (one stop), then to that day's events and "+N more" |
| Arrow keys | A day left or right, a week up or down; past the month shows the next one |
| Home, End | The start or end of the week |
| PageUp, PageDown | The same day a month before or after; in the week and day views, a week or a day |
| Enter, Space (on an event) | Opens it (`onEventClick`) |
| Escape (on an event) | Back to its day; during a drag, puts the event back |
| Enter, Space (on a day) | With `onSlotSelect`, chooses the whole day for a new event |
| Shift + Left, Right (on an event) | With `onEventMove`, moves it a day earlier or later (mirrored right to left) |
| Shift + Up, Down (on an event) | With `onEventMove`, moves it a week in the month, or a quarter hour in the week and day views |

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `events` | `CalendarEvent[]` | required | `{ id, title, start, end?, allDay?, repeating?, tone? }`. |
| `onEventClick` | `(event) => void` | | An event is clicked, or pressed with Enter or Space. |
| `month` | `Date` | | The month shown (controlled), any day in it. Use with `onMonthChange`. |
| `defaultMonth` | `Date` | today's | The month shown at first, any day in it. The week and day views open on that day. |

components.name: Fab
components.summary: A floating action button: the one main action of a screen, such as "New project" or "Compose", in a round, raised button fixed to a corner.
components.guide:
# Fab

A floating action button: the one main action of a screen, such as "New project" or "Compose", in a round, raised button fixed to a corner. It's a primary [Button] (npx serupa-docs Button), so loading, disabled and focus all work the same.

**Also called:** floating action button.

```jsx
import { Fab } from '@diki-stwn/serupa-ds';

<Fab icon="add" label="New project" onClick={create} />
<Fab icon="edit" label="Compose" extended />
<Fab icon="chat" label="Help" size="sm" placement="bottom-start" />
```

## When to use

- The one action people come to a screen for, such as "New project" or "Compose".
- When that action must stay in reach as people scroll.

## When not to use

- On wide screens, a regular [Button] (npx serupa-docs Button) in the header is often clearer.
- Any other action on the same screen: use a [Button] (npx serupa-docs Button) in the page, since there's only one FAB per screen.
- An icon action in a toolbar or a row: use [IconButton] (npx serupa-docs IconButton).

## Anatomy

Drawn from the `Extended` story. It's a primary [Button] (npx serupa-docs Button), so its icon and label are Button's.

1. **Button** (`.srp-fab`): the round, raised primary button, fixed to a corner of the screen; extended, a pill with the label.
2. **Icon** (`.srp-btn__icon`): what the action does, the whole button when it isn't extended.
3. **Label** (`.srp-btn__label`): the action in words beside the icon, when `extended`. With `extended="auto"` it folds to nothing while the page scrolls down and opens again on the way up.

## Usage

- One per screen, for the action people come to the screen for. Other actions go in the page.
- Leave room at the end of the content so the FAB never covers the last item.
- On a phone, an extended FAB covers a lot of a long list. `extended="auto"` folds it to its icon while the page scrolls down and opens it again on the way back up or at the top, so the label is there when people look for the action and out of the way while they read. It's named by its label either way. The width changes at once and the label fades in, or appears at once with reduced motion.

## Placement

- The offset is measured from the safe area. On a phone with a home bar or a notch, and with `viewport-fit=cover` in the viewport meta tag, the button sits above the bar instead of under it.

### Do and don't

- **Do:** Use one FAB, for the action people come to the screen for. (`DoOneFab`)
- **Don't:** Put several FABs on one screen: they compete and cover the content. (`DontSeveral`)

## Accessibility

- It's a real `<button>` named by `label`. Put it where it comes in the reading order (often after the main content), since it's fixed but still focused in source order.
- `shadow-lg` at rest and `shadow-xl` on hover lift it off the page; the colors and focus ring are Button's primary (checked in Button's tests and `Fab.test.tsx`).
- While it's fixed to a corner, the page gets that much scroll padding at that edge (the FAB's size and twice its offset, 104px by default), so what the keyboard focuses scrolls into view clear of it, not under it (WCAG 2.4.11). With a sticky Navbar at the top, the larger padding wins.
- It isn't printed: fixed to the viewport, it would repeat on every page.

### Keyboard

| Key | Does |
| --- | --- |
| Tab | To the button, in its place in the source order (not where it floats) |
| Enter, Space | Press it |

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | string | none | Goes to the root `<button>`. |
| `icon` | icon name \| element | required | A custom or Material Symbols name, or any element (24px) |
| `label` | string | required | Shown next to the icon when extended; otherwise its `aria-label`, and a Tooltip on hover and keyboard focus |
| `extended` | boolean \| `'auto'` | `false` | Shows the label: a 56px pill instead of a circle. In a corner it is never wider than the screen less its offset on both sides, so a long label ends in an ellipsis. `'auto'`: shrinks to the 56px circle while the page scrolls down, and shows the label again scrolling up or at the top |
| `size` | `'md'` \| `'sm'` | `'md'` | 56px or 40px |
| `placement` | `'bottom-end'` \| `'bottom-start'` \| `'top-end'` \| `'top-start'` \| `'static'` | `'bottom-end'` | The corner of the screen it's fixed to, 24px in; start and end follow the text direction. `static` leaves it in the page for you to place |

Every other Button prop works the same: `onClick`, `loading`, `disabled`, `destructive`, `ref`. It sits at `z-30`: above the page, under dialogs and toasts.

## Component tokens

Each is an optional override: set it on the page, a container or one FAB. The list lives in `src/components/Fab/fab.tokens.json` (also in `design-tokens/components/`). Button's primary tokens set the colors.

<!-- token-table:start (made from fab.tokens.json by npm run tokens: edit the descriptions there) -->
| Token | Default | Use |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--fab-size` | `spacing-14` | The height (and width, without a label) of a medium FAB (56px). |
| `--fab-size-sm` | `spacing-10` | The height of a small FAB (40px). |
| `--fab-icon-size` | `spacing-6` | The icon (24px). |
| `--fab-label-max` | `container-xs` | How wide an extended="auto" FAB's label can open (320px); it folds to 0 while the page scrolls down. |
| `--fab-shadow` | `elevation-overlay` | The raised shadow at rest. |
| `--fab-shadow-hover` | `elevation-modal` | The shadow on hover. |
| `--fab-radius` | `radius-pill` | The corners (round). |
| `--fab-offset` | `spacing-6` | The distance from the corner of the screen (24px). |
| `--fab-padding-x` | `spacing-5` | Padding at the sides of an extended FAB (20px). |
| `--fab-z-index` | `z-30` | The stacking level: above the page, under dialogs and toasts. |
<!-- token-table:end -->

components.name: FabMenu
components.summary: A floating action button that opens a few related actions, such as "New document", "New folder" and "Upload a file", when a screen's main action comes in kinds.
components.guide:
# FabMenu

A floating action button that opens a few related actions, such as "New document", "New folder" and "Upload a file", when a screen's main action comes in kinds. It's a [Fab] (npx serupa-docs Fab) whose press opens a [Menu] (npx serupa-docs Menu), so each action shows its words, on touch too.

**Also called:** speed dial, FAB menu.

```tsx
import { FabMenu } from "@diki-stwn/serupa-ds";

<FabMenu icon="add" label="Create" actions={[
  { label: "New document", icon: "description", onSelect: newDoc },
  { label: "New folder", icon: "create_new_folder", onSelect: newFolder },
  { label: "Upload a file", icon: "upload", onSelect: upload },
]} />
```

## When to use

- A screen's main action comes in a few kinds people pick between: create a document, a folder or an upload.
- On a phone, where those would otherwise be three buttons fighting for the bottom of the screen.

## When not to use

- One main action: use a [Fab] (npx serupa-docs Fab), which does it in one press.
- More than six actions, or actions with nothing in common: use a [Menu] (npx serupa-docs Menu) from a button in the page, or put them in the page itself.
- On wide screens with room in the header: a [Button] (npx serupa-docs Button) or a split button there is easier to find.

## Usage

- Give it 3 to 6 `actions`, each with short words that say what it makes or does ("New folder", not "Folder"). The words always show: an icon alone is a guess.
- `label` names the Fab and the menu ("Create"). Pick an `icon` that says "more than one thing", such as `add`.
- It's fixed to a corner like a Fab (`placement`), and the actions open toward the middle of the screen: above a Fab at the bottom, under one at the top, lined up with its outer edge, 8px off it (`--fab-menu-offset`).
- Every Fab prop works the same (`extended`, `size`, `disabled`, `loading`). `open` and `onOpenChange` open it yourself.
- A `disabled` action is still read and reached, so people learn it's there; `destructive` paints one in danger colors.

## Accessibility

- **Role and name:** the Fab is a button with `aria-haspopup="menu"` and `aria-expanded`, named by `label`. The actions are `menuitem`s in a `role="menu"` with the same name.
- **Keyboard:** Enter, Space or Down on the Fab opens it on the first action, Up on the last; Up and Down move, Home and End go to the ends, a letter jumps to the action that starts with it, Enter or Space picks, and Escape, Tab, a pick or a press outside closes it. Closing puts focus back on the Fab. It's [Menu] (npx serupa-docs Menu)'s keyboard.
- **Contrast:** the Fab keeps [Fab] (npx serupa-docs Fab)'s and the actions [Menu] (npx serupa-docs Menu)'s, in every theme.
- **What's still yours:** a `label` that says what the actions have in common, and words for each one that make sense read alone.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | string | none | Goes to the Fab's `<button>`. |
| `actions` | `FabMenuAction[]` | | `{ label, icon?, onSelect, disabled?, destructive? }`, 3 to 6. |
| `icon` | `IconSource` | | The Fab's icon. |
| `label` | `string` | | The Fab's name, and the menu's. |
| `placement` | `'bottom-end'` \| `'bottom-start'` \| `'top-end'` \| `'top-start'` \| `'static'` | `'bottom-end'` | The corner it's fixed to; the actions open toward the middle. |
| `open` | `boolean` | | Open it yourself (controlled), with `onOpenChange`. |
| `onOpenChange` | `(open: boolean) => void` | | Called when it opens or closes. |

`extended`, `size`, `disabled`, `className`, `ref` and the other [Fab] (npx serupa-docs Fab) props go to the Fab's `<button>`.

## Component tokens

Each is an optional override: set it on the page, a container or one FabMenu. The list lives in `src/components/FabMenu/fab-menu.tokens.json` (also in `design-tokens/components/`).

<!-- token-table:start (made from fab-menu.tokens.json by npm run tokens: edit the descriptions there) -->
| Token | Default | Use |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--fab-menu-offset` | `spacing-2` | The space between the Fab and its menu (8px). |
<!-- token-table:end -->

components.name: Field
components.summary: A label, an optional hint and a message (an error, a warning or "checking…") around one form control, wired up for screen readers.
components.guide:
# Field

A label, an optional hint and a message (an error, a warning or "checking…") around one form control, wired up for screen readers. The label names the control, the hint and error are added to its `aria-describedby`, and an error makes the control invalid. It works with Input, Textarea, Select and any native control, a plain `<select>` with its options included. With `group` it renders a `<fieldset>` and `<legend>` for a set of checkboxes or radios.

**Also called:** form field, form label, fieldset.

```jsx
import { Field, Input, Textarea } from '@diki-stwn/serupa-ds';

<Field label="Email" hint="We only use it for receipts." error={emailError} required>
  <Input type="email" value={email} onChange={(e) => setEmail(e.target.value)} />
</Field>

<Field label="Company" optional><Input /></Field>
<Field label="Notes" hint="Anything the team should know."><Textarea rows={3} /></Field>

// a set of choices: a fieldset with a legend
<Field group label="Plan" hint="You can change it later." error={planError}>
  <RadioGroup name="plan" value={plan} onValueChange={setPlan}>
    <Radio value="free">Free</Radio>
    <Radio value="pro">Pro</Radio>
  </RadioGroup>
</Field>
```

## When to use

- Any form control that needs a visible label, with or without a hint or an error: an [Input] (npx serupa-docs Input), a [Select] (npx serupa-docs Select), a [Textarea] (npx serupa-docs Textarea) or a native control.
- A set of checkboxes or radios that answer one question, with `group`.

## When not to use

- A single [Checkbox] (npx serupa-docs Checkbox) or [Switch] (npx serupa-docs Switch): it carries its own label (its children), so use it on its own.
- A control with no visible label, such as a row checkbox in a table: give the control an `aria-label` instead.

## Anatomy

Drawn from the `Horizontal` story.

1. **Label** (`.srp-field__label`): names the control; clicking it focuses the control.
2. **Optional** (`.srp-field__optional`): says the field can be left empty, when most are required.
3. **Control** (`.srp-field__control`): the input, select or other control it wraps.
4. **Hint** (`.srp-field__hint`): help on what to enter, linked to the control for screen readers.
5. **Error** (`.srp-field__error`): what's wrong and how to fix it, with an icon, linked to the control too. A warning (`.srp-field__warning`) or "checking…" (`.srp-field__checking`) sits in the same place.

## Usage

- Keep labels short and specific ("Work email", not "Please enter your email address"). Put format help in the hint, never only in the placeholder.
- Show errors after someone leaves the field or submits, not on every keystroke, and on submit move focus to the first field with an error.
- Native constraints (`required`, `type="email"`, `minLength`, `pattern`, `min`…) speak for themselves: once people have changed the control and left it, or tried to send the form (`:user-invalid`), and it fails one, the error slot says which, in the provider's words (`invalidValue`; English keeps the browser's own message), with `aria-invalid` and the description. It goes as soon as the value is fine, and on the form's reset. An `error` you pass, or a FormErrors message, wins. So a red border is never the only sign.
- Mark both: `required` on every field that must be filled and `optional` on every one that can be left empty, and say once before the form what the `*` means ("Fields marked * are required."). The [Forms](?path=/docs/guides-forms--docs) guide says why. The `*` is hidden from screen readers, which say "required" from the control.
- Stack fields with `gap-5` or `gap-6` between them.
- For a dense settings page, use `orientation="horizontal"`: the labels line up in a column at the start and the controls beside them. Keep labels short enough for the 192px column (`--field-label-width`). Give fields a full-width parent: a horizontal field stacks again on its own once it's too narrow for both columns. A set of checkboxes or radios (`group`) stays stacked.

- Use `warning` for advice that doesn't stop the form: "A project with this name was archived last year", "This date is a public holiday". The control stays valid and the form sends. If the answer can't be sent, it's an `error`.
- Use `checking` while an answer is checked on the server (a username, an address, a coupon), with words that say what: "Checking the name…". Set it once the check takes longer than a moment, and replace it with an `error`, a `warning` or nothing when the answer comes. Field shows one message at a time: an error, then "checking…", then a warning.
- Don't confirm a right answer field by field. People expect it to be right; a green tick on each field is noise.

### Do and don't

- **Do:** Put format help in the hint, where it stays in view while people type. (`DoHintForFormat`)
- **Don't:** Put it only in the placeholder: it goes at the first keystroke, and its pale text is hard to read. (`DontPlaceholderFormat`)

### Errors from the server

When the server answers a submit with errors by field name, wrap the form in `FormErrors` and pass them all at once. Each Field finds its own message by its control's `name` (or the Field's own `name`, for a control that names itself differently), and shows it like `error`: `aria-invalid` on the control, the message in its description. Typing in the field, or changing it, takes its message away, since it was about the value that was sent. A new `errors` object (the next submit) shows every message again, and `null` clears them. A Field's own `error` wins over the server's.

```tsx
<form action={send}>
  <FormErrors errors={state.errors}>
    <ErrorSummary />
    <Field label="Email"><Input name="email" type="email" /></Field>
    <Field label="Username"><Input name="username" /></Field>
  </FormErrors>
</form>
```

### Layout

Label, control, hint and error stack with 6px between them (`--field-gap`): the hint sits under the box, and the error under the hint. With `orientation="horizontal"`, the label takes a 192px column (`--field-label-width`) 16px from the control (`--field-column-gap`). Its text sits on the control's first line (baselines aligned), and the hint and error go under the control. Once the control column would be narrower than 256px (`--field-control-min-width`), it wraps under the label, so the field is stacked again. The label is `text-sm` in `font-medium`; the hint and the message are a size smaller, `text-xs`. The message's 14px icon sits centered on its first line. A group's legend lays out exactly like a label.

## Accessibility

- Screen readers read the label as the control's name and the hint and error as its description, so a person hears "Email, required, invalid entry, We only use it for receipts. Enter an email address like name@example.com."
- Say what went wrong and how to fix it, not just "Invalid". The error icon is decorative; the words carry the meaning.
- With an error, the control also points at it with `aria-errormessage`, at any depth. The error stays in the description too, because not every screen reader reads `aria-errormessage` yet.
- Clicking the label focuses the control, as with an input, also for Slider, SegmentedControl and ColorPicker. Their root is a `<div>`, which a label can't focus by itself, so Field moves focus to their thumb or checked option.
- The `*` is hidden from screen readers, which hear `aria-required` instead. A fieldset can't carry `aria-required`, so with `group` the legend also says "Required" in words, hidden from sight (the `required` label, "Wajib diisi" in `idLabels`): the set is read as "Contact by, Required, group" whatever it holds.
- An error that appears or changes after the Field mounts (after a submit, for example) is announced politely, since focus is usually elsewhere and a description is only read on focus. An error already there on first render isn't announced, and neither are errors that appear as an ErrorSummary in the same form takes focus, since the summary reads them all.
- If nothing on the page has the control's id (a control Field can't reach, with no `id` passed), Field warns once in the console: the label would name nothing.
- For radios and checkboxes use `group`: screen readers announce the legend when focus enters the set.
- A warning and "checking…" join the control's description like an error, and are announced politely when they appear, but don't make the control invalid. While checking, the Field has `aria-busy`. The warning's icon and the spinner are decorative.
- Label, hint, error, warning and `*` keep 4.5:1 on `surface` in every theme (`Field.test.tsx`).
- **Keyboard:** nothing of its own. Tab goes to the control it wraps, and a click on the label focuses that control.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `label` | text or element | | A `<label>` linked to the control; with `group`, the fieldset's `<legend>` |
| `hint` | text or element | | Help under the control (with `group`, under the choices), above the error, in `text-muted`; added to the control's `aria-describedby` |
| `warning` | text or element | | Advice under the control, in `warning-text` with an icon, that doesn't block sending: the control stays valid. Added to its `aria-describedby` and said politely. An error takes its place |
| `checking` | text or element | | While the answer is being checked: the words ("Checking the address…") with a small spinner, under the control; `aria-busy` on the Field. Added to the description and said politely. Takes a warning's place; an error takes its place |
| `error` | text or element | | A message under the control, in `danger-text` with an icon; makes the control invalid (`invalid` on Serupa components, `aria-invalid` on DOM elements) and is added to its `aria-describedby` |
| `required` | boolean | `false` | A `*` after the label (hidden from screen readers) and `aria-required` on the control; with `group`, "Required" in words in the legend for screen readers. Add the control's own `required` too if you want the browser's check |
| `optional` | boolean or text | `false` | "(optional)" after the label (the `fieldOptional` label, "(opsional)" in `idLabels`), or your own words. Ignored with `required` |
| `disabled` | boolean | `false` | Disables the control (with `group`, every control in the fieldset) and draws the label and hint in `disabled-text` |
| `group` | boolean | `false` | A `<fieldset>` and `<legend>` around a set of controls; the hint and error describe the fieldset |
| `orientation` | `'vertical' \| 'horizontal'` | `'vertical'` | `'horizontal'`: the label in a column beside the control, the hint and error under the control. It stacks again when narrow. Not with `group` |
| `id` | string | | The control's id; by default the control's own `id`, or a generated one |
| `name` | string | | The name that picks this field's message from a surrounding `FormErrors`; by default the control's own `name` |

Field takes one control as its child (any number with `group`). The control keeps its own props, `ref` and `aria-describedby` (Field's ids are added after yours). `className`, `ref` and any other attribute go to the outer element (a `<fieldset>` with `group`, otherwise a `<div>`), which has `data-component="field"`: a ref lets an app scroll to or measure a field with an error.

### FormErrors

| Prop | Type | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `errors` | `Record<string, ReactNode>` \| null | | The form's errors by field name, as the server sent them. Each Field inside shows its own; a new object shows them all again, `null` clears them |
| `children` | element | | The form, or the part of it the errors are about |

## Component tokens

Each is an optional override: set it on the page, a container or one field. The list lives in `src/components/Field/field.tokens.json` (also in `design-tokens/components/`).

<!-- token-table:start (made from field.tokens.json by npm run tokens: edit the descriptions there) -->
| Token | Default | Use |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--field-text` | `text` | Text with no token of its own (the label, hint and error have theirs) |
| `--field-label-color` | `text` | Label |
| `--field-hint-color` | `text-muted` | Hint and "(optional)" |
| `--field-error-color` | `danger-text` | Error message and its icon |

components.name: FieldList
components.summary: Rows people add and remove in a form, such as phone numbers, emergency contacts or the lines of an invoice.
components.guide:
# FieldList

Rows people add and remove in a form, such as phone numbers, emergency contacts or the lines of an invoice. Each row is a named group of a few fields with its own Remove button, and Add comes after the last row. Focus follows each change, and each change is announced.

**Also called:** repeater, dynamic fields, form list.

```tsx
import { FieldList, Field, Input } from "@diki-stwn/serupa-ds";

<FieldList
  label="Phone numbers"
  itemLabel={(i) => "Phone " + (i + 1)}
  addLabel="Add phone"
  name="phones"
  newItem={() => ({ number: "" })}
  defaultValue={[{ number: "" }]}
  min={1}
  max={5}
>
  {(row, { name, update }) => (
    <Field label="Number">
      <Input name={name("number")} type="tel" value={row.number} onChange={(e) => update({ number: e.target.value })} />
    </Field>
  )}
</FieldList>
```

## When to use

- A form that takes a few of the same thing, in a number people choose: phone numbers, addresses, guests, invoice lines.
- Rows of up to three short fields each, so a row stays one line on a laptop.

## When not to use

- Picking from a known set of things: use a [CheckboxGroup] (npx serupa-docs Checkbox), a multiple [Combobox] (npx serupa-docs Combobox) or a [TransferList] (npx serupa-docs TransferList).
- Short values that need no fields of their own, such as tags or email addresses: use a [TagGroup] (npx serupa-docs TagGroup) with an [Input] (npx serupa-docs Input).
- Rows with many fields, or rows people mostly read: use a [Table] (npx serupa-docs Table), with a [Dialog] (npx serupa-docs Dialog) to add or edit one.

## Anatomy

Drawn from the `Errors` story.

1. **Legend** (`.srp-field-list__label`): the list's name.
2. **Row** (`.srp-field-list__row`): one item, a group named by `itemLabel`.
3. **Fields** (`.srp-field-list__fields`): the row's fields, side by side, wrapping in a narrow column.
4. **Remove** (`.srp-field-list__remove`): takes the row away; hidden at `min`.
5. **Row error** (`.srp-field-list__row-error`): what's wrong with that row.
6. **List error** (`.srp-field-list__error`): what's wrong with the list as a whole.
7. **Add** (`.srp-field-list__add`): adds a row at the end; at `max`, the limit shows beside it.

## Usage

- Name the rows by what they are, with their place: `itemLabel={(i) => "Phone " + (i + 1)}`. Screen readers hear it as the row's name, and it's in each Remove button ("Remove Phone 2") and in what's announced ("Phone 3 added").
- Say what Add adds: "Add phone", not "Add" or "Add more".
- Set `min` when the form needs at least that many: the list starts with `min` empty rows, and Remove is hidden while it has no more. Set `max` when there is a limit: Add then says why it does nothing ("Limit reached: 5.").
- Give each row's fields a `Field` with a visible label. Rows can repeat the same labels: the row's name tells them apart for screen readers.
- Pass `name` for a plain form submit: `name("number")` in a row gives `phones[1].number`.
- Show an error by row with `errors` (the row's place to its message), and one for the whole list with `error` ("Add a mobile number"). A row's error reaches its fields as `error` in the render function, to mark them invalid.
- `reorderable` puts a handle on each row when the order matters, such as the stops of a trip. Leave it off otherwise.

## Accessibility

- **Role and name:** a `<fieldset>` named by its legend. Each row is a group (`role="group"`) named by `itemLabel`, and described by its error. The list's hint and error describe the fieldset.
- **Keyboard:** Tab moves through each row's fields and its Remove button, then Add. Add and Remove are buttons; at `max`, Add stays a Tab stop (`aria-disabled`) and its description says why it does nothing.
- **Focus:** Add moves focus to the new row's first field. Remove moves it to the row before, or to Add when the first row goes. A row keeps its own fields as the rows around it come and go, so nothing typed moves to another row.
- **Announcements:** adding or removing a row is said politely ("Phone 3 added", "Phone 2 removed").
- **Contrast:** its legend, hint, limit and errors read 4.5:1 on the surface in every theme (`FieldList.test.tsx`).
- **What's still yours:** a visible label on each field, and the words for the rows and Add.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | `string` | | Goes to the `<fieldset>` |
| `label` | `ReactNode` | | The legend: the list's name |
| `hint` | `ReactNode` | none | Under the legend |
| `itemLabel` | `(index) => string` | | Each row's name from its place, counted from 0 |
| `children` | `(row, { index, label, name, update, error }) => ReactNode` | | One row's fields. `name(field)` gives its native name, `update(next)` changes the row (a value, or a function of the current one), `error` is the row's error |
| `newItem` | `() => T` | | The value of a row people add |
| `addLabel` | `string` | | The Add button's words |
| `value` / `defaultValue` | `T[]` | `min` new rows | The rows, controlled or to start with |
| `onValueChange` | `(rows) => void` | | Called with the rows when one is added, removed, changed or moved |
| `min` | number | `0` | The fewest rows: Remove is hidden while it has this many |
| `max` | number | none | The most rows: Add then does nothing and says why |
| `name` | `string` | none | The start of each field's native name (`phones[0].number`) |
| `error` | `ReactNode` | none | An error for the whole list, under the rows |
| `errors` | `ReactNode[]` | none | An error for each row, by place |
| `reorderable` | boolean | `false` | A handle on each row puts the rows in order ([SortableList] (npx serupa-docs SortableList)) |
| `disabled` | boolean | `false` | Disables every field, Remove and Add |

`className`, `ref` and other props go to the `<fieldset>`, which has `data-component="field-list"`.

## Component tokens

Each is an optional override: set it on the page, a container or one FieldList. The list lives in `src/components/FieldList/field-list.tokens.json` (also in `design-tokens/components/`).

<!-- token-table:start (made from field-list.tokens.json by npm run tokens: edit the descriptions there) -->
| Token | Default | Use |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--field-list-label-color` | `text` | The legend, the list's name (4.5:1 on the surface). |
| `--field-list-hint-color` | `text-muted` | The hint under the legend and the note beside Add at the limit (4.5:1 on the surface). |
| `--field-list-error-color` | `danger-text` | A row's error and the list's error (4.5:1 on the surface). |
| `--field-list-label-weight` | `font-medium` | The legend's weight. |
| `--field-list-gap` | `spacing-3` | Space between the legend, the rows and Add (12px). |
| `--field-list-row-gap` | `spacing-3` | Space between the fields of a row, and before its Remove button (12px). |
| `--field-list-error-gap` | `spacing-1` | Space between an error's icon and its words (4px). |
| `--field-list-field-min-width` | `spacing-40` | The narrowest a field gets before a row's fields wrap onto more lines (160px). |
<!-- token-table:end -->

components.name: FileUpload
components.summary: A drop area with a button for choosing files, and the chosen files listed under it with their size and a remove button.
components.guide:
# FileUpload

A drop area with a button for choosing files, and the chosen files listed under it with their size and a remove button. It checks file types, sizes and counts on the way in. Uploading is up to you: read the files from `onFilesChange`, or send them with a form through `name`.

**Also called:** dropzone, file input, file uploader.

```tsx
import { FileUpload } from "@diki-stwn/serupa-ds";

<FileUpload accept="image/*" maxSize={5_000_000} hint="PNG or JPG, up to 5 MB" onFilesChange={setAvatar} />

<FileUpload multiple maxFiles={10} accept=".pdf,.docx" files={files} onFilesChange={setFiles}
  onReject={(r) => console.log(r)} />
```

## When to use

- People attach one or more files to a form or a message: a profile photo, receipts, documents.
- Files must be a certain type, size or number, and people should hear about a bad file before they submit.
- Uploads where people often drag files in from their desktop or file manager.

## When not to use

- An empty area that only invites people to add content, with no file picker: use [EmptyState] (npx serupa-docs EmptyState) with `variant="dashed"` instead.
- Showing how far an upload has got: FileUpload doesn't upload; show a [Progress] (npx serupa-docs Progress) bar while your upload runs.

## Anatomy

Drawn from the `ReadOnly` story.

1. **Drop zone** (`.srp-file-upload__zone`): where files are dropped, with a button to choose them.
2. **Title** (`.srp-file-upload__title`): what to add.
3. **Hint** (`.srp-file-upload__hint`): which types and sizes are accepted.
4. **File list** (`.srp-file-upload__list`): the files added so far.
5. **File** (`.srp-file-upload__item`): one file, drawn as an [Attachment] (npx serupa-docs Attachment): its kind's icon, the name (a long one is cut in the middle so its ending stays), its kind and size, and a remove button.

## Usage

- Say the allowed types and the largest size in `hint` ("PNG or JPG, up to 5 MB"), and keep it in step with `accept` and `maxSize`. Both are client-side guidance only: always validate file types and sizes on the server.
- Without `multiple`, a new file replaces the old one; set `multiple` (and `maxFiles` if there's a limit) when people may add several.
- Use `onReject` if you need to log refused files or show the reason elsewhere; the messages already show under the area.
- A refused type says what the field takes, in words from `accept`: "photo.heic isn’t a PNG or JPG." Types with no short name, such as `application/vnd.ms-excel`, get "photo.heic: this type of file isn’t accepted."
- Change `title` and `buttonLabel` to name what's expected ("Drag your CV here", "Choose a CV").
- Uploading as files are added: keep each file's upload in your state and return it from `fileStatus`. Pass `onRetry` to give a failed file a retry button, and remove a file from `files` to cancel it.

```tsx
const [files, setFiles] = useState<File[]>([]);
const [status, setStatus] = useState(new Map<File, FileUploadStatus>());
<FileUpload multiple files={files} onFilesChange={(next) => { setFiles(next); next.filter((f) => !status.has(f)).forEach(upload); }}
  fileStatus={(f) => status.get(f)} onRetry={upload} thumbnails />
// upload(f) sets { state: "uploading", progress } as it goes, then { state: "done" } or { state: "error", message }.
```

## Behavior

- The button opens the file picker; files can also be dropped on the area, which highlights while they're dragged over it. Text or a link dragged across it doesn't highlight it. While it can take files, a file dropped just outside the area is ignored rather than opened by the browser in place of the page. A dropped folder is refused ("Invoices is a folder: choose the files in it instead."), and a file that's already in the list is skipped with a message ("report.pdf is already added.").
- Pasting (Ctrl+V, ⌘V on Apple devices) while focus is on the choose button or a remove button adds the clipboard's files, such as a screenshot, checked like dropped ones. It works from the keyboard alone. A paste with no files in it does nothing. `readOnly` and `disabled` ignore it.
- Files that don't fit are listed under the area in danger text and passed to `onReject`; the same file picked twice is skipped quietly.
- Removing a file moves focus to the next file's remove button, or the one before it, so clearing several files stays in the list; with none left, focus goes to the choose button.
- A long file name is cut in the middle, as Finder and Drive do: "quarterly-report-fi…t-2026.pdf". The last few characters and the extension stay, so files that differ only by year or version still look different. Hover shows the full name, and it's laid out in its own direction. It is cut wherever FileUpload sits, a grid cell or a flex row included, so a long name never widens the page.
- With `fileStatus`, each file shows its upload: while `uploading`, a small bar under its name, filled to `progress` (0 to 100) or moving on its own without one; when `done`, "Complete" with a check after its size; on `error`, a danger outline and the `message` (default "Couldn’t upload") under its name, and with `onRetry` a "Try again" button before the remove button. FileUpload doesn't upload anything itself.
- Each file's icon shows its kind, the same icon an [Attachment] (npx serupa-docs Attachment) shows for it: PDF, image, spreadsheet, document, slides, archive, code, audio, video or other, from its MIME type and then its extension.
- With `thumbnails`, an image file shows a 40px picture of itself in place of its type icon. The picture is decoded in the browser (`createImageBitmap`) and drawn on a canvas, so no URL made from the file reaches the page. An image the browser can't decode, such as HEIC in most browsers, keeps the icon.
- The native input always holds the listed files, including dropped ones, so a form sends exactly what's shown.
- `readOnly` shows the files without remove buttons and ignores the button and drops; the files are still submitted. `disabled` also draws it in the neutral disabled colors and leaves the files out of the form.

### Do and don't

- **Do:** Say the allowed types and the largest size in `hint`, matching `accept` and `maxSize`. (`DoSayLimits`)
- **Don't:** Leave the limits out: people learn them only when a file is refused. (`DontHideLimits`)

## Accessibility

- The button is the keyboard and screen-reader way in; dragging is an extra. Messages about refused files are `role="alert"`, so they're announced. They come from labels (`fileWrongType`, `fileTooLarge`, `fileTooMany`, `fileOnlyOne`, `fileFolder`, `fileAlreadyAdded`), Indonesian in `idLabels`, and `onReject` gets the same text.
- Adding and removing files are said politely, since the list changes away from focus: "report.pdf added.", "3 files added.", "report.pdf removed." (`filesAdded`, `fileRemoved`).
- Each upload bar is a `progressbar` named by its file. A file that was uploading is said politely when it finishes or fails: "report.pdf: complete", "report.pdf: Couldn’t upload" (`progressComplete`, `fileError`); one that arrives done, such as a restored draft, isn't. A retry button is named by its text and the file ("Try again report.pdf", `tryAgain`) and described by the failure message. Thumbnails are decorative (`aria-hidden`): the name next to them says what the file is.
- Submitted without a required file, FileUpload doesn't let the browser point its bubble at the hidden input: it shows "Choose a file." (`fileMissing`) in the same alert area, makes the button invalid and described by it, and focuses the button when it's the first invalid field. Choosing a file clears it.
- In a [Field] (npx serupa-docs Field), the button is named by the label and its own text ("Due date, Choose a file") and described by the Field's hint and error, then the `hint`. `aria-describedby` goes to the button too. A button supports none of `aria-invalid`, `aria-errormessage` and `aria-required`, so the button is described by the Field's `error` (or your own `aria-errormessage`), and with `required` by "Required" first (`labels.required`). `aria-invalid` goes on the native input.
- Text keeps 4.5:1 (also while dragging), and the icons 3:1, in every theme; the dashed outline is a field's border (`field-border`, darker under the pointer), since its words and the Choose button mark it (`FileUpload.test.tsx`).
- In forced colors (Windows High Contrast), the drag-over area turns its border solid and `Highlight`, so the state still shows without the primary fill.
- **Keyboard:** Tab reaches the choose button, where Enter or Space opens the file picker, then each failed file's retry button and each chosen file's remove button. Dropping files needs a pointer, so the button is the keyboard's way in; Ctrl+V (⌘V) there pastes copied files. Read-only, the choose button stays focusable but opens nothing.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `files` | `File[]` | | Controlled. |
| `onFilesChange` | `(files: File[]) => void` | | When files are added or removed. |
| `onReject` | `(rejections) => void` | | Files that weren't added, each with `reason` (`'type'`, `'size'`, `'count'`, `'folder'` or `'duplicate'`) and a `message`. |
| `accept` | `string` | | As for `<input accept>`: MIME types, `image/*` or extensions. |
| `multiple` | `boolean` | `false` | Without it, a new file replaces the old one. |
| `maxSize` | `number` | | The largest file, in bytes. |
| `maxFiles` | `number` | | The most files, with `multiple`. |
| `disabled` | `boolean` | `false` | |
| `invalid` | `boolean` | `false` | A solid danger outline on the drop area and `aria-invalid` on the native input. Set for you in a Field with an `error`, whose message describes the button. |
| `required` | `boolean` | `false` | `required` on the native input (the form's check) and a hidden "Required" in the button's description. A required Field adds the description for you. |
| `readOnly` | `boolean` | `false` | The files are listed and submitted but can't change: the button stays focusable with `aria-disabled` and opens no picker, drops are ignored, and there are no remove buttons. |
| `name` | `string` | | Sends the files with a form. |
| `form` | `string` | | The id of the form the files submit with, when the FileUpload sits outside it. |
| `id` | `string` | | Goes to the native input, so a `<label htmlFor>` or Field can point at it. Clicking such a label opens the picker and puts focus on the choose button. |
| `title` | `ReactNode` | `'Drag files here'` or `'Drag a file here'` | |
| `buttonLabel` | `string` | `'Choose files'` or `'Choose a file'` | |
| `hint` | `ReactNode` | | A muted line such as "PNG or JPG, up to 5 MB". The button is described by it. |
| `removeLabel` | `(name) => string` | `` `Remove ${name}` `` | The remove buttons' names. |
| `fileStatus` | `(file) => FileUploadStatus \| null` | | Each file's upload: `{ state: 'uploading' \| 'done' \| 'error', progress?, message? }`. |
| `onRetry` | `(file) => void` | | A failed file's retry button calls it. Without it there's no retry button. |
| `thumbnails` | `boolean` | `false` | A picture of each image file in place of its type icon. |

`formatFileSize(bytes, locale?)` is exported too: `1.5 MB` or `820 kB`, in steps of 1000, as macOS, iOS and Android count (so a `maxSize` of `5_000_000` reads "5 MB", and one of `5 * 1024 * 1024` reads "5.2 MB"), or with a locale the same as FormattedNumber's `format="bytes"` (`formatFileSize(1_500_000, "id-ID")` is `1,5 MB`). FileUpload writes each size, and the size in a refusal, in the provider's locale. `className`, `ref` and other props go to the root `<div>`. Its `focus()` and `autoFocus` move focus to the choose button, so a form library that focuses the first invalid field after a failed submit lands on it.

## Component tokens

Each is an optional override: set it on the page, a container or one upload. The list lives in `src/components/FileUpload/file-upload.tokens.json` (also in `design-tokens/components/`).

| `--file-upload-zone-border` | `field-border` | The drop area's dashed outline: a field's border, which darkens under the pointer (zone-border-hover). Its words and the Choose button mark it, as a field's label does. |
| `--file-upload-zone-border-hover` | `field-border-hover` | The drop area's outline while the pointer is over it (a click there browses for files). |

components.name: FilterBar
components.summary: The filters on a list or a table, as a row of chips.
components.guide:
# FilterBar

The filters on a list or a table, as a row of chips. "Add filter" opens a menu of the fields not yet in use; each chip says its filter in words ("Status is Open or Closed") and opens its editor in a popover; its × removes it, and "Clear all" removes every one. The value is plain data, so the app can keep it in the URL, and an optional results count is announced as it changes.

**Also called:** filters, filter chips, faceted search.

```tsx
import { FilterBar, type FilterField } from "@diki-stwn/serupa-ds";

const fields: FilterField[] = [
  { id: "status", label: "Status", type: "select", multiple: true, options: [{ value: "open", label: "Open" }, { value: "closed", label: "Closed" }] },
  { id: "owner", label: "Owner", type: "select", options: ["Ana", "Budi"] },
  { id: "due", label: "Due", type: "date-range" },
  { id: "archived", label: "Archived", type: "boolean" },
  { id: "q", label: "Title", type: "text" },
];

// value: { status: ["open"], due: { start: "2026-11-02", end: "2026-11-08" } }
<FilterBar fields={fields} value={filters} onValueChange={setFilters} resultsCount={rows.length} />
```

## When to use

- A list, table or board people narrow by several fields, where the filters in use should stay visible.
- Filters people add a few at a time from a longer set of fields.

## When not to use

- One or two filters that are always there: put a [SearchInput] (npx serupa-docs SearchInput), [Select] (npx serupa-docs Select) or [SegmentedControl] (npx serupa-docs SegmentedControl) in a [Toolbar] (npx serupa-docs Toolbar).
- Many filters people set at once, as a form: put them in a [Drawer] (npx serupa-docs Drawer) with an Apply button.
- Switching between saved views: use [Tabs] (npx serupa-docs Tabs) or a Select.

## Anatomy

Drawn from the `Playground` story.

1. **Chip** (`.srp-filter-bar__chip`): one filter, outlined; dashed while nothing is chosen.
2. **Chip button** (`.srp-filter-bar__edit`): the filter in words; it opens the filter's editor.
3. **Remove** (`.srp-filter-bar__remove`): takes the filter away.
4. **Add filter** (`.srp-filter-bar__add`): a menu of the fields not in use.
5. **Clear all** (`.srp-filter-bar__clear`): takes every filter away.
6. **Count** (`.srp-filter-bar__count`): how many results are left, at the end.

## Usage

- Order `fields` as people think of them, most used first: the menu lists them in that order.
- Keep labels short ("Status", "Due"): they start each chip.
- Give `resultsCount` whenever you know it: it tells people what their filters did, and screen readers hear it change.
- The value has a key for each filter in use: `select` gives a string (or an array with `multiple`), `date-range` `{ start, end }` as "yyyy-mm-dd" (either may be null, and its chip then says "Due from Nov 2, 2026" or "Due until Nov 8, 2026" with the `filterFrom` and `filterUntil` labels), `boolean` `true`, `text` a string. A filter whose editor closes with nothing chosen is taken out.
- A `boolean` filter is on as soon as it's added, with no editor to open first; its chip opens a switch to turn it off.
- Put a sort or a view switch in `actions`, so it sits with the filters and before the count.

### Do and don't

- **Do:** Give `resultsCount` whenever you know it: it tells people what their filters did, and screen readers hear it change. (`DoShowCount`)
- **Don't:** Leave it out when you know it: people can't tell whether a filter narrowed anything. (`DontHideCount`)

## Accessibility

- **Role and name:** the bar is a `group` named "Filters" (or `aria-label`), with the chips in a list. Each chip is a button that says its filter in full, and opens a dialog named by the field; its × is "Remove filter: Status".
- **Keyboard:** see the table. After a chip is removed, focus moves to the next chip (or the one before, or "Add filter"); after "Clear all", to "Add filter"; closing an editor returns focus to its chip.
- **Long chips:** a chip too long for the bar ends in an ellipsis and shows what it says in full in a tooltip on hover and on keyboard focus; its name is still the whole sentence.
- **Announcements:** the count is a `status`, so a change is read out politely.
- **Contrast:** chip text reads 4.5:1 on the chip and its outline 3:1, the count 4.5:1 on the page, in every theme (`FilterBar.test.tsx`).
- **What's still yours:** labels and option names that make sense read aloud in a sentence ("Owner is Ana").

### Keyboard

| Key | Does |
| --- | --- |
| Tab | Through each chip and its ×, then "Add filter", "Clear all" and any actions |
| Enter, Space (on a chip) | Opens its editor |
| Escape | Closes the editor (or the menu) |
| Enter (in a text filter) | Closes it and keeps the text |
| ↑ ↓ (in the menu) | Moves between fields |

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `fields` | `FilterField[]` | | `{ id, label, type }`, `type` one of `'select'` (with `options` and `multiple`), `'date-range'`, `'boolean'`, `'text'` (with `placeholder`) |
| `value` | `FilterValues` | | The filters in use, by field id (controlled) |
| `defaultValue` | `FilterValues` | `{}` | The filters it starts with (uncontrolled) |
| `onValueChange` | `(value) => void` | | Called with every filter in use when one is added, changed, removed or cleared |
| `resultsCount` | `number` | | Shown at the end as "24 results" and announced when it changes |
| `actions` | `ReactNode` | | Before the count, such as a sort Select |
| `id` | `string` | | Goes to the root `<div>`. |

`className`, `ref` and other props go to the root `<div>`.

## Component tokens

Each is an optional override: set it on the page, a container or one FilterBar. The list lives in `src/components/FilterBar/filter-bar.tokens.json` (also in `design-tokens/components/`).

<!-- token-table:start (made from filter-bar.tokens.json by npm run tokens: edit the descriptions there) -->
| Token | Default | Use |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--filter-bar-text` | `text` | Chip text (4.5:1 on chip-bg). |
| `--filter-bar-muted` | `text-muted` | The results count (4.5:1 on the page). |
| `--filter-bar-chip-bg` | `surface` | A chip's background. |
| `--filter-bar-chip-border` | `border-strong` | A chip's outline: the light one a tag and an outline Badge have (its words mark the chip). |
| `--filter-bar-chip-bg-hover` | `surface-hover` | A chip's fill under the pointer. |
| `--filter-bar-chip-open` | `pressed` | A chip's fill while held and while its editor is open (its text keeps 4.5:1 on it). |
| `--filter-bar-focus-ring` | `focus-ring` | The ring around a focused chip. |
| `--filter-bar-chip-radius` | `radius-control` | A chip's corners (6px). |
| `--filter-bar-gap` | `spacing-2` | Space between chips, buttons and the count (8px). |
| `--filter-bar-editor-width` | `spacing-56` | The narrowest an editor is (224px). |
<!-- token-table:end -->

components.name: Form
components.summary: A `<form>` checked against one schema.
components.guide:
# Form

A `<form>` checked against one schema. The schema says what each answer must be and what to say when it isn't; the form shows that on each field at the right moment, lists every problem at the top when a submit fails, and hands `onSubmit` the checked values, typed. No field needs wiring: each Field finds its message by its control's `name`.

**Also called:** form validation, schema form, form wrapper.

```tsx
import * as z from "zod";
import { Form, Field, Input, Button } from "@diki-stwn/serupa-ds";

const SignUp = z.object({
  name: z.string().min(1, "Enter your full name"),
  email: z.email("Enter an email address like name@example.com"),
});

<Form aria-label="Create an account" schema={SignUp} onSubmit={async (values) => { await api.signUp(values); }}>
  <Field label="Full name"><Input name="name" autoComplete="name" /></Field>
  <Field label="Email"><Input name="email" type="email" autoComplete="email" /></Field>
  <Button type="submit">Create account</Button>
</Form>
```

## When to use

- Any form people submit: sign-up, checkout, settings, an application. One schema gives the rules, the messages and the types.
- A form in steps ([FormSteps](#steps)), one that keeps a draft, or one whose server can turn the answers down.

## When not to use

- A single control that saves itself as it changes, such as a [Switch] (npx serupa-docs Switch) in a settings list: no submit, so no form to check.
- Editing one value where it's shown: use [InlineEdit] (npx serupa-docs InlineEdit).
- A search box: use [SearchInput] (npx serupa-docs SearchInput) in a plain `<form role="search">`.

## Anatomy

Drawn from the `MultiStep` story. The parts are FormSteps'.

1. **Progress** (`.srp-form-steps__progress`): the Stepper above the steps, showing which one people are on.
2. **Step** (`.srp-form-steps__panel`): one step's fields; the steps not showing stay in the form, hidden.
3. **Step heading** (`.srp-form-steps__title`): the step's title; focus moves here when people move to the step.
4. **Buttons** (`.srp-form-steps__actions`): Next (or the last step's submit button), then Back.

## Usage

- **Any schema library.** Pass a Zod 4 (or 3.24 and later), Valibot 1, ArkType or other [Standard Schema](https://standardschema.dev). Serupa depends on none of them: use the one the project has. Without a schema, the controls' own constraints (`required`, `type="email"`, `maxLength`) are checked, in the provider's words.
- **Names are paths.** `name="address.city"` is `{ address: { city } }`, and a [FieldList] (npx serupa-docs FieldList)'s `people[1].email` is `{ people: [, { email }] }`. A schema issue at that path is that field's message.
- **Values come as the controls hold them**: text as strings, a lone checkbox as `true` or `false`, a set of checkboxes with one name as the values checked, radios as the one checked. Turn text into numbers or dates in the schema: `z.string().min(1, "Enter your age").transform(Number).pipe(z.number().min(18, "You must be 18 or over"))`.
- **When it checks** (the [Forms](?path=/docs/guides-forms--docs) rules): a field when it's left, never while it's typed in; once it has shown a message, again as it changes, so the message goes the moment the answer is right; everything on submit. A message that depends on another field ("The passwords don't match") updates as either changes.
- **The messages** are the schema's: say what's wrong and how to fix it, "Enter a date in the future", not "Invalid date". The same words show on the field and in the summary.
- **A failed submit** shows an [ErrorSummary] (npx serupa-docs ErrorSummary) at the top, listing the problems in the fields' order, each a link to its field; it takes focus, and the page's title starts with "Error:" while it shows. `summary={false}` leaves it out (place your own `<ErrorSummary />` inside the form, or focus moves to the first field with a problem).
- **The server's answer**: return `{ errors: { email: "That email already has an account" }, message }` from `onSubmit`, or pass `errors` and `message` (a form action's answer). Each shows on its field, and in the summary; `message` shows in an alert at the top. Editing a field takes its server message away.
- **Checks after the schema**, such as "That username is taken": `checks={{ username: async (value, { signal }) => … }}` runs once the field passes the schema, says "Checking…" under it meanwhile, cancels an older check when the value changes, and waits for a pause in typing. Submit waits for them.
- **Fields that depend on others**: `useFormValue("country")` inside the form gives a field's value as it changes. Render the dependent field only when it applies, and let the schema require it only then.
- **Drafts**: `draft="application"` keeps the answers in the browser as people type and fills them back in when they come back; passwords (shown or hidden), card numbers and one-time codes are never kept. It's forgotten once the form is sent. `useForm()` gives `draftSavedAt` for a [SaveStatus] (npx serupa-docs SaveStatus), `draftRestored`, and `discardDraft()` for a "Start again" button.
- **Unsaved changes**: `warnUnsaved` asks before the page is closed or reloaded while there are changes that weren't sent. In a [Dialog] (npx serupa-docs Dialog), pass `onUnsavedChanges` to its `unsaved`, so closing it asks "Discard changes?" first.
- **Sending**: a submit [Button] (npx serupa-docs Button) inside shows loading while `onSubmit`'s promise runs, and a second submit does nothing until it settles. Keep what people typed when it fails.
- **`defaultValues`** fill the fields by name; a control's own `value` or `defaultValue` wins. Put the named control straight inside its Field for this; one wrapped deeper takes `defaultValue` itself.

### Steps

`FormSteps` splits one Form into steps with a [Stepper] (npx serupa-docs Stepper) above them. Next checks only the current step's fields and moves on when they pass; Back and the Stepper's done steps go back without checking. Moving to a step focuses its heading. The last step's button submits the whole form; a problem on an earlier step is in the summary, and its link opens that step. Steps not showing stay in the form (`hidden="until-found"`), so their answers are kept and sent.

```tsx
<Form aria-label="Open an account" schema={Business} onSubmit={open}>
  <FormSteps submitLabel="Open the account">
    <FormStep title="Business">…fields…</FormStep>
    <FormStep title="Address">…fields…</FormStep>
    <FormStep title="Plan">…fields…</FormStep>
  </FormSteps>
</Form>
```

## Accessibility

- **Role and name:** a `<form>`. Give it a name (`aria-label`, or `aria-labelledby` its heading) when the page has more than one, so it's a form landmark.
- **Messages:** each is on its field (the control is `aria-invalid` and described by it) and said politely when it appears, as Field does. A failed submit's summary takes focus and is read whole; each link moves focus to its field and shows the field's label.
- **Focus:** nothing moves while people type. A failed submit focuses the summary (or with `summary={false}`, the first field with a problem); FormSteps focuses the new step's heading.
- **Keyboard:** the form's own: Enter in a text field submits it. In FormSteps, Enter in a text field goes to the next step (checking it first), and submits on the last; Next (or the submit button) comes before Back in the Tab order.
- **Contrast:** it draws no text of its own; the fields, summary, alert and buttons each meet 4.5:1 in every theme.
- **What's still yours:** a label on every field ([Field] (npx serupa-docs Field)), messages that say how to fix the answer, and `autoComplete` on fields about the person.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `schema` | Standard Schema | none | Zod, Valibot, ArkType. Its messages are the fields' errors and `onSubmit` gets its output |
| `defaultValues` | object | none | The values the fields start with, by name |
| `onSubmit` | `(values, form) => void \| { errors, message } \| Promise` | | Called with the checked values. Answer `{ errors, message }` when the server turns them down |
| `checks` | `{ [name]: (value, { values, signal }) => message \| Promise }` | none | Checks once a field passes the schema |
