| `errors` | `{ [name]: ReactNode } \| null` | none | Messages from a server, such as a form action's answer; a new object shows them again |
| `message` | `ReactNode` | none | A server message that isn't one field's, in an alert at the top |
| `draft` | `string` | none | Keeps a draft in the browser under this key |
| `warnUnsaved` | boolean | `false` | Asks before the page goes while there are changes |
| `summary` | boolean | `true` | The ErrorSummary at the top after a failed submit |
| `onUnsavedChanges` | `(unsaved) => void` | | When the form gets changes that weren't sent, and when it has none again |
| `onEdit` | `(values) => void` | | The unchecked values whenever a field changes |

`id`, `className`, `ref` and other props go to the `<form>`, which has `data-component="form"` and `noValidate`.

`useForm()` inside the form gives `values()`, `defaults`, `validate(names?)`, `setErrors(errors, message?)`, `submit()`, `reset()`, `discardDraft()`, `dirty`, `submitting`, `submitCount`, `draftSavedAt` and `draftRestored`. `useFormValue(name)` gives one field's value as it changes.

**FormSteps:** `children` (FormStep elements), `submitLabel` (the last step's button), `step` / `defaultStep` / `onStepChange` (from 0), `headingLevel` (2 to 6, default 2). **FormStep:** `title`, `description`, `optional`, `children`.

## Component tokens

Each is an optional override: set it on the page, a container or one Form. The list lives in `src/components/Form/form.tokens.json` (also in `design-tokens/components/`).

<!-- token-table:start (made from form.tokens.json by npm run tokens: edit the descriptions there) -->
| Token | Default | Use |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--form-focus-ring` | `focus-ring` | The ring around a step's heading when it has focus from the keyboard. |
| `--form-gap` | `spacing-6` | Space between the form's parts: the summary, each field, the buttons (24px). |
| `--form-actions-gap` | `spacing-3` | Space between FormSteps' Next (or submit) and Back buttons (12px). |
| `--form-steps-gap` | `spacing-8` | Space between FormSteps' progress bar, the step and its buttons (32px). |
| `--form-step-title-weight` | `font-semibold` | The weight of each step's heading. |
<!-- token-table:end -->

components.name: FormattedDate
components.summary: Writes a date, a time or a range of dates the way the reader's language does: "November 20, 2026" in English, "20 November 2026" in Indonesian, "٢٠ نوفمبر ٢٠٢٦" in Egyptian Arabic.
components.guide:
# FormattedDate

Writes a date, a time or a range of dates the way the reader's language does: "November 20, 2026" in English, "20 November 2026" in Indonesian, "٢٠ نوفمبر ٢٠٢٦" in Egyptian Arabic. A `"yyyy-mm-dd"` day stays that day in every time zone, and a moment is shown in the reader's own time.

**Also called:** date format, date display, formatted time.

```tsx
import { FormattedDate, formatDate } from "@diki-stwn/serupa-ds";

<FormattedDate value="2026-11-20" />                                        // "Nov 20, 2026"
<FormattedDate value="2026-11-20" dateStyle="long" />                       // "November 20, 2026"
<FormattedDate value={order.placedAt} dateStyle="long" timeStyle="short" />  // "November 20, 2026 at 9:30 AM", in the reader's time
<FormattedDate value="2026-11-20" to="2026-11-22" />                        // "Nov 20 – 22, 2026"
<FormattedDate value={meeting.at} timeStyle="short" dateStyle={false} timeZone="Asia/Jakarta" />  // "4:30 PM"
<FormattedDate value="2026-11-20" options={{ month: "long", year: "numeric" }} />  // "November 2026"

formatDate("2026-11-20", "id", { dateStyle: "long" })                      // "20 November 2026", outside React or in a Server Component
```

## When to use

- Any date people read or act on: a due date, the day an order was placed, an invoice's date, a column of dates in a table.
- An event's dates, or a stay's, as a range: the month and year are said once.

## When not to use

- How long ago or how soon, when that matters more than the day ("3 minutes ago", "in 2 days"): [RelativeTime] (npx serupa-docs RelativeTime), which switches to the date itself after a week.
- How long something takes ("1 hr, 30 min"): [Duration] (npx serupa-docs Duration).
- A date people type or pick: [DateField] (npx serupa-docs DateField) or [DatePicker] (npx serupa-docs DatePicker).

## Anatomy

Drawn from the `WithTime` story.

1. **Date** (`.srp-formatted-date`): the `<time>` holding the words, with the moment in its `datetime`.
2. **Half** (`.srp-formatted-date__half`): the date, or the time, of a date with a time. The line wraps between the two halves, never inside one. Only short halves (the short and medium styles) are kept whole: a long one ("Wednesday, September 30, 2026") wraps like a sentence, as it could be wider than the line.

## Usage

- `value` is a `Date`, a timestamp in milliseconds, an ISO date and time (`"2026-11-20T09:30:00Z"`), or a plain `"yyyy-mm-dd"` day. Pass a day as that string: `new Date("2026-11-20")` is UTC midnight, which is the 19th west of Greenwich, while `"2026-11-20"` is the 20th everywhere.
- `dateStyle` is `'medium'` by default; `'full'`, `'long'` and `'short'` say more or less, and `false` leaves the date out for a time on its own. `timeStyle` adds the time of day; a `"yyyy-mm-dd"` day has none, so it's left out there.
- `to` makes a range: "Nov 20 – 22, 2026", "Nov 28 – Dec 3, 2026". A range that starts and ends on the same day is written once.
- `timeZone` writes a moment in that IANA zone ("Asia/Jakarta"), the way a venue's local time is shown to someone elsewhere. Without it, a moment is in the reader's zone.
- `options` takes any other `Intl.DateTimeFormat` option. With one of the parts (`weekday`, `year`, `month`, `day`, `hour`, `minute`…), only those parts are written, and `dateStyle` and `timeStyle` are left out, as Intl asks: `{ month: "long", year: "numeric" }` is "November 2026".
- The words follow the locale from `SerupaProvider` (or the `locale` prop, or the browser's), with its own digits and month names.
- A value it can't read, or a day not on the calendar ("2026-02-31"), shows nothing; in development it warns once (`date-value`). Options Intl rejects, such as a `timeZone` of "WIB", write a medium date with a `date-options` warning, rather than throwing and unmounting the page.

## Behavior

- Rendered on the server, a moment with no `timeZone` is written in UTC, since the server can't know the reader's zone, and the page hydrates with the same text. Right after, it's rewritten in the reader's zone. A `"yyyy-mm-dd"` day, and a moment with `timeZone`, are the same on the server and in the browser and never change. Pass `timeZone` when the server knows the reader's zone, so the first text is the final one.
- It's inline text in the surrounding font and color, and wraps like the sentence around it.
- With a `locale` of its own it carries that locale's direction (`dir`) with its `lang`, so an English date in a right-to-left page keeps its order; without one it takes the page's.

## Accessibility

- **Role and name:** a `<time>` whose text is the date in words and whose `datetime` is the machine-readable day (`"2026-11-20"`) or instant (`"2026-11-20T09:30:00.000Z"`). A range is a `<span>` with a `<time>` for each end's own words.
- **Keyboard:** none: inline text, not focusable.
- **Contrast:** it takes the surrounding text's color, so it reads as the text around it does.
- **What's still yours:** say what the date is ("Due", "Placed on"), in the words beside it. Use `'long'` or `'full'` where a short date could be misread: "11/12/26" is 12 November in the UK and 11 December in the US.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | string | none | Goes to the root `<time>` (the `<span>` for a range). |
| `value` | `Date \| number \| string` | | The moment, or a `"yyyy-mm-dd"` day. |
| `to` | `Date \| number \| string` | | Where a range ends. |
| `dateStyle` | `'full' \| 'long' \| 'medium' \| 'short' \| false` | `'medium'` | How much of the date; `false` for none. |
| `timeStyle` | `'full' \| 'long' \| 'medium' \| 'short'` | none | The time of day too. |
| `timeZone` | `string` | the reader's | An IANA zone a moment is written in. |
| `options` | `Intl.DateTimeFormatOptions` | | Any other Intl option; with parts, they write it alone. |
| `locale` | `string` | the provider's, else the browser's | When it differs from the provider's, the element carries `lang`. |

Every other prop, `className` and `ref` go to the `<time>` (the `<span>` for a range), which has `data-component="formatted-date"`.

## Component tokens

None: it uses the surrounding text's font and color.

components.name: FormattedNumber
components.summary: Writes a number the way the reader's language does: `1.234,5` in Indonesian, `1,234.5` in English, `١٬٢٣٤٫٥` in Egyptian Arabic.
components.guide:
# FormattedNumber

Writes a number the way the reader's language does: `1.234,5` in Indonesian, `1,234.5` in English, `١٬٢٣٤٫٥` in Egyptian Arabic. It also writes short numbers (1.2K), percentages, money, file sizes and units, so a page doesn't mix localized dates with English numbers.

**Also called:** number format, currency display.

```tsx
import { FormattedNumber, formatNumber } from "@diki-stwn/serupa-ds";

<FormattedNumber value={1234.5} />                                   // "1,234.5"
<FormattedNumber value={1234567} format="compact" />                 // "1.2M", with "1,234,567" as its tooltip
<FormattedNumber value={0.456} format="percent" />                   // "46%"
<FormattedNumber value={19.99} format="currency" currency="USD" />    // "$19.99" in en, "US$19,99" in id
<FormattedNumber value={1500000} format="bytes" />                   // "1.5 MB"
<FormattedNumber value={50} format="unit" unit="kilometer-per-hour" />  // "50 km/h"
<FormattedNumber value={0.031} format="percent" options={{ signDisplay: "always", maximumFractionDigits: 1 }} />  // "+3.1%"

formatNumber(1234, "id-ID", { format: "compact" })                  // "1,2 rb", outside React or in a Server Component
```

## When to use

- Any number people read: counts, totals, prices, percentages, sizes, measurements, in text or in a table.
- Large counts where the exact figure doesn't matter at a glance (followers, views): `format="compact"`.

## When not to use

- A number people type: use [NumberInput] (npx serupa-docs NumberInput), which formats as they type.
- Codes that only look like numbers (an order number, a phone number, a postcode): write them as they are, since grouping would change them.
- A share of a task that's in progress: use [Progress] (npx serupa-docs Progress); a level within a range: [Meter] (npx serupa-docs Meter).

## Usage

- The words follow the locale from `SerupaProvider` (or the `locale` prop, or the browser's), including its digits.
- `percent` takes a fraction, as `Intl.NumberFormat` does: `0.45` is 45%. Divide by 100 first if your value is already a percentage.
- `currency` needs `currency`, an ISO 4217 code. The amount uses that currency's usual minor units (2 for USD and EUR, 0 for JPY); pass `options={{ maximumFractionDigits: 0 }}` to drop them, or `minimumFractionDigits: 2` to show them. Without a code it writes a plain number.
- `bytes` steps by 1000, like `formatFileSize`, with one decimal under 10 ("1.5 MB") and none above ("820 kB"). A size that rounds up to 1000 takes the next unit (999,999 is "1 MB", not "1,000 kB"), and bytes are whole and written by their long name ("2 bytes" for 1.5, "1 byte"), as `formatFileSize` writes them too, with or without a locale. Steps of 1000, as macOS, iOS and Android count and as the SI names kB, MB and GB mean, so 1,500,000 bytes is "1.5 MB". Write a limit as `5_000_000` to have it read "5 MB"; `5 * 1024 * 1024` reads "5.2 MB".
- `unit` takes any unit `Intl.NumberFormat` knows (`"celsius"`, `"liter"`, `"kilometer-per-hour"`), written short.
- `options` takes any other `Intl.NumberFormat` option and wins over the format's own: `maximumFractionDigits`, `signDisplay`, `currencyDisplay: "name"`, `compactDisplay: "long"`.
- Options Intl rejects, such as a currency `"US"` or a unit `"km/h"`, write the plain number with a `number-options` warning in development, rather than throwing and unmounting the page.
- Each locale and set of options builds its `Intl.NumberFormat` once and keeps it, so a long table of numbers re-renders without building thousands of formatters.
- In a table column, numbers line up on tabular digits; align the column to the end too.
- `animate` makes a changed value show what moved: only the characters that differ from the last value fade in out of a slight blur ("Rp 1.485.000" to "Rp 1.500.000" fades "500"). Use it for a number that changes now and then while someone watches it: a cart total, a dashboard figure after a filter, a count after an action. Leave it off for a value that ticks every second (a timer, a live price), where the fade would never settle, and in long tables.

### Do and don't

- **Do:** Pass `percent` a fraction, as `Intl.NumberFormat` takes it: `0.45` is 45%. (`DoFraction`)
- **Don't:** Pass a value that's already a percentage: 45 comes out as 4,500%. Divide by 100 first. (`DontWholePercent`)

## Accessibility

- It's a `<data>` whose `value` holds the number for machines; screen readers read its words.
- A compact number's full value is in `title`, which shows on hover but isn't reliably read out. Where the exact figure matters, show it as text.
- It doesn't wrap: "Rp 150.000" stays on one line.
- With `animate`, the changed characters stay inline text, so a screen reader still reads one number. The change isn't announced: when it matters, say it with `announce()` as well. With reduced motion, the characters change at once.
- **Keyboard:** none: inline text, not focusable.
- With a `locale` of its own it carries that locale's direction (`dir`) with its `lang`, so "50 km/h" in English keeps its order in a right-to-left page.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | string | none | Goes to the root `<data>`. |
| `value` | `number \| bigint` | | The number. `NaN` renders an empty `<data>`. |
| `format` | `'decimal' \| 'compact' \| 'percent' \| 'currency' \| 'bytes' \| 'unit'` | `'decimal'` | How to write it. |
| `currency` | `string` | | With `currency`: the ISO 4217 code, `"IDR"`, `"USD"`. |
| `unit` | `string` | | With `unit`: a unit `Intl.NumberFormat` knows. |
| `options` | `Intl.NumberFormatOptions` | | Any other options; they win. |
| `animate` | `boolean` | `false` | When the value changes, the characters that changed fade in over `motion-change-sm`. |
| `locale` | `string` | the provider's, else the browser's | When it differs from the provider's, the element carries `lang`, so screen readers read the number in that language. |
Every other prop, `className` and `ref` go to the `<data>`, which has `data-component="formatted-number"` and `data-format`. Your own `title` wins over the compact tooltip.

`formatNumber(value, locale?, options?)` gives the same words outside React, and in a Server Component; `options` takes `format` and every `Intl.NumberFormat` option.

## Component tokens

None: it uses the surrounding text's font and color, with tabular digits. With `animate`, the change uses the `motion-change-sm` role, `ease-enter` and `blur-xs`.

components.name: Grid
components.summary: Cells in equal columns, or as many columns as fit, with the same space between them from the spacing scale.
components.guide:
# Grid

Cells in equal columns, or as many columns as fit, with the same space between them from the spacing scale. Use it for a set of cards, a gallery, a dashboard's tiles.

**Also called:** layout grid, columns.

```jsx
import { Grid, Card } from '@diki-stwn/serupa-ds';

// As many columns as fit, each at least 256px: one on a phone, two or three on wider screens
<Grid>{projects.map((p) => <Card key={p.id} title={p.name} />)}</Grid>

<Grid columns={3} gap={6}>…</Grid>
// Up to three: three on a wide screen, two, then one as it narrows, each at least 240px
<Grid columns={3} minColumnWidth="240px">…</Grid>
// Two cards on a wide screen share the width instead of leaving empty columns
<Grid fill>{featured}</Grid>
<Grid minColumnWidth="container-3xs" as="ul">…</Grid>
<Grid minColumnWidth="12rem" gap={2}>…</Grid>
```

## When to use

- A set of similar items side by side: cards, a gallery, a dashboard's tiles.
- Columns that should follow the screen's width without writing breakpoints.

## When not to use

- Items in a single column or a single row: use [Stack] (npx serupa-docs Stack) instead.
- Data in rows and columns that people compare: use [Table] (npx serupa-docs Table) instead.
- Setting the page's width and side padding: use [Container] (npx serupa-docs Container) instead.

## Usage

- Prefer `columns="auto"` with a `minColumnWidth` that suits the content, so the grid fits any screen. A fixed number of columns stays the same on a phone.
- To cap the columns ("never more than three"), give `columns` a number and a `minColumnWidth`: the grid shows that many on a wide screen and fewer as they would get narrower than `minColumnWidth`, with no breakpoints.
- When the design names the columns at each width, give `columns` (and `gap`) one value per width: `columns={{ base: 1, sm: 2, lg: 4 }}`. The widths are `sm` (640px), `md` (768px) and `lg` (1024px); each holds until the next one set. With `minColumnWidth` too, each is "up to".
- Use `fill` when a few cells should share the width (two featured cards). Leave it off when cells should line up with fuller rows above or in other grids.
- Use `as="ul"` when the cells are a list of things.
- Use the same `gap` as the layout around the grid, so the spacing reads as one system.

### Do and don't

- **Do:** Use `columns="auto"` with a `minColumnWidth` that suits the content, so a narrow screen gets fewer, wider columns. (`DoAutoColumns`)
- **Don't:** Fix the number of columns on its own: it stays the same on a phone and squeezes every cell. (`DontFixedColumns`)

## Accessibility

- The reading and tab order follow the children, row by row: keep them in the order people see them.
- Use `as="ul"` when the cells are a list of things. It then carries `role="list"`, since Safari stops calling a list without bullets a list.
- **Keyboard:** none: a layout box, not focusable.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | string | none | Goes to the root element (`as`). |
| `columns` | `1` to `12` \| `'auto'`, or a number per width: `{ base, sm, md, lg }` | `'auto'` | A number of equal columns, or as many as fit. A number with `minColumnWidth` is "up to": that many, fewer on a narrower grid |
| `minColumnWidth` | a CSS length, or a sizing token name such as `'container-3xs'` | `container-3xs` (256px) with `'auto'`, none with a number | The narrowest a column gets. On a grid narrower than that, the one column takes the whole width |
| `fill` | boolean | `false` | With `'auto'` or "up to": a short row's cells stretch across the empty columns (`auto-fit`). A fixed number of columns ignores it |
| `gap` | a spacing step: `0` `0.5` `1` `1.5` `2` `2.5` `3` `3.5` `4` `5` `6` `7` `8` `9` `10` `11` `12` `14` `16` `20` `24` | `4` (16px) | The space between cells. Or one per width: `{ base: 2, md: 4 }` |
| `as` | `'div'` \| `'section'` \| `'ul'` \| `'ol'` | `'div'` | The element. A list loses its bullets, margins and padding |

A fixed number of columns doesn't change with the screen: for that, use `'auto'`, or add a `minColumnWidth`. A Grid inside another starts from its own defaults; it doesn't take the outer one's `gap` or `minColumnWidth`. `className`, `style`, `ref` and everything else go to the element, which has `data-component="grid"`.

## Component tokens

Each is an optional override: set it on the page, a container or one element. The list lives in `src/components/Grid/grid.tokens.json` (also in `design-tokens/components/`).

<!-- token-table:start (made from grid.tokens.json by npm run tokens: edit the descriptions there) -->
| Token | Default | Use |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--grid-gap` | `spacing-4` | The space between cells when gap isn't given (16px). |
| `--grid-min-column` | `container-3xs` | The narrowest a column gets with columns="auto" when minColumnWidth isn't given (256px). |
<!-- token-table:end -->

components.name: Heading
components.summary: A heading, `h1` to `h6`, in the system's type.
components.guide:
# Heading

A heading, `h1` to `h6`, in the system's type. `level` sets the element, which is what screen readers and the page's outline see; `size` sets the look. So a card's title can be an `h3` that looks like body text, or a page's `h1` can be small.

**Also called:** title, headline.

```jsx
import { Heading } from '@diki-stwn/serupa-ds';

<Heading level={1}>Projects</Heading>
<Heading>Recent activity</Heading>                 {/* h2 */}
<Heading level={3} size="base">Billing</Heading>  {/* an h3 at text-base */}
```

## When to use

- A page's title, and the titles of the sections on it.
- Any title people should be able to jump to with a screen reader, whatever size it looks.

## When not to use

- Text that should only look large or bold, without starting a section: use [Text] (npx serupa-docs Text) with `size` and `weight` instead.
- A card's title: use `title` on [Card] (npx serupa-docs Card)'s `CardHeader`, with `headingLevel`.
- A heading only screen reader users need, for a section that's clear by sight: use [VisuallyHidden] (npx serupa-docs VisuallyHidden) with `as="h2"` (or the level that fits).

## Usage

- Set `level` from the page's outline, then change the look with `size` if the default doesn't fit.
- It has no margins: space it with the layout, such as a [Stack] (npx serupa-docs Stack).
- Keep headings short, so they wrap less and are quick to scan.

### Do and don't

- **Do:** Keep headings short, so they're quick to scan: "Billing". (`DoShort`)
- **Don't:** Write a sentence as the heading: it wraps and is slow to scan. (`DontSentence`)

## Accessibility

- Pick the level from the page's outline, never from the look: that's what `size` is for.
- One `h1` per page, naming it.
- Headings keep 4.5:1 on `surface` in every theme (`Heading.test.tsx`).
- **Keyboard:** none: it isn't focusable. Screen reader users move between headings with their own keys, so keep the levels in order.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | string | none | Goes to the root heading (`<h1>`–`<h6>`, by `level`). |
| `level` | `1`–`6` | `2` | The element. Keep the levels in order down the page, without skipping |
| `size` | `'sm'` \| `'base'` \| `'lg'` \| `'xl'` \| `'2xl'` \| `'3xl'` \| `'4xl'` \| `'5xl'` | the level's | A step of the type scale, with its line height. Each level's own: 1 `3xl`, 2 `2xl`, 3 `xl`, 4 `lg`, 5 `base`, 6 `sm` |

Every heading is `font-semibold` in `text`, with no margins (space it with the layout). `2xl` and up are tracked tight (`tracking-tight`), and long headings wrap in balanced lines; one long word or URL breaks rather than widen a flex row or grid column. `className`, `style`, `ref` and everything else go to the heading, which has `data-component="heading"`.

## Component tokens

Each is an optional override: set it on the page, a container or one heading. The list lives in `src/components/Heading/heading.tokens.json` (also in `design-tokens/components/`). A `--heading-size-*` override changes the size only: set the matching `--heading-line-height-*` with it (for an h1 at `text-4xl`, `--heading-line-height-1: var(--text-4xl--line-height)`), or a large size keeps the level's shorter line height and wrapped lines crowd.

<!-- token-table:start (made from heading.tokens.json by npm run tokens: edit the descriptions there) -->
| Token | Default | Use |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--heading-text` | `text` | The heading's color. |
| `--heading-weight` | `font-semibold` | The weight of every level (600). |
| `--heading-size-1` | `text-3xl` | The size of a level 1 heading (text-3xl). |
| `--heading-size-2` | `text-2xl` | The size of a level 2 heading (text-2xl). |
| `--heading-size-3` | `text-xl` | The size of a level 3 heading (text-xl). |
| `--heading-size-4` | `text-lg` | The size of a level 4 heading (text-lg). |
| `--heading-size-5` | `text-base` | The size of a level 5 heading (text-base). |
| `--heading-size-6` | `text-sm` | The size of a level 6 heading (text-sm). |
| `--heading-line-height-1` | `text-3xl--line-height` | The line height of a level 1 heading (text-3xl's). Set it with --heading-size-1. |
| `--heading-line-height-2` | `text-2xl--line-height` | The line height of a level 2 heading (text-2xl's). Set it with --heading-size-2. |
| `--heading-line-height-3` | `text-xl--line-height` | The line height of a level 3 heading (text-xl's). Set it with --heading-size-3. |
| `--heading-line-height-4` | `text-lg--line-height` | The line height of a level 4 heading (text-lg's). Set it with --heading-size-4. |
| `--heading-line-height-5` | `text-base--line-height` | The line height of a level 5 heading (text-base's). Set it with --heading-size-5. |
| `--heading-line-height-6` | `text-sm--line-height` | The line height of a level 6 heading (text-sm's). Set it with --heading-size-6. |
<!-- token-table:end -->

components.name: Highlight
components.summary: Shows text with the parts that match a search marked, ignoring case and accents, for search results, Combobox options and a command palette.
components.guide:
# Highlight

Shows text with the parts that match a search marked, ignoring case and accents, for search results, [Combobox] (npx serupa-docs Combobox) options and a command palette.

**Also called:** mark, match highlighting.

```tsx
import { Highlight, highlightRanges } from "@diki-stwn/serupa-ds";

<Highlight query="lodz">Łódź, Poland</Highlight>              // marks "Łódź"
<Highlight query="strasse">Straße des 17. Juni</Highlight>     // marks "Straße"
<Highlight query="york new" words>New York, United States</Highlight>
highlightRanges("Łódź, Poland", "lodz")                        // [[0, 4]]
```

## When to use

- Showing why a search result, an option or a command matched what was typed.
- Pointing at a word or phrase inside a longer text that people searched for.

## When not to use

- Emphasis that doesn't come from a search: use `<strong>` or `<em>` in [Text] (npx serupa-docs Text).
- A label or count next to text: use a [Badge] (npx serupa-docs Badge).
- Long rich content: Highlight takes plain text, not elements.

## Anatomy

Drawn from the `InOptions` story.

1. **Text** (`.srp-highlight`): the whole text, read as one string.
2. **Match** (`.srp-highlight__mark`): the part that matches what was typed.

## Usage

- Pass the same query the list was filtered with, so what's marked is what matched.
- Matching ignores case, accents, width and hiragana versus katakana, as Combobox does: "lodz" marks "Łódź", "sao" marks "São", and "strasse" marks "Straße". The marks cover the text as written.
- `words` marks each word of the query wherever it is ("york new" marks "New" and "York"). Without it, the query is one phrase.
- A query can also be a list of terms. Overlapping or touching matches become one mark.
- `highlightRanges(text, query, words)` returns the same matches as `[start, end)` offsets, for drawing them yourself.

### Do and don't

- **Do:** Mark what a search matched, with the same query the list was filtered by. (`DoMarkMatches`)
- **Don't:** Use it for emphasis in running text, where nothing was searched: use `<strong>` in [Text] (npx serupa-docs Text). (`DontEmphasis`)

## Accessibility

- Matches are `<mark>` elements, which assistive tech exposes as highlighted text; the words themselves are unchanged, so the text reads as written.
- A match isn't marked by color alone: it's also semibold. Inside an option or menu item (`role="option"`, `"menuitem"`, `"menuitemradio"`, `"menuitemcheckbox"`), which is filtered as people type, it keeps the text's weight and is underlined instead, so the letters don't widen on each keystroke and the text and its ellipsis stay put. The text keeps 4.5:1 on the tint in every theme (`Highlight.test.tsx`).
- In forced-colors mode marks use the system's Mark and MarkText colors.
- **Keyboard:** none: inline text, not focusable.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | string | none | Goes to the root `<span>`. |
| `children` | `string` | | The text to show. |
| `query` | `string \| string[]` | | What to mark. Empty marks nothing. |
| `words` | `boolean` | `false` | Mark each word of the query on its own. |

Every other prop, `className` and `ref` go to the `<span>`, which has `data-component="highlight"`; each match is `<mark class="srp-highlight__mark">`.

## Component tokens

Each is an optional override: set it on the page, a container or one highlight. The list lives in `src/components/Highlight/highlight.tokens.json` (also in `design-tokens/components/`).

<!-- token-table:start (made from highlight.tokens.json by npm run tokens: edit the descriptions there) -->
| Token | Default | Use |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--highlight-bg` | `warning-subtle` | Behind a match. |
| `--highlight-text` | `text` | A match's text (4.5:1 on bg). |
| `--highlight-weight` | `font-semibold` | A match's weight, so it isn't marked by color alone (not in an option or menu item, where it's underlined instead). |
| `--highlight-radius` | `rounded-xs` | A match's corners (2px). |
<!-- token-table:end -->

components.name: HoverCard
components.summary: A preview of what a link points to: a person, a page, a repository.
components.guide:
# HoverCard A preview of what a link points to: a person, a page, a repository. It opens when the pointer rests on the link, or keyboard focus stays on it, so people can check who or what it is before they follow it. **Also called:** preview card, link preview. ```tsx import { HoverCard, Link, Avatar } from "@diki-stwn/serupa-ds"; @dewi}> Dewi Lestari

Design lead, Payments

See Dewi's projects ``` ## When to use - A mention, an author's name or a link to a record, where a glance at the details saves a trip to another page. ## When not to use - A short hint about a control: use [Tooltip] (npx serupa-docs Tooltip). - Something people open on purpose to act on (a form, filters, settings): use [Popover] (npx serupa-docs Popover), which opens on a press. - Anything that only exists in the card. A touch screen has no hover, so a tap on the link goes straight to its page. Only a long press opens the card there, and only where the browser has interest invokers. Everything in the card must also be on the page the link opens. ## Usage - The trigger is one element that takes focus, usually a link. The card adds nothing to its name: it's a preview, not part of the link. - Keep the card short: a name, a picture, a line or two and a link or two. It's 320px wide and grows taller, scrolling inside itself past the screen's height. - It waits 500ms before opening (`openDelay`), so a pointer crossing a list of links doesn't open a card for each. It closes 300ms after the pointer and focus leave both the link and the card (`closeDelay`), so crossing the gap to the card keeps it. ### Do and don't - **Do:** Keep the card short: a name, a picture, a line or two and a link or two. (`Open`) - **Don't:** Fill it with a page of content: it covers what people were reading. Link to the full page instead. (`DontLongCard`) ## Accessibility - **Role and name:** the card is a plain group in the top layer, placed right after the link in the page's order, so a screen reader's reading order reaches it after the link while it's open. The link's own name and target are unchanged. - **Keyboard:** focus resting on the link opens the card after `openDelay` (keyboard focus only, not a click). Tab then goes into the card, and Shift+Tab back to the link. Focus leaving both closes it. Escape closes it from anywhere and, from inside the card, puts focus back on the link (WCAG 1.4.13: dismissible, hoverable, persistent). - **Pointer:** the pointer can move from the link onto the card, and the card stays while it's there. - **Touch:** the link points at the card with `interestfor` (interest invokers), so where the browser has them (Chrome 142 and later, including on Android), a long press on the link opens the card at once. The browser's own showing is canceled and the card opens itself, so the delays and Escape stay the same with a mouse or the keyboard. A tap outside or Escape closes it. Elsewhere the attribute does nothing. - **Contrast:** its text reads 4.5:1 on its background in every theme (`HoverCard.test.tsx`). - **What's still yours:** the same details reachable without hover (the page the link opens), and links in the card with names that make sense on their own. | Key | Does | | --- | --- | | Tab | To the link: once focus rests there, the card opens. Tab again goes into the card | | Shift+Tab | From the card's first link back to the link it previews | | Escape | Closes the card, from anywhere; from inside it, focus goes back to the link | ## Props | Prop | Type | Default | Notes | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `trigger` | `ReactElement` | | The link it previews: one element that takes focus. | | `children` | `ReactNode` | | What the card shows. Links and buttons are fine. | | `placement` | `Placement` | `'bottom'` | `'top'`, `'bottom'`, `'left'`, `'right'`, with `'-start'` or `'-end'`. It flips when there's no room. | | `openDelay` | `number` | `500` | Milliseconds the pointer or focus rests on the link before it opens. | | `closeDelay` | `number` | `300` | Milliseconds after the pointer and focus leave the link and the card before it closes. | | `open` | `boolean` | | Controlled, with `onOpenChange`. | | `defaultOpen` | `boolean` | `false` | Open at first (uncontrolled). | | `onOpenChange` | `(open, { reason }) => void` | | `reason`: `'hover'`, `'focus'`, `'blur'`, `'escape'` or `'outside'`. | | `disabled` | `boolean` | `false` | Never opens. | | `id` | `string` | generated | The card's id. | `className`, `style`, `ref` and other props go to the card's `
`. ## Component tokens Each is an optional override: set it on the page, a container or one HoverCard. The list lives in `src/components/HoverCard/hover-card.tokens.json` (also in `design-tokens/components/`). | Token | Default | Use | | --- | --- | --- | | `--hover-card-bg` | `surface-overlay` | The card's background. | | `--hover-card-text` | `text` | The card's text (4.5:1 on bg). | | `--hover-card-border` | `border-overlay` | The card's border. | | `--hover-card-divider` | `border-overlay` | What a divider or separator inside it reads as `border`: its own edge color, since in dark `border` is the surface's own color and a line in it vanished | | `--hover-card-shadow` | `elevation-overlay` | The card's shadow. | | `--hover-card-radius` | `radius-surface` | The corners (8px). | | `--hover-card-border-width` | `border-width-1` | The border's width (1px). | | `--hover-card-width` | `container-xs` | The card's width (320px), never wider than the screen. | | `--hover-card-padding` | `space-content` | Space inside, on every side (16px). | | `--hover-card-offset` | `spacing-2` | The gap between the link and the card (8px). | | `--hover-card-z-index` | `z-popover` | Its stacking level, for a browser without the top layer. |

components.name: Icon
components.summary: Shows one icon as an inline SVG: from Material Symbols, always in the **Rounded** style with **Fill** on, or one of your own custom icons.
components.guide:
# Icon Shows one icon as an inline SVG: from Material Symbols, always in the **Rounded** style with **Fill** on, or one of your own custom icons. Use it on its own or pass an icon straight to Button's `startIcon` or `endIcon`, or IconButton's `icon`. **Also called:** glyph, symbol. ```jsx import { Icon, Button, IconButton } from '@diki-stwn/serupa-ds'; // 24px, decorative // meaningful: announced as "Error" // any of the ~3,800 Material Symbols works by name ``` ## When to use - A symbol next to a label that helps people find it quickly: in buttons, menus, list rows and navigation. - A status (success, warning, error, info) next to the message it belongs to. - A large symbol in an empty state or an illustration. ## When not to use - A button that shows only an icon: use [IconButton] (npx serupa-docs IconButton) instead; it requires the label an icon alone doesn't have. - A photo, a screenshot or any other picture: use [Image] (npx serupa-docs Image) instead. - A person's or team's picture: use [Avatar] (npx serupa-docs Avatar) instead. ## Usage Find icons in the Material Symbols catalog (Rounded style) at fonts.google.com/icons. Names are lowercase with underscores (`arrow_forward`, `more_vert`); the import for a name is the same words in PascalCase (`ArrowForward`, `MoreVert`; a name starting with a digit gets `Icon` in front: `Icon10k`). - Use Material Symbols Rounded, filled, and custom icons drawn to the same rules. Don't mix in other icon sets or the Outlined/Sharp styles. - Before drawing a custom icon, check that Material Symbols doesn't already have one for that meaning. - One icon per meaning across the product: `delete`, not `delete` in one place and `remove` in another. - **Right to left:** arrows and chevrons that point along the line of reading (`arrow_forward`, `chevron_right`, `send`, `undo`…) flip by themselves in right-to-left text, so `` points the way an Arabic or Hebrew reader goes. Icons of things (a clock, a check, media controls) don't. Use `mirror` for your own arrows (`true`) or for an icon you already turn yourself (`false`). ### Setup: by name There's no font to load. Every icon is an SVG drawn in the page, so it shows at once and nothing flashes while a file loads. - **Every Material Symbol works by name** (`name="category"`, `startIcon="category"`), about 3,800 of them, with autocomplete in TypeScript. Find one on the Foundations › Icons page of the docs: search, then click to copy its name. A name loads the first time a page draws it, so it appears a moment later that first time: the icons the components use come from a small file (about 14 KB), and any other name from the part of the full set that holds it. The set is cut into 32 parts of about 86 KB each (9 to 20 KB gzipped), in name order, so a page downloads only the parts its names are in. Apps that draw no names never download any of it. Both are dynamic imports, so this needs a bundler that splits them into files of their own, as Vite, Next.js, webpack and Rollup do by default. A build that puts everything in one file (esbuild without `--splitting`, Rollup with `inlineDynamicImports`, a single-chunk webpack or IIFE build) puts the full set in it too, about 2.7 MB (510 KB gzipped). There, draw imported icons (`icon={Close}`) or `registerIcons` the ones you use by name, and keep names out of the bundle's reach. - **An imported icon works too** (`icon={Category}` with `import { Category } from "@diki-stwn/serupa-ds/icons"`), the same icon either way. It draws on the first render, and only the icons you import ship in your bundle, so prefer it for icons you know ahead of time. - **Outlined icons** come from `@diki-stwn/serupa-ds/icons/outlined`, under the same export names: `import { Home } from "@diki-stwn/serupa-ds/icons/outlined"`. Use them for the unselected state of something that shows a selected one filled, such as navigation and tabs (`icon={current ? HomeFilled : Home}`, with `import { Home as HomeFilled } from "@diki-stwn/serupa-ds/icons"`), or where a lighter set suits the page. Each outlined icon's `name` is the name and `:outlined` (`"home:outlined"`), so `registerIcons(Home)` draws it as `name="home:outlined"` without replacing the filled `home`. An icon with no outlined drawing (about a third, such as `add` or `close`) is the filled one, so any name can be imported from either. The names-only set the components draw is filled. - **An empty shape by name is solid**: in the filled set, `radio_button_unchecked` draws as a disc and `check_box_outline_blank` as a square, so a "not yet" next to a `check_circle` reads as a dot. Use `trip_origin` for an empty ring by name, or import the outlined icon. - **The components' own icons** (Dialog's close, Checkbox's check, Select's chevron) are imported by each component, so they draw at once and on the server, and a bundle keeps only the icons of the components it uses. - **On a plain page** (`serupa.iife.js`), every name works. The components' own icons and the everyday ones are in `serupa.iife.js`; the full set (about 490 KiB gzipped) is `serupa-icons.iife.js`, which `serupa.iife.js` adds to the page from its own folder the first time an Icon names one outside that set, so keep the two files side by side. A page that names many icons can include `serupa-icons.iife.js` itself, after `serupa.iife.js`, so they draw on the first try. - **Server rendering:** the components' own icons and imported icons (`icon={Close}`) render on the server. A name (`name="close"`, `startIcon="close"`) shows its empty box until the page loads in the browser. To draw it on the server, pass the imported icon instead, or register what you draw by name once before rendering: `registerIcons(Close, Add)`, or `registerIcons(await import("@diki-stwn/serupa-ds/icons"))` for every name. - `registerIcons({ name, d })` adds an icon of your own in Material's shape (`d` on the 960-unit grid) under a name. A name that isn't a Material Symbol or one of your icons draws an empty 1em box and logs a console warning. Names are snake_case (`arrow_forward`); for a name in another spelling, such as the export name `Home` or `arrow-forward`, the warning says which name to use. ### Custom icons For what Material Symbols doesn't have, add your own SVG icons. They work everywhere a Material Symbols name does, with the same sizes, colors and accessibility: ```jsx ``` **Draw** each icon so it sits with Material Symbols Rounded: - A 24×24 frame (`viewBox="0 0 24 24"`) with about 2px of padding around the shape. - Filled shapes with rounded corners and ends, like the Rounded style. Outlined (stroke) icons work too, at a 2px stroke. - One color. The build draws every shape in the text color, so icons follow the theme. Parts that should show the background must be holes (a cut-out path, or `fill-rule="evenodd"`), not white shapes. - Only shapes: outline text and flatten masks, gradients and effects before exporting. Figma's "Export as SVG" and Illustrator's "Export As SVG" both work. **Add** them: 1. Put the SVG in `assets/Icons/` (the Icons set on the design system page). The file name is the icon's name: lowercase letters and digits, words joined by `-` or `_`, such as `serupa-sparkle.svg`. A prefix such as `serupa-` keeps your names apart from Material Symbols; a custom icon with the same name as a Material Symbol replaces it everywhere. 2. Run `node tools/icons/build.mjs` (or `node tools/icons/build.mjs path/to/folder`), then `npm run build`. It writes the icons and their names (`CustomIconName`, so TypeScript autocompletes them) into `src/icons.ts`; the build puts them in `dist/`. 3. Run it again after changing or removing a file. `node tools/icons/build.mjs --check` fails if the components are out of step, for CI. The build keeps only the shapes and removes editor leftovers (ids, classes, sizes, Figma and Illustrator metadata). It refuses a file, with the reason, when it holds anything that could run code or load something (scripts, event handlers, links, images), anything that isn't a plain shape (text, gradients, masks, filters, ``), another grid, or a second color. A refused file stops the build, and the components stay as they were. `Serupa.customIcons` lists the custom icons' names. ### Sizes The same for Material Symbols and custom icons. | `size` | Token | Size | Use | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `"xs"` | `icon-size-xs` | 14px | Inside `sm` buttons, next to `text-xs` | | `"sm"` | `icon-size-sm` | 16px | Inside `md` buttons, next to `text-sm` | | `"md"` | `icon-size-md` | 20px | Inside `lg` buttons, list rows, inputs, next to `text-base` | | `"lg"` | `icon-size-lg` | 24px | Default: toolbars, navigation, standalone | | `"xl"` | `icon-size-xl` | 40px | Empty states, illustrations | Every step is on the 4px spacing grid except `xs`, and each fits inside the line height of the text it sits beside. Inline in running text it's centered on the text (`vertical-align: middle`), so it doesn't make the line taller; in a flex row with `items-center` it's centered the same way. ### Weight Match an icon to the weight of the text beside it. The drawings are weight 400, which goes with regular and medium text. Next to `font-semibold` text use `weight="semibold"`; next to `font-bold` text and headings use `weight="bold"`. The weight thickens the icon's lines by a stroke of the `icon-weight-semibold` (0.02em) or `icon-weight-bold` (0.035em) token round the drawing, the same share of the icon at every size, so the small details stay open. Custom icons keep their own drawing. ```tsx

Quick start

``` Every icon is the 24px design (Material Symbols' optical size 24), scaled. ### Color Icons take the text color (`currentColor`). Set it with an alias, never a palette color: `text` or `text-muted` for neutral icons, and `success`, `warning`, `danger` or `info` for status icons. Icons that carry meaning need 3:1 contrast against their background. ### Common icons | Action | Name | | --- | --- | | Create / add | `add` | | Edit | `edit` | | Delete | `delete` | | Close | `close` | | Search | `search` | | Settings | `settings` | | More | `more_vert`, `more_horiz` | | Next / back | `arrow_forward`, `arrow_back` | | Menu open | `expand_more`, `chevron_right` | | Success / error / warning / info | `check_circle`, `error`, `warning`, `info` | ### Do and don't - **Do:** Use one icon for one meaning across the product: `delete` wherever something is deleted. (`DoOneMeaning`) - **Don't:** Mix icons for the same action: people wonder whether `remove` and `close` do something different. (`DontMixedIcons`) ## Accessibility - **Role and name:** icons are decorative by default (`aria-hidden`). Give an icon an `aria-label` only when it's the sole carrier of meaning, such as a status icon without text. With `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby` it becomes `role="img"` with that name. - **Next to text:** leave it decorative; the text already says what it means. - **Icon-only buttons:** the button needs the name, not the icon: pass `aria-label` to the Button, or use [IconButton] (npx serupa-docs IconButton), which requires a `label`. - **Contrast:** icons that carry meaning need 3:1 against their background (see Color, under Usage). - **Translation:** icons are SVGs with no text, so translation tools and screen readers never see an icon's name. - **Keyboard:** none: the svg is `focusable="false"`, so it's never a Tab stop of its own, in a button or not. ## Props | Prop | Type | Default | Notes | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `id` | string | none | Goes to the root ``. | | `name` | `IconName`: any Material Symbol's name, a custom icon's name, or a name you registered | | Give `name` or `icon`. A custom icon with the same name as a Material Symbol wins. All names autocomplete. | | `icon` | `IconData`: a Material Symbol imported from `@diki-stwn/serupa-ds/icons` (or `@diki-stwn/serupa-ds/icons/outlined`) | | Give `name` or `icon`: `icon={ArrowForward}`. | | `size` | `'xs' \| 'sm' \| 'md' \| 'lg' \| 'xl' \| number \| string` | 24px, or the button's icon size inside a Button | A step of the icon scale (the `icon-size-*` tokens: 14, 16, 20, 24, 40px), pixels as a number (or a string of one: `"20"` is 20px), or any CSS length. Sets the font size; the icon is 1em square. | | `weight` | `'regular' \| 'semibold' \| 'bold'` | `'regular'` | How heavy a Material Symbol's lines are, to go with the text beside it (the `icon-weight-*` tokens). See Weight, under Usage. Custom icons keep their own drawing. | | `mirror` | `boolean \| 'auto'` | `'auto'` | Flips the icon in right-to-left text (`dir="rtl"`), so it points the way reading goes. `'auto'` flips Material Symbols' directional icons (`arrow_forward`, `arrow_back`, `chevron_left`, `chevron_right`, `navigate_next`, `first_page`, `last_page`, `send`, `reply`, `undo`, `redo`, `open_in_new`, `logout`, the panel and dock icons such as `left_panel_close`, and the like) and nothing else; `true` flips any icon (your own custom arrow), `false` none (an icon you turn yourself). | | `aria-label` | `string` | | Makes the icon meaningful: `role="img"` with this name. Without it (or `aria-labelledby`) the icon is `aria-hidden`. | `className`, `style`, `ref` and other `` props go to the outer ``, which has `data-icon` with the icon's name. Also exported: `registerIcons(...icons)` adds icons that work by name, `getIcon(name)` returns the Material Symbol (or registered icon) for a name, and the `MaterialIconName` type lists every name. Every icon prop in the system (Button's `startIcon`, `endIcon` and `icon`, IconButton and Fab's `icon`, Input's icons, and the rest) takes a name, an imported icon or any element (`IconSource`). ## Component tokens None: it draws in `currentColor` at 1em of its font size, so it takes its color from the text and its size from `size` or the text around it.

components.name: IconButton
components.summary: A button that shows only an icon: a menu trigger, a close button, a toolbar action.
components.guide:
# IconButton

A button that shows only an icon: a menu trigger, a close button, a toolbar action. It's a [Button] (npx serupa-docs Button) with `icon`, and a `label` you can't leave out, because an icon alone has no name for screen readers.

**Also called:** icon-only button.

```jsx
import { IconButton } from '@diki-stwn/serupa-ds';

<IconButton icon="more_vert" label="More actions" onClick={openMenu} />
<IconButton icon="edit" label="Edit" variant="secondary" shape="round" />
<IconButton icon="delete" label="Delete file" destructive />
<IconButton icon="open_in_new" label="Open in a new tab" href={url} target="_blank" />
```

## When to use

- An action whose icon people know at a glance: close, search, settings, more actions.
- Toolbars, table rows and card headers, where a labeled button would take too much room.
- A menu trigger, such as the "More actions" button that opens a [Menu] (npx serupa-docs Menu).

## When not to use

- An action whose icon isn't widely understood: use a [Button] (npx serupa-docs Button) with a label and a `startIcon`.
- A setting that stays on or off, such as bold or mute: use [ToggleButton] (npx serupa-docs ToggleButton) with `icon` and `aria-label`.
- The one main action of a screen that must stay in reach while people scroll: use [Fab] (npx serupa-docs Fab).

## Usage

- Write the `label` as the action ("Delete file"). It also shows in a [Tooltip] (npx serupa-docs Tooltip) when people point at the button or reach it with Tab, so sighted keyboard and touch users can tell what an icon does, not only screen reader users. A native `title` showed only after the mouse rested on it.
- For a tooltip that says more than the label ("Delete file (can't be undone)"), wrap the button in your own Tooltip: it replaces the built-in one (the button then has `aria-describedby`), so only one shows.
- Set `hideTitle` where visible text right beside the button already says the label, so the same words don't pop up next to themselves.
- Give icon buttons in one row the same `size` and `variant`, and match the size of the buttons and fields beside them.
- Use `shape="round"` only where round buttons are the pattern; square follows Button's corners.

### Do and don't

- **Do:** Use icons people know at a glance, such as search, settings and close. (`DoKnownIcons`)
- **Don't:** Leave people to guess a newer action from its icon: give it words, as a [Button] (npx serupa-docs Button) with a `startIcon`. (`DontGuessIcon`)

## Accessibility

- The label is the button's name: say what it does ("Delete file"), not what it shows ("Trash can").
- The built-in tooltip is the button's label (Tooltip's `role="label"`), so screen readers say the name once, not again as a description. It shows on focus as well as hover, stays while the pointer moves onto it, and Escape hides it (WCAG 1.4.13).
- Every size is at least 24×24px, the WCAG 2.2 target size.
- The rest is Button's: focus ring, contrast, forced colors and reduced motion (checked in Button's tests); IconButton's own checks are in `IconButton.test.tsx`.

### Keyboard

| Key | Does |
| --- | --- |
| Tab | To the button |
| Enter, Space | Press it |

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | string | none | Goes to the root `<button>`. |
| `icon` | icon name \| element | required | A custom or Material Symbols name, or any element |
| `label` | string | required | Its `aria-label`, and a Tooltip on hover and focus. An `aria-label` passed instead (from JavaScript, or props spread from a Button) is used as the label |
| `shape` | `'square'` \| `'round'` | `'square'` | The Button's corners, or a circle |
| `hideTitle` | boolean | `false` | Leaves out the tooltip, when visible text beside it already shows the label (a Tooltip of your own replaces it by itself). |
| `variant` | as Button | `'ghost'` | Ghost by default, the usual look for an icon on its own |
| `surface` | as Button | none | Over a photo or a colored panel: white for dark media, black for light |

Every other Button prop works the same: `size` (24, 32 or 44px square; on a touch screen each takes a press 44px across, as a Button does), `destructive`, `loading`, `disabled`, `href`, `onClick`, `ref`. A given `title` shows instead of the tooltip.

## Component tokens

Each is an optional override: set it on the page, a container or one button. The list lives in `src/components/IconButton/icon-button.tokens.json` (also in `design-tokens/components/`). Every Button token applies too.

<!-- token-table:start (made from icon-button.tokens.json by npm run tokens: edit the descriptions there) -->
| Token | Default | Use |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--icon-button-radius-round` | `radius-pill` | The corners of a round icon button (shape="round"). |
<!-- token-table:end -->

components.name: IconTile
components.summary: An icon centered in a tinted rounded square (or a circle), to mark what a card, a settings row or an empty state is about at a glance.
components.guide:
# IconTile

An icon centered in a tinted rounded square (or a circle), to mark what a card, a settings row or an empty state is about at a glance.

**Also called:** icon container, icon box.

```tsx
import { IconTile } from "@diki-stwn/serupa-ds";

<IconTile icon="cloud_done" tone="primary" />
<IconTile icon="warning" tone="warning" size="lg" />
<IconTile icon="person" shape="circle" size="xl" />
<IconTile icon="lock" tone="danger" label="Locked" />   // says something the text beside it doesn't
```

## When to use

- At the start of a Card's header, a settings row or a feature list, beside the title that says what it is.
- At the top of an EmptyState, as a quieter mark than an Illustration.

## When not to use

- A person or a team: use [Avatar] (npx serupa-docs Avatar) instead.
- A status that needs words, such as "Paid" or "Failed": use [Badge] (npx serupa-docs Badge) instead.
- An icon inside text or a button: use [Icon] (npx serupa-docs Icon) on its own.
- A pressable icon: use [IconButton] (npx serupa-docs IconButton) instead.

## Anatomy

Drawn from the `InACard` story.

1. **Tile** (`.srp-icon-tile`): the tinted square, in the tone's fill.
2. **Icon** (`.srp-icon-tile__icon`): centered, in the tone's color.

## Usage

- Pick the `tone` for what the row is about, not for decoration: `neutral` (default) for most things, `primary` for your product's own features, and a status (`success`, `warning`, `danger`, `info`) only when the row is about that state, such as a trial ending.
- `size`: `sm` (32px) beside one line of text, `md` (40px, default) beside a title and a line, `lg` (48px) and `xl` (64px) for an empty state or a feature list.
- Keep the shape the same across a list: squares for things, `shape="circle"` when it sits among Avatars.
- `icon` takes a Material Symbols name, a custom icon or an element, as [Icon] (npx serupa-docs Icon) does.

### Do and don't

- **Do:** Pick the `tone` for what the row is about: `neutral` for most things, and a status only where the row is that status. (`DoNeutralTones`)
- **Don't:** Color tiles for decoration: a real warning no longer stands out from the rest. (`DontDecorativeTones`)

## Accessibility

- Decorative by default: the tile is `aria-hidden`, since the title beside it says what the row is. When the icon says something the text doesn't, such as that a row is locked, pass `label`: the tile becomes `role="img"` named by it.
- Every tone keeps its icon at 3:1 or more on its fill, in every theme (`IconTile.test.tsx`), and the tones differ by icon as well as color when you choose icons that say the state (a warning sign for warning).
- In forced colors (Windows High Contrast), where fills are dropped, an outline keeps the tile's shape.
- **Keyboard:** none: it isn't interactive.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `icon` | string or element | | The icon: a Material Symbols name, a custom icon or any element. |
| `tone` | `'neutral' \| 'primary' \| 'success' \| 'warning' \| 'danger' \| 'info'` | `'neutral'` | The fill and the icon's color. |
| `size` | `'sm' \| 'md' \| 'lg' \| 'xl'` | `'md'` | 32, 40, 48 or 64px, with a 16, 20, 24 or 32px icon. |
| `shape` | `'square' \| 'circle'` | `'square'` | Rounded corners, or a circle. |
| `label` | string | none | Makes the tile an image with this name; without it, it's hidden from screen readers. |

`id`, `className`, `style`, `ref` and other props go to the `<span>`, which has `data-component="icon-tile"`.

## Component tokens

Each is an optional override: set it on the page, a container or one tile. The list lives in `src/components/IconTile/icon-tile.tokens.json` (also in `design-tokens/components/`).

<!-- token-table:start (made from icon-tile.tokens.json by npm run tokens: edit the descriptions there) -->
| Token | Default | Use |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--icon-tile-neutral-bg` | `secondary` | A neutral tile's fill. |
| `--icon-tile-neutral-icon` | `text-muted` | A neutral tile's icon (3:1 on its fill). |
| `--icon-tile-primary-bg` | `primary-subtle` | A primary tile's fill. |
| `--icon-tile-primary-icon` | `primary-text` | A primary tile's icon (3:1 on its fill). |
| `--icon-tile-success-bg` | `success-subtle` | A success tile's fill. |
| `--icon-tile-success-icon` | `success-text` | A success tile's icon (3:1 on its fill). |
| `--icon-tile-warning-bg` | `warning-subtle` | A warning tile's fill. |
| `--icon-tile-warning-icon` | `warning-text` | A warning tile's icon (3:1 on its fill). |
| `--icon-tile-danger-bg` | `danger-subtle` | A danger tile's fill. |
| `--icon-tile-danger-icon` | `danger-text` | A danger tile's icon (3:1 on its fill). |
| `--icon-tile-info-bg` | `info-subtle` | An info tile's fill. |
| `--icon-tile-info-icon` | `info-text` | An info tile's icon (3:1 on its fill). |
| `--icon-tile-radius` | `radius-surface` | The corners at sizes md and lg (8px). |
| `--icon-tile-radius-sm` | `radius-control` | The corners at size sm (6px). |
| `--icon-tile-radius-xl` | `radius-container` | The corners at size xl (12px). |
<!-- token-table:end -->

## Related

- [Avatar] (npx serupa-docs Avatar): a person's picture or initials.
- [Icon] (npx serupa-docs Icon): the icon on its own.
- [EmptyState] (npx serupa-docs EmptyState): often starts with an IconTile.

components.name: Illustration
components.summary: A small line drawing for an empty state, an error page or a finished flow.
components.guide:
# Illustration

A small line drawing for an empty state, an error page or a finished flow. It's drawn in the theme's own colors, so it fits every theme and follows a brand's overrides without new artwork.

**Also called:** spot illustration, artwork.

```tsx
import { EmptyState, Illustration } from "@diki-stwn/serupa-ds";

<EmptyState icon={<Illustration name="search" />} title="No results for “mars”" description="Check the spelling or try a broader search." />
```

## When to use

- A page or a large panel that's empty, failed or done, where a picture helps the moment read at a glance: a first-run list, no search results, offline, no access, a finished sign-up.

## When not to use

- Inside a card, a table or a menu: there's no room. Use EmptyState's `icon` with an icon name ([EmptyState] (npx serupa-docs EmptyState)).
- As the only way to say what happened. The title beside it says that; the picture only supports it.
- For a brand's own artwork: pass that as an element to EmptyState's `icon` instead.

## Anatomy

Drawn from the `Search` story.

1. **Fill** (`.srp-illustration__fill`): the soft shapes, in `--illustration-fill`.
2. **Line** (`.srp-illustration__line`): the outlines, 3:1 on the surface.
3. **Accent** (`.srp-illustration__accent`): the one detail that says what happened, in the primary color.

## Usage

- Pick the picture that matches the title: `empty` for nothing yet, `search` for no results, `error` for a failure, `offline` for no connection, `no-access` for a missing permission, `success` for done.
- One per view. `md` (160px) suits a page, `sm` (96px) a side panel or a dialog, `lg` (224px) a full error page.
- Recolor it with the tokens below, not by editing paths: `--illustration-accent` set to `var(--danger)` makes the error picture red.

### Do and don't

- **Do:** Pick the picture that matches the title: `search` for no results, `error` for a failure. (`DoMatchTitle`)
- **Don't:** Pick a picture that says something else, such as `success` over "No results". (`DontMismatch`)

## Accessibility

- **Role and name:** hidden from screen readers by default (`aria-hidden`), because the text beside it says the same thing. With `label`, it's `role="img"` with that name: use it only when the picture adds something the text doesn't.
- **Keyboard:** not focusable (`focusable="false"`, also in old Edge).
- **Contrast:** its outlines and accent read 3:1 on the surface in every theme (`Illustration.test.tsx`), as WCAG 1.4.11 asks of a graphic. In forced colors the lines take the system colors.
- **What's still yours:** the title and description that say what happened, and the action that gets the person out.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `name` | `'empty' \| 'search' \| 'error' \| 'offline' \| 'no-access' \| 'success'` | `'empty'` | Which picture. |
| `size` | `'sm' \| 'md' \| 'lg'` | `'md'` | 96, 160 or 224px wide, at 4:3. |
| `label` | `string` | | Makes it an image with this name. Without it, it's hidden from screen readers. |
| `id` | string | none | Goes to the `<svg>`. |

`className`, `ref` and other props go to the `<svg>`.

## Component tokens

Each is an optional override: set it on the page, a container or one Illustration. The list lives in `src/components/Illustration/illustration.tokens.json` (also in `design-tokens/components/`).

<!-- token-table:start (made from illustration.tokens.json by npm run tokens: edit the descriptions there) -->
| Token | Default | Use |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--illustration-line` | `text-muted` | The outlines (3:1 on the surface behind). |
| `--illustration-fill` | `secondary` | The shapes' soft fill. |
| `--illustration-accent` | `primary-text` | The one detail that says what happened: the lens, the check, the slash (3:1 on the surface behind). |
| `--illustration-size-sm` | `spacing-24` | size="sm" (96px wide). |
| `--illustration-size-md` | `spacing-40` | size="md" (160px wide). |
| `--illustration-size-lg` | `spacing-56` | size="lg" (224px wide). |
<!-- token-table:end -->

components.name: Image
components.summary: A picture in a frame: a fixed ratio, rounded corners, a placeholder while it loads and a fallback if it fails.
components.guide: # Image A picture in a frame: a fixed ratio, rounded corners, a placeholder while it loads and a fallback if it fails. It can open full size in a viewer, and show a remove button. **Also called:** picture, img. ```tsx import { Image } from "@diki-stwn/serupa-ds"; remove(upload)} /> ``` ## When to use - Photos, screenshots and other pictures in a page, a card or a gallery. - Pictures in a set that should all have the same shape, whatever their own size. - Uploads people may want to see full size, or remove. ## When not to use - A person's, team's or project's picture: use [Avatar] (npx serupa-docs Avatar) instead. - A symbol for an action or a status: use [Icon] (npx serupa-docs Icon) instead. - A purely decorative background: use a CSS `background-image` instead. ## Anatomy Drawn from the `Removable` story. 1. **Picture** (`.srp-image__img`): the image, with its alternative text. 2. **View** (`.srp-image__view`): opens it full size. 3. **Remove** (`.srp-image__remove`): takes it away, when it can be removed. ## Usage - Write `alt` to say what the picture shows. Use `""` only for a picture that's there for decoration. - Use `fit="contain"` when the whole picture must show, such as a receipt or a document. - With `viewable`, pass a larger `fullSrc` when `src` is a small thumbnail. Without it, the viewer shows the largest `srcSet` candidate, or `src`. - For a picture shown at many widths, pass `srcSet` with widths (`"hero-640.jpg 640w, hero-1280.jpg 1280w"`) so small screens load a small file. You can leave `sizes` out on a lazy picture: Image sets `sizes="auto"`, and the browser picks by the width the frame is laid out at. Give `sizes` for a `priority` picture, which loads before layout. - Use `sources` for another crop on phones (`media`) or a lighter format (`type: "image/avif"`): each becomes a `` in a `` around the ``, tried in order before `src`. - Use `darkSrc` for a version drawn for a dark page (a chart, a diagram, a logo on dark), and `dim` to darken a photo a shade on a dark page so a bright one doesn't glare. - Ask for confirmation yourself before `onRemove` removes something for good. ## Behavior - It loads lazily (`loading="lazy"`) and decodes off the main thread (`decoding="async"`) by default. For the main picture at the top of a page, pass `priority`: it loads at once with `fetchpriority="high"`, so it shows sooner (Largest Contentful Paint). - With `ratio="auto"`, pass the picture's `width` and `height`: the frame takes their shape before the picture arrives (at most as wide as its container), so the page doesn't jump when it loads. Without them, the frame has no height until then, and Image warns in the console once. With a fixed ratio and no size of its own (no `className` or `style` on the picture, no width on the frame), the frame takes its container's full width, so it has its shape while loading and keeps it if the picture fails. Give it a width (`frameProps={{ style: { width: 240 } }}` or a utility class) for a smaller one. - While loading, the frame shows the placeholder fill with a lighter band sweeping through it every 2s, like Loader's skeleton (a still fill with reduced motion or forced colors). The band moves on `translate`, so it costs no repaints. In server-rendered HTML the picture is never hidden, so it paints as soon as it arrives, before your script runs or without it. A picture that hydrates from that HTML stays shown, since it may have painted in part already. A lazy picture that mounts on the client and is still loading a frame later is hidden and fades in over 200ms when it arrives (at once with reduced motion); a `priority` one is never hidden. A frame with `ratio="auto"` is at least 48px until the picture arrives, so give it a width and set `width` and `height` on the `` to avoid a jump. - On a lazy picture whose `srcSet` (or a source's) lists widths, `sizes` gets `auto` in front: `"auto"` alone when none was given, or `"auto, "`, so a browser that doesn't know `auto` uses yours (or the whole screen width). An eager or `priority` picture, `x` descriptors, or a `sizes` that already starts with `auto` are left as given. - With `sources`, the `` is `display: contents`, so the frame and the `` lay out exactly as without. - `darkSrc` is the first ``, for `(prefers-color-scheme: dark)` in server HTML. In the browser, a theme that fixes the frame's color scheme (a `*-dark` or `*-light` `data-theme`, a `data-mode`) decides instead, and the picture swaps when any `data-theme`, `data-mode` or `data-brand` on the page changes. The viewer opens the version shown. - `dim` lays `--image-dim` at 20% over a loaded picture in a dark color scheme only (`light-dark()`); the remove button stays above it, and forced colors drop it. - For a reader saving data (Data Saver, `navigator.connection.saveData`, or `prefers-reduced-data: reduce`), only a `priority` picture loads at once; any other is lazy even with `loading="eager"`. Each `srcSet` (the ``'s and each source's) is cut to its smallest version. Server HTML can't know this, so it changes once the page's script runs, before a lazy picture loads. - The viewer is a large Dialog titled with the alt text: Escape, the × or a click on the backdrop close it, and focus goes back to the picture. Its picture has the frame's placeholder while it loads (in the shape `width` and `height` give, or the thumbnail's) and the frame's fallback if it fails. Since the title already names it, the picture itself has `alt=""`, so it isn't read twice. - The remove button only calls `onRemove`; ask for confirmation yourself if removing can't be undone. - Once a removed picture is gone, focus moves to the next picture's remove button in the same list, else the one before, so it isn't lost (as with Badge's tags). A handler that moves focus itself is left alone. ### Do and don't - **Do:** Write alt text that says what the picture shows, or `alt=""` when it is only decoration. (`DoDescribe`) - **Don't:** Use the file name as alt text: screen readers read "IMG_2041.jpg" out, which tells nobody anything. (`DontFileName`) ## Accessibility - `alt` is required by the types. A failed picture's fallback is a `role="img"` named by the alt text. The `` stays in the frame, hidden under it, so its className, style, id, data-* and ref keep working and the frame keeps its size. - The view button is named "View image: " and has `aria-haspopup="dialog"`; the remove button is named "Remove image: ". Both work with the keyboard and show a focus ring. - The fallback icon and the remove button keep 3:1 in every theme (`Image.test.tsx`). - **Keyboard:** with `viewable`, the picture is a button: Enter or Space opens it full size in a Dialog, Escape closes it, and focus comes back. With `onRemove`, its × is a Tab stop too. A plain image adds no Tab stop. ## Props | Prop | Type | Default | Notes | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `id` | string | none | Goes to the ``, not the frame around it. | | `src` | `string` | | The picture's address. | | `alt` | `string` | | Required. What the picture shows; `""` only for a decorative picture. | | `ratio` | `'auto' \| 'square' \| '4:3' \| 'video' \| number` | `'auto'` | The frame's shape. A number is width / height. `auto` keeps the picture's own shape. | | `fit` | `'cover' \| 'contain'` | `'cover'` | With a fixed ratio: fill and crop, or fit whole. | | `priority` | `boolean` | `false` | The main picture at the top of a page: `loading="eager"` and `fetchpriority="high"` instead of lazy. | | `rounded` | `boolean` | `true` | Corners from `--image-radius`. | | `fallback` | `ReactNode` | a broken-image icon | Shown if the picture fails to load. | | `viewable` | `boolean` | `false` | Makes the picture a button that opens it full size in a Dialog. | | `fullSrc` | `string` | the largest `srcSet` candidate, or `src` | A larger version for the viewer. | | `viewLabel` | `string` | `"View image: "` | The view button's name. | | `onRemove` | `() => void` | | Shows a remove button in the top end corner. | | `removeLabel` | `string` | `"Remove image: "` | The remove button's name. | | `darkSrc` | `string` | | A version for a dark color scheme: the page's dark theme, or the screen's preference where the theme follows it. | | `dim` | `boolean` | `false` | Darkens a loaded photo a shade in a dark color scheme. | | `sources` | `{ srcSet, media?, type?, sizes?, width?, height? }[]` | | Other versions, each a `` in a `` ahead of `src`: for a media query (art direction) or a format. `width` and `height` for a version with another shape. | | `frameProps` | `HTMLAttributes` | | For the frame, such as `style={{ width: 240 }}`. | `ref`, `className`, `loading`, `width`, `height`, `srcSet`, `sizes`, `onLoad`, `onError` and other `` props go to the ``. ## Component tokens Each is an optional override: set it on the page, a container or one image. The list lives in `src/components/Image/image.tokens.json` (also in `design-tokens/components/`). | Token | Default | Use | | --- | --- | --- | | `--image-bg` | `surface-muted` | The frame's fill while the picture loads, and behind a failed one. | | `--image-shine` | `surface` | The lighter band that sweeps through the fill while the picture loads (at 60%). | | `--image-dim` | `black` | With dim, the layer that darkens a photo in a dark color scheme (at 20%). | | `--image-fallback-color` | `text-muted` | The broken-image icon (3:1 on bg). | | `--image-focus-ring` | `focus-ring` | A viewable picture's keyboard focus ring. | | `--image-edge` | `picture-edge` | The hairline just inside a loaded photo's edge, so a white or black picture keeps its shape on a page of the same color. Not with fit="contain". | | `--image-radius` | `radius-surface` | The frame's corners with rounded (8px). | | `--image-min-size` | `spacing-12` | The least width and height of an 'auto' frame before the picture arrives (48px). | | `--image-fallback-icon` | `spacing-6` | The broken-image icon's size (24px). | | `--image-remove-offset` | `spacing-2` | The remove button's distance from the corner (8px). | | `--image-remove-shadow` | `elevation-part` | The remove button's shadow, so it stands out on any picture. |

components.name: ImageCropper
components.summary: A picture in a frame of a fixed shape, which people move and zoom to choose the part to keep: a profile photo, a team logo, a cover.
components.guide:
# ImageCropper

A picture in a frame of a fixed shape, which people move and zoom to choose the part to keep: a profile photo, a team logo, a cover. The app gets the crop in the picture's own pixels, and `cropImage` draws it.

**Also called:** image crop, avatar editor, photo cropper.

```tsx
import { Field, ImageCropper, cropImage, type CropArea } from "@diki-stwn/serupa-ds";

const [area, setArea] = React.useState<CropArea | null>(null);

<Field label="Profile photo" hint="Shown round, beside your name.">
  <ImageCropper src={URL.createObjectURL(file)} shape="round" onCropChange={setArea} />
</Field>

// on Save: a 256px square PNG of the crop
const photo = area && await cropImage(src, area, { width: 256 });
```

## When to use

- After someone picks a picture for a place with a fixed shape: an avatar, a logo, a cover or banner, a card's picture.
- When the server crops the original: send `onCropChange`'s area with it.

## When not to use

- Picking the file: use [FileUpload] (npx serupa-docs FileUpload), then show the picked file here.
- Showing a picture: use [Image] (npx serupa-docs Image) (its `fit` and `ratio` crop for display without changing the file).
- Editing a picture (rotating, filters, drawing): a full editor is outside a design system.

## Anatomy

Drawn from the `Playground` story.

1. **Frame** (`.srp-image-cropper__frame`): the crop's shape (`aspect`), with the picture behind it filling it edge to edge. A round one dims the picture outside a circle and rings it.
2. **Thirds** (`.srp-image-cropper__grid`): thin lines in thirds while the picture is dragged.
3. **Zoom row** (`.srp-image-cropper__zoom`): Zoom out, a small [Slider] (npx serupa-docs Slider) named "Zoom", Zoom in.

## Usage

- Name it: a [Field] (npx serupa-docs Field) label ("Profile photo") or `aria-label`.
- Match `aspect` and `shape` to where the picture goes: `shape="round"` for an avatar, `aspect={16 / 9}` for a cover. A round crop is still a square picture; the avatar draws the circle.
- `onCropChange(area)` fires once the picture loads (centered, as large as fits) and after every move or zoom, with `{ x, y, width, height }` in the picture's own whole pixels. Keep the last one for Save.
- `cropImage(src, area, { width, type, quality })` resolves to a Blob of the crop, `width` pixels wide (default: the crop's own width). A picture from another site needs CORS: give it `crossOrigin="anonymous"` here and in `cropImage`'s options, or crop on the server.
- The picture always covers the frame, so a crop never has an empty edge, and zoom 1 is as far out as it goes.
- To start from a crop saved before, give it as `defaultCrop` (or `crop` with `onCropChange`, controlled): the picture is moved and zoomed to show it.
- A new `src` starts over: centered at `defaultZoom`. While it loads the zoom row waits; if it can't be loaded, the frame says so and the zoom row goes.

### Do and don't

- **Do:** Show the shape it will have: round for an avatar, with the hint saying where it's shown. (`ProfilePhoto`)
- **Don't:** Crop a picture people didn't pick, or skip the step when the shape won't fit most pictures: a cover from a phone photo needs it. (`Cover`)

## Accessibility

- **Role and name:** a `group` named by its Field label or `aria-label`. In it, the frame is a focusable group named "Crop area" and described by how to use it ("Drag the picture or use the arrow keys to move it, and plus or minus to zoom."). The zoom is a slider named "Zoom", read as a percentage, between the "Zoom out" and "Zoom in" buttons.
- **Keyboard:** Tab reaches the frame, then the zoom row; the slider takes its usual keys.

| Key | Does |
| --- | --- |
| Tab | To the frame, then Zoom out, the slider and Zoom in |
| ArrowLeft, ArrowRight, ArrowUp, ArrowDown | On the frame: move the picture the way the arrow points, a tenth of the frame |
| Shift with an arrow | Move it half the frame |
| + (or =), − | On the frame: zoom in or out a tenth, around the middle |

- **Pointer and touch:** drag the picture, or tap a spot to bring it to the middle (2.5.7: moving needs no drag, and zooming has buttons). Two fingers pinch to zoom, around their middle; a trackpad pinch (Ctrl with the wheel) zooms too. The page doesn't scroll under a finger on the frame (`touch-action: none`); a plain mouse wheel scrolls the page.
- **Contrast:** the failure text reads 4.5:1 on the frame in every theme (`ImageCropper.test.tsx`). In forced colors, the frame's edge and the ring use the system text color.
- **What's still yours:** the label, where the picture will be shown, and a text alternative wherever the cropped picture appears.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `src` | `string` | | The picture: a URL, or an object URL of a picked file. A new one starts over. |
| `aspect` | `number` | `1` | The crop's width over its height: `16 / 9`, `3 / 4`. |
| `shape` | `'rect' \| 'round'` | `'rect'` | `'round'` dims the picture outside a circle (an ellipse with another aspect). |
| `crop` | `CropArea \| null` | | The crop (controlled), in the picture's pixels; use with `onCropChange`. |
| `defaultCrop` | `CropArea \| null` | | The crop at first (uncontrolled), such as a saved one; centered when left out. |
