| `defaultZoom` | `number` | `1` | The zoom at first; 1 shows the whole width or height. |
| `maxZoom` | `number` | `4` | How far in it zooms. |
| `onCropChange` | `(area: CropArea) => void` | | The crop in the picture's pixels, on load and after each change. |
| `crossOrigin` | `'' \| 'anonymous' \| 'use-credentials'` | | For another site's picture, so `cropImage` can read it. |
| `disabled` | `boolean` | | Turns moving and zooming off. |

| `id` | `string` | | Goes to the root `<div role="group">`; inside a Field, the Field's label names it through this id. |

`className`, `ref` and other props go to the root `<div>`.

## Component tokens

Each is an optional override: set it on the page, a container or one ImageCropper. The list lives in `src/components/ImageCropper/image-cropper.tokens.json` (also in `design-tokens/components/`).

<!-- token-table:start (made from image-cropper.tokens.json by npm run tokens: edit the descriptions there) -->
| Token | Default | Use |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--image-cropper-bg` | `surface-muted` | The frame behind the picture, seen while it loads or when it can't. |
| `--image-cropper-edge` | `picture-edge` | The hairline round the frame, so a pale picture keeps its edge. |
| `--image-cropper-scrim` | `overlay` | A round crop: what dims the picture outside the circle. |
| `--image-cropper-guide` | `white` | A round crop: the ring on the circle, over the picture. |
| `--image-cropper-grid` | `white` | The lines in thirds shown while the picture is dragged. |
| `--image-cropper-focus-ring` | `focus-ring` | The frame's focus ring. |
| `--image-cropper-fallback-color` | `text-muted` | The icon and words in the frame when the picture can't be loaded. |
| `--image-cropper-grid-opacity` | `opacity-60` | How strongly the thirds show while dragging. |
| `--image-cropper-radius` | `radius-control` | The frame's corners, as a field's. |
| `--image-cropper-max-width` | `container-xs` | The widest it grows (20rem); it fills a narrower column. |
| `--image-cropper-gap` | `spacing-2` | Between the frame and the zoom row (8px). |
| `--image-cropper-zoom-gap` | `spacing-1` | Between the zoom buttons and the slider (4px). |
<!-- token-table:end -->

components.name: InlineEdit
components.summary: Text people can change where it is: a project name, a card title, a slug.
components.guide:
# InlineEdit

Text people can change where it is: a project name, a card title, a slug. It shows the text with a pencil on hover; a click, Enter or Space opens a field in the same place, Enter or leaving the field saves, and Escape puts the text back.

**Also called:** click to edit, editable text.

```tsx
import { InlineEdit } from "@diki-stwn/serupa-ds";

<InlineEdit label="Project name" defaultValue="Apollo launch plan" onValueChange={rename} />

const [slug, setSlug] = React.useState("apollo-plan");
<InlineEdit label="Slug" value={slug} onValueChange={setSlug}
  validate={(v) => (/\s/.test(v) ? "Use dashes instead of spaces." : null)} />

<InlineEdit label="Description" placeholder="Add a description" size="sm" />
```

## When to use

- One short value on a page people already look at and change now and then: a name, a title, a label.
- Lists or boards where opening a form for each rename would be slow.

## When not to use

- Several fields that are saved together, or a value people must review before saving: use a form with [Field] (npx serupa-docs Field) and a Save button.
- Long text over several lines: use a [Textarea] (npx serupa-docs Textarea) in a form.
- Text most people only read: show it as text, and put editing behind an Edit button.

## Anatomy

Drawn from the `States` story.

1. **Value** (`.srp-inline-edit__view`): the text as it reads; activating it starts editing.
2. **Text** (`.srp-inline-edit__text`): the value, or the placeholder when it's empty.
3. **Edit icon** (`.srp-inline-edit__icon`): says the text can be edited.

## Usage

- Give every InlineEdit a `label` that says what the text is ("Project name"). It names the field, and the button is read as "Project name: Apollo, Edit".
- Save in `onValueChange`, which runs only when the text has changed. If saving can fail, keep the old value and tell people, for example with a [Toast] (npx serupa-docs Toast).
- Use `validate` for rules the text must meet. Return a message to keep the field open with that message under it; return nothing to save. For a check on the server ("That slug is taken."), return a Promise of the message.
- Set a `placeholder` when the text can be empty, so the empty button still shows something to click.
- Match `size` to what's around it; both modes use Input's heights and padding at every size.

## Behavior

- Opening selects the text, so typing replaces it.
- Enter saves and Escape cancels; both put focus back on the button. Leaving the field (Tab or a click elsewhere) saves too and leaves focus where it went. Switching to another window or browser tab isn't leaving it: the field stays open for when people come back.
- Leaving with a text that `validate` refuses keeps the field open with its message, and the message is said, so people know why it didn't close. Focus isn't pulled back: it stays where they went, and the field is still there to come back to (or Escape there to put the text back).
- While a Promise from `validate` is pending, the field is `aria-busy` and stays open. Only the latest check counts: typing or Escape drops the one running, and a rejected Promise keeps the field open without a message (resolve to a message instead).
- Escape inside a [Dialog] (npx serupa-docs Dialog) or [Drawer] (npx serupa-docs Drawer) only cancels the edit; the dialog stays open.
- With `editing` and `onEditingChange` you open and close it yourself, for example from a Rename item in a [Menu] (npx serupa-docs Menu). Each time it opens, the field starts from the current text.
- `disabled` and `readOnly` show the text without a button; `disabled` also mutes it (`--inline-edit-text-disabled`, still 4.5:1). Inside a `<fieldset disabled>` the button is disabled: the text is muted the same way, with no hover, pointer or pencil.
- While someone types with an input method (Japanese, Chinese, Korean), Enter and Escape confirm or cancel the composition, not the edit.

### Do and don't

- **Do:** Set a `placeholder` when the text can be empty, so the empty button still shows something to click. (`DoPlaceholder`)
- **Don't:** Leave an empty value without a placeholder: there's nothing to see or click. (`DontEmpty`)

## Accessibility

- At rest it's a `<button>` whose name is the label, the text and "Edit" (from `SerupaProvider` labels: "Ubah" in Indonesian). The visible text is part of the name, so voice control users can say what they see.
- While editing it's an [Input] (npx serupa-docs Input) named by `label`; a validation message makes it `aria-invalid` and describes it. Focus stays in the field, where screen readers don't read the description again, so the message is also said politely on each failed try.
- The pencil shows on hover and keyboard focus, and always on touch screens, which have no hover. It also always shows when the value is empty and there is no `placeholder`, since the button then has no text to find it by (a placeholder such as "Add notes" is better).
- The text and the placeholder keep 4.5:1 on the page and on the hover background in every theme (`InlineEdit.test.tsx`).

### Keyboard

| Key | Does |
| --- | --- |
| Enter / Space | On the text, opens the field with the text selected |
| Enter | In the field, saves (unless `validate` keeps it open with an error) and returns focus to the text |
| Escape | Puts the text back and returns focus, without closing a Dialog or Drawer around it |
| Tab | Leaves the field, which saves |

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | string | none | Goes to the root `<div>`. |
| `label` | `string` | | Required. What the text is. |
| `value` | `string` | | Controlled. |
| `defaultValue` | `string` | `''` | Uncontrolled. |
| `onValueChange` | `(value: string) => void` | | On save, when the text changed. |
| `onCancel` | `() => void` | | On Escape. |
| `validate` | `(value: string) => ReactNode \| Promise<ReactNode>` | | Return a message to keep it open, or nothing to save; a Promise for a check on the server. |
| `placeholder` | `string` | | Shown when the text is empty. |
| `size` | `'sm' \| 'md' \| 'lg'` | `'md'` | Input's sizes. |
| `editing`, `onEditingChange` | `boolean`, `(editing: boolean) => void` | | Open and close it yourself. |
| `defaultEditing` | `boolean` | `false` | Open at first, with the field focused, without controlling it. |
| `disabled`, `readOnly` | `boolean` | `false` | The text without a button. |
| `editLabel` | `string` | `'Edit'` | The last word of the button's name. |
| `inputProps` | `InputProps` | | For the field: `maxLength`, `spellCheck`, `autoComplete`, `inputMode`… |

Every other prop, `className` and `ref` go to the outer `<div>`. `autoFocus` focuses the edit button (or the field, while editing). It has `data-component="inline-edit"`, `data-size` and `data-state` (`viewing` or `editing`).

## Component tokens

Each is an optional override: set it on the page, a container or one InlineEdit. The field and the button's height and padding use Input's tokens. The list lives in `src/components/InlineEdit/inline-edit.tokens.json` (also in `design-tokens/components/`).

<!-- token-table:start (made from inline-edit.tokens.json by npm run tokens: edit the descriptions there) -->
| Token | Default | Use |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--inline-edit-text` | `text` | The text in the button. |
| `--inline-edit-placeholder` | `text-muted` | The placeholder when the text is empty. |
| `--inline-edit-text-disabled` | `text-muted` | The text of a disabled InlineEdit. |
| `--inline-edit-icon` | `text-muted` | The pencil. |
| `--inline-edit-text-muted-shaded` | `text-muted-shaded` | The placeholder and pencil icon on the hovered button, where `text-muted` would fall under 4.5:1 on the shaded fill. |
| `--inline-edit-bg-hover` | `surface-hover` | The button's background on hover. |
| `--inline-edit-bg-pressed` | `pressed` | The button's background while pressed, one step past hover. |
| `--inline-edit-error` | `danger-text` | The validation message. |
| `--inline-edit-focus-ring` | `focus-ring` | The button's keyboard focus ring. |
| `--inline-edit-radius` | `radius-control` | The button's corners (6px). |
| `--inline-edit-gap` | `spacing-1` | Space between the field and its message (4px). |
<!-- token-table:end -->

components.name: Input
components.summary: A single-line text field: a native `<input>` in a box that can hold icons.
components.guide:
# Input A single-line text field: a native `` in a box that can hold icons. Three sizes at the control heights (24, 32 and 44px, like Button), a focus ring, and invalid, read-only and disabled states. Field colors come from the alias tokens (`field`, `field-border`, `placeholder`), so text keeps 4.5:1 and the focus ring 3:1 in every theme. **Also called:** text input, text field. ```jsx import { Input, InputAction } from '@diki-stwn/serupa-ds'; setEmail(e.target.value)} /> // invalid: say what's wrong in text, linked to the field

Enter an email address like name@example.com.

// a count at the end of the field: "12 / 30" // buttons inside the box, at the end: a text action, or an icon action named by its label setCode(e.target.value)} actions={ apply(code)} />} /> navigator.clipboard.writeText(link)} />} /> ``` ## When to use - A short answer on one line that people type freely: a name, an email address, a URL, a phone number. - A code or an ID people copy in, such as a coupon or an invite code. ## When not to use - An answer that can run past one line: use [Textarea] (npx serupa-docs Textarea). - A choice from a known list: use [Select] (npx serupa-docs Select), or [Combobox] (npx serupa-docs Combobox) for a long one. - A number people step up and down, such as a quantity: use [NumberInput] (npx serupa-docs NumberInput). - A password or a search: use [PasswordInput] (npx serupa-docs PasswordInput) or [SearchInput] (npx serupa-docs SearchInput). ## Anatomy Drawn from the `Icons` story. 1. **Field** (`.srp-input__field`): where the text is typed. 2. **Leading icon** (`.srp-input__icon--start`): an optional picture of what goes in, such as a search glass. 3. **Trailing icon** (`.srp-input__icon--end`): an optional picture or status at the end. 4. **Actions** (`.srp-input__actions`): InputAction buttons at the very end of the box: a text action is the field's height less 6px (26px at md), an icon action its icon with 4px round it (24px at md). ## Usage - Match the input's size to the buttons beside it: an `md` input with an `md` Button lines up exactly. - Keep labels above the field, short and specific; use the placeholder only for an example of the format. - Show errors after someone leaves the field or submits, not on every keystroke. - Show a count only when there's a limit people need to plan around, such as a short title. - Use `mask` for text with a structured shape, such as a card number (`"9999 9999 9999 9999 ?999"`, supporting 12–19 digits), a date (`"99/99/9999"`) or an IBAN (`"AA99 **** **** **** ?**** **** **** **** **"`, up to 34 characters). `9` takes a digit, `a` a letter, `A` a letter in capitals, `*` either, and `?` marks optional trailing slots for variable-length identifiers. `\` makes the next character plain, and everything else shows as it is. People type only the letters and digits; the spaces and slashes appear by themselves, a paste is laid into the pattern, and the caret stays where they were typing. Keep the format in the label or hint too ("Expiry date, MM/YY"), and check the value on the server: a mask shapes text, it doesn't validate it. For phone numbers with a country picker, use [PhoneInput] (npx serupa-docs PhoneInput). - Use `actions` for a button that works on what's in the field: Apply for a coupon, Copy for a link, Clear, or Show. Keep it to one or two. Give an icon action a `label` that names what it does to what ("Copy invite link", not "Copy"); a text action shows its label as its words. A button that sends the whole form belongs outside the field, as a Button. - Use `prefix` and `suffix` for fixed text people shouldn't type, such as "https://", "@" or "kg". Keep it short, and keep the unit in the label too ("Weight (kg)") when the field makes no sense without it. ### Do and don't - **Do:** Give a field a width that fits what goes in it: a short field for a postcode says how much to type. (`DoFitWidth`) - **Don't:** Make every field full width: a five-digit postcode as wide as a street address looks like it wants more. (`DontFullWidthShort`) - **Do:** Say in the error how to put it right, through [Field] (npx serupa-docs Field)'s `error`. (`DoHelpfulError`) - **Don't:** Only say that something is wrong: "Invalid input" leaves people guessing what to change. (`DontVagueError`) ## States | State | Look | | --- | --- | | Rest | `field` background, 1px `field-border` | | Hover | `field-border-hover` | | Focus | The border and a 1px ring hugging it in `focus-ring` (2px in all), shown at once and faded out on blur; a visible outline in forced-colors mode | | Invalid | `danger` border, and a `danger` focus ring | | Read-only | `field-readonly` background, no hover change; still focusable and selectable | | Disabled | `field-readonly` background, `disabled-border` edge and `disabled-text` at full opacity, `not-allowed` cursor | ## Accessibility - A field the browser fills in (a saved address, a login) keeps the field's colors, and its border doubles inward until it's focused, so the fill shows in more than color. - On iOS the field's text is 16px at every size, so Safari doesn't zoom the page when it takes focus; the box keeps its height. - A `prefix` or `suffix` is added to the field's `aria-describedby` (after your own), so screen readers say "https://" or "kg" too. A press on it focuses the field. Its `text-muted` keeps 4.5:1 on the field in every theme (`Input.test.tsx`). - Every input needs a name: a visible `

components.name: Kanban
components.summary: A board of columns of cards, such as a sprint or a sales pipeline, that people move by dragging a handle, by keyboard, or from each card's "Move to…" menu.
components.guide:
# Kanban

A board of columns of cards, such as a sprint or a sales pipeline, that people move by dragging a handle, by keyboard, or from each card's "Move to…" menu. Each move is said out loud, and nothing changes until the card is dropped.

**Also called:** board, task board, kanban board.

```tsx
import { Kanban, type KanbanColumn } from "@diki-stwn/serupa-ds";

interface Task { id: string; title: string }

const [columns, setColumns] = useState<KanbanColumn<Task>[]>([
  { id: "todo", title: "To do", items: tasks.todo },
  { id: "doing", title: "In progress", limit: 3, items: tasks.doing },
  { id: "done", title: "Done", items: tasks.done },
]);

<Kanban aria-label="Sprint 42" columns={columns} getKey={(t) => t.id} getLabel={(t) => t.title}
  renderCard={(t) => <TaskCard task={t} />} onMove={(next, move) => { setColumns(next); save(move); }} />
```

## When to use

- Work that moves through stages, where people see every stage at once and move items between them: tasks, tickets, leads, hiring.
- A column that should hold only a few items at a time (a work-in-progress limit).

## When not to use

- Reordering one list: use [SortableList] (npx serupa-docs SortableList).
- Many items with many fields to compare or sort: a [Table] (npx serupa-docs Table) with a status column reads better, and a status [Select] (npx serupa-docs Select) per row moves them.
- Stages in a fixed order that one item passes through: use a [Stepper] (npx serupa-docs Stepper) or [Timeline] (npx serupa-docs Timeline).

## Anatomy

Drawn from the `Default` story.

1. **Column** (`.srp-kanban__column`): one stage, a `section` named by its heading.
2. **Title** (`.srp-kanban__title`): the stage's name.
3. **Count** (`.srp-kanban__count`): how many cards, with the limit when there is one, and "Over limit" past it.
4. **Card** (`.srp-kanban__card`): one item: its handle, your content and its menu.
5. **Handle** (`.srp-kanban__handle`): picks the card up, by pointer or keyboard.
6. **Move to…** (`.srp-kanban__menu`): moves the card to another column without dragging.

## Usage

- `columns` is controlled: apply the new columns from `onMove`, which also gives the move (`item`, `from` and `to`, each a column id and index) for saving.
- `getLabel` names each card in words; it's read on its buttons and in every announcement, so keep it short and unique on the board ("Fix login", not "Task").
- `renderCard` draws what's on the card. Put links and buttons there as you like; the handle and the menu are Kanban's. Each card redraws only when its item, place or `renderCard` changes, so on a big board define `renderCard` outside the component or in a `useCallback`: a new function every render redraws every card.
- `limit` warns, it doesn't block: a column past its limit says "Over limit", and cards can still move in. Refuse a move in `onMove` if your process needs that.
- Name the board with `aria-label` ("Sprint 42"). Set `headingLevel` to fit the page's outline (3 by default).

## Behavior

- **Pointer:** press the handle and move; the card follows the pointer, the column it would land in is outlined, and the other cards make room. Near the board's edge the board scrolls sideways, and near a column's top or bottom the column scrolls. Let go to drop, or let the drag be canceled (a pointer cancel) to put it back.
- **Keyboard:** Tab to a handle, Space or Enter picks the card up. Up and Down move it within its column, Left and Right to the column before or after in reading order (mirrored right to left), Home and End to the top and bottom. Space or Enter drops it; Escape, Tab or a click elsewhere puts it back. Focus stays on the card's handle as it moves.
- **Move to…:** each card's menu lists the other columns; picking one puts the card at the end of that column and keeps focus on it. It's the way to move a card with one tap or click (WCAG 2.5.7).
- A narrow board scrolls sideways in its own box, so the page doesn't.

### Loading and failed

- **Loading:** set `loading` and pass the columns you know with no cards yet. Each column keeps its title and shows two placeholder cards with no count, and the board is `aria-busy`, so nothing below it moves when the cards arrive. Name the wait in `loadingLabel` ("Loading tasks"): a screen reader hears it once, after the loader's delay, so a quick load says nothing. When you refresh cards already shown, keep them in and set `busy`: they stay until the new ones arrive.
- **Failed:** in place of the board, a danger [Alert] (npx serupa-docs Alert) that says what didn't load and offers Retry in `actions`. It's `role="alert"`, so the failure is heard as it appears. On Retry, go back to loading.

```tsx
type Task = { id: string; title: string };
{state === 'failed' ? <Alert tone="danger" actions={<Button size="sm" onClick={load}>Retry</Button>}>The board didn't load.</Alert>
  : <Kanban aria-label="Sprint 42" columns={state === 'loading' ? STAGES : columns} loading={state === 'loading'} loadingLabel="Loading tasks"
      getKey={(t: Task) => t.id} getLabel={(t: Task) => t.title} renderCard={(t: Task) => t.title} onMove={setColumns} />}
```

### Do and don't

- **Do:** Give each card a short, unique name with `getLabel` ("Fix login"): it's read on its buttons and in every announcement. (`Default`)
- **Don't:** Give cards the same name ("Task"): screen reader users can't tell which one moved. (`DontVagueCards`)

## Accessibility

- **Roles and names:** the board is a `group` named by `aria-label`; each column a `section` (a region) named by its heading, with its cards in a list named the same way.
- **Handle:** a button named "Move Fix login", described by the keyboard instructions, and `aria-pressed` while the card is picked up.
- **Announcements:** each step is said politely: "Picked up Fix login. To do, position 1 of 3.", "Fix login, Done, position 2 of 5.", "Fix login moved to Done, position 2 of 5.", and "Canceled. Fix login is back in To do, position 1 of 3."
- **Without dragging:** the keyboard and the "Move to…" menu both move a card without a drag (WCAG 2.5.7), and the menu also works with a screen reader's virtual cursor.
- **Over limit:** said in words with a warning icon, not by color alone (WCAG 1.4.1).
- **Contrast:** titles, counts, "Over limit" and card text read 4.5:1, and the handle 3:1, in every theme (`Kanban.test.tsx`).
- **What's still yours:** the content of each card, and saying so if a move fails to save.

### Keyboard

| Key | Does |
| --- | --- |
| Tab | To each card's handle and its "Move to…" menu button |
| Space, Enter (on a handle) | Picks the card up; again, drops it where it is |
| ↑ ↓ | Moves the picked-up card within its column |
| ← → | Moves it to the column before or after (mirrored right to left) |
| Home, End | To the top or bottom of its column |
| Escape, Tab | Puts it back where it was |

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `columns` | `KanbanColumn<T>[]` | | Required. `{ id, title, items, limit? }` for each column, in order. |
| `getKey` | `(item: T) => string \| number` | | Required. A stable key for each card. |
| `getLabel` | `(item: T) => string` | | Required. The card's name in words. |
| `renderCard` | `(item: T, state) => ReactNode` | | Required. What the card shows; `state` has `column`, `index` and `dragging`. |
| `onMove` | `(columns, move) => void` | | Required. The new columns and the move, when a card is dropped somewhere new. |
| `headingLevel` | `2 \| 3 \| 4 \| 5 \| 6` | `3` | The column headings' level. |
| `disabled` | `boolean` | `false` | Shows the cards without handles or menus. |
| `loading` | `boolean` | `false` | Its cards are loading: sets `aria-busy`, and while no column has cards yet, each shows two placeholder cards and no count. |
| `loadingLabel` | `string` | `"Loading…"` | Said once as the placeholder cards appear. |

`id`, `className`, `ref` and other props go to the board's `<div>`.

## Component tokens

Each is an optional override: set it on the page, a container or one Kanban. The list lives in `src/components/Kanban/kanban.tokens.json` (also in `design-tokens/components/`).

<!-- token-table:start (made from kanban.tokens.json by npm run tokens: edit the descriptions there) -->
| Token | Default | Use |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--kanban-text` | `text` | Titles and card text (4.5:1 on the column and the card). |
| `--kanban-muted` | `text-muted` | Counts, handles and the empty column's words (4.5:1 on the column). |
| `--kanban-column-bg` | `surface-muted` | A column's background. |
| `--kanban-card-bg` | `surface` | A card's background. |
| `--kanban-card-border` | `border` | A card's outline. |
| `--kanban-card-border-active` | `primary-text` | The border of the card being moved, as in SortableList. |
| `--kanban-target-border` | `primary-text` | The outline of the column a moving card would land in (3:1). |
| `--kanban-over` | `danger-text` | A count over its column's limit (4.5:1 on the column). |
| `--kanban-handle-active` | `primary-subtle` | A picked-up card's handle. |
| `--kanban-handle-bg-hover` | `secondary` | The drag handle's background on hover, as SortableList's. |
| `--kanban-handle-bg-pressed` | `secondary-hover` | The drag handle's background while held down, a step past its hover. |
| `--kanban-focus-ring` | `focus-ring` | The ring around a focused handle. |
| `--kanban-column-radius` | `radius-surface` | A column's corners (8px). |
| `--kanban-card-radius` | `radius-control` | A card's corners (6px). |
| `--kanban-card-shadow` | `elevation-raised` | The card being dragged: level 2, raised, as in SortableList. |
| `--kanban-gap` | `spacing-3` | Space between columns (12px). |
| `--kanban-padding` | `spacing-3` | Space inside a column (12px). |
| `--kanban-card-padding` | `spacing-2` | Space inside a card (8px). |
| `--kanban-column-width` | `spacing-72` | A column's width (288px). |
<!-- token-table:end -->

components.name: Kbd
components.summary: Shows a keyboard key or shortcut as keycaps, in help text, tooltips, menus and empty states.
components.guide:
# Kbd Shows a keyboard key or shortcut as keycaps, in help text, tooltips, menus and empty states. **Also called:** keycap, keyboard key. ```tsx import { Kbd } from "@diki-stwn/serupa-ds";

Press / to search.

// ⌘ K on a Mac, Ctrl + K elsewhere // inside a control ``` ## When to use - Telling people about a keyboard shortcut: in help text, a tooltip or an empty state. - Instructions that name a key, such as "Press Enter to send". ## When not to use - Code, or a command people type: use the native `` element instead. - A shortcut hint at the end of a menu item: use [Menu] (npx serupa-docs Menu)'s `shortcut` prop instead. - A short label such as a status or a count: use [Badge] (npx serupa-docs Badge) instead. ## Anatomy Drawn from the `InText` story. 1. **Key** (`.srp-kbd__key`): one key, as it's printed on the keyboard. 2. **Plus** (`.srp-kbd__plus`): between keys pressed together. ## Usage - Pass a combination as `keys`, one key each, and a single key as children. - Use `mod` for shortcuts that follow the platform, so Mac users see ⌘ and others see Ctrl. - Kbd only shows the keys: wire the shortcut yourself. ### Named keys These names (in any case, and with any spaces, `_` or `-`: `page_up` and `Page Up` are `pageup`) show as symbols on Apple devices and as words elsewhere, and screen readers hear the key's name: | Name | Apple | Elsewhere | | --- | --- | --- | | `mod` | ⌘ | Ctrl | | `cmd`, `meta` | ⌘ | ⊞ | | `ctrl` | ⌃ | Ctrl | | `alt`, `option` | ⌥ | Alt | | `shift` | ⇧ | Shift | | `enter`, `return` | ↵ | Enter | | `backspace`, `delete` | ⌫, ⌦ | Backspace, Del | | `tab`, `esc`, `space` (or `" "`) | ⇥, Esc, Space | Tab, Esc, Space | | `up`, `down`, `left`, `right` (or `ArrowUp`…`ArrowRight`, as `KeyboardEvent.key` names them) | ↑ ↓ ← → | ↑ ↓ ← → | | `home`, `end` | ↖ ↘ | Home, End | | `pageup` (`pgup`), `pagedown` (`pgdn`) | ⇞ ⇟ | PgUp, PgDn | | `capslock`, `insert` (`ins`), `fn` | ⇪, Ins, fn | Caps Lock, Ins, Fn | Use `mod` for shortcuts that follow the platform. Any other text shows as it is, and single letters show in capitals. ## Behavior - Inside a `SerupaProvider` with `platform` set (`"apple"` or `"other"`, worked out on the server from the User-Agent or `Sec-CH-UA-Platform`), the right keys show from the first render, the server's too. Without it, the platform is read in the browser after the page loads, so server-rendered pages show the words first. - It sits with the text, so it can go inline in a sentence. Every Kbd is 20px tall, so it fits inside any line of 14px text or larger without stretching it, and looks the same in a sentence, a tooltip, Prose, a list of shortcuts and a command's row. - A one-character key (K, ⌘, ↑) is square, so the keys of a combination line up; a word (Esc, Ctrl) gets 6px each side. - Inside a control, such as a search button, use `size="sm"`: 16px keys with a thin, light outline and no + between them, so they don't crowd the control's edges. ### Do and don't - **Do:** Use `mod` for a shortcut that follows the platform: Mac users see ⌘K and others see Ctrl+K. (`DoMod`) - **Don't:** Write `ctrl` for a shortcut that is ⌘ on a Mac: Mac users press keys that don't work. (`DontHardcodeCtrl`) ## Accessibility - A combination is one `` holding a `` per key, as HTML recommends. Symbols are hidden from screen readers and replaced with the key's name, through the `keyName` label (so "Panah atas" and "Spasi" in `idLabels`); the + between keys is hidden. - Labels and the + keep 4.5:1 in every theme (`Kbd.test.tsx`). - **Keyboard:** none: it shows keys, it doesn't take them. ## Props | Prop | Type | Default | Notes | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `id` | string | none | Goes to the root ``. | | `keys` | `string[]` | | A combination, one key each. Or pass a single key as children. | | `size` | `'sm' \| 'md'` | `'md'` | `md`: 20px keys, wherever text is around them. `sm`: 16px quiet keys with no +, inside a control such as a search button. | `className`, `ref` and other props go to the outer ``. ## Component tokens Each is an optional override: set it on the page, a container or one key. The list lives in `src/components/Kbd/kbd.tokens.json` (also in `design-tokens/components/`). | Token | Default | Use | | --- | --- | --- | | `--kbd-bg` | `surface-muted` | A key's background. | | `--kbd-border` | `border-control` | A key's outline, thicker at the bottom like a keycap. | | `--kbd-text` | `text` | The key's label (4.5:1 on bg). | | `--kbd-separator` | `text-muted` | The + between keys in a combination. | | `--kbd-border-sm` | `border` | size="sm"'s outline, quieter, for a key inside a control such as a search button. | | `--kbd-radius` | `radius-inner` | A key's corners (4px). | | `--kbd-height-sm` | `spacing-4` | size="sm" (16px), for a key inside a control such as a search button. | | `--kbd-height-md` | `spacing-5` | size="md", the default (20px): the one height wherever text is around the key. | | `--kbd-padding-x` | `spacing-1.5` | Space on each side of a word such as Esc (6px). A one-character key is square instead. | | `--kbd-gap` | `spacing-1` | Space between keys and the + in a combination (4px). | | `--kbd-padding-x-sm` | `spacing-1` | size="sm"'s space on each side of a word (4px). | | `--kbd-gap-sm` | `spacing-0.5` | size="sm"'s space between keys, which has no + (2px). | | `--kbd-border-bottom-width` | `border-width-2` | A key's bottom edge, thicker like a keycap's (2px; sm uses 1px all round). |

components.name: KeyboardShortcuts
components.summary: Keyboard shortcuts for an app, in one place: `useShortcut` sets one up where it's used, and `<KeyboardShortcuts>` is the help dialog that lists them all, opened with <kbd>?</kbd>.
components.guide:
# KeyboardShortcuts

Keyboard shortcuts for an app, in one place: `useShortcut` sets one up where it's used, and `<KeyboardShortcuts>` is the help dialog that lists them all, opened with <kbd>?</kbd>.

**Also called:** shortcut help, hotkeys dialog, cheat sheet.

```tsx
import { KeyboardShortcuts, useShortcut } from "@diki-stwn/serupa-ds";

function Inbox() {
  useShortcut(["mod", "K"], openSearch, { description: "Search", group: "Navigation" });
  useShortcut(["C"], compose, { description: "New message", group: "Messages" });
  return …;
}

// Once, in the app's layout:
<KeyboardShortcuts />
```

## When to use

- An app people use every day, where shortcuts save time: a mail client, an editor, a dashboard.
- Listing shortcuts so people can find them, instead of a page in the docs.

## When not to use

- Keys inside one widget, such as arrows in a list or Escape in a popup: the component handles those, on its own element.
- Showing one shortcut in help text or a tooltip: use [Kbd] (npx serupa-docs Kbd).

## Anatomy

Drawn from the `WithListedShortcuts` story.

1. **Group** (`.srp-keyboard-shortcuts__group`): the shortcuts for one part of the app.
2. **Heading** (`.srp-keyboard-shortcuts__heading`): names the group.
3. **Shortcut** (`.srp-keyboard-shortcuts__row`): one shortcut: what it does and its keys.
4. **What it does** (`.srp-description-list__term`): the row's action, in words.
5. **Keys** (`.srp-description-list__details`): the keys to press for it.

## Usage

- Call `useShortcut(keys, handler, { description, group })` in the component the shortcut belongs to. It works while that component is mounted, so a page's shortcuts come and go with the page.
- Write keys as [Kbd] (npx serupa-docs Kbd) takes them, pressed together: `["mod", "K"]`, `["shift", "up"]`, `["?"]`. `mod` is ⌘ on Apple devices and Ctrl elsewhere. One key plus its modifiers: two keys in a row such as `["G", "I"]` aren't supported, so that shortcut isn't set up, and a development warning says so.
- Give it a `description` to list it, and a `group` to put it under a heading. Without a description, it works but isn't listed.
- Put one `<KeyboardShortcuts />` in the app's layout. Also open it from a help menu or button (`open` and `onOpenChange`), since many people don't know <kbd>?</kbd>.
- List shortcuts you don't set up with `useShortcut`, such as an editor's, with `shortcuts`.
- Use the shortcuts people already know for what they already do: `mod`+K to search or open a command list, `mod`+Z to undo (a [Toast] (npx serupa-docs Toast)'s `toast.undo` answers it), `mod`+, for settings, <kbd>?</kbd> for this list, <kbd>Esc</kbd> to close. Don't give those keys another job, and don't make a new shortcut by adding Shift or Alt to one of them for something unrelated: people expect a modifier to vary the same command.
- Keep custom shortcuts for what people do most. Everything a shortcut does must also be reachable with a button or a menu item.
- Prefer shortcuts with `mod`. A single character key (<kbd>?</kbd>, <kbd>N</kbd>) is quick, but speech input or a stray key can set it off, so [WCAG 2.1.4](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/character-key-shortcuts.html) asks that people can turn it off. The dialog has a **Single-key shortcuts** switch for that whenever one is set up (<kbd>?</kbd> itself, by default): off, every shortcut that is one character key with no mod, ctrl, cmd or alt stops working on every page of the app (kept in `localStorage`), and named keys such as <kbd>F2</kbd> or <kbd>Esc</kbd> keep working. With it off, <kbd>?</kbd> no longer opens the dialog, so keep a help menu item or button that opens it.

## Behavior

- A shortcut runs when its keys are pressed anywhere on the page, and the browser's default for those keys is prevented.
- It doesn't run while someone types in a text field (an input, a textarea, a select or an editable area, also inside a web component's shadow root), unless it has `mod`, ctrl or cmd, or `inInputs`. So <kbd>C</kbd> and <kbd>/</kbd> still type.
- It doesn't run when it's one character key and the person turned **Single-key shortcuts** off in the dialog.
- It doesn't run while a modal (a Dialog, a Drawer or this help) is open, since the page behind it is inert. It also doesn't run while an input method is composing, or when another handler already handled the key.
- When two set up the same keys, the newest wins. A panel that opens can take a key from the page, and the page gets it back when the panel closes.
- Symbols such as <kbd>?</kbd> match whatever the keyboard layout needs to type them, so Shift isn't checked. Letters and digits also match by their position, so <kbd>alt</kbd>+<kbd>K</kbd> works on a Mac, where Option changes the character. A letter matches by position only when the key types no Latin letter (Option on a Mac, a Cyrillic or Greek layout), so on AZERTY or Dvorak it goes by the letter typed.
- The dialog lists each group in the order its first shortcut was set up, with "Show keyboard shortcuts" under General. With one group, it has no heading. The same keys and description are listed once, however many components set them up.

### Do and don't

- **Do:** Give each shortcut a `description` and a `group`, so the list has headings to scan by. (`WithListedShortcuts`)
- **Don't:** Leave shortcuts without a group: they pile up in one long list. (`DontUngrouped`)

## Accessibility

- **Keyboard:**

| Key | Does |
| --- | --- |
| <kbd>?</kbd> | Opens the list (`helpKeys`), unless **Single-key shortcuts** is off. |
| <kbd>Tab</kbd> | Moves through the dialog: its close button. |
| <kbd>Escape</kbd> | Closes it, and focus goes back to where it was. |

- The dialog is a [Dialog] (npx serupa-docs Dialog), titled "Keyboard shortcuts". Each group is a heading over a `<dl>`: what a shortcut does, then its keys in [Kbd] (npx serupa-docs Kbd), so screen readers hear "Search, Control K".
- **Contrast:** group headings read 4.5:1 on the dialog in every theme (`KeyboardShortcuts.test.tsx`).
- **What's still yours:** don't take keys the browser or screen readers use (such as Ctrl+L, Ctrl+T, or a screen reader's single-letter keys in browse mode, which it handles before the page), and let people turn off single-key shortcuts (WCAG 2.1.4).

## useShortcut(keys, handler, options)

| Argument or option | Type | Default | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `keys` | `string \| string[]` | | The keys, pressed together, as Kbd takes them. |
| `handler` | `(event: KeyboardEvent) => void` | | Runs when they're pressed. |
| `description` | string | | Lists it in the dialog. |
| `group` | string | `"General"` | The heading it's listed under. |
| `enabled` | boolean | `true` | `false` turns it off for now. |
| `inInputs` | boolean | `false` | Also runs while typing in a text field. |

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | string | none | Goes to the `<dialog>`. |
| `title` | ReactNode | `"Keyboard shortcuts"` | The dialog's title. |
| `shortcuts` | `{ keys, description, group? }[]` | | Shortcuts to list that aren't set up with `useShortcut`. |
| `helpKeys` | `string[] \| false` | `["?"]` | The keys that open it; `false` for none. |
| `open` | boolean | | Controlled: whether it's open. |
| `defaultOpen` | boolean | `false` | Uncontrolled: open at first. |
| `onOpenChange` | `(open, details) => void` | | Called when it opens or closes. |

`className`, `ref` and other `<dialog>` attributes go to the [Dialog] (npx serupa-docs Dialog).

## Component tokens

Each is an optional override: set it on the page, a container or one KeyboardShortcuts. The list lives in `src/components/KeyboardShortcuts/keyboard-shortcuts.tokens.json` (also in `design-tokens/components/`).

<!-- token-table:start (made from keyboard-shortcuts.tokens.json by npm run tokens: edit the descriptions there) -->
| Token | Default | Use |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--keyboard-shortcuts-heading` | `text-muted` | A group's heading (4.5:1 on the dialog). |
| `--keyboard-shortcuts-divider` | `border` | The line between rows. |
| `--keyboard-shortcuts-row-padding` | `spacing-2` | Space above and below each row (8px). |
| `--keyboard-shortcuts-group-gap` | `spacing-5` | Space between groups (20px). |
| `--keyboard-shortcuts-heading-weight` | `font-semibold` | A group's heading. |
<!-- token-table:end -->

components.name: Lightbox
components.summary: A set of pictures shown full size, one at a time, over the page.
components.guide:
# Lightbox

A set of pictures shown full size, one at a time, over the page. People move through them with the arrows, the arrow keys or a swipe, and see where they are ("2 of 5"), so a gallery, a product's photos or the screenshots in a report can be looked at closely without leaving the page.

**Also called:** image viewer, media viewer, photo gallery viewer, slideshow.

```tsx
import { Image, Lightbox } from "@diki-stwn/serupa-ds";

const photos = [
  { src: "/photos/bromo.jpg", alt: "A hillside at dusk", caption: "Bromo, before sunrise", width: 1600, height: 1000 },
  { src: "/photos/lombok.jpg", alt: "The sea under a pale sky", width: 1600, height: 1000 },
];
const [open, setOpen] = React.useState(false);
const [index, setIndex] = React.useState(0);

{photos.map((p, i) => (
  <button key={p.src} type="button" aria-haspopup="dialog" onClick={() => { setIndex(i); setOpen(true); }}>
    <Image src={p.src} alt={p.alt} ratio="square" />
  </button>
))}
<Lightbox items={photos} open={open} onOpenChange={setOpen} index={index} onIndexChange={setIndex} />
```

## When to use

- A gallery or a set of photos people open to see each one large and move on to the next.
- A product's pictures, or the screenshots attached to a report or a ticket.

## When not to use

- One picture on its own: give the [Image] (npx serupa-docs Image) `viewable`, which opens it full size by itself.
- Pictures people should see together on the page, side by side, with no need to enlarge them: a [Carousel] (npx serupa-docs Carousel) or a grid of Images.
- Files that aren't pictures, such as PDFs: list them as [Attachment] (npx serupa-docs Attachment)s, each opening in its own viewer.

## Anatomy

Drawn from the `Default` story.

1. **Stage** (`.srp-lightbox__stage`): the picture, as large as the screen lets it be, with its own shape.
2. **Caption** (`.srp-lightbox__caption`): the picture's `caption`, under it.
3. **Arrows** (`.srp-lightbox__nav`): the previous and next buttons, with "2 of 4" between them.

## Usage

- Open it from the thumbnail people pressed, at that picture's `index`. Closing it puts focus back on the thumbnail.
- Write each picture's `alt` as you would for an [Image] (npx serupa-docs Image): it's the dialog's title while that picture shows, and what a screen reader says on each move. A file name ("IMG_2041.jpg") tells nobody anything.
- Pass `width` and `height` when you know them: the stage takes the picture's shape before it arrives, so nothing jumps.
- Pass the large version as `src`, and a small one to the thumbnails. The pictures on either side load ahead, so moving on is quick.
- `loop` suits a slideshow people go round; without it, the arrows stop at the ends, which says when the set is done. The arrow that reaches an end turns off, and focus moves to the other one.

### Do and don't

- **Do:** Name each picture by what it shows: "A hillside at dusk". It's the dialog's title, and what a screen reader says on each move. (`DoName`)
- **Don't:** Name pictures by their file ("IMG_final.jpg"), which tells nobody which one they're on. (`DontFileNames`)

## Behavior

- It's a [Dialog] (npx serupa-docs Dialog) (size lg): Escape, the × or a click on the backdrop close it, and focus comes back to where it was.
- A picture that fails to load shows a broken-image icon on its stage; the arrows still move on.
- A sideways swipe with a finger or a pen moves to the next or previous picture. A mouse drag doesn't, so the page can still be selected as usual.
- With one picture there are no arrows and no count.

## Accessibility

- **Role and name:** a modal dialog titled with the shown picture's `alt`, and described by "2 of 5". The picture itself has empty alt text, so it isn't read twice.
- **Keyboard:** see below. Focus starts on the × and stays in the dialog.
- **Moves are said:** each move says the new picture's alt text and where it is ("The sea under a pale sky, 2 of 4").
- **Contrast:** the caption and the count read 4.5:1 on the dialog in every theme (`Lightbox.test.tsx`).
- **What's still yours:** alt text that says what each picture shows, and the button that opens it.

### Keyboard

| Key | Does |
| --- | --- |
| Right arrow, Left arrow | The next or previous picture (the other way round in right-to-left text) |
| Home, End | The first or last picture |
| Escape | Closes it, and focus goes back to the button that opened it |

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `items` | `LightboxItem[]` | | `{ src, alt, caption?, width?, height? }`: the pictures, in order. |
| `open` | `boolean` | | Whether it's open (controlled). |
| `defaultOpen` | `boolean` | `false` | Whether it's open at first. |
| `onOpenChange` | `(open: boolean, details) => void` | | Asked to open or close: Escape, the × or the backdrop. |
| `index` | `number` | | The picture shown, from 0 (controlled). |
| `defaultIndex` | `number` | `0` | The picture shown at first. |
| `onIndexChange` | `(index: number) => void` | | Another picture was asked for: the arrows, the keys or a swipe. |
| `loop` | `boolean` | `false` | After the last picture comes the first again. |
| `id` | string | none | Goes to the `<dialog>`. |

`className`, `ref` and other props go to the `<dialog>`.

## Component tokens

Each is an optional override: set it on the page, a container or one Lightbox. The list lives in `src/components/Lightbox/lightbox.tokens.json` (also in `design-tokens/components/`).

<!-- token-table:start (made from lightbox.tokens.json by npm run tokens: edit the descriptions there) -->
| Token | Default | Use |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--lightbox-stage-bg` | `surface-muted` | The stage behind a picture while it loads, or if it fails. |
| `--lightbox-caption-color` | `text-muted` | The caption and the count (4.5:1 on the dialog). |
| `--lightbox-fallback-color` | `text-muted` | The broken-image icon when a picture fails. |
| `--lightbox-edge` | `picture-edge` | A faint line around the picture, so a white one stays apart from a white dialog. |
| `--lightbox-stage-radius` | `radius-surface` | The stage's corners (8px). |
| `--lightbox-fallback-icon` | `spacing-6` | The broken-image icon's size (24px). |
| `--lightbox-stage-max-height` | `spacing-40` | Space kept free above and below the stage: the title, the arrows and the screen's edges (160px). |
| `--lightbox-gap` | `spacing-3` | Space between the picture, its caption and the arrows (12px). |
<!-- token-table:end -->

components.name: Link
components.summary: An inline text link: underlined, in the primary color or the surrounding text's.
components.guide:
# Link

An inline text link: underlined, in the primary color or the surrounding text's. `external` opens a new tab and says so, and `as` renders your router's link so client-side navigation keeps working.

**Also called:** anchor, hyperlink.

```jsx
import { Link, Text } from '@diki-stwn/serupa-ds';

<Text>Read <Link href="/docs">the guide</Link> before you start.</Text>
<Link href="https://status.example.com" external>Status page</Link>
<Text size="sm" tone="muted">By signing up you agree to the <Link href="/terms" tone="neutral">terms</Link>.</Text>
<Link href="/pricing" underline="hover">Pricing</Link>

// With a router (React Router, Next.js…)
<Link as={RouterLink} to="/settings">Settings</Link>
```

## When to use

- Going to another page or place from inside a sentence.
- Lists of links where the place already says they're links: a nav bar, a footer, a list of related pages.
- Pointing to another site, with `external` so people know it opens a new tab.

## When not to use

- For an action that doesn't go anywhere, use a [Button] (npx serupa-docs Button) (`variant="link"` if it should look like a link).
- A call to action that should stand out, such as "Get started": use a [Button] (npx serupa-docs Button) with `href`.
- The trail of pages above the current one: use [Breadcrumb] (npx serupa-docs Breadcrumb).

## Anatomy

Drawn from the `External` story.

1. **Link** (`.srp-link`): the words that go somewhere.
2. **External icon** (`.srp-link__icon`): says it opens another site or a new tab, also in words for screen readers.

## Usage

- Keep the default underline in body text; use `underline="hover"` only where the place already says it's a link. Don't combine it with `tone="neutral"`: that link looks like plain text until it's hovered, so Link warns in the console.
- Use `tone="neutral"` in muted small print, such as terms under a form, so the link takes the text's color.
- With a router, register its link component once with `configure({ link })`, or pass it in `as`, so client-side navigation keeps working.
- A bare URL as the text is fine: it breaks across lines, even in a flex row or grid column, rather than push the layout wider.
- Check any `href` that comes from people, such as a profile's website: allow only `https:`, `http:`, `mailto:` or your own paths. React still renders a `javascript:` link, which runs code when clicked.

### Do and don't

- **Do:** Make the link's words say where it goes: "Read the refund policy". (`DoSayWhere`)
- **Don't:** Link "click here" or "more": out of its sentence, as in a screen reader's list of links, it says nothing. (`DontClickHere`)

## Accessibility

- Underlined by default, so a link in a sentence doesn't rely on color alone (WCAG 1.4.1). Use `underline="hover"` only where the place already says it's a link: a nav bar, a footer, a list of links. Color alone doesn't do it in a sentence: the primary color is only 3.1–3.4:1 against body text in the light themes and 1.8–2.6:1 in the dark ones, under the 3:1 that 1.4.1 asks of a link set apart by color.
- The primary color keeps 4.5:1 on `surface`, on hover too, and the focus ring 3:1, in every theme (`Link.test.tsx`).
- With `external`, screen readers hear "(opens in a new tab)" after the text, from the `opensInNewTab` label ("(terbuka di tab baru)" in `idLabels`). Link stays a Server Component: only that note is a small client component.
- The new-tab icon stays on the line of the last word: with a text label, the last word and the icon don't break apart, so the icon never starts a line by itself.
- Write link text that makes sense on its own ("Read the pricing guide", not "click here"): screen reader users often move from link to link.
- The keyboard focus ring follows the text when a link wraps onto two lines.
- `autoFocus` focuses the link once it mounts, also through `as` (React's own `autoFocus` works only on form controls). Use it sparingly, such as for the one way on from a confirmation page.

### Keyboard

| Key | Does |
| --- | --- |
| Tab | To the link |
| Enter | Follow it (Space scrolls the page, as on any link) |

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `tone` | `'primary'` \| `'neutral'` | `'primary'` | The primary color, or the surrounding text's color (still underlined) |
| `surface` | `'dark'` \| `'light'` | none | Over a photo or a colored panel: white for dark media, black for light, in every theme |
| `underline` | `'always'` \| `'hover'` | `'always'` | Always underlined, or only on hover and focus (a link in a paragraph stays underlined) |
| `external` | boolean | `false` | Opens a new tab (`target="_blank"`, adds `noopener noreferrer` to your `rel`), with a new-tab icon and "(opens in a new tab)" for screen readers. Your `target="_self"` (or `_parent`, `_top`) keeps it in the tab, without the icon or the note |
| `as` | a component | the `configure({ link })` link, else `'a'` | Your router's link component; it gets `className`, `ref` and every other prop. Set it once for the app with `configure({ link })`; `as` wins for one link. Typed: the props and `ref` are those of the element `as` names, so `as={RouterLink} to="/x"` checks `to`, and without `as` they're an `<a>`'s. A link set only with `configure({ link })` is typed as an `<a>`, so pass it `href`. |

`href`, `id`, `className`, `style`, `ref`, `target`, `rel` and everything else go to the element (an `<a>`, or what `as` names), which has `data-component="link"`. It has no font size of its own: it takes the text around it.

## Component tokens

Each is an optional override: set it on the page, a container or one link. The list lives in `src/components/Link/link.tokens.json` (also in `design-tokens/components/`).

<!-- token-table:start (made from link.tokens.json by npm run tokens: edit the descriptions there) -->
| Token | Default | Use |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--link-text` | `primary-text` | tone="primary" text and underline (4.5:1 on surface). |
| `--link-text-hover` | `primary-text-hover` | tone="primary" on hover. |
| `--link-focus-ring` | `focus-ring` | The keyboard focus ring. |
| `--link-on-dark` | `white` | surface="dark": the link, its hover and its focus ring over dark media. |
| `--link-on-light` | `black` | surface="light": the link, its hover and its focus ring over light media. |
| `--link-thickness` | `decoration-1` | The underline's thickness (1px). |
| `--link-thickness-hover` | `decoration-2` | The underline's thickness on hover (2px). |
| `--link-offset` | `underline-offset-2` | The gap between the text and the underline (2px). |
| `--link-icon-gap` | `spacing-0.5` | Space before the new-tab icon of an external link (2px). |
| `--link-focus-radius` | `radius-inner` | The focus ring's corners (4px). |
<!-- token-table:end -->

components.name: List
components.summary: Rows of related things: people, files, notifications, settings.
components.guide:
# List

Rows of related things: people, files, notifications, settings. Each row has a title, an optional muted description, something before it (an Avatar or an icon) and something after it (a date, a Badge, an action). A row can be a link or a button; trailing actions stay outside it, so controls are never nested. A press anywhere on the row works, trailing meta ("3 days ago") included, except on a trailing action, which keeps its own press.

**Also called:** list view, item list, virtualized list.

```jsx
import { List, ListItem, Avatar, Badge, IconButton } from '@diki-stwn/serupa-ds';

<List variant="card" aria-label="Members">
  {people.map((p) => (
    <ListItem key={p.id} href={`/people/${p.id}`}
      leading={<Avatar name={p.name} src={p.photo} alt="" size="sm" />}
      title={p.name} description={p.email}
      trailing={<IconButton icon="more_horiz" label={`More for ${p.name}`} />} />
  ))}
</List>

<List>
  <ListItem leading="description" title="Report.pdf" description="2 MB" trailing="Yesterday" />
  <ListItem leading="settings" title="Open settings" onClick={openSettings} />
</List>
```

## When to use

- A set of similar things people scan and pick from: people, files, notifications, settings.
- Rows that each open something or do one thing, with an action of their own at the end.
- A list beside a detail view, where the selected row shows what's open.
- Hundreds or thousands of rows people scroll through, with `ListVirtualItems` inside (see Thousands of rows): members, files, events, log lines.

## When not to use

- Data with several columns to compare or sort: use [Table] (npx serupa-docs Table) instead.
- Items with pictures or a lot of content each: use [Card] (npx serupa-docs Card)s in a [Grid] (npx serupa-docs Grid).
- Actions behind a button: use [Menu] (npx serupa-docs Menu) instead.
- An app's main navigation: use [Sidebar] (npx serupa-docs Sidebar) instead.

## Anatomy

Drawn from the `Settings` story.

1. **Item** (`.srp-list__item`): one row.
2. **Leading** (`.srp-list__leading`): an optional icon, avatar or image before the text.
3. **Title** (`.srp-list__title`): the row's main line.
4. **Description** (`.srp-list__description`): a second line with more detail.
5. **Trailing** (`.srp-list__trailing`): an optional value, badge, switch or action at the end.

## Usage

- Put actions in `trailing`, never inside the row's link or button, and name them for their row ("More for Ada Lovelace").
- Use `as="ol"` when the order matters.
- Use `divided="inset"` when every row leads with an avatar or icon: the lines start at the text, so the pictures read as one column.
- Use `variant="card"` for a list that stands on its own; inside a Card or a panel that already has a frame, keep it `plain`.
- With a router, pass its link component as `as` and its props (such as `to`) in `linkProps`.

### Picking rows

Set `selectionMode="multiple"` when people pick rows to act on several at once: files to move, messages to archive, members to remove. Give each `ListItem` a `value`, keep the picked values in state, and put a `ListSelectAll` and the actions (TableActionBar's pattern) above the list.

```tsx
const [picked, setPicked] = React.useState<string[]>([]);
<ListSelectAll values={files.map((f) => f.id)} selected={picked} onSelectedChange={setPicked} />
<List aria-label="Files" selectionMode="multiple" selected={picked} onSelectedChange={setPicked}>
  {files.map((f) => <ListItem key={f.id} value={f.id} title={f.name} description={f.size} trailing={<IconButton icon="more_vert" label={`More for ${f.name}`} />} />)}
</List>
```

- Each row gets a checkbox named by its title. A press on the row picks it, and Shift with a press picks the run from the last one picked. A row with `href` or `onClick` keeps its link or button: only its checkbox picks it.
- `selectionMode="single"` picks one row at a time, with no checkboxes: a picked row is shaded (with a bar at its start when more contrast is asked for).
- A `disabled` row can't be picked. Leave it out of `ListSelectAll`'s `values`.

### Loading, empty and failed

- **Loading:** set `loading` on the List and put a `ListLoadingItems` inside it, with `rows` set to about as many as will come and with the shape the rows will have: `description` when they have a second line, and `leading` set to `'icon'` or to the Avatar's size (`'sm'`, `'md'` and so on). Each placeholder is as tall as the real row, so nothing jumps when the data arrives. Name the wait in `label` ("Loading members"): a screen reader hears it once, after the loader's delay, so a quick load says nothing.
- **Empty:** in place of the List, an `EmptyState` that says what's missing and offers the action that adds the first one.
- **Failed:** in place of the List, a danger `Alert` that says what didn't load and offers Retry in `actions`. It's `role="alert"`, so the failure is heard as it appears. On Retry, go back to loading.

```tsx
{state === 'failed' ? <Alert tone="danger" actions={<Button size="sm" onClick={load}>Retry</Button>}>Members didn't load.</Alert>
  : state === 'loaded' && !members.length ? <EmptyState size="sm" title="No members yet" />
  : <List aria-label="Members" loading={state === 'loading'}>
      {state === 'loading' ? <ListLoadingItems rows={4} showDescription leading="sm" label="Loading members" />
        : members.map((m) => <ListItem key={m.id} title={m.name} description={m.email} leading={<Avatar name={m.name} size="sm" />} />)}
    </List>}
```

### Thousands of rows

Put a `ListVirtualItems` inside the List in place of its rows, and the List draws only the rows in view, so ten thousand people, files or log lines scroll as smoothly as ten. The rows are ListItems and look the same.

```tsx
<List variant="card" aria-label="Members">
  <ListVirtualItems count={people.length} itemKey={(i) => people[i].id}
    renderItem={(i) => <ListItem title={people[i].name} description={people[i].email} />} />
</List>
```

- The List then scrolls inside itself, 384px tall at most (`--list-virtual-height`). Set the token, or a `style` height, to fill a panel.
- Give the List an `aria-label` (or `aria-labelledby` pointing at a heading): it's a scrolling region people can Tab to. It takes focus while it has rows and scrolls with the arrows, Page Up, Page Down, Home and End.
- Pass `itemKey` when rows can be added, removed or reordered, so each row keeps its element.
- Set `estimatedItemHeight` near a typical row's height (56px fits a row with a description). Rows are measured once drawn, so rows of different heights are fine; the guess only sets the scroll range until the first rows are seen.
- Rows can be links or buttons. Tab moves through the rows that are drawn, and the row with focus stays drawn while it's scrolled away, so focus is never lost.
- Each drawn row has `aria-posinset` and `aria-setsize`, so screen readers say "5,001 of 10,000" though only a few rows are in the page.
- Rows not drawn aren't in the page: the browser's find (Ctrl+F) and printing don't see them. Offer a search or filter, and keep a plain List for up to a couple of hundred rows.
- While the first rows load, use `loading` and `ListLoadingItems` as above, in the same List: each placeholder is as tall as the row that replaces it.

It draws the rows in view and 4 more on each side (`overscan`); an empty `<li>` above and below them stands in for the rest, so the scrollbar is the right size. Rows not measured yet count as the average height of those seen, and when a row above the view turns out taller or shorter, the row at the top of the view stays where it is. Past 15 million px of rows (about 270,000 rows of 56px), the scroll range stays at 15 million and is scaled, under every browser's height limit, so every row, the last included, can be reached: the scrollbar moves through the rows faster than one pixel per pixel, while the keys and the wheel still move row by row. On the server it draws the first 20 rows.

### Do and don't

- **Do:** Keep the title short, and put the detail in `description` and the status in `trailing`. (`DoTitleAndDetail`)
- **Don't:** Write everything into the title: it wraps, and people can't scan down the names. (`DontCrammedTitle`)

## Accessibility

- It's a real list, so screen readers say how many rows there are, Safari's VoiceOver included (`role="list"` keeps the role it would drop from a list without bullets). Name it with `aria-label` when there's no heading over it.
- A whole row is one link or button, named by its title and description; trailing actions are separate controls, so give them names that say which row they're for ("More for Ada Lovelace").
- An Avatar beside a written name repeats it, so give it `alt=""`, as in the example above. Otherwise every row reads the name twice ("Ada Lovelace Ada Lovelace ada@example.com"). An icon beside a title that says the same is decorative too.
- Selected rows have a bar and `aria-current` or `aria-pressed`, not only a background.
- Titles and descriptions keep 4.5:1 on plain and shaded rows, and the selected bar 3:1, in every theme (`List.test.tsx`).
- **Keyboard:** an item with `href` or `onClick` has one Tab stop, its main area, where Enter (Space too for a button) acts. A disabled one is skipped. Controls in `trailing` are Tab stops of their own. Plain items add none.
- **With `selectionMode`:** the list is a grid (`role="grid"`, `aria-multiselectable` when multiple) of rows named by their titles, with `aria-selected`. It's one Tab stop: Up and Down move between rows, Home and End go to the ends, Right and Left reach the row's checkbox, link and actions. Space picks the focused row, Shift with Up or Down picks as it moves, Ctrl or Cmd+A picks every row, and Enter follows the row's link or presses its button. A picked row has a checked box and the primary bar, not only a background.

### Keyboard

| Key | Does |
| --- | --- |
| Tab | A link or button row's main area, then its trailing controls. With `selectionMode`, the list is one Tab stop, on the last row focused |
| Enter | Follows the row's link or presses its button; with `selectionMode`, picks a row that has neither |
| Space | Presses a button row; with `selectionMode`, picks or clears the focused row (with Shift, the run from the last one picked) |
| Down / Up | With `selectionMode`: the next or previous row (with Shift, picking as it moves) |
| Home / End | With `selectionMode`: the first or last row |
| Right / Left | With `selectionMode`: into the row, through its checkbox, link and actions, and back to the row |
| Ctrl+A / Cmd+A | With `selectionMode="multiple"`: picks every row that isn't disabled |

## Props

### List

| Prop | Type | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | string | none | Goes to the root `<ul>` or `<ol>`. |
| `variant` | `'plain'` \| `'card'` | `'plain'` | Bare rows, or rows in a bordered, rounded frame |
| `divided` | boolean \| `'inset'` | `true` | Lines between rows; `'inset'` starts each line where the text starts, after the avatar or icon, so a list of people reads as one group per row |
| `as` | `'ul'` \| `'ol'` | `'ul'` | `ol` when the order matters |
| `loading` | boolean | `false` | Its rows are loading: sets `aria-busy` on the list. Pair it with `ListLoadingItems` |
| `selectionMode` | `'none'` \| `'single'` \| `'multiple'` | `'none'` | Rows people pick: a grid with one Tab stop, and a checkbox per row when multiple |
| `selected` / `defaultSelected` | string[] | | The picked rows' values |
| `onSelectedChange` | `(values) => void` | | Called with the picked rows' values |

`className`, `style`, `ref`, `aria-label` and everything else go to the list, which has `data-component="list"`.

### ListItem

| Prop | Type | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `title` | node | required | The main line |
| `description` | node | none | A second, muted line |
| `leading` | an icon name or node | none | Before the text: a 20px muted icon, an Avatar, an image |
| `trailing` | node | none | After the text, outside any link or button |
| `href` | string | none | Makes the main area a link |
| `onClick` | function | none | Makes the main area a button (without `href`) |
| `as` | a component | the `configure({ link })` link, else `'a'` | Your router's link component; its props (such as `to`) go in `linkProps`. Set it once for the app with `configure({ link })`; `as` wins for one link. |
| `linkProps` | object | none | Extra props for the link or button |
| `selected` | boolean | `false` | Shaded (with a bar at its start when more contrast is asked for); `aria-current="true"` on a link (an `aria-current` in `linkProps`, such as `"page"` for the current page of a nav list, wins), `aria-pressed` on a button |
| `disabled` | boolean | `false` | Draws a link or button row in `disabled-text` and stops it; with `selectionMode`, it can't be picked |
| `value` | string | | With `selectionMode`: what `onSelectedChange` reports for this row |

`className`, `ref` and everything else go to the `<li>`.

### ListSelectAll

The "Select all" box over a List with `selectionMode="multiple"`: checked when every row is picked, a dash (said as mixed) when some are. Picks outside `values` are kept.

| Prop | Type | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `values` | string[] | required | The values of the rows it picks: the enabled ones |
| `selected` | string[] | required | The List's picked values |
| `onSelectedChange` | `(values) => void` | required | Called with every value, or none of them |
| `children` | node | `"Select all"` | Its label |

Every other prop goes to the Checkbox.

### ListLoadingItems
