components.name: LoadMore
components.summary: The end of a list that loads in pages: "Showing 20 of 134" over a Load more button, or infinite scroll, and an announcement of what each load added.
components.guide:
# LoadMore

The end of a list that loads in pages: "Showing 20 of 134" over a Load more button, or infinite scroll, and an announcement of what each load added. People keep their place in a long list, and screen reader users hear that new items arrived.

**Also called:** load more button, more results button.

```tsx
import { LoadMore } from "@diki-stwn/serupa-ds";

<LoadMore onLoadMore={loadNextPage} count={items.length} total={total} hasMore={items.length < total} />
```

## When to use

- A feed, a search result list or a history where people mostly read the newest items and sometimes want more.
- With `infinite`, a feed people scroll through, where pressing a button each page would get in the way.

## When not to use

- A table or a list people come back to at a given place, compare across pages, or link to: use [Pagination] (npx serupa-docs Pagination), so each page has an address.
- A list whose end matters, such as a footer below it: infinite scroll keeps pushing that end away. Use the button.

## Anatomy

Drawn from the `LongText` story.

1. **Summary** (`.srp-load-more__summary`): how many are shown of how many there are.
2. **Load more** (`.srp-load-more__button`): adds the next page of items below the ones shown.

## Usage

- Pass `count` (how many are shown) and `total` when you know it, so people see "Showing 20 of 134" and hear "20 more loaded. Showing 40 of 134."
- Return the fetch's promise from `onLoadMore`: the button shows loading and takes no second press until it settles. Or set `loading` from your own fetch state. A rejected promise just ends the loading state: show the error yourself (an [Alert] (npx serupa-docs Alert) above the button, say), since LoadMore says nothing about it.
- Set `hasMore={false}` after the last page. The button gives way to "You've reached the end" (`endText`, or `null` for nothing). If the button had focus, focus moves to that text, or with `null` to the "Showing 30 of 30" line (with no line either, to LoadMore itself, which is not a Tab stop), so it isn't lost.
- Put it right after the list, inside the same region, so new items appear just above it.

### Do and don't

- **Do:** Pass `count` and `total` when you know them, so people see "Showing 20 of 134". (`Default`)
- **Don't:** Leave them out when you know them: people can't tell how far they are through. (`WithoutTotal`)

## Accessibility

- **Role and name:** a plain group with a native `<button>` named "Load more" (or `label`). A long `label` wraps onto more lines on a phone instead of being cut off. The summary and end text are plain text.
- **Announcements:** when `count` grows, the number added is said politely through the shared live region ("20 more loaded. Showing 40 of 134."). Without `count`, "More loaded" is said once a promise from `onLoadMore` settles. The button's own "Loading" isn't said, so a load is one message.
- **Focus:** focus stays on the button, which moves down below the new items, so the next Tab goes on from there. Once the load lands, the button is scrolled back into view (only as far as needed), so keyboard users see where they are rather than pressing again off screen. When the last page leaves no button, focus goes to the end text instead of falling back to the page.
- **Infinite scroll:** it loads when the button comes within 200px of the viewport, once per approach, and again only after `count` changes, so a load that adds nothing doesn't repeat. The button stays for keyboard and screen reader users, who don't scroll to load, and as the fallback where IntersectionObserver is missing.
- **Contrast:** the summary and end text read 4.5:1 on the page in every theme (`LoadMore.test.tsx`).
- **What's still yours:** keep loaded items when people go back to the list, and tell people when a load fails (an [Alert] (npx serupa-docs Alert) with a retry).

### Keyboard

| Key | Does |
| --- | --- |
| Tab | To the Load more button |
| Enter | Loads the next page. Focus stays on the button, or moves to the end text after the last page |

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | string | none | Goes to the root `<div>`. |
| `onLoadMore` | `() => void \| PromiseLike` | | Required. Loads the next page; return a promise for loading and one press at a time. |
| `hasMore` | boolean | `true` | `false` once there's nothing more. |
| `loading` | boolean | `false` | Loading from your own fetch state. |
| `count` | number | | How many items are shown; when it grows, what was added is announced. |
| `total` | number | | How many in all, for "Showing 20 of 134". |
| `infinite` | boolean | `false` | Loads as it nears the viewport; the button stays. |
| `label` | `ReactNode` | `"Load more"` | The button's text. |
| `endText` | `ReactNode` | `"You've reached the end"` | Shown once `hasMore` is false; `null` shows nothing. |

The words are the labels `loadMore`, `showingOf`, `loadedMore`, `moreLoaded` and `allLoaded`; change them with `<SerupaProvider labels>`. `className`, `ref` and other props go to the `<div>`.

## Component tokens

Each is an optional override: set it on the page, a container or one LoadMore. The list lives in `src/components/LoadMore/load-more.tokens.json` (also in `design-tokens/components/`).

<!-- token-table:start (made from load-more.tokens.json by npm run tokens: edit the descriptions there) -->
| Token | Default | Use |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--load-more-text` | `text-muted` | "Showing 20 of 134" and the end text (4.5:1 on the page). |
| `--load-more-gap` | `spacing-3` | Space between the summary and the button (12px). |
| `--load-more-padding` | `spacing-4` | Space above and below (16px). |
<!-- token-table:end -->

components.name: Loader
components.summary: Shows that something is loading when you can't say how far along it is.
components.guide: # Loader Shows that something is loading when you can't say how far along it is. Three looks: a **ring** (a quarter arc turning on a faint track), **dots** (three pulsing dots) and **text** (words with a shine sweeping through them). For placeholder shapes where the content will be, use [Skeleton] (npx serupa-docs Skeleton). **Also called:** spinner, loading indicator. ```jsx import { Loader } from '@diki-stwn/serupa-ds'; // ring, 24px, text color, "Loading…" // a page or an empty area that is loading // softer: chat replies, inline waits // words with a shine // white, on a dark scrim or a photo // next to text that already says it: decorative Loading projects… ``` ## When to use - Content or a result is on its way and you can't tell how long it will take: a list loading, a search running. - A reply or an AI task is being prepared and people should see that work is going on. ## When not to use - Waits you can measure (uploads, imports): use [Progress] (npx serupa-docs Progress) instead; a progress bar tells people how long it will take. - The layout of what's coming is known: use [Skeleton] (npx serupa-docs Skeleton), which holds its place while it loads. - A button whose action is running: use `

components.name: Logo
components.summary: The product's logo at a set height, with a version for dark themes and a small mark for narrow screens.
components.guide: # Logo The product's logo at a set height, with a version for dark themes and a small mark for narrow screens. The browser fetches only the version it shows. **Also called:** brand mark, logotype. ```tsx import { Logo } from "@diki-stwn/serupa-ds"; ``` ## When to use - The brand at the start of a [Navbar] (npx serupa-docs Navbar) or [Sidebar] (npx serupa-docs Sidebar), on a sign-in page, or in a footer. - Where the logo must follow the theme: a dark version in dark themes, without code that reads the theme. ## When not to use - A picture of content, such as a photo or a chart: use [Image] (npx serupa-docs Image), which keeps a frame, a placeholder and a fallback. - A person or a team: use [Avatar] (npx serupa-docs Avatar). - A brand that is only text: put the name in the link, styled as you like. ## Anatomy Drawn from the `Default` story. 1. **Picture** (`.srp-logo__picture`): with a dark version or a mark, a `` that offers them to the browser ahead of the full logo. It takes no room of its own. 2. **Logo** (`.srp-logo`): the ``, at the size's height, named by `alt`. ## Usage - Give it the full logo (`src`) drawn for a light background, and, where it can be shown on dark, `darkSrc`. A theme with no dark version shows `src` as is, so pick one that reads on both if you have only one. - `markSrc` (and `markDarkSrc`) is the small square symbol. `variant="mark"` always shows it; `variant="auto"` shows it below `collapseBelow` (768px by default, where Navbar folds its links) and the full logo from there up. - `size` sets the height (24, 32 or 40px); the width follows the picture's shape. SVG files keep it sharp at every size. - It isn't a link. Put it in the app's link home (a router link, or ``), name the link ("Acme home") and pass `alt=""`, so a screen reader doesn't read the name twice. ### Do and don't - **Do:** Give it `darkSrc` (and `markDarkSrc`) wherever it can show on dark. (`Default`) - **Don't:** Ship only the light logo: in a dark theme it's dark on dark. (`LightOnly`) ## Accessibility - **Role and name:** an `img` named by `alt`, the brand's name. With `alt=""` inside a named link, it's left out and the link carries the name. - **Keyboard:** none of its own: it isn't focusable. The link it sits in takes focus and shows its ring. - **Contrast:** the logo's own colors are the picture's. A dark version for dark themes keeps it readable there (WCAG 1.4.11 asks 3:1 for the parts needed to recognise it, though logotypes are exempt from 1.4.3). - **What's still yours:** `alt`, the link's name, and versions that read on light and dark backgrounds. ## Props | Prop | Type | Default | Notes | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `src` | `string` | | The full logo, for a light background. | | `alt` | `string` | | The brand's name; `""` inside a named link. | | `darkSrc` | `string` | | The full logo for a dark background, shown in a dark theme (or when the screen prefers dark, where the theme follows it). | | `markSrc` | `string` | | The small mark alone, for narrow spaces. | | `markDarkSrc` | `string` | | The small mark for a dark background. | | `variant` | `'full' \| 'mark' \| 'auto'` | `'full'` | `auto` shows the mark below `collapseBelow`. Without `markSrc`, always the full logo. | | `collapseBelow` | `'sm' \| 'md' \| 'lg'` | `'md'` | With `auto`: below 640, 768 or 1024px the mark shows. | | `size` | `'sm' \| 'md' \| 'lg'` | `'md'` | The height: 24, 32 or 40px. | `className`, `id`, `ref` and other props (`width`, `height`, `loading`, `fetchPriority`) go to the ``. ## Component tokens Each is an optional override: set it on the page, a container or one Logo. The list lives in `src/components/Logo/logo.tokens.json` (also in `design-tokens/components/`). | Token | Default | Use | | --- | --- | --- | | `--logo-height-sm` | `spacing-6` | Its height at size sm (24px): a compact bar or a footer. | | `--logo-height-md` | `spacing-8` | Its height at size md (32px), the default: a Navbar or Sidebar. | | `--logo-height-lg` | `spacing-10` | Its height at size lg (40px): a sign-in page or a splash. |

components.name: MaskedValue
components.summary: Shows a sensitive value with most of it hidden behind bullets, keeping just enough for its owner to recognize it: "•••• 1208" for a card, "a••••" for an email.
components.guide:
# MaskedValue

Shows a sensitive value with most of it hidden behind bullets, keeping just enough for its owner to recognize it: "•••• 1208" for a card, "a••••" for an email. Screen readers hear what it is and the part kept ("Card number ending in 1208"), never a row of bullets. With `revealable`, a Show button lets the owner see the whole value until they leave the page.

**Also called:** masked text, redacted value, obfuscated value.

```tsx
import { MaskedValue, maskValue } from "@diki-stwn/serupa-ds";

<MaskedValue value={card.number} label="Card number" />                      // •••• 1208
<MaskedValue value={user.phone} label="Phone" end={3} />                     // •••• 402
<MaskedValue value={key.secret} label="API key" start={8} end={0} revealable />  // a Show button, then sk_live_••••

maskValue("4111111111111208")   // "•••• 1208", the same text outside React
```

## When to use

- A value a passer-by, a screenshot or a shared screen shouldn't show, but its owner needs to tell apart from others: a card or account number, a phone number or email on a profile, a national id, a key or a token.
- An amount people chose to hide, such as a balance on a shared screen: `end={0}` and `revealable`.

## When not to use

- A value someone types: use [PasswordInput] (npx serupa-docs PasswordInput), or an [Input] (npx serupa-docs Input) with `type="password"`.
- A value the reader isn't allowed to see at all. Mask it on the server and send only the end: masking in the browser only hides it from people looking at the screen.
- A key someone needs to copy once, right after making it: show it whole with a [CopyButton] (npx serupa-docs CopyButton), and say it won't be shown again.

## Anatomy

Drawn from the `Revealable` story.

1. **Show button** (`.srp-masked-value__toggle`): with `revealable`, an IconButton before the value that shows and hides it. It comes first so it stays put as the value appears.
2. **Value** (`.srp-masked-value__text`): the kept characters after four bullets, or the whole value once shown. Hidden from screen readers while masked.

## Usage

- Keep the least that lets the owner recognize it: the last four of a card or an id, the last three or four of a phone, the first letter of an email, a key's prefix. The Data formats page lists them.
- The bullets are always four, whatever the length, so they don't give away how long the value is. Asking to keep more than half keeps nothing.
- `label` is what the value is, as a noun: "Card number", "Phone". Screen readers hear it with the end kept, and the Show button is named after it.
- Offer `revealable` only to the person the value belongs to. It hides again when they switch tabs or put the app in the background.
- Control it with `revealed` and `onRevealedChange` to ask for a password before showing, or to log who looked.

### Do and don't

- **Do:** Keep the end the owner knows it by, such as a card's last four. (`Default`)
- **Don't:** Hide it all: with nothing kept, nobody can tell which card it is. (`DontHideAll`)

## Accessibility

- **Role and name:** inline text. While masked, the bullets are hidden from screen readers (`aria-hidden`), and a hidden text says what it is and the end kept, from the `maskedEnding` and `maskedHidden` labels: "Card number ending in 1208", "Balance, hidden". Shown, the value is plain text.
- **Keyboard:** with `revealable`, the Show button is a toggle button (`aria-pressed`) in the tab order, named by the `showValue` label ("Show Card number"). Its name stays the same whichever way it's pressed; its icon changes. Focus stays on it.
- **Contrast:** it takes the text color around it. The Show button is an IconButton, with its contrast and its 44px target on touch screens.
- **What's still yours:** the words for `label`, in the reader's language; asking again before showing something very sensitive; masking on the server what the reader may not see at all.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `value` | string | required | The whole value. Only the characters kept are in the page until it's shown |
| `label` | string | required | What it is, as a noun ("Card number"): read with the end kept, and names the Show button |
| `end` | number | `4` | Characters kept at the end. `0` hides it all |
| `start` | number | `0` | Characters kept at the start, such as an email's first letter or a key's prefix |
| `revealable` | boolean | `false` | A Show button before it (`aria-pressed`); the value hides again when the page is left |
| `revealed` | boolean | | Whether the whole value shows (controlled), with `revealable` |
| `defaultRevealed` | boolean | `false` | Whether the whole value shows at first (uncontrolled), with `revealable` |
| `onRevealedChange` | (revealed) => void | | Called when Show is pressed, or the value hides because the page was left |
| `id` | string | none | Goes to the root `<span>`. |

`className`, `ref` and other props go to the `<span>`. `maskValue(value, start?, end?)` gives the masked text outside React, counting characters as people see them.

## Component tokens

Each is an optional override: set it on the page, a container or one MaskedValue. The list lives in `src/components/MaskedValue/masked-value.tokens.json` (also in `design-tokens/components/`).

<!-- token-table:start (made from masked-value.tokens.json by npm run tokens: edit the descriptions there) -->
| Token | Default | Use |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--masked-value-gap` | `spacing-1` | Between the value and the Show button (4px). |
<!-- token-table:end -->

components.name: MentionInput
components.summary: A multi-line text field where typing "@" opens a list of people to mention, at the caret.
components.guide:
# MentionInput

A multi-line text field where typing "@" opens a list of people to mention, at the caret. Picking one writes "@Name" into the text, so a comment, a reply or a note can bring someone in, and the app can notify them.

**Also called:** mentions, @-mentions, user tagging.

```tsx
import { MentionInput, mentionsIn } from "@diki-stwn/serupa-ds";

const people = [{ id: "ayu", label: "Ayu Lestari", description: "Design lead" }, { id: "budi", label: "Budi Santoso" }];
const [text, setText] = React.useState("");
<Field label="Comment" hint="Type @ to mention someone.">
  <MentionInput options={people} value={text} onValueChange={setText} autoResize maxRows={8} />
</Field>

// on Send: who to notify
const notify = mentionsIn(text, people).map((p) => p.id);

// a large directory: load the matches as people type, and show them as given
<MentionInput aria-label="Reply" options={matches} filter={false} onSearch={(q) => { if (q != null) search(q); }} />
```

## When to use

- A comment, a reply, a chat message or a note where people bring someone in by name.
- Any text where a few known names or things are referred to inline, such as `#` for a channel (`trigger="#"`).

## When not to use

- Picking people as the field's value, such as assignees or reviewers: use [Combobox] (npx serupa-docs Combobox) `multiple`, which shows each one as a tag.
- A single line of text: use [Input] (npx serupa-docs Input), or Combobox `freeText` for suggestions.

## Anatomy

Drawn from the `Default` story.

1. **Field** (`.srp-textarea`): a [Textarea] (npx serupa-docs Textarea), with every prop it takes.
2. **List** (`.srp-mention-input__popup`): the people who match, under the line the caret is on. Each option shows an [Avatar] (npx serupa-docs Avatar), the name and its `description` line.

## Usage

- Say how it works under the field ("Type @ to mention someone."), in the Field's hint or the placeholder. Nothing else shows that "@" does something.
- The text stays plain: a mention is "@" and the label, as people see it. Use `mentionsIn(text, options)` when the text is sent, to find who to notify: at each "@" it takes the longest whole name written there, so "@Ayu Lestari" is Ayu Lestari and not also an "Ayu". Labels should be unique, such as a full name, so a mention points to one person.
- "@" counts only at the start of the text or after a space or an opening bracket, so an email address doesn't open the list. A space right before the caret closes it, and a space inside a name doesn't ("@Ayu L" still matches).
- `filter` (on by default) keeps the options whose label holds what's typed, ignoring case and accents, with names that start with it first. For a large directory, pass `filter={false}`, load matches in `onSearch`, and pass them as `options`.
- `description` tells people with the same first name apart (a role or a team). Mark someone who can't be mentioned here `disabled`, and say why in their description ("Can't see this project").
- Use `value` with `onValueChange`, which picking a mention also calls. `onChange` gets the textarea's own events, but a mention put in isn't one.
- It takes `name` and goes into a form like a Textarea: it submits its text and puts `defaultValue` back on reset.

### Do and don't

- **Do:** Say how to mention, in the hint: "Type @ to mention someone." (`DoSayHow`)
- **Don't:** Leave the field with no word that @ does anything. (`DontHide`)

## Accessibility

- **Role and name:** a `<textarea>` (a textbox), named by its Field or `aria-label`. It has `aria-autocomplete="list"`, and while the list is open, `aria-controls` names the listbox and `aria-activedescendant` the highlighted option. (A textarea can't take `role="combobox"`, so it stays a textbox.) The listbox is named by the same label.
- **Said:** how many match ("3 results", or "No results") is said politely after typing pauses, as in Combobox (4.1.3).
- **Keyboard:** see below. Focus never leaves the field, so typing goes on after a pick, with the caret after the name and its space.
- **Contrast:** options and their second line read 4.5:1 on the list, the highlighted one too, in every theme (`MentionInput.test.tsx`).
- **What's still yours:** the hint that says how to mention, unique labels, and notifying the people `mentionsIn` returns.

### Keyboard

| Key | While the list is open |
| --- | --- |
| Down arrow, Up arrow | Highlight the next or previous person, past those who can't be picked, wrapping at the ends |
| Enter, Tab | Put the highlighted person in |
| Escape | Close the list for this mention; the next "@" opens it again. A dialog the field is in stays open |
| Shift+Tab | Leave the field, and the list closes (as a click outside it does) |

Every other key types. Nothing is taken while an input method is composing a character.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | string | none | Goes to the native `<textarea>` (not the wrapper), so a `<label htmlFor>` or a Field can point at it. |
| `options` | `MentionOption[]` | | `{ id, label, description?, avatar?, disabled? }`: who can be mentioned. |
| `value` | `string` | | The text (controlled). |
| `defaultValue` | `string` | `''` | The text at first. |
| `onValueChange` | `(value: string) => void` | | Every change, typing or a mention put in. |
| `onSearch` | `(query: string \| null) => void` | | What's typed after "@" while the list is open, then `null`. |
| `onMention` | `(option: MentionOption) => void` | | A mention was put in. |
| `triggerChar` | `string` | `'@'` | The character that starts a mention. |
| `filter` | `boolean` | `true` | Narrows `options` to what's typed. Off when you filter. |
| `maxOptions` | `number` | `8` | The most options shown. |

Every [Textarea] (npx serupa-docs Textarea) prop works too (`size`, `rows`, `autoResize`, `maxRows`, `showCount`, `actions`, `invalid`, `name`…). `ref` and other props go to the `<textarea>`; `className` and `style` go to the wrapper. `mentionQuery(text, caret, trigger?)` is exported too: the open mention at a caret, or `null`.

## Component tokens

Each is an optional override: set it on the page, a container or one MentionInput. The list lives in `src/components/MentionInput/mention-input.tokens.json` (also in `design-tokens/components/`).

components.name: Menu
components.summary: A list of actions behind a button: a row's "More" menu, an "Actions" dropdown, a user menu.
components.guide:
# Menu

A list of actions behind a button: a row's "More" menu, an "Actions" dropdown, a user menu. It follows the WAI-ARIA menu button pattern and opens next to its button in the browser's top layer.

**Also called:** dropdown menu, action menu, overflow menu.

```jsx
import { Menu, ContextMenu, MenuItem, MenuGroup, MenuSeparator, Button, IconButton, Card } from '@diki-stwn/serupa-ds';

<Menu trigger={<Button variant="secondary" endIcon="expand_more">Actions</Button>}>
  <MenuItem icon="edit" shortcut={['mod', 'E']} onSelect={edit}>Edit</MenuItem>
  <MenuItem icon="content_copy" onSelect={duplicate}>Duplicate</MenuItem>
  <MenuItem href="/share" icon="link">Share link</MenuItem>
  <MenuSeparator />
  <MenuGroup label="Danger zone">
    <MenuItem icon="delete" destructive onSelect={remove}>Delete</MenuItem>
  </MenuGroup>
</Menu>

<Menu trigger={<IconButton icon="more_vert" label="Row actions" />} placement="bottom-end">…</Menu>

<Menu trigger={<Button variant="secondary">File</Button>}>
  <MenuItem icon="add">New</MenuItem>
  <MenuSub icon="share" label="Share">
    <MenuItem icon="mail">Email</MenuItem>
    <MenuItem icon="link">Copy link</MenuItem>
  </MenuSub>
</Menu>

// a right-click (or Shift+F10) menu on an area
<ContextMenu aria-label="File actions" target={<Card tabIndex={0}>Report.pdf</Card>}>
  <MenuItem icon="open_in_new" onSelect={open}>Open</MenuItem>
  <MenuItem icon="edit" onSelect={rename}>Rename</MenuItem>
</ContextMenu>
```

`ContextMenu` is the same menu opened from an area instead of a button: at the pointer on a right-click (or a long press on touch), or at the focused element on Shift+F10 or the Menu key.

## When to use

- A set of actions on one item that would crowd the page as buttons, such as a table row's "More" menu.
- Grouping related actions behind one "Actions" button in a toolbar.
- A user or account menu with a few actions and links.
- `ContextMenu`: shortcuts to actions on a thing people right-click, such as a file, a row or a spot on a canvas.

## When not to use

- Picking a value: use [Select] (npx serupa-docs Select) instead (or [Combobox] (npx serupa-docs Combobox) for a long list).
- Navigation links: use a plain list of links instead, or [Navbar] (npx serupa-docs Navbar) or [Sidebar] (npx serupa-docs Sidebar) for an app's pages.
- One or two actions: show them as [Button] (npx serupa-docs Button)s instead, so people don't have to open anything.
- Content with fields or text: use [Popover] (npx serupa-docs Popover) instead.
- A `ContextMenu` as the only way to an action: people rarely look for right-click menus, and many can't right-click. Put each of its actions on a button or a `Menu` too.

## Anatomy

Drawn from the `BottomEnd` story, opened.

1. **Item** (`.srp-menu__item`): one action; Enter or a click runs it.
2. **Icon** (`.srp-menu__icon`): an optional picture of the action.
3. **Label** (`.srp-menu__label`): the action, in words.
4. **Shortcut** (`.srp-menu__shortcut`): the keys that do the same, when there are some.
5. **Group label** (`.srp-menu__group-label`): names a group of items.
6. **Separator** (`.srp-menu__separator`): a line between groups.
7. **Destructive item** (`.srp-menu__item--destructive`): an action that deletes or can't be undone, in the danger color and words that say so.

## Usage

- The trigger is one element that passes its ref and props on to a DOM element: a Button, IconButton or link, or your own component written with `React.forwardRef` (or the `ref` prop in React 19) that spreads what it gets. A text, several elements or a Fragment throws an error that names the component, and a trigger that drops its ref warns once in the console ("Serupa: Menu's trigger doesn't forward its ref to an element.").
- Start each label with a verb ("Edit", "Duplicate", "Delete") and keep it short.
- Put the most used actions first, and destructive ones last, after a `MenuSeparator` or in their own `MenuGroup`.
- Keep `disabled` items in place rather than hiding them, so people learn the action exists. A `ContextMenu` is the exception: it's a shortcut to what can be done to that thing now, so leave out what can't.
- Put nothing only in a `ContextMenu`. A right-click or long press is hidden until someone tries it, so each of its actions is also on the page, in a toolbar, a row's menu or the item's own page.
- For a setting people turn on and off, use one `MenuCheckboxItem` ("Show grid", checked or not) rather than a pair such as "Show grid" and "Hide grid", which leaves people unsure which state they're in.
- Use a `MenuSub` for a set of related choices that would make the menu long ("Share", "Move to"). Keep it to one level where you can: each level is one more step for keyboard and screen reader users, and harder to reach with a pointer. Never put the only way to do something two levels down.
- Give a `ContextMenu` target `tabIndex={0}` (or use a focusable element), so keyboard users can reach it and press Shift+F10, and say in its hint or a Tooltip that it has one. Leave the browser's own menu where people expect it, such as on text they edit or links: `disabled` does that.
- For settings, use `MenuCheckboxItem` (on or off, such as "Show grid") or a `MenuRadioGroup` of `MenuRadioItem`s (one of a set, such as a sort order). Put them in their own `MenuGroup` or `MenuRadioGroup`, to keep settings apart from actions. The menu's items unmount once it has closed, so you hold the state: `checked` with `onCheckedChange`, and `value` with `onValueChange`.
- Labels line up by themselves. When some of a menu's items have an `icon` (or a check), the items without one keep that space, so every label and group heading starts in one column. Each submenu works this out for its own items. Give icons to all of a menu's items or to none where you can; a few icons among plain items draw the eye to those few.
- `shortcut` only shows a hint: wire the shortcut yourself, and show only shortcuts that work. Give it as keys, `['mod', 'K']`, and it follows the platform as [Kbd] (npx serupa-docs Kbd) does: "⌘K" on a Mac and "Ctrl+K" elsewhere, with modifiers in each platform's order ("⇧⌘K", "Ctrl+Shift+K") (a SerupaProvider's `platform` decides from the server render). Text (`"Ctrl+Shift+P"`) shows as written, for a shortcut that is the same everywhere.
- Don't take keys the browser keeps: ⌘N, ⌘T and ⌘W can't be caught at all, and ⌘D, ⌘R and ⌘O already bookmark, reload and open a file. Add Shift or Alt, as the stories do (see [KeyboardShortcuts] (npx serupa-docs KeyboardShortcuts)).

### Do and don't

- **Do:** Put the actions people use most first, and a destructive one last, after a separator. (`DoDestructiveLast`)
- **Don't:** Put Delete first, where the menu opens and a slip of Enter runs it. (`DontDestructiveFirst`)

## Accessibility

- A `MenuSub` is a `menuitem` with `aria-haspopup="menu"` and `aria-expanded`; its submenu is a `menu` named by the item's label, next to the item at its end edge (on the right, or the left in rtl, flipping when there's no room).
- `role="menu"` with `menuitem`s, `group`s and `separator`s; only the highlighted item takes focus.
- A `MenuCheckboxItem` is a `menuitemcheckbox` and a `MenuRadioItem` a `menuitemradio`, with `aria-checked`. The check before the label is hidden from assistive tech, which reads `aria-checked` instead.
- A `shortcut` is given to assistive tech as `aria-keyshortcuts`, worked out from what's shown ("⌘⇧K" becomes `Meta+Shift+K`, "Ctrl+Shift+P" becomes `Control+Shift+P`; `mod` is `Meta` on a Mac and `Control` elsewhere), and the shown `<kbd>` is left out of the item's name, so it's read as "Edit" with its shortcut, not "Edit command E". Hyphens separate too ("Cmd-K" is `Meta+K`), a last `+` is the key ("Ctrl++" is `Control+Plus`), and "G then I" is two presses in a row (`G I`). Pass `aria-keyshortcuts` to set it yourself.
- It fades and grows in out of its trigger over 150ms, and fades and shrinks back over 100ms when it closes. Its items arrive and leave with it, as one. With `prefers-reduced-motion` it only fades. The motion is a transition, so closing it while it opens turns back from where it is. Its items stay while it fades out, inert, and focus goes back at once; a submenu open when the menu closes closes and fades with it. A `ContextMenu` and a `MenuSub`'s submenu move the same way. One open on arrival (`defaultOpen`, or `open` on the first render) is there from the first frame. Firefox and Safari can't keep a closing menu in the top layer yet, so there it closes at once. From the keyboard there is no motion: opened by Enter, Space or an arrow (a submenu by ArrowRight) it is there at once, and Escape takes it away at once.
- Labels, shortcuts and group headings keep 4.5:1 (also on the highlighted item) and icons 3:1, in every theme (`Menu.test.tsx`).

### Keyboard

| Key | On the button | In the menu |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Enter, Space | Opens it on the first item | Chooses the item. Space on a `MenuCheckboxItem` or `MenuRadioItem` changes it and keeps the menu open, so several settings take one trip |
| ↓ / ↑ | Opens it on the first / last item | The next / previous item, wrapping |
| Home, End | | The first or last item |
| Letters | | The next item starting with them. Letters typed within half a second make one word ("de" finds Delete past Duplicate), the same letter again steps through the items starting with it, and accents and case don't matter ("e" finds "Éditer"). A Space within half a second of a letter is part of the word ("save as" finds "Save as…"), so it doesn't choose |
| Escape | | Closes it; focus goes back to the button. The phone's Back gesture or button does the same, innermost menu first |
| Tab | | Closes it and moves on |
| → (← in rtl), Enter, Space | | On a `MenuSub`: opens its submenu on the first item |
| ← (→ in rtl), Escape | | In a submenu: closes it, and focus goes back to the item that opened it |

On a `ContextMenu`'s target, Shift+F10 or the Menu key opens it at the focused element, and a right-click opens it at the pointer. In it the keys are the same, and Escape or a choice puts focus back where it was.

In a submenu, ↑ ↓ Home End and letters move among its own items only. Choosing an item in a submenu closes every level and focus goes back to the button.

A mouse opens the menu as the button is pressed, so it can be dragged onto an item and let go there to choose it, as in a desktop app's menus; a quick click opens it and leaves it open. A touch or pen opens it on the tap, and so does a mouse when the trigger has its own `onClick` (which can call `preventDefault()` to stop it). Hovering an item highlights it, and a press outside closes the menu. Hovering a `MenuSub` opens its submenu after 150ms, and it closes 150ms after the pointer settles on another item. While the pointer keeps moving toward the submenu, across the items below or above on the way, it stays open, as native menus do.

## Props

### Menu

| Prop | Type | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `trigger` | one element | required | The button that opens it. It gets `aria-haspopup`, `aria-expanded`, `aria-controls` and the keys, and keeps its own handlers and ref. It can be wrapped in a [Tooltip] (npx serupa-docs Tooltip) |
| `children` | nodes | required | `MenuItem`, `MenuGroup` and `MenuSeparator` |
| `placement` | as Tooltip | `'bottom-start'` | Where it opens; it flips when there's no room and slides to stay on screen. With no room on either side it opens on the roomier one and scrolls inside, so every item can be reached |
| `open`, `onOpenChange` | boolean, function | | Control it yourself. onOpenChange(open, { reason }) says why: `'trigger'`, `'select'` (an item chosen), `'escape'`, `'blur'` (Tab) or `'outside'` |
| `defaultOpen` | boolean | `false` | Open at first, without controlling it |
| `aria-label` | string | | The menu's name. Without it, the button's text names it |
| `className`, `style`, other HTML attributes and a ref | | | Go on the menu panel: `data-testid`, an `id`, other `aria-*` and a ref reach it, as on Radix's and React Aria's menu content. Its `onKeyDown` runs before the menu's keys and can call `preventDefault()` to stop them |

The menu panel's id is made for you unless you pass one, and the trigger's `aria-controls` points at it while it's open. An id on the trigger stays on the trigger.

### ContextMenu

| Prop | Type | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `target` | one element | required | The area it belongs to. A right-click, a long press, Shift+F10 or the Menu key in it opens the menu. It keeps its own handlers and ref, and its `onContextMenu` can call `preventDefault()` to stop it |
| `children` | nodes | required | `MenuItem`, `MenuGroup`, `MenuSub` and `MenuSeparator` |
| `aria-label` | string | required | The menu's name ("File actions"), since there's no button to take it from |
| `open`, `onOpenChange` | boolean, function | | Control it yourself. Opened this way, it shows at the target's corner. onOpenChange(open, { reason }) says why: `'trigger'`, `'select'` (an item chosen), `'escape'`, `'blur'` (Tab) or `'outside'` |
| `disabled` | boolean | `false` | Leaves the browser's own menu in place |
| `className`, `style`, other HTML attributes and a ref | | | Go on the menu panel: `data-testid`, an `id`, other `aria-*` and a ref reach it. Its `onKeyDown` runs before the menu's keys and can call `preventDefault()` to stop them |

An id on the target stays on the target.

### MenuItem

| Prop | Type | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `onSelect` | `(event) => void` | | Runs when it's chosen (click, Enter or Space). The menu then closes and focus goes back to the button, unless you call `event.preventDefault()`. If it moves focus itself (to the next row, after deleting this one), focus stays there |
| `icon` | icon name \| element | | A muted 16px icon before the label |
| `shortcut` | string \| string[] | | A hint at the end (wire the shortcut yourself). Keys, `['mod', 'K']`, show as ⌘K on a Mac and Ctrl+K elsewhere; text shows as written. Also sets `aria-keyshortcuts` |
| `destructive` | boolean | `false` | Danger colors |
| `disabled` | boolean | `false` | Still reachable with the keys (so people learn it exists), but can't be chosen |
| `as` | component | | Makes it a link with this component instead of the `configure({ link })` one, such as a router's Link. Typed: its props are those of the element `as` names, so `as={RouterLink} to="/settings"` checks `to`, and without `as` they're an `<a>`'s (`href`, `target`, `rel`) |

`href` makes it a link (the `configure({ link })` component). `target` and `rel` go to a link item, and `target="_blank"` without `rel` gets `rel="noopener noreferrer"`. `className`, `ref` and the rest go to the item: the link, or a `<div>` for an action.

### MenuCheckboxItem

| Prop | Type | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `checked` | boolean | required | Whether it's on |
| `onCheckedChange` | `(checked) => void` | | Called with the other state when it's chosen. The menu then closes, unless `onSelect` calls `event.preventDefault()` |

It also takes MenuItem's `onSelect`, `icon`, `shortcut` and `disabled`.

### MenuRadioGroup and MenuRadioItem

| Prop | Type | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `value` (group) | string | required | The chosen item's value |
| `onValueChange` (group) | `(value) => void` | | Called with an item's value when it's chosen, unless it was chosen already |
| `label` (group) | node | | A small heading that names the group, as on `MenuGroup` |
| `value` (item) | string | required | The value the group chooses with this item |

A `MenuRadioItem` also takes MenuItem's `onSelect`, `icon`, `shortcut` and `disabled`.

### MenuSub

| Prop | Type | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `label` | node | required | The item's label, which also names the submenu |
| `children` | nodes | required | `MenuItem`, `MenuGroup`, `MenuSeparator`, or another `MenuSub` |
| `icon` | icon name \| element | | A muted 16px icon before the label |
| `disabled` | boolean | `false` | Still reachable with the keys, but doesn't open |

`MenuGroup` takes a `label` (a small heading that names the group); `MenuSeparator` is a line. Every part takes `className`, `style` and `ref`.

## Component tokens

Each is an optional override: set it on the page, a container or one menu. The list lives in `src/components/Menu/menu.tokens.json` (also in `design-tokens/components/`).

<!-- token-table:start (made from menu.tokens.json by npm run tokens: edit the descriptions there) -->

| `--menu-border` | `border-overlay` | The menu's border. |

components.name: Menubar
components.summary: An application's menu bar: File, Edit, View along the top of an editor or tool, each opening a menu.
components.guide:
# Menubar

An application's menu bar: File, Edit, View along the top of an editor or tool, each opening a menu. The whole bar is one Tab stop, the arrow keys move across it, and with a menu open, ← and → go straight to the next menu, open, as in a desktop app.

**Also called:** menu bar, application menu.

```tsx
import { Menubar, MenubarMenu, MenuItem, MenuSub, MenuSeparator } from "@diki-stwn/serupa-ds";

<Menubar aria-label="Editor">
  <MenubarMenu label="File">
    <MenuItem icon="add" shortcut={['alt', 'N']} onSelect={create}>New</MenuItem>
    <MenuSub icon="share" label="Share">
      <MenuItem icon="mail" onSelect={email}>Email</MenuItem>
    </MenuSub>
    <MenuSeparator />
    <MenuItem icon="print" shortcut={['mod', 'P']} onSelect={print}>Print</MenuItem>
  </MenubarMenu>
  <MenubarMenu label="Edit">
    <MenuItem icon="undo" shortcut={['mod', 'Z']} onSelect={undo}>Undo</MenuItem>
  </MenubarMenu>
</Menubar>
```

## When to use

- An editor or tool with many commands people come back to: a document editor, a report builder, a diagram tool.
- When those commands fall into a few familiar groups (File, Edit, View, Insert, Help) that people expect along the top.

## When not to use

- A few actions on one thing: use a [Menu] (npx serupa-docs Menu) behind one button instead.
- Buttons people press often, such as an editor's bold and italic: use a [Toolbar] (npx serupa-docs Toolbar), so each is one press away.
- Navigation between an app's pages: use [Navbar] (npx serupa-docs Navbar) or [Sidebar] (npx serupa-docs Sidebar). A menubar is for commands, not links.
- A phone-sized layout: a row of menus is hard to aim at and to read there. Put the commands in one Menu or a [Drawer] (npx serupa-docs Drawer) instead.

## Anatomy

Drawn from the `Open` story.

1. **Bar** (`.srp-menubar`): the row that holds the menus' names, one Tab stop.
2. **Menu name** (`.srp-menubar__item`): opens its menu; pressed while it's open.
3. **Menu** (`.srp-menu`): the menu it opens, a [Menu] (npx serupa-docs Menu).

## Usage

- Name the bar (`aria-label`, "Editor"), so screen readers say which menu bar it is.
- Keep to the names people know, in the usual order: File, Edit, View, then your own, then Help. Use one word each where you can.
- Put each command in one place. A command also on a Toolbar is fine; the same command in two menus is not.
- `disabled` keeps a menu in the bar while nothing in it can be used yet, so people learn it's there. Disable single items with MenuItem's own `disabled` rather than the whole menu where you can.
- Each `MenubarMenu` holds what a [Menu] (npx serupa-docs Menu) holds: `MenuItem`, `MenuSub`, `MenuGroup`, `MenuSeparator`, `MenuCheckboxItem` and `MenuRadioGroup`. Their props and rules are Menu's. `shortcut` only shows a hint: wire the shortcut yourself.
- `defaultOpen` on one menu opens it on arrival, for a walkthrough or a screenshot.

### Do and don't

- **Do:** Keep to the names people know, in the usual order: File, Edit, View, then your own, then Help. (`DoFamiliarNames`)
- **Don't:** Rename or reorder the usual menus: people can't find what they know is there. (`DontNewNames`)

## Accessibility

- **Role and name:** `role="menubar"`, named by `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby`. Each name is a `menuitem` button with `aria-haspopup="menu"` and `aria-expanded`, and its menu is a `menu` named by it. A disabled menu's name has `aria-disabled` and stays reachable.
- **Keyboard:** below. The bar keeps the last name used as its Tab stop.
- **Pointer:** a click opens or closes a menu, a mouse press opens it so it can be dragged onto an item (as in Menu). While a menu is open, pointing at another name opens that one, and the two swap at once with no fade, as in a desktop app.
- **Contrast:** names read 4.5:1 on the bar, under the pointer and while open, and the focus ring 3:1, in every theme (`Menubar.test.tsx`). In forced colors the open name is drawn in Highlight.
- **What's still yours:** the bar's name, wiring the shortcuts you show, and keeping commands where people expect them.

### Keyboard

| Key | On a name in the bar | In an open menu |
| --- | --- | --- |
| → / ← (mirrored in rtl) | The next / previous name, wrapping | Closes it and opens the next / previous menu on its first item (on a `MenuSub`, → opens the submenu instead, and ← in a submenu closes it) |
| ↓ / ↑, Enter, Space | Opens its menu on the first / last item | As in Menu |
| Home, End | The first or last name | The first or last item |
| Letters | The next name starting with them | The next item starting with them |
| Escape | | Closes it; focus goes back to its name |
| Tab | Leaves the bar | Closes it and leaves the bar |

## Props

### Menubar

| Prop | Type | Default | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `aria-label` | `string` | | The bar's name. Or name it with `aria-labelledby`. |
| `children` | `ReactNode` | | Its `MenubarMenu`s, in order. |
| `id` | `string` | | Goes to the root `<div role="menubar">`. |

`className`, `ref` and other props go to the `<div role="menubar">`. Its `onKeyDown` runs first and can call `preventDefault()` to stop the bar's keys.

### MenubarMenu

| Prop | Type | Default | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `label` | `ReactNode` | required | The menu's name in the bar. |
| `children` | `ReactNode` | | Its items, as in a Menu. |
| `disabled` | `boolean` | `false` | Reachable with the keys, but doesn't open. |
| `defaultOpen` | `boolean` | `false` | Open on arrival. |
| `id` | `string` | | Goes to the name's `<button>`; its menu is named by it. |

`className`, `ref` and other props go to the name's `<button>`. Outside a Menubar it is a plain Menu behind that button.

## Component tokens

Each is an optional override: set it on the page, a container or one Menubar. The list lives in `src/components/Menubar/menubar.tokens.json` (also in `design-tokens/components/`).

<!-- token-table:start (made from menubar.tokens.json by npm run tokens: edit the descriptions there) -->
| Token | Default | Use |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--menubar-bg` | `surface` | The bar's background. |
| `--menubar-border` | `border` | The line under the bar. |
| `--menubar-item-text` | `text` | A menu's name (4.5:1 on bg, on the hover and on the open background). |
| `--menubar-item-bg-hover` | `highlight` | A menu name's background under the pointer. |
| `--menubar-item-bg-pressed` | `pressed` | Its background while held down, one step past hover. |
| `--menubar-item-bg-open` | `pressed` | The background of the name whose menu is open. |
| `--menubar-focus-ring` | `focus-ring` | The focus ring around a menu's name (3:1 on bg). |
| `--menubar-text-disabled` | `disabled-text` | Disabled: the text, icon or mark, in place of fading it (3:1 or more on its background, more with more contrast). |
| `--menubar-item-radius` | `radius-control` | A menu name's corners (6px). |
| `--menubar-padding` | `spacing-1` | Space inside the bar, on every side (4px). |
| `--menubar-gap` | `spacing-1` | Space between the menus' names (4px). |
| `--menubar-item-padding-x` | `spacing-3` | Space each side of a menu's name (12px). |
| `--menubar-item-height` | `control-height-sm` | A menu name's height (32px). |
<!-- token-table:end -->

components.name: Meter
components.summary: Shows a measurement within a known range: storage used, a plan's seats, a password's strength, a battery level.
components.guide:
# Meter

Shows a measurement within a known range: storage used, a plan's seats, a password's strength, a battery level. Give it `low`, `high` and `optimum` and it colors itself by zone, as HTML's `<meter>` does: success in the best zone, warning in the next, danger in the worst. It isn't [Progress] (npx serupa-docs Progress), which shows how far along a task is.

**Also called:** gauge.

```tsx
import { Meter } from "@diki-stwn/serupa-ds";

<Meter value={72} label="Storage" showValue />
// low values are good: up to 80% is fine, then warning, over 95% danger
<Meter value={92} low={80} high={95} optimum={0} label="Storage" showValue formatValue={(v) => `${v}%, almost full`} />
// high values are good: a battery
<Meter value={18} low={20} high={60} optimum={100} label="Battery" showValue />
<Meter value={7.2} max={10} label="Storage" showValue formatValue={(v, _, m) => `${v} of ${m} GB`} />
```

## When to use

- A level or amount within fixed limits: storage, a quota, seats, a score, a strength or a temperature.
- When the value is better or worse depending on where it falls, with `low`, `high` and `optimum`.

## When not to use

- How far along a task is (an upload, an import): use [Progress] (npx serupa-docs Progress) instead.
- A value people set themselves: use [Slider] (npx serupa-docs Slider) instead.
- A count with no maximum, such as unread messages: use a [Badge] (npx serupa-docs Badge) or text.

## Anatomy

Drawn from the `CustomValue` story.

1. **Label** (`.srp-meter__label`): what is measured.
2. **Value** (`.srp-meter__value`): the amount, in words or numbers.
3. **Track** (`.srp-meter__track`): the whole range.
4. **Fill** (`.srp-meter__fill`): how much of it is used, in the color of its zone (low, medium, high).

## Usage

- Give every meter a `label` that says what it measures ("Storage"), or an `aria-label`.
- Use `formatValue` when a percentage isn't the clearest words: "7.2 of 10 GB", "Strong".
- Color isn't enough on its own: when a zone matters, say it in the value or nearby text too ("92%, almost full").
- Pick `optimum` by what's good. Under `low`: low values are good (storage used, errors). Over `high`: high values are good (battery, a score). In between, or left out: the middle zone is good and both ends are less good (a temperature, a word count).
- The percentage follows the locale from `SerupaProvider` (or the browser), as Progress does: "72%", "%72" in Turkish, "72 %" in French.

## Zones

With `low` and `high` set, the zone (also in `data-state`) is worked out the way browsers do it for `<meter>`:

| `optimum` | Under `low` | `low` to `high` | Over `high` |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| under `low` | optimum (success) | suboptimal (warning) | poor (danger) |
| over `high` | poor (danger) | suboptimal (warning) | optimum (success) |
| in between, or left out | suboptimal (warning) | optimum (success) | suboptimal (warning) |

Without `low` and `high` the bar is primary and `data-state` is `none`. `meterState(value, min, max, low, high, optimum)` returns the same zone, for text that goes with it.

## Behavior

- The value is clamped between `min` and `max`, and the fill moves to a new value over 300ms (at once with `prefers-reduced-motion`).

### Do and don't

- **Do:** Say the zone in words as well as color: "92%, almost full". (`DoSayTheZone`)
- **Don't:** Leave a bare "92%" where only the color warns: people who can't tell the colors apart miss it. (`DontColorOnly`)

## Accessibility

- `role="meter"` with `aria-valuenow`, `aria-valuemin`, `aria-valuemax` and `aria-valuetext` (the shown value). It's named by its `label`.
- Outside the best zone, the value also says where it falls, shown with `showValue` and read out, so the warning the color gives is seen and heard in words too (WCAG 1.4.1): "92%, high", "12%, low" or "45%, medium". The words come from the `meterZone` label in `SerupaProvider`. With `formatValue`, your words are read as they are, so say the zone in them.
- The track has a 1px `border-control` edge, a soft line by design (3:1 with more contrast), so the whole scale shows, and its inside is the page's surface. Every zone's fill keeps 3:1 against it, and the label and value 4.5:1, in every theme (`Meter.test.tsx`). In forced-colors mode the track gets a border and the fill uses Highlight.
- **Keyboard:** none: it shows a value and isn't focusable. Use a Slider for a value people set.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | string | none | Goes to the root `<div>`. |
| `value` | `number` | | Between `min` and `max`, clamped. |
| `min` | `number` | `0` | The lowest possible value. |
| `max` | `number` | `100` | The highest possible value. |
| `low` | `number` | | Values under it are low. |
| `high` | `number` | | Values over it are high. |
| `optimum` | `number` | the middle | The best value; it decides which zone is good (see Zones). |
| `size` | `'sm' \| 'md' \| 'lg'` | `'md'` | The bar is 4, 8 or 12px thick. |
| `label` | `ReactNode` | | A visible name above the bar. Otherwise pass `aria-label`. |
| `showValue` | `boolean` | `false` | The value at the end of the label row, in the read-out's words. |
| `formatValue` | `(value, min, max) => string` | the share, as the locale writes a percentage | The value's words, shown and read out. Without it, the value adds the zone outside the best one. |

Every other prop, `className` and `ref` go to the outer `<div>`. It has `data-component="meter"`, `data-size` and `data-state` (`optimum`, `suboptimal`, `poor` or `none`).

## Component tokens

Each is an optional override: set it on the page, a container or one meter. The list lives in `src/components/Meter/meter.tokens.json` (also in `design-tokens/components/`).

<!-- token-table:start (made from meter.tokens.json by npm run tokens: edit the descriptions there) -->
| Token | Default | Use |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--meter-track` | `track` | The empty part of the bar: the shared `track` gray, Apple's level (zinc-200 in light, zinc-700 in dark), with no edge. |
| `--meter-track-border` | `track` | The bar's 1px edge: the track's own color by default, so no edge shows; set it to outline the bar. |
| `--meter-fill` | `primary` | The filled part, without low and high zones (3:1 on the track and the surface). |
| `--meter-fill-optimum` | `success` | The filled part in the best zone. |
| `--meter-fill-suboptimal` | `warning` | The filled part in the next zone. |
| `--meter-fill-poor` | `danger` | The filled part in the worst zone. |
| `--meter-label-color` | `text` | The label. |
| `--meter-value-color` | `text-muted` | The value at the end of the label row (4.5:1). |
| `--meter-fill-edge` | `primary-edge` | The primary fill's 1px edge (Yellow Light; transparent where the fill is 3:1 on the page) |
| `--meter-height-sm` | `spacing-1` | The bar's thickness, size sm (4px). |
| `--meter-height-md` | `spacing-2` | The bar's thickness, size md (8px, the default). |
| `--meter-height-lg` | `spacing-3` | The bar's thickness, size lg (12px). |
| `--meter-radius` | `radius-pill` | The bar's ends. |
| `--meter-gap` | `spacing-1.5` | Space between the label row and the bar (6px). |
| `--meter-label-weight` | `font-medium` | The label's weight. |
| `--meter-duration` | `motion-change-lg` | How long the fill takes to move to a new value. |
<!-- token-table:end -->

components.name: Navbar
components.summary: The bar across the top of an app: the brand on the left, the main page links, and actions on the right (search, a user menu, sign in).
components.guide:
# Navbar The bar across the top of an app: the brand on the left, the main page links, and actions on the right (search, a user menu, sign in). Below 768px wide, or wider when they don't fit between the brand and the actions, the links fold into a menu button that opens them in a panel under the bar. A NavbarMenu in the bar opens a panel of grouped links with a line about each (a mega menu). **Also called:** header, top bar, app bar. ```jsx import { Navbar, NavbarLink, Button, Avatar } from '@diki-stwn/serupa-ds'; Acme} actions={<>} > Dashboard Projects Team ``` ## When to use - The top level of an app or site with a handful of main pages. - A place for the brand and app-wide actions, such as search, a user menu or sign in. - A few top-level sections that each hold several pages worth a line of explanation, such as Products or Resources on a marketing site: a `NavbarMenu` with `NavbarMenuGroup`s of `NavbarMenuLink`s. ## When not to use - Many pages, or pages in groups and levels: use a [Sidebar] (npx serupa-docs Sidebar) instead. - Switching between views of the same thing on one page: use [Tabs] (npx serupa-docs Tabs) instead. - Showing where a page sits in a hierarchy: use a [Breadcrumb] (npx serupa-docs Breadcrumb) instead. ## Anatomy Drawn from the `Playground` story. 1. **Brand** (`.srp-navbar__brand`): the product's name or logo, linking home. 2. **Links** (`.srp-navbar__links`): the main sections of the site. 3. **Current link** (`.srp-navbar__link--active`): the section you're in. 4. **Actions** (`.srp-navbar__actions`): search, account or other actions at the end. ## Usage - A NavbarMenu's parts (the `Menus` story): its button (`.srp-navbar__menu-button`), with the section's name and a chevron that turns while it's open; the panel (`.srp-navbar__menu-panel`) across the bar under it; its groups (`.srp-navbar__menu-group`), each a title over a list of links; and each link (`.srp-navbar__menu-link`), its name and a muted line about it. - Keep the links to the main pages, a few short words each; below 768px, or when they don't fit beside the brand and the actions (seven links, long translated labels), they fold into the menu button. More links than fit below the bar scroll inside the panel, and in the panel a long label wraps onto more lines. - Mark the current page with `current` on its NavbarLink. - Register your router's link component once with `configure({ link })`, or pass it in `as`, so links don't reload the page. - Keep `actions` compact below 768px, such as one small button and an Avatar. If they don't fit, the brand shrinks and ends in an ellipsis so the menu button stays on screen (a brand passed as text shows whole on hover and focus; in a link of your own, put the name in a [TruncatedText] (npx serupa-docs TruncatedText) to do the same); if they still don't, they scroll sideways within the bar (Tab scrolls each into view), and the page never does. - Set `size` to the same width as the page's Container, so the bar lines up with the content. - For a section with several pages, use a `NavbarMenu` with a `label` and its links, grouped in `NavbarMenuGroup`s with a `title` when there are more than a handful. Give each `NavbarMenuLink` a short `description` when the name alone doesn't say what's there. Keep a panel to what fits on one screen: it's a way in, not a site map. - A NavbarMenu's button doesn't go anywhere itself. Give the section's own page a link in its panel, such as "All products". ### Do and don't - **Do:** Keep the links to the main pages, a few short words each. (`DoFewLinks`) - **Don't:** Put every page in the bar: most fold away, and the main ones get lost among them. (`DontEveryPage`) ## Accessibility - It's a `
` (the banner landmark, when it's the page's top-level header) holding a `
` named "Main", so people can jump to the links. - The current page has `aria-current="page"`, a shaded background and, when more contrast is asked for, a 2px bar along its bottom (at the start of a link in a menu panel). Hover shades a link (`surface-hover`; `surface-hover-raised` in a menu panel; zinc-100 in light, like the current page) but never draws the bar; the current page darkens one step under the pointer. In forced colors (Windows High Contrast), where the shading is dropped, it has an outline. - On small screens the menu button has `aria-expanded` and `aria-controls`. Escape closes the menu and returns focus to the button. On a phone, the Back gesture or button closes it the same way, an open NavbarMenu panel first, before it leaves the page. - With the menu open, Tab goes from the button into the links, in the order they appear, since the panel opens under the bar: the links come after the button in the DOM while it's open. Tab past the last link, any move of focus out of the bar, or a press outside it closes the menu. - The panel fades in as it opens and unrolls down from the bar, over 150ms, and fades back out when it closes, as Popover and Menu do.
