components.name: NotificationCenter
components.summary: A drawer of past notifications with read states: newest first, unread ones with a dot and a bolder title, and buttons to mark them read or clear the list.
components.guide:
# NotificationCenter

A drawer of past notifications with read states: newest first, unread ones with a dot and a bolder title, and buttons to mark them read or clear the list. `useToastHistory` keeps the toasts already shown for it, so a message missed while it was up can be found again.

**Also called:** inbox, notification panel.

```tsx
import { Badge, Button, NotificationCenter, Toaster, useSerupa, useToastHistory } from "@diki-stwn/serupa-ds";

function Layout() {
  const [open, setOpen] = React.useState(false);
  const history = useToastHistory();
  const { labels } = useSerupa();
  return <>
    <Toaster />
    {/* The count in words in the name ("Notifications, 2 unread"), so the Badge is hidden and isn't read as a bare "2". */}
    <Button variant="ghost" aria-label={labels.notificationsUnread(history.unread)} onClick={() => setOpen(true)}>
      {labels.notificationCenter} {history.unread ? <Badge count={history.unread} aria-hidden="true" /> : null}
    </Button>
    <NotificationCenter items={history.items} open={open} onOpenChange={setOpen}
      onMarkRead={history.markRead} onMarkAllRead={() => history.markRead()} onClear={history.clear} />
  </>;
}
```

## When to use

- An app that shows toasts people may miss: they go after a few seconds, and someone away from the screen, or using a magnifier, never sees them.
- An inbox of app notifications (mentions, finished exports, failed payments) that people check from a bell in the header.

## When not to use

- Something people must act on now: use an [Alert] (npx serupa-docs Alert) on the page or a [Dialog] (npx serupa-docs Dialog).
- A full activity feed with filters and paging: build a page with [List] (npx serupa-docs List) and [Pagination] (npx serupa-docs Pagination).

## Anatomy

Drawn from the `Open` story.

1. **List** (`.srp-notification-center__list`): the notifications, newest first.
2. **Notification** (`.srp-notification-center__item`): one notification.
3. **Icon** (`.srp-notification-center__icon`): its tone: info, success, warning or danger.
4. **Title** (`.srp-notification-center__title`): what happened.
5. **Description** (`.srp-notification-center__description`): more about it.
6. **Time** (`.srp-notification-center__time`): when it happened.
7. **Unread** (`.srp-notification-center__dot`): marks one not read yet, also in words for screen readers.

## Usage

- Call `useToastHistory()` once, in the layout that renders the `<Toaster>`, and pass its `items` to the NotificationCenter. It keeps up to `limit` (50) toasts shown while it's mounted.
- Or pass your own `items` (from a server, say): `{ id, title, description?, tone?, time?, read? }`, newest first. Keep `read` in your state and set it in `onMarkRead` and `onMarkAllRead`.
- Show the unread count on the button that opens it, with a [Badge] (npx serupa-docs Badge) `count`, and name the button so the count is heard too ("Notifications, 3 unread"): `labels.notificationsUnread(count)` from `useSerupa()` writes it in the page's language. Hide the Badge (`aria-hidden="true"`) so the number isn't read twice.
- Give `onMarkRead`, `onMarkAllRead` and `onClear` for the buttons you want; without a handler, its button isn't shown.
- Give `settingsHref` when your app has notification settings, so people can turn off what they don't want from where they meet too many.

## Behavior

- It's a [Drawer] (npx serupa-docs Drawer) from the end edge (the right in a left-to-right page): it opens and closes like one, and takes its `placement`, `size` and `modal` props.
- Each notification shows its tone icon, title, description and time ("5 min. ago", in [RelativeTime] (npx serupa-docs RelativeTime)). Unread ones have a dot at the end and a semibold title.
- "Mark as read" goes away once chosen, and focus moves to its notification, so it isn't lost.
- When you take the focused notification out of `items` (an inbox that hides read ones), focus goes to the one now in its place, else the last, else the "No notifications yet" line, not to the page.
- `useToastHistory` records a toast when it's shown, unread. A toast replaced by its id (`toast.promise`'s "Saving…" then "Saved") stays one entry with the newer words. A repeat ("×3" in the Toaster) moves it back to the top, unread again.
- With no notifications, it says "No notifications yet" (`emptyText`).

### Do and don't

- **Do:** Write titles that say what happened ("Payment failed", "Invoice sent"). (`Open`)
- **Don't:** Write titles like "Update": people have to open each one to learn what it's about. (`DontVagueTitles`)

## Accessibility

- **Keyboard:**

| Key | Does |
| --- | --- |
| <kbd>Tab</kbd> | Moves through the drawer: each "Mark as read", the footer buttons and the ×. |
| <kbd>Enter</kbd> / <kbd>Space</kbd> | Chooses the focused button. |
| <kbd>Escape</kbd> | Closes it, and focus goes back to where it was. |

- The drawer is named by its title, "Notifications". The list is a `<ul>`, so screen readers hear how many there are.
- An unread one's title starts with "Unread:", for screen readers; the dot is hidden from them. Tone icons are hidden too, so put the meaning in the title.
- **Contrast:** descriptions and times read 4.5:1, and the unread dot 3:1, on the drawer in every theme (`NotificationCenter.test.tsx`). In forced colors (Windows high contrast) the dot is drawn in CanvasText, so it doesn't vanish into the Canvas background.
- **What's still yours:** name the button that opens it with the unread count, and say what each notification is about in its title, not only its tone.

## useToastHistory(options)

| Option or field | Type | Default | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `limit` | number | `50` | The most kept; older ones drop off. |
| `items` | `NotificationItem[]` | | Returned: the toasts shown since it mounted, newest first. |
| `unread` | number | | Returned: how many are unread. |
| `markRead` | `(id?) => void` | | Returned: marks one read, or every one with no id. |
| `clear` | `() => void` | | Returned: empties the list. |

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | string | none | Goes to the `<dialog>`. |
| `items` | `{ id, title, description?, tone?, time?, read? }[]` | | The notifications, newest first. |
| `title` | ReactNode | `"Notifications"` | The drawer's title. |
| `onMarkRead` | `(id) => void` | | Shows "Mark as read" on unread ones. |
| `onMarkAllRead` | `() => void` | | Shows "Mark all as read" in the footer while one is unread. |
| `onClear` | `() => void` | | Shows "Clear all" in the footer while the list has any. It can't be undone, so it asks first in the footer ("Clear every notification? This can’t be undone."), with focus on "Keep them"; the destructive "Clear all" beside it calls `onClear`. When the button chosen goes away, focus moves to the other one or to the empty line. |
| `emptyText` | ReactNode | `"No notifications yet"` | What shows with none. |
| `settingsHref` | string | | Where people choose which notifications they get. The footer then starts with a "Notification settings" link to it, so someone who gets too many can turn some off from the drawer. |
| `description`, `footer`, `unsaved` | never | | Not taken: the list is the content, the footer holds its buttons, and there is nothing to edit. |
| `open` | boolean | | Controlled: whether it's open. |
| `defaultOpen` | boolean | `false` | Uncontrolled: open at first. |
| `onOpenChange` | `(open, details) => void` | | Called when people ask to close it. |

`placement`, `size`, `modal`, `className`, `ref` and other `<dialog>` attributes go to the [Drawer] (npx serupa-docs Drawer).

## Component tokens

Each is an optional override: set it on the page, a container or one NotificationCenter. The list lives in `src/components/NotificationCenter/notification-center.tokens.json` (also in `design-tokens/components/`).

<!-- token-table:start (made from notification-center.tokens.json by npm run tokens: edit the descriptions there) -->
| Token | Default | Use |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--notification-center-unread` | `primary` | The unread dot (3:1 on the drawer). |
| `--notification-center-divider` | `border` | The line between notifications. |
| `--notification-center-description` | `text-muted` | A notification's description and time (4.5:1 on the drawer). |
| `--notification-center-icon-info` | `info` | The info tone's icon. |
| `--notification-center-icon-success` | `success` | The success tone's icon. |
| `--notification-center-icon-warning` | `warning` | The warning tone's icon. |
| `--notification-center-icon-danger` | `danger` | The danger tone's icon. |
| `--notification-center-focus-ring` | `focus-ring` | The ring around a notification (or the empty line) focused after "Mark as read". |
| `--notification-center-unread-edge` | `primary-edge` | The unread dot's 1px edge (Yellow Light; transparent where the fill is 3:1 on the page) |
| `--notification-center-row-padding` | `spacing-3` | Space above and below each notification (12px). |
| `--notification-center-unread-weight` | `font-semibold` | An unread notification's title. |
<!-- token-table:end -->

components.name: NumberInput
components.summary: A field for a number, with − and + buttons at the end.
components.guide:
# NumberInput

A field for a number, with − and + buttons at the end. People can type freely; the arrow keys and buttons change it by `step`, and it's kept within `min` and `max`. It uses Input's box, sizes and tokens.

**Also called:** nudger, quantity input, counter, spin button.

```tsx
import { NumberInput } from "@diki-stwn/serupa-ds";

<NumberInput aria-label="Quantity" defaultValue={1} min={1} max={99} />

const [price, setPrice] = React.useState<number | null>(9.5);
<NumberInput aria-label="Price" value={price} onValueChange={setPrice} step={0.5} min={0} />

// Money: the symbol where the locale puts it ("$19.99", "19,99 €"), stored as whole cents
const [cents, setCents] = React.useState<number | null>(1999);
<NumberInput aria-label="Price" currency="USD" minorUnits value={cents} onValueChange={setCents} min={0} />
```

## When to use

- A count or an amount people know exactly: a quantity, a price, a number of seats.
- Small changes up or down from a starting value, with the arrow keys or the − and + buttons.

## When not to use

- A value where its place in a range matters more than the exact number: use [Slider] (npx serupa-docs Slider).
- Digits that aren't an amount, such as a phone number, a postcode or a card number: use [Input] (npx serupa-docs Input) with the right `type` or `inputMode`.

## Anatomy

Drawn from the `Controlled` story.

1. **Field** (`.srp-input__field`): where the number is typed.
2. **Steppers** (`.srp-number-input__steppers`): the buttons that lower and raise it by one step.
3. **Step** (`.srp-number-input__step`): one of them; holding it repeats.

## Usage

- Label it with [Field] (npx serupa-docs Field) and put the unit in the label or hint ("Weight (kg)").
- Set `min`, `max` and `step` to the real limits, so the field keeps values within them.
- Match the `size` to the fields and buttons beside it.
- For money, set `currency` to its ISO 4217 code. The symbol goes where the locale writes it, and the value keeps the currency's decimals however coarse `step` is, so `12.5` stays $12.50. A `value` or `defaultValue` with more decimals than that is taken as shown: `19.995` shows as $20.00, and the form gets 20. With `formatOptions`, it's the same for the decimals they show. A controlled parent that keeps 19.995 isn't told, because nothing was edited.
- Store money as whole minor units with `minorUnits`: `value`, `defaultValue`, `onValueChange`, `min`, `max` and `step` are then cents (`1999` is $19.99, `step={5}` is five cents), which avoids floating-point sums such as `0.1 + 0.2`. The minor units come from ISO 4217: 2 for most currencies, including IDR, 0 for JPY and KRW, 3 for KWD.

## States

| State | Look |
| --- | --- |
| Rest | `field` background, 1px `field-border`, the − and + buttons in `text-muted` |
| Hover | `field-border-hover`; the − or + under the pointer takes a `field-hover` fill, `field-pressed` while pressed |
| Focus | Like Input: the border and a 1px ring hugging it in `focus-ring` (2px in all), and a visible outline in forced-colors mode |
| Invalid | `danger` border, and a `danger` focus ring |
| Read-only | `field-readonly` background, no hover change; still focusable and selectable; − and + are off with a plain cursor |
| Disabled | `field-readonly` background, `disabled-border` edge and `disabled-text` at full opacity, `not-allowed` cursor; − and + are off too |

## Behavior

- On blur the text is parsed in the locale's marks, clamped, rounded to the step's decimals and written back in the locale's form. The locale's group mark counts as grouping only when the digits are grouped in threes, so `1.500` is 1500 in `id-ID` and `de-DE`, and `9.5` or `9,5` is 9.5 in any locale. Spaces, a currency symbol or %, a typographic minus and digits in other scripts are accepted. Text that isn't a number goes back to the last number, and screen readers are told (“abc” wasn’t accepted, so the previous value was kept.). Switching to another window or browser tab isn't leaving the field: the text waits until people come back.
- The value is written in the locale's own digits, as Meter, Pagination and Calendar write numbers: `١٢٥٠٫٥` in `ar-EG`, `۱۲۵۰٫۵` in `fa-IR`. People can type digits in any script, Latin ones too, and the form always gets Latin digits (`1250.5`). Pass `numberingSystem="latn"` to show Latin digits instead.
- A typed number outside `min`..`max` is brought back within them on blur or Enter, as spinbuttons do. A `value` the app set outside them is left alone when people only tab through. A decimal mark left at the end (`5.` or `7,`) is read without it on blur or Enter. `onInvalidInput(text, "range")` tells the app, so a form can say "Quantity was reduced to 100"; text that isn't a number calls it with `"unreadable"`.
- **Forms get the number.** With `name`, the form submits the number itself from a hidden input (`1500000`, not "Rp 1.500.000"; whole cents with `minorUnits`, so `1999` for $19.99), and the visible field has no name. `form` works for a field outside its form. A disabled field sends nothing.
- **Form reset** puts `defaultValue` back, in the field and in what the form sends. A controlled field shows its `value` again.
- Leave `locale` unset in most products so it follows the `SerupaProvider` locale, or the visitor's browser without one.
- A typed number outside the limits isn't reported until blur, so a half-typed number never jumps.
- The buttons are out of the Tab order, since the arrow keys do the same, and are disabled at the limits.
- Holding − or + repeats: one step on the press, then after 400ms one every 50ms, until the pointer goes up or leaves the button, Escape is pressed, or the limit is reached. A screen reader's click is one step.

### Do and don't

- **Do:** Put the unit in the label, "Weight (kg)", and set `min`, `max` and `step` to the real limits. (`DoUnitInLabel`)
- **Don't:** Leave the unit out: people have to guess whether it's kilograms or pounds. (`DontNoUnit`)

## Accessibility

- Each stepper button takes presses over at least 24px (WCAG 2.5.8), even at size `sm` where it's 22px: a box behind it reaches past its edges without moving anything.
- A press anywhere else on the box, on the icon, the side padding or the gap by a prefix, focuses the field with the caret at the end, as Input's box does.
- `role="spinbutton"` with `aria-valuenow`, `aria-valuemin` and `aria-valuemax`. It's `type="text"` with `inputMode` numeric or decimal, which avoids the native number field's scroll-wheel and locale problems.
- The − and + keep 3:1 and the number 4.5:1 on the field in every theme (`NumberInput.test.tsx`).

### Keyboard

| Key | Does |
| --- | --- |
| ArrowUp, ArrowDown | ± `step`. From a typed value between steps, the first press goes to the nearest step that way (0.1 ↑ with `step={0.25}` is 0.25), as the native field and Slider do. Money shown with finer decimals than its step keeps them ($19.99 ↑ with a step of $1 is $20.99) |
| PageUp, PageDown, Shift+Arrow | ± `largeStep` steps |
| Home, End | `min`, `max` (when set) |
| Enter | Tidies the typed number (clamps and rounds it) |

## Props

Every Input prop works (`size`, `invalid`, `startIcon`, `prefix`, `suffix`, `placeholder`, `disabled`, `readOnly`…), except `type` and `endIcon`. A `suffix` such as "kg" or "%" sits before the steppers.

| Prop | Type | Default | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | string | none | Goes to the native `<input>` (not the wrapper), so a `<label htmlFor>` or a Field can point at it. |
| `value` | `number \| null` | | Controlled. `null` is an empty field. After a step, Enter or blur the field shows `value`, so a parent that keeps or changes the number it gets is what people see. |
| `defaultValue` | `number \| null` | | Uncontrolled. |
| `onValueChange` | `(value: number \| null) => void` | | As people type (numbers within range), on blur (clamped), and from the keys and buttons. |
| `min`, `max` | `number` | | Limits. The field snaps into them when it loses focus. |
| `onInvalidInput` | `(text: string, reason: 'range' \| 'unreadable') => void` | | When typed text isn't kept as it is: a number brought back within `min`..`max`, or text that isn't a number. The same words show under the field (`.srp-input-rejected`, read with it) until the text changes. |
| `step` | `number` | `1` | How much the arrows and buttons change it. Its decimals set how many the value keeps. |
| `largeStep` | `number` | `10` | Steps moved by PageUp, PageDown and Shift with an arrow. |
| `steppers` | `boolean` | `true` | The − and + buttons. |
| `decrementLabel`, `incrementLabel` | `string` | `'Decrease'`, `'Increase'` | The buttons' names. |
| `locale` | `string` | the nearest `SerupaProvider`'s, else the browser's | Whose decimal and group marks are read and written: `1.500,25` in `id-ID`, `1,500.25` in `en-US`. When it differs from the provider's, the field carries `lang`. |
| `currency` | `string` | | An ISO 4217 code: shows the amount as money and keeps its decimals. Short for `formatOptions={{ style: 'currency', currency }}`; `formatOptions` still wins. |
| `minorUnits` | `boolean` | `false` | With `currency`: the value props and `onValueChange` are whole minor units (cents). `aria-valuenow` stays in the currency's units. |
| `formatOptions` | `Intl.NumberFormatOptions` | no grouping | How the number is shown: `{ style: 'currency', currency: 'IDR' }`, `{ useGrouping: true }`, `{ style: 'percent' }` (the value is the fraction, so 0.15 shows 15%; it keeps the decimals the format shows and steps one percent unless `step` says otherwise), `{ style: 'unit', unit: 'kilometer' }` (set `step` for decimals: with the default step of 1, 2.5 km is 3 km), or `currencySign: 'accounting'` (a negative in parentheses, read back as negative). `notation: 'compact'` is for showing only: a typed "1.5K" reads as 1.5. Sets `aria-valuetext` too. |
| `numberingSystem` | string | the locale's | The digits the value is written in: `"latn"` for Latin, `"arab"` for Arabic-Indic. Typed digits are read in any script either way |

`className` and `style` go to the box; `ref` and every other prop go to the `<input>`.

## Component tokens

Each is an optional override: set it on the page, a container or one field. The box uses Input's tokens. The list lives in `src/components/NumberInput/number-input.tokens.json` (also in `design-tokens/components/`).

<!-- token-table:start (made from number-input.tokens.json by npm run tokens: edit the descriptions there) -->
| Token | Default | Use |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--number-input-stepper` | `text-muted` | The − and + icons (3:1 on the field). |
| `--number-input-stepper-hover` | `text` | The icons on hover. |
| `--number-input-stepper-bg-hover` | `field-hover` | The buttons' background on hover. |
| `--number-input-stepper-bg-pressed` | `field-pressed` | A step button's background while it's held down, one step past hover. |
| `--number-input-text-disabled` | `disabled-text` | Disabled: the text, icon or mark, in place of fading it (3:1 or more on its background, more with more contrast). |
| `--number-input-stepper-radius` | `radius-inner` | The buttons' corners (4px). |
| `--number-input-stepper-padding` | `spacing-1` | Space around each button's icon (4px). |
| `--number-input-stepper-gap` | `spacing-0.5` | Space between the − and + buttons (2px). |
<!-- token-table:end -->

components.name: OfflineBanner
components.summary: Says when the connection drops and when it comes back, on screen and to screen readers.
components.guide:
# OfflineBanner

Says when the connection drops and when it comes back, on screen and to screen readers. Put one in the app's layout: it shows nothing while the app is online.

**Also called:** connection banner, offline indicator.

```tsx
import { OfflineBanner } from "@diki-stwn/serupa-ds";

<OfflineBanner />
<OfflineBanner>Changes are kept and sent when you're back.</OfflineBanner>
<OfflineBanner online={!syncFailing} placement="top" onOnlineChange={(online) => online && sync()} />
```

## When to use

- Any app people use on the move or keep open for hours, where a dropped connection would otherwise show up as buttons that do nothing.
- An app that keeps working offline, to say what still works and that changes will be sent later.

## When not to use

- To report one request that failed: say it where it failed, with an [Alert] (npx serupa-docs Alert) or a [Toast] (npx serupa-docs Toast) and a way to try again.
- For the save state of one document: use [SaveStatus] (npx serupa-docs SaveStatus).

## Anatomy

Drawn from the `WithMoreWords` story.

1. **Bar** (`.srp-offline-banner`): the raised surface, fixed to an edge of the screen or in the page.
2. **Icon** (`.srp-offline-banner__icon`): a cloud crossed out while offline, a cloud with a check once it's back.
3. **Words** (`.srp-offline-banner__text`): the title, "You’re offline" or "Back online" (`.srp-offline-banner__title`), and your own words after it.

## Usage

- Put it once, near the root of the app. It follows `navigator.onLine` and the browser's `online` and `offline` events.
- The browser only knows whether there's a network, not whether your server answers: on a café's sign-in page or a dead mobile connection it can say online. When your requests keep failing, set `online={false}` yourself, and leave the prop out again (or set `true`) when they work.
- Add words after "You’re offline" as children: what still works, or what happens to their changes. Keep it to a sentence.
- It's fixed to the bottom of the screen, in the middle, by default; `placement="top"` puts it at the top, where a bottom navigation bar or a chat box sits. `placement="inline"` keeps it where you put it, under a header, say.
- `onOnlineChange` runs when the connection drops (`false`) and comes back (`true`): a good moment to send what was waiting.
- Rendered on the server it shows nothing (the server is online); in the browser it shows straight away if the page loaded offline.

## Behavior

- Offline, the bar slides in from its edge and stays until the connection comes back.
- Back online, it says "Back online" with a success icon for 2 seconds, then slides away.
- With reduced motion, it fades without sliding.

### Do and don't

- **Do:** Add one sentence after "You're offline": what still works, or what happens to their changes. (`WithMoreWords`)
- **Don't:** Explain at length: people don't read a paragraph in a banner. (`DontParagraph`)

## Accessibility

- **Announcements:** "You’re offline" and "Back online" are said once each through the polite live region the components share, which moves into an open Dialog or Drawer so they're heard there too. The bar isn't a live region itself, so it isn't read twice.
- **Role and name:** a plain `<div>`, with an icon screen readers skip and the words.
- **Keyboard:** none: nothing in it takes focus. It never covers a focused control's place in the tab order, nor the control itself: while a fixed bar shows, a field Tab moves to (or a #link jumps to) scrolls into view clear of it (WCAG 2.4.11), and the bar adds its room to that end of the page (the start for a top bar, the end for a bottom one) so the first or last field can scroll clear too. With a sticky Navbar, a top bar sits just below it, so the Navbar's links and Menu button stay in reach, and the room counts both.
- **Contrast:** its words read 4.5:1 and its icons 3:1 on its background in every theme (`OfflineBanner.test.tsx`).
- **What's still yours:** keep what people typed while offline, and don't let buttons that need the server look like they worked. A fixed bar covers the bottom of the page: leave room for it, or use `placement="top"` or `"inline"`, where it would cover something people need.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | `string` | | Goes to the `<div>`. |
| `online` | `boolean` | follows the browser | Set it when the app knows better than `navigator.onLine`. |
| `placement` | `'bottom' \| 'top' \| 'inline'` | `'bottom'` | Fixed to an edge of the screen, in the middle, or in the page. |
| `children` | `ReactNode` | | More words after "You’re offline". |
| `onOnlineChange` | `(online: boolean) => void` | | Runs when it drops and when it comes back. |

`className`, `ref` and other props go to the `<div>`, which has `data-component="offline-banner"` and `data-state="offline"` or `"back"`.

## Component tokens

Each is an optional override: set it on the page, a container or one OfflineBanner. The list lives in `src/components/OfflineBanner/offline-banner.tokens.json` (also in `design-tokens/components/`).

<!-- token-table:start (made from offline-banner.tokens.json by npm run tokens: edit the descriptions there) -->
| Token | Default | Use |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--offline-banner-bg` | `surface-overlay` | The bar's background. |
| `--offline-banner-border-color` | `border-overlay` | Its border. |
| `--offline-banner-text` | `text` | The words (4.5:1 on bg). |
| `--offline-banner-icon` | `text-muted` | The icon while offline (3:1 on bg). |
| `--offline-banner-icon-online` | `success` | The icon once it's back online (3:1 on bg). |
| `--offline-banner-shadow` | `elevation-overlay` | Its shadow, which lifts it off the page. |
| `--offline-banner-radius` | `radius-surface` | The corners (8px). |
| `--offline-banner-padding-x` | `spacing-4` | Space inside, at the start and end (16px). |
| `--offline-banner-padding-y` | `spacing-2` | Space inside, above and below (8px). |
| `--offline-banner-gap` | `spacing-2` | Between the icon and the words (8px). |
| `--offline-banner-offset` | `spacing-4` | From the edge of the screen when fixed (16px). |
| `--offline-banner-z-index` | `z-toast` | Its stacking level when fixed: with the toasts, over the page and its dialogs. |
<!-- token-table:end -->

components.name: PageSection
components.summary: One full-width band of a long page, such as a landing page's hero, features, pricing or questions.
components.guide:
# PageSection

One full-width band of a long page, such as a landing page's hero, features, pricing or questions. It gives the band its background, its space above and below, and keeps its content to a Container's width, spaced in a column.

**Also called:** section, band, strip, hero.

```tsx
import { PageSection, Heading, Button } from "@diki-stwn/serupa-ds";

<PageSection spacing="lg" align="center" size="md" aria-labelledby="hero">
  <Heading level={1} id="hero">Plan the work. Ship it together.</Heading>
  <Button size="lg">Start free</Button>
</PageSection>

<PageSection tone="muted" divider aria-labelledby="features">…</PageSection>
```

## When to use

- The bands of a marketing or landing page: a hero, features, pricing, questions, a closing call to action.
- Any long page split into parts that each span the page, such as a help center's home.

## When not to use

- A group of related content inside an app's page: use a [Card] (npx serupa-docs Card), or a heading and a [Stack] (npx serupa-docs Stack).
- A page's width alone, with no band: use [Container] (npx serupa-docs Container) instead.
- A short centered page, such as sign-in: use [Center] (npx serupa-docs Center) instead.

## Anatomy

Drawn from the `Playground` story.

1. **Band** (`.srp-page-section`): the full-width `<section>`, with its tone, its spacing above and below, and its divider.
2. **Inner box** (`.srp-page-section__inner`): the Container inside the band, which keeps the content to `size` and lays it out with `gap`.

## Usage

- Alternate `tone="plain"` and `tone="muted"` down a long page, so each band reads as its own. Add `divider` between two plain bands.
- Use `spacing="lg"` for the hero, `md` (the default) for the bands below it, and `sm` for a short one, such as a row of logos.
- Give every band on a page the same `size`, unless it's a hero or a closing call to action, which read better narrower (`md`) and centered (`align="center"`).
- The band's children are spaced 32px apart (`gap`); lay out what's inside each child with a Stack or a Grid.

### Do and don't

- **Do:** Alternate plain and muted bands, so each part of a long page reads as its own. (`DoAlternate`)
- **Don't:** Put two muted bands one after the other: the edge between them disappears. (`DontSameTone`)

## Accessibility

- **Role and name:** a `<section>` by default. Name it with `aria-labelledby` pointing at its heading, so it's a region people can jump to. Use `as="div"` for a band with no heading of its own.
- **Keyboard:** none: a layout box, not focusable.
- **Contrast:** text and muted text read 4.5:1 on the muted band in every theme (`PageSection.test.tsx`).
- **Reflow:** the content wraps inside the Container's width, so nothing scrolls sideways at 320px (WCAG 1.4.10).
- **What's still yours:** one h1 on the page (in the hero), and headings that go down a level at a time in the bands below it.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | string | none | Goes to the band's element (`as`), so a link can point at the section. |
| `tone` | `'plain'` \| `'muted'` | `'plain'` | The page's own background, or a step below it |
| `divider` | boolean | `false` | A line across the top |
| `spacing` | `'sm'` \| `'md'` \| `'lg'` | `'md'` | Space above and below: 32px; 48px, 64px from 768px; 64px, 96px from 768px |
| `size` | `'prose'` \| `'md'` \| `'lg'` \| `'xl'` \| `'2xl'` \| `'full'` | `'xl'` | The content's width, a [Container] (npx serupa-docs Container) size |
| `align` | `'start'` \| `'center'` | `'start'` | Centers the content and its lines of text |
| `gap` | a spacing step: `0` to `24` | `8` (32px) | The space between the children |
| `as` | `'section'` \| `'div'` \| `'header'` \| `'footer'` \| `'aside'` | `'section'` | The element |

A value that isn't on the list falls back to the default. `className`, `style`, `ref` and everything else go to the outer element, which has `data-component="page-section"`; the content is in a Container with `.srp-page-section__inner`.

## Component tokens

Each is an optional override: set it on the page, a container or one PageSection. The list lives in `src/components/PageSection/page-section.tokens.json` (also in `design-tokens/components/`).

<!-- token-table:start (made from page-section.tokens.json by npm run tokens: edit the descriptions there) -->
| Token | Default | Use |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--page-section-bg-muted` | `surface-muted` | The background with tone="muted". |
| `--page-section-border` | `border` | The line on top with divider. |
| `--page-section-padding-y-sm` | `spacing-8` | Space above and below with spacing="sm" (32px). |
| `--page-section-padding-y-md` | `spacing-12` | Space above and below with spacing="md", below 768px (48px). |
| `--page-section-padding-y-md-wide` | `spacing-16` | Space above and below with spacing="md", from 768px (64px). |
| `--page-section-padding-y-lg` | `spacing-16` | Space above and below with spacing="lg", below 768px (64px). |
| `--page-section-padding-y-lg-wide` | `spacing-24` | Space above and below with spacing="lg", from 768px (96px). |
| `--page-section-gap` | `spacing-8` | The space between the children when gap isn't given (32px). |
<!-- token-table:end -->

components.name: Pagination
components.summary: Moves through pages of results: previous and next arrows around the page numbers, with … where pages are skipped.
components.guide:
# Pagination

Moves through pages of results: previous and next arrows around the page numbers, with … where pages are skipped. It always shows the same number of slots, so the arrows stay put as the page changes. Pages are buttons, or links with `getHref` when each page has its own URL.

**Also called:** pager.

```jsx
import { Pagination } from '@diki-stwn/serupa-ds';

const [page, setPage] = React.useState(1);
<Pagination count={totalPages} page={page} onPageChange={setPage} />

// Each page has a URL (server rendering, shareable links)
<Pagination count={20} page={page} getHref={(n) => `/orders?page=${n}`} />

<Pagination count={8} size="sm" siblings={0} />

// Which items show: "21–30 of 245" before the pages
<Pagination count={25} page={3} total={245} pageSize={10} />

// …and a page-size select
<Pagination count={Math.ceil(245 / per)} page={page} onPageChange={setPage} total={245} pageSize={per}
  pageSizeOptions={[10, 25, 50]} onPageSizeChange={(n, { page: p }) => { setPer(n); setPage(p); }} />
```

## When to use

- Long lists or tables of results split into pages, where people jump to a page or come back to one: orders, search results, logs.
- Results where each page should have its own URL, to share, bookmark or render on the server.

## When not to use

- A feed people scroll through without caring which page they're on: use a "Load more" [Button] (npx serupa-docs Button) under the list instead.
- Steps of a task done in order: use [Stepper] (npx serupa-docs Stepper) instead.
- A few views of the same thing: use [Tabs] (npx serupa-docs Tabs) instead.

## Anatomy

Drawn from the `PageSize` story.

1. **Summary** (`.srp-pagination__summary`): which items are shown of how many.
2. **Previous and next** (`.srp-pagination__arrow`): go one page back or forward.
3. **Page** (`.srp-pagination__item`): a page to go to.
4. **Current page** (`.srp-pagination__item--current`): the page you're on.
5. **Gap** (`.srp-pagination__ellipsis`): stands for the pages not shown.
6. **Page size** (`.srp-pagination__page-size`): how many items a page holds.

## Usage

- Put it under the list or table it pages through.
- When pages have URLs, pass `getHref` so every page is a link; clicks still call `onPageChange`. They go through your router's link set with `configure({ link })`, or `linkAs`.
- The row stays on one line. When it's wider than its box (the defaults need about 340px), it shows fewer `siblings` and then fewer `boundaries` until it fits, and goes back to what you asked when there's room again. The arrows stay at the ends either way. Within one width the number of slots stays the same, so the arrows don't move as you page. `size="sm"` fits more.
- Page numbers are written in the digits of the locale from `SerupaProvider` (or the browser), as Calendar writes its
  days: ١ ٢ ٣ in Egyptian Arabic, ۱ ۲ ۳ in Persian. A page's name comes from `pageLabel`, so translate it with the
  other labels.

- With `total` and `pageSize`, a summary before the pages says which items show: "21–30 of 245", in the locale's digits and grouping ("1.001–1.010 dari 12.345" in id-ID). The pages sit at the end of the row, and wrap under the summary when both don't fit on one line. Change its words with the `itemsOf` label.
- With `pageSizeOptions` (and `pageSize`), an "Items per page" select after the summary offers the sizes, in the locale's digits. Picking one calls `onPageSizeChange(size, page)` with the page that keeps the first item shown in view: page 5 at 10 a page starts with item 41, which is on page 2 at 25 a page. Set both; an uncontrolled `page` moves by itself. Change its label with the `perPage` label.

`paginationRange(page, count, siblings, boundaries)` returns the same list of pages and ellipses, for building your own.

### Do and don't

- **Do:** Pass `total` and `pageSize`, so people see how many items there are and which ones show. (`DoShowTotal`)
- **Don't:** Show pagination when everything fits on one page: leave it out instead. (`DontOnePage`)

## Accessibility

- It's a `<nav>` landmark named "Pagination" with a list. The current page has `aria-current="page"`; the ellipses are hidden from screen readers.
- At the first or last page the arrow is disabled (a link loses its `href` and gets `aria-disabled`).
- Pages, also on hover, the current page and the ellipsis keep 4.5:1 in the six themes the tests draw (blue, yellow and violet, light and dark) (`Pagination.test.tsx`).
- The arrows point the other way in right-to-left text. They follow the nearest `dir`, so a `dir="ltr"` block on a right-to-left page keeps left-to-right arrows.
- After a page change, move focus to the top of the new results (or announce them) so keyboard and screen reader users know the list changed.

### Keyboard

| Key | Does |
| --- | --- |
| Tab | To each page, the arrows and any link or button in it; a disabled arrow is skipped |
| Enter | Goes to that page (Space too, when the pages are buttons) |

An arrow that takes you to the first or last page turns disabled, so focus moves to the other arrow instead of falling back to the top of the page.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | string | none | Goes to the root `<nav>`. |
| `count` | number | required | How many pages there are |
| `page` | number | none | The current page, from 1 (controlled) |
| `defaultPage` | number | `1` | The page it starts on when uncontrolled |
| `onPageChange` | `(page) => void` | none | Called with the new page |
| `getHref` | `(page) => string` | none | Makes every page a link. Clicks still call `onPageChange` |
| `linkAs` | a component | the `configure({ link })` link, else `'a'` | With `getHref`, your router's link component for the page links (it gets `href`, `className` and the rest). The disabled arrows stay plain `<a>` |
| `siblings` | number | `1` | Pages on each side of the current one |
| `boundaries` | number | `1` | Pages always shown at each end |
| `size` | `'sm'` \| `'md'` \| `'lg'` | `'md'` | 24px, 32px or 44px squares; `lg` has 16px text and a large page-size select, to sit beside large fields and buttons. On a touch screen every size takes a press 44px high, and the gap between two pages splits at its middle |
| `aria-label` | string | `"Pagination"` | The nav's name |
| `previousLabel`, `nextLabel` | string | `"Previous page"`, `"Next page"` | The arrows' names |
| `pageLabel` | `(page) => string` | `"Page " + page` | A page's name |
| `total` | number | none | How many items there are in all. With `pageSize`, shows the summary |
| `pageSize` | number | none | How many items a page holds. With `total`, shows the summary |
| `pageSizeOptions` | number[] | none | The page sizes to offer in an "Items per page" select after the summary. Needs `pageSize` |
| `onPageSizeChange` | (pageSize, details: { page }) => void | none | Called with the size picked, and details: `page` is the page that keeps the first item shown in view |
| `jump` | boolean | `false` | A "Go to page" number field after the pages, for long lists: Enter goes to the page typed (one out of range goes to the nearest end), and the page is said, since focus stays in the field. With `getHref` and no `onPageChange`, it follows that page's link. Not shown for one page |

`className`, `style`, `ref` and everything else go to the `<nav>`, which has `data-component="pagination"`.

## Component tokens

Each is an optional override: set it on the page, a container or one pagination. The list lives in `src/components/Pagination/pagination.tokens.json` (also in `design-tokens/components/`).

<!-- token-table:start (made from pagination.tokens.json by npm run tokens: edit the descriptions there) -->
**Colors**

| Token | Default | Use |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--pagination-text` | `text` | A page number and the arrows. |
| `--pagination-bg-hover` | `secondary` | A page or arrow on hover. |
| `--pagination-bg-pressed` | `pressed` | A page or arrow while it's pressed, one step past hover. |
| `--pagination-bg-current` | `primary` | The current page's background. |
| `--pagination-text-current` | `on-primary` | The current page's number (4.5:1 on current-bg). |
| `--pagination-ellipsis` | `text-muted` | The … between page ranges (4.5:1 on surface). |
| `--pagination-focus-ring` | `focus-ring` | The keyboard focus ring. |
| `--pagination-summary` | `text-muted` | The summary with total and pageSize, "21–30 of 245" (4.5:1 on surface). |
| `--pagination-text-disabled` | `disabled-text` | Previous or next when there's no page that way (3:1 or more on the page). |
| `--pagination-edge-current` | `primary-edge` | The current page's 1px edge inside its fill (Yellow Light; transparent where the fill is 3:1 on the page) |

**Type**

| --- | --- | --- |
| `--pagination-font-size` | `text-sm` | Page numbers (14px). |
| `--pagination-weight-current` | `font-semibold` | The current page's weight (600). |

**Sizing**

| --- | --- | --- |
| `--pagination-size` | `control-height-md` | A page's width and height at size md (32px). |
| `--pagination-size-sm` | `control-height-sm` | At size sm (24px). |

**Spacing**

components.name: PasswordInput
components.summary: A password field with a button at the end that shows and hides what was typed, so people can check it before they submit.
components.guide:
# PasswordInput

A password field with a button at the end that shows and hides what was typed, so people can check it before they submit. It's Input's box, so it has the same sizes, states and tokens.

**Also called:** password field, show password field.

```jsx
import { PasswordInput, Field } from '@diki-stwn/serupa-ds';

<Field label="Password"><PasswordInput /></Field>

// Sign-up: let the password manager suggest one
<Field label="New password" hint="At least 12 characters"><PasswordInput autoComplete="new-password" /></Field>

<PasswordInput revealed={shown} onRevealedChange={setShown} />
```

## When to use

- Signing in, signing up, and changing a password.
- Any secret people type and may want to check before they submit, such as a PIN.

## When not to use

- Text that isn't secret: use [Input] (npx serupa-docs Input).

## Anatomy

Drawn from the `CapsLockOn` story.

1. **Field** (`.srp-input__field`): where the password is typed, hidden as dots.
2. **Show password** (`.srp-password-input__toggle`): shows and hides what was typed.

## Usage

- Label it with [Field] (npx serupa-docs Field), and put the password rules in the hint ("At least 12 characters"), not only in an error.
- Set `autoComplete="new-password"` when people create a password, so password managers suggest one; the default suits sign-in.
- Match the `size` to the other fields in the form.
- A press anywhere on the box other than the reveal button, such as on the icon or the side padding, focuses the field with the caret at the end, as Input's box does.

### Do and don't

- **Do:** Put the password rules in the hint, so people see them before they type. (`InAField`)
- **Don't:** Show the rules only in an error: people learn them by failing. (`DontRulesOnlyInError`)

## States

| State | Look |
| --- | --- |
| Rest | `field` background, 1px `field-border`, the eye button in `text-muted` |
| Hover | `field-border-hover`; the eye under the pointer takes a `field-hover` fill, `field-pressed` while pressed |
| Focus | Like Input: the border and a 1px ring hugging it in `focus-ring` (2px in all), and a visible outline in forced-colors mode |
| Caps Lock on | While it has focus, a caps-lock icon shows before the eye |
| Invalid | `danger` border, and a `danger` focus ring |
| Read-only | `field-readonly` background, no hover change; still focusable and selectable; the eye still shows and hides the password |
| Disabled | `field-readonly` background, `disabled-border` edge and `disabled-text` at full opacity, `not-allowed` cursor; the eye is off |

## Accessibility

- The show/hide button takes presses over at least 24px (WCAG 2.5.8), even at size `sm` where it's 22px: a box behind it reaches past its edges without moving anything.
- The button is named "Show password" and has `aria-pressed`, so screen readers say whether the password is shown. Its `aria-controls` points at the field when the field has an `id` (Field gives it one).
- Clicking it keeps focus in the field, so typing carries on. It's also reachable with Tab, and Enter or Space press it.
- Spell check and auto-capitalization are off, so a shown password isn't underlined or changed.
- Showing or hiding the password keeps the caret and any selection where they were (changing the field's type would put the caret at the start), so typing goes on where it stopped. In a long password the field also stays scrolled to the caret, rather than jumping back to the start.
- While Caps Lock is on and the field has focus, a caps-lock icon shows before the eye. Its words, "Caps Lock is on", are its tooltip, join the field's description and are read out once (the `capsLockOn` label). It goes away when Caps Lock is turned off or focus leaves. `capsLockHint={false}` turns it off.
- Pasting is never blocked, so a password manager or a copied password can fill the field (WCAG 3.3.8, accessible authentication). Don't add an `onPaste` that prevents it.
- The text keeps 4.5:1 and the eye icon 3:1 on the field in every theme (`PasswordInput.test.tsx`).

### Keyboard

| Key | Does |
| --- | --- |
| Tab | To the field, then to the show and hide button |
| Enter, Space | On the button: show or hide the password; focus stays on the button |
| Caps Lock | While the field has focus: shows a caps-lock icon and reads out "Caps Lock is on" |

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | string | none | Goes to the native `<input>` (not the wrapper), so a `<label htmlFor>` or a Field can point at it. |
| `revealed` | boolean | none | Shows the password as text (controlled) |
| `defaultRevealed` | boolean | `false` | Shows it at first (uncontrolled) |
| `onRevealedChange` | `(revealed) => void` | none | Called when the button is pressed |
| `toggleLabel` | string | `"Show password"` | The button's name |
| `size` | `'sm'` \| `'md'` \| `'lg'` | `'md'` | 24, 32 or 44px, like Input |
| `invalid` | boolean | `false` | A danger border and `aria-invalid` |
| `startIcon` | an icon name or element | none | A decorative icon before the text |
| `capsLockHint` | boolean | `true` | Shows a caps-lock icon and reads out "Caps Lock is on" while it is |

`autoComplete` defaults to `"current-password"`; use `"new-password"` when creating one. `ref`, `value`, `onChange` and every other input attribute go to the `<input>`; `className` and `style` go to the box, which has `data-component="password-input"`.

## Component tokens

The field uses Input's tokens. These style the show/hide button; each is an optional override. The list lives in `src/components/PasswordInput/password-input.tokens.json` (also in `design-tokens/components/`).

<!-- token-table:start (made from password-input.tokens.json by npm run tokens: edit the descriptions there) -->
| Token | Default | Use |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--password-input-toggle` | `text-muted` | The show/hide button's icon (3:1 on the field). |
| `--password-input-toggle-hover` | `text` | The icon on hover. |
| `--password-input-toggle-bg-hover` | `field-hover` | The button's background on hover. |
| `--password-input-toggle-bg-pressed` | `field-pressed` | The show/hide button's background while it's held down, one step past hover. |
| `--password-input-focus-ring` | `focus-ring` | The button's keyboard focus ring. |
| `--password-input-caps` | `placeholder` | The Caps Lock icon (3:1 or more on the field). |
| `--password-input-toggle-radius` | `radius-inner` | The button's corners (4px). |
| `--password-input-toggle-padding` | `spacing-1` | Space around the button's icon (4px). |
<!-- token-table:end -->

components.name: PeriodPicker
components.summary: A month, a quarter or a year, picked from a grid: for a report's month, a billing period or a dashboard's quarter.
components.guide:
# PeriodPicker

A month, a quarter or a year, picked from a grid: for a report's month, a billing period or a dashboard's quarter. It looks like a [Select] (npx serupa-docs Select) and opens a popup with the year between two arrows over 12 months, 4 quarters or 12 years. The button shows the period in words ("November 2026", "Q4 2026", "2026") and a form gets it as `2026-11`, `2026-Q4` or `2026`.

**Also called:** month picker, month and year picker, quarter picker, fiscal period selector.

```jsx
import { PeriodPicker, Field } from '@diki-stwn/serupa-ds';

<Field label="Report month">
  <PeriodPicker name="month" value={month} onValueChange={(value, { range }) => setMonth(value)} />
</Field>

// a quarter, no earlier than the first one on record and no later than this one
<PeriodPicker aria-label="Quarter" unit="quarter" min="2023-Q1" max="2026-Q4" defaultValue="2026-Q4" />

// a fiscal year
<PeriodPicker aria-label="Fiscal year" unit="year" name="year" />
```

## When to use

- A whole month, quarter or year is the answer: a statement, an invoice period, a report, a target.
- Filters on a dashboard or a report page where the data is kept by month or quarter.

## When not to use

- A day: use a [DatePicker] (npx serupa-docs DatePicker), or a [DateField] (npx serupa-docs DateField) for one people know by heart.
- Any span of days, such as "the last 30 days" or a trip: use a [DateRangePicker] (npx serupa-docs DateRangePicker).
- A month and year people know by heart, far from now (a card's expiry date): two [Selects] (npx serupa-docs Select) or typed fields are quicker than paging.

## Anatomy

Drawn from the `Months` story.

1. **Button** (`.srp-period-picker__button`): the chosen period in words, or the placeholder, and a calendar icon at the end.
2. **Popup** (`.srp-period-picker__panel`): a dialog named "Choose a month" (or quarter, or year).
3. **Header** (`.srp-period-picker__header`): the year, or the twelve years shown, between the arrows to the page before and after.
4. **Period** (`.srp-period-picker__period`): one month, quarter or year in the grid. The chosen one is filled with `primary`, the current one is `primary` text in semibold, and ones outside `min` and `max` are faded and struck through.

## Usage

- Pick the `unit` the data is kept in. People can't choose half a quarter, so don't offer months when the report only exists by quarter.
- Set `min` and `max` to the periods that have data: no period before the account was opened, none in the future for a statement.
- `onValueChange` gets the value and the period's first and last days (local midnight), ready for a query: `{ start: 1 Nov 2026, end: 30 Nov 2026 }`.
- Months are named in the locale ("November 2026", "Dezember 2025", "Agustus 2025") and years in its digits. A quarter's short name comes from the labels: "Q4" in English, "K4" in Indonesian.
- Years page twelve at a time, from a year that divides by 12 (2016 to 2027, 2028 to 2039), so the same year is always in the same place.

### Do and don't

- **Do:** Keep it to the periods that have data: a statement from the month the account opened to this one. (`DoBoundToData`)
- **Don't:** Offer every month: people pick a month with no statement, or one still to come, and get an empty page. (`DontOpenEnded`)

## States

| State | Look |
| --- | --- |
| Rest | `field` background, 1px `field-border`, the icon in `text-muted` |
| Placeholder | "Choose a month" (or `placeholder`) in the `placeholder` color |
| Hover | `field-border-hover`; a period under the pointer is `secondary`, as in Calendar |
| Focus | Like the other fields: the border and a 1px ring hugging it take the `focus-ring` color (danger when invalid), and stay while the popup is open; a period in the popup gets an outline |
| Open | The popup under the button (above it when there's no room), fading in |
| Invalid | `danger` border, and `aria-invalid` |
| Read-only | `field-readonly` background; it doesn't open |
| Disabled | `field-readonly` background, `disabled-border` edge and `disabled-text` at full opacity, `not-allowed` cursor; it doesn't open |

## Accessibility

- **Role and name:** the button is a `combobox` with `aria-haspopup="dialog"` and `aria-expanded`, named by a Field, a `<label>` or `aria-label`, and it reads the chosen period in words. The popup is a `dialog`; its grid is named by the year over it, which is announced when it changes. Each period is a button named in full ("February 2025", "Q1 2025"), the chosen one's cell is `aria-selected`, the current one is `aria-current="date"`, and ones outside `min` and `max` are `aria-disabled`.
- **Long values:** a period or placeholder that doesn't fit (a long month name in a narrow field) ends in an ellipsis and shows whole on hover and on the button's keyboard focus ([TruncatedText] (npx serupa-docs TruncatedText)); the button reads all of it.
- **Keyboard:** see the table. Focus moves into the grid when it opens, onto the chosen period (else the current one), and back to the button when it closes. In right-to-left text the left and right arrows swap.
- **Contrast:** text and placeholder keep 4.5:1 on `field`, the icon 3:1; periods and the year 4.5:1 on the popup, the chosen one on `primary` and the current one in `primary`, in every theme (`PeriodPicker.test.tsx`). The resting border is soft on purpose (`field-border`: about 1.5:1 in light, 1.4:1 to 1.9:1 in dark), under the 3:1 WCAG 1.4.11 asks of a control's edge: a deliberate design exception. The label above the field, its fill in dark, the stronger border on hover and the 3:1 focus ring mark it, and more contrast (`data-contrast="more"` or the system setting) brings back a 3:1+ border.
- **What's still yours:** a name for it (Field, `<label>` or `aria-label`), and the error text when a required period is missing.

### Keyboard

| Key | Does |
| --- | --- |
| Enter, Space, ↓, ↑ (on the button) | Opens the popup |
| ← → | The period before or after, onto the page before or after past its ends |
| ↑ ↓ | The same place a row up or down |
| Home, End | The row's first or last period |
| PageUp, PageDown | A year back or on (twelve years for years) |
| Enter, Space | Chooses the period and closes |
| Escape | Closes without a change |

Keys stop at `min` and `max`.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `unit` | `'month'` \| `'quarter'` \| `'year'` | `'month'` | What is chosen |
| `value` | string \| null | | The chosen period (controlled): `"2026-11"`, `"2026-Q4"` or `"2026"` |
| `defaultValue` | string \| null | | The period it starts with (uncontrolled), written the same way |
| `onValueChange` | `(value, details: { range: { start, end } }) => void` | | Called with the picked period, and details: `range` is its first and last days |
| `min`, `max` | string | | The earliest and latest periods that can be chosen, written as `value` is |
| `locale` | string | the provider's, else the browser's | Month names and digits |
| `placeholder` | string | "Choose a month" | Shown with nothing chosen |
| `size` | `'sm'` \| `'md'` \| `'lg'` | `'md'` | 24, 32 or 44px, like Select |
| `invalid` | boolean | `false` | A danger border and `aria-invalid`; set for you in a Field with an error |
| `required` | boolean | `false` | A period must be chosen: `aria-required` on the button, and the form isn't sent without one (the button is marked invalid and takes focus). A required Field sets only `aria-required`, as it does on an Input |
| `name` | string | | A form gets the value under it, and a form reset brings back `defaultValue` |
| `open` | boolean | | Whether the popup shows (controlled), with `onOpenChange`. Opened this way, focus stays where it is |
| `defaultOpen` | boolean | `false` | Shows the popup open at first, without moving focus into it |
| `onOpenChange` | (open, { reason }) => void | | Called when the popup asks to open or close, and why |
| `disabled` | boolean | `false` | It can't open, and the form doesn't get its value |
| `readOnly` | boolean | `false` | Shows the period but can't open: focusable and read out (`aria-readonly`), and the form still gets its value, unlike `disabled` |

`ref`, `id`, `aria-*` and other props go to the `<button>`; `className` and `style` go to the wrapper (`data-component="period-picker"`, `data-state`, `data-unit`), full width by default.

## Component tokens

Each is an optional override: set it on the page, a container or one PeriodPicker. The list lives in `src/components/PeriodPicker/period-picker.tokens.json` (also in `design-tokens/components/`).

<!-- token-table:start (made from period-picker.tokens.json by npm run tokens: edit the descriptions there) -->
**Colors**

| Token | Default | Use |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--period-picker-bg` | `field` | The button's background. |
| `--period-picker-text` | `text` | The chosen period on the button, and the popup's text (4.5:1 on both backgrounds). |
| `--period-picker-placeholder` | `placeholder` | The placeholder on the button. |
| `--period-picker-border` | `field-border` | The button's outline (3:1 on the page). |
| `--period-picker-border-hover` | `field-border-hover` | The button's outline on hover. |
| `--period-picker-invalid` | `field-border-invalid` | The outline and focus ring when invalid. |
| `--period-picker-bg-disabled` | `field-readonly` | The button's background when read-only or disabled. |
| `--period-picker-icon` | `text-muted` | The calendar icon on the button. |
| `--period-picker-focus-ring` | `focus-ring` | The focus ring, on the button and on a period. |
| `--period-picker-panel-bg` | `surface-overlay` | The popup's background. |
| `--period-picker-panel-border` | `border-overlay` | The popup's outline. |
| `--period-picker-period-bg-hover` | `secondary` | A period under the pointer, as in Calendar: a step lighter than the panel in dark, before pressed. |
| `--period-picker-period-bg-pressed` | `pressed` | A period while pressed. |
| `--period-picker-current` | `primary-text` | This month, quarter or year (4.5:1 on panel-bg). |
| `--period-picker-bg-selected` | `primary` | The chosen period's fill. |
| `--period-picker-text-selected` | `on-primary` | The chosen period's text (4.5:1 on selected-bg). |
| `--period-picker-border-disabled` | `disabled-border` | Disabled: the edge. |
| `--period-picker-text-disabled` | `disabled-text` | Disabled: the text, icon or mark, in place of fading it (3:1 or more on its background, more with more contrast). |
| `--period-picker-panel-divider` | `border-overlay` | What a divider or separator inside it reads as `border`: its own edge color, since in dark `border` is the surface's own color and a line in it vanished |
| `--period-picker-edge-selected` | `primary-edge` | The selected period's 1px edge inside its fill (Yellow Light; transparent where the fill is 3:1 on the page) |

**Radius**

| --- | --- | --- |
| `--period-picker-radius` | `radius-control` | The button's corners. |
| `--period-picker-panel-radius` | `radius-surface` | The popup's corners. |
| `--period-picker-period-radius` | `radius-control` | A period's corners. |

**Shadow**

| Token | Default | Use |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--period-picker-panel-shadow` | `elevation-overlay` | The popup's shadow. |

**Spacing**

| Token | Default | Use |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--period-picker-padding-x` | `spacing-3` | The button's side padding at md (12px). |
| `--period-picker-panel-padding` | `spacing-3` | Space inside the popup (12px). |
| `--period-picker-panel-width` | `spacing-64` | The popup's width (256px), at most the screen's less 16px a side. |
| `--period-picker-gap` | `spacing-1` | Space between the periods (4px). |

**Sizing**

| Token | Default | Use |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--period-picker-height-sm` | `control-height-sm` | The button's height at sm (24px). |
| `--period-picker-height-md` | `control-height-md` | The button's height at md (32px). |
| `--period-picker-height-lg` | `control-height-lg` | The button's height at lg (44px). |

**z-index**

| Token | Default | Use |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--period-picker-z-index` | `z-popover` | The popup's stacking level. |
