components.name: PhoneInput
components.summary: A phone number field with a country menu at the start.
components.guide:
# PhoneInput

A phone number field with a country menu at the start. It groups the number the way that country writes it as people type ("812-3456-7890"), and reports it in E.164 ("+6281234567890"), the form to store and send to an SMS service. It's Input's box, so it has the same sizes, states and tokens.

**Also called:** phone number field, telephone input.

```jsx
import { PhoneInput, Field, formatPhone } from '@diki-stwn/serupa-ds';

<Field label="Mobile number"><PhoneInput defaultCountry="ID" name="phone" /></Field>

// Controlled, in E.164
<PhoneInput value={phone} onValueChange={(value, { complete }) => { setPhone(value); setDone(complete); }} />

// Only the countries you serve
<PhoneInput countries={["ID", "SG", "MY"]} />

formatPhone("+6281234567890");   // "+62 812-3456-7890"
```

## When to use

- Sign-up, checkout and contact forms that ask for a phone number, above all when people from more than one country fill them in.

## When not to use

- A number you only show: write it with `formatPhone`, in a `<a href="tel:+6281234567890">`.
- Extensions or short codes: use [Input] (npx serupa-docs Input) with `type="tel"`.

## Anatomy

Drawn from the `ByArea` story.

1. **Country** (`.srp-phone-input__country`): chooses the country, which sets the dialing code and the format.
2. **Dialing code** (`.srp-phone-input__dial`): the country's code, before the number.
3. **Number** (`.srp-input__field`): where the rest of the number is typed.

## Usage

- Label it with [Field] (npx serupa-docs Field). Say in the hint what the number is for ("We'll text you a code").
- Store the E.164 value, not the text in the field. `onValueChange` gives it, and `name` submits it.
- Digits typed on an Arabic, Persian or Bengali keyboard, or full width from a Japanese or Chinese IME (٠١٠, ０９０, ＋８１), are read as the same number, so the field and the value are always in ASCII digits. The calling codes are written in ASCII digits too, in the prefix (+20) and the country list (Egypt (+20)), even where the locale has its own digits (`ar-EG`), so they match the number beside them and what people dial.
- **Form reset** puts `defaultValue` and `defaultCountry` back, in the field and in what the form sends. A controlled field shows its `value` again.
- `complete` says whether the number has a length the country uses. Use it to enable submit or to show an error after blur. It doesn't check that the number exists.
- Set `defaultCountry` to where most of your users are. Without it, the country comes from the locale's region (`id-ID` gives Indonesia), else the US.
- Pasting or typing a number that starts with `+` or `00` picks the country from its calling code. Where countries share one, the area decides: `+1 416…` is Canada, `+1 684…` American Samoa, `+7 7…` Kazakhstan, `+44 1481…` Guernsey.
- A pasted `tel:` link reads as its number (`tel:+4930123456`, parameters such as `;phone-context=` too). An extension at the end ("ext. 12", "x12", "#12", "Durchwahl 12", `;ext=12`) is left off, not joined onto the number. Ask for it in a field of its own.
- A trunk prefix typed at the start (the `0` of `0812…`) is dropped, since the calling code replaces it. So is a calling code typed without `+` ("62 812…" with Indonesia picked), once the number is too long to be a national one.
- A `+` code PhoneInput doesn't know warns once in the console; its digits are read as a number in the picked country.
- A press on the box past the number field focuses the field with the caret at the end, as the text cursor over the box promises; a press on the country menu opens its list.

### Do and don't

- **Do:** Label it with [Field] (npx serupa-docs Field) and say in the hint what the number is for ("We'll text you a code"). (`DoSayWhy`)
- **Don't:** Ask without saying why: people wonder whether to give a real number. (`DontNoReason`)

## States

| State | Look |
| --- | --- |
| Rest | `field` background, 1px `field-border`, the country and its calling code at the start |
| Hover | `field-border-hover`; the country picker under the pointer takes a `field-hover` fill, `field-pressed` while pressed |
| Focus | Like Input: the border and a 1px ring hugging it in `focus-ring` (2px in all), and a visible outline in forced-colors mode. The box draws the one ring whether the country menu or the number has focus; the menu also takes its `field-hover` fill while it has focus |
| Invalid | `danger` border, and a `danger` focus ring |
| Read-only | `field-readonly` background, no hover change; still focusable and selectable; the country can't be changed, and its picker keeps a plain cursor |
| Disabled | `field-readonly` background, `disabled-border` edge and `disabled-text` at full opacity, `not-allowed` cursor; the calling code is in `disabled-text` too, and the country can't be changed |

## Accessibility

- The country menu is a button showing the calling code, named by its text, "Country" with the country and the code ("Country: Indonesia +62"), the visible code included so a voice command that says it works. It opens a list of the countries, as Combobox's list looks, with a search field at its top: the field is a combobox for the listbox under it, and how many match is said after a pause. Each option has the country's name in the locale's words and its calling code; the picked one is selected and has a check.
- The search finds a country by its name, ignoring case and accents ("cote" finds Côte d'Ivoire), by its ISO code ("id") or by its calling code ("62" or "+62"). Names that start with what's typed come first.
- In a right-to-left page the calling code still reads left to right, "+20", in the prefix and in each option.
- One focus ring, on the box, for the menu and the number alike. The menu takes its hover fill while it has focus, so it's clear which part does.
- The number is `type="tel"` with `inputmode="tel"` and `autocomplete="tel"`, so phones show the dial pad and browsers fill in the saved number with its country code. The field reads a "+44 …" and moves the country to match. `tel-national` would fill the digits alone under the default country, a wrong number that looks right.
- Backspace next to a space or dash removes the digit before it, so deleting never gets stuck on the grouping.
- The calling code keeps 4.5:1 and the chevron 3:1 on the field in every theme (`PhoneInput.test.tsx`).

### Keyboard

| Key | Does |
| --- | --- |
| Tab | The country menu, then the number field. In the open list, closes it and goes on to the number |
| Enter / Space / Down / Up | On the country menu, opens the list on the picked country, focus in its search field |
| A letter | On the country menu, opens the list searching for it; a digit does too, to find a calling code |
| Down / Up | In the list, move through the countries, wrapping at the ends |
| Enter | In the list, picks the highlighted country and puts focus in the number |
| Escape | Closes the list, nothing picked, focus back on the menu |
| Backspace / Delete | Next to a space, dash or bracket in the number, removes the digit beyond it rather than the punctuation |

## Countries

Every calling code in the world: 244 countries and territories, one row each in `PHONE_COUNTRIES` (`phone.ts`).

- About 120 have their usual grouping and the national number's shortest and longest lengths. The rest keep their digits ungrouped and accept 4 digits up to E.164's 15 in all.
- Germany groups by its area code, which is 2 to 5 digits: Berlin is "30 123456", a mobile "151 23456789", Cologne "221 1234567", and the rest "4621 1234567". Tokyo and Osaka (one digit) and London (two) group the same way.
- The North American Numbering Plan (+1) tells Canada and the Caribbean and Pacific territories from the US by the area code.
- A row you pass in `countries` replaces the built-in one with the same code, or adds a country: `{ code: "SG", dial: "65", trunk: "", pattern: "## ## ## ##", min: 8, max: 8 }`. The row can also have `patterns` (groupings by the number's start) and `areas` (for a shared calling code).

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | string | none | Goes to the native `<input type="tel">` (not the wrapper), so a `<label htmlFor>` or a Field can point at it. |
| `value` | string | none | The number in E.164 (controlled) |
| `defaultValue` | string | none | The number at first (uncontrolled), in E.164 |
| `onValueChange` | `(value, { country, national, complete }) => void` | none | Called with E.164 (`""` when empty) as the number or country changes |
| `country` | string | none | The picked country's ISO code (controlled) |
| `defaultCountry` | string | the locale's region, else `"US"` | The country at first |
| `onCountryChange` | `(country) => void` | none | Called when the country changes, from the menu or a pasted number |
| `countries` | `Array<string \| PhoneCountry>` | every country | The countries in the menu, as ISO codes or your own rows, sorted by name |
| `countryLabel` | string | `"Country"` | The menu's name |
| `name` | string | none | Submits the E.164 number in a hidden input. With `form`, the hidden input belongs to that form too |
| `size` | `'sm'` \| `'md'` \| `'lg'` | `'md'` | 24, 32 or 44px, like Input |
| `invalid` | boolean | `false` | A danger border and `aria-invalid` |

`ref`, `placeholder`, `disabled`, `readOnly`, `onBlur` and the other input attributes go to the tel `<input>`; `className` and `style` go to the box, which has `data-component="phone-input"`.

### Helpers

- `formatPhone(e164, preferCountry?)`: "+62 812-3456-7890". A number with no known calling code comes back as it was.
- `parsePhone(text, preferCountry?, countries?)`: `{ country, national }` from "+62 0812…" or "0062…", or `undefined`. `preferCountry` decides a shared calling code while the area isn't typed yet.

## Component tokens

The box and the number use Input's tokens. These style the country part; each is an optional override. The list lives in `src/components/PhoneInput/phone-input.tokens.json` (also in `design-tokens/components/`).

<!-- token-table:start (made from phone-input.tokens.json by npm run tokens: edit the descriptions there) -->
| Token | Default | Use |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--phone-input-dial` | `text` | The calling code (4.5:1 on the field). |
| `--phone-input-chevron` | `text-muted` | The chevron (3:1 on the field). |
| `--phone-input-divider` | `field-border` | The line between the country part and the number: the field's own edge color. |
| `--phone-input-bg-hover` | `field-hover` | The country part's background on hover, as the other buttons inside fields. |
| `--phone-input-bg-pressed` | `field-pressed` | The country picker's background while it's held down, one step past hover. |
| `--phone-input-listbox-bg` | `surface-overlay` | The country list's background. |
| `--phone-input-listbox-border` | `border-overlay` | The country list's outline, and the line under its search field. |
| `--phone-input-option-color` | `text` | A country's name, the search text, and the calling code of the highlighted country. |
| `--phone-input-option-bg-active` | `highlight` | The highlighted country (hover or arrow keys). |
| `--phone-input-option-indicator` | `highlight-indicator` | The 2px bar at the highlighted country's start: none by default (the gray fill marks it), `text`-dark with more contrast. |
| `--phone-input-muted` | `text-muted` | A country's calling code in the list, the search icon and the no-match message. |
| `--phone-input-focus-ring` | `focus-ring` | The box's focus ring while the country button has keyboard focus (the field's own is Input's). |
| `--phone-input-gap` | `spacing-1` | Space around the chevron (4px). |
| `--phone-input-offset` | `spacing-1` | The gap between the box and the country list (4px). |
| `--phone-input-listbox-shadow` | `elevation-overlay` | The country list's shadow. |
| `--phone-input-listbox-radius` | `radius-surface` | The country list's corners (8px). |
| `--phone-input-listbox-max-height` | `spacing-80` | The country list's height, search field included, before it scrolls (320px). |
| `--phone-input-z-index` | `z-popover` | The country list's stacking order, where the top layer isn't available. |
<!-- token-table:end -->

components.name: PinInput
components.summary: A one-time code or PIN, shown as one box per character, such as the 6-digit code texted at sign-in.
components.guide:
# PinInput

A one-time code or PIN, shown as one box per character, such as the 6-digit code texted at sign-in. It's one native field under the boxes, so a phone's "from Messages" suggestion, a paste and a password manager fill every box at once, and forms, labels and screen readers treat it as an Input.

**Also called:** OTP input, one-time code input, verification code input.

```tsx
import { PinInput, Field } from "@diki-stwn/serupa-ds";

<Field label="Verification code" hint="We sent a 6-digit code to your phone." error={error}>
  <PinInput value={code} onValueChange={setCode} onComplete={verify} name="code" />
</Field>

// a 4-digit PIN, hidden
<PinInput aria-label="PIN" length={4} mask />

// letters and digits
<PinInput aria-label="Invite code" type="alphanumeric" length={5} />
```

## When to use

- A short code people copy from somewhere else: a verification code from a text or an email, a 2FA code, a device pairing code.
- A short PIN of a fixed length.

## When not to use

- A password, or a code of no fixed length: use [PasswordInput] (npx serupa-docs PasswordInput) or [Input] (npx serupa-docs Input).
- Long codes such as license keys or recovery codes, which people paste rather than type: use an Input, so they can read and fix the whole text.
- A number people work out, such as an amount: use [NumberInput] (npx serupa-docs NumberInput).

## Anatomy

Drawn from the `Alphanumeric` story.

1. **Boxes** (`.srp-pin-input__boxes`): one box per character, so you see how many are left.
2. **Box** (`.srp-pin-input__box`): one character.
3. **Filled box** (`.srp-pin-input__box--filled`): a character already typed.

## Usage

- `length` (default 6) sets the boxes. Characters that don't fit `type` are dropped as people type or paste, so "123-456" and "123 456" both fill six boxes.
- Use `onComplete` to check the code as soon as the last box fills, and show any error with Field's `error`. Don't clear the code on an error, so people can fix one character.
- It submits with a form through `name`, as an Input does. `required` and the built-in `pattern` (exactly `length` characters) take part in form validation.
- `autoComplete="one-time-code"` is set for you, so phones offer a texted code above the keyboard. Pass `autoComplete="off"` for a PIN that shouldn't be filled in.
- The code reads left to right, also on a right-to-left page. Digits typed on an Arabic, Persian or Bengali keyboard, or full-width from a Japanese or Chinese IME (٤٥٦, ４５６), are kept as the ASCII digits they stand for, so the value is always 0–9 (and A–Z with `alphanumeric`).
- In a narrow container the boxes shrink together and stay square, down to 24px each, so six `lg` or eight `md` boxes still fit a 320px screen. A longer code that doesn't fit even at 24px wraps onto a second row instead of making the page scroll sideways (WCAG 1.4.10).

### Do and don't

- **Do:** Keep the code when it's wrong, and show the error with Field's `error`, so people can fix one character. (`DoKeepCode`)
- **Don't:** Clear the boxes on an error: people have to type the whole code again. (`DontClearCode`)

## States

| State | Look |
| --- | --- |
| Rest | A row of `field` boxes with a 1px `field-border` and 6px corners |
| Hover | Every box takes `field-border-hover` |
| Focus | The box the caret is in takes the `focus-ring` color on its border and a ring hugging it (2px in all), and an empty one shows a caret line, steady under reduced motion; a visible outline in forced-colors mode |
| Invalid | `danger` borders, and a `danger` ring on the box with the caret |
| Read-only | `field-readonly` boxes, no hover change; still focusable |
| Disabled | `field-readonly` boxes, `disabled-border` edges and `disabled-text`, `not-allowed` cursor |

## Accessibility

- **Role and name:** one `<input>` with a text role (a password field with `mask`). Name it with Field's label, `<label htmlFor>`, `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby`. Screen readers read the code, not the boxes, which are `aria-hidden`.
- **Keyboard:** it's one Tab stop. The caret stays at the end, and the box it's in gets the focus color, border and ring, which stay visible in forced colors. Forced colors don't paint the selected code over the boxes either: each box shows only its own digit.

| Key | Does |
| --- | --- |
| A digit (or a letter, with `type="alphanumeric"`) | Fills the next empty box. Other characters are ignored |
| Backspace | Empties the last filled box |
| Arrows, Home, End | Nothing: the caret stays after the last character |
| Ctrl+V / Cmd+V | Pastes a code into every box at once |

- **Contrast:** the characters read 4.5:1 on the boxes, and the focus ring and danger border 3:1 on the surface, in every theme (`PinInput.test.tsx`). The resting border is soft on purpose (`field-border`: about 1.5:1 in light, 1.4:1 to 1.9:1 in dark), under the 3:1 WCAG 1.4.11 asks of a control's edge: a deliberate design exception. The label above the field, its fill in dark, the stronger border on hover and the 3:1 focus ring mark it, and more contrast (`data-contrast="more"` or the system setting) brings back a 3:1+ border.
- **Target size:** the boxes are at least 24px, and the field under them takes a press anywhere on the row (WCAG 2.5.8).
- **What's still yours:** say how many characters the code has, and where it was sent, in the label or hint. Don't put a time limit on it that people can't extend (WCAG 2.2.1).

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | string | none | Goes to the native `<input>`, so a `<label htmlFor>` works. |
| `length` | number | `6` | How many characters, one box each, up to 32. |
| `value` | string | | Controlled. |
| `defaultValue` | string | | Uncontrolled. |
| `onValueChange` | `(value: string) => void` | | Called with the code as it changes. |
| `onComplete` | `(value: string) => void` | | Called with the code once every box is filled. |
| `type` | `'numeric'` \| `'alphanumeric'` | `'numeric'` | Digits only, with a number keypad, or letters and digits. |
| `mask` | boolean | `false` | A dot in each filled box, and a password field. |
| `size` | `'sm'` \| `'md'` \| `'lg'` | `'md'` | Square boxes, 24, 32 or 44px. |
| `invalid` | boolean | `false` | Danger borders and `aria-invalid`. Field's `error` sets it. |

`ref`, `name`, `required`, `disabled`, `readOnly`, `autoFocus`, `aria-*` and every other input attribute go to the `<input>`. `className` and `style` go to the wrapping `<span>`, which has `data-component="pin-input"` and `data-size`.

## Component tokens

Each is an optional override: set it on the page, a container or one PinInput. The list lives in `src/components/PinInput/pin-input.tokens.json` (also in `design-tokens/components/`).

<!-- token-table:start (made from pin-input.tokens.json by npm run tokens: edit the descriptions there) -->
| Token | Default | Use |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--pin-input-bg` | `field` | A box's background. |
| `--pin-input-text` | `text` | The characters (4.5:1 on bg). |
| `--pin-input-border` | `field-border` | A box's border (3:1 on the surface). |
| `--pin-input-border-hover` | `field-border-hover` | The boxes' border on hover. |
| `--pin-input-focus-ring` | `focus-ring` | The border and ring of the box the caret is in. |
| `--pin-input-invalid` | `field-border-invalid` | Every box's border when invalid (3:1 on the surface). |
| `--pin-input-bg-readonly` | `field-readonly` | The boxes' background when read-only or disabled. |
| `--pin-input-border-disabled` | `disabled-border` | Disabled: the edge. |
| `--pin-input-text-disabled` | `disabled-text` | Disabled: the text, icon or mark, in place of fading it (3:1 or more on its background, more with more contrast). |
| `--pin-input-radius` | `radius-control` | A box's corners (6px). |
| `--pin-input-box-sm` | `control-height-sm` | A box's width and height, size="sm" (24px). |
| `--pin-input-box-md` | `control-height-md` | A box's width and height, size="md", the default (32px). |
| `--pin-input-box-lg` | `control-height-lg` | A box's width and height, size="lg" (44px). |
| `--pin-input-gap` | `spacing-2` | Space between the boxes (8px). |
| `--pin-input-border-width` | `border-width-1` | A box's border (1px). |
<!-- token-table:end -->

components.name: Popover
components.summary: A small panel next to its trigger for content people interact with: a short form, filters, details with links.
components.guide:
# Popover

A small panel next to its trigger for content people interact with: a short form, filters, details with links. It's a non-modal dialog: the rest of the page stays usable, and it closes on Escape, a click outside, or when focus moves elsewhere.

**Also called:** floating panel, dropdown panel.

```jsx
import { Popover, Button, Field, Input } from '@diki-stwn/serupa-ds';

<Popover title="Share" trigger={<Button variant="outline" startIcon="share">Share</Button>}>
  {(close) => (
    <form onSubmit={(e) => { e.preventDefault(); invite(); close(); }}>
      <Field label="Email"><Input type="email" /></Field>
      <Button type="submit">Invite</Button>
    </form>
  )}
</Popover>

<Popover aria-label="About billing" placement="right-start" initialFocus="panel"
  trigger={<IconButton icon="info" label="About billing" />}>
  You're billed on the 1st of each month.
</Popover>
```

## When to use

- A short form tied to one control, such as sharing with an email address or renaming in place.
- Filters or settings people adjust and then close, while the page stays in view.
- Details with links or buttons about one item, such as a person's card or an explanation with a "Learn more" link.

## When not to use

- A short hint: use [Tooltip] (npx serupa-docs Tooltip) instead.
- A list of actions: use [Menu] (npx serupa-docs Menu) instead.
- Something people must finish or dismiss before going on: use [Dialog] (npx serupa-docs Dialog) instead.

## Anatomy

Drawn from the `Playground` story, opened.

1. **Title** (`.srp-popover__title`): an optional heading that names the popover.
2. **Body** (`.srp-popover__body`): its content.

## Usage

- The trigger is one element that passes its ref and props on to a DOM element: a Button, IconButton or link, or your own component written with `React.forwardRef` (or the `ref` prop in React 19) that spreads what it gets. A text, several elements or a Fragment throws an error that names the component, and a trigger that drops its ref warns once in the console ("Serupa: Menu's trigger doesn't forward its ref to an element.").
- Keep it small: a few fields or a short paragraph. If it needs scrolling, use a [Drawer] (npx serupa-docs Drawer) or a [Dialog] (npx serupa-docs Dialog).
- Give it a `title`, or an `aria-label` when there's none, so it has a name.
- Keep it outside any `<form>`. The panel renders where it's placed, so inside a form its own form nests in the page's (Enter reloads the page) and Enter in its field submits the page's form. Place it after the form; a field that belongs to the page's form can say so with the `form` attribute. In development it warns (`overlay-in-form`).
- Use the function form of `children` to close it from a Done, Cancel or submit button.
- When it holds only text, set `initialFocus="panel"`: there's no control inside to focus.
- Show one at a time, and never open a popover from inside another: a chain of them is hard to follow and to close. For a second level of choices, use a [Menu] (npx serupa-docs Menu)'s `MenuSub`, or move the task into a [Dialog] (npx serupa-docs Dialog).
- Don't use a popover for a warning: a click elsewhere closes it, so people can miss it. Use an [Alert] (npx serupa-docs Alert) in the page, or a Dialog with `alert` when people must answer.
- A click outside closes it, often by accident, so keep what people typed: hold the fields' values in your state, and save or reuse them when it opens again. A Cancel button is the way to throw them away.
- On a phone, a panel by its button is small to tap and covers what's around it. Set `sheet="mobile"` and under 640px it becomes a sheet along the foot of the screen, the screen's width, as Dialog's `fullScreen="mobile"` fills it; `sheet` makes it one everywhere. For a sheet people pull taller, or one with a backdrop, use a bottom [Drawer] (npx serupa-docs Drawer) with `snapPoints`.

### Do and don't

- **Do:** Keep it small: a few fields or a short paragraph. (`DoKeepSmall`)
- **Don't:** Put a long form in a popover: it needs scrolling. Use a Drawer or a Dialog instead. (`DontLongForm`)

## Accessibility

- The panel is a `role="dialog"` named by its title (or `aria-label`); the trigger has `aria-expanded` and `aria-controls`.
- The title is an `<h2>`, as in Dialog, so screen reader users can jump to it by heading; set `headingLevel` to fit the page's outline.
- Opening moves focus inside; Escape and `close()` return it to the trigger. It sits right after the trigger in the tab order, so Tab moves from the trigger into it.
- A click outside or focus moving elsewhere closes it, without moving focus.
- Text and the title keep 4.5:1 on the panel in every theme (`Popover.test.tsx`).
- It fades and grows in out of its trigger over 150ms, and fades and shrinks back over 100ms when it closes; with reduced motion it only fades. The motion is a transition, so closing it while it opens turns back from where it is. Its content stays while it fades out, inert, and focus goes back to the trigger at once. One open on arrival (`defaultOpen`, or `open` on the first render) is there from the first frame. Firefox and Safari can't keep a closing popover in the top layer yet, so there it closes at once. From the keyboard there is no motion: opened by Enter or Space it is there at once, and Escape takes it away at once.
- As a sheet it is the same non-modal dialog, with the same keys and focus. It rises from the foot of the screen over 200ms and sinks back over 100ms (with reduced motion it only fades), stops 64px short of the top and scrolls inside, and its padding clears a phone's home bar. A `sheet="mobile"` one follows the screen while it's open: turned wide, it goes back next to its trigger.

### Keyboard

| Key | Does |
| --- | --- |
| Enter / Space | On the trigger, opens it and moves focus inside |
| Tab | From the trigger into the panel, which sits right after it; out of the panel, closes it |
| Escape | Closes it and returns focus to the trigger. The phone's Back gesture or button does the same |

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |

components.name: Progress
components.summary: Shows how far along a task is when you can tell: an upload, a setup, a quota.
components.guide:
# Progress

Shows how far along a task is when you can tell: an upload, a setup, a quota. Use a bar in forms, cards and lists, and the ring where space is tight. When you can't tell how far along it is, leave `value` out, or use the lighter Loader.

**Also called:** progress bar.

```tsx
import { Progress } from "@diki-stwn/serupa-ds";

<Progress value={45} label="Uploading report.pdf" showValue />
<Progress value={3} max={8} label="Setup" showValue formatValue={(v, m) => `${v} of ${m} steps`} />
<Progress tone="warning" value={92} label="Storage" showValue />
<Progress variant="circle" value={30} showValue aria-label="Storage used" />
<Progress label="Preparing your export" />   // indeterminate
```

## When to use

- A task that takes a while and whose progress you can measure: an upload, an import, an export.
- How much of something is used: storage, a plan's quota, seats.
- How far people are through a set of steps, shown as a single value.

## When not to use

- A short wait you can't measure, such as content loading: use [Loader] (npx serupa-docs Loader) instead.
- Steps people move through, each with its own title: use [Stepper] (npx serupa-docs Stepper) instead.
- A value people set themselves: use [Slider] (npx serupa-docs Slider) instead.

## Anatomy

Drawn from the `AnnounceComplete` story.

1. **Label** (`.srp-progress__label`): what is in progress.
2. **Value** (`.srp-progress__value`): how far along, as a percentage.
3. **Track** (`.srp-progress__track`): the whole task.
4. **Fill** (`.srp-progress__fill`): the part done.

## Usage

- Give every bar a `label` that says what's in progress ("Uploading report.pdf"), or an `aria-label` for the ring.
- Use `formatValue` when a percentage isn't the clearest words: "3 of 8 steps", "4.6 of 5 GB".
- The percentage follows the locale from `SerupaProvider` (or the browser): "45%" in English, "%45" in Turkish,
  "45 %" in French, "٤٥٪" in Egyptian Arabic, the same digits Calendar uses for its days. A `formatValue` of your
  own should do the same, for example with `Intl.NumberFormat(locale)`.
- Keep `tone="primary"` for ordinary progress; switch to `warning` or `danger` when a quota is nearly full, and say so in the label or nearby text too.
- Start without a `value` while the length is unknown, then pass one as soon as you know it (the files are counted, the size is known): a bar that shows progress is easier to wait for.
- Keep the same shape for the whole task: don't swap a ring for a bar, or a [Loader] (npx serupa-docs Loader) for a Progress, halfway, or the page jumps and people lose track of it.
- When stopping is safe, put a Cancel button by it. When stopping loses work, say so before it stops ("Stop the import? The 3 files done so far are kept.").
- When the task finishes, replace the bar with the result or a confirmation, such as a [Toast] (npx serupa-docs Toast).

## Behavior

- The fill moves to a new value over 300ms.
- Indeterminate: a segment slides across the bar (right to left in right-to-left text, following the nearest `dir`), or a quarter arc turns. Both stand still with `prefers-reduced-motion`.

### Do and don't

- **Do:** Say what's in progress, and how far in the units people count: "Importing contacts, 3 of 8 files". (`DoSayWhat`)
- **Don't:** Label it only "Loading": it doesn't say what is loading or how long is left. (`DontJustLoading`)

## Accessibility

- `role="progressbar"` with `aria-valuenow`, `aria-valuemin`, `aria-valuemax` and `aria-valuetext`; an indeterminate one has no value. The bar is named by its `label`.
- Every tone's fill keeps 3:1 on the page and on the bar's track, the track's border-control edge a soft line by design (3:1 with more contrast), and the label and value 4.5:1, in every theme (`Progress.test.tsx`). The bar's track is the page's surface inside that edge; the ring's track stays secondary, since its arc runs along the page. In forced-colors mode the bar's track gets a border and the fill uses Highlight; the ring's track is GrayText under a Highlight arc, so the arc stands apart from it in every high-contrast theme (a CanvasText track can sit too close to Highlight, as black and dark navy do).
- Value changes aren't read out on their own, since reading every step is noisy. `announceComplete` says when it's done, politely ("Upload: complete", from `labels.progressComplete`, or your own words); for milestones in between, use `announce()` or your own live region.
- **Keyboard:** none: it isn't focusable.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | string | none | Goes to the root `<div>`. |
| `value` | `number \| null` | | From 0 to `max`, clamped. Leave it out for an indeterminate bar or ring. |
| `max` | `number` | `100` | The value that means done. |
| `variant` | `'bar' \| 'circle'` | `'bar'` | A full-width bar or a ring. |
| `size` | `'sm' \| 'md' \| 'lg'` | `'md'` | The bar is 4, 8 or 12px thick; the ring is 24, 40 or 64px. |
| `tone` | `'primary' \| 'success' \| 'warning' \| 'danger'` | `'primary'` | The fill color. Say what the color means in text too. |
| `label` | `ReactNode` | | Bar only: a visible name above the bar. Otherwise pass `aria-label`. |
| `showValue` | `boolean` | `false` | The value at the end of the label row, or inside the ring (md and lg). |
| `formatValue` | `(value, max) => string` | the percentage, as the locale writes it | The value's words, shown and read out. |
| `announceComplete` | `boolean \| string` | `false` | Says it's done when the value reaches `max`: `true` for "Name: complete", or your own words. |
| `onComplete` | `() => void` | | Called each time the value reaches `max` (not when it starts there). |

Every other prop, `className` and `ref` go to the outer `<div>`. It has `data-component="progress"`, `data-variant`, `data-size`, `data-tone` and `data-state` (`loading`, `complete` or `indeterminate`).

## Component tokens

Each is an optional override: set it on the page, a container or one progress indicator. The list lives in `src/components/Progress/progress.tokens.json` (also in `design-tokens/components/`).

<!-- token-table:start (made from progress.tokens.json by npm run tokens: edit the descriptions there) -->
**Colors**

| Token | Default | Use |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--progress-track` | `track` | The empty part of the bar: the shared `track` gray, Apple's level (zinc-200 in light, zinc-700 in dark), with no edge. |
| `--progress-track-border` | `track` | The bar's 1px edge: the track's own color by default, so no edge shows; set it to outline the bar. |
| `--progress-ring-track` | `track` | The ring's empty part: the shared `track` gray, as the bar's (zinc-200 in light, zinc-700 in dark). The arc runs along the page on both sides, so it keeps 3:1 there. |
| `--progress-fill` | `primary` | The done part, tone="primary" (the default; 3:1 on the track and the surface). |
| `--progress-fill-success` | `success` | The done part, tone="success". |
| `--progress-fill-warning` | `warning` | The done part, tone="warning". |
| `--progress-fill-danger` | `danger` | The done part, tone="danger". |
| `--progress-label-color` | `text` | The label above the bar. |
| `--progress-value-color` | `text-muted` | The value (45%) next to the label or inside the ring (4.5:1 on surface). |
| `--progress-fill-edge` | `primary-edge` | The bar's and the ring's 1px edge (Yellow Light; transparent where the fill is 3:1 on the page) |

**Sizing**

| Token | Default | Use |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--progress-height-sm` | `spacing-1` | The bar's thickness, size="sm" (4px). |
| `--progress-height-md` | `spacing-2` | The bar's thickness, size="md", the default (8px). |
| `--progress-height-lg` | `spacing-3` | The bar's thickness, size="lg" (12px). |
| `--progress-circle-sm` | `spacing-6` | The ring, size="sm" (24px). |
| `--progress-circle-md` | `spacing-10` | The ring, size="md" (40px). |
| `--progress-circle-lg` | `spacing-16` | The ring, size="lg" (64px). |

**Border**

| Token | Default | Use |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--progress-radius` | `radius-pill` | The bar's ends. |
| `--progress-stroke-width` | `stroke-width-3` | The ring's thickness, in 24ths of its size (3: 3px at 24px). |

**Spacing**

| Token | Default | Use |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--progress-gap` | `spacing-1.5` | Space between the label row and the bar (6px). |

**Type**

| Token | Default | Use |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--progress-label-weight` | `font-medium` | The label's weight (500). |

**Motion**

| Token | Default | Use |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--progress-duration` | `motion-change-lg` | How long the fill takes to move to a new value. |
<!-- token-table:end -->

components.name: Prose
components.summary: Styles for content nobody wrote in components: HTML from Markdown, a CMS or a rich-text editor, such as a help article, a changelog or a blog post.
components.guide:
# Prose

Styles for content nobody wrote in components: HTML from Markdown, a CMS or a rich-text editor, such as a help article, a changelog or a blog post. base.css takes the browser's spacing off headings and paragraphs so that app screens line up, which leaves such content as one wall of text; inside Prose it reads as a document again.

**Also called:** rich text, article content.

```tsx
import { Prose } from "@diki-stwn/serupa-ds";

<Prose as="article" dangerouslySetInnerHTML={{ __html: html }} />
```

## When to use

- Around HTML you don't control element by element: rendered Markdown, CMS fields, rich-text editor output, or a long page of plain elements such as terms of service.

## When not to use

- Around your app's own screens and components: they space themselves with Stack and the spacing utilities, and Prose would add space between them.
- For one line or paragraph of text: use [Text] (npx serupa-docs Text), and [Heading] (npx serupa-docs Heading) for a heading.

## Usage

- Sanitize HTML from users or a CMS before you pass it to `dangerouslySetInnerHTML` (through your Trusted Types policy, if the page has one), or render the Markdown to elements: Prose only styles what's inside it.
- Each block is spaced from the one before it, with more space before a heading and none before the first block, so nothing needs a margin of its own. Lists, quotes, details, cells and definitions are spaced the same way inside.
- The column is capped at about 65 characters a line (`container-prose`), the comfortable reading width. Give it a `className` such as `max-w-none` to fill its container.
- Lists get their bullets and numbers back (disc, then circle and square when nested), indented with logical properties, so they sit on the right in RTL.
- Links are base.css's bare links: Link's colors, underline and focus ring, and a long URL wraps. A visited link takes its own shade (`link-visited`), so readers can see what they've already read; app screens keep Link's one color.
- A wide table or code block scrolls in its own box instead of widening the page. Images and videos never overflow the column, and an image that fails to load shows its alt text in muted italics.

### Do and don't

- **Do:** Keep the default column, capped at about 65 characters a line, for anything people read. (`DoReadingWidth`)
- **Don't:** Stretch reading text across a wide screen: lines get too long to follow back to the next. (`DontFullWidth`)

## Accessibility

- **Role and name:** none of its own. It's a `<div>` by default; use `as="article"` for content that stands on its own, such as a post. The headings inside keep their levels, so start them below the page's own.
- **Keyboard:** none of its own. Links inside take the base focus ring, and a table or code block that scrolls can be scrolled with the trackpad or the scrollbar.
- **Contrast:** body text, headings, quotes and list markers keep 4.5:1 on the page, and a visited link reads 4.5:1 on `surface` and `surface-muted` in every theme (`Prose.test.tsx`, and the foundation check for `link-visited`). Browsers allow only a color change on a visited link, so it's a reading aid, never the only way to tell something.
- **What's still yours:** sanitized HTML, sensible heading levels, and alt text on the images.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `as` | `'div'` \| `'article'` \| `'section'` | `'div'` | The element. |
| `children` | `ReactNode` | | The content, or pass HTML with `dangerouslySetInnerHTML`. |
| `id` | `string` | | Goes to the element. |

`className`, `ref` and other props go to the element.

## Component tokens

Each is an optional override: set it on the page, a container or one Prose. The list lives in `src/components/Prose/prose.tokens.json` (also in `design-tokens/components/`).

<!-- token-table:start (made from prose.tokens.json by npm run tokens: edit the descriptions there) -->
| Token | Default | Use |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--prose-text` | `text` | The body text (4.5:1 on the page). |
| `--prose-heading` | `text` | Headings. |
| `--prose-link-visited` | `link-visited` | A visited link: a shade apart from primary, 4.5:1 on the page in every theme. |
| `--prose-marker` | `text-muted` | List bullets and numbers. |
| `--prose-quote-text` | `text-muted` | A blockquote's text. |
| `--prose-quote-border` | `border-strong` | The bar at a blockquote's start. |
| `--prose-code-bg` | `surface-muted` | Behind inline code and code blocks. |
| `--prose-table-border` | `border` | The line under each table row. |
| `--prose-caption` | `text-muted` | Figure captions, and the alt text of an image that failed to load. |
| `--prose-quote-border-width` | `border-width-4` | The width of a blockquote's bar (4px). |
| `--prose-code-radius` | `radius-inner` | Inline code's corners. |
| `--prose-pre-radius` | `radius-control` | A code block's corners (6px). |
| `--prose-flow` | `spacing-4` | Space before each block after the first (16px). |
| `--prose-flow-heading` | `spacing-8` | Space before a heading, and around a rule (32px). |
| `--prose-flow-after-heading` | `spacing-3` | Space between a heading and what follows it (12px). |
| `--prose-flow-list` | `spacing-2` | Space between list items (8px). |
| `--prose-list-indent` | `spacing-6` | The indent of lists and definitions (24px). |
| `--prose-quote-indent` | `spacing-4` | Space between a blockquote's bar and its text (16px). |
| `--prose-pre-padding` | `spacing-4` | Space inside a code block (16px). |
<!-- token-table:end -->

components.name: QRCode
components.summary: Draws a QR code from a value, such as a payment link, a sign-in link or an authenticator setup string, so a phone can pick it up from the screen.
components.guide:
# QRCode

Draws a QR code from a value, such as a payment link, a sign-in link or an authenticator setup string, so a phone can pick it up from the screen. It is dark on light with its quiet zone in every theme, dark ones included, because scanners need that whatever the page looks like. A status over it says when the code is loading, has expired (with a button for a new one) or has been scanned.

**Also called:** QR, barcode, 2D code, scan code.

```tsx
import { QRCode } from "@diki-stwn/serupa-ds";

<QRCode value={order.payUrl} label="QR code to pay order 1042" />
<QRCode value={login.url} label="Code to sign in on your phone" status={login.status} onRefresh={login.renew} />
<QRCode value={setupUri} label="Authenticator setup code" size="lg" logo="/brand-mark.svg" />
```

## When to use

- Handing something from a screen to a phone: paying at a counter or on a kiosk, signing in on a TV or a desktop with the phone, setting up an authenticator, opening a page on the phone that was found on a computer.
- A code that runs out: `status="expired"` with `onRefresh`, and `"scanned"` once the server sees it used.

## When not to use

- As the only way. Someone using a screen reader, or the phone that shows the code, can't scan it: put the link, the setup key or a "Pay in the app" button beside it, with a [CopyButton] (npx serupa-docs CopyButton) where it helps.
- For a long text. A code holds about 2,300 characters at most, and long ones get too dense to scan from a small screen: link to a page that holds the rest.
- To decorate. A code that does nothing for the reader is noise.

## Anatomy

Drawn from the `Statuses` story.

1. **Code** (`.srp-qr-code__code`): the SVG image, named by `label`.
2. **Light** (`.srp-qr-code__light`): the white square under the modules, quiet zone included, and the square behind a logo.
3. **Dark modules** (`.srp-qr-code__dark`): one path of every dark module.
4. **Status** (`.srp-qr-code__status`): over the faded code, with a status other than `active`.
5. **Message** (`.srp-qr-code__message`): "Code expired" or "Scanned".
6. **Check** (`.srp-qr-code__icon`): beside "Scanned".

## Usage

- Keep the value short. A short URL makes a code with big modules that scans fast, even at `sm`.
- `label` says what it is for, with the thing it opens: "QR code to pay order 1042". It is the image's accessible name.
- `size="md"` (160px) suits most screens. `lg` (240px) is for a counter or a long value; `sm` (96px) only beside text, for a short URL.
- `level` trades size for damage tolerance: `M` (the default) for a screen, `Q` or `H` for print that may get scuffed. A `logo` turns it up to `H` by itself, and covers about 4% of the code.
- Keep it dark on light. The `--qr-code-dark` token takes a brand color only when it keeps about 4.5:1 on white, and a light-on-dark code is one many scanners can't read.
- Don't show a stale code as working: switch to `"expired"` when the server says so, so the person gets a new one before trying.

### Do and don't

- **Do:** A short URL, which makes big modules that scan fast, even from a screen. (`Default`)
- **Don't:** A long text in the code: it packs the modules too small to scan. Link to a page that holds the text. (`DontLongValue`)

## Accessibility

- **Role and name:** the code is an SVG with `role="img"`, named by `label`. Its modules are one path with no text.
- **Keyboard:** the code isn't focusable, since there is nothing to do with it. With `status="expired"` and `onRefresh`, the "Get a new code" button is in the tab order and works with Enter and Space.
- **Status:** a status that changes after the code shows is said politely ("Code expired", "Scanned", from the `qrExpired` and `qrScanned` labels); loading shows a [Loader] (npx serupa-docs Loader) with its own name. The button's words come from the `qrRefresh` label.
- **Contrast:** the code is black on white in every theme and in forced colors. The status message reads 4.5:1 over the faded code in every theme (`QRCode.test.tsx`).
- **What's still yours:** another way to get what the code holds, for anyone who can't scan it; the words for `label`; telling the server's state to `status`.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `value` | string | required | What the code holds, encoded as UTF-8 |
| `label` | string | required | What it is for: the image's accessible name |
| `size` | `'sm' \| 'md' \| 'lg'` | `'md'` | 96, 160 or 240px, quiet zone included |
| `level` | `'L' \| 'M' \| 'Q' \| 'H'` | `'M'` (`'H'` with `logo`) | How much of it can be damaged and still scan: about 7, 15, 25 or 30% |
| `logo` | string | | An image URL drawn in the middle on a light square |
| `status` | `'active' \| 'loading' \| 'expired' \| 'scanned'` | `'active'` | A message over the faded code |
| `onRefresh` | () => void | | With `status="expired"`: the "Get a new code" button calls it |
| `id` | string | none | Goes to the root `<div>`. |

`className`, `ref` and other props go to the `<div>`. A value too long for any code draws an empty square and warns in development. `encodeQR(value, level?)` gives the modules as rows of booleans, for drawing the code yourself (on a canvas, in a PDF).

## Component tokens

Each is an optional override: set it on the page, a container or one QRCode. The list lives in `src/components/QRCode/qr-code.tokens.json` (also in `design-tokens/components/`).

<!-- token-table:start (made from qr-code.tokens.json by npm run tokens: edit the descriptions there) -->
| Token | Default | Use |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--qr-code-dark` | `black` | The dark modules: black in every theme, since scanners need the contrast. A brand color works only if it keeps about 4.5:1 on light. |
| `--qr-code-light` | `white` | The light modules and the quiet zone: white in every theme, dark mode included (most scanners can't read a light-on-dark code). |
| `--qr-code-status-bg` | `surface` | Behind a status, where the faded code shows through. |
| `--qr-code-status-text` | `text` | A status message over the faded code (4.5:1). |
| `--qr-code-scanned-icon` | `success-text` | The check beside "Scanned". |
| `--qr-code-radius` | `radius-inner` | The corners, kept small: the quiet zone is part of the code. |
| `--qr-code-size-sm` | `spacing-24` | size="sm", quiet zone included (96px): a code beside text, for a short URL. |
| `--qr-code-size-md` | `spacing-40` | size="md", the default (160px). |
| `--qr-code-size-lg` | `spacing-60` | size="lg" (240px): a payment code to scan from across a counter, or a long value. |
| `--qr-code-faded` | `opacity-10` | How much of the code shows behind a status: a trace, so the message reads 4.5:1 over it. |
<!-- token-table:end -->

components.name: Quote

components.guide:

components.name: Radio
components.summary: Native radios for one choice from a short list.
components.guide:
# Radio and RadioGroup

Native radios for one choice from a short list. `RadioGroup` names them, holds the value and lays them out; each `Radio` is drawn from tokens like Checkbox, sits centered on its label's first line, and the whole label picks it. Arrow keys move the choice, as browsers do for radios.

**Also called:** radio button, radio group.

```jsx
import { Radio, RadioGroup, Field } from '@diki-stwn/serupa-ds';

<Field group label="Plan" hint="You can change it later." error={error}>
  <RadioGroup name="plan" value={plan} onValueChange={(value) => setPlan(value)}>
    <Radio value="free" description="Up to 3 projects.">Free</Radio>
    <Radio value="pro" description="Unlimited projects and history.">Pro</Radio>
  </RadioGroup>
</Field>

// uncontrolled, in a row
<RadioGroup aria-label="Density" defaultValue="md" orientation="horizontal">
  <Radio value="sm">Compact</Radio>
  <Radio value="md">Default</Radio>
  <Radio value="lg">Roomy</Radio>
</RadioGroup>
```

## When to use

- One choice from 2 to about 5 options people should compare, such as a plan.
- When seeing every option at once helps people choose, for example with a `description` under each.

## When not to use

- More than about 5 options: a [Select] (npx serupa-docs Select) saves space.
- Any number of choices: use [checkboxes] (npx serupa-docs Checkbox).
- On and off: use a [Checkbox] (npx serupa-docs Checkbox) or a [Switch] (npx serupa-docs Switch), not two radios.

## Anatomy

Drawn from the `Disabled` story.

1. **Circle** (`.srp-radio__control`): the ring that shows chosen or not, over the native radio button.
2. **Dot** (`.srp-radio__dot`): fills the ring when it's chosen.
3. **Label** (`.srp-radio__text`): what choosing it means; clicking it chooses it too.
4. **Description** (`.srp-radio__description`): optional detail under the label.

## Usage

- Pick a default when one is safe, so the group never starts empty; leave it empty when the choice has to be deliberate.
- Stack options; use a row only for short labels that fit on one line.
- `variant="card"` makes each radio a bordered card, pressed as a whole: for a few choices that each need a sentence, a price or a delivery time (plans, shipping methods, onboarding questions). The radios stay native, so the arrow keys and the form value work as in a plain group. Keep cards to about two to five options; past that, a plain group or a Select scans faster.

```tsx
<Field label="Delivery" group>
  <RadioGroup variant="card" orientation="horizontal" defaultValue="standard">
    <Radio value="standard" description="3 to 5 days, free">Standard</Radio>
    <Radio value="express" description="Next day, Rp 25.000">Express</Radio>
  </RadioGroup>
</Field>
```

### Do and don't

- **Do:** Cards when each option needs a line to choose by: a delivery time, a price, what a plan includes. (`DoCardsWithDetails`)
- **Don't:** Cards for options that explain themselves, such as sizes: the borders add bulk and nothing to choose by, so a plain row reads faster. (`DontCardsForShortOptions`)
- **Do:** Radios for two to about five options, all in view at once. (`DoFewOptions`)
- **Don't:** A long column of radios, such as every province: people scroll and scan a list a Select or Combobox would search. (`DontLongList`)

## States

| State | Look |
| --- | --- |
| Unchecked | `field` background, 1px `field-border` |
| Checked | `primary` fill and border, with a dot in `on-primary` (6, 6 or 8px) |
| Hover | `field-border-hover`; a checked radio turns `primary-hover` |
| Focus | From the keyboard: a 2px `focus-ring` outline 2px out (`focus-ring-width`, `focus-ring-offset`), like Button. The gap is transparent, so it reads on any background, and forced-colors mode draws it too |
| Invalid | `danger` border while unchecked, and a `danger` focus ring |
| Read-only | Looks as it is, with a default cursor and no hover or press change |
| Disabled | Neutral colors at full opacity: a `disabled-border` circle with a `disabled-text` dot when chosen, and a `disabled-text` label; `not-allowed` cursor; also inside a disabled fieldset (`Field group disabled`) |
| Card | A `surface` card with a 1px `border` and 16px padding, the label in `font-medium`; `field-border-hover` under the pointer; checked, a 2px `primary` border drawn inside, so nothing moves (the dot shows it too); the focus ring goes around the whole card; invalid, a `danger` border while unchecked; in forced colors, a checked card's border is Highlight |

## Accessibility

- A press anywhere within 24px of the row counts (WCAG 2.5.8): when the row is shorter, its hit area reaches past what is drawn, so nothing moves. On a touch screen it's 44px high, as Apple and Material ask; in a group it stops halfway into the gap, so neighbors never share a point.
- They're real radios: Tab moves to the group (to the picked one), arrow keys move the choice, and screen readers announce the position ("2 of 3").
- Name the group: wrap it in `Field group` (a `<fieldset>` and `<legend>`, with the hint and error describing it), or give the RadioGroup an `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby`.
- A radio's label (its `children`) names it; a description is read after it. The dot is decorative. In development, a radio with no label and no `aria-label` warns, and so does one given `label=` (put the text in `children`).
- The label and description keep 4.5:1, and the checked fill, dot, focus ring and invalid border 3:1, in every theme (`Radio.test.tsx`). The resting border is soft on purpose (`field-border`: about 1.5:1 in light, 1.4:1 to 1.9:1 in dark), under the 3:1 WCAG 1.4.11 asks of a control's edge: a deliberate design exception. The label beside the radio, its fill in dark, the stronger border on hover and the 3:1 focus ring mark it, and more contrast (`data-contrast="more"` or the system setting) brings back a 3:1+ border.
- Native constraints (`required`) show too: a box that fails them takes the `invalid` border once people have changed it or tried to send the form (`:user-invalid`), never on first paint. Inside a Field, the Field then says which constraint fails, in its error slot (in the provider's words), with `aria-invalid` and the description, so the border is never the only sign; an `error` you pass wins. On its own, the border is only a color: set `invalid` and say the problem in text when you check it yourself. To keep the browser out of it, leave out the attribute and check the value in your own code.
- A form reset checks the radio that was checked first, and an uncontrolled RadioGroup's choice follows it, so the next click works as expected. A controlled group shows its `value` again.

### Keyboard

| Key | Does |
| --- | --- |
| Tab | Into the group, on the checked radio (or the first, when none is) |
| ↑ ↓ ← → | The previous or next radio, checking it; wraps, and skips disabled ones. Nothing in a read-only group |
| Space | Check the focused radio, when none is checked |

## Props

### RadioGroup props

| Prop | Type | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | string | none | Goes to the root `<div role="radiogroup">`. A `<label htmlFor>` can't name it; inside a Field, the Field's label names it through this id. |
| `value` | string \| number \| null | | The picked radio's value (controlled). `null` picks none |
| `defaultValue` | string \| number | | The value picked at first (uncontrolled) |
| `onValueChange` | `(value, details: { event }) => void` | | Called with the picked radio's value and details (`event`: the change event), like SegmentedControl's and Tabs' |
| `name` | string | generated | The radios' name, for forms |
| `orientation` | `'vertical'` \| `'horizontal'` | `'vertical'` | A stack 8px apart, or a wrapping row 16px apart |
| `size` | `'sm'` \| `'md'` \| `'lg'` | `'md'` | Every radio's size, unless one sets its own |
| `variant` | `'plain'` \| `'card'` | `'plain'` | Every radio's look, unless one sets its own. Cards fill the column, or share a wrapping row (each at least 192px) with `orientation="horizontal"`, 12px apart |
| `invalid` | boolean | `false` | `aria-invalid` on the group, and a danger border on each unchecked radio. Field sets it from its error |
| `disabled` | boolean | `false` | Disables every radio (and sets `aria-disabled` on the group) |
| `required` | boolean | `false` | `aria-required` on the group, `required` on each radio |
| `readOnly` | boolean | `false` | Focusable and read out (`aria-readonly` on the group), and the form still sends the choice, unlike `disabled`; arrows, Space and clicks don't change it, and `onValueChange` doesn't run |

Other props (`id`, `aria-label`, `aria-labelledby`, `className`…) and `ref` go to the `<div role="radiogroup">`, which has `data-component="radio-group"` and `data-orientation`.

### Radio props

| Prop | Type | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `value` | string \| number | | What the group reports when this radio is picked |
| `children` | node | | The label. Without one, give the radio an `aria-label` |
| `description` | node | | A muted second line under the label, linked with `aria-describedby` (and kept out of the name) |
| `size` | `'sm'` \| `'md'` \| `'lg'` | the group's, or `'md'` | A 14px circle with `text-xs`, 16px with `text-sm`, 20px with `text-base` |
| `invalid` | boolean | `false` | A danger border and `aria-invalid`. In a group, set `invalid` on the RadioGroup instead |
| `variant` | `'plain'` \| `'card'` | the group's, or `'plain'` | `'card'`: the radio, label and description in a bordered card pressed as a whole |

Other props (`id`, `disabled`, `aria-*`, `onChange`…) and `ref` go to the `<input type="radio">`. `className` and `style` go to the `<label>`, which has `data-component="radio"` and `data-size`. In a group, the group sets `name` and `checked` (a radio's own are ignored). Outside one, a Radio is a plain radio: pass `name` and `checked` or `defaultChecked` yourself.

## Component tokens

Each is an optional override: set it on the page, a container or one radio. The list lives in `src/components/Radio/radio.tokens.json` (also in `design-tokens/components/`).

<!-- token-table:start (made from radio.tokens.json by npm run tokens: edit the descriptions there) -->
**Colors**

components.name: RangeCalendar
components.summary: A calendar on the page that picks a range of days: the check-in and check-out of a booking, a report's period, the first and last day of a leave request.
components.guide:
# RangeCalendar

A calendar on the page that picks a range of days: the check-in and check-out of a booking, a report's period, the first and last day of a leave request. The first day picked is the start and the next on or after it the end, with the days between shaded as the pointer or focus moves. DateRangePicker's popup is a RangeCalendar, so the two pick the same way.

**Also called:** date range calendar.

```tsx
import { RangeCalendar } from "@diki-stwn/serupa-ds";

<RangeCalendar months={2} value={stay} onValueChange={(r) => setStay(r)} min={new Date()} isDateDisabled={booked} />
```

## When to use

- A range picked on a page or panel where the calendar can stay open: a booking page, an analytics side panel, a request form with room for it.
- Days that some can't be picked from, shown as such (`isDateDisabled`): booked nights, holidays.

## When not to use

- A range in a form row or a filter, where two typed fields fit better and the calendar can wait in a popup: use [DateRangePicker] (npx serupa-docs DateRangePicker).
- One day: use [Calendar] (npx serupa-docs Calendar), or [DatePicker] (npx serupa-docs DatePicker) in a form.

## Anatomy

Drawn from the `Playground` story.

1. **Months** (`.srp-range-calendar__months`): one Calendar month, or two side by side.
2. **Ends** (`.srp-calendar__day--selected`): the start and end days, filled.
3. **Range** (`.srp-calendar__day--in-range`): the days between, shaded.
4. **Status** (`.srp-range-calendar__status`): what to pick next, or the range once it's picked.

## Usage

- Use `months={2}` where there's room: a range often runs into the next month. Two months stack on a narrow screen.
- The first pick is the start; a day before it moves the start, and the next day on or after it is the end. The value changes only when both ends are picked. Show what the range means beside it ("5 nights").
- Use `min`, `max` and `isDateDisabled` for days that can't be an end. A disabled day can sit inside a range; check the whole range yourself when it can't.
- Escape, or a press outside the days, leaves the value as it was; Escape drops a half-picked range.

### Do and don't

- **Do:** `months={2}` where there's room, so a range that crosses the month shows whole. (`DoTwoMonths`)
- **Don't:** One month for a range that runs into the next: its end is out of sight, and people page back and forth to check it. (`DontOneMonth`)

## Accessibility

- **Role and name:** a group named "Choose dates" (or your `aria-label`, or a surrounding Field's label, whose hint then describes it), holding a grid per month named by its month. The ends are selected days named "…, start date" and "…, end date", and the days between "…, in the range", in words as well as the fill.
- **Keyboard:** each month is Calendar's grid (the table below).
- **Said aloud:** the line under the months says what to pick next ("Choose the end date") and, once both are picked, the range ("Selected range: Nov 3 – 8, 2026"), as a polite live region.
- **Contrast:** the ends, the days between and the status line read 4.5:1 in every theme (`RangeCalendar.test.tsx`).
- **What's still yours:** what the range means (nights, working days), and whether a range over a disabled day is allowed.

### Keyboard

| Key | Does |
| --- | --- |
| Tab | To the month buttons, then the day that holds the Tab stop in each month |
| Arrow keys | The day before or after, or the same day a week away; the range previews as focus moves once the start is picked. With two months, crossing into the month the other grid shows moves focus there, and the months stay put |
| PageUp, PageDown | The same day a month before or after; with Shift, a year |
| Home / End | The first or last day of the week |
| Enter / Space | Picks the focused day: the first pick is the start, a day before it moves the start, and one on or after it is the end |
| Escape | Drops a half-picked range, keeping the value as it was |

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | `string` | | Goes to the outer `<div>` |
| `value` | `{ start, end }` \| `null` | | The picked range (controlled); each end a `Date` or `"yyyy-mm-dd"` |
| `defaultValue` | `{ start, end }` | | The range at first (uncontrolled) |
| `onValueChange` | `(range, details: { iso }) => void` | | Called once both ends are picked, start first; `details.iso` is the same range as `"yyyy-mm-dd"` strings |
| `months` | `1` \| `2` | `1` | Months side by side |
| `month` / `defaultMonth` / `onMonthChange` | `Date` | the start's month | The first month shown |
| `min` / `max` | `Date` \| `string` | | The earliest and latest days that can be an end |
| `isDateDisabled` | `(date) => boolean` | | Days that can't be an end, struck through |
| `locale` | `string` | the provider's | Names and the first day of the week |
| `calendar` | as Calendar's | `'gregory'` | The calendar system the months follow (`'persian'`, `'islamic-umalqura'`, `'buddhist'` and more, as in Calendar). The range read out after a pick is in it too. Values stay `Date`s. |
| `weekStartsOn` | `0`–`6` | the locale's | |
| `weekNumbers` | boolean | `false` | Week numbers before the days, as Calendar's `weekNumbers` |
| `headingLevel` | 2 \| 3 \| 4 \| 5 \| 6 | `2` | Each month title's heading level, to fit the page's outline |
| `autoFocus` | `boolean` | `false` | Focus the start day (or today) when it appears |

`className`, `ref` and other props go to the outer `<div>`.

## Component tokens

Each is an optional override: set it on the page, a container or one RangeCalendar. The list lives in `src/components/RangeCalendar/range-calendar.tokens.json` (also in `design-tokens/components/`).

<!-- token-table:start (made from range-calendar.tokens.json by npm run tokens: edit the descriptions there) -->
| Token | Default | Use |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--range-calendar-status-color` | `text-muted` | The line under the months that says what to pick next, and the range once it's picked (4.5:1 on the page). |
| `--range-calendar-months-gap` | `spacing-6` | The space between two months side by side, or stacked. |
<!-- token-table:end -->

components.name: Rating
components.summary: Stars to pick a score (how was your stay, how useful was this article) or to show one (a product's average).
components.guide:
# Rating

Stars to pick a score (how was your stay, how useful was this article) or to show one (a product's average). Picking works like any radio group, with a native radio per star, so it's keyboard, form and screen reader ready.

**Also called:** star rating.

```tsx
import { Rating } from "@diki-stwn/serupa-ds";

const [stars, setStars] = React.useState<number | null>(null);
<Field label="How was your stay?">
  <Rating value={stars} onValueChange={setStars} clearable name="stay" />
</Field>

<Rating aria-label="Your rating" allowHalf defaultValue={3.5} />

// showing a score: one image named "4.3 out of 5"
<Rating readOnly value={4.3} aria-label="Average" />
```

## When to use

- A quick, familiar score: reviews, feedback after a task, how useful a page was.
- Showing an average or a review's score next to its text (`readOnly`).

## When not to use

- A choice between named options ("Poor", "Fair", "Good"): use a [RadioGroup] (npx serupa-docs Radio) or a [SegmentedControl] (npx serupa-docs SegmentedControl), so each option says what it means.
- A number on a wide scale, such as 0 to 100: use a [Slider] (npx serupa-docs Slider) or a [NumberInput] (npx serupa-docs NumberInput).
- A yes or no ("Was this helpful?"): use two [Buttons] (npx serupa-docs Button) or [ToggleButtons] (npx serupa-docs ToggleButton).

## Anatomy

Drawn from the `Disabled` story.

1. **Star** (`.srp-rating__star`): one point of the score.
2. **Filled** (`.srp-rating__fill`): the part of each star the score covers, half stars too.
3. **Empty** (`.srp-rating__empty`): the part it doesn't.

## Usage

- Label it with [Field] (npx serupa-docs Field) or `aria-label`, and say what's being rated.
- Set `clearable` when no rating is a valid answer, so a second pick on the same star clears it.
- Use `allowHalf` only where half stars mean something to people. A press still lands on the whole star, and where in it picks the half, so halves need no bigger size.
- For a read-only score, pass the exact average (`value={4.27}`): the stars draw any fraction, and the name rounds it to one decimal ("4.3 out of 5"). Put the number of reviews in text beside it.

## Behavior

- A click (or a tap) on a star picks it; with `allowHalf`, the start half of a star picks the half and the end half the whole star, and the hover shows which.
- Each star takes presses over its height and the whole step to its neighbors, so a press between two stars picks the nearer one. Stars are at least 24px apart, center to center (WCAG 2.2's target size, 2.5.8): at `sm` the gap between them is 4px, and md or lg stars shrinking to fit a narrow box stop at 22px. With `allowHalf` each star is still one target; the half's own radio is there for the keyboard and screen readers. The stars up to the pointer light up while it hovers, without picking.
- Form reset brings back `defaultValue`, also for a rating outside the form that `form` names. With `name`, the rating is sent with the form as one value.
- In a right-to-left page the stars run from the right, and halves fill from the right.

### Do and don't

- **Do:** Label the stars with what's being rated: "How was the delivery?". (`DoSayWhatsRated`)
- **Don't:** Show stars with no visible label: people have to guess what they're rating. (`DontBareStars`)

## Accessibility

- **Role and name:** interactive, it's a `role="radiogroup"` named by its Field label or `aria-label`, holding a native radio per choice, named by the `ratingStars` label ("1 star", "3.5 stars"; "3,5 bintang" in `idLabels`). `readOnly` is one `role="img"` named by the `ratingValue` label ("4.3 out of 5", after its own `aria-label`: "Average, 4.3 out of 5").
- **Keyboard:** native radio group keys, below. The focused star gets the focus ring.
- **Contrast:** the filled and empty star colors are 3:1 on the page in every theme (`Rating.test.tsx`). In forced colors, empty stars use the system's gray text and filled ones its text color.
- **What's still yours:** say what the rating is for in the label, and show the count of reviews in text next to a read-only average.

### Keyboard

| Key | Does |
| --- | --- |
| Tab | To the picked star (or the first, with none picked), then out of the group |
| ArrowRight, ArrowDown | Pick the next star (or half); ArrowLeft in a right-to-left page |
| ArrowLeft, ArrowUp | Pick the one before; ArrowRight in a right-to-left page |
| Space | Pick the focused star; with `clearable`, on the picked one, clear it |
| Backspace, Delete | With `clearable`, clear the rating |

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | `string` | | Goes to the root (the radio group, or the image when `readOnly`). |
