components.name: RelativeTime
components.summary: Says how long ago, or how far ahead, a moment is, in the reader's language: "3 minutes ago", "yesterday", "in 2 hours".
components.guide:
# RelativeTime Says how long ago, or how far ahead, a moment is, in the reader's language: "3 minutes ago", "yesterday", "in 2 hours". It keeps itself up to date, and the exact date is its tooltip. **Also called:** time ago, relative date. ```tsx import { RelativeTime } from "@diki-stwn/serupa-ds";

Edited

// "3 hr. ago" // "in 1 day" rather than "tomorrow" ``` ## When to use - Recent activity, where "how long ago" matters more than the exact time: edits, comments, messages, last sign-in. - Something coming up soon: "in 15 minutes". ## When not to use - Dates people compare or act on, such as a due date in a table or a receipt: show the date itself. - Times more than a few months away, where "last year" is too vague: show the date. RelativeTime does this itself after a week (`absoluteAfter`). ## Usage - Pass `date` as a `Date`, a timestamp in ms or an ISO string. Strings without a time zone (`"2026-10-24 09:30"`) are read in the browser's time zone, so prefer ISO strings with `Z` or an offset. - A day on its own, `"2026-10-24"` (a date column, ``), is that day on the reader's calendar and is counted in days or more: "today", "yesterday", "in 3 days". Its tooltip is the date alone, and its `datetime` the day itself. - The words follow the locale from `SerupaProvider` (or the `locale` prop, or the browser's): "3 menit yang lalu" in Indonesian, "٣ ساعات" digits in Egyptian Arabic. `relativeTime(date, now, locale)` gives the same words outside React, however far (it doesn't switch to a date). - Use `numeric="always"` where elapsed time matters more than the calendar, such as in logs. - More than 7 days away, ago or ahead, it shows the date instead of words: "Oct 24, 2026" rather than "340 days ago". Set `absoluteAfter` to another number of days, or `false` to keep the words however far, and `absoluteFormat` to write the date another way. - An invalid `date` shows nothing; in development it warns once in the console. ## Behavior - Under 45 seconds it says "now", then minutes (under 45), hours (under 22), days (under 26), months (under 11) and years, rounded. - Every RelativeTime on the page updates on one shared clock every 15 seconds, and at once when the tab comes back into view. The clock stops when none is mounted. - Rendered on the server, it shows the server's words at the time of the request (one moment for every RelativeTime rendered in the same second), hydrates without a mismatch, and switches to the browser's clock straight after. ### Do and don't - **Do:** Use `numeric="always"` where elapsed time matters more than the calendar, such as in logs ("1 day ago"). (`DoNumericInLogs`) - **Don't:** Use calendar words in a log: "yesterday" says less about how long ago it was. (`DontCalendarWordsInLogs`) ## Accessibility - It's a `` with a machine-readable `datetime`, read out as its words. - The exact date is in `title`, which shows on hover but isn't reliably read out or reachable by keyboard. Where the exact time matters, show it as text too or wrap it in a [Tooltip] (npx serupa-docs Tooltip) on a focusable element. - It doesn't announce its updates: a live region that changes every minute would be noise. - **Keyboard:** none: inline text, not focusable. - With a `locale` of its own it carries that locale's direction (`dir`) with its `lang`, so "3 minutes ago" in English keeps its order in a right-to-left page. ## Props | Prop | Type | Default | Notes | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `id` | string | none | Goes to the root ``. | | `date` | `Date \| number \| string` | | The moment. An invalid date renders an empty ``. | | `format` | `'long' \| 'short' \| 'narrow'` | `'long'` | "3 minutes ago", "3 min. ago", "3m ago". | | `numeric` | `'auto' \| 'always'` | `'auto'` | "yesterday" or "1 day ago". With `'auto'`, days, months and years are counted on the reader's calendar: 01:00 seen at 23:00 the same day is "22 hours ago", and the 1st seen on the 27th is "26 days ago", not "last month". `'always'` counts elapsed time. | | `titleFormat` | `Intl.DateTimeFormatOptions \| false` | `{ dateStyle: 'long', timeStyle: 'short' }` | The tooltip's date; `false` leaves it out. Your own `title` wins. | | `absoluteAfter` | `number \| false` | `7` | After this many days, ago or ahead, it shows the date instead of words. `false`: words however far. | | `absoluteFormat` | `Intl.DateTimeFormatOptions` | `{ dateStyle: 'medium' }` | How that date is written. | | `locale` | `string` | the provider's, else the browser's | When it differs from the provider's, the element carries `lang`, so screen readers read the words in that language. | Every other prop, `className` and `ref` go to the ``, which has `data-component="relative-time"`. ## Component tokens None: it uses the surrounding text's font and color, with tabular digits.

components.name: SaveStatus
components.summary: A small line that says whether autosaved changes are safe: "Saving…", "Saved 2 minutes ago", or "Couldn't save" with a Try again button.
components.guide:
# SaveStatus

A small line that says whether autosaved changes are safe: "Saving…", "Saved 2 minutes ago", or "Couldn't save" with a Try again button. People can trust autosave without a Save button, and screen reader users hear when a save lands or fails.

**Also called:** autosave indicator, sync status.

```tsx
import { SaveStatus } from "@diki-stwn/serupa-ds";

<SaveStatus status={status} savedAt={savedAt} onRetry={save} />
```

## When to use

- A form, editor or settings page that saves on its own as people type or change things. Put it near the title or the top of the form, where people look for it.

## When not to use

- A form with a Save button: the button's own loading and `successText` ([Button] (npx serupa-docs Button)) say it.
- A one-off action's result ("Copied", "Sent"): use a [Toast] (npx serupa-docs Toast).

## Anatomy

Drawn from the `Failed` story.

1. **Icon** (`.srp-save-status__icon`): shows saving, saved or failed beside the words.
2. **Status** (`.srp-save-status__text`): the state in words, announced as it changes.
3. **Try again** (`.srp-save-status__retry`): after a failure, saves again.

## Usage

- Set `status` from your save: `'saving'` when a save starts, `'saved'` with `savedAt` when it finishes, `'error'` when it fails. Use `'idle'` before anything has changed.
- Pass `onRetry` so people can try a failed save again, and keep their changes until it works.
- Say why in `errorText` when you know ("Couldn't save: you're offline").
- Debounce saves while people type, so it doesn't flicker between Saving and Saved on every key.

## Behavior

- Saving shows a small ring and "Saving…". Saved shows a check and "Saved", and with `savedAt`, how long ago ("Saved 2 minutes ago"), kept current by [RelativeTime] (npx serupa-docs RelativeTime). An error shows an error icon and the text in the danger color, then Try again.
- Idle renders an empty line of the same height, so the page doesn't move when it starts.
- A new status cross-fades with the one before it, in the same place: the old one fades out (inert, hidden from screen readers) while the new one fades in, with a short scale and blur when motion is allowed. The first status just shows.

### Do and don't

- **Do:** Say why a save failed in `errorText` when you know, and pass `onRetry`. (`DoReasonAndRetry`)
- **Don't:** Show a failure with no reason and no retry: people can't tell what went wrong or what to do. (`DontDeadEnd`)

## Accessibility

- **Announcements:** "Saved" is said once, politely, and the error once, at once (danger interrupts, the rest wait, as in Toast and Alert), when the status changes to them. "Saving…" isn't, since it comes and goes with every save, and neither is the time ticking ("2 minutes ago"). A SaveStatus that first renders with "saved" says nothing, but one that first renders with "error" (shown only once a save fails) says the error.
- **Keyboard:** Try again is a Tab stop when it shows. Nothing else is. Once Try again is pressed it goes with the error, and focus stays on the status line (not a Tab stop) instead of falling to the page, so Tab goes on from there.
- **Contrast:** its text reads 4.5:1 on the page, the error too, in every theme (`SaveStatus.test.tsx`).
- **What's still yours:** keep changes when a save fails, and don't move focus to SaveStatus.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | string | none | Goes to the root `<div>`. |
| `status` | `'idle' \| 'saving' \| 'saved' \| 'error'` | | Required. Where saving is. |
| `savedAt` | `Date \| number` | | When the last save finished, for "Saved 2 minutes ago". |
| `onRetry` | `() => void` | | Shows Try again after an error. |
| `errorText` | `ReactNode` | `"Couldn't save"` | What went wrong. |

`className`, `ref` and other props go to the `<div>`.

## Component tokens

Each is an optional override: set it on the page, a container or one SaveStatus. The list lives in `src/components/SaveStatus/save-status.tokens.json` (also in `design-tokens/components/`).

<!-- token-table:start (made from save-status.tokens.json by npm run tokens: edit the descriptions there) -->
| Token | Default | Use |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--save-status-text` | `text-muted` | The text and the ring (4.5:1 on the page). |
| `--save-status-saved` | `success` | The check once saved. |
| `--save-status-error` | `danger-text` | The error's icon, text and Try again (4.5:1 on the page). |
| `--save-status-icon-size` | `spacing-4` | The icon's size (16px). |
| `--save-status-gap` | `spacing-1.5` | Space between the icon, the text and Try again (6px). |
<!-- token-table:end -->

components.name: ScrollArea
components.summary: A box whose content scrolls inside it, such as a long activity list in a card or a row of chips in a narrow column.
components.guide:
# ScrollArea

A box whose content scrolls inside it, such as a long activity list in a card or a row of chips in a narrow column. Its scrollbars are thin and in the theme's colors, and while its content overflows it's a Tab stop and a named region, so keyboard and screen reader users can reach and scroll it.

**Also called:** scroll container, scroll box.

```tsx
import { ScrollArea } from "@diki-stwn/serupa-ds";

<ScrollArea aria-label="Recent activity" fade style={{ maxHeight: 240 }}>
  {activity.map((a) => <ActivityItem key={a.id} {...a} />)}
</ScrollArea>
```

## When to use

- A part of a page that holds more than its space: a feed in a dashboard card, a filter list in a sidebar, a row of tags that runs past its column.
- Anywhere you'd write `overflow: auto` on a div: ScrollArea adds what that div needs to be reachable by keyboard and named for screen readers, only while it scrolls.

## When not to use

- A data table: use [Table] (npx serupa-docs Table), whose frame already scrolls this way.
- Code: use [CodeBlock] (npx serupa-docs CodeBlock).
- A long list of thousands of rows: use a [List] (npx serupa-docs List) with `ListVirtualItems`, which draws only the rows in view.
- The page itself: let the page scroll. A box that scrolls inside a page that scrolls is harder to use, above all on a phone.

## Usage

- Give it a size: a `maxHeight` (or `height`) for `orientation="vertical"`, the default; a width narrower than its content for `"horizontal"`; both for `"both"`.
- Name it with `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby` for what it holds ("Recent activity"). The name is used only while it scrolls; with none it's "Scrolling content".
- With `fade`, an edge with more past it fades out over 32px, a hint that there's more: use it where the scrollbar alone can go unnoticed (a phone, a row of chips). The faded edge isn't for reading, so keep padding at the edges; it fades the box's own border there too, so put a border on a wrapper around it if it needs one. Something scrolled into view inside it (a control reached with Tab, a `scrollIntoView`) stops clear of the fade.
- The scrollbar is the browser's own, so dragging, clicking the track, touch and screen readers work as they do everywhere; only its width and colors change.

### Do and don't

- **Do:** Give it a size: a `maxHeight` (or `height`) for the default vertical scroll. (`Vertical`)
- **Don't:** Leave out the size: it never scrolls, and pushes the rest of the page down. (`DontNoSize`)

## Accessibility

- **Role and name:** while its content overflows, `role="region"` named by `aria-label`, `aria-labelledby` or "Scrolling content"; when everything fits, a plain `<div>` with no role, no name and no Tab stop.
- **Keyboard:**

| Key | Does |
| --- | --- |
| Tab | Reaches it while it scrolls (WCAG 2.1.1), with a focus ring inside its edge. |
| Arrow keys | Scroll it a step. |
| Page Up, Page Down, Home, End | Scroll it a page, or to the start or end. |

- **Contrast:** the scrollbar thumb and the focus ring read 3:1 on the surface in every theme (`ScrollArea.test.tsx`). In forced colors the scrollbar is the system's.
- **What's still yours:** its size and name, and keeping a box that scrolls out of another box that scrolls the same way.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | `string` | | Goes to the box. |
| `orientation` | `"vertical" \| "horizontal" \| "both"` | `"vertical"` | Which way it scrolls. |
| `fade` | `boolean` | `false` | Fades an edge with more past it. |
| `aria-label` | `string` | `"Scrolling content"` | Its name while it scrolls. |
| `aria-labelledby` | `string` | | The id of what names it, such as a heading. |
| `children` | `ReactNode` | | What scrolls. |

`className`, `style`, `ref`, `onScroll` and other props go to the box.

## Component tokens

Each is an optional override: set it on the page, a container or one ScrollArea. The list lives in `src/components/ScrollArea/scroll-area.tokens.json` (also in `design-tokens/components/`).

<!-- token-table:start (made from scroll-area.tokens.json by npm run tokens: edit the descriptions there) -->
| Token | Default | Use |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--scroll-area-thumb` | `border-control` | The scrollbar's thumb (3:1 on the surface). |
| `--scroll-area-focus-ring` | `focus-ring` | The ring inside its edge while it has focus. |
| `--scroll-area-fade` | `spacing-8` | How far an edge with more past it fades, with fade (32px). |
<!-- token-table:end -->

components.name: SearchInput
components.summary: A search field: a search icon at the start, and a × at the end once something is typed.
components.guide:
# SearchInput

A search field: a search icon at the start, and a × at the end once something is typed. Escape clears it and Enter calls `onSearch`. It uses Input's box, sizes and tokens.

**Also called:** search, search field, search box.

```tsx
import { SearchInput } from "@diki-stwn/serupa-ds";

<SearchInput aria-label="Search projects" placeholder="Search projects" onSearch={run} />

// filter as people type
const [q, setQ] = React.useState("");
<SearchInput aria-label="Filter" value={q} onChange={(e) => setQ(e.target.value)} loading={fetching} />
```

## When to use

- Searching a site, an app or a large set of records, with `onSearch` on Enter.
- Filtering a list or a table on the page as people type.

## When not to use

- Picking one value from a known list: use [Combobox] (npx serupa-docs Combobox).
- A search that suggests as people type, or shows their recent searches before they type: use [Combobox] (npx serupa-docs Combobox) with `freeText` and `startIcon="search"`, its `SearchWithRecent` story shows how (recent searches when it opens empty, suggestions while typing, Clear recent searches beside it).
- A one-line answer in a form that isn't a search: use [Input] (npx serupa-docs Input).

## Anatomy

Drawn from the `Invalid` story.

1. **Search icon** (`.srp-search-input__icon`): says the field searches.
2. **Field** (`.srp-input__field`): where the search is typed.
3. **Clear** (`.srp-search-input__clear`): empties the field, as Escape does.

## Usage

- Put it in a `<form role="search">` when it searches the whole site or app.
- Name it with a visible label or `aria-label`, and use the placeholder for what can be searched ("Search projects").
- Set `loading` while results are on their way, so people know the search is running.

## States

| State | Look |
| --- | --- |
| Rest | `field` background, 1px `field-border`, the search icon in `text-muted` |
| Hover | `field-border-hover`; the × that clears it takes a `field-hover` fill under the pointer |
| Focus | Like Input: the border and a 1px ring hugging it in `focus-ring` (2px in all), and a visible outline in forced-colors mode |
| Loading | A small Loader in the search icon's place, announced as `loadingLabel` |
| Invalid | `danger` border, and a `danger` focus ring |
| Read-only | `field-readonly` background, no hover change; still focusable and selectable |
| Disabled | `field-readonly` background, `disabled-border` edge and `disabled-text` at full opacity, `not-allowed` cursor |

## Behavior

- The × shows only when there's text and the field isn't disabled or read-only. Clicking it clears the field and keeps focus there.
- Escape clears a field that has text, and stops there, so a surrounding Dialog or Popover stays open. On an empty field Escape passes through.
- A form reset empties the field, or puts `defaultValue` back, and the × follows it.
- The browser's own clear button is hidden, so there's only one ×.
- A press anywhere else on the box, on the search icon or the side padding, focuses the field with the caret at the end, as Input's box does.

### Do and don't

- **Do:** Say in the placeholder what can be searched: "Search invoices by number or customer". (`DoSayWhat`)
- **Don't:** Write only "Search...": people have to guess what they can find. (`DontBareSearch`)

## Accessibility

- The clear button takes presses over at least 24px (WCAG 2.5.8), even at size `sm` where it's 22px: a box behind it reaches past its edges without moving anything.
- `type="search"` (a searchbox) with `enterkeyhint="search"`. Name it with a `<label>` or `aria-label`; a placeholder isn't a name.
- The icon and × keep 3:1 and the text 4.5:1 on the field in every theme (`SearchInput.test.tsx`).

### Keyboard

| Key | Does |
| --- | --- |
| Tab | To the field, then to the × when there's text |
| Enter | Calls `onSearch` with the text, and submits the form it's in |
| Escape | Clears the field (when it has text and isn't read-only); without text, Escape goes on to what's around it, such as a Dialog |

## Props

Every Input prop works (`size`, `invalid`, `value`, `defaultValue`, `onChange`, `placeholder`, `disabled`…), except `type`, `startIcon` and `endIcon`.

| Prop | Type | Default | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | string | none | Goes to the native `<input type="search">` (not the wrapper), so a `<label htmlFor>` or a Field can point at it. |
| `onSearch` | `(value: string) => void` | | Called with the text when Enter is pressed. |
| `onClear` | `() => void` | | Called after the × or Escape clears the field. `onChange` also gets an empty value first, so controlled fields follow. |
| `clearLabel` | `string` | `'Clear search'` | The ×'s name. |
| `loading` | `boolean` | `false` | A small loader in place of the search icon, announced as `loadingLabel`. |
| `loadingLabel` | `string` | `'Searching'` | The loader's name. |

`className` and `style` go to the box; `ref` and every other prop go to the `<input>`.

## Component tokens

Each is an optional override: set it on the page, a container or one field. The box uses Input's tokens. The list lives in `src/components/SearchInput/search-input.tokens.json` (also in `design-tokens/components/`).

<!-- token-table:start (made from search-input.tokens.json by npm run tokens: edit the descriptions there) -->
| Token | Default | Use |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--search-input-icon-color` | `text-muted` | The search icon (3:1 on the field). |
| `--search-input-clear` | `text-muted` | The clear button's icon. |
| `--search-input-clear-hover` | `text` | The clear button's icon on hover. |
| `--search-input-clear-bg-hover` | `field-hover` | The clear button's background on hover. |
| `--search-input-clear-bg-pressed` | `field-pressed` | The clear button's background while it's held down, one step past hover. |
| `--search-input-focus-ring` | `focus-ring` | The clear button's keyboard focus ring. |
| `--search-input-clear-radius` | `radius-inner` | The clear button's corners (4px). |
| `--search-input-clear-padding` | `spacing-1` | Space around the clear button's icon (4px). |
<!-- token-table:end -->

components.name: SegmentedControl
components.summary: Picks one of a few options shown side by side, such as a view (List, Board) or a period (Day, Week, Month).
components.guide:
# SegmentedControl

Picks one of a few options shown side by side, such as a view (List, Board) or a period (Day, Week, Month). It's a radio group drawn as segments, with the selection sliding between them.

**Also called:** segmented button, button toggle group.

```tsx
import { SegmentedControl } from "@diki-stwn/serupa-ds";

<SegmentedControl aria-label="Period" defaultValue="week"
  options={[{ value: "day", label: "Day" }, { value: "week", label: "Week" }, { value: "month", label: "Month" }]} />

<SegmentedControl aria-label="View" value={view} onValueChange={setView}
  options={[{ value: "list", icon: "list", label: "List" }, { value: "board", icon: "view_kanban", label: "Board" }]} />

<SegmentedControl aria-label="Text alignment" size="sm" options={[
  { value: "left", icon: "format_align_left", "aria-label": "Left" },
  { value: "center", icon: "format_align_center", "aria-label": "Center" },
]} />
```

## When to use

- Switching how the same content is shown, such as List and Board.
- One choice from 2 to about 5 short options that applies right away, such as Day, Week, Month.

## When not to use

- Switching panels of content: use [Tabs] (npx serupa-docs Tabs).
- Tools that share one value, such as alignment (one on) or text styles (any number on): use a [ToggleGroup] (npx serupa-docs ToggleGroup). On/off buttons that each keep their own state: [ToggleButton] (npx serupa-docs ToggleButton)s in a [ButtonGroup] (npx serupa-docs ButtonGroup). A SegmentedControl picks a view or a value, and is one Tab stop with arrows, as [Choose a component](../../../docs/ChooseAComponent.mdx) explains.
- More than about five options: use [RadioGroup] (npx serupa-docs Radio) or [Select] (npx serupa-docs Select).

## Anatomy

Drawn from the `WithIcons` story.

1. **Item** (`.srp-segmented__item`): one choice, a radio in a group.
2. **Selected item** (`.srp-segmented__item--selected`): the choice that's on, in the text color (`--segmented-control-text-selected`) rather than the muted one.
3. **Icon** (`.srp-segmented__icon`): an optional picture of the choice.
4. **Label** (`.srp-segmented__label`): the choice, in words.

Once the script runs, the raised surface under the selected item is the **indicator** (`.srp-segmented__indicator`), its own element that slides to the new choice and that the `--segmented-control-indicator*` tokens style. Before that, in the page's first paint from the server, the selected item draws the surface itself, so style the surface through those tokens rather than on `.srp-segmented__item--selected`.

## Usage

- Keep labels to one or two words, so the segments stay short and even. Use nouns for what each one shows ("List", "Board"), not verbs.
- Use words in every segment or icons in every segment, not a mix: segments with words beside icon-only ones look unequal and read unevenly.
- Every segment picks a value. Don't make one an action ("Add view"): put that in a Button next to the control.
- When the segments don't all fit, they share the width by content: short labels stay whole and a long one ends in an ellipsis, with its full label as its title on hover. That title isn't there for touch or the keyboard, so keep labels short enough to fit the narrowest screen, or use a [Select] (npx serupa-docs Select).
- Give an icon-only segment an `aria-label`, and use icons alone only when they're widely understood.
- Icon-only segments are at least 24px wide, so even in `sm` their centers are 24px apart, which meets WCAG 2.2's target size (2.5.8).
- Use `fullWidth` in narrow spaces such as a panel or a phone layout, and match the `size` to the controls beside it.

### Do and don't

- **Do:** Keep each label to one or two words: "Newest", "Oldest", "Popular". (`DoShortLabels`)
- **Don't:** Write sentences as labels: the segments come out uneven and cut off in a narrow space. (`DontSentences`)

## Accessibility

- Every option takes a press over at least 24px of height (WCAG 2.5.8), also at `size="sm"`, where options are drawn 18px tall, without taking more room. On a touch screen it's 44px high, as Apple and Material ask (the width stays, so segments never overlap).
- `role="radiogroup"` with `role="radio"` segments and `aria-checked`.
- In a [Field] (npx serupa-docs Field), the label names the radiogroup through `aria-labelledby`, and the hint and error describe it. Its own `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby` wins.
- The outline is the same soft hairline as a form field's (`field-border`), under the 3:1 WCAG 1.4.11 asks of a control's edge, by design, as fields are: the control also shows by its muted track and its raised selection, and more contrast (`data-contrast="more"` or the system setting) brings back a 3:1 outline. Labels keep 4.5:1 in every theme (`SegmentedControl.test.tsx`). The selected segment changes three ways (a raised surface, an outline and a darker label), so it doesn't rely on one color. In forced colors (Windows high contrast) the selection is Highlight and its label HighlightText, exactly as set, so the browser's text backplate can't hide the label, and hovering the selected segment keeps it HighlightText.
- `invalid` sets `aria-invalid` on the group and turns its outline danger (3:1 on the page in every theme); `required` sets `aria-required`. Put the reason in text next to it: inside a [Field] (npx serupa-docs Field), its `error` and `required` do all of this.
- `readOnly` sets `aria-readonly`. Segments stay focusable and the arrow keys move focus between them, so people can hear every option, but neither a click nor a key changes the selection. With `name`, the value is still sent with the form, which `disabled` doesn't do.
- The selection slides over 200ms, and jumps with `prefers-reduced-motion` or when an arrow key picks the segment.

### Keyboard

| Key | Does |
| --- | --- |
| Tab | To the selected segment: the control is one Tab stop |
| Right / Down | The next segment, selecting it (Left and Right swap in right-to-left pages), skipping disabled ones and wrapping |
| Left / Up | The previous segment, the same way |
| Home / End | The first or last segment |

Your `onKeyDown` runs before the control's own keys, so `e.preventDefault()` in it overrides one. `onFocus` and `onBlur` fire when focus enters or leaves the control, not as the arrow keys move between segments, so a form library's "touched on blur" waits until people leave it.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | string | none | Goes to the root `<div role="radiogroup">`. A `<label htmlFor>` can't name it; inside a Field, the Field's label names it through this id. |
| `options` | `{ value, label?, icon?, 'aria-label'?, disabled? }[]` | | The segments, in order. An icon-only segment needs `aria-label`. |
| `value` | `V` | | Controlled. `V` is the segments' values, a `string` by default: it's inferred from `options`, or given as `SegmentedControl<'list' \| 'board'>`, so `onValueChange` gets that union; given, a value outside it is a type error. |
| `defaultValue` | `V` | the first enabled option | Uncontrolled. |
| `onValueChange` | `(value: V) => void` | | When a different segment is chosen. |
| `size` | `'sm' \| 'md' \| 'lg'` | `'md'` | 24, 32 or 44px tall, like the control heights, so it lines up with an Input, Select or Button of the same size. |
| `fullWidth` | `boolean` | `false` | Fills its container with equal segments. When a label doesn't fit its equal share, the segments share the width by content instead, still filling it, so short labels give their spare room to long ones. |
| `disabled` | `boolean` | `false` | |
| `invalid` | `boolean` | `false` | A danger outline and `aria-invalid`. Field's `error` sets it. |
| `required` | `boolean` | `false` | `aria-required` on the group. Field's `required` sets it. |
| `readOnly` | `boolean` | `false` | Focusable and read out, but the selection doesn't change; the value is still submitted. |
| `name` | `string` | | Sends the value with a form, in a hidden input. |
| `form` | `string` | | The id of a form it sits outside of: its hidden input submits, and resets, with that form. |

Name it with `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby`. `className`, `ref` and other props go to the root `<div>`. Its `focus()` and `autoFocus` move focus to the selected segment, or else the first one that isn't disabled, so a form library that focuses the first invalid field after a failed submit lands on it.

## Component tokens

Each is an optional override: set it on the page, a container or one control. The list lives in `src/components/SegmentedControl/segmented-control.tokens.json` (also in `design-tokens/components/`).

components.name: Select
components.summary: A native `<select>` styled like Input: the same three heights (24, 32 and 44px), colors, focus ring and states, with a chevron and an optional left icon.
components.guide:
# Select

A native `<select>` styled like Input: the same three heights (24, 32 and 44px), colors, focus ring and states, with a chevron and an optional left icon. It keeps everything the browser gives a select for free: the system picker on phones, type-to-find, and full keyboard and screen-reader support.

Where the browser lets a page style the list (`appearance: base-select`, in Chromium-based browsers today), the open list is drawn like Combobox's: an overlay surface with the shared shadow and corners, rows at control height, the gray highlight fill on the option under the pointer or keyboard, and a tick on the chosen one. Everywhere else the browser draws its own list. Your code and the way it reads out are the same either way.

**Also called:** dropdown, select input, picker.

```jsx
import { Select, Field } from '@diki-stwn/serupa-ds';

<Field label="Role">
  <Select options={["Viewer", "Editor", "Admin"]} value={role} onChange={(e) => setRole(e.target.value)} />
</Field>

<Select aria-label="Country" placeholder="Choose a country" options={countries} />

// labels, disabled options and groups
<Select aria-label="Time zone" startIcon="schedule" options={[
  { label: "Europe", options: [{ value: "Europe/London", label: "London (GMT+1)" }, { value: "Europe/Paris", label: "Paris (GMT+2)" }] },
  { value: "UTC", label: "UTC", disabled: true },
]} />

// or your own options
<Select aria-label="Sort"><option value="new">Newest</option><option value="old">Oldest</option></Select>
```

## When to use

- One choice from a short, fixed list of about 5 to 15 plain-text options, such as a role, a country or a time zone.
- Forms used on phones, where the system picker is easier than a custom list.

## When not to use

- 2 to 4 options: use [radios] (npx serupa-docs Radio), which show every choice at once.
- A long list people search through, options loaded as people type, options with more than a line of text (an avatar, a description), or several choices: use a [Combobox] (npx serupa-docs Combobox).
- Picking more than one option from a short list: use [checkboxes] (npx serupa-docs Checkbox); Select doesn't support `multiple`.
- A few options that change a view right away, such as Day, Week, Month: use [SegmentedControl] (npx serupa-docs SegmentedControl).

## Anatomy

Drawn from the `WithIcon` story.

1. **Leading icon** (`.srp-select__icon--start`): an optional picture of what is chosen.
2. **Field** (`.srp-select__field`): the native select, showing the chosen option.
3. **Chevron** (`.srp-select__icon--chevron`): says it opens a list.

## Usage

- Order options the way people expect: alphabetically, by frequency, or in their natural order (sizes, dates).
- Pick a sensible default when there is one; use a placeholder only when no default makes sense.
- Match its size to the inputs and buttons beside it.

### Do and don't

- **Do:** Give it a label above, in a [Field] (npx serupa-docs Field), which stays in view after a choice is made. (`DoLabelAbove`)
- **Don't:** Use the placeholder as the only label: once a value is chosen, nothing says what the field was for. (`DontPlaceholderLabel`)
- **Do:** Show two to four choices as [radios] (npx serupa-docs Radio), all in view at once. (`DoRadiosForFew`)
- **Don't:** Hide a few choices in a Select: people have to open it to see what they can pick. (`DontSelectForFew`)

## States

| State | Look |
| --- | --- |
| Rest | `field` background, 1px `field-border`, chevron in `text-muted` |
| Placeholder | The placeholder in the `placeholder` color until something is picked, and again after a form reset |
| Hover | `field-border-hover` |
| Focus | The border and a 1px ring hugging it in `focus-ring` (2px in all), like Input; a visible outline in forced-colors mode |
| Invalid | `danger` border, and a `danger` focus ring |
| Read-only | `field-readonly` background, default cursor, no hover change; the value at full contrast |
| Disabled | `field-readonly` background, `disabled-border` edge and `disabled-text` at full opacity, `not-allowed` cursor |
| Open, where the list is styled | `picker-bg` surface with a `picker-border` border, `picker-radius` corners and `picker-shadow`, at least as wide as the box and at most `picker-max-height` tall, then scrolling. Rows are `option-height` tall (`option-height-touch` on a touch screen) |
| Option under the pointer or keyboard | `option-bg-active` fill; with more contrast also a 2px `option-indicator` bar at the start edge, and in forced-colors mode a `Highlight` outline |
| Chosen option | A tick in `check` at the start |
| Disabled option | At 50% |
| Group label | `group-label`, `text-xs` medium |

## Accessibility

- A field the browser fills in (a saved address, a login) keeps the field's colors, and its border doubles inward until it's focused, so the fill shows in more than color.
- On iOS the field's text is 16px at every size, so Safari doesn't zoom the page when it takes focus; the box keeps its height.
- It's the browser's own select, so screen readers, the keyboard (arrows, Home/End, type to find) and the phone's picker all work without extra code.
- `readOnly` is for a value people should see but not change (a review step, a locked setting). The browser has no read-only select, so Select cancels the keys and press that would open or change it, and puts back a value a phone's picker sets. Unlike `disabled`, it stays in the Tab order and keeps its full contrast.
- Every select needs a name: Field, a `<label htmlFor>` or `aria-label`. The placeholder isn't a label.
- The chevron and left icon are decorative and don't take clicks: a click anywhere in the box opens the select.
- Text and placeholder keep 4.5:1 on `field`; the chevron, focus ring and invalid border 3:1, in every theme. In a styled list, options and group labels keep 4.5:1 on the list and on the highlight fill, and the tick 3:1; with more contrast the bar keeps 3:1 on the fill (`Select.test.tsx`). The fill alone is under 3:1 on the list, by design, as in Combobox and Menu (see `highlight-indicator`). The resting border is soft on purpose (`field-border`: about 1.5:1 in light, 1.4:1 to 1.9:1 in dark), under the 3:1 WCAG 1.4.11 asks of a control's edge: a deliberate design exception. The label above the field, its fill in dark, the stronger border on hover and the 3:1 focus ring mark it, and more contrast (`data-contrast="more"` or the system setting) brings back a 3:1+ border.
- Native constraints (`required` with an empty first option) show too: a field that fails them takes the `invalid` border once people have edited it or tried to send the form (`:user-invalid`), never on first paint. Inside a Field, the Field then says which constraint fails, in its error slot (in the provider's words), with `aria-invalid` and the description, so the border is never the only sign; an `error` you pass wins. On its own, the border is only a color: set `invalid` and say the problem in text when you check it yourself. To keep the browser out of it, leave out the attribute and check the value in your own code.

### Keyboard

| Key | Does |
| --- | --- |
| Tab | To the select |
| ↑ ↓ | The previous or next option (on macOS, and where the list is styled, opens the list; then moves through it) |
| Alt+↓, Space | Opens the list |
| Enter | In an open list, picks the option and closes it |
| Esc | Closes the open list without changing the value |
| A letter | The next option that starts with it |

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | string | none | Goes to the native `<select>` (not the wrapper), so a `<label htmlFor>` or a Field can point at it. |
| `size` | `'sm'` \| `'md'` \| `'lg'` | `'md'` | 24px with `text-xs`, 32px with `text-sm`, 44px with `text-base`, like Input |
| `options` | array | | Strings (value and label), `{ value, label, disabled }`, or groups `{ label, options, disabled }`. `<option>` and `<optgroup>` children come after them |
| `placeholder` | string | | A first, empty option shown in the placeholder color until something is picked. It can't be picked back. An uncontrolled Select starts on it |
| `startIcon` | icon name or element | | A decorative icon before the text (14, 16 or 20px, in `text-muted`) |
| `invalid` | boolean | `false` | A danger border and focus ring, and `aria-invalid` |
| `readOnly` | boolean | `false` | Focusable and read out (`aria-readonly`), and a form still sends the value, unlike `disabled`; keys, a press and the phone's picker don't change it, and `onChange` doesn't run |

Everything else (`value`, `defaultValue`, `onChange`, `name`, `disabled`, `required`, `id`, `aria-*`) and `ref` go to the `<select>`. `className` and `style` go to the box, so `className="w-48"` sets its width (full width by default). The box has `data-component="select"` and `data-size`. `multiple` isn't supported (a native multi-select is hard to use): it's ignored with a warning; use checkboxes. Inside a `<fieldset disabled>` the box takes the disabled look too, as the native select is disabled with it.

## Component tokens

Each is an optional override: set it on the page, a container or one select. The list lives in `src/components/Select/select.tokens.json` (also in `design-tokens/components/`). The defaults are the same shared tokens Input uses.

<!-- token-table:start (made from select.tokens.json by npm run tokens: edit the descriptions there) -->
**Colors**

| Token | Default | Use |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--select-bg` | `field` | Background, and the options where the browser draws them |
| `--select-bg-disabled` | `field-readonly` | Background when read-only or disabled |
| `--select-text` | `text` | The chosen value, and the options where the browser draws them |
| `--select-border` | `field-border` | Border |
| `--select-border-hover` | `field-border-hover` | Border on hover |
| `--select-placeholder` | `placeholder` | The placeholder |
| `--select-icon-color` | `text-muted` | Chevron and left icon |
| `--select-focus-ring` | `focus-ring` | Border and ring while focused |
| `--select-invalid` | `field-border-invalid` | Border and ring when invalid |
| `--select-picker-bg` | `surface-overlay` | The list of options, where the browser draws it with the page's styles (appearance: base-select). |
| `--select-picker-border` | `border-overlay` | The list's border. |
| `--select-option-bg-active` | `highlight` | The option under the pointer or the keyboard, as Combobox's. |
| `--select-option-indicator` | `highlight-indicator` | The 2px bar at the highlighted item's start: none by default (the gray fill marks it), `text`-dark with more contrast. |
| `--select-check` | `primary-text` | The tick by the chosen option. |

| `--select-border-disabled` | `disabled-border` | Disabled: the edge. |
| `--select-text-disabled` | `disabled-text` | Disabled: the text, icon or mark, in place of fading it (3:1 or more on its background, more with more contrast). |
| `--select-picker-divider` | `border-overlay` | What a divider or separator inside it reads as `border`: its own edge color, since in dark `border` is the surface's own color and a line in it vanished |

**Sizing**

| `--select-height-sm` | `control-height-sm` | Height, sm (24px), like Input sm. |
| `--select-height-md` | `control-height-md` | Height, md (32px, default). |
