components.name: ShowMore
components.summary: Long text cut after a few lines, with a "Show more" button under it that shows the rest.
components.guide:
# ShowMore

Long text cut after a few lines, with a "Show more" button under it that shows the rest. It keeps a list of reviews, comments or product descriptions short enough to scan, while each one is a press away from in full.

**Also called:** read more, expandable text.

```tsx
import { ShowMore } from "@diki-stwn/serupa-ds";

<ShowMore lines={3}>{review.text}</ShowMore>
```

## When to use

- A review, comment, bio or description that is sometimes long, in a list or a card where every item should take about the same room.
- Help text or terms under a form field that most people won't need to read in full.

## When not to use

- Text people must read before acting, such as a warning or a price condition: show all of it.
- A single line that has to fit, such as a file name: [Text] (npx serupa-docs Text) `truncate`.
- A section with its own heading that can be opened and closed: [Accordion] (npx serupa-docs Accordion).
- A preview that links to the full item on its own page: [Text] (npx serupa-docs Text) `lines`, with the link.

## Anatomy

Drawn from the `Expanded` story.

1. **Text** (`.srp-show-more__text`): the long text, cut after `lines` lines with an ellipsis while closed.
2. **Toggle** (`.srp-show-more__toggle`): the link-style button under the text, "Show more" or "Show less"; there only when the text is cut, or open.

## Usage

- Pick `lines` for the shortest useful preview: 2 or 3 in a dense list, 4 to 6 for a description on its own page.
- The button only appears when the text is cut, and its check runs again when the width changes, so a short comment shows as it is and a phone shows the button where a wide screen may not.
- Keep the children to text and inline content (links, emphasis) or a few paragraphs. A cut line is drawn with an ellipsis; a table or image inside would be cut off without one.
- Controlled, `expanded` with `onExpandedChange`, when something else opens it too (a "Show all" for the page). Otherwise `defaultExpanded`.

### Do and don't

- **Do:** Show enough to judge whether to read on: two or three lines of a review. (`DoEnoughLines`)
- **Don't:** One line, which says too little, so people open every one to find out. (`DontOneLine`)

## Accessibility

- **Role and name:** the button is a `<button>` named "Show more", then "Show less" (the `showMore` and `showLess` labels), with `aria-expanded` and `aria-controls` pointing at the text.
- **Hidden lines:** they are cut for the eye only. Screen readers read the whole text and find-in-page finds it, so nobody who can't see the screen misses any of it.
- **Keyboard:** Tab reaches the button; Enter or Space opens and closes. Focus stays on the button, which keeps its place under the text.
- **Contrast:** the button is a link-style [Button] (npx serupa-docs Button), 4.5:1 in every theme; the text keeps the color of where it sits.
- **What's still yours:** a heading or the author's name before each item, so people know whose text they're reading.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | `string` | | Goes to the outer `<div>`. |
| `lines` | `number` | `3` | Lines shown while closed (1 to 6; more counts as 6), the last cut with an ellipsis. |
| `expanded` | `boolean` | | Open (controlled). Use with `onExpandedChange`. |
| `defaultExpanded` | `boolean` | `false` | Open at first (uncontrolled). |
| `onExpandedChange` | `(expanded: boolean) => void` | | Called with the new state when the button is pressed. |
| `children` | `ReactNode` | | The long text. |

`className`, `ref` and other props go to the outer `<div>`, which has `data-component="show-more"` and `data-expanded` while open.

## Component tokens

Each is an optional override: set it on the page, a container or one ShowMore. The list lives in `src/components/ShowMore/show-more.tokens.json` (also in `design-tokens/components/`).

<!-- token-table:start (made from show-more.tokens.json by npm run tokens: edit the descriptions there) -->
| Token | Default | Use |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--show-more-gap` | `spacing-1` | Space between the text and the button (4px). |
<!-- token-table:end -->

components.name: Sidebar
components.summary: A vertical nav for an app's pages: an optional header (a logo, a workspace switcher), sections of items with icons, badges and nested groups, and a footer pinned to the bottom (settings, the signed-in user).
components.guide:
# Sidebar A vertical nav for an app's pages: an optional header (a logo, a workspace switcher), sections of items with icons, badges and nested groups, and a footer pinned to the bottom (settings, the signed-in user). `collapsed` narrows it to a 64px icon rail. **Also called:** side navigation, side nav, navigation rail. ```jsx import { Sidebar, SidebarSection, SidebarItem, Badge } from '@diki-stwn/serupa-ds';
} footer={} collapsed={collapsed}> } />
…
``` ## When to use - An app with many pages, or pages in sections and groups. - Navigation people use all the time, which should stay in view beside the content. - When the screen has room for a column, or for a 64px icon rail with `collapsed`. ## When not to use - A handful of top-level pages: use a [Navbar] (npx serupa-docs Navbar) instead. - Small screens: Sidebar doesn't hide on its own, so put the nav in a [Drawer] (npx serupa-docs Drawer) or use a [Navbar] (npx serupa-docs Navbar), whose links fold into a menu button. - Switching between views on one page: use [Tabs] (npx serupa-docs Tabs) instead. ## Anatomy Drawn from the `Playground` story. 1. **Header** (`.srp-sidebar__header`): the product's name or a switcher, at the top. 2. **Section title** (`.srp-sidebar__section-title`): names a group of links. 3. **Link** (`.srp-sidebar__item`): a page to go to. 4. **Current link** (`.srp-sidebar__item--active`): the page you're on. 5. **Icon** (`.srp-sidebar__icon`): a picture of the page; it alone shows when the sidebar is collapsed, with the name as a tooltip. 6. **Badge** (`.srp-sidebar__badge`): an optional count, such as unread items. 7. **Nested links** (`.srp-sidebar__list--nested`): the pages under a link, shown when it's open. 8. **Footer** (`.srp-sidebar__footer`): the account or settings, at the bottom. ## Usage It takes its parent's height and scrolls its items when they don't fit, so give the parent a height (a full-height flex row, as above). - Give top-level items an `icon`, so they still show when the sidebar is collapsed, and use a string `label` so the tooltip can show it. - Group related items under a `SidebarSection` with a short `title`; keep nesting to one level of SidebarItems. - Mark the current page with `current`; a group holding it, at any depth, starts open. - Put settings and the signed-in user in `footer`, so they stay at the bottom. - Collapsed, the header and footer have the 64px rail too: pass a logo mark or an avatar then, such as a [Logo] (npx serupa-docs Logo) with `variant={collapsed ? "mark" : "full"}`. Longer text there ends in an ellipsis rather than spilling over the page. - Collapsing and expanding slide over 200ms without laying out the page on every frame. The column's width changes once: at the start when expanding, and at the end when collapsing. In between, only the sidebar's visible edge moves, so a heavy page beside it doesn't stutter. Toggling again mid-way turns back from where it is. With reduced motion it switches at once. ### Do and don't - **Do:** Group related pages under `SidebarSection`s with short titles. (`DoGroupSections`) - **Don't:** Put every page in one long run: people have to read it top to bottom to find anything. (`DontFlatList`) ## Accessibility - It's a `
` landmark with lists of links; section titles name their lists. - The current page has `aria-current="page"`, a shaded background and, when more contrast is asked for, a 2px bar at its start. Hover shades an item (`surface-hover`, zinc-100 in light, like the current page) but never draws the bar; the current page itself darkens one step under the pointer. A group holding it is text-colored, so the trail stays visible when it's closed. - A group is a button with `aria-expanded` and `aria-controls`. A closed group's items are `hidden="until-found"`: find-in-page still finds them, and a match opens the group. - A label too long for the sidebar ends in an ellipsis and shows in full in a tooltip on hover and on the item's keyboard focus, while screen readers read it whole from the item. - Collapsed, each label stays in the page for screen readers and shows as a tooltip on hover and focus, on a group's button too. Use a string `label` so the tooltip can show it. - Collapsed, an item's badge is hidden on screen like its label but still read: the tooltip names the item ("Inbox") and the badge describes it ("4"), and an 8px dot on the icon's corner shows there is one. The dot keeps 3:1 in every theme, and is CanvasText in forced-colors mode. - In a collapsed rail, a group's menu keeps each item's link component (`as`, such as a router's Link, with its own props) and its link attributes, and marks the current page with `aria-current="page"` in medium weight. - Items, the current page, hovered items and section titles keep 4.5:1 in every theme (`Sidebar.test.tsx`). - **Keyboard:** Tab moves through the items. Enter follows a link, and Enter or Space opens or closes a group. Collapsed, focus shows each label as a tooltip, and a group opens its items in a Menu, with the Menu's own keys. ## Props ### Sidebar | Prop | Type | Default | What it does | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `id` | string | none | Goes to the root `
`. | | `children` | SidebarSections or SidebarItems | none | The items | | `header` | node | none | Above the items | | `footer` | node | none | Pinned to the bottom, under a line | | `collapsed` | boolean | `false` | A 64px rail of icons. Labels, text or elements, become tooltips (and stay the items' names); groups open their items in a menu. Switching keeps focus in the item it was in: a nested link's focus goes to its group's button | | `aria-label` | string | `"Main"` | The nav's name | `className`, `style`, `ref` and everything else go to the `
`, which has `data-component="sidebar"`. ### SidebarSection | Prop | Type | Default | What it does | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `title` | node | none | A small heading that names the section's list. Hidden when collapsed | ### SidebarItem | Prop | Type | Default | What it does | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `label` | node | required | The item's text | | `icon` | an icon name or element | none | A 20px icon; top-level items need one to show when collapsed | | `current` | boolean | `false` | The current page: shaded, with a bar in the primary color and `aria-current="page"` | | `badge` | node | none | At the end, such as a count Badge. Collapsed, a dot on the icon shows there is one, and screen readers still read the badge | | `children` | SidebarItems | none | Makes it a group: a button that shows and hides them. They unfold and fold with the chevron, as an Accordion panel does (only a fade under reduced motion); opened or closed from the keyboard, they show and hide at once | | `defaultOpen` | boolean | open when a child is active | Whether a group starts open | | `open` | boolean | none | Whether a group is open, controlled. Pair it with `onOpenChange` | | `onOpenChange` | (open, { reason }) => void | none | Called when the group's button asks to open or close it, with `reason: 'trigger'` | | `as` | a component | the `configure({ link })` link, else `'a'` | Your router's link component. Set it once for the app with `configure({ link })`; `as` wins for one item. Typed: the props are those of the element `as` names, so `as={RouterLink} to="/inbox"` checks `to`, and without `as` they're an ``'s. A link set only with `configure({ link })` is typed as an ``, so pass it `href`. The `ref` is an `HTMLElement`: the link, or a group's button. | `href`, `className`, `ref` and everything else go to the link (an ``, or what `as` names), or to a group's button. ## Component tokens Each is an optional override: set it on the page, a container or one sidebar. The list lives in `src/components/Sidebar/sidebar.tokens.json` (also in `design-tokens/components/`). **Colors** | Token | Default | Use | | --- | --- | --- | | `--sidebar-bg` | `surface` | The sidebar's background. | | `--sidebar-border` | `border` | The line on its inner edge. | | `--sidebar-item-text` | `text-muted` | An item (4.5:1 on bg). | | `--sidebar-item-text-hover` | `text` | An item on hover. | | `--sidebar-item-text-active` | `text` | The current page's item. | | `--sidebar-dot` | `primary-text` | Collapsed: the dot on an item's icon when it has a badge (3:1 on bg and on the current page's highlight). | | `--sidebar-item-bg-hover` | `surface-hover` | An item's background on hover: zinc-100 in light themes, as the current page's, so the shade shows on a white sidebar. Only the current page draws the bar, with more contrast. | | `--sidebar-item-bg-pressed` | `pressed` | An item's background while it's pressed, one step past hover. | | `--sidebar-item-bg-active` | `highlight` | The current page's item background. | | `--sidebar-item-bg-active-hover` | `pressed` | The current page's item background under the pointer: one step past its rest. | | `--sidebar-item-indicator` | `highlight-indicator` | The 2px bar at the start of the current page's item, which hover never draws. Drawn only with more contrast: by default it has no width (`highlight-indicator-width`), and the fill alone marks the item. | | `--sidebar-section-title-color` | `text-muted` | A section's title (4.5:1 on bg). | | `--sidebar-focus-ring` | `focus-ring` | The keyboard focus ring. | | `--sidebar-focus-gap-color` | `surface` | The gap between the focus ring and a filled item (the current page, or a hovered or pressed one), so the ring keeps 3:1 against what it touches. | **Type** | Token | Default | Use | | --- | --- | --- | | `--sidebar-item-size` | `text-sm` | Item text (14px). | | `--sidebar-item-weight` | `font-medium` | Item weight (500). | | `--sidebar-section-title-size` | `text-xs` | Section titles (12px). | **Sizing** | Token | Default | Use | | --- | --- | --- | | `--sidebar-width` | `container-3xs` | The sidebar's width (256px). | | `--sidebar-width-collapsed` | `spacing-16` | Its width when collapsed to icons (64px). | | `--sidebar-icon-size` | `spacing-5` | An item's icon (20px). | **Spacing** | Token | Default | Use | | --- | --- | --- | | `--sidebar-padding` | `spacing-3` | Space inside the sidebar (12px). | | `--sidebar-item-padding-x` | `spacing-3` | An item's side padding (12px). | | `--sidebar-item-padding-y` | `space-item` | An item's top and bottom padding: 8px, 4px in the compact density. | | `--sidebar-item-gap` | `spacing-3` | Space between an item's icon and label (12px). | | `--sidebar-section-gap` | `spacing-6` | Space between sections (24px). | | `--sidebar-nested-indent` | `spacing-11` | Where nested items' labels start, lined up with their parent's label (44px). | **Border** | Token | Default | Use | | --- | --- | --- | | `--sidebar-border-width` | `border-width-1` | The edge line (1px). | **Radius** | Token | Default | Use | | --- | --- | --- | | `--sidebar-item-radius` | `radius-control` | An item's corners (6px). |

components.name: SidebarLayout
components.summary: Puts a narrow column beside a wide one, and stacks them once the space gets too narrow for both.
components.guide:
# SidebarLayout

Puts a narrow column beside a wide one, and stacks them once the space gets too narrow for both. It follows the space it's in rather than the screen, so filters beside results, a summary beside a form or a list beside its detail need no CSS of their own.

**Also called:** two-column layout, aside layout, split layout.

```tsx
import { SidebarLayout, Card } from "@diki-stwn/serupa-ds";

<SidebarLayout sidebar={<Card>…filters…</Card>}>
  …results…
</SidebarLayout>

<SidebarLayout sidebarPlacement="end" sidebarWidth="container-xs" sidebar={<Card>…order summary…</Card>}>
  …the form…
</SidebarLayout>
```

## When to use

- Filters beside a list of results, a page's sections beside its content, a summary beside a form, a list beside the detail of the item picked.
- Two columns that should stack on a phone without a breakpoint of your own, including inside a Dialog, a Drawer or a Card.

## When not to use

- The app's navigation beside every page: use [AppShell] (npx serupa-docs AppShell) with a [Sidebar] (npx serupa-docs Sidebar) instead.
- Columns of equal width: use [Grid] (npx serupa-docs Grid) instead.
- Two panes people resize by dragging: use [Splitter] (npx serupa-docs Splitter) instead.

## Anatomy

Drawn from the `Playground` story.

1. **Sidebar** (`.srp-sidebar-layout__side`): the narrow column, `sidebarWidth` wide while the two share a line.
2. **Content** (`.srp-sidebar-layout__content`): the wide column, which takes the rest.

## Usage

- Put what supports the content in the narrow column, and the content itself in `children`. On a phone the narrow column comes first (or last, with `sidebarPlacement="end"`), so keep it short.
- `sidebarWidth` takes a sizing token name: `container-3xs` (256px, the default) for filters, `container-xs` (320px) for a summary with prices.
- `contentMin` (50 by default) is how narrow the wide column may get, as a percentage of the whole, before the two stack. Raise it when the content needs more room, such as a table.
- `align="start"` keeps each column its own height, so a short side doesn't stretch down beside a long page. Leave it at `stretch` for two panels side by side.

### Do and don't

- **Do:** Put what helps people with the main content in the narrow column: filters, a summary, a page's sections. (`DoSupportingSide`)
- **Don't:** Put the page's main content in the narrow column: on a phone it comes first, and people scroll past it to find the rest. (`DontMainInSide`)

## Accessibility

- **Role and name:** none of its own: a layout box. Give each column the landmark or heading it needs, such as `<aside aria-label="Filters">` or a Card `as="section"` with `aria-labelledby`.
- **Keyboard:** none: a layout box, not focusable.
- **Reading order:** the HTML follows what people see: the narrow column first with `sidebarPlacement="start"`, last with `"end"`, side by side or stacked, so the Tab order matches the screen (WCAG 1.3.2, 2.4.3). Nothing is reordered with CSS.
- **Reflow:** at 320px, or at 400% zoom, the columns stack and nothing scrolls sideways (1.4.10).
- **What's still yours:** the headings and landmarks inside each column.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | string | none | Goes to the root element (`as`). |
| `sidebar` | ReactNode | required | The narrow column |
| `children` | ReactNode | none | The wide column |
| `sidebarPlacement` | `'start'` \| `'end'` | `'start'` | Which side the narrow column is on, in the HTML too |
| `sidebarWidth` | string | `'container-3xs'` (256px) | The narrow column's width side by side: a sizing token name or a CSS length |
| `contentMin` | number, 1 to 99 | `50` | The narrowest the wide column gets, as a percentage of the whole, before the two stack |
| `gap` | a spacing step: `0` to `24` | `6` (24px) | The space between the columns |
| `align` | `'stretch'` \| `'start'` | `'stretch'` | Both as tall as the taller, or each its own height |
| `as` | `'div'` \| `'section'` \| `'main'` \| `'article'` | `'div'` | The element |

A value that isn't on the list falls back to the default. `className`, `style`, `ref` and everything else go to the element, which has `data-component="sidebar-layout"`. Each column is a `<div>`: `.srp-sidebar-layout__side` and `.srp-sidebar-layout__content`.

## Component tokens

Each is an optional override: set it on the page, a container or one SidebarLayout. The list lives in `src/components/SidebarLayout/sidebar-layout.tokens.json` (also in `design-tokens/components/`).

<!-- token-table:start (made from sidebar-layout.tokens.json by npm run tokens: edit the descriptions there) -->
| Token | Default | Use |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--sidebar-layout-side-width` | `container-3xs` | The narrow column's width side by side, when sidebarWidth isn't given (256px). |
| `--sidebar-layout-gap` | `spacing-6` | The space between the columns when gap isn't given (24px). |
<!-- token-table:end -->

components.name: SignaturePad
components.summary: A place to sign: people draw their signature with a mouse, pen or finger, or type their full name instead.
components.guide:
# SignaturePad

A place to sign: people draw their signature with a mouse, pen or finger, or type their full name instead. The app gets the signature as SVG (and a PNG from `signatureToPng`), with the typed name.

**Also called:** signature field, e-signature input.

```tsx
import { Field, SignaturePad, signatureToPng } from "@diki-stwn/serupa-ds";

<Field label="Sign to accept the terms" error={error}>
  <SignaturePad name="signature" onValueChange={(value) => setSignature(value)} />
</Field>

// later, for an app that stores pictures
const png = signature && await signatureToPng(signature.svg);
```

## When to use

- Accepting terms, a delivery, a consent form or a timesheet, where a signature is expected and a typed name counts as one.
- Anywhere the app keeps the picture of a signature to show or print later.

## When not to use

- A legally qualified electronic signature (one tied to a certificate or an identity check): that is a service's job; use its own flow.
- A plain "I agree": use a [Checkbox] (npx serupa-docs Checkbox).
- Collecting a name only: use an [Input] (npx serupa-docs Input) with `autoComplete="name"`.

## Anatomy

Drawn from the `Playground` story.

1. **Method switch** (`.srp-signature-pad__method`): a [SegmentedControl] (npx serupa-docs SegmentedControl), Draw or Type.
2. **How-to text** (`.srp-signature-pad__how`): what to do; while drawing it points to Type. It describes the group.
3. **Box** (`.srp-signature-pad__box`): an outlined surface with a line near its foot; the strokes, or the typed name, sit on the line.
4. **Actions** (`.srp-signature-pad__actions`): Undo (the last stroke) and Clear (every stroke), while drawing.

## Usage

- Name it: a [Field] (npx serupa-docs Field) label ("Sign to accept the terms") or `aria-label`. In a Field, its hint and error describe it.
- Keep Type: it's how people who can't draw with a pointer sign (WCAG 2.5.7 Dragging movements, 2.1.1 Keyboard), and some people prefer it. Treat a typed name as a signature as much as a drawing.
- `onValueChange(value, details)` gives `{ method, svg, name }` (null while empty) after each stroke, undo, clear, typed change or switch, with `details.reason`. The SVG is a standalone document sized to the box, in black, so it prints on paper whatever the theme.
- With `name`, a hidden input sends the SVG with the form ("" while empty), and `form.reset()` empties it. Check that it isn't empty yourself, and show the error in the Field.
- To show a saved signature, pass it back as `defaultValue` (or `value`, controlled): a typed one by its `name`, a drawn one by the SVG SignaturePad made.
- `defaultMethod="type"` starts on the name field, as on a page most people fill in with a keyboard.
- A drawing and a typed name are kept apart while people switch; the value follows the method shown.

### Do and don't

- **Do:** Name it with a [Field] (npx serupa-docs Field) label that says what signing means ("Sign to accept the terms"). (`DoSayWhatItMeans`)
- **Don't:** Show a bare pad: people don't know what they're agreeing to. (`DontBarePad`)

## Accessibility

- **Role and name:** a `group` named by its Field label or `aria-label`, described by its how-to text (and a Field's hint and error). The method switch is a radio group named "Signature method"; when the signature is invalid, it and the name field carry `aria-invalid` (a group can't). The drawing box is an image named "Signature area, empty" or "Signature drawn".
- **Keyboard:** Tab reaches the switch; the arrow keys pick Draw or Type. The drawing box isn't a Tab stop, because nothing in it works by keyboard; Type is the keyboard way, and the how-to text says so. In Type, the "Full name" field takes the name. Undo and Clear are buttons; when they empty the box, focus goes back to the switch.
- **Touch:** the page doesn't scroll while a finger draws in the box (`touch-action: none`); it scrolls as usual everywhere else.
- **Contrast:** on the surface, the how-to text and the ink read 4.5:1, and the line 3:1, in every theme; the box outline is the field's border, as a Textarea has (`SignaturePad.test.tsx`). In forced colors, the outline, line and ink use the system text color.
- **What's still yours:** the label, telling people what they're signing, and the error when they haven't.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | `string` | | Goes to the root `<div role="group">`. A `<label htmlFor>` can't name a group; inside a Field, the Field's label names it through this id. |
| `value` | `SignatureValue \| null` | | The signature (controlled), as `onValueChange` gave it or as saved before. A drawn one is read back from its SVG's paths. |
| `defaultValue` | `SignatureValue \| null` | | The signature at first (uncontrolled), such as one saved before; `form.reset()` goes back to it. |
| `onValueChange` | `(value: SignatureValue \| null, details: { reason }) => void` | | After each stroke, undo, clear, typed change or switch of method. `reason`: `"draw"`, `"undo"`, `"clear"`, `"type"`, `"method"` or `"reset"`. |
| `defaultMethod` | `"draw" \| "type"` | `"draw"` | How it starts. |
| `name` | `string` | | Sends the SVG with a form in a hidden input. |
| `form` | `string` | | The id of a form elsewhere on the page. |
| `disabled` | `boolean` | `false` | Turns drawing, typing and the buttons off. |
| `readOnly` | `boolean` | `false` | Shows a signature already given: nothing draws, the method switch and a typed name are read-only but still focusable, Undo, Clear and the how-to text are left out, and the form still sends it, unlike `disabled`. |
| `invalid` | `boolean` | `false` | `aria-invalid` and a danger outline. Field sets it from its error. |
| `required` | `boolean` | `false` | A signature must be given: the form isn't sent without one (the pad is marked invalid and its method switch takes focus), and the typed name is `aria-required`. |

`SignatureValue` is `{ method: "draw" | "type"; svg: string; name: string }`. `signatureToPng(svg, scale = 2)` resolves to a PNG `Blob` drawn in the browser (null on the server). `className`, `ref` and other props go to the group's `<div>`; `ref.current.focus()` and `autoFocus` focus the method switch.

## Component tokens

Each is an optional override: set it on the page, a container or one SignaturePad. The list lives in `src/components/SignaturePad/signature-pad.tokens.json` (also in `design-tokens/components/`).

<!-- token-table:start (made from signature-pad.tokens.json by npm run tokens: edit the descriptions there) -->
| Token | Default | Use |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--signature-pad-bg` | `surface` | The drawing box's background. |
| `--signature-pad-bg-readonly` | `field-readonly` | The drawing box's background while read-only: a step flatter, as a read-only field's, so a saved signature reads as not editable. |
| `--signature-pad-border` | `field-border` | The drawing box's outline: the field's border, as a Textarea has. The line marks where to sign (3:1). |
| `--signature-pad-border-invalid` | `danger` | The drawing box's outline while the signature is invalid (3:1). |
| `--signature-pad-ink` | `text` | The drawn strokes and the typed name (4.5:1 on bg). |
| `--signature-pad-line` | `text-muted` | The line to sign on (3:1 on bg). |
| `--signature-pad-hint` | `text-muted` | The how-to text under the switch (4.5:1). |
| `--signature-pad-radius` | `radius-control` | The drawing box's corners. |
| `--signature-pad-gap` | `spacing-2` | The space between the switch, the how-to text, the box and the buttons. |
| `--signature-pad-height` | `spacing-40` | The drawing box's height (160px). |
| `--signature-pad-stroke` | `border-width-2` | The drawn strokes' width on screen (the SVG value draws them 2.5px). |
<!-- token-table:end -->

components.name: Skeleton
components.summary: Gray placeholder shapes where content is loading, so the layout is already in place and nothing jumps when the content arrives.
components.guide:
# Skeleton Gray placeholder shapes where content is loading, so the layout is already in place and nothing jumps when the content arrives. Lines stand in for text, a circle for an avatar, a rectangle for an image or a card. It replaces ``, which is deprecated and leaves in the next major. **Also called:** placeholder, shimmer, loading placeholder. ```tsx import { Skeleton } from "@diki-stwn/serupa-ds"; // one line of text-sm, full width // a paragraph: the last line is 60% wide // an avatar, 40px // an image or card // the shape of what's coming: name one skeleton, the rest are decorative
``` ## When to use - The layout of what's coming is known, such as a list, a card, a profile or a table, so placeholders can hold its place while it loads. ## When not to use - You can't tell what shape the content will take, or the wait is a task rather than content (a search, an AI reply): use [Loader] (npx serupa-docs Loader). - Waits you can measure (uploads, imports): use [Progress] (npx serupa-docs Progress). - A list, table or grid that loads its own rows: Table, List, DataGrid, Kanban and Chart draw their own skeleton rows while `loading` is set. ## Anatomy Drawn from the `Profile` story. 1. **Skeleton** (`.srp-skeleton`): the whole placeholder, named "Loading" (or your label) for screen readers. 2. **Line** (`.srp-skeleton__line`): one line of text, as tall as the size's text line. 3. **Bone** (`.srp-skeleton__bone`): the gray shape with the sweeping shine. ## Usage - **text** (default): `lines` lines, each as tall as the size's text line (16, 20 or 24px) with a bar as tall as the type (12, 14 or 16px) and `radius-inner` corners. Full width; with several lines the last is 60% wide, so it reads as a paragraph. Give it a width class (`w-1/2`, `w-48`) for a short line such as a name. - **circle**: 16, 24 or 40px at `sm`, `md` and `lg`, fully round. `className="size-12"` sets another size. - **rect**: full width and 96px tall (`--skeleton-rect-height`), `radius-control` corners. Set the size with classes (`h-40`, `w-48 h-32`); for a ratio, `h-auto aspect-video`. - Lines and rects stretch to their container and shrink beside an avatar in a row, while the circle keeps its size. - Match the real layout closely and keep it short: a few rows, not a screenful. - On a dark scrim, photo or video, `tone="inverse"` makes it white. Not on `surface-inverse`, which turns light in dark themes: there, leave the tone as `neutral` and it takes `text-inverse` from its parent. - If loading fails, replace it with an error message and a way to retry. The fill is the text color at 10% (`--skeleton-fill`), so it fits any surface and theme. A lighter band (the text color at 5%) sweeps through it from left to right every 2 seconds, easing in and out. ### Show-after delay and minimum time Like Loader, it waits 300ms before it shows, so a quick load never flashes it; while it waits it is hidden but its shapes keep their space. Once shown it stays at least 500ms: keep it mounted and pass `loading={false}` when the content arrives, rather than removing it, and it renders nothing once the 500ms are up. ## Accessibility - **Role and name:** a skeleton with a label is a `role="progressbar"` without a value, named by `label` ("Loading…"), and `label` is announced once through the shared polite status region when it appears. `label=""` makes it decorative (`aria-hidden`). - In a group of skeletons, name one ("Loading profile") and pass `label=""` to the rest, so it's announced once, and set `aria-busy` on the area. - **Keyboard:** none: it isn't focusable. - **Contrast:** it's a placeholder, not content: the fill is the text color at 10%, which isn't held to a contrast ratio. - In forced colors (Windows high contrast) the browser drops background colors, so the bones keep a still `GrayText` fill instead of going blank. - Under reduced motion it's a still fill, without the shine. - **What's still yours:** `aria-busy` on the area that's loading, and moving focus sensibly when the content replaces it. ## Props | Prop | Type | Default | Notes | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `shape` | `'text'` \| `'circle'` \| `'rect'` | `'text'` | Lines of text, an avatar, or an image or card | | `lines` | number, 1 to 20 | `1` | With `shape="text"`: how many lines | | `size` | `'sm'` \| `'md'` \| `'lg'` | `'md'` | Text lines `text-xs`, `text-sm` or `text-base`; the circle 16, 24 or 40px | | `tone` | `'neutral'` \| `'inverse'` | `'neutral'` | `neutral` takes the text color; `inverse` is white in every theme, for dark scrims and media | | `label` | string | `'Loading…'` | Its accessible name, announced when it appears. `''` makes it decorative | | `delay` | number (ms) | `300` | Waits this long before showing. `0` shows it at once | | `loading` | boolean | `true` | Pass `false` when the content arrives. Once shown, it stays at least 500ms, then renders nothing | | `id` | string | none | Goes to the root ``. | `className`, `style`, `ref` and other attributes go to the outer ``, which has `data-component="skeleton"`, `data-shape` and `data-size` for tests. ## Component tokens Each is an optional override: set it on the page, a container or one Skeleton. The list lives in `src/components/Skeleton/skeleton.tokens.json` (also in `design-tokens/components/`). ```css .gallery { --skeleton-rect-height: var(--spacing-48); } ``` | Token | Default | Use | | --- | --- | --- | | `--skeleton-inverse` | `white` | Color with `tone="inverse"` | | `--skeleton-size-sm` | `spacing-4` | The circle at size sm (16px) | | `--skeleton-size-md` | `spacing-6` | The circle at size md (24px) | | `--skeleton-size-lg` | `spacing-10` | The circle at size lg (40px) | | `--skeleton-rect-height` | `spacing-24` | Height of the rect when no class sets one (96px) | | `--skeleton-fill` | `opacity-10` | Strength of the fill (the text color) | | `--skeleton-shine` | `opacity-5` | Strength of the band that sweeps through it | | `--skeleton-radius` | `radius-control` | Corners of the rect (6px) | | `--skeleton-text-radius` | `radius-inner` | Corners of the text lines (4px) |

components.name: SkipLink
components.summary: The "Skip to content" link that keyboard and screen reader users need first on every page (WCAG 2.4.1 Bypass Blocks).
components.guide:
# SkipLink

The "Skip to content" link that keyboard and screen reader users need first on every page (WCAG 2.4.1 Bypass Blocks). It's out of sight until Tab reaches it, then shows at the top of the page; following it moves focus to the main content, past the header and navigation.

**Also called:** skip to content link.

```tsx
import { SkipLink } from "@diki-stwn/serupa-ds";

<SkipLink />
<Navbar sticky>…</Navbar>
<main id="main">…</main>
```

## When to use

- Once on every page with a header or navigation before its main content: put it first in the `<body>`, before the Navbar.

## When not to use

- For links within a page's content (a table of contents, "Back to top"): use a [Link] (npx serupa-docs Link) to the section's `#id`.
- For something only screen readers should read: use [VisuallyHidden] (npx serupa-docs VisuallyHidden).

## Usage

- Give the main content `id="main"`, or pass its id as `target`. With no element of that id on the page, following it warns in development and does nothing more than a plain `#` link.
- Its text is "Skip to content" (`labels.skipToContent`, "Langsung ke konten" in Indonesian). Pass children for other words, such as "Skip to results" with `target="results"`.
- It's a real link to `#main`, so it works before the script loads, and the address shows `#main` after it's followed.

### Do and don't

- **Do:** Say where it goes: "Skip to content", or "Skip to results" with `target="results"`. (`DoSayWhere`)
- **Don't:** Write "Click here": it says nothing about where it goes. (`DontClickHere`)

## Accessibility

- **Role and name:** a link, named by its text.
- **Keyboard:** the first Tab on the page shows it at the top start of the viewport, above a sticky Navbar, with the focus ring. Enter moves focus to the target, even when that isn't focusable, such as a `<main>`: it gets `tabindex="-1"` until focus leaves it, so it isn't left as a stray tab stop. The next Tab goes on from inside the main content.
- **Not covered:** a sticky [Navbar] (npx serupa-docs Navbar) keeps the page's `scroll-padding-top` at its height, so the target scrolls into view below the bar, not under it (WCAG 2.4.11).
- **Contrast:** its text reads 4.5:1 on its background in every theme (`SkipLink.test.tsx`). In forced colors its border is CanvasText. It isn't printed.
- **What's still yours:** one SkipLink, first on the page, and a target that holds the main content.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `target` | `string` | `"main"` | The id of the element it skips to. |
| `children` | `ReactNode` | "Skip to content" | The link's text. |
| `id` | `string` | | Goes to the `<a>`. |
| `onClick` | `(e) => void` | | Called first; call `e.preventDefault()` to stop it moving focus. |

`className`, `ref` and other props go to the `<a>`.

## Component tokens

Each is an optional override: set it on the page, a container or one SkipLink. The list lives in `src/components/SkipLink/skip-link.tokens.json` (also in `design-tokens/components/`).

<!-- token-table:start (made from skip-link.tokens.json by npm run tokens: edit the descriptions there) -->
| Token | Default | Use |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--skip-link-bg` | `surface-raised` | The shown link's background. |
| `--skip-link-text` | `primary-text` | The link's text (4.5:1 on its background). |
| `--skip-link-border` | `border` | The shown link's border. |
| `--skip-link-focus-ring` | `focus-ring` | The focus ring around it while it's shown. |
| `--skip-link-shadow` | `elevation-overlay` | Lifts it above the page and a sticky Navbar. |
| `--skip-link-radius` | `radius-control` | Its corners. |
| `--skip-link-border-width` | `border-width-1` | Its border's width. |
| `--skip-link-offset` | `spacing-3` | How far it sits from the viewport's top and start edges. |
| `--skip-link-padding-x` | `spacing-4` | Space at its start and end. |
| `--skip-link-padding-y` | `spacing-2` | Space above and below its text. |
<!-- token-table:end -->

components.name: Slider
components.summary: Picks a number, or a range with two thumbs, by dragging along a track or with the keyboard.
components.guide:
# Slider

Picks a number, or a range with two thumbs, by dragging along a track or with the keyboard. Use it when the exact number matters less than its place in a range (volume, a price filter); for exact numbers, use NumberInput, or pair the two.

**Also called:** range input, range slider.

```tsx
import { Slider } from "@diki-stwn/serupa-ds";

<Slider aria-label="Volume" defaultValue={50} />

const [price, setPrice] = React.useState<[number, number]>([20, 80]);
<Slider aria-label="Price" value={price} onValueChange={setPrice} max={200} step={5} formatValue={(v) => `$${v}`} />
```

## When to use

- A value where its place in a range matters more than the exact number: volume, brightness, a zoom level.
- A range with two ends, such as a price filter (pass a pair as the value).

## When not to use

- An exact number people type, such as a quantity: use [NumberInput] (npx serupa-docs NumberInput), or pair the two.
- A few named options, such as Small, Medium, Large: use [SegmentedControl] (npx serupa-docs SegmentedControl) or [radios] (npx serupa-docs Radio).

## Anatomy

Drawn from the `Marks` story.

1. **Track** (`.srp-slider__track`): the whole range.
2. **Fill** (`.srp-slider__fill`): the part up to the value.
3. **Thumb** (`.srp-slider__thumb`): drag it, or focus it and use the arrow keys, to set the value.
4. **Mark** (`.srp-slider__mark-label`): a named value along the track.
5. **Value** (`.srp-slider__value`): the value, in words or numbers.

## Usage

- Show a visible label next to it and point `aria-labelledby` at it, or use `aria-label`.
- Use `formatValue` whenever the number has a unit or a currency, so screen readers hear "$40", not "40".
- Update what's on screen in `onValueChange`, and save or fetch in `onValueCommit`, which runs once per change.
- Set `step` to the precision people need, so values snap to sensible numbers.
- In a narrow column, such as a mixer or a level beside a picture, set `orientation="vertical"`. Keep it horizontal everywhere else: a horizontal track is easier to read and to label.
- For a value with a middle, such as a balance or an offset from -10 to +10, set `origin={0}` so the fill starts in the middle and shows which way it leans.
- Use `marks` when a few values matter, such as `[{ value: 0, label: "Off" }, { value: 100, label: "Max" }]`, or `marks` alone for a tick per step on a short scale. Keep the labels short: they sit on one line under the track while there's room, and wrap when it's narrow.
- Use `showValue` when people need to see the number while they drag, and there is no label nearby that shows it.
- Use `inputs` when an exact number matters as much as the rough one, such as a price filter: a number field (`.srp-slider__input`, a [NumberInput] (npx serupa-docs NumberInput)) sits beside each thumb, after the track for one and at either end for a range. It brings NumberInput's code with it, so a page that imports Slider and not NumberInput grows by about 6.5 KiB.

## Behavior

- A press anywhere on the track moves the nearest thumb there, and dragging follows the pointer even off the slider. On a touch screen, a swipe across the page that starts on the slider scrolls the page instead (`touch-action: pan-y`, `pan-x` when vertical): the thumb goes back and nothing commits.
- Range thumbs can't cross.
- The thumb grows a little while pressed; it doesn't with `prefers-reduced-motion`.
- `marks` draws a tick for each mark between the ends, and its label centered under it. With labels, the slider is taller by one line of small text, so nothing overlaps what follows. A label longer than its room (the track up to halfway to the next mark, less 8px, `--slider-mark-label-gap`) wraps within it, and the slider grows to hold the extra lines. `true` draws a mark per step, or one per `largeStep` steps past 100 marks. Marks off the track are left out. A press on a label moves the nearest thumb there.
- With `inputs`, a number typed in a field moves its thumb at once, and a thumb that moves rewrites its field. A field takes numbers between `min` and `max` (for a range, up to the other thumb); one past them waits for Enter or for the field to be left, then comes back inside. `onValueCommit` runs when the field is left or Enter pressed after a change, as at the end of a drag. The fields show the number itself in the locale's digits, not `formatValue`'s words.
- `showValue` shows the value, as `formatValue` writes it (without one, the number in the locale's digits: "٤٠" in `ar-EG`), in a small chip over a thumb while it's focused, hovered or dragged. The chip floats and takes no room, so leave space above the slider. Near an end, the chip and the end mark labels move inward, so they stay inside the slider's box.

### Do and don't

- **Do:** Use `formatValue` for a value with a unit or currency, and write the mark labels the same way. (`DoFormatValue`)
- **Don't:** Leave a price or a measurement as a bare number: people and screen readers can't tell its unit. (`DontBareNumber`)

## Accessibility

- The slider takes a press over at least 24px of height (WCAG 2.5.8), past the 20px thumb, without taking more room, and 44px on a touch screen, as Apple and Material ask.
- Each thumb is a native `<input type="range">` (role `slider`) over the drawn one, unseen, with its value, `min`, `max`, `step` and `aria-orientation`. Screen readers' adjust gestures (VoiceOver's swipe up and down, TalkBack's volume keys) work reliably only on a native range, and they move the thumb by `step` and call `onValueCommit` as a key does. A range's thumbs limit each other, and the pair is a named `group`.
- The fill and the thumb's ring keep 3:1 on the page in every theme, so the control and its value can be seen (`Slider.test.tsx`). The track is a light gray fill inside the basic border, as Meter's and Progress's. In forced-colors mode it uses system colors.
- In a [Field] (npx serupa-docs Field), the label names the thumb (a range's group) through `aria-labelledby`, and the hint and error describe it. Its own `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby` wins.
- `invalid` sets `aria-invalid` on each thumb and turns the fill and the thumb's ring danger (3:1 on the page in every theme). Color alone doesn't say what's wrong, so put the reason in text next to it: inside a [Field] (npx serupa-docs Field), its `error` does both.
- `readOnly` keeps the thumbs in the Tab order with `aria-readonly`, so people can still hear the value, but keys and presses don't change it. With `name`, the value is still sent with the form, which `disabled` doesn't do.
- A slider always has a value, so `required` has nothing to check. It's accepted, so Field's `required` doesn't reach the DOM, and has no effect.
- Marks and the value chip are `aria-hidden`. The thumb's `aria-valuetext` already says the value, and mark labels would be read as stray text. Mark labels keep 4.5:1 on the page, and the chip's text 4.5:1 on the chip, in every theme (`Slider.test.tsx`).
- With `inputs`, each number field is named as its thumb is (the label, or "Minimum" and "Maximum" in a range), so a screen reader hears which value it changes. It's one more Tab stop per thumb.
- `disabled`, or a disabled `<fieldset>` around it, disables the thumbs' range inputs: out of the Tab order, ignoring keys and presses, and left out of the form.

### Keyboard

| Key | Does |
| --- | --- |
| ArrowRight, ArrowUp | + `step` (ArrowLeft raises it in right-to-left pages) |
| ArrowLeft, ArrowDown | − `step` |
| Shift+Arrow, PageUp, PageDown | ± `largeStep` steps |
| Home, End | The ends; a range thumb stops at the other thumb |

Your `onKeyDown` runs before the slider's own keys, so `e.preventDefault()` in it overrides one. `onFocus` and `onBlur` fire when focus enters or leaves the slider, not as it moves between a range's two thumbs, so a form library's "touched on blur" waits until people leave the whole control.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | string | none | Goes to the root `<div>`. A `<label htmlFor>` can't name it; inside a Field, the Field's label names it through this id. |
| `value` | `number \| [number, number]` | | Controlled. A pair makes a range with two thumbs. |
| `defaultValue` | `number \| [number, number]` | `min` | Uncontrolled. |
| `onValueChange` | `(value) => void` | | As it moves. |
| `onValueCommit` | `(value) => void` | | Once when a drag ends or a key press changes it: for saving or fetching. |
| `min`, `max` | `number` | `0`, `100` | |
| `step` | `number` | `1` | Values snap to it. |
| `largeStep` | `number` | `10` | Steps moved by PageUp, PageDown and Shift with an arrow. |
| `size` | `'sm' \| 'md' \| 'lg'` | `'md'` | 4px track and 16px thumb, 6px and 20px, or 8px and 24px (`lg`, beside lg fields in a form). |
| `disabled` | `boolean` | `false` | |
| `invalid` | `boolean` | `false` | A danger fill and ring, and `aria-invalid` on the thumbs. Field's `error` sets it. |
| `readOnly` | `boolean` | `false` | Focusable and read out, but it doesn't move; the value is still submitted. |
| `formatValue` | `(value: number) => string` | | The words read out for a value (`aria-valuetext`), such as "$40". |
| `thumbLabels` | `[string, string]` | `['Minimum', 'Maximum']` | A range's thumb names. By default the `sliderMinimum` and `sliderMaximum` labels ("Minimum", "Maksimum" in `idLabels`). |
| `marks` | `boolean \| { value: number; label?: ReactNode }[]` | | Ticks on the track: `true` for every step, or the listed values with text under them. Visual only. |
| `showValue` | `boolean` | `false` | The value over the thumb while it's focused, hovered or dragged. Visual only. |
| `inputs` | `boolean` | `false` | A number field beside each thumb, kept in step with it, for typing an exact value. |
| `orientation` | `'horizontal'` \| `'vertical'` | `'horizontal'` | `'vertical'` runs the track bottom to top, min at the bottom, `--slider-length` long; Up and Right raise it, in either direction of text, and the thumbs say `aria-orientation="vertical"`. Mark labels sit to the right of the track, the value chip to its left |
| `origin` | `number` | `min` | Where a single thumb's fill starts: `0` on a -10 to +10 scale fills from the middle toward the thumb, either way. A range ignores it. |
| `name` | `string` | | The thumbs' range inputs take it (two with the same name for a range), so the value is sent with a form. |
| `form` | `string` | | The id of a form it sits outside of: its thumbs submit, and reset, with that form. |
| `required` | `boolean` | | Accepted so Field's `required` doesn't reach the page. A slider always has a value, so it has no effect. |

Name a single slider with `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby`; on a range they name the group. `className`, `ref` and other props go to the root `<div>`. Its `focus()` and `autoFocus` move focus to the first thumb (none when disabled), so a form library that focuses the first invalid field after a failed submit lands on the slider.

## Component tokens

Each is an optional override: set it on the page, a container or one slider. The list lives in `src/components/Slider/slider.tokens.json` (also in `design-tokens/components/`).

<!-- token-table:start (made from slider.tokens.json by npm run tokens: edit the descriptions there) -->
**Colors**

| Token | Default | Use |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--slider-track` | `track` | The track: the light gray Apple uses, as Switch's, Meter's and Progress's. The fill and the thumb's ring carry the 3:1. |
| `--slider-fill` | `primary` | The selected part of the track. |
| `--slider-thumb-bg` | `field` | The thumb's inside. |
| `--slider-thumb-border` | `primary` | The thumb's ring (3:1 on the surface). |
| `--slider-focus-ring` | `focus-ring` | The thumb's keyboard focus ring. |
| `--slider-invalid` | `danger` | The fill and the thumb's ring when invalid. |
| `--slider-mark` | `field` | The marks' ticks, cut into the track. |
| `--slider-mark-off` | `border-strong` | A mark's tick past the fill, on the light track. |
| `--slider-mark-label` | `text-muted` | The marks' text under the track (4.5:1 on the surface). |
| `--slider-value-bg` | `surface-inverse` | showValue's chip over the thumb. |
| `--slider-value-text` | `text-inverse` | showValue's text (4.5:1 on value-bg). |
| `--slider-fill-disabled` | `disabled-surface` | Disabled: the fill, whatever its color when enabled. |
| `--slider-text-disabled` | `disabled-text` | Disabled: the text, icon or mark, in place of fading it (3:1 or more on its background, more with more contrast). |
| `--slider-fill-edge` | `primary-edge` | The filled range's and the thumb's 1px edge (Yellow Light; transparent where the fill is 3:1 on the page) |

**Sizing**

components.name: SortableList
components.summary: A list people put in their own order: tasks by priority, steps in a flow, columns in a table.
components.guide:
# SortableList A list people put in their own order: tasks by priority, steps in a flow, columns in a table. Each row has a handle; people drag it, tap it and then tap where the row goes, or pick the row up with the keyboard and move it with the arrow keys. Every step is announced to screen readers. **Also called:** reorderable list, drag and drop list. ```tsx import { SortableList } from "@diki-stwn/serupa-ds"; const [tasks, setTasks] = React.useState([{ id: "brief", title: "Write the brief" }, { id: "review", title: "Review the designs" }]); t.id} getLabel={(t) => t.title} renderItem={(t) => {t.title}} onReorder={(next) => setTasks(next)} /> ``` ## When to use - An order people choose and that matters: priorities, a playlist, the steps of a checklist, which columns show first. - Short lists that fit on one screen, up to a few dozen rows. ## When not to use - An order that follows from the data (date, name, size): offer sorting, such as Table's sortable headers. - Moving items between groups or columns, such as a kanban board: use [Kanban] (npx serupa-docs Kanban). - Very long lists where dragging far is the main job: dragging scrolls at the edges, but offer "Move to top" or a position field as well. ## Anatomy Drawn from the `Horizontal` story. 1. **Item** (`.srp-sortable-list__item`): one thing to put in order. 2. **Handle** (`.srp-sortable-list__handle`): drag it, or press Space and use the arrow keys, to move the item. 3. **Content** (`.srp-sortable-list__content`): what the item shows. ## Usage - Name the list with `aria-label` (or `aria-labelledby`), and give each item a short name with `getLabel`. The name goes on its handle ("Reorder Write the brief") and in every announcement. - `getKey` must return a stable id, not the index, so focus and any state inside a row follow it as it moves. - Save the new order in `onReorder`. It's called once, on drop, and only when the position changed; it gets the new array and `{ from, to }` (from 0). If saving can fail, put the old order back and say so. - Keep buttons and links inside rows: only the handle starts a drag. ## Behavior - Pointer: press the handle and move more than 4px; the row follows the pointer and the others move out of its way. Letting go drops it. A press without moving picks the row up, as Space does; a press on another row's handle then drops it in that row's place, and a press on its own handle drops it where it is (WCAG 2.5.7: no drag needed). Picked up from the keyboard, it can still be dragged: dragging its handle carries it on with the pointer, and dragging another row's handle puts it back and drags that row instead. Held near the top or bottom edge of the list's scrolling container (or of the window), it scrolls that way, faster nearer the edge, so a row can be moved past the screen. - Keyboard: Space or Enter on a handle picks the row up. The arrow keys move it one place, Home and End to either end. Space or Enter drops it, and Escape, Tab or a click elsewhere puts it back where it was. Focus stays on its handle throughout. - Nothing is reported until the drop, so a canceled move leaves your data alone. - `disabled` shows the rows without handles. - `orientation="horizontal"` lays the items out in a row (a board's columns, a set of tabs) that scrolls sideways inside itself when it doesn't fit: a drag moves sideways and scrolls at the left and right edges, and Left and Right follow the reading direction, so in right-to-left ArrowLeft moves an item later. Up and Down still move it earlier and later. ### Do and don't - **Do:** Give each item a short name with `getLabel`: it goes on its handle ("Reorder Write the brief") and in every announcement. (`DoShortNames`) - **Don't:** Name items in sentences: every handle and announcement repeats them in full. (`DontLongNames`) ## Accessibility - A `
    ` of `
  • ` rows (the role keeps it a list in Safari). Each handle is a button named "Reorder" and the item's name, described by the keyboard instructions, with `aria-pressed` while its row is picked up. - Screen readers hear each step in a polite live region: "Picked up Gemini, position 2 of 4.", "Gemini, position 3 of 4.", "Dropped Gemini at position 4 of 4." or "Canceled. Gemini is back at position 2 of 4." The words come from `SerupaProvider` labels (Indonesian in `idLabels`). - Screen reader users in browse mode activate the handle with Enter, which picks the row up the same way. - The handle is at least 24 by 24px, and it keeps 3:1 (the text 4.5:1) on the row in every theme (`SortableList.test.tsx`). The row being moved, from the keyboard or the pointer, carries the one focus ring, around the whole row, and its handle's own ring hides.
