components.name: Sparkline
components.summary: A small trend line that sits in a sentence, a table cell or a stat card, with a dot on the latest value.
components.guide:
# Sparkline

A small trend line that sits in a sentence, a table cell or a stat card, with a dot on the latest value. Screen readers hear what it measures and its first, last, low and high numbers, since the shape alone doesn't say them.

**Also called:** microchart, trend line, inline chart.

```tsx
import { Sparkline } from "@diki-stwn/serupa-ds";

<Sparkline data={[12, 14, 11, 15, 18, 16, 21]} label="Sign-ups, last 7 weeks" />
```

## When to use

- A trend next to the number it belongs to: a stat card's "1,240 sign-ups", a row in a table of accounts, a line of text.
- Many small trends side by side, on one scale (`min` and `max`), to compare their shapes at a glance.

## When not to use

- When the reader needs exact values, dates or more than one series: use a chart with axes and a table view.
- For one value against a range or a goal: use [Meter] (npx serupa-docs Meter) or [Progress] (npx serupa-docs Progress).

## Anatomy

Drawn from the `Area` story.

1. **Area** (`.srp-sparkline__area`): with `area`, the fill under the line.
2. **Line** (`.srp-sparkline__line`): the values, oldest on the left, 2px wide whatever the box's shape.
3. **Dot** (`.srp-sparkline__dot`): the latest value.

## Usage

- Give `label` the measure and the period ("Revenue, last 12 weeks"): the summary adds the numbers.
- Show the latest number as text beside it. The sparkline is the shape of the trend, not the place to read a value.
- Pass `format` (Intl.NumberFormat options) so the summary reads the numbers as the page shows them: a currency, a percent, a unit.
- Several sparklines that will be compared need the same `min` and `max`, or each fills its own box and a small change looks as large as a big one.
- Its size is set by `--sparkline-width` and `--sparkline-height`: set them in em to follow the text around it.

### Do and don't

- **Do:** Show the latest number as text beside it: the sparkline is the shape of the trend. (`DoShowLatest`)
- **Don't:** Show the line alone: people can't read a value off its shape. (`Default`)

## Accessibility

- **Role and name:** `role="img"`, named by `label` and a summary: "Sign-ups: from 12 to 21, low 11, high 21", in the provider's number format. The words are a label (`sparklineSummary`), so `<SerupaProvider labels>` and the language packs translate them.
- **Keyboard:** not focusable: it has nothing to do. The numbers are in its name.
- **Contrast:** its line reads 3:1 on the surface in every theme (`Sparkline.test.tsx`), as WCAG 1.4.11 asks of a graphic. In forced colors the line and the dot take CanvasText.
- **What's still yours:** the latest value as text beside it, and a table or a chart with axes where the exact numbers matter. Its trend is in its color and shape only, so don't let the color carry a meaning (red for down) the text doesn't say.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `data` | `number[]` | | The numbers, oldest first. Anything not finite is left out. |
| `label` | `string` | | What it measures. Its accessible name starts with it. |
| `format` | `Intl.NumberFormatOptions` | | How the numbers read in the summary. |
| `area` | `boolean` | `false` | Fills under the line. |
| `min` | `number` | the lowest value | The bottom of the scale. |
| `max` | `number` | the highest value | The top of the scale. |
| `id` | string | none | Goes to the `<svg>`. |

`className`, `ref` and other props go to the `<svg>`.

## Component tokens

Each is an optional override: set it on the page, a container or one Sparkline. The list lives in `src/components/Sparkline/sparkline.tokens.json` (also in `design-tokens/components/`).

<!-- token-table:start (made from sparkline.tokens.json by npm run tokens: edit the descriptions there) -->
| Token | Default | Use |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--sparkline-line` | `chart-1` | The line and the end dot (3:1 on the surface behind). |
| `--sparkline-area` | `chart-seq-1` | The fill under the line, with area. |
| `--sparkline-width` | `spacing-20` | The width (80px). |
| `--sparkline-height` | `spacing-5` | The height (20px). |
| `--sparkline-dot` | `spacing-1.5` | The end dot's diameter (6px). |
<!-- token-table:end -->

components.name: SplitButton
components.summary: A main action joined to an arrow button that opens a menu of other ways to do it: Publish, with Schedule and Save as draft one click away.
components.guide:
# SplitButton

A main action joined to an arrow button that opens a menu of other ways to do it: Publish, with Schedule and Save as draft one click away. The common choice stays one click; the others don't take room of their own.

**Also called:** button with dropdown, split dropdown button.

```tsx
import { SplitButton, MenuItem } from "@diki-stwn/serupa-ds";

<SplitButton onClick={publish} menuLabel="More publish options" menu={<>
  <MenuItem onSelect={schedule}>Schedule</MenuItem>
  <MenuItem onSelect={saveDraft}>Save as draft</MenuItem>
</>}>Publish</SplitButton>
```

## When to use

- One action people take most of the time, with a few variations of it: Save and Save a copy, Send and Send later, Merge and Squash and merge.

## When not to use

- Actions that aren't ways to do the same thing: use separate [Button] (npx serupa-docs Button)s or a [ButtonGroup] (npx serupa-docs ButtonGroup).
- No main action, only a list of choices: use a [Menu] (npx serupa-docs Menu) on one Button.
- Picking one option that stays chosen: use [Select] (npx serupa-docs Select) or [SegmentedControl] (npx serupa-docs SegmentedControl).

## Anatomy

Drawn from the `Default` story.

1. **Main button** (`.srp-btn`): runs the main action (`onClick`) and shows its label.
2. **Menu button** (`.srp-split-button__menu`): the arrow, named by `menuLabel`, which opens the menu.

## Usage

- Label the main button with the action itself ("Publish"), and the menu with what it holds ("More publish options").
- Put the variations in the menu, not unrelated actions, and keep it short: three to five items.
- Give both halves one variant (the `variant` prop does). Two primary halves get an edge between them in their text color.
- Use `loading` while the main action runs: the main button shows a Loader and can't be pressed twice; the menu stays usable.

### Do and don't

- **Do:** Put other ways of doing the main action in the menu: Schedule, Save as draft. (`DoVariations`)
- **Don't:** Put unrelated actions there: nobody looks for Rename or Delete behind Publish. Use a [Menu] (npx serupa-docs Menu) of its own. (`DontUnrelated`)

## Accessibility

- **Role and name:** a `role="group"` (name it with `aria-label` when the page has several) holding two buttons. The main one is named by its label; the arrow by `menuLabel`, with `aria-haspopup="menu"` and `aria-expanded`, and the same words as a tooltip.
- **Keyboard:** Tab reaches each half. Enter or Space on the main button runs it; on the arrow, Enter, Space or Down opens the menu on its first item and Up on its last. Escape closes it and puts focus back on the arrow (from Menu).
- **Contrast:** each half keeps Button's colors and contrast in every theme. The edge between two primary halves is decoration, so it has no minimum.
- **What's still yours:** a `menuLabel` that says what the menu holds, and an `aria-label` on the group when there are several on the page.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | string | none | Goes to the wrapper `<div>`. |
| `children` | `ReactNode` | | Required. The main action's label |
| `onClick` | `(event) => void` | | Runs the main action |
| `menu` | `ReactNode` | | Required. `MenuItem`, `MenuGroup` and `MenuSeparator` |
| `menuLabel` | `string` | | Required. The arrow button's name ("More publish options") |
| `variant` | `'primary'` \| `'secondary'` \| `'outline'` | `'primary'` | Both halves |
| `size` | `'sm'` \| `'md'` \| `'lg'` | `'md'` | Both halves |
| `destructive` | `boolean` | `false` | The danger color, for a main action that deletes or can't be undone |
| `startIcon` | icon | | An icon before the main label |
| `disabled` | `boolean` | `false` | Turns off both halves |
| `loading` | `boolean` | `false` | The main button shows a Loader and can't be pressed again; the menu stays usable |
| `placement` | placement | `'bottom-end'` | Where the menu opens |
| `open`, `defaultOpen`, `onOpenChange` | | | The menu's open state, as on Menu |

`aria-label` and `aria-labelledby` name the group. `className`, `ref` and other props go to the wrapper `<div>`.

## Component tokens

Each is an optional override: set it on the page, a container or one SplitButton. The list lives in `src/components/SplitButton/split-button.tokens.json` (also in `design-tokens/components/`).

<!-- token-table:start (made from split-button.tokens.json by npm run tokens: edit the descriptions there) -->
| Token | Default | Use |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--split-button-divider` | `opacity-40` | How strong the edge between two primary halves is: their text color at this opacity (40%). |
<!-- token-table:end -->

components.name: Splitter
components.summary: Two panes with a handle between them that people drag, or move with the keys, to give one pane more room: a list and its detail, a sidebar and an editor, code and its output.
components.guide:
# Splitter

Two panes with a handle between them that people drag, or move with the keys, to give one pane more room: a list and its detail, a sidebar and an editor, code and its output.

**Also called:** resizable panels, split view, split pane.

```tsx
import { Splitter } from "@diki-stwn/serupa-ds";

<Splitter separatorLabel="Folders" defaultSize={25} min={15} max={50} collapsible storageKey="mail-folders" style={{ height: "100%" }}>
  <FolderList />
  <MessageList />
</Splitter>

<Splitter orientation="vertical" defaultSize={70} separatorLabel="Editor">
  <Editor />
  <Terminal />
</Splitter>
```

## When to use

- Two areas people work in side by side, where how much room each needs depends on the task: a list and detail, a sidebar and editor.
- A panel people sometimes want out of the way (`collapsible`), such as a file tree.

## When not to use

- A sidebar that opens over the page on phones: use [Drawer] (npx serupa-docs Drawer), since a handle is hard to drag on a small screen.
- A fixed layout people don't need to change: use [Grid] (npx serupa-docs Grid) or [Stack] (npx serupa-docs Stack).
- Switching between views rather than showing two at once: use [Tabs] (npx serupa-docs Tabs).

## Anatomy

Drawn from the `Playground` story.

1. **First pane** (`.srp-splitter__pane--first`): one side.
2. **Handle** (`.srp-splitter__handle`): drag it, or focus it and use the arrow keys, to share the space; Enter collapses a pane.
3. **Second pane** (`.srp-splitter__pane--second`): the other side.

## Usage

- Name the handle after the pane it resizes (`separatorLabel="Folders"`), so a screen reader says what moving it changes.
- Give the Splitter a height (a vertical one needs it; a horizontal one fills its parent's height when you give it one), and set `min` so the first pane never gets too narrow to use.
- Printed, the panes show their whole content rather than their scrolled windows: the Splitter drops its height, the panes grow to fit, and the separator isn't printed.
- Set `storageKey` so people's layout comes back on their next visit. It's read after the page loads, so a server-rendered page first shows `defaultSize`.
- Sizes are percent of the Splitter, so the layout keeps its proportions when the window resizes.
- Each pane scrolls on its own. Put one Splitter inside another's pane for three panes.

## Behavior

- Dragging the handle moves it with the pointer, even outside the handle, between `min` and `max`. Without dragging (WCAG 2.5.7): a press on the handle, then a press anywhere else in the Splitter, puts the handle there; that second press is the Splitter's, so a button under it isn't pressed. Pressing the handle again, Escape or leaving it cancels. The handle is 8px wide, with a 1px line down its middle that turns 2px primary on hover, while dragged and on focus.
- With `collapsible`, Enter on the handle or a double-click collapses the first pane to 0, and again brings it back at its last size. A collapsed pane is hidden, so Tab skips what's in it, and an arrow key brings it back at `min`. When your code collapses it (a controlled `size` of 0) while focus is inside it, focus moves to the handle.
- Collapsing and bringing back with Enter or a double-click slides: the handle and the second pane glide to their new place while the first pane wipes out or in with them, over 200ms. Press Enter again mid-way and it turns back from where it is. Dragging, the arrow keys and a `size` your code sets move at once, and with reduced motion so does the toggle.
- In a right-to-left page the first pane is on the right, and the arrow keys follow what you see: ArrowLeft moves the handle left.

### Do and don't

- **Do:** Name the handle after the pane it resizes (`separatorLabel="Folders"`). (`DoNameHandle`)
- **Don't:** Give it a generic name ("Resize"): screen reader users can't tell which pane it changes. (`DontGenericHandle`)

## Accessibility

- **Role and name:** the WAI-ARIA window splitter pattern. The handle is a focusable `role="separator"` with `aria-orientation`, `aria-valuenow` (the first pane's size in percent), `aria-valuemin`, `aria-valuemax` and `aria-controls` pointing at the first pane. It's named by `separatorLabel`, or "Resize panes" (the `resizePanes` label, "Ubah ukuran panel" in `idLabels`).
- **Keyboard:** Tab reaches the handle; the table below says what each key does there.
- **Grab zone:** the 8px handle takes a press over 16px with a mouse or pen, reaching 4px into each pane without moving anything, and over 24px on a touch screen, reaching 8px, so a finger can grab it.
- **Contrast:** the handle's line is 3:1 on the page in every theme, and the focus ring shows around the handle (`Splitter.test.tsx`). In forced colors the line uses the system's text and highlight colors.
- **What's still yours:** a name for each pane's content (a heading, or `nav` and `main` landmarks inside), and a layout that still works when a pane is at `min`.

### Keyboard

| Key | Does |
| --- | --- |
| Tab | To the handle, between the first pane's content and the second's |
| ArrowLeft, ArrowRight | Move the handle by `step` (a side-by-side Splitter; left and right as you see them, also right to left) |
| ArrowUp, ArrowDown | Move the handle by `step` (`orientation="vertical"`) |
| Home, End | Move the handle to `min` and `max` |
| Enter | With `collapsible`: collapse the first pane, or bring it back at its last size |

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | `string` | | Goes to the root `<div>`. |
| `children` | two `ReactNode`s | | The first and second panes. The handle resizes the first; the second takes the rest. |
| `orientation` | `'horizontal' \| 'vertical'` | `'horizontal'` | Side by side (the first at the start) or stacked (the first on top). |
| `size` | `number` | | The first pane's size in percent (controlled). |
| `defaultSize` | `number` | `50` | The first pane's size at first (uncontrolled). `0` starts it collapsed when `collapsible`. |
| `onSizeChange` | `(size: number) => void` | | Each new size in percent, while dragging or moving with the keys. |
| `min`, `max` | `number` | `10`, `90` | The first pane's least and largest size, in percent. |
| `step` | `number` | `5` | How far an arrow key moves the handle, in percent. |
| `collapsible` | `boolean` | `false` | Enter and a double-click collapse the first pane and bring it back. |
| `storageKey` | `string` | | Keeps an uncontrolled size in `localStorage` under this key. |
| `separatorLabel` | `string` | `'Resize panes'` | The handle's accessible name: say what it resizes. |

`className`, `style`, `ref` and other props go to the root `<div>`, which has `data-component="splitter"` and `data-direction`.

## Component tokens

Each is an optional override: set it on the page, a container or one Splitter. The list lives in `src/components/Splitter/splitter.tokens.json` (also in `design-tokens/components/`).

<!-- token-table:start (made from splitter.tokens.json by npm run tokens: edit the descriptions there) -->
| Token | Default | Use |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--splitter-line` | `border-control` | The handle's line (3:1 on the page). |
| `--splitter-line-active` | `primary-text` | The line on hover, while dragged and on focus. |
| `--splitter-focus-ring` | `focus-ring` | The handle's focus ring. |
| `--splitter-handle-size` | `spacing-2` | How thick the handle is, the area a pointer can grab (8px). |
<!-- token-table:end -->

components.name: Stack
components.summary: Lays its children out in a column, or a row, with the same space between each, taken from the spacing scale.
components.guide:
# Stack Lays its children out in a column, or a row, with the same space between each, taken from the spacing scale. Use it for most layout inside a page: a form's fields, a card's content, a row of buttons. **Also called:** flex stack, VStack, HStack, inline, cluster. ```jsx import { Stack, Button } from '@diki-stwn/serupa-ds'; {items.map((i) =>
  • {i.name}
    • )}     ``` ## When to use - Things one after another with even space between them: a form's fields, a card's content, a row of buttons. - Spacing siblings from the spacing scale, instead of a margin on each one. ## When not to use - Items in columns that line up from row to row: use [Grid] (npx serupa-docs Grid) instead. - Setting the page's width and side padding: use [Container] (npx serupa-docs Container) instead. - Buttons joined into one control: use [ButtonGroup] (npx serupa-docs ButtonGroup) instead. ## Usage - Use a larger gap between groups and a smaller one inside them, such as `gap={6}` between fields and `gap={2}` between buttons. - Set `wrap` on a row that may not fit on narrow screens. `direction="row" wrap` is the cluster (or inline) layout: tags, filters or buttons side by side, wrapping onto more lines as the space runs out, the same gap across and down. - To change the layout with the screen's width, give `direction`, `gap` or `align` one value per width: `direction={{ base: 'column', md: 'row' }}` stacks on a phone and sits side by side from 768px. The widths are `sm` (640px), `md` (768px) and `lg` (1024px); each holds until the next one set. Media queries draw it, so server HTML is already laid out. - Pick the element with `as`: `ul` or `ol` for a list, `form` or `fieldset` for a form's fields. - Nest Stacks for more complex layouts, such as a row of buttons at the end of a column of fields. ### Do and don't - **Do:** Use a larger gap between groups and a smaller one inside them, such as `gap={6}` between groups and `gap={2}` within. (`DoNestedGaps`) - **Don't:** Use one gap for everything: nothing shows which items belong together. (`DontOneGap`) ## Accessibility - Stack only lays things out: the reading and tab order stay the order of the children, so keep it the same as what people see. - Use `as="ul"` or `as="ol"` when the items are a list, so screen readers say how many there are. It then carries `role="list"`, since Safari stops calling a list without bullets a list. - **Keyboard:** none: a layout box, not focusable. ## Props | Prop | Type | Default | What it does | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `id` | string | none | Goes to the root element (`as`). | | `direction` | `'column'` \| `'row'`, or one per width: `{ base, sm, md, lg }` | `'column'` | One under another, or side by side | | `gap` | a spacing step: `0` `0.5` `1` `1.5` `2` `2.5` `3` `3.5` `4` `5` `6` `7` `8` `9` `10` `11` `12` `14` `16` `20` `24` | `4` (16px) | The space between items: `gap={6}` is `spacing-6`, 24px. Or one per width: `{ base: 2, lg: 6 }` | | `align` | `'stretch'` \| `'start'` \| `'center'` \| `'end'` \| `'baseline'` | `'stretch'` in a column, `'center'` in a row | Cross-axis alignment. Or one per width; a width left out follows that width's direction | | `justify` | `'start'` \| `'center'` \| `'end'` \| `'between'` | `'start'` | Main-axis distribution | | `wrap` | boolean | `false` | Lets a row wrap onto more lines | | `as` | `'div'` \| `'section'` \| `'ul'` \| `'ol'` \| `'nav'` \| `'header'` \| `'footer'` \| `'form'` \| `'fieldset'` \| `'span'` | `'div'` | The element. A list loses its bullets, margins and padding | A value that isn't on the list falls back to the default. `className`, `style`, `ref` and everything else go to the element, which has `data-component="stack"`. ## Component tokens Each is an optional override: set it on the page, a container or one element. The list lives in `src/components/Stack/stack.tokens.json` (also in `design-tokens/components/`). | Token | Default | Use | | --- | --- | --- | | `--stack-gap` | `spacing-4` | The space between items when gap isn't given (16px). |

components.name: StatTile
components.summary: One key number on a card, for the top of a dashboard: what it is, the number, how it changed since the period before (in words, with an arrow), and an optional trend line.
components.guide:
# StatTile

One key number on a card, for the top of a dashboard: what it is, the number, how it changed since the period before (in words, with an arrow), and an optional trend line. Screen readers hear it in that order, and the trend's numbers in its name.

**Also called:** KPI card, stat card, metric tile, scorecard.

```tsx
import { StatTile } from "@diki-stwn/serupa-ds";

<StatTile
  label="Revenue"
  value="€48,200"
  change={{ amount: "12%", direction: "up" }}
  period="vs last month"
  trend={[38200, 40100, 39500, 42800, 41900, 44600, 46100, 48200]}
/>
```

## When to use

- The few numbers a dashboard leads with, each with how it changed: revenue, orders, active users.
- One number beside a [Chart] (npx serupa-docs Chart), as its headline.
- A row of them with a heading: [StatsRow](../../blocks/StatsRow/StatsRow.mdx) lays out two to four, with loading and a failed load.

## When not to use

- A number against a known range or a goal, such as storage used: use [Meter] (npx serupa-docs Meter).
- More than a handful of numbers, or numbers people compare row by row: use a [Table] (npx serupa-docs Table) or [DescriptionList] (npx serupa-docs DescriptionList).
- When the shape over time is the point, with dates and values to read: use a [Chart] (npx serupa-docs Chart).

## Anatomy

Drawn from the `Default` story.

1. **Label** (`.srp-stat-tile__label`): what the number is.
2. **Value** (`.srp-stat-tile__value`): the number, large, in tabular figures.
3. **Change** (`.srp-stat-tile__change`): a [Badge] (npx serupa-docs Badge) that says "Up 12%" with an arrow, green or red by whether that is good news, and the period beside it.
4. **Trend** (`.srp-stat-tile__trend`): a [Sparkline] (npx serupa-docs Sparkline) across the tile.

## Usage

- Format `value` and `change.amount` yourself, as the rest of the page shows numbers: a currency, a percent, a unit.
- Say whether a change is good news with `change.good`. By default a rise is green and a fall red; a rise in costs or a fall in refunds turns that round.
- Give `period` what the change compares with ("vs last month"), so "Up 12%" means something.
- Several tiles in a row go in a list, each `as="li"`, so a screen reader says how many there are. On a phone they stack.
- Tiles that will be compared share one scale only if their trends do: the trend fits its own numbers, so a small change can look large.

### Loading

- Set `loading` while the number loads: a placeholder of the same height takes its place and the tile is `aria-busy`. Name the wait in `loadingLabel` ("Loading revenue"); in a row of tiles, name the first and pass `""` to the rest, so it's said once.

### Do and don't

- **Do:** Say whether a change is good news, so a rise in costs is red. (`DoSayWhatIsGood`)
- **Don't:** Leave every rise green: costs going up isn't good news. (`DontRiseIsAlwaysGood`)

## Accessibility

- **Role and name:** a plain card-like box with no role of its own: it reads label, value, change and period in that order. In a list, `as="li"` makes each one a list item.
- **Not by color alone:** the change says "Up", "Down" or "No change" in words, with an arrow, as well as its color (WCAG 1.4.1).
- **The trend:** an image named by the label, how many periods, and its first, last, low and high values ("Revenue, last 8 periods: from €38,200 to €48,200, low €38,200, high €48,200"), in the provider's language and number format. `trendFormat` sets how they read.
- **Keyboard:** not focusable: it has nothing to do. Put a link to the details beside it, or in the card, when there is one.
- **Contrast:** the label, the value and the period read 4.5:1 on the card in every theme (`StatTile.test.tsx`); the badge keeps its own 4.5:1 and the trend line 3:1.
- **Words:** "Up", "Down", "No change" and the trend's name are labels (`statTileUp`, `statTileDown`, `statTileFlat`, `statTileTrend`), so `<SerupaProvider labels>` and the language packs translate them.
- **What's still yours:** the value's and the amount's formatting, and saying what a change means where it matters ("Revenue is up because of the spring sale").

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `label` | `string` | | What the number is. |
| `value` | `ReactNode` | | The number, formatted. |
| `change` | `{ amount: string; direction: 'up' \| 'down' \| 'flat'; good?: boolean }` | | How it changed. `good` defaults to true for up. |
| `period` | `string` | | What the change compares with. |
| `trend` | `number[]` | | Values over time, oldest first; two or more draw a Sparkline. |
| `trendLabel` | `string` | label and period count | The trend's name, before its numbers. |
| `trendFormat` | `Intl.NumberFormatOptions` | | How the trend's numbers read. |
| `loading` | `boolean` | `false` | A placeholder in place of the number, and `aria-busy`. |
| `loadingLabel` | `string` | `"Loading…"` | The placeholder's name; `""` to leave it unnamed. |
| `as` | `'div' \| 'li' \| 'article'` | `'div'` | The element. |
| `id` | string | none | Goes to the card. |

`className`, `ref` and other props go to the tile's element.

## Component tokens

Each is an optional override: set it on the page, a container or one StatTile. The list lives in `src/components/StatTile/stat-tile.tokens.json` (also in `design-tokens/components/`).

<!-- token-table:start (made from stat-tile.tokens.json by npm run tokens: edit the descriptions there) -->
| Token | Default | Use |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--stat-tile-bg` | `surface` | The tile's background, as an outline Card's. |
| `--stat-tile-border` | `border` | The tile's edge. |
| `--stat-tile-label-text` | `text-muted` | The label and the period (4.5:1 on the card). |
| `--stat-tile-value-text` | `text` | The number (4.5:1 on the card). |
| `--stat-tile-value-weight` | `font-semibold` | The number's weight (600). |
| `--stat-tile-label-size` | `text-sm` | The label's and the period's size (text-sm). |
| `--stat-tile-value-size` | `text-2xl` | The number's size (text-2xl). |
| `--stat-tile-value-line-height` | `text-2xl--line-height` | The number's line height. |
| `--stat-tile-padding` | `spacing-5` | Space inside the tile, on every side (20px), as a Card's. |

components.name: StatusTracker
components.summary: A strip of bars, one a day, for uptime or a job's history: up, degraded, down or no data, told apart by shape as well as color.
components.guide:
# StatusTracker

A strip of bars, one a day, for uptime or a job's history: up, degraded, down or no data, told apart by shape as well as color. Each day can be reached by keyboard or pointer and is said in words ("Sep 25, 2026: Down. Outage, 42 minutes"), and a summary line sums it up ("96.5% up over 90 days, 3 incidents").

**Also called:** uptime bar, uptime tracker, status page bar.

```jsx
import { StatusTracker } from '@diki-stwn/serupa-ds';

<StatusTracker label="API" days={[
  { date: "2026-11-04", state: "up" },
  { date: "2026-11-05", state: "degraded", note: "Slow responses" },
  { date: "2026-11-06", state: "down", note: "Outage, 42 minutes" },
]} />

<StatusTracker label="Nightly build" days={runs} summary={`Last failure ${lastFailure}`} legend={false} />
```

## When to use

- A status page or a service's detail page: how it has done over the last 30 or 90 days.
- The history of a scheduled job, a check or a backup, one bar a run.

## When not to use

- A value over time: use a [Sparkline] (npx serupa-docs Sparkline) or a [Chart] (npx serupa-docs Chart).
- Only the state right now: a [Badge] (npx serupa-docs Badge) with a dot says it.
- A list of incidents people read: use a [Timeline] (npx serupa-docs Timeline).

## Anatomy

Drawn from the `Playground` story.

1. **Day** (`.srp-status-tracker__day`): one bar. Up is solid, degraded striped, down half as tall, no data an outline.
2. **Caption** (`.srp-status-tracker__caption`): the focused or pointed day in words.
3. **Summary** (`.srp-status-tracker__summary`): the share of days up and the number of incidents, or your own line.
4. **Legend** (`.srp-status-tracker__legend`): the four states with their shapes.

## Usage

- Give days oldest first, one entry for each day in the range, with `state: "none"` for days without data so the strip's length stays true.
- Add a `note` to each bad day: what happened and for how long. It's said with the day.
- The summary counts degraded and down days as incidents, and the share of days up among the days with data. Pass `summary` for your own measure (minutes of downtime, say), or `null` for none.
- With more days than fit, the strip scrolls sideways in its own box, starting at the latest day.

### Do and don't

- **Do:** Give the days without data `state: "none"`, so they show as unknown. (`ThirtyDays`)
- **Don't:** Count them as up: the strip and the share then claim uptime nobody measured. (`DontGuessUp`)

## Accessibility

- **Role and name:** the strip is a list named by `label`; each day is an item named with its date, its state in words and its note. State is shown by shape too, not by color alone (WCAG 1.4.1).
- **Keyboard:** the strip is one tab stop, on the latest day; see the table.
- **Contrast:** the up, degraded and down bars keep 3:1 against the page (a day without data is outlined in the light `border-strong`, as a tag is), the caption 4.5:1, the summary and legend 4.5:1, in every theme (`StatusTracker.test.tsx`). In forced-colors mode the bars are drawn in the system's text color, the stripes kept.
- **What's still yours:** a `label` that says what is tracked, and notes that say what happened.

### Keyboard

| Key | Does |
| --- | --- |
| Tab | To the latest day (one stop for the strip) |
| ← → | The day before or after (mirrored right to left) |
| Home, End | The first or latest day |
| Escape | Hides the caption |

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `days` | `StatusDay[]` | | `{ date, state, note? }`, oldest first; `date` a Date or "yyyy-mm-dd", `state` `'up'`, `'degraded'`, `'down'` or `'none'` |
| `label` | `string` | | What it tracks; names the strip |
| `summary` | `ReactNode \| null` | worked out | The line under the strip; `null` for none |
| `legend` | `boolean` | `true` | The key to the four states |
| `id` | `string` | | Goes to the root `<div>`. |

`className`, `ref` and other props go to the root `<div>`.

## Component tokens

Each is an optional override: set it on the page, a container or one StatusTracker. The list lives in `src/components/StatusTracker/status-tracker.tokens.json` (also in `design-tokens/components/`).

<!-- token-table:start (made from status-tracker.tokens.json by npm run tokens: edit the descriptions there) -->
| Token | Default | Use |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--status-tracker-up` | `success` | An up day's bar (3:1 on the page). |
| `--status-tracker-degraded` | `warning` | A degraded day's stripes and outline (3:1). |
| `--status-tracker-down` | `danger` | A down day's bar (3:1). |
| `--status-tracker-none` | `border-strong` | A day without data: its outline, the light one a tag and an outline Badge have (the legend and the day's name say it, so it needn't be 3:1). |
| `--status-tracker-text` | `text` | The caption (4.5:1). |
| `--status-tracker-muted` | `text-muted` | The summary and legend (4.5:1). |
| `--status-tracker-focus-ring` | `focus-ring` | The ring around the focused day. |
| `--status-tracker-radius` | `rounded-xs` | A bar's corners (2px). |
| `--status-tracker-gap` | `spacing-0.5` | Space between bars (2px). |
| `--status-tracker-height` | `spacing-8` | The bars' height (32px). |
<!-- token-table:end -->

components.name: Stepper
components.summary: Shows where people are in a task split into steps, such as sign-up, checkout or setup.
components.guide:
# Stepper Shows where people are in a task split into steps, such as sign-up, checkout or setup. Each step has a numbered circle and a title; completed steps show a check. Use it for 3 to about 7 steps. For switching between views use Tabs, and for a single value use Progress. **Also called:** progress indicator, steps, wizard steps, progress tracker. ```tsx import { Stepper } from "@diki-stwn/serupa-ds"; // let people go back to finished steps // stacked, for narrow spaces ``` ## When to use - A task split into 3 to about 7 steps done in order, such as sign-up, checkout or setup. - People need to see which steps are done and how many are left. - People may go back to a finished step to change it. ## When not to use - Views people can open in any order: use [Tabs] (npx serupa-docs Tabs) instead. - How far along one thing is, such as an upload: use [Progress] (npx serupa-docs Progress) instead. - Where a page sits in the site: use [Breadcrumb] (npx serupa-docs Breadcrumb) instead. ## Anatomy Drawn from the `LongLabels` story. 1. **Step** (`.srp-stepper__step`): one stage of the task. 2. **Indicator** (`.srp-stepper__indicator`): its number, or a mark when it's done or has a problem. 3. **Title** (`.srp-stepper__title`): the stage's name. 4. **Description** (`.srp-stepper__description`): optional detail under the title. 5. **Connector** (`.srp-stepper__connector`): the line to the next step, filled once this one is done. 6. **Current step** (`.srp-stepper__step--current`): the stage you're on. ## Usage - Keep step titles to a word or two, and put any detail in `description`. - Mark a step people can skip with `optional: true` rather than writing it in the title; it shows the "Optional" tag. - Set `status: 'error'` on a step with a problem, so people can find it from the stepper. Use `status: 'warning'` for a softer problem that doesn't stop people going on, such as photos still to add. - Pass `onStepClick` only when going back is safe: it makes completed steps buttons that go back to them. - For a form people can fill in any order, add `clickable="all"`: every step but the current one becomes a button, upcoming ones too. ## Behavior - Upcoming steps have an outlined circle with their number, in the digits of the locale from `SerupaProvider` (or the browser), as Calendar writes its days: ٣ in Egyptian Arabic. The current step is filled in primary with a ring around it. Completed steps are filled with a check, and the line after them turns primary. Error steps are filled in danger. Warning steps have a warning-subtle circle, ringed and marked in warning text. - Horizontal lines stretch between steps, level with the middle of the circles. - When a horizontal Stepper is too narrow for its titles side by side (a phone, or 400% zoom), it keeps the circles and lines and shows one line under them: "Step 2 of 4: Profile". It switches back as soon as the titles fit, and the page never scrolls sideways. With many steps the lines shrink to 4px, and if the circles still don't fit they take the `sm` size, so eight steps fit a 320px screen. For descriptions people need to read on a phone, use `orientation="vertical"`. ### Do and don't - **Do:** Title each step in a word or two, with any detail in `description` and `optional: true` for the "Optional" tag. (`DoShortTitles`) - **Don't:** Write sentences as step titles, or "(optional)" into one: the steps crowd and wrap. (`DontLongTitles`) ## Accessibility - An `
    ` inside a `
    `. The current step has `aria-current="step"`, and completed, error or warning steps add ", completed", ", has an error" or ", needs attention" for screen readers, so the state isn't shown by color alone. - Numbers and text keep 4.5:1, and circles, rings and marks keep 3:1, in every theme (`Stepper.test.tsx`). - When it's too narrow and shows only the current step, the other titles stay in the list, clipped, so screen readers still read every step. The "Step 2 of 4" line is hidden from them, since the list already says it. This keeps it within reflow (WCAG 1.4.10) at 320px. - In forced colors (Windows high contrast) the current and completed circles are Highlight with HighlightText, exactly as set, so the browser's text backplate can't hide the number or check. ### Keyboard | Key | Does | | --- | --- | | Tab | With `onStepClick`, to each completed step (every step but the current one with `clickable="all"`); otherwise nothing in it takes focus | | Enter / Space | On a step button, goes to that step; focus stays on it as it becomes the current step | ## Props | Prop | Type | Default | Notes | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `id` | string | none | Goes to the root `
    `. | | `steps` | `{ title, description?, optional?, status? }[]` | | `status: 'error'` marks a step with a problem, `'warning'` one with a softer problem. | | `current` | `number` | | The current step's index, from 0. Steps before it are complete; `steps.length` marks them all complete. | | `orientation` | `'horizontal' \| 'vertical'` | `'horizontal'` | | | `size` | `'sm' \| 'md'` | `'md'` | 24px circles with `text-xs`, or 32px with `text-sm`. | | `onStepClick` | `(index: number) => void` | | Makes completed steps buttons that go back to them. | | `clickable` | `'completed' \| 'all'` | `'completed'` | Which steps `onStepClick` makes buttons: the completed ones, or every step but the current one. | | `labels` | `{ completed?, error?, warning?, optional?, stepOf? }` | `'completed'`, `'has an error'`, `'needs attention'`, `'Optional'`, "Step 2 of 4" | Words read out after a step's title, the optional tag, and the line shown when it's too narrow for every title. | It renders a `
    `; name it with `aria-label` (default `'Progress'`). `className`, `ref` and other props go to the `
    `. ## useSteps(options) The state of a form split into steps, to go with Stepper: which step is open, a check before each step forward, and focus moved to each step as it opens. ```tsx import { Stepper, useSteps } from "@diki-stwn/serupa-ds"; const s = useSteps({ steps, validate: (i) => checkStep(i), onComplete: submit });
    { e.preventDefault(); s.next(); }}> {steps.map((step, i) => (

    {step.title}

    {/* the step's fields */}
    ))} ``` - `next()` runs `validate` on the current step first. If it returns `false` (or a promise of `false`, for a check on the server), people stay on the step and the Stepper marks it "has an error". Show the field errors yourself, with Field or ErrorSummary. On the last step, a passing check calls `onComplete`. - `back()` and a press on a finished step in the Stepper go back with no check. `goTo(i)` forward checks every step on the way and stops on the first one that fails. - Every step stays rendered, and the others are `hidden`. Whatever was typed in a step, controlled or not, is still there on the way back, so nothing is asked for twice (WCAG 3.3.7). - When the step changes, focus moves to its heading (`tabIndex={-1}`), so a screen reader says which step people are on. It doesn't move focus on the first render. - A second `next()` while a check is still running does nothing, so a double press of Next moves one step. - With `transition: true`, each step slides in from the way people are going: forward from the end, back from the start, mirrored right to left. It runs as a View Transition, so under reduced motion the steps only crossfade, and where View Transitions are missing they swap at once. `panelProps` then names the open step for it, in `style`. | Returns | Type | Notes | | --- | --- | --- | | `current` | `number` | The open step, from 0. | | `next` / `back` / `goTo(i)` | functions | `next` and `goTo` resolve to whether they moved. | | `isFirst` / `isLast` | `boolean` | For the Back button and the Next or Submit label. | | `stepperProps` | object | Spread on Stepper: `steps` with errors marked, `current` and `onStepClick`. | | `panelProps(i)` | `{ id, hidden, aria-labelledby, style? }` | Spread on each step's container. | | `headingProps(i)` | `{ id, tabIndex, ref }` | Spread on each step's heading. | Options: `steps` (as Stepper takes them), `validate(index)`, `onComplete()`, `defaultStep` (default `0`) and `transition` (default `false`). ## Component tokens Each is an optional override: set it on the page, a container or one stepper. The list lives in `src/components/Stepper/stepper.tokens.json` (also in `design-tokens/components/`). **Colors** | Token | Default | Use | | --- | --- | --- | | `--stepper-indicator-bg` | `surface` | An upcoming step's circle. | | `--stepper-indicator-border` | `border-control` | An upcoming step's ring (3:1 on the surface). | | `--stepper-indicator-text` | `text-muted` | An upcoming step's number. | | `--stepper-indicator-text-shaded` | `text-muted-shaded` | An upcoming step's number while its head is held down (4.5:1 on the washed fill). | | `--stepper-wash-pressed` | `text` | The color washed over a step's indicator while its head is held down, at layer-pressed strength. | | `--stepper-bg-active` | `primary` | The current and completed steps' circle. | | `--stepper-text-active` | `on-primary` | The number or check on them. | | `--stepper-bg-error` | `danger` | A step with an error. | | `--stepper-text-error` | `on-danger` | The mark on it. | | `--stepper-warning-bg` | `warning-subtle` | A step with a warning. | | `--stepper-warning-border` | `warning-text` | Its ring. | | `--stepper-warning-text` | `warning-text` | The mark on it. | | `--stepper-title-color` | `text` | Step titles. | | `--stepper-description-color` | `text-muted` | The line under a title, and "Optional". | | `--stepper-connector` | `border-control` | The line to an upcoming step. | | `--stepper-connector-complete` | `primary` | The line after a completed step. | | `--stepper-focus-ring` | `focus-ring` | A clickable step's keyboard focus ring. | | `--stepper-edge-active` | `primary-edge` | The current and complete steps' edge and the complete connector's, inside their fill (Yellow Light; transparent where the fill is 3:1 on the page) | **Sizing** | Token | Default | Use | | --- | --- | --- | | `--stepper-indicator-size-sm` | `spacing-6` | The circle, size="sm" (24px). | | `--stepper-indicator-size-md` | `spacing-8` | The circle, size="md", the default (32px). | **Border** | Token | Default | Use | | --- | --- | --- | | `--stepper-connector-width` | `border-width-2` | The line's thickness (2px). | | `--stepper-radius` | `radius-pill` | The circle. | **Spacing** | Token | Default | Use | | --- | --- | --- | | `--stepper-gap` | `spacing-3` | Space between a circle and its text (12px). | | `--stepper-connector-gap` | `spacing-2` | Space around a line (8px). | **Type** | Token | Default | Use | | --- | --- | --- | | `--stepper-title-weight` | `font-medium` | Step titles (500). | **Motion** | Token | Default | Use | | --- | --- | --- | | `--stepper-press-scale` | `scale-100` | Size of a step's indicator while its head is held down. 100%: off by default, since a press shows as the held wash (layer-pressed). Set it, e.g. to `var(--scale-95)`, to add a shrink. | | `--stepper-layer-pressed` | `opacity-10` | How strong the wash of the text color is on a step's indicator while its head is held down (10%). |

components.name: Switch
components.summary: An on/off setting that takes effect at once.
components.guide:
# Switch

An on/off setting that takes effect at once. It's a native checkbox with `role="switch"`, so screen readers announce "on" and "off", drawn as a track (the input, `appearance: none`) and a thumb that slides along it. The track sits centered on the label's first line (each size's track is as tall as its line), and a click anywhere on the label flips it.

**Also called:** toggle, toggle switch, lightswitch.

```jsx
import { Switch } from '@diki-stwn/serupa-ds';

<Switch checked={wifi} onCheckedChange={setWifi}>Wi-Fi</Switch>

<Switch defaultChecked description="Pause notifications from 10 pm to 7 am.">Quiet hours</Switch>

// a settings list: the label first, the switch at the end of the row
<Switch labelPlacement="start" className="w-full justify-between">Autoplay videos</Switch>

// no visible label
<Switch aria-label="Enable rule" />
```

## When to use

- A setting that applies right away, like turning on Wi-Fi.
- A list of settings, each turned on or off on its own row.

## When not to use

- If the change waits for a Save button, use a [Checkbox] (npx serupa-docs Checkbox).
- An on/off button in a toolbar, such as bold: use [ToggleButton] (npx serupa-docs ToggleButton).

## Anatomy

Drawn from the `LongLabel` story.

1. **Track** (`.srp-switch__control`): the pill that shows on or off, over the native checkbox.
2. **Thumb** (`.srp-switch__thumb`): slides to the on side when it's on.
3. **Label** (`.srp-switch__text`): what it turns on; clicking it switches too.
4. **Description** (`.srp-switch__description`): optional detail under the label.

## Usage

- Label the setting, not the state: "Wi-Fi", not "Turn Wi-Fi on". The switch shows on or off.
- Don't change the label with the state, and don't add "On" and "Off" text beside it.
- In a settings list, put the label first and the switch at the end of the row.
- Add `icon` where color alone may not tell on from off, such as a switch on a busy or tinted surface: a check appears on the thumb while it's on.
- When a flip saves to a server, set `loading` while the request runs. Flip `checked` in `onChange` (optimistic) or once the save succeeds, and if it fails, put it back and say so in text nearby.

### Do and don't

- **Do:** Name the setting, and let the switch show whether it's on. (`DoNameTheSetting`)
- **Don't:** Describe the state in the label, such as "Notifications are on": it has to change with every flip. (`DontLabelTheState`)
- **Do:** Use [checkboxes] (npx serupa-docs Checkbox) in a form that waits for Save. (`DoCheckboxInForm`)
- **Don't:** Use switches there: people expect a switch to apply at once, so a flip seems to do nothing. (`DontSwitchInForm`)

## States

| State | Look |
| --- | --- |
| Off | A `track` track (the light gray Apple uses), a white thumb at the start, with the `elevation-part` shadow and no edge, as Apple's, in every theme |
| On | A `primary` track, the white thumb at the end |
| Hover | `border-strong` off, `primary-hover` on |
| Focus | From the keyboard: a 2px `focus-ring` outline 2px out (`focus-ring-width`, `focus-ring-offset`), like Button. The gap is transparent, so it reads on any background, and forced-colors mode draws it too |
| Invalid | A `danger` track while off, and a `danger` focus ring |
| Read-only | Looks as it is, with a default cursor and no hover change |
| Pending | A small `primary` ring turns on the thumb (3:1 on the thumb, on or off), with a `progress` cursor and no hover change |
| Disabled | Neutral colors at full opacity: a `disabled-surface` track in a `disabled-border` edge, a `disabled-text` thumb and label, and a `not-allowed` cursor; also inside a disabled fieldset |

The thumb slides in 100ms (`motion-press`, `ease-move`: feedback for a toggle takes 100ms or less) and jumps with `prefers-reduced-motion`. It follows the text direction: in right-to-left pages it starts on the right.

## Accessibility

- A press anywhere within 24px of the row counts (WCAG 2.5.8): when the row is shorter, its hit area reaches past what is drawn, so nothing moves. On a touch screen it's 44px high, as Apple and Material ask.
- A native checkbox with `role="switch"`: Space flips it, forms submit it (as a checkbox), and screen readers say "on" or "off". It also carries the native `switch` attribute, so Safari 18 on iPhone gives its haptic tick when it flips, as a system switch does. The tick follows the phone's own haptics setting, and the switch always shows its change, so the tick is never the only feedback.
- The label names it; a description is read after it. The thumb is decorative.
- `loading` sets `aria-busy` and stops clicks and Space from flipping it until the save is done, so a change can't be sent twice. It stays focusable and is still submitted. The ring is Loader's: a quarter arc on a faint track of the same color, turning once a second (`motion-loop-spinner`). It is decorative (`aria-hidden`), stands still and breathes with `prefers-reduced-motion`, and uses system colors in forced-colors mode.
- `readOnly` keeps it focusable and read out with `aria-readonly`, but a click or Space doesn't flip it, and `onChange` doesn't run (your `onClick` does). The browser's own `readonly` does nothing on a checkbox, so Switch cancels the click. An on read-only switch is still submitted, which `disabled` isn't.
- In forced-colors mode the track gets a border and the thumb and on track use system colors.
- The label and description keep 4.5:1; the tracks on the page, each thumb on its track (at rest and on hover) and the focus ring 3:1, in every theme (`Switch.test.tsx`).

### Keyboard

| Key | Does |
| --- | --- |
| Tab | To the switch |
| Space | Turn it on or off |

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | string | none | Goes to the native `<input role="switch">` (not the wrapper), so a `<label htmlFor>` or a Field can point at it. |
| `children` | node | | The label. Without one, give the switch an `aria-label` |
| `size` | `'sm'` \| `'md'` \| `'lg'` | `'md'` | A 28×16px track and 12px thumb with `text-xs`; 36×20 and 16 with `text-sm`; 44×24 and 20 with `text-base` |
| `description` | node | | A muted second line under the label, linked with `aria-describedby` (and kept out of the name) |
| `labelPlacement` | `'end'` \| `'start'` | `'end'` | The label after the track, or before it as in a settings list |
| `invalid` | boolean | `false` | A 2px danger edge on the track (on or off), a danger focus ring, and `aria-invalid` |
| `readOnly` | boolean | `false` | Focusable and read out (`aria-readonly`), but clicks and Space don't flip it; an on switch is still submitted |
| `icon` | boolean | `false` | A check on the thumb while on, so on and off differ by shape as well as by color; decorative, the name stays the label |
| `loading` | boolean | `false` | While a change is saved: a ring on the thumb, `aria-busy`, and clicks and Space don't flip it |

`onCheckedChange(checked, { event })` runs after `onChange` with the new state, the same shape as ToggleButton's `onPressedChange`, so you needn't read `event.target.checked`. Not while read-only or loading.

Everything else (`checked`, `defaultChecked`, `onChange`, `name`, `value`, `disabled`, `id`, `aria-*`) and `ref` go to the `<input type="checkbox" role="switch">` (`type` and `role` can't be changed). `className` and `style` go to the `<label>` around it, which has `data-component="switch"` and `data-size`.

## Component tokens

Each is an optional override: set it on the page, a container or one switch. The list lives in `src/components/Switch/switch.tokens.json` (also in `design-tokens/components/`).

<!-- token-table:start (made from switch.tokens.json by npm run tokens: edit the descriptions there) -->
**Colors**

| `--switch-track-hover` | `track-hover` | The track while off, on hover: track-hover, a step darker than track. |
| `--switch-track-pressed` | `track-pressed` | The off track while held down: track-pressed, one step past track-hover. |

| `--switch-thumb` | `white` | The thumb while off: white in every theme, as Apple's. |
| `--switch-thumb-checked` | `white` | The thumb while on: white in every theme, as Apple's. |
| `--switch-thumb-ink-dark` | `text-inverse` | In a dark theme, the loading ring and the check on the white thumb: the dark inverse text, 3:1 or more on white in every brand (a dark theme's brand colors are light). |

components.name: TabNav
components.summary: Moves between the sub-pages of one thing, such as a project's Overview, Activity and Settings, when each has its own URL.
components.guide:
# TabNav

Moves between the sub-pages of one thing, such as a project's Overview, Activity and Settings, when each has its own URL. It looks like [Tabs] (npx serupa-docs Tabs), but it's a `nav` of links: the current page is marked with `aria-current="page"`, and people move with Tab and follow a link with Enter, as on any link.

**Also called:** navigation tabs, tab links.

```jsx
import { TabNav, TabNavLink } from '@diki-stwn/serupa-ds';

<TabNav aria-label="Project">
  <TabNavLink href="/atlas" current>Overview</TabNavLink>
  <TabNavLink href="/atlas/activity" icon="history">Activity</TabNavLink>
  <TabNavLink href="/atlas/settings">Settings</TabNavLink>
</TabNav>

// with your router's link, as pills
<TabNav aria-label="Project" variant="pill" size="sm">
  <TabNavLink as={RouterLink} to="/atlas" current>Overview</TabNavLink>
</TabNav>
```

## When to use

- The sub-pages of a project, a repository, an account or a record, where each is a page people can link to, bookmark and open in a new tab.
- Under a [PageHeader](../../blocks/PageHeader/PageHeader.mdx), for the sections of the thing it names (its `sections` draw a TabNav).

## When not to use

- Panels on the same page that people switch between without leaving it: use [Tabs] (npx serupa-docs Tabs) instead.
- The app's main pages: use a [Navbar] (npx serupa-docs Navbar) or a [Sidebar] (npx serupa-docs Sidebar) instead.
- Jumping to a section further down a long page: use a [TableOfContents] (npx serupa-docs TableOfContents) instead.
- Steps people go through in order: use a [Stepper] (npx serupa-docs Stepper) instead.

## Anatomy

Drawn from the `Default` story.

1. **Link list** (`.srp-tabs__list`): the links, in one row that scrolls when they don't fit.
2. **Link** (`.srp-tabs__tab`): goes to its page; the current one has the line (or fill) under it.
3. **Icon** (`.srp-tabs__icon`): an optional picture beside the link's name.

## Usage

- Mark exactly one link `current`: the page people are on. Where a sub-page has pages of its own (Settings, then Billing), keep its link current on them too.
- Keep labels to a word or two, as with Tabs. When the links don't fit, the row scrolls sideways, the edge with more links fades out, and the current one is scrolled into view.
- Use the same `variant` and `size` as any Tabs on the same screen, so the two read as one family. TabNav takes Tabs' look and tokens: restyling Tabs restyles it too.
- `as` renders your router's link, and `configure({ link })` sets it once for the app, as for Link.

### Do and don't

- **Do:** Mark the page people are on with the tab line, so they can see where they are at a glance. (`Default`)
- **Don't:** Show sub-pages as a row of plain links, where only a bolder weight marks the current one. (`DontPlainLinks`)

## Accessibility

- **Role and name:** a `nav` landmark holding a list of links. Give it an `aria-label` that names the thing ("Project"), since a page often has more than one `nav`. The current link has `aria-current="page"`, which screen readers say as "current page".
- **Keyboard:** each link is a Tab stop, and Enter follows it. There are no arrow keys and no tab roles, because those promise panels on this page, which isn't what happens.
- **Contrast:** link labels keep 4.5:1, and the current line and pill 3:1 against `surface`, in every theme, as on Tabs (`TabNav.test.tsx`). The focus ring sits inside the link, so the scrolling row can't clip it.
- **What's still yours:** the `aria-label`, and setting `current` on the right link for the page that's showing.

## Props

### TabNav

| Prop | Type | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | string | none | Goes to the `<nav>`. |
| `variant` | `'line'` \| `'pill'` | `'line'` | A line under the current page's link, or its link filled in `primary` |
| `size` | `'sm'` \| `'md'` \| `'lg'` | `'md'` | 32px, 36px or 44px links; `lg` has 16px text, as on Tabs |

`className`, `ref` and other props go to the `<nav>`. It has `data-component="tab-nav"` and `data-variant`.

### TabNavLink

| Prop | Type | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `current` | boolean | `false` | This is the page people are on: `aria-current="page"`, drawn as the selected tab |
| `icon` | string \| element | | An icon before the label: an icon name or any element |
| `as` | element type | `configure({ link })`, else `'a'` | Your router's link component; it gets the rest of the props |

`href`, `className`, `ref` and other props go to the link, which sits in an `<li>`. It has `data-state="active"` or `"inactive"`.

## Component tokens

TabNav has no tokens of its own. It's drawn with Tabs' classes, so [Tabs' tokens] (npx serupa-docs Tabs) (`--tabs-height-md`, `--tabs-indicator`, `--tabs-text` and the rest) style it too.

components.name: Table
components.summary: A data table built on native table markup: a header row, body rows and an optional footer, in a bordered frame that scrolls sideways when the table is too wide.
components.guide:
# Table A data table built on native table markup: a header row, body rows and an optional footer, in a bordered frame that scrolls sideways when the table is too wide. Rows shade on hover (or every other one with `striped`), can be selected with a checkbox column (`TableSelectCell`) or opened to show their details (`TableExpandCell`), and columns can be sorted, resized, pinned while the rest scroll, and shown or hidden (`TableColumnsMenu`). **Also called:** data table. ```jsx import { Table, TableHead, TableBody, TableFoot, TableRow, TableHeaderCell, TableCell, TableSelectCell } from '@diki-stwn/serupa-ds'; Name Role setSort(sort === 'ascending' ? 'descending' : 'ascending')}>Calls {people.map((p) => ( toggle(p.id)} /> {p.name} {p.role} {p.calls} ))}
…
``` ## When to use - Data with several values per row that people compare down the columns: members and their roles, orders and their totals. - People need to sort by a column, or read numbers lined up under each other. ## When not to use - Items with a line or two of text each, such as people or files: use [List] (npx serupa-docs List) instead. - Items with pictures or a lot of content each: use [Card] (npx serupa-docs Card)s in a [Grid] (npx serupa-docs Grid). - Laying out a page or a form in columns: use [Grid] (npx serupa-docs Grid) or [Stack] (npx serupa-docs Stack); a table is for data. ## Anatomy Drawn from the `Sortable` story. 1. **Caption** (`.srp-table__caption`): names the table for everyone, screen readers too. 2. **Header row** (`.srp-table__head`): the column names. 3. **Sortable header** (`.srp-table__header--sortable`): a column you can sort by; the arrow says which way. 4. **Row** (`.srp-table__row`): one record. 5. **Cell** (`.srp-table__cell`): one value; numbers line up at the end. 6. **Footer** (`.srp-table__foot`): totals or a summary. ## Usage Table only lays out what you give it: sorting, filtering and selection state stay in your code. Sort text columns with `useCollator().compare`, so names sort the way people in the page's locale expect ("Item 2" before "Item 10", "Äpfel" beside "Apfel" in German). - Give every table a `caption`. When a heading on the page already says what it holds, add `hideCaption` so screen readers still hear it. - Set `align="end"` on number columns, in the header and the cells, so the digits line up. - A number given to `TableCell` as its child (`{p.calls}`) is written in the locale's digits, ungrouped as given: 1204 in en-US, ١٢٠٤ in ar-EG. For grouping, currency or units, put a `FormattedNumber` in the cell. - When rows change under the user (sorting, filtering, paging), use `layout="fixed"` so the columns don't jump: set `width` on the header cells that need it (`"40%"`, `"8rem"`, or a number of pixels) and the others share what's left. Long text wraps in its cell. With the default `layout="auto"`, each column is as wide as its content on that page. - Use `size="sm"` for dense data, and `striped` when long rows are hard to follow across. - With selectable rows, put a `TableActionBar` just before the table: while rows are selected it shows "3 selected", your actions for them (Delete, Export) and "Clear selection" (`onClear`). Pass it the count; it's hidden at 0. It reads out each new count, including the first when you render it only while rows are selected, but keeping it mounted also moves focus to "Select all" when Clear empties the selection. - When the table shows one page of many, give the bar `total` (how many rows match, on every page) and `onSelectAll`: once some rows are selected it offers "Select all 1,240", and says "All 1,240 selected" when `count` reaches the total, so a bulk action can reach every row without paging through. Keep the selection as "every matching row" rather than a list of ids when the rows aren't all loaded, and let it go when the search or filters change. Add `sticky` to keep the bar at the top while a long table scrolls past; set `--table-action-bar-top` to the height of your page's own sticky header. - To make each row open a page, give the `TableRow` an `href` (with `target` and `rel` as on a link). The row gets one real link, in its first `TableCell` (or the one you mark `link`), stretched over the whole row: a click anywhere on it follows the link, Ctrl/Cmd-click and middle-click open a new tab, and the keyboard tabs to it. Buttons, checkboxes and links in other cells sit above it and work on their own. Don't use `onClick` on a row for this: it reaches the mouse only, and warns in development. - A button that removes its own row (Delete, Archive) takes focus away with the row, and focus then falls to the top of the page. Move it yourself once the row is gone: to the same button in the next row, else the one before, else the table's heading. With a confirmation Dialog, pass that element as its `finalFocus`. - Let people widen a column whose content gets cut or wraps a lot: `resizable` on its `TableHeaderCell`, in a table with `layout="fixed"`, starting from a `width` in pixels. A handle at the header's end edge drags; with focus, the arrow keys move it 16px at a time and Home and End go to `minWidth` (48) and `maxWidth` (800); a double-click fits the column to its widest cell on one line. A click on the handle (or Enter or Space on it) opens Narrower, Wider and Fit to content, so a width never needs a drag (WCAG 2.5.7). Uncontrolled, the column keeps its own width; to remember widths, pass `width` and `onWidthChange` together and keep the number. - When a table scrolls sideways, keep the column that names each row in view with `pinStart`, and a column of row actions with `pinEnd`. Pinned cells take their row's shading, and lift with a shadow while there's more to scroll to under them (where scroll-state container queries are supported). It's the first and the last cell of each row, so put a select or expand column after the name, or leave it unpinned. - The column tools' parts: a resize handle (`.srp-table__resize`) at a resizable header's end edge; a pinned first or last column (`pinStart`, `pinEnd`) that stays in view; an expand button (`.srp-table__expand-button`) whose chevron turns down while the row's details (`.srp-table__detail`) show under it; and the Columns button (`TableColumnsMenu`). - For tables with more columns than people need at once, put a `TableColumnsMenu` above the table with the same list you draw the columns from (`columns`, each `{ id, label, visible, required? }`), and draw the table from the list `onColumnsChange(columns, { id, visible })` gives back. Mark the column that names each row `required`; the last one shown can't be cleared either, so the table is never empty. - For rows with more than fits in their cells (an order's note, a log entry's message), start each row with a `TableExpandCell` (`label`: the row's name, `expanded`, `onExpandedChange`, `controls`: the detail row's id) and follow it with a `TableDetailRow` (`id`, `open`, `colSpan` of every column). The header row gets a `TableExpandCell inHeader`. `striped` counts only the rows of data, so open details don't swap the shading. - With `stickyHeader`, give the frame a height through `containerProps`. The frame measures the header and keeps that much scroll padding at the top, so a focused link or button in a row scrolls into view below the header, not under it (WCAG 2.4.11). - For thousands of rows, use `TableVirtualBody` in place of `TableBody`: it draws only the rows in view of the frame, plus a few either side, so 10,000 rows scroll as quickly as 20. Give the frame a height (`containerProps={{ style: { maxHeight: 480 } }}`, usually with `stickyHeader`), since without one every row is in view. Columns size to the rows drawn, so set widths (`table-layout: fixed` or a width per header cell) where a column mustn't shift while scrolling. Each drawn row gets `aria-rowindex` and the table `aria-rowcount`, a row with focus stays drawn when it scrolls away, and `striped` shades the same rows as a `TableBody` would. In print it draws every row, up to the first 5,000 (about 100 pages); for more, offer an export (CSV) instead of print. Sorting and filtering stay yours: sort the data, then draw row `index` from it. ## Behavior - The frame scrolls when the table is wider than it, and then becomes a focusable region named by the caption. A table that fits adds no tab stop. - A row's hover shading eases in only while the pointer is over the body, so "Select all" repaints every row at once. - With `stickyHeader`, the header stays at the top of the frame and lifts with a shadow once rows scroll under it. At the top it is flat. - A resize handle's width buttons open under the handle, or above it when there's no room, with focus on the first that can be pressed. They appear and go at once. Escape or a press outside closes them. - A row's details chevron turns down while its details show, and turns back as they hide. Under reduced motion it turns at once. - Nothing in the table reorders, filters or selects rows by itself: it draws the order and state you pass. ### Do and don't - **Do:** End-align number columns, in the header and the cells, so the digits line up by place. (`DoAlignNumbers`) - **Don't:** Leave amounts start-aligned like text: 85.50 and 14,520.00 then look alike at a glance. (`DontStartNumbers`) ### Loading, empty and failed The table keeps its header and caption in every state, so the page doesn't move and people know what's coming. - **Loading:** set `loading` on the Table and draw a `TableLoadingRows` in place of the `TableBody`, with `columns` set to every column and `rows` to about as many rows as will come (up to a screenful). Each placeholder row is as tall as a real one, at either `size`, so nothing jumps when the data arrives. Name the wait in `label` ("Loading projects"): a screen reader hears it once, after the loader's delay, so a quick load says nothing. `loading` sets `aria-busy` on the table while it lasts. To reload rows already shown, keep them and set `loading`, or swap them for placeholders if the old ones would mislead. - **Empty:** a `TableBody` with one `TableMessageRow` (`colSpan` of every column) holding an `EmptyState size="sm"`: what's missing, and the action that adds the first one. - **Failed:** the same row with a danger `Alert`, which says what didn't load and offers Retry in `actions`. A danger Alert is `role="alert"`, so the failure is heard as it appears. On Retry, go back to loading. ```tsx … {state === 'loading' ? : {state === 'failed' ? Retry}>Projects didn't load. : projects.length ? projects.map((p) => …) : } }
``` ## Accessibility - It's a real ``, so screen readers announce rows, columns and headers. Give it a `caption` (or `aria-label`) so people know what it holds. - When it's too wide and scrolls, the frame becomes a focusable region named by the caption, so keyboard users can scroll it with the arrow keys. When it fits, it adds no tab stop. - A sortable header is a button, and its `
` has `aria-sort` once sorted. After sorting, the button keeps focus, and the new order is read out politely ("Sorted by Amount, ascending.", the `tableSorted` label), because `aria-sort` alone is only heard when focus comes back to the header. Nothing is read on the first render. - `TableActionBar` is a group named by its count ("2 selected"), and a new count is read out politely, since the bar appears away from the checkbox that was pressed. When it hides with focus in it (after "Clear selection", or an action that empties the selection), focus moves to the first checkbox of the table after it (the header's "Select all"), so it isn't dropped on the page. "Select all 1,240" goes away once it has done its job, and focus moves on to the bar's next button. Its count reads 4.5:1 on the bar in every theme. - A row with `href` is one link, named by its link cell's text ("Ada"), so screen readers hear one link per row, not a clickable row they can't find. Focus on it rings the whole row. - A resize handle is a focusable `separator` named for its column ("Resize Name column", the `tableResizeColumn` label), with `aria-valuenow`, `aria-valuemin` and `aria-valuemax` in pixels, so screen readers say the width as it changes. Before a width is set, its value is the column's drawn width. It's described as "Press Enter for width buttons" (the `tableResizeHint` label), since a separator can't say it opens anything. It's 12px wide; the arrow keys do what dragging does, and its popover's three buttons do the same for a pointer (Narrower and Wider move 16px; the `tableNarrower`, `tableWider` and `tableFitColumn` labels). - A `TableExpandCell`'s button is named for its row ("Details, Order 1001", `tableRowDetails`), with `aria-expanded` and `aria-controls` pointing at the `TableDetailRow`, which stays in the page, hidden, while closed. The header's cell is named "Details" (`tableDetails`) for screen readers and shows nothing. In right-to-left pages the chevron points left. - `TableColumnsMenu` is a [Popover] (npx serupa-docs Popover) titled "Columns" (`tableColumns`) of [Checkbox] (npx serupa-docs Checkbox)es named by the columns; a required column's box is checked and disabled. - In print, the frame shows the whole table instead of its scrolled window, the header row repeats on every page, and a row isn't split across pages. `TableVirtualBody` prints up to 5,000 rows and appends a localized summary row ("Showing 5,000 of 12,345") when more rows exist. - Text and muted text keep 4.5:1 on plain, hovered, striped and selected rows, and the header text on its background; the selected bar keeps 3:1 (every theme, `Table.test.tsx`). Selection isn't shown by color alone: the bar shows it, and a `TableSelectCell`'s checkbox ("Select Ada, checked") says it to screen readers. Browsers ignore `aria-selected` on a plain table's rows, so `selected` doesn't set it; give selectable rows a `TableSelectCell`.
