components.name: TableOfContents
components.summary: An "On this page" list of links to the sections of a long page, as a navigation landmark.
components.guide:
# TableOfContents

An "On this page" list of links to the sections of a long page, as a navigation landmark. It reads the page's headings (or takes a list), marks the section being read as the page scrolls, and a click scrolls to that section and moves focus to its heading.

**Also called:** TOC, on this page, page outline.

```jsx
import { TableOfContents } from '@diki-stwn/serupa-ds';

// from the h2 and h3 headings in <main>
<aside className="sticky top-4"><TableOfContents /></aside>

// from one article, under a 64px sticky header
<TableOfContents container="#article" offset={80} />

// your own list
<TableOfContents items={[{ id: "install", label: "Installation" }, { id: "npm", label: "With npm", level: 3 }]} />

// a narrow rail of dashes that shows the list on hover, focus or a tap
<TableOfContents variant="rail" />
```

## When to use

- A long page people scan and jump around in: documentation, a policy, a settings page with many sections, a long form.
- Beside the content on a wide screen, kept in view with `position: sticky`.
- `variant="rail"` where a side column has no room for the titles: a 24px column of dashes that shows the list in a panel when people point at it, Tab into it or tap it.

## When not to use

- Moving between pages: use a [Sidebar] (npx serupa-docs Sidebar) or [Tabs] (npx serupa-docs Tabs).
- A short page with two or three sections: the headings are enough.
- Steps people go through in order: use a [Stepper] (npx serupa-docs Stepper).

## Anatomy

Drawn from the `Playground` story.

1. **Title** (`.srp-toc__title`): "On this page"; it names the landmark.
2. **Link** (`.srp-toc__link`): one section; deeper ones step in, and the current one is marked by a line in primary, twice as wide as the others.

With `variant="rail"` (the `Rail` story), two more parts:

- **Rail** (`.srp-toc__rail`): a dash (`.srp-toc__dash`) per section, 12px long and 4px shorter a level, the current one in primary.
- **Panel** (`.srp-toc__panel`): the title and the links, over the page from the rail's top end corner, 256px wide at most.

## Usage

- Keep it to two levels (the default `h2, h3`): deeper lists are hard to scan.
- Give the headings `scroll-margin-top` the height of any sticky header, and set `offset` to about the same plus a little, so a section counts as reached when its heading clears the header.
- Headings without an `id` get one from their text ("Beta part" becomes `beta-part`), kept unique on the page, so links to them can be shared: a page opened with one (`#beta-part`) scrolls to that heading once its id is made. Headings added, removed or renamed later, such as content loaded after the page, update the list.
- On a phone, put it at the top of the page or in an [Accordion] (npx serupa-docs Accordion), not beside the text.
- The rail is for a column beside the text with little room, such as a docs page's end edge. Give it room to its start side: its panel opens over the page from its top end corner. Where people need the titles in view to choose (a long settings page), use the list.

## Behavior

- The list marks the section being read as the page scrolls. A click scrolls to the heading (smoothly unless motion is reduced), puts its id in the address and moves focus to it.
- The rail shows its panel while the pointer is over it or the panel, while focus is on one of its links, or after a tap (touch or pen) until a tap elsewhere or a link. The panel fades and grows in and out; from the keyboard it's there at once; under reduced motion it only fades. Escape hides it until the pointer and focus leave. The panel is at most the window's height less `--table-of-contents-panel-gap` (64px), and a longer list scrolls inside it, so every link stays in reach on a page of many headings.

### Do and don't

- **Do:** Keep it to two levels (the default `h2, h3`). (`DoTwoLevels`)
- **Don't:** Go three or four levels deep: the list becomes hard to scan. (`DontDeepLevels`)

## Accessibility

- **Role and name:** a `nav` landmark named by its title (or `aria-label` with `title={null}`), holding a list of links. The current section's link has `aria-current="location"`, and is marked by a wider line, not by color alone.
- **The rail:** its dashes are hidden from screen readers; the links are in the panel, so a screen reader reads the same landmark and links as the list, shown or not. A hidden panel takes no presses.
- **Motion:** the scroll is smooth only when the reader hasn't asked for reduced motion.
- **Contrast:** links read 4.5:1 on the page and on the rail's panel, the current section's line and dash 3:1, in every theme (`TableOfContents.test.tsx`).
- **What's still yours:** headings that say what each section is about.

### Keyboard

| Key | Does |
| --- | --- |
| Tab | Through the links. In the rail, Tab to the first link shows the panel |
| Enter | Follows the focused link. Focus then moves to the section's heading, so the next Tab continues from there in the content |
| Escape | In the rail, hides the panel with focus kept, until the pointer and focus leave (WCAG 1.4.13) |

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `items` | `TocItem[]` | | `{ id, label, level? }`: your own entries instead of the headings |
| `container` | `Element \| string` | `<main>`, else `<body>` | Where to read the headings from. They may scroll with the page or in a pane of their own (`overflow: auto`). |
| `headings` | `string` | `"h2, h3"` | Which headings it lists |
| `title` | `ReactNode \| null` | "On this page" | The title and the landmark's name; `null` for none |
| `variant` | `"list" \| "rail"` | `"list"` | `"rail"`: dashes that show the list in a panel on hover, focus or a tap |
| `offset` | `number` | `96` | How far from the top of the window (or of the pane the headings scroll in), in pixels, a heading counts as reached |
| `id` | `string` | | Goes to the `<nav>`. |

`className`, `ref` and other props go to the `<nav>`.

## Component tokens

Each is an optional override: set it on the page, a container or one TableOfContents. The list lives in `src/components/TableOfContents/table-of-contents.tokens.json` (also in `design-tokens/components/`).

<!-- token-table:start (made from table-of-contents.tokens.json by npm run tokens: edit the descriptions there) -->
| Token | Default | Use |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--table-of-contents-muted` | `text-muted` | The links (4.5:1 on the page). |
| `--table-of-contents-title` | `text` | The title, and a link under the pointer (4.5:1). |
| `--table-of-contents-current` | `text` | The current section's link (4.5:1). |
| `--table-of-contents-line` | `border` | The line along the links. |
| `--table-of-contents-line-current` | `primary-text` | The line beside the current section's link (3:1). |
| `--table-of-contents-focus-ring` | `focus-ring` | The ring around a focused link. |
| `--table-of-contents-dash` | `border-strong` | The rail's dashes (decorative: the links are in its panel). |
| `--table-of-contents-panel` | `surface-overlay` | The rail's panel, over the page. |
| `--table-of-contents-panel-border` | `border-overlay` | The rail's panel's edge. |
| `--table-of-contents-panel-divider` | `border-overlay` | What a divider or separator inside it reads as `border`: its own edge color, since in dark `border` is the surface's own color and a line in it vanished |
| `--table-of-contents-panel-gap` | `spacing-16` | How much shorter than the window the rail's panel is at most (64px): room for a sticky column's offset above and a margin below. A longer list scrolls inside it. |
<!-- token-table:end -->

components.name: Tabs
components.summary: Switches between related panels in one place, such as a project's Overview, Activity and Settings.
components.guide:
# Tabs

Switches between related panels in one place, such as a project's Overview, Activity and Settings. It follows the WAI-ARIA tabs pattern: `Tabs` holds the state, `TabList` the row of `Tab`s, and each `TabPanel` the content for the tab with the same `value`.

**Also called:** tabbed interface.

```jsx
import { Tabs, TabList, Tab, TabPanel } from '@diki-stwn/serupa-ds';

<Tabs defaultValue="overview">
  <TabList aria-label="Project">
    <Tab value="overview">Overview</Tab>
    <Tab value="activity" icon="history">Activity</Tab>
    <Tab value="settings" disabled>Settings</Tab>
  </TabList>
  <TabPanel value="overview">…</TabPanel>
  <TabPanel value="activity">…</TabPanel>
  <TabPanel value="settings">…</TabPanel>
</Tabs>

// controlled, as pills
<Tabs value={view} onValueChange={setView} variant="pill" size="sm">…</Tabs>
```

## When to use

- Several views of the same thing that people switch between, one at a time: a project's Overview, Activity and Settings.
- A page with more content than fits, where each part stands on its own and people know which one they want.
- Panels that should keep their state while people look elsewhere, such as a half-filled form: hidden panels stay in the page.

## When not to use

- Choosing a value, such as a period (Day, Week, Month) for the same content: use [SegmentedControl] (npx serupa-docs SegmentedControl) instead. It's a radio group, not a set of panels.
- Steps people go through in order: use [Stepper] (npx serupa-docs Stepper) instead.
- Moving between the sub-pages of one thing that each have their own URL, such as a project's Overview and Settings: use [TabNav] (npx serupa-docs TabNav) instead. It looks like Tabs but is a nav of links. For the app's main pages, use a [Navbar] (npx serupa-docs Navbar) or a [Sidebar] (npx serupa-docs Sidebar).
- Sections people may want open side by side, or read one after another: use [Accordion] (npx serupa-docs Accordion) instead.

## Anatomy

Drawn from the `Pill` story.

1. **Tab list** (`.srp-tabs__list`): the tabs, in one row that scrolls when they don't fit.
2. **Tab** (`.srp-tabs__tab`): shows its panel; the arrow keys move between tabs.
3. **Icon** (`.srp-tabs__icon`): an optional picture beside the tab's name.
4. **Panel** (`.srp-tabs__panel`): the content of the chosen tab.

## Usage

- Keep tab labels to a word or two. When the tabs don't fit, the row scrolls sideways: the edge with more tabs past it fades out, and the selected tab, or one reached with Tab, is always scrolled into view clear of the fade, but people can still miss the tabs out of view. It scrolls in a CSS grid track or a flex row too, without widening the page.
- Use `orientation="vertical"` for a settings page or anything with more than about six tabs: a column at the start of the panels, which has room for them all.
- Set `activation="manual"` when a panel is slow to show, so arrowing past a tab doesn't select it.
- Keep each panel's controls about that panel: a Save or a filter inside one tab changes only what's in that tab. Controls that act on every tab go above the tab row.
- Hidden panels keep their state. Set `keepMounted={false}` on a panel that doesn't need to, so it renders only while it's selected.
- The browser's find-in-page searches kept panels too. They're `hidden="until-found"`, so a match on another tab selects that tab and shows it, as Accordion opens an item. A disabled tab's panel isn't searched.
- Show a tab people can't use yet as `disabled` rather than leaving it out, when knowing it exists helps them.
- Tabs people open and close, such as documents or queries: give each closable `Tab` an `onClose` that removes it, and the `TabList` an `onAdd` and `addLabel` for a "+ New query" button after the tabs. A closable tab has a × at its end for the pointer, and Delete closes it from the keyboard. Leave `onClose` off a tab that must stay, such as a pinned one. (`Closable`)
- When the selected tab is removed, uncontrolled Tabs select the next enabled tab (or else the previous one) and call `onValueChange`. If focus was on the closed tab (its own close button, or a Delete key you handle), it moves to the tab now selected, not to the page. With `value`, set it to another tab yourself when you remove the selected one; Tabs warns in the console otherwise.

### Do and don't

- **Do:** Keep each label to a word or two, so every tab stays in view. (`DoShortLabels`)
- **Don't:** Write long labels: the row scrolls, and people miss the tabs past the edge. (`DontLongLabels`)
- **Do:** Use a [SegmentedControl] (npx serupa-docs SegmentedControl) to pick a value, such as a period, for the same content. (`DoSegmentedForValue`)
- **Don't:** Use tabs for that: tabs say each choice has its own panel, and screen readers announce them that way. (`DontTabsForValue`)

## Accessibility

- `role="tablist"`, `"tab"` and `"tabpanel"`, with `aria-selected`, `aria-controls` and `aria-labelledby` set for you.
- Only the selected tab is in the Tab order, and the shown panel itself can take focus when it starts with text, so keyboard users always reach the content. A panel that starts with a link, button or field leaves the stop to that, so Tab from the tab lands on it directly; a kept panel of another tab is out of the Tab order. When a controlled `value` matches no tab (a stale link, data still loading), the first enabled tab takes the Tab stop instead, so the list can still be reached.
- Tab labels keep 4.5:1, and the selected line and pill 3:1 against `surface`, in every theme (`Tabs.test.tsx`). The focus ring sits inside the tab so the scrolling row can't clip it.
- The selected line or fill slides from the tab selected before. Pick another tab mid-slide and it turns back from where it is, not from the last tab. With reduced motion it moves at once, and so it does when an arrow, Home or End picks the tab.
- In forced-colors mode the selected tab is marked in `Highlight`.
- A closable tab's × is for the pointer and is hidden from screen readers: a tab can't hold a second button. The tab's description says "Press Delete to close." instead (`aria-keyshortcuts="Delete"`). The + after the tabs is a button beside the tab list, with `addLabel` as its visible words.

### Keyboard

| Key | Does |
| --- | --- |
| Tab | Into the tab list (on the selected tab), then to the selected panel |
| ← → | The previous or next tab, wrapping, following the text direction; disabled tabs are skipped. Also selects it unless `activation="manual"`. With `orientation="vertical"`, ↑ ↓ do this instead |
| Home, End | The first or last tab |
| Enter, Space | Selects the focused tab |
| Delete | Closes the focused tab, when it has `onClose`. Focus goes to the tab selected next, or to the tab beside it |

## Props

### Tabs

| Prop | Type | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | string | none | Goes to the root `<div>`. |
| `value` | string | | The selected tab (controlled), with `onValueChange` |
| `defaultValue` | string | the first enabled tab | The tab selected at first (uncontrolled) |
| `onValueChange` | `(value) => void` | | Called when a tab is chosen |
| `variant` | `'line'` \| `'pill'` | `'line'` | A line under the selected tab, or the selected tab filled in `primary` |
| `size` | `'sm'` \| `'md'` \| `'lg'` | `'md'` | 32px, 36px or 44px tabs; `lg` has 16px text, to sit beside large fields and buttons and give a touch-sized target |
| `activation` | `'auto'` \| `'manual'` | `'auto'` | Whether arrow keys also select, or only move (then Enter or Space selects). Use manual when a panel is slow to show |
| `orientation` | `'horizontal'` \| `'vertical'` | `'horizontal'` | A row over the panels, or a column beside them (`aria-orientation`, ↑ ↓). The line variant's line moves to the column's end side |

### TabList, Tab and TabPanel

- `TabList`: the row. Give it an `aria-label` when nothing on the page says what the tabs are for. `onAdd` with `addLabel` ("New query") shows a + after the tabs; select the new tab in it, and focus goes with the selection. It scrolls sideways when the tabs don't fit (down, when vertical and its height is limited), fading out the edge with more tabs past it, and keeps the selected tab in view.
- `Tab`: `value` (required), `icon` (a name or element), `disabled`, `onClose` (a × at its end and the Delete key close it; remove the tab in it), and every `<button>` prop.
- `TabPanel`: `value` (required). Hidden panels stay in the page and keep their state; `keepMounted={false}` renders a panel only while it's selected.

Each part takes `className`, `style`, `ref` and other props. `Tabs` has `data-component="tabs"` and `data-variant`; tabs and panels have `data-state="active"` or `"inactive"`.

## Component tokens

Each is an optional override: set it on the page, a container or one set of tabs. The list lives in `src/components/Tabs/tabs.tokens.json` (also in `design-tokens/components/`).

<!-- token-table:start (made from tabs.tokens.json by npm run tokens: edit the descriptions there) -->
**Colors**

| Token | Default | Use |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--tabs-text` | `text-muted` | A tab's label (4.5:1 on surface). |
| `--tabs-text-hover` | `text` | A tab's label on hover. |
| `--tabs-text-selected` | `text` | The selected tab's label (line). |
| `--tabs-indicator` | `primary-text` | The line under the selected tab (3:1 on surface). |
| `--tabs-border` | `border` | The line under the whole tab list (line). |
| `--tabs-pill-bg-hover` | `secondary` | A pill tab's background on hover. |
| `--tabs-pill-bg-pressed` | `pressed` | A pill tab's background while it's pressed, before it's selected, one step past hover. |
| `--tabs-pill-bg-selected` | `primary` | The selected pill tab's background. |
| `--tabs-pill-text-selected` | `on-primary` | The selected pill tab's label. |
| `--tabs-focus-ring` | `focus-ring` | The keyboard focus ring, on a tab and on the panel. |

components.name: TagGroup
components.summary: Short labels people remove or pick: the labels on a ticket, the recipients of a message, the skills on a profile.
components.guide:
# TagGroup

Short labels people remove or pick: the labels on a ticket, the recipients of a message, the skills on a profile. The tags are one Tab stop, the arrow keys move between them, and Delete or the × removes one without losing focus.

**Also called:** chip group, tag list.

```tsx
import { TagGroup } from "@diki-stwn/serupa-ds";

<TagGroup label="Labels" items={[{ id: "design", label: "Design" }, { id: "bug", label: "Bug" }]}
  onRemove={(id) => setItems((t) => t.filter((x) => x.id !== id))} />
```

## When to use

- A short list of things on a record that people take off one at a time: labels, recipients, attached categories.
- A set of words people pick from, several at once or one, where each choice is a word rather than a setting: interests, skills, topics (`selectionMode`).

## When not to use

- A status or a count that nobody acts on: use [Badge] (npx serupa-docs Badge).
- Filters on a list or table, with an editor per filter: use [FilterBar] (npx serupa-docs FilterBar), whose chips say the filter in words.
- Two to five options of a setting, one shown pressed: use [SegmentedControl] (npx serupa-docs SegmentedControl) or [ToggleGroup] (npx serupa-docs ToggleGroup).
- Picking values while typing: use [Combobox] (npx serupa-docs Combobox) with `multiple`.

## Anatomy

Drawn from the `Default` story.

1. **Label** (`.srp-tag-group__label`): names the group, above the tags.
2. **Tags** (`.srp-tag-group__tags`): the grid, a wrapping row of tags.
3. **Tag** (`.srp-tag-group__tag`): one tag's row.
4. **Text** (`.srp-tag-group__text`): the tag's words, after a tick when it's picked.
5. **Remove** (`.srp-tag-group__remove`): the × that takes the tag off, in its own cell.

Past `max`, a Show more button follows the tags; with none, the `emptyText` words take their place.

## Usage

- Give it a `label`, shown above the tags, so the group has a name; or `aria-label` when the screen already says what they are.
- With `onRemove`, take the tag out of `items` in it. Focus moves to the next tag (or the one before, or the group), and "Design removed" is said.
- With `selectionMode`, a press, Space or Enter picks a tag. A picked tag has a tick as well as its color.
- Give a recipient tag its `avatar`, or a label tag an `icon` for its kind, when the picture helps people find one at a glance. Both are decorative, so the words still have to say it all.
- Use `max` for a list that can grow long: the rest wait behind "Show more", which becomes "Show less".
- Pass `emptyText` ("No labels yet") so a list with nothing in it still says so.
- Keep each tag to a word or two; long ones wrap inside the tag.

### Do and don't

- **Do:** A word or two in each tag. (`DoShortTags`)
- **Don't:** Sentences in tags: they stop reading as tags, and each takes a row of its own. Put a sentence in the text beside them. (`DontSentences`)

## Accessibility

- **Role and name:** a grid (`role="grid"`) named by its label, with a row per tag; the tag's words are its first cell and its × the second, a button named "Remove Design". Picked tags have `aria-selected`, and a multiple-choice group `aria-multiselectable`.
- **Keyboard:** one Tab stop, on the last tag focused (the table below).
- **Focus:** removing a tag moves focus to the next one, so it's never dropped to the page.
- **Contrast:** a tag's words read 4.5:1 in every theme, picked or not. A plain tag's border is the light `border-strong` a field has, since its words mark it; a picked tag's border keeps 3:1 (`TagGroup.test.tsx`).
- **What's still yours:** the label, and what removing or picking a tag does in your app (saving it, undoing it).

### Keyboard

| Key | Does |
| --- | --- |
| Tab | Into the tags, on the last one focused, and on out; the × buttons aren't Tab stops |
| Right / Left | The next or previous tag, in the reading direction |
| Down / Up | The next or previous tag |
| Home / End | The first or last tag |
| Delete / Backspace | Removes the focused tag (with `onRemove`); focus moves to the next |
| Space / Enter | Picks or clears the focused tag (with `selectionMode`) |

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | `string` | | Goes to the outer `<div>` |
| `items` | `TagItem[]` | | `{ id, label, disabled?, icon?, avatar? }`, in order. `icon` (an icon name or element) and `avatar` (a picture such as `<Avatar size="xs" />`, drawn at 20px inside the tag's border) sit before the words and are decorative: the words name the tag. A selected tag shows its check where its icon was |
| `label` | `ReactNode` | | The group's visible label |
| `onRemove` | `(id) => void` | | Shows a × on each tag; Delete and Backspace remove too |
| `selectionMode` | `'none' \| 'single' \| 'multiple'` | `'none'` | Picking tags |
| `selected` / `defaultSelected` | `string[]` | | The picked ids |
| `onSelectedChange` | `(ids) => void` | | Called with the picked ids |
| `max` | `number` | all | Show this many, and "Show more" for the rest |
| `emptyText` | `ReactNode` | | Shown when there are no tags |

`className`, `ref` and other props go to the outer `<div>`.

## Component tokens

Each is an optional override: set it on the page, a container or one TagGroup. The list lives in `src/components/TagGroup/tag-group.tokens.json` (also in `design-tokens/components/`).

<!-- token-table:start (made from tag-group.tokens.json by npm run tokens: edit the descriptions there) -->
**Colors**

| Token | Default | Use |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--tag-group-bg` | `surface` | A tag's background. |
| `--tag-group-text` | `text` | A tag's words (4.5:1 on bg). |
| `--tag-group-border` | `border-strong` | A tag's border: the light one a field and an outline Badge have. Its words mark the tag, so the edge needn't be 3:1; a picked tag's border is. |
| `--tag-group-bg-hover` | `surface-hover` | A tag that can be picked, under the pointer. A picked tag keeps its own colors, as a pressed ToggleButton does. |
| `--tag-group-bg-pressed` | `pressed` | A tag that can be picked, while it's held down, one step past bg-hover. |
| `--tag-group-bg-selected` | `primary-subtle` | A picked tag's background. |
| `--tag-group-text-selected` | `primary-text` | A picked tag's words and tick (4.5:1 on bg-selected). |
| `--tag-group-border-selected` | `primary-text` | A picked tag's border. |
| `--tag-group-remove-hover` | `surface-hover` | The × button's background under the pointer. |
| `--tag-group-remove-pressed` | `pressed` | The × while it's held down, one step past remove-hover. |
| `--tag-group-label` | `text` | The group's label. |
| `--tag-group-muted` | `text-muted` | The empty text. |
| `--tag-group-focus-ring` | `focus-ring` | The focus ring around the focused tag. |
| `--tag-group-more` | `primary-text` | The Show more and Show less button's words (4.5:1 on the page). |
| `--tag-group-more-hover` | `primary-text-hover` | The Show more and Show less button's words on hover, as a link's (4.5:1 on the page). |
| `--tag-group-icon` | `text-muted` | A tag's leading icon (decorative; the words name the tag). |
| `--tag-group-border-disabled` | `disabled-border` | Disabled: the edge. |
| `--tag-group-text-disabled` | `disabled-text` | Disabled: the text, icon or mark, in place of fading it (3:1 or more on its background, more with more contrast). |

**Radius**

| Token | Default | Use |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--tag-group-radius` | `radius-control` | A tag's corners, as other controls'. |

**Spacing**

| Token | Default | Use |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--tag-group-gap` | `spacing-2` | The space between tags (8px). |
| `--tag-group-label-gap` | `spacing-1.5` | The space between the label and the tags, as between a Field's label and its control (6px). |
| `--tag-group-avatar-size` | `spacing-5` | The picture before a tag's words (20px), inside the tag's border with 1px clear of it, so the circle never breaks the line. |
| `--tag-group-avatar-text` | `spacing-2` | The initials in a tag's 20px picture (8px), so two letters fit its circle even with wider letter spacing (WCAG 1.4.12). The person's name is in the tag beside it. |
| `--tag-group-icon-size` | `spacing-3.5` | A tag's icon, the check of a selected tag and the × (14px), beside the 12px label, as in a small Button. |
<!-- token-table:end -->

components.name: Text
components.summary: Body text in the system's type: a paragraph, a caption, an error line.
components.guide:
# Text

Body text in the system's type: a paragraph, a caption, an error line. `size`, `tone` and `weight` set only what you give them, so anything you leave out follows the parent, and Text can sit inside a card, a cell or a button without fighting it.

**Also called:** paragraph, body text.

```jsx
import { Text } from '@diki-stwn/serupa-ds';

<Text>Invite people to work on this project with you.</Text>
<Text size="sm" tone="muted">Last edited 2 hours ago</Text>
<Text as="span" weight="semibold">6 of 10</Text> seats used
<Text tone="danger" size="sm">The name is already taken.</Text>
<Text as="span" truncate style={{ maxWidth: 200 }}>{fileName}</Text>
```

## When to use

- Paragraphs, captions and short lines of supporting text, such as "Last edited 2 hours ago".
- Changing the size, tone or weight of part of a sentence, with `as="span"`.
- A single line that may be too long for its space, such as a file name, cut short with `truncate`.
- A preview of a long description, review or comment, cut after a few lines with `lines`, when the full item is a link away. To open the rest in place, use [ShowMore] (npx serupa-docs ShowMore).
- User content with long words or URLs: they break onto the next line, even in a flex row or grid column, rather than push the layout wider.

## When not to use

- A page or section title: use [Heading] (npx serupa-docs Heading) instead.
- Text that goes somewhere: use [Link] (npx serupa-docs Link) instead.
- A form control's help or error message: use `hint` and `error` on [Field] (npx serupa-docs Field), which wire it to the control for screen readers.
- A keyboard key or shortcut: use [Kbd] (npx serupa-docs Kbd) instead.

## Usage

- Leave `size`, `tone` and `weight` out unless you need them, so the text follows its parent.
- Use `as="span"` inside other text, and a `p` (the default) for paragraphs.
- It has no margins: space paragraphs with the layout, such as a [Stack] (npx serupa-docs Stack).
- Leave text people may want to copy selectable (an order number, an address, an error message): don't put `select-none` on it, and don't wrap it in a button.
- Give running text `measure` on a wide page (an article, a long description, help text), so each line stops near 65 characters: longer lines are hard to follow back to the next one. Lines under 80 characters are WCAG's advice (1.4.8, AAA). It's the same width as `max-w-prose` and Container's `size="prose"`, without the utility classes.
- Text's tokens (`--text-color`, `--text-color-muted`, `--text-color-primary`, `--text-color-danger`) only change Text's tones. They're separate from the shared theme colors such as `--text` and `--text-muted`, which they default to, and from the type sizes such as `--text-sm`: overriding `--text-color-muted` changes muted Text, not every muted color on the page.

### Do and don't

- **Do:** Cut a preview with `lines` and link to the full item, so the rest is a press away. (`DoLinesWithLink`)
- **Don't:** Cut text with no way to the rest: the hidden lines are lost to anyone who reads the screen. (`DontLinesAlone`)

## Accessibility

- Every tone keeps 4.5:1 on `surface` in every theme (`Text.test.tsx`). On other backgrounds, check it yourself.
- Don't use color alone to say something is wrong: say it in the words too.
- A truncated line hides the rest. To show it on hover, keyboard focus and tap, use [TruncatedText] (npx serupa-docs TruncatedText); otherwise put the full text somewhere else on the page.
- With `lines`, the hidden lines are still read by screen readers and found by find-in-page; only the eye misses them. Give people who see the screen a way to the rest: a link to the full item, or, to open it in place, [ShowMore] (npx serupa-docs ShowMore) instead of Text.
- **Keyboard:** none: inline text, not focusable.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | string | none | Goes to the root element (`as`). |
| `as` | `'p'` \| `'span'` \| `'div'` \| `'label'` \| `'strong'` \| `'em'` \| `'small'` \| `'li'` \| `'figcaption'` | `'p'` | The element |
| `size` | `'xs'` \| `'sm'` \| `'base'` \| `'lg'` \| `'xl'` | inherited | A step of the type scale, with its line height |
| `tone` | `'neutral'` \| `'muted'` \| `'primary'` \| `'danger'` | inherited | `text`, `text-muted`, `primary` or `danger-text` |
| `weight` | `'normal'` \| `'medium'` \| `'semibold'` \| `'bold'` | inherited | 400, 500, 600 or 700 |
| `truncate` | boolean | `false` | One line, cut with an ellipsis. It becomes a block, so give it a width or a parent that has one |
| `lines` | number | none | At most this many lines (1 to 6; more counts as 6), the last cut with an ellipsis (CSS line-clamp), for a preview of long text. It sets no style attribute, so it holds under a strict Content Security Policy. Ignored with `truncate` |
| `measure` | boolean | `false` | Caps the line at about 65 characters (`container-prose`, 65ch in the text's own size), for running text on a wide page. A span stays inline, so use it on a block (`p`, `div`, `li`) |

Text has no margins (space it with the layout). `className`, `style`, `ref`, `htmlFor` (with `as="label"`) and everything else go to the element, which has `data-component="text"`.

## Component tokens

Each is an optional override: set it on the page, a container or one element. The list lives in `src/components/Text/text.tokens.json` (also in `design-tokens/components/`).

<!-- token-table:start (made from text.tokens.json by npm run tokens: edit the descriptions there) -->
| Token | Default | Use |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--text-color` | `text` | tone="neutral". |
| `--text-color-muted` | `text-muted` | tone="muted": secondary text (4.5:1 on surface). |
| `--text-color-primary` | `primary-text` | tone="primary". |
| `--text-color-danger` | `danger-text` | tone="danger": error text (4.5:1 on surface and danger-subtle). |
<!-- token-table:end -->

components.name: TimePicker
components.summary: A time-of-day field: people type a time, or pick one from a list.
components.guide:
# TimePicker

A time-of-day field: people type a time, or pick one from a list.

**Also called:** time input, time selector.

```tsx
import { Field, TimePicker } from "@diki-stwn/serupa-ds";

const [start, setStart] = React.useState<string | null>("09:00");
<Field label="Start time">
  <TimePicker value={start} onValueChange={setStart} min="08:00" max="18:00" step={15} name="start" />
</Field>
```

## When to use

- A time of day: a meeting start, an opening hour, a reminder time.
- When times usually fall on regular slots (every 15 or 30 minutes) but people may also type an exact time.
- When only some hours are allowed, such as business hours.

## When not to use

- A length of time, such as "45 minutes": use [NumberInput] (npx serupa-docs NumberInput) with the unit in the label instead.
- A date as well as a time: pair a [DatePicker] (npx serupa-docs DatePicker) with a TimePicker; TimePicker holds the time only.
- A handful of fixed slots that people must choose from: use [Select] (npx serupa-docs Select) or a [Radio] (npx serupa-docs Radio) group instead. TimePicker accepts typed times between the slots.

## Anatomy

Drawn from the `Disabled` story.

1. **Field** (`.srp-input__field`): where the time is typed.
2. **Clock button** (`.srp-time-picker__button`): opens a list of times to choose from instead.

## Usage

- Wrap it in [Field] (npx serupa-docs Field) with a label that says which time it is ("Start time", "Remind me at").
- Set `step` to the slots people usually pick, and `min` and `max` to the hours that are allowed.
- Leave `hour12` and `locale` unset in most products so times follow the visitor's settings.
- Use `name` in a plain form: it sends `"HH:mm"`, whatever the display format.

## States

| State | Look |
| --- | --- |
| Rest | `field` background, 1px `field-border`, the clock button in `text-muted` |
| Hover | `field-border-hover`; the clock button under the pointer takes a `field-hover` fill, `field-pressed` while pressed |
| Focus | Like Input: the border and a 1px ring hugging it in `focus-ring` (2px in all), and a visible outline in forced-colors mode |
| Invalid | `danger` border, and a `danger` focus ring |
| Read-only | `field-readonly` background, no hover change; still focusable and selectable; the clock button is off with a plain cursor, so the list of times doesn't open |
| Disabled | `field-readonly` background, `disabled-border` edge and `disabled-text` at full opacity, `not-allowed` cursor; the clock button is off and the list of times doesn't open |

## Behavior

- People type `2:30 pm`, `2:30p`, `2pm`, `14:30`, `1430` or `9`. Without AM or PM, 13–23 are afternoon and 0–11 morning. The locale's own form is read too, as the field writes it: `오후 2:05` in Korean, `٢:٠٥ م` in Egyptian Arabic, `۱۴:۰۵` in Persian, with digits in any script. The text is read on blur and Enter; text that isn't a time, or a time outside `min`–`max`, puts back the last good value. Switching to another window or browser tab isn't leaving the field: the text waits until people come back.
- The list opens on ↓ or ↑ in the field, or the clock button, with the chosen time (or the one nearest the typed text) highlighted and near the top.
- A press anywhere on the box, on its start padding or past the clock button, focuses the field with the caret at the end, as the text cursor over the box promises.
- In the list: ↑ ↓ move one time, PageUp and PageDown four, Ctrl+Home and Ctrl+End to the ends, Enter picks, Escape closes, Tab closes and moves on. Typing while the list is open moves the highlight to the nearest time, and Enter then keeps what was typed. Focus stays in the field throughout, the clock button included.
- The list fades and grows in from the edge facing the field, and fades and shrinks back out a little faster on close, inert while it goes, as Menu, Popover and DatePicker do. Closed mid-way, it turns back from where it is. Under reduced motion it only fades. From the keyboard there is no motion: opened by an arrow the list is there at once, and Escape takes it away at once.

### Do and don't

- **Do:** Wrap it in a [Field] (npx serupa-docs Field) with a label that says which time it is ("Start time"). (`DoSayWhichTime`)
- **Don't:** Label it just "Time": people can't tell whether it's the start, the end or a reminder. (`DontJustTime`)

## Accessibility

- The field is an ARIA combobox (`aria-haspopup="listbox"`, `aria-expanded`, `aria-activedescendant`) and the list a `role="listbox"` with `aria-selected` on the chosen time. The check is decorative.
- The placeholder and the format in the field's description ("Format: hh:mm AM/PM", after a Field hint) follow the locale's order, separator and AM/PM words: "hh.mm" in id-ID, "오전/오후 hh:mm" in ko. The words come from the `formatHint` label.
- With a `locale` of its own the time carries that locale's direction (`dir`), in the field and the list, so "3:45 PM" in a right-to-left page keeps its order (not "PM 3:45").
- The clock button is out of the tab order, since ↓ in the field does the same.
- Times keep 4.5:1 (also highlighted), and the check and clock icon 3:1, in every theme (`TimePicker.test.tsx`).

### Keyboard

| Key | Does |
| --- | --- |
| Down / Up | In the field, opens the list; in the list, the next or previous time |
| PageDown / PageUp | Four times down or up the list |
| Ctrl+Home / Ctrl+End | The first or last time (Alt works too) |
| Enter | Picks the highlighted time, or reads what was typed; with the list closed, reads what was typed |
| Escape | Closes the list |
| Tab | Closes the list and moves on; the clock button isn't a Tab stop |

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | string | none | Goes to the native `<input>` (not the wrapper), so a `<label htmlFor>` or a Field can point at it. |
| `value` / `defaultValue` | `string \| null` | | The time as `"HH:mm"` (24-hour), controlled or not. The same format as `<input type="time">`; seconds (`"14:05:00"`, as a database's time column gives) are read and dropped. |
| `onValueChange` | `(value: string \| null) => void` | | Called with `"HH:mm"`, or `null` when the field is cleared. |
| `onInvalidInput` | `(text, reason) => void` | | Called when typed text is put back: `"unreadable"` (not a time) or `"unavailable"` (outside `min`..`max`). Screen readers also hear that it wasn't accepted (`inputNotAccepted`). The same words show under the field (`.srp-input-rejected`, read with it) until the text changes. |
| `min`, `max` | `string` | `"00:00"`, `"23:59"` | The earliest and latest times, typed or picked. |
| `step` | `number` | `30` | **Minutes** between the times in the list, counted from `min` (or midnight). Under 1, it's 30. Typed times don't have to fall on a step. `<input type="time">` counts its `step` in seconds, so a native `step={900}` (15 minutes) becomes `step={15}` here; `step={900}` would list a time every 15 hours. |
| `locale` | `string` | the nearest `SerupaProvider`'s, else the browser's (en-US until a server-rendered page hydrates) | How times are written. When it differs from the provider's, the field and the options carry `lang`, so screen readers read them in that language. |
| `hour12` | `boolean` | the locale's | 12-hour (2:30 PM) or 24-hour (14:30). |
| `size`, `invalid` | | `'md'`, `false` | Like Input. |
| `name` | `string` | | Adds a hidden input that sends `"HH:mm"`. With `form`, the hidden input belongs to that form too. |
| `placeholder` | `string` | the locale's format: `"hh:mm AM/PM"` (en-US), `"hh:mm"` (en-GB), "hh.mm" (id-ID) | |
| `listLabel` | `string` | `"Choose a time"` | The list's name, and the clock button's. |
| `open` | `boolean` | | Whether the list of times shows (controlled), with `onOpenChange`. |
| `defaultOpen` | `boolean` | `false` | Shows the list at first. Focus stays in the field either way. |
| `onOpenChange` | `(open, { reason }) => void` | | Called when the list asks to open or close, and why. |

`disabled`, `readOnly`, `id`, `aria-*`, `onBlur`, `onKeyDown` and `ref` go to the text field; `className` and `style` to the box.

`autoComplete` is `off` unless you pass one.

## Component tokens

Each is an optional override: set it on the page, a container or one picker. The list lives in `src/components/TimePicker/time-picker.tokens.json` (also in `design-tokens/components/`).

<!-- token-table:start (made from time-picker.tokens.json by npm run tokens: edit the descriptions there) -->
| Token | Default | Use |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--time-picker-button` | `text-muted` | The clock button's icon (3:1 on the field). |
| `--time-picker-button-hover` | `text` | The clock button's icon on hover. |
| `--time-picker-button-bg-hover` | `field-hover` | The clock button's background on hover, as the other buttons inside fields. |
| `--time-picker-button-bg-pressed` | `field-pressed` | The clock button's background while it's held down, one step past hover. |

components.name: TimeZonePicker
components.summary: A searchable list of time zones, by city, with each one's offset now and its name in the reader's language.
components.guide:
# TimeZonePicker

A searchable list of time zones, by city, with each one's offset now and its name in the reader's language. People find their zone by typing a city, a zone's name or an offset, and the value is the zone's IANA name, ready for dates and servers.

**Also called:** time zone select, timezone dropdown.

```tsx
import { TimeZonePicker } from "@diki-stwn/serupa-ds";

<Field label="Time zone"><TimeZonePicker defaultValue="Asia/Jakarta" /></Field>
<TimeZonePicker aria-label="Time zone" value={zone} onValueChange={setZone} />
<TimeZonePicker aria-label="Office" zones={["Asia/Jakarta", "Asia/Makassar", "Asia/Jayapura"]} />
```

## When to use

- A setting people choose once, such as their profile's time zone, or a meeting's zone when it isn't theirs.
- Anywhere a time is entered for a place other than where the reader is.

## When not to use

- To show a time in the reader's own zone: the browser already knows it. Format the time with their zone, and only ask when they want another.
- A short, fixed list of offices: a [Select] (npx serupa-docs Select) with their names says more than a list of cities.

## Usage

- Put it in a [Field] (npx serupa-docs Field) with a label, or give it `aria-label`. It's a [Combobox] (npx serupa-docs Combobox), so its other props (`size`, `clearable`, `disabled`, `readOnly`, `name`, `invalid`…) work the same. `readOnly` keeps it focusable and read out with `aria-readonly`, and a form still sends the zone, while typing and presses neither open the list nor change it.
- The value is an IANA name ("America/New_York"), which `Intl.DateTimeFormat`'s `timeZone`, `Temporal` and most servers take. Store that, not the offset: the offset changes with daylight saving time.
- The reader's own zone comes first, marked "Your time zone", so most people pick it without typing. The rest run from the furthest behind UTC to the furthest ahead, then by city.
- Each option shows its offset at the moment: in March, New York is UTC−05:00 before the 9th and UTC−04:00 after. Set `at` to show the offsets on another date, such as the meeting's.
- `zones` limits the list to the zones you pass, in the same order.
- The whole list (about 420 zones, each with its name in the locale) is made when the field is first focused, pointed at or opened, not when the page renders, so a page with several pickers loads as fast as one with none. Until then it knows only its value's zone and the reader's own.
- Typing finds a city ("jakarta"), a zone's name in the reader's language ("Waktu Indonesia"), the IANA name ("argentina") or an offset ("+7", "07:00", "utc-5", "−3:30").
- Zones go by their current names ("Europe/Kyiv", "Asia/Kolkata", "Asia/Ho_Chi_Minh"), the ones servers, databases and `Temporal` use, even where the browser still lists an older spelling. A value under an old name ("Europe/Kiev") shows too, and the picker hands back the current one. Typing the old name ("kiev") still finds it, as do common abbreviations and big cities that share a zone ("pst", "wib", "mumbai").
- The cities are as the IANA names spell them, in English ("New York"); the zone names are the browser's, in the locale (`locale`, the provider's, or the browser's). A `locale` of its own brings its direction too: with `locale="ar-EG"` in a left-to-right page, "UTC+07:00 · توقيت غرب إندونيسيا" reads right to left.

### Do and don't

- **Do:** Put it in a [Field] (npx serupa-docs Field) with a label that says whose time zone it is ("Meeting time zone"). (`DoSayWhose`)
- **Don't:** Show a bare picker: people can't tell whether it's their zone or the event's. (`DontBarePicker`)

## Accessibility

- **Role and name:** a Combobox: an `input` with `role="combobox"` and a `listbox` of `option`s. Each option is named by its city, and its offset and zone name are its `aria-description`, so a screen reader hears both.
- **Keyboard:** as [Combobox] (npx serupa-docs Combobox): type to filter, Up and Down to move, Enter to pick, Escape to close.
- **Contrast:** as Combobox, which its tests check in every theme.
- **What's still yours:** label it, and say what the zone is for when it isn't the reader's own ("The meeting's time zone").

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | `string` | | Goes to the input. |
| `zones` | `string[]` | every zone the browser knows, and UTC | The IANA names to offer. |
| `at` | `Date \| number` | now | The moment the offsets are for. |
| `locale` | `string` | the provider's, else the browser's | The language of the zone names. |
| `value` / `defaultValue` / `onValueChange` | `string \| null` | | The IANA name, as Combobox's value. |
| `placeholder` | `string` | "Search a city or time zone" (the `timeZonePlaceholder` label) | Shown in the empty field. |

Every other [Combobox] (npx serupa-docs Combobox) prop works too, except `options`, `loadOptions`, `filter` and `multiple`, which TimeZonePicker sets. `className` goes to its box, with `srp-time-zone-picker`; `ref` goes to the input.

`timeZoneInfo(zone, locale, at)` gives one zone's city, offset and name, and `allTimeZones()` the zones the browser knows, for showing a zone elsewhere the way the picker does.

## Component tokens

None of its own: it's a Combobox, and Combobox's tokens (`--combobox-…`, and Input's for the field) set its look.

components.name: Timeline
components.summary: An ordered list of events, each with a marker on a line that joins them, a title, a time and optional content.
components.guide:
# Timeline

An ordered list of events, each with a marker on a line that joins them, a title, a time and optional content. Use it for activity feeds, order history and audit logs, so people can see what happened and when.

**Also called:** activity feed, history.

```tsx
import { Timeline, TimelineItem } from "@diki-stwn/serupa-ds";

<Timeline aria-label="Order history">
  <TimelineItem title="Order placed" time="12 Mar, 09:14" dateTime="2026-03-12T09:14" tone="primary" icon="shopping_cart">
    Two items, paid by card.
  </TimelineItem>
  <TimelineItem title="Payment confirmed" time="12 Mar, 09:15" tone="success" icon="check" />
  <TimelineItem title="Out for delivery" time="15 Mar, 08:02" />
</Timeline>

// milestones along a line, scrolling sideways in its own box; down a line again under 480px
<Timeline orientation="horizontal" stackWhenNarrow aria-label="Order tracking">…</Timeline>
```

## When to use

- A record of events in order: an order's progress, a ticket's history, the changes to a document.
- An activity feed, where each event has a time and maybe a little more to say.

## When not to use

- Steps someone still has to work through, with a current one: use [Stepper] (npx serupa-docs Stepper).
- Rows to sort, filter or compare: use [Table] (npx serupa-docs Table).
- A plain list without times: use a list, or [Sidebar] (npx serupa-docs Sidebar) for navigation.

## Anatomy

Drawn from the `Alternate` story.

1. **Rail** (`.srp-timeline__rail`): the line the events hang on, oldest to newest.
2. **Event** (`.srp-timeline__item`): one thing that happened.
3. **Marker** (`.srp-timeline__marker`): a dot or an icon on the rail, in the event's tone.
4. **Time** (`.srp-timeline__time`): when it happened.
5. **Title** (`.srp-timeline__title`): what happened.
6. **Body** (`.srp-timeline__body`): more about it.

## Usage

- Keep one order, oldest first or newest first, and say which if it isn't obvious.
- Put the status in the title ("Delivery delayed"), not only in the marker's color.
- Give `dateTime` a machine-readable value whenever `time` is relative or shortened ("2 hours ago"), so the moment stays exact. Without `dateTime` the time is a plain `<span>`: a `<time>` needs a value machines can read.
- Use icons for a few kinds of event that people learn to scan for; dots are enough otherwise.
- `align="alternate"` suits a wide page with short entries. Below 768px it falls back to one side.
- `orientation="horizontal"` suits a few milestones with short titles: order tracking, a project's phases. Each event is 192px wide (wider when there's room), and past the width it has the timeline scrolls sideways in its own box, so the page never does. Set `stackWhenNarrow` to show the events down a line when its box is under 480px wide, as on a phone, instead of scrolling. A long history of events reads better vertical.

### Loading and failed

- **Loading:** show three or so events with a [Skeleton] (npx serupa-docs Skeleton) for each title (`size="lg"`, half the width) and time (`size="md"`, `w-24`), and `aria-busy` on the list. Each skeleton line is as tall as a line of its text, so the events keep their height when the history arrives. Give the first Skeleton a `label` ("Loading history") and the others `label=""`: a screen reader hears the wait once, after the skeleton's delay, and a quick load says nothing.
- **Failed:** in place of the list, a danger [Alert] (npx serupa-docs Alert) that says what didn't load and offers Retry in `actions`. It's `role="alert"`, so the failure is heard as it appears. On Retry, go back to loading.

```tsx
{state === 'failed' ? <Alert tone="danger" actions={<Button size="sm" onClick={load}>Retry</Button>}>The order history didn't load.</Alert>
  : state === 'loading' ? (
    <Timeline aria-label="Order history" aria-busy>
      {[0, 1, 2].map((i) => (
        <TimelineItem key={i}
          title={<Skeleton size="lg" className="w-1/2" label={i === 0 ? 'Loading history' : ''} />}
          time={<Skeleton size="md" className="w-24" label="" />} />
      ))}
    </Timeline>
  ) : <Timeline aria-label="Order history">{events.map(…)}</Timeline>}
```

### Do and don't

- **Do:** Put the status in the title: "Delivery delayed". (`DoStatusInTitle`)
- **Don't:** Give every entry a generic title and leave the status to the marker's color. (`DontColorOnly`)

## Accessibility

- **Role and name:** an `<ol>`: screen readers announce a list and how many events it has (with `role="list"`, so Safari does too). Name it with `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby` when the page has more than one list.
- **Keyboard:** nothing in a vertical timeline is focusable. Links and buttons you put in the content keep their own focus. While a horizontal timeline scrolls, its box takes focus, with a focus ring, so arrow keys scroll it (WCAG 2.1.1), and it's a region named by the `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby` you give the Timeline, or by the `timeline` label ("Timeline"). When the events fit, or `stackWhenNarrow` has stacked them, it's no Tab stop, and the name stays on the list.
- **Contrast:** titles and content read 4.5:1 on the page, and times do too, in every theme (`Timeline.test.tsx`).
- **Markers:** the marker and line are `aria-hidden`. Color is decoration, so the title has to carry the status. In forced colors, the dots and line draw in the system text color.
- **What's still yours:** a meaningful order, a title for every event, and a `dateTime` when the shown time is relative.

## Props

### Timeline

| Prop | Type | Default | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `align` | `'start' \| 'alternate'` | `'start'` | `'alternate'` puts events on both sides of a centered line from 768px up |
| `orientation` | `'vertical' \| 'horizontal'` | `'vertical'` | `'horizontal'` puts events along a line, following the text direction, scrolling sideways in its own box |
| `stackWhenNarrow` | `boolean` | `false` | With `orientation="horizontal"`, shows events down a line when its box is under 480px wide |
| `children` | `TimelineItem`s | | The events, in order |
| `id` | `string` | | Goes to the `<ol>` |

`className`, `ref` and other props go to the `<ol>`. With `orientation="horizontal"`, `className`, `style`, `aria-label` and `aria-labelledby` go to the scrolling box around it (`data-component="timeline"`, `data-orientation="horizontal"`), and the rest still to the `<ol>`.

### Keyboard

| Key | Does |
| --- | --- |
| Tab | To a horizontal timeline's box while it scrolls, then to any links or buttons in its events |
| ← → | Scroll a focused horizontal timeline sideways |

### TimelineItem

| Prop | Type | Default | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `title` | `ReactNode` | | What happened |
| `time` | `ReactNode` | | When, as people read it, in a `<time>` |
| `dateTime` | `string` | | The same moment for machines, on the `<time>` |
| `icon` | an icon name or element | | An icon in a tinted circle instead of a dot |
| `tone` | `'neutral' \| 'primary' \| 'success' \| 'warning' \| 'danger' \| 'info'` | `'neutral'` | The marker's color |
| `children` | `ReactNode` | | More about the event, below the title and time |

`className`, `ref` and other props go to the `<li>`.

## Component tokens

Each is an optional override: set it on the page, a container or one Timeline. The list lives in `src/components/Timeline/timeline.tokens.json` (also in `design-tokens/components/`).

<!-- token-table:start (made from timeline.tokens.json by npm run tokens: edit the descriptions there) -->
**Colors**

| --- | --- | --- |
| `--timeline-text` | `text` | The content's text (4.5:1 on the page). |
| `--timeline-title-color` | `text` | An event's title. |
| `--timeline-time-color` | `text-muted` | An event's time (4.5:1 on the page). |
| `--timeline-line` | `border` | The line joining the markers. |
| `--timeline-dot-neutral` | `border-strong` | The dot of a neutral event. |
| `--timeline-icon-neutral` | `text-muted` | The icon of a neutral event (3:1 on its circle). |

| `--timeline-icon-primary` | `primary-text` | The icon of a primary event (3:1 on its circle). |
| `--timeline-icon-bg-primary` | `primary-subtle` | The circle behind a primary event's icon. |
| `--timeline-dot-success` | `success` | The dot of a success event. |
| `--timeline-icon-success` | `success-text` | The icon of a success event (3:1 on its circle). |
| `--timeline-icon-bg-success` | `success-subtle` | The circle behind a success event's icon. |

| `--timeline-icon-warning` | `warning-text` | The icon of a warning event (3:1 on its circle). |

**Border**

components.name: Toast
components.summary: A short message that confirms something happened ("Changes saved", "Moved to trash") without getting in the way.
components.guide:
# Toast

A short message that confirms something happened ("Changes saved", "Moved to trash") without getting in the way. Call `toast()` from anywhere; messages show in the `<Toaster>`, which you render once near the root of the app, and go away on their own.

**Also called:** snackbar, notification.

```jsx
import { Toaster, toast } from '@diki-stwn/serupa-ds';

// once, near the root
<Toaster />

toast("Link copied");
toast({ title: "Changes saved", tone: "success" });
toast({ title: "Moved to trash", action: { label: "Undo", onClick: restore } });
toast({ title: "Upload failed", description: "The file is over 10 MB.", tone: "danger", autoDismiss: false, action: { label: "Retry", onClick: retry } }); // stays until closed

// replace a toast as work goes on
const id = toast({ title: "Saving…", autoDismiss: false });
await save();
toast({ id, title: "Saved", tone: "success" });

// or let toast.promise do the same from one call
toast.promise(save(), {
  loading: "Saving…",
  success: "Saved",
  error: (e) => ({ title: "Couldn't save", description: String(e) }),
});

toast.dismiss(id);   // or toast.dismiss() for all

// undo instead of "Are you sure?": hide it now, delete it for good only if Undo isn't chosen
hide(file);
toast.undo({ title: "Moved to trash", commit: () => deleteFile(file), onUndo: () => show(file) });
```

## When to use

- Confirming an action people just took, when the result isn't obvious on the page: "Link copied", "Invite sent".
- Offering a quick undo after an action, such as moving something to the trash.
- Reporting on work that finishes in the background, such as a save or an export.

## When not to use

- Something people must read or act on before going on: use a [Dialog] (npx serupa-docs Dialog) instead.
- A problem that stays until it's fixed, or a message about one part of the page: use an [Alert] (npx serupa-docs Alert) near that part instead.
- An error on one field: use the error in [Field] (npx serupa-docs Field) instead.

## Usage

- Keep the title short and say what happened, in a few words: "Changes saved", not "Your changes have been saved successfully."
- Use one `action` at most, for something quick such as Undo; the toast may go before people reach it.
- Every toast goes by itself after 5 seconds, one with an action too. Turn that off with `autoDismiss: false` only for a message someone has to act on, such as a failed upload with Retry; it then stays until it's closed. `<Toaster duration autoDismiss>` sets both for the whole app, and a toast's own options win.
- For work that takes a while, show a toast with `autoDismiss: false` and replace it by `id` when the work is done, as above, or hand the work to `toast.promise`.
- Render one `<Toaster>` for the whole app, and keep its `placement` the same on every page. If two are mounted at once (one in a layout and one in a page), only the newer shows toasts, so none appears twice, and a development warning says so; when it unmounts, the older one takes over.
- A burst can't bury the page: at most `limit` toasts show (3), and the same message again (same words and tone, with no `id` or `action`) adds a count to the toast that's showing ("Network error ×12") and starts its time over, rather than stacking. The stack stays clear of a phone's notch and home indicator. On a short screen, such as a phone in landscape, only as many as fit show, and the rest wait under the "+2 more" line, so none runs off the top or bottom. On a phone, a toast's action goes under the text, lined up with it, so the text keeps its width.
- On a touch screen, swipe a toast sideways to dismiss it. It follows the finger and fades as it goes. Let go past a third of its width, or flick it (even gently), and it carries on at your finger's speed and closes. Otherwise it slides back. Its time stops while it's under your finger.

### Do and don't

- **Do:** Say what happened in a few words: "Changes saved". (`DoShortTitle`)
- **Don't:** Write a sentence: the toast may go before people finish reading it. (`DontWordyTitle`)
- **Do:** Offer one quick action, such as Undo, for something people may want back. (`DoOneQuickAction`)
- **Don't:** Put something people must act on in a toast: a declined card belongs in a [Dialog] (npx serupa-docs Dialog) or an [Alert] (npx serupa-docs Alert) that stays. (`DontMustAct`)

## Accessibility

- Focus is never left behind a toast (WCAG 2.4.11): while toasts show at the top or bottom edge, the page's scroll padding there is the room they take, so tabbing to a control under them scrolls it clear. A page's own `scroll-padding` still wins.
- Each new toast is read out through the shared polite live region, so it doesn't interrupt. A repeat that only adds to a toast's count isn't read each time: once the burst stops (a second with no repeat), the message is read once more with the count ("Network error. 12 times.", `labels.toastRepeated`). The count reads as "12 times" with the title, not "×12".
- The time stops while a toast is hovered or anything in it has focus, and while the window is in the background (WCAG 2.2.1), so a toast with an `action` can go by itself like any other: hovering it, or reaching it with F8, holds it. Give one `autoDismiss: false` when people have to act on it. For anything they must act on before going on, an Alert or a Dialog is still better.
- F8 moves focus to the newest toast (a screen reader reads it, and Tab reaches its buttons), and F8 or Escape takes focus back to where it was. The first toast with an action adds "Press F8 to reach it." to what's announced (`labels.toastShortcut`), while a Toaster is in the page. When a toast closes with keyboard focus in it (its ×, its action, or `toast.dismiss()`), focus goes back where F8 came from, or else to the toast next to it. Closed with the mouse, focus isn't moved to the next toast, so that one's time keeps running.
- Each toast has a close button, so swiping is never the only way to close one (WCAG 2.5.1). The Toaster is a named region people can find.
- Titles and descriptions keep 4.5:1 and icons 3:1 in every theme (`Toast.test.tsx`).
- Toasts fade and slide in from their edge over 200ms, and fade and slide back toward it over 150ms when they close; the toasts left glide to their new place over 200ms instead of jumping, each keeping its place in the stack. One pushed into the waiting line by a newer toast shrinks and fades toward the "+2 more" line instead, and that line fades in and out and glides with the toasts. With `prefers-reduced-motion` toasts only fade, and the others move at once. The motion is a transition, so a toast shown again while it fades out turns back. A closing toast is inert while it fades, and focus moves on at once. Toasts already there as the Toaster arrives (shown from its first render) don't slide in.

### Keyboard

| Key | Does |
| --- | --- |
| F8 | To the newest toast; pressed again in a toast, back to where focus was |
| Escape | In a toast reached with F8, back to where focus was |
| Ctrl+Z (⌘Z on Apple devices) | Chooses Undo on the newest `toast.undo` shown, one per press. Not in a text field, where it undoes the typing, and not when your app handled the keys first (`preventDefault`) |
| Tab | Within a toast, to its action and its close button |

## Props

### toast(options)

| Option | Type | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `title` | node | required | The main line (a string alone is the title) |
| `description` | node | | A muted line under it |
| `tone` | `'neutral'` \| `'info'` \| `'success'` \| `'warning'` \| `'danger'` | `'neutral'` | An icon in the tone's color; neutral has none |
| `action` | `{ label, onClick }` | | One button, such as Undo. Choosing it also closes the toast |
| `duration` | number | the Toaster's, `5000` | Milliseconds before it goes; `0` keeps it until it's closed, as `autoDismiss: false` does |
| `autoDismiss` | boolean | the Toaster's, `true` | Whether it goes by itself after `duration`; `false` keeps it until it's closed, for a message someone has to act on |
| `announcement` | string | title and description | What screen readers hear, when the title isn't plain text |
| `id` | string | new | Reuse one to replace a toast that's showing |

It returns the toast's id. `toast.dismiss(id)` closes one, `toast.dismiss()` all of them.

### toast.promise(work, messages)

Shows `messages.loading` while `work` (a promise, or a function that returns one) runs, then replaces that same toast with `messages.success` or `messages.error`. Each message is a title string or `toast()` options; `success` and `error` can also be functions that get the result or the error. The loading toast stays until the work settles (`autoDismiss: false`); the result gets the success or danger tone unless the message sets one, and the usual duration. Since it's one toast replaced in place, screen readers hear the loading message and then the result. It returns `work`'s promise, so you can still await it or catch its error.

### toast.undo(options)

The undo pattern, in place of a confirmation: do the action in the page at once (the item leaves the list), and let `toast.undo` hold the real work until it's sure. It shows a toast with an Undo button, and takes `toast()` options except `action`, plus the ones below. Its time follows `autoDismiss` and `duration` like any toast's, so a Toaster with `autoDismiss={false}`, which some apps need for WCAG 2.2.1 (Timing Adjustable), keeps an undo toast until it's closed too.

| Option | Type | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `commit` | `() => void` | Required. Does the action for good. It runs once, when the toast closes without Undo: its time runs out, it's closed with ×, `toast.dismiss` closes it, or the page is left (`pagehide`). It also runs when a new `toast.undo` with the same `id` replaces it, and when no Toaster shows it (none is mounted, or the last one unmounts), since its Undo can't be reached then; that case warns in development (`toast-undo-no-toaster`). |
| `onUndo` | `() => void` | Runs instead of `commit` when Undo is chosen: put things back. |
| `undoLabel` | string | The button's text. Default: "Undo" (`labels.undo`). |

It returns the toast's id. Keep the usual duration or longer, so people have time to notice. The toast's time stops while it's hovered or focused, and F8 reaches its Undo button. Ctrl+Z (⌘Z on Apple devices) chooses Undo on the newest one too, from anywhere but a text field, since that's where people try undo first. With `duration: 0` it stays, and commits only when it's closed or the page is left.

### Toaster

| Prop | Type | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | string | none | Goes to the Toaster's root `<section>`, the region toasts show in. |
| `placement` | `'bottom-end'` \| `'bottom-start'` \| `'bottom'` \| `'top-start'` \| `'top'` \| `'top-end'` | `'bottom-end'` | Where toasts appear, 16px from the edges; `'top'` and `'bottom'` are centered, and start and end follow the text direction. The newest is nearest the edge. |
| `aria-label` | string | `'Notifications'` | The region's name |
| `dismissLabel` | string | `'Dismiss'` | The close buttons' name |
| `duration` | number | `5000` | How long each toast stays, in milliseconds, unless it sets its own |
| `autoDismiss` | boolean | `true` | Whether toasts go by themselves; `false` keeps every one until it's closed, unless a toast sets its own |
| `limit` | number | `3` | The most toasts shown at once. The newest show; older ones wait under a "+2 more" line and come back as others close. One never shown waits with its time not yet started; one already seen keeps its time running while it waits, so toasts still go in the order they came |

`ref`, `className`, `style` and other props go to the `<section>`, which has `data-component="toaster"` and `data-position`.

## Component tokens

Each is an optional override: set it on the page or the Toaster. The list lives in `src/components/Toast/toast.tokens.json` (also in `design-tokens/components/`).

| `--toast-title-color` | `text` | The title. |
| `--toast-description-color` | `text-muted` | The description (4.5:1 on surface). |
| `--toast-icon-info` | `info` | The icon of an info toast (3:1 on surface). |
| `--toast-icon-success` | `success` | The icon of a success toast. |
| `--toast-icon-warning` | `warning` | The icon of a warning toast. |
| `--toast-icon-danger` | `danger` | The icon of a danger toast. |
| `--toast-focus-ring` | `focus-ring` | The ring around a toast that F8 moved focus to. |
| `--toast-divider` | `border-overlay` | What a divider or separator inside it reads as `border`: its own edge color, since in dark `border` is the surface's own color and a line in it vanished |
