components.name: ToggleButton
components.summary: A Button that stays on or off, for a setting that applies right away: bold in a text editor, mute, show the grid.
components.guide:
# ToggleButton

A Button that stays on or off, for a setting that applies right away: bold in a text editor, mute, show the grid. It has `aria-pressed`, and when it's on it turns primary-subtle with primary text.

**Also called:** on/off button, state button.

```jsx
import { ToggleButton, ButtonGroup } from '@diki-stwn/serupa-ds';

<ToggleButton defaultPressed startIcon="grid_on">Show grid</ToggleButton>
<ToggleButton pressed={muted} onPressedChange={setMuted} icon={muted ? 'volume_off' : 'volume_up'} aria-label="Mute" />

<ButtonGroup aria-label="Text formatting">
  <ToggleButton icon="format_bold" aria-label="Bold" />
  <ToggleButton icon="format_italic" aria-label="Italic" />
</ButtonGroup>
```

## When to use

- A setting that applies right away and stays on or off: bold in a text editor, mute, show the grid.
- A toolbar of independent options that can be on at the same time, such as bold and italic.

## When not to use

- For one choice out of several (Day, Week, Month), use a [SegmentedControl] (npx serupa-docs SegmentedControl) or [radios] (npx serupa-docs Radio) instead: a set of toggles can all be on at once.
- A labeled on/off setting in a form or a settings list: use [Switch] (npx serupa-docs Switch).
- An action that doesn't stay on, such as Save: use [Button] (npx serupa-docs Button).

## Usage

- Group related toggles that each keep their own state (mute, captions) in a [ButtonGroup] (npx serupa-docs ButtonGroup) with an `aria-label` that says what they're for ("Playback"), and put several groups of tools in a [Toolbar] (npx serupa-docs Toolbar).
- To give a set of toggles one value, with one on at a time (alignment) or any number (text styles), use a [ToggleGroup] (npx serupa-docs ToggleGroup).
- Use `variant="ghost"` in toolbars and the default `outline` elsewhere.
- Give the toggles in one group the same `size`.

### Do and don't

- **Do:** Group related toggles in a ButtonGroup with a name, in one size. (`DoGroup`)
- **Don't:** Scatter related toggles in mixed sizes, with no group to name them. (`DontScatter`)

## Accessibility

- `aria-pressed` tells screen readers it's on or off. Keep the label the same either way ("Bold", not "Make bold" / "Remove bold"), since the state is announced separately.
- An icon-only toggle needs an `aria-label`.
- Pressed text keeps 4.5:1 on its background, and the pressed border 3:1 on `surface`, in the six themes the tests draw (blue, yellow and violet, light and dark) (`ToggleButton.test.tsx`). In Windows high-contrast mode it uses the system highlight colors.

### Keyboard

| Key | Does |
| --- | --- |
| Tab | To the button |
| Enter, Space | Turn it on or off (`aria-pressed`) |

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | string | none | Goes to the root `<button>`. |
| `pressed` | boolean | none | Whether it's on (controlled) |
| `defaultPressed` | boolean | `false` | Whether it starts on (uncontrolled) |
| `onPressedChange` | `(pressed) => void` | none | Called with the new state |
| `variant` | `'outline'` \| `'ghost'` | `'outline'` | Ghost suits toolbars |

Every other Button prop works (`size`, `icon`, `startIcon`, `endIcon`, `disabled`, `onClick`…), except `destructive` and `loading`. An `onClick` that calls `preventDefault()` stops the toggle. Disabled while on, it is drawn in neutrals (the highlight fill, muted text, the control border), so it still reads as on but not as something to press. It renders Button's element, with `data-component="button"` and the class `srp-toggle-button`.

## Component tokens

Each is an optional override: set it on the page, a container or one toggle. The list lives in `src/components/ToggleButton/toggle-button.tokens.json` (also in `design-tokens/components/`).

<!-- token-table:start (made from toggle-button.tokens.json by npm run tokens: edit the descriptions there) -->
| Token | Default | Use |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--toggle-button-bg-pressed` | `primary-subtle` | The background while pressed (on). |
| `--toggle-button-text-pressed` | `primary-text` | Text and icon while pressed (4.5:1 on bg-pressed). |
| `--toggle-button-border-pressed` | `primary-text` | The outline variant's border while pressed (3:1 on surface). |
| `--toggle-button-bg-pressed-held` | `primary-subtle-pressed` | The background of an on toggle while held down, one step past bg-pressed. |
| `--toggle-button-text-pressed-held` | `primary-text-hover` | Text and icon of an on toggle while held down (4.5:1 on bg-pressed-held). |
| `--toggle-button-bg-pressed-disabled` | `highlight` | The background while on and disabled. |
| `--toggle-button-text-pressed-disabled` | `text-muted` | Text and icon while on and disabled (3.4:1 and up on bg-pressed-disabled, as on a disabled Button). |
| `--toggle-button-border-pressed-disabled` | `border-control` | The outline variant's border while on and disabled (3:1 on surface). |
<!-- token-table:end -->

components.name: ToggleGroup
components.summary: A set of ToggleButtons that share one value: one on at a time, such as text alignment or a view mode, or any number, such as bold, italic and underline.
components.guide:
# ToggleGroup

A set of [ToggleButton] (npx serupa-docs ToggleButton)s that share one value: one on at a time, such as text alignment or a view mode, or any number, such as bold, italic and underline. It looks like a [ButtonGroup] (npx serupa-docs ButtonGroup) and reports the buttons that are on as one array.

**Also called:** toggle button group, icon toggle group.

```tsx
import { ToggleGroup, ToggleButton } from "@diki-stwn/serupa-ds";

// one at a time
<ToggleGroup aria-label="Text alignment" value={align} onValueChange={setAlign} required>
  <ToggleButton value="left" icon="format_align_left" aria-label="Align left" />
  <ToggleButton value="center" icon="format_align_center" aria-label="Align center" />
  <ToggleButton value="right" icon="format_align_right" aria-label="Align right" />
</ToggleGroup>

// any number
<ToggleGroup aria-label="Text style" selectionMode="multiple" defaultValue={["bold"]}>
  <ToggleButton value="bold" icon="format_bold" aria-label="Bold" />
  <ToggleButton value="italic" icon="format_italic" aria-label="Italic" />
</ToggleGroup>
```

## When to use

- Settings in a toolbar that apply right away, where one is on at a time (alignment, a list or grid view) or several can be (text styles), and you want them as one value.

## When not to use

- One choice in a form, or one that changes what the page shows (Day, Week, Month as tabs of a view): use a [SegmentedControl] (npx serupa-docs SegmentedControl) or a [RadioGroup] (npx serupa-docs Radio), which are radios and read as a choice.
- One on/off setting: a [ToggleButton] (npx serupa-docs ToggleButton) alone, or a [Switch] (npx serupa-docs Switch) in a form.
- Actions that don't stay on (Copy, Paste): a [ButtonGroup] (npx serupa-docs ButtonGroup) of Buttons.

## Usage

- Give each ToggleButton a `value`. Children without one, such as a Divider, render as they are.
- `selectionMode="single"` (the default) turns the others off when one turns on. Pressing the one that's on turns it off, unless `required`.
- `size`, `variant` and `disabled` on the group reach the buttons that don't set their own.
- `attached` and `orientation` work as on ButtonGroup: an attached row wider than its container wraps as separate toggles (with `data-wrapped` on the group) and joins again once there's room.
- Put it in a [Toolbar] (npx serupa-docs Toolbar) to give a row of groups one Tab stop with arrow keys.

### Do and don't

- **Do:** Set `size` on the group, so every toggle in it matches. (`DoGroupSize`)
- **Don't:** Size each toggle on its own: one row ends up with buttons of different heights. (`DontMixedSizes`)

## Accessibility

- **Role and name:** a `role="group"`. Name it with `aria-label` ("Text alignment"). Each button keeps `aria-pressed`, so screen readers say "Align left, toggle button, pressed".
- **Keyboard:** nothing of its own. Each button is a Tab stop, and Enter or Space presses it, as in a ButtonGroup. Inside a Toolbar, the arrow keys move between the buttons.
- **Contrast:** each button keeps ToggleButton's colors, which read 4.5:1 on and off in every theme (see [ToggleButton] (npx serupa-docs ToggleButton)). The group adds none.
- **What's still yours:** a name for the group and one for each icon-only button.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | string | none | Goes to the root `<div role="group">`. |
| `selectionMode` | `'single'` \| `'multiple'` | `'single'` | One on at a time, or any number. |
| `value` | `string[]` | | The values of the buttons that are on (controlled). |
| `defaultValue` | `string[]` | `[]` | The values on at first. |
| `onValueChange` | `(value: string[]) => void` | | Called when a button is pressed. |
| `required` | boolean | `false` | With `selectionMode="single"`, one stays on. |
| `disabled` | boolean | `false` | Turns every button off and out of use. |
| `size` | `'sm'` \| `'md'` \| `'lg'` | | For buttons that don't set their own. |
| `variant` | `'outline'` \| `'ghost'` | | For buttons that don't set their own. |
| `attached` | boolean | `true` | Joins them, as ButtonGroup does. |
| `orientation` | `'horizontal'` \| `'vertical'` | `'horizontal'` | A row or a column. |
| `aria-label` | string | none | What the buttons are for. |

`className`, `style`, `ref` and other props go to the `<div>`, which has `data-component="toggle-group"`, `data-type` and `data-orientation`.

## Component tokens

None of its own: its spacing and borders are ButtonGroup's tokens (`--button-group-gap`, `--button-group-overlap`), and the buttons' colors are ToggleButton's.

components.name: Toolbar
components.summary: A set of controls, such as an editor's formatting buttons, that takes one Tab stop instead of one per control.
components.guide:
# Toolbar

A set of controls, such as an editor's formatting buttons, that takes one Tab stop instead of one per control. Once focus is in it, the arrow keys move between the controls, so keyboard users get past a long row of buttons in one keystroke.

**Also called:** action bar, button toolbar.

```tsx
import { Toolbar, ButtonGroup, ToggleButton, IconButton, Divider, Menu, MenuItem, Button } from "@diki-stwn/serupa-ds";

<Toolbar aria-label="Text formatting">
  <ButtonGroup aria-label="Style">
    <ToggleButton icon="format_bold" aria-label="Bold" />
    <ToggleButton icon="format_italic" aria-label="Italic" />
  </ButtonGroup>
  <Divider orientation="vertical" />
  <IconButton variant="ghost" icon="link" label="Insert link" />
  <Menu trigger={<Button variant="ghost" endIcon="expand_more">More</Button>}>
    <MenuItem>Clear formatting</MenuItem>
  </Menu>
</Toolbar>

// a column of tools
<Toolbar aria-label="Drawing tools" orientation="vertical">
  <ToggleButton icon="edit" aria-label="Pen" />
  <ToggleButton icon="ink_eraser" aria-label="Eraser" />
</Toolbar>
```

## When to use

- Several controls that act on the same thing, such as text formatting above an editor, or the tools beside a canvas.
- A row of actions on a selection (Download, Move, Delete) that people use often enough that one Tab stop helps.

## When not to use

- Two or three buttons, such as Cancel and Save: a [ButtonGroup] (npx serupa-docs ButtonGroup) with `attached={false}` keeps each one in the Tab order, which is what people expect there.
- One choice out of a few: use [SegmentedControl] (npx serupa-docs SegmentedControl) or a [RadioGroup] (npx serupa-docs Radio).
- A site's main links: use [Navbar] (npx serupa-docs Navbar) or [Sidebar] (npx serupa-docs Sidebar). A toolbar is for controls, not navigation.

## Anatomy

Drawn from the `MoreMenu` story.

1. **Toolbar** (`.srp-toolbar`): the row (or column) of controls, on its own surface, with one Tab stop.
2. **More** (`.srp-toolbar__more`): with `overflow`, the button at the end of the row that opens the controls with no room; it shows only while one is hidden.

## Usage

- Put any controls inside, at any depth: Buttons, IconButtons, ToggleButtons, ButtonGroups, a Menu's trigger, a Select or an Input. Set `size` on the toolbar and every button in it takes it, in its ButtonGroups too (a button's own `size` still wins); give a Select or an Input in it the same `size` yourself.
- Use a vertical [Divider] (npx serupa-docs Divider) between groups in a row, or a horizontal one in a column. It takes the row's height.
- Disabled controls are skipped by the arrow keys. To keep one reachable so people can find it, use `aria-disabled` instead of `disabled`.
- When a row may not fit (a narrow window, a side panel), set `overflow`: the row stops wrapping, and the controls with no room move into a More menu at the end, which shows only while something is in it. Give the controls that must stay `data-priority` (higher stays longer, default 0); among equals the last moves first. Buttons, IconButtons and ToggleButtons move (a ButtonGroup moves whole, each button its own item, a toggle as a checked item); fields, Selects and Menus stay where they are, and a Divider left with nothing on one side goes with them. Choosing an item presses the control itself. Don't build a More menu by hand for this. (`MoreMenu`)
- Controls added or removed later join the arrow-key order on their own.
- Inside a text field, the arrows, Home and End stay the field's. Tab leaves the field.
- A composite with its own arrow keys, such as a SegmentedControl, keeps them. Prefer ToggleButtons in a ButtonGroup, which the toolbar moves through one by one.

### Do and don't

- **Do:** Group related controls, with a [Divider] (npx serupa-docs Divider) between the groups. (`DoGroupControls`)
- **Don't:** Put a form's Cancel and Save in a toolbar: Tab should reach each one, so use a [ButtonGroup] (npx serupa-docs ButtonGroup). (`DontFormButtons`)

## Accessibility

- **Role and name:** a `role="toolbar"` with `aria-orientation`. Name it with `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby`, which you need when a page has more than one toolbar.
- **Keyboard:** the [WAI-ARIA toolbar pattern](https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/toolbar/). It has one Tab stop, the control used last or else the first.

| Key | Moves focus to |
| --- | --- |
| Right / Left arrow | The next or previous control, in a row (mirrored right to left), wrapping at the ends |
| Down / Up arrow | The next or previous control, in a column |
| Home / End | The first or last control |
| Tab / Shift+Tab | Out of the toolbar |

With `overflow`, hidden controls leave the arrow-key order and the More button joins it at the end; a control chosen from its menu is pressed as if clicked, and focus returns to More.

Your `onKeyDown` runs before the toolbar's own keys, so `e.preventDefault()` in it keeps the toolbar from moving focus on that key. A Menu opened from the toolbar keeps its own keys, and closing it returns focus to its trigger.

- **Contrast:** it adds no colors to its controls. Text placed straight inside reads 4.5:1 on its background in every theme (`Toolbar.test.tsx`).
- **What's still yours:** a name for each icon-only control, and a name for the toolbar.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | string | none | Goes to the root `<div role="toolbar">`. |
| `orientation` | `'horizontal'` \| `'vertical'` | `'horizontal'` | A wrapping row, moved through with Left and Right, or a column, moved through with Up and Down. |
| `overflow` | boolean | `false` | In a row, moves the controls with no room into a More menu at the end, instead of wrapping. Lowest `data-priority` first. |
| `moreLabel` | string | `'More'` | The More button's name (`labels.toolbarMore`). |
| `size` | `'sm'` \| `'md'` \| `'lg'` | none | The size of every Button, IconButton and ToggleButton in it that doesn't set its own (24, 32 or 44px). |
| `aria-label` | string | none | What the controls are for ("Text formatting"). |
| `children` | `ReactNode` | | The controls, at any depth. |

`className`, `style`, `ref` and other props go to the `<div>`, which has `data-component="toolbar"` and `data-orientation`.

## Component tokens

Each is an optional override: set it on the page, a container or one Toolbar. The list lives in `src/components/Toolbar/toolbar.tokens.json` (also in `design-tokens/components/`).

<!-- token-table:start (made from toolbar.tokens.json by npm run tokens: edit the descriptions there) -->
| Token | Default | Use |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--toolbar-bg` | `surface` | The background, behind the controls. |
| `--toolbar-border` | `border` | The edge round the toolbar's surface, so it reads as one in light themes too. |
| `--toolbar-text` | `text` | Text color inherited by plain text inside (4.5:1 on bg). |
| `--toolbar-radius` | `radius-control` | The corners. Unset, they are concentric with the controls inside: radius-control plus the padding and the 1px edge (11px). |
| `--toolbar-padding` | `spacing-1` | Space inside, on every side (4px). |
| `--toolbar-gap` | `spacing-1` | Space between the controls (4px). |
<!-- token-table:end -->

components.name: Tooltip
components.summary: A short hint about one element, shown while it's hovered or focused: what an icon button does, a keyboard shortcut, why something is unavailable.
components.guide:
# Tooltip

A short hint about one element, shown while it's hovered or focused: what an icon button does, a keyboard shortcut, why something is unavailable. It sits next to the element in the browser's top layer, so nothing on the page can cover or clip it.

**Also called:** hint, info tooltip.

```jsx
import { Tooltip, IconButton, Button } from '@diki-stwn/serupa-ds';

<Tooltip content="Download as PDF">
  <IconButton icon="download" label="Download" />
</Tooltip>

<Tooltip content="Ctrl + S" placement="bottom">
  <Button>Save</Button>
</Tooltip>

// the tooltip is the only name: role="label"
<Tooltip content="Settings" role="label">
  <button className="…"><Icon name="settings" /></button>
</Tooltip>
```

## When to use

- Naming an icon-only button, such as Download or Settings.
- Showing a keyboard shortcut for a control.
- Saying why a control is unavailable.

## When not to use

- Content with links, buttons or fields: use a [Popover] (npx serupa-docs Popover) instead. People can't reach anything inside a tooltip: focus leaving the element hides it, and touch screens never show it. A link on its inverse fill also reads under 4.5:1 in every theme (1.84:1 to 3.43:1). A focusable element in `content` warns once in development (`tooltip-interactive`).
- Anything people need to do the task: put it in the page instead, such as the `hint` of a [Field] (npx serupa-docs Field). Touch screens have no hover.
- Error or status messages: use the error in [Field] (npx serupa-docs Field) or an [Alert] (npx serupa-docs Alert) instead.

## Usage

- The trigger is one element that passes its ref and props on to a DOM element: a Button, IconButton or link, or your own component written with `React.forwardRef` (or the `ref` prop in React 19) that spreads what it gets. A text, several elements or a Fragment throws an error that names the component, and a trigger that drops its ref warns once in the console ("Serupa: Menu's trigger doesn't forward its ref to an element.").
- Keep `content` to a short line of text, a few words where you can.
- A label in the element cut with an ellipsis (a long Button label in a narrow column) shows in full on its own line over `content`, since the tooltip takes the place of the title the Button would give it. Screen readers don't hear it twice: that line is hidden from them, as it is already the element's name. With `role="label"` the content is the name, so it isn't added.
- Use `role="label"` only when the tooltip is the element's only name; otherwise keep the default, which adds to the element's own name.
- An IconButton already shows its label in a Tooltip. Wrap it in your own only to say more than the label: yours replaces the built-in one.
- A Tooltip can be the `trigger` of a Menu or Popover (`<Menu trigger={<Tooltip content="More"><IconButton … /></Tooltip>}>`): the props and ref they add pass through to the element, with its own handlers run first and its own id kept.
- Keep the default `placement` unless it covers something people need to see.

### Do and don't

- **Do:** Name an icon-only button in a word or two. (`DoNameIcon`)
- **Don't:** Hide what people need to finish the task, such as a password rule, in a tooltip: touch screens never show it. Put it in the [Field] (npx serupa-docs Field)'s `hint`. (`DontNeededInfo`)

## Accessibility

- It shows on keyboard focus as well as hover, and only for the focus ring (not after a click). A tap on a touch screen doesn't show it, and a press anywhere outside hides it.
- The element points at the tooltip with `interestfor` (interest invokers), so where the browser has them (Chrome 142 and later, including on Android), a long press on a touch screen shows it at once. The browser's own showing is canceled and the tooltip shows itself, so the delay, the warm-up and Escape stay the same with a mouse or the keyboard. Elsewhere the attribute does nothing. It works on a `<button>` or a link.
- WCAG 1.4.13: Escape hides it from anywhere, the pointer can move onto it without it closing, and it stays until the pointer or focus leaves.
- Don't put anything only in a tooltip that people need to do the task: touch screens have no hover, and few people know a long press shows it.
- A disabled `<button>` can't take focus or hover events, so a tooltip on it never shows. For a Serupa [Button] (npx serupa-docs Button), pass `disabledReason` with `disabled`: it stays focusable, and a Tooltip with the same words shows on hover and focus. For other elements, use `aria-disabled` instead of `disabled`.
- It fades in and slides 4px away from the element over 150ms, and fades and slides back over 100ms as it hides; with `prefers-reduced-motion` it only fades. Moving from one tooltip to the next (the warm-up) swaps them at once, with no fade either way. Firefox and Safari can't keep a hiding tooltip in the top layer yet, so there it hides at once.
- The text keeps 4.5:1 on the tooltip in every theme (`Tooltip.test.tsx`). In forced-colors mode it gets a border.

### Keyboard

| Key | Does |
| --- | --- |
| Tab | To the element: the tooltip shows with its focus ring |
| Escape | Hides it, from anywhere, without closing a Dialog or Menu around it |

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `content` | node | required | A short line of text. No links or buttons: people can't reach them |
| `children` | one element | required | Something that takes focus: a Button, IconButton or link. It gets the events and the `aria-` wiring, and keeps its own handlers and ref |
| `placement` | `'top'` \| `'bottom'` \| `'left'` \| `'right'`, each with `-start` or `-end` | `'top'` | Where it goes. It flips to the other side when there's no room and slides to stay on screen |
| `openDelay` | number | `400` | Milliseconds the pointer rests before it shows. Keyboard focus shows it at once, and so does the pointer while another tooltip is open or closed less than 300ms ago (the warm-up) |
| `role` | `'description'` \| `'label'` | `'description'` | Adds to the element's name (`aria-describedby`), or is its name (`aria-labelledby`) |
| `open`, `onOpenChange` | boolean, function | | Control it yourself. onOpenChange(open, { reason }) says why: `'hover'`, `'focus'`, `'blur'`, `'trigger'` (a press on the element), `'escape'` or `'outside'` |
| `defaultOpen` | boolean | `false` | Shown at first, without controlling it |
| `disabled` | boolean | `false` | Never shows |

`id` isn't a prop of its own: an id given here goes to the trigger, unless the trigger has one, which stays. The tooltip's id is made for you.

`className` and `style` go to the tooltip, which has `role="tooltip"`, `data-component="tooltip"`, `data-state` and `data-side`.

## Component tokens

Each is an optional override: set it on the page, a container or one tooltip. The list lives in `src/components/Tooltip/tooltip.tokens.json` (also in `design-tokens/components/`).

<!-- token-table:start (made from tooltip.tokens.json by npm run tokens: edit the descriptions there) -->
| Token | Default | Use |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--tooltip-bg` | `surface-inverse` | The background: the inverse surface, so it stands out in light and dark themes. |
| `--tooltip-text` | `text-inverse` | The text (4.5:1 on the background). |
| `--tooltip-shadow` | `elevation-raised` | The shadow. |
| `--tooltip-radius` | `radius-control` | The corners (6px). |
| `--tooltip-padding-x` | `spacing-2` | Padding at the sides (8px). |
| `--tooltip-padding-y` | `spacing-1` | Padding at the top and bottom (4px). |
| `--tooltip-offset` | `spacing-1.5` | The gap between the tooltip and what it describes (6px). |
| `--tooltip-max-width` | `spacing-60` | The widest a tooltip gets before it wraps (240px). |
| `--tooltip-z-index` | `z-tooltip` | The stacking level where the browser has no top layer (popover). |
<!-- token-table:end -->

components.name: Tour
components.summary: A short guided walk through a page: one step at a time, a small panel points at a part of the page, says what it's for, and offers Back, Next and Done.
components.guide:
# Tour

A short guided walk through a page: one step at a time, a small panel points at a part of the page, says what it's for, and offers Back, Next and Done. Use it to show someone new the few things they need first.

**Also called:** product tour, walkthrough, coach marks.

```tsx
import { Tour } from "@diki-stwn/serupa-ds";

<Tour
  open={open}
  onOpenChange={setOpen}
  steps={[
    { title: "Welcome to Projects", content: "A quick look at the three things you'll use most." },
    { target: "#search", title: "Find a project", content: "Search by name or owner." },
    { target: newButton, title: "Start something new", content: "Opens a blank board.", placement: "bottom-end" },
  ]}
/>
```

## When to use

- A first visit to a page or a new feature, where three to five pointers save someone from hunting.
- Something they asked for: a "Take the tour" button in Help, so they can see it again.

## When not to use

- To explain one control: a [Tooltip] (npx serupa-docs Tooltip) or a [Popover] (npx serupa-docs Popover) next to it does that without a walk.
- For a task with steps they must finish: use a [Stepper] (npx serupa-docs Stepper) in the page, or a [Dialog] (npx serupa-docs Dialog).
- For anything they need every time: put it in the page. A tour is seen once and forgotten.

## Anatomy

Drawn from the `Default` story, opened.

1. **Title** (`.srp-tour__title`): the step's heading, which names its panel. The panel is a non-modal dialog next to the step's element, or in the middle of the screen when there's none.
2. **Close button** (`.srp-tour__close`): ends the tour.
3. **Text** (`.srp-tour__text`): what the step says, which describes the panel.
4. **Step count** (`.srp-tour__count`): "Step 1 of 3", when there's more than one step.
5. **Actions** (`.srp-tour__actions`): Back (from the second step) and Next, or Done on the last step.

The element the step points at gets a 2px primary ring (`[data-tour-target]`), set by the tour and taken off when it moves on.

## Usage

- Keep it short: three to five steps, a title and a sentence or two each. Say what the part does for them, not what it is.
- Start it from something they press, or once on a first visit, and remember (onFinish, onOpenChange) that they've seen it.
- A target is a CSS selector, an element or a ref. It's looked up each time its step shows; one that isn't on the page puts the step in the middle of the screen, so a missing part never breaks the tour.
- The page stays usable while it's open: nothing is dimmed and a press outside doesn't end it, so they can try what a step points at.
- Placement says where the panel goes ('bottom' by default); it flips when there's no room.

### Do and don't

- **Do:** Say what each part does for people, in a title and a sentence or two. (`Default`)
- **Don't:** Describe what the part is ("This is the search field"): they can already see that. (`DontSayWhatItIs`)

## Accessibility

- **Role and name:** each step is a `dialog` named by its title (a heading, level 2 by default: `headingLevel` fits it to the page) and described by its text.
- **Focus:** showing a step moves focus to its panel, so a screen reader reads its title and text; when the tour ends, focus goes back to where it was.
- **Contrast:** its text and its step count read 4.5:1 on its background in every theme (`Tour.test.tsx`).
- **What's still yours:** the target's own name, and a way to start the tour again. It isn't modal, so don't put anything in a step that must be done before going on.

### Keyboard

| Key | Does |
| --- | --- |
| Tab, Shift+Tab | Moves between the close button, Back and Next, and any link in the step; from Next it goes around to the close button, so focus never lands on the page under the panel. Click the page to leave the tour open and work there. |
| Enter, Space | Presses the focused button. |
| Escape | Ends the tour; focus goes back. |

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `steps` | `TourStep[]` | | Each `{ target?, title, content?, placement? }`. `target` is a selector, an element or a ref; left out, the step sits in the middle. |
| `open` | `boolean` | | Show it yourself (controlled), with `onOpenChange`. |
| `defaultOpen` | `boolean` | `false` | Show it at first (uncontrolled). |
| `onOpenChange` | `(open, { reason }) => void` | | `reason` is `'escape'` or `'close'` (the close button, or Done). |
| `step` | `number` | | The step shown, from 0 (controlled), with `onStepChange`. |
| `defaultStep` | `number` | `0` | The step shown each time it opens (uncontrolled). |
| `onStepChange` | `(step) => void` | | Called with the new step on Back or Next. |
| `onFinish` | `() => void` | | Called when Done is pressed on the last step, before it closes. |
| `headingLevel` | `2 \| 3 \| 4 \| 5 \| 6` | `2` | The heading level of each title. |

`className`, `id`, `ref` and other props go to the panel's `<div>` (its title and text take ids made from `id`). The words (Back, Next, Done, Step 2 of 4, Close) come from `<SerupaProvider labels>`.

## Component tokens

Each is an optional override: set it on the page, a container or one Tour. The list lives in `src/components/Tour/tour.tokens.json` (also in `design-tokens/components/`).

<!-- token-table:start (made from tour.tokens.json by npm run tokens: edit the descriptions there) -->
| Token | Default | Use |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--tour-bg` | `surface-overlay` | The panel's background. |
| `--tour-text` | `text` | The text (4.5:1 on bg). |
| `--tour-muted` | `text-muted` | "Step 2 of 4" (4.5:1 on bg). |
| `--tour-border` | `border-overlay` | The panel's edge. |
| `--tour-ring` | `primary-text` | The ring round the element a step points at (3:1 on the page). |
| `--tour-focus-ring` | `focus-ring` | The panel's focus ring, when the keyboard brings focus to it. |
| `--tour-divider` | `border-overlay` | What a divider or separator inside it reads as `border`: its own edge color, since in dark `border` is the surface's own color and a line in it vanished |
| `--tour-shadow` | `elevation-overlay` | The panel's shadow. |
| `--tour-radius` | `radius-surface` | The panel's corners (8px). |
| `--tour-border-width` | `border-width-1` | The panel's edge (1px). |
| `--tour-ring-width` | `outline-width-2` | The ring round the element (2px). |
| `--tour-ring-offset` | `outline-offset-2` | The gap between the element and its ring (2px). |
| `--tour-title-size` | `text-base` | The step's title (16px). |
| `--tour-title-weight` | `font-semibold` | The step's title. |
| `--tour-width` | `container-2xs` | The panel's width (288px), never wider than the screen. |
| `--tour-padding` | `space-content` | Space inside the panel (16px). |
| `--tour-gap` | `spacing-3` | Space between the title, the text and the buttons (12px). |
| `--tour-offset` | `spacing-3` | The gap between the element and the panel (12px). |
| `--tour-z-index` | `z-popover` | Its stacking order, for a browser without the top layer. |
<!-- token-table:end -->

components.name: TransferList
components.summary: Two lists, Available and Chosen, with Add and Remove between them, for picking a set out of many: the columns a table shows, the permissions a role has, the people on a team.
components.guide:
# TransferList

Two lists, Available and Chosen, with Add and Remove between them, for picking a set out of many: the columns a table shows, the permissions a role has, the people on a team.

**Also called:** dual list, shuttle, list builder, pick list.

```tsx
import { TransferList } from "@diki-stwn/serupa-ds";

<Field label="Columns" hint="The table shows them in this order.">
  <TransferList name="columns" options={columns} defaultValue={["name", "email"]} />
</Field>
<TransferList aria-label="Permissions" options={permissions} value={granted} onValueChange={setGranted} />
```

## When to use

- Picking several from a long list (a dozen or more), where seeing what's chosen apart from what isn't helps: columns, permissions, members, fields to export.
- The order of the chosen ones matters: they're kept in the order they were added.

## When not to use

- A handful of choices: a [CheckboxGroup] (npx serupa-docs Checkbox) shows them all at once with one box each.
- Choosing from hundreds by typing: a multiple [Combobox] (npx serupa-docs Combobox) finds them faster.
- Reordering what's chosen: pair it with a [SortableList] (npx serupa-docs SortableList), or use that alone.

## Anatomy

Drawn from the `NothingChosen` story.

1. **List** (`.srp-transfer-list__side`): Available, then Chosen; each scrolls past its height.
2. **Title** (`.srp-transfer-list__title`): the list's name, with its **count** (`.srp-transfer-list__count`).
3. **Options** (`.srp-transfer-list__options`): a CheckboxGroup, with All first.
4. **Moves** (`.srp-transfer-list__moves`): Add and Remove, between the lists.
5. **Empty** (`.srp-transfer-list__empty`): "None", in a list with nothing in it.

## Usage

- `options` is everything there is, each `{ value, label, description?, disabled? }`, in the order Available shows them. A disabled option can't be checked, so it stays in whichever list it's in: use it for one that's always on.
- `value` and `onValueChange` (controlled) or `defaultValue` hold the chosen values. Add puts the checked ones at the end of Chosen; Remove puts them back in their place in Available.
- Name it with a [Field] (npx serupa-docs Field) label (`Field` names the group), or `aria-label`. `availableLabel` and `chosenLabel` rename the two lists ("Hidden" and "Shown", "Not on the team" and "On the team"); the default words follow `SerupaProvider` labels in all its languages.
- With `name`, each chosen value is a hidden input, so a form submits them in order (`formData.getAll(name)`), and resetting the form puts `defaultValue` back.
- A choice it requires is yours to check: say so in the label, and count the values on submit.

### Do and don't

- **Do:** A list people pick some of and leave the rest, such as the columns a table shows. (`Default`)
- **Don't:** A handful of options: a [CheckboxGroup] (npx serupa-docs Checkbox) shows them at once, with one box each and no moving. (`DontFewOptions`)

## Behavior

- Each list is a group of checkboxes with an All box first (with two or more in it), named by its title, which counts what's in it: "Available (12)".
- Add and Remove move the checked ones. Each move is said politely: "Name and Company moved to Chosen."
- With nothing checked, Add and Remove stay where they are and keep focus, saying why they do nothing ("Check the ones to add first"), so a move never drops focus.
- Each list scrolls past its height (`--transfer-list-side-max-height`). On a phone the lists stack, with the buttons in a row between them.
- `disabled`, or a disabled `<fieldset>` around it, turns off every box and both buttons, and submits nothing.

## Accessibility

- **Role and name:** a `role="group"` named by its Field label or `aria-label`, holding two groups of native checkboxes, each named by its title and count, and two buttons.
- **Keyboard:** Tab reaches each box, then Add and Remove; Space checks a box.
- **Contrast:** its text and counts read 4.5:1 on the lists' background in every theme (`TransferList.test.tsx`).
- **What's still yours:** the label (with "required" in it when it is), telling people what the order means if it matters, and checking a count other than "at least one" on submit.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | string | none | Goes to the root `<div>`. |
| `options` | `TransferListOption[]` | | `{ value, label, description?, disabled? }`. |
| `value` | `string[]` | | The chosen values (controlled), in the order they were added. |
| `defaultValue` | `string[]` | `[]` | The chosen values at first (uncontrolled). |
| `onValueChange` | `(value: string[]) => void` | | Called after each move. |
| `name` | `string` | | Submits each chosen value as a hidden input. |
| `form` | `string` | | The id of a form elsewhere that the values belong to. |
| `disabled` | `boolean` | `false` | Turns off both lists and the buttons. |
| `readOnly` | `boolean` | `false` | Shows both lists without letting them change: the boxes are read-only but still focusable, Add and Remove are left out, and the form still sends the chosen values, unlike `disabled`. |
| `required` | `boolean` | `false` | At least one value must be chosen: the form isn't sent while Chosen is empty (both lists are marked invalid and the first available box takes focus). Say it in the label too, since the group can't carry `aria-required`. |
| `invalid` | `boolean` | `false` | Marks every box invalid. Field sets it from its error. |
| `availableLabel` | `string` | "Available" | The first list's name. |
| `chosenLabel` | `string` | "Chosen" | The second list's name. |

`className`, `ref` and other props go to the root `<div>`, which has `data-component="transfer-list"`.

## Component tokens

Each is an optional override: set it on the page, a container or one TransferList. The list lives in `src/components/TransferList/transfer-list.tokens.json` (also in `design-tokens/components/`).

<!-- token-table:start (made from transfer-list.tokens.json by npm run tokens: edit the descriptions there) -->
| Token | Default | Use |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--transfer-list-side-bg` | `surface` | Each list's background. |
| `--transfer-list-side-border` | `border` | Each list's border. |
| `--transfer-list-muted-text` | `text-muted` | A list's count and its "None" (4.5:1 on side-bg). |
| `--transfer-list-side-radius` | `radius-surface` | Each list's corners (8px). |
| `--transfer-list-side-padding` | `spacing-3` | Space inside each list (12px). |
| `--transfer-list-side-max-height` | `spacing-60` | How tall a list grows before it scrolls (240px). |
| `--transfer-list-gap` | `spacing-3` | Space between the lists and the move buttons (12px). |
<!-- token-table:end -->

components.name: TreeView
components.summary: Nested items that open and close, such as folders and files, a table of contents or categories.
components.guide:
# TreeView

Nested items that open and close, such as folders and files, a table of contents or categories. People pick one item, or several, and move through the tree with the arrow keys in one Tab stop.

**Also called:** tree, nested list navigation.

```tsx
import { TreeView, type TreeViewItem } from "@diki-stwn/serupa-ds";

const files: TreeViewItem[] = [
  { id: "src", label: "src", icon: "folder", children: [
    { id: "index", label: "index.ts", icon: "draft" },
  ] },
  { id: "readme", label: "README.md", icon: "draft" },
];

<TreeView aria-label="Files" items={files} defaultExpanded={["src"]} onValueChange={(ids) => open(ids[0])} />

// several picked
<TreeView aria-label="Files" items={files} selectionMode="multiple" value={picked} onValueChange={setPicked} />

// checkboxes: a folder checks or clears everything under it
<TreeView aria-label="Files" items={files} cascade value={picked} onValueChange={setPicked} />
```

## When to use

- A hierarchy people browse and pick from: folders and files, an org chart, nested categories.
- A table of contents with sections inside sections (`selectionMode="none"` when the items only open and close).

## When not to use

- One level of items: use a [RadioGroup] (npx serupa-docs Radio), a [Select] (npx serupa-docs Select) or a [Combobox] (npx serupa-docs Combobox).
- A site's navigation with links: use [Sidebar] (npx serupa-docs Sidebar), whose groups open and close, since a tree's items aren't links.
- Sections of content that open and close: use [Accordion] (npx serupa-docs Accordion).
- Rows with columns: use a [Table] (npx serupa-docs Table).

## Anatomy

Drawn from the `Multiple` story.

1. **Item** (`.srp-tree-view__item`): one node, with the nodes under it.
2. **Toggle** (`.srp-tree-view__toggle`): opens and closes the nodes under it; the arrow keys do too.
3. **Icon** (`.srp-tree-view__icon`): an optional picture, such as a folder or a file.
4. **Label** (`.srp-tree-view__label`): the node's name.
5. **Selected item** (`.srp-tree-view__item--selected`): a node chosen now.
6. **Group** (`.srp-tree-view__group`): the nodes under an open one, set in.

## Usage

- Pass `items`, each with a unique `id` and a `label`. An item with `children` opens and closes, even when its children are an empty array (a folder with nothing in it yet).
- Closed items' children aren't in the page, so a large tree costs only the items in view.
- `value` and `defaultValue` hold the picked ids, and `expanded` and `defaultExpanded` the open ones. Both are arrays, controlled or not.
- Give an item `textValue` when its label isn't plain text, so typing still finds it.
- A disabled item can still be focused and read, so people know it's there, but it can't be picked, opened or closed.
- When the focused item leaves the page from outside (you take it out of `items`, or close its parent through `expanded`), focus goes to its nearest parent in view, else the item now in its place, not to the page.
- `cascade` gives each row a checkbox, for picking files to share or permissions to grant. Checking a folder checks every item under it, and a folder with only some of its items checked shows a dash (mixed). Disabled items keep their state when a folder above them changes. `value` holds every checked item, folders included; set `cascadeValue="leaves"` to get only the items with no children, such as the files to upload. (`Cascade`)
- Your `onKeyDown` runs before the tree's own keys, so `e.preventDefault()` in it keeps the tree from acting on that key.

### Loading and failed

- **The first load:** in place of the tree, a few [Skeleton] (npx serupa-docs Skeleton) lines (`size="md"`) in a box with `aria-busy`. Give the first a `label` ("Loading files") and the others `label=""`. Render the tree once its top level is here: an empty tree has nothing to focus.
- **A folder that loads when it opens:** give it `children: []` so it can open, then load its children in `onExpandedChange`. Until they come, its one child is a disabled "Loading…" item: people can reach it and hear it, but not pick it. When the children arrive, focus on that item goes to the first of them.
- **Failed:** the same item says so: "Didn't load. Close and open the folder to try again." Closing and opening the folder loads it again. When the whole tree fails, show a danger [Alert] (npx serupa-docs Alert) with Retry in `actions` in its place.

```tsx
const children = kids === 'loading' ? [{ id: 'docs-wait', label: 'Loading…', disabled: true }]
  : kids === 'failed' ? [{ id: 'docs-wait', label: "Didn't load. Close and open the folder to try again.", disabled: true }]
  : kids;   // [] until the folder first opens
<TreeView aria-label="Files" items={[{ id: 'docs', label: 'docs', icon: 'folder', children }]} expanded={open}
  onExpandedChange={(next) => { setOpen(next); if (next.includes('docs') && (kids === 'failed' || !kids.length)) loadDocs(); }} />
```

### Do and don't

- **Do:** Open the folders down to the selected item with `defaultExpanded`, so people see where they are. (`DoOpenToSelection`)
- **Don't:** Start with everything closed when something is selected: the selection is hidden. (`DontHideSelection`)

## Accessibility

- **Role and name:** a `role="tree"` of `role="treeitem"`s with `aria-level`, `aria-posinset`, `aria-setsize` and `aria-expanded`. The children of an open item are in a `role="group"`. Picked items have `aria-selected`. With `selectionMode="multiple"`, the tree has `aria-multiselectable`. With `cascade`, rows have `aria-checked` (`true`, `false` or `"mixed"`) in place of `aria-selected`, and the box beside each label is hidden from screen readers, since `aria-checked` already says it. Name it with `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby`.
- **Keyboard:** the [WAI-ARIA tree pattern](https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/treeview/). It has one Tab stop: the item used last, or else the first picked one, or else the first.

| Key | Does |
| --- | --- |
| Down / Up arrow | Moves to the next or previous item in view |
| Right arrow | Opens a closed item, or moves to an open item's first child (Left right to left) |
| Left arrow | Closes an open item, or moves to its parent (Right right to left) |
| Home / End | Moves to the first or last item in view |
| Enter / Space | Picks the item (toggles it with `selectionMode="multiple"`), or opens and closes it with `"none"`. With `cascade`, checks or clears it and everything under it: a mixed folder checks everything |
| * | Opens every sibling of the item |
| A letter | Moves to the next item starting with what was typed. Letters within half a second make one word, and a Space between them is part of it ("my files" finds "my files", not "my file") |
| Shift + Down / Up | With `"multiple"`: moves and picks |
| Shift + Space | With `"multiple"`: picks every item from the one picked last |
| Ctrl / Cmd + A | With `"multiple"`: picks every item in view. With `cascade`: checks every item, or clears them all when all are checked |

- **Pointer:** a click on a row picks it (Shift+click picks a range with `"multiple"`), and a click on its chevron opens or closes it without picking. The chevron is a 24px target (WCAG 2.5.8) around its 20px icon.
- **Contrast:** labels read 4.5:1 on the background, and the picked row's on its highlight, in every theme (`TreeView.test.tsx`). With more contrast the picked row also has a 2px bar at its start.
- **What's still yours:** a name for the tree, and labels that make sense read alone ("Invoices", not "Folder 3").

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | string | none | Goes to the root `<ul role="tree">`. |
| `items` | `TreeViewItem[]` | | `{ id, label, textValue?, icon?, children?, disabled? }`, nested. |
| `selectionMode` | `'single'` \| `'multiple'` \| `'none'` | `'single'` | One picked item, any number, or none (items only open and close). |
| `cascade` | boolean | `false` | A checkbox on each row; a folder checks and clears everything under it, and shows mixed when only some are checked. Takes the place of `selectionMode`. |
| `cascadeValue` | `'all'` \| `'leaves'` | `'all'` | With `cascade`: whether `value` lists every checked item, folders included, or only the checked items with no children. |
| `value` | `string[]` | | The picked ids (controlled). |
| `defaultValue` | `string[]` | `[]` | The picked ids at first. |
| `onValueChange` | `(value: string[]) => void` | | Called when the picked ids change. |
| `expanded` | `string[]` | | The open ids (controlled). |
| `defaultExpanded` | `string[]` | `[]` | The open ids at first. |
| `onExpandedChange` | `(expanded: string[]) => void` | | Called when an item opens or closes. |
| `aria-label` | string | | What the tree holds ("Files"). |

`className`, `style`, `ref` and other props go to the `<ul role="tree">`, which has `data-component="tree-view"`.

## Component tokens

Each is an optional override: set it on the page, a container or one TreeView. The list lives in `src/components/TreeView/tree-view.tokens.json` (also in `design-tokens/components/`).

components.name: TruncatedText
components.summary: Text that may not fit its space, such as a file name in a narrow column: cut with an ellipsis, with the whole text shown beside it on hover, keyboard focus or a tap.
components.guide:
# TruncatedText Text that may not fit its space, such as a file name in a narrow column: cut with an ellipsis, with the whole text shown beside it on hover, keyboard focus or a tap. Text that fits stays plain text. **Also called:** ellipsis, text overflow, line clamp. ```tsx import { TruncatedText } from "@diki-stwn/serupa-ds"; quarterly-report-final-version-2.pdf quarterly-report-final-version-2026.pdf {comment} ``` ## When to use - A name or value the app doesn't control, in a space that can't grow: a file name in a list, an email address in a table cell, a project title in a card's header. - Rows that must stay one line high, where some values fit and some don't. ## When not to use - Text that has room to wrap: let it wrap. Cutting text is the last resort, since most people never open what's hidden. - A long description or comment to open in place: [ShowMore] (npx serupa-docs ShowMore). - A preview whose full text is a link away, with nothing to show on hover: [Text] (npx serupa-docs Text) with `lines`. - The label of a Button, a tab or a menu item: put a [Tooltip] (npx serupa-docs Tooltip) on the control, which already shows a cut label in full. ## Usage - It is a block as wide as its container, so the container decides where it cuts: a grid column, a table cell with a width, a flex item (it can shrink below its text's width). - A grid column or flex item that holds it must be allowed to shrink below the text's width, or the whole text widens it: a `minmax(0, 1fr)` column, or `min-width: 0` on the flex item (`min-w-0`). - Pass the text as a string. Style it from the parent, or with `className`: it uses the surrounding font and color. - `lines` allows 2 to 6 lines before the cut, for a title that may take two lines but not three. - Keep it out of a `

`: the full text is drawn in an element of its own beside it, which a paragraph can't hold. Use `as="p"` to make it the paragraph. - Put what people need in order to tell rows apart at the start of the text, where the cut never reaches. - Names told apart by their ends, such as files ("report-2025.pdf", "report-2026.pdf"), ids and addresses, take `mode="middle"`: the start is cut and the last few characters stay, with the extension (up to 10 characters) and the 6 before it. (`Middle`) ### Do and don't - **Do:** Put what tells the rows apart at the start: "March 2026 statement, account…". (`DoDifferenceFirst`) - **Don't:** Start every row with the same words: the cut leaves each one the same text, and people open them one by one to find theirs. (`DontSameStart`) ## Accessibility - **Role and name:** plain text with no role. The whole text stays in the element, so screen readers, find-in-page and a copy get all of it, cut or not. With `mode="middle"`, the end drawn again after the cut is generated content with empty alternative text, so it isn't read or copied twice. The text shown on hover repeats it for the eye, so it is hidden from screen readers and nothing points at it. - **Keyboard:** cut text takes a tab stop, and focus shows the whole text; `Esc` hides it. Text that fits has no tab stop. Inside a link, a button or another element that takes focus, it adds no tab stop of its own: that control's keyboard focus shows the whole text. - **Touch:** a tap shows the whole text, and the next tap, or a tap elsewhere, hides it. Inside a link or a button, a tap is the control's: it follows the link or opens the picker, and the whole text stays in the control's name. - **Contrast:** it takes the surrounding text's color; its focus ring reads 3:1 on the surface in every theme (`TruncatedText.test.tsx`). - **What's still yours:** a width for its container, and a color for the text that reads 4.5:1 on its background. ## Props | Prop | Type | Default | Notes | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `children` | `string` | | The text. All of it stays in the page | | `id` | string | none | Goes to the root element | | `lines` | number | `1` | How many lines it may take before the cut: 1 to 6 (more counts as 6). It sets no style attribute, so it holds under a strict Content Security Policy | | `as` | `'span'` \| `'p'` \| `'div'` | `'span'` | The element. Whichever it is, it's a block as wide as its container | | `mode` | `'end'` \| `'middle'` | `'end'` | Where one line is cut. `'middle'` keeps the end in view ("quarterly-rep…n-2026.pdf"), laid out in the text's own direction (`dir="auto"`), so a right-to-left name keeps its end on the left. With `lines` (2 or more) it's cut at the end | | `placement` | `'top'` \| `'bottom'` \| `'left'` \| `'right'`, or with `-start` / `-end` | `'top'` | Where the whole text shows. It flips when there's no room | `className`, `ref` and other props go to the element, which has `data-component="truncated-text"`, and `data-truncated` while it's cut (and `data-end`, the end drawn again, while it's cut in the middle). ## Component tokens Each is an optional override: set it on the page, a container or one TruncatedText. The list lives in `src/components/TruncatedText/truncated-text.tokens.json` (also in `design-tokens/components/`). The whole text shows in a [Tooltip] (npx serupa-docs Tooltip), which has its own tokens. | Token | Default | Use | | --- | --- | --- | | `--truncated-text-focus-ring` | `focus-ring` | The ring inside its edge while cut text has keyboard focus. |

components.name: TypeToConfirm
components.summary: A field and a destructive button for an action that can't be undone: the button works only once the person types a phrase, usually the name of what's being deleted.
components.guide:
# TypeToConfirm

A field and a destructive button for an action that can't be undone: the button works only once the person types a phrase, usually the name of what's being deleted. It makes them stop and read what's at stake.

**Also called:** confirmation input, type to delete.

```tsx
import { TypeToConfirm } from "@diki-stwn/serupa-ds";

<TypeToConfirm phrase="acme/web" confirmLabel="Delete this repository" onConfirm={deleteRepository} />
```

## When to use

- Deleting or resetting something big and permanent (a repository, a workspace, an account), usually in a [Dialog] (npx serupa-docs Dialog) that says what will be lost.

## When not to use

- Everyday actions that can be undone: do them at once and offer Undo (a [Toast] (npx serupa-docs Toast) action).
- Small destructive actions: a [Dialog] (npx serupa-docs Dialog) with a clear destructive button is enough. Asking to type for everything trains people to type without reading.

## Anatomy

Drawn from the `Default` story.

1. **Phrase** (`.srp-type-to-confirm__phrase`): the words to type, shown so they can be copied.
2. **Field** (`.srp-input`): where they're typed.
3. **Confirm** (`.srp-type-to-confirm__button`): stays unavailable until the words match.

## Usage

- Make the phrase the name of the thing (`acme/web`), not a word like "DELETE", so typing it is a check that it's the right one.
- Say what can't be undone in `hint`, or above it in the Dialog.
- Name the action on the button (`confirmLabel`): "Delete this repository", not "Confirm". A long one wraps onto more lines rather than widening the page on a phone.
- `onConfirm` can return a promise: the button shows loading until it settles and takes no second press.

## Behavior

- The button takes no press until what's typed matches the phrase. Spaces around it don't count. Letter case must match unless `caseSensitive={false}`, which also takes Turkish "İ" and "ı" as "i". An accent typed or pasted as a separate mark ("e" + "´", as in macOS file names) matches the same letter written as one ("é"), but a missing accent doesn't. Full-width letters (an IME left in full-width mode) match the usual ones, and a run of spaces counts as one.
- Enter in the field confirms once it matches.
- Pasting is allowed (WCAG 3.3.8): the point is reading the phrase, not retyping it.
- The field turns off autocomplete, spellcheck, autocapitalize and autocorrect, which would change what's typed.
- `onMatch` is called when it starts or stops matching.

### Do and don't

- **Do:** Make the phrase the thing's own name (`acme/web`), and name the action on the button. (`Default`)
- **Don't:** Ask for a word like "DELETE" with a "Confirm" button: typing it checks nothing about which thing is going. (`DontGenericWord`)

## Accessibility

- **Role and name:** a text field labeled "To confirm, type" and the phrase, then a button named by `confirmLabel`.
- **Contrast:** the label and the destructive button read 4.5:1 in every theme (Field and Button).
- **What's still yours:** say what will be lost, and put it in a Dialog or a clearly separated danger zone.

### Keyboard

| Key | Does |
| --- | --- |
| Tab | To the field, then to the button. The button is focusable before it works (`aria-disabled`), and its description says why ("Type “acme/web” first") |
| Enter | In the field: confirms, once the text matches the phrase |

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | string | none | Goes to the root `<div>`. |
| `phrase` | `string` | | Required. What to type, usually the thing's name. |
| `confirmLabel` | `ReactNode` | | Required. The button's label: the action in words. |
| `onConfirm` | `() => unknown` | | Required. Runs on the button or Enter once the phrase matches. Can return a promise. |
| `label` | `ReactNode` | `"To confirm, type"` and the phrase | The field's label. |
| `hint` | `ReactNode` | | Help under the label, such as what can't be undone. |
| `caseSensitive` | `boolean` | `true` | Whether letter case must match too. |
| `onMatch` | `(matched: boolean) => void` | | Called when what's typed starts or stops matching. |
| `disabled` | `boolean` | `false` | Disables the field and the button. |

`className`, `ref` and other props go to the wrapper `<div>`.

## Component tokens

Each is an optional override: set it on the page, a container or one TypeToConfirm. The list lives in `src/components/TypeToConfirm/type-to-confirm.tokens.json` (also in `design-tokens/components/`).

<!-- token-table:start (made from type-to-confirm.tokens.json by npm run tokens: edit the descriptions there) -->
| Token | Default | Use |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--type-to-confirm-gap` | `spacing-3` | Space between the field and the button (12px). |
| `--type-to-confirm-phrase-weight` | `font-semibold` | The phrase's weight in the label. |
<!-- token-table:end -->

components.name: VisuallyHidden
components.summary: Content that screen readers announce but nobody sees: "(opens in a new tab)", the label of an icon-only control you build yourself, a heading for a section that's obvious by sight.
components.guide: # VisuallyHidden Content that screen readers announce but nobody sees: "(opens in a new tab)", the label of an icon-only control you build yourself, a heading for a section that's obvious by sight. With `focusable` it shows while it has keyboard focus, for a control only keyboard users need. For the page's "Skip to content" link, use [SkipLink] (npx serupa-docs SkipLink). **Also called:** screen-reader only, sr-only. ```jsx import { VisuallyHidden } from '@diki-stwn/serupa-ds'; 3 unread messages Filters // A control for keyboard users, shown while it has focus Keyboard shortcuts ``` ## When to use - Words that make something clear to screen reader users when sight already makes it clear: "3 unread messages" shown as "3". - A heading for a section that's obvious by sight, so screen reader users can jump to it. - Your own focusable content that shows when someone presses Tab, with `focusable`. For the page's "Skip to content" link, use [SkipLink] (npx serupa-docs SkipLink): it has the words in both languages and moves focus to the main content. ## When not to use - Naming an icon-only button: use [IconButton] (npx serupa-docs IconButton) instead; its `label` is required. - Saying a link opens a new tab: use `external` on [Link] (npx serupa-docs Link), which adds "(opens in a new tab)" for you. - A "Skip to content" link: use [SkipLink] (npx serupa-docs SkipLink), which also moves focus to the main content. - Hiding something from everyone, screen readers included: use the `hidden` attribute or `display: none` instead. ## Usage - Keep it short and put it where it's read in context, such as right after the number it explains. - Pick the element with `as`: a heading level that fits the page's outline, or `div` for a skip link. - Put a skip link first in the page, pointing at the main content's `id`. ### Do and don't - **Do:** Keep it short and put it right after what it explains ("3 unread messages"). (`DoRightAfter`) - **Don't:** Put it far from what it explains: a screen reader says "unread messages … 3". (`DontFarAway`) ## Accessibility - It's clipped to 1px and taken out of the layout, not `display: none`, so screen readers still read it. - Don't hide anything someone who can see needs: if it matters, show it. - Focusable content takes its own place in the layout when shown: style it with your page so it doesn't push content around, or put it in a fixed spot. - **Keyboard:** none of its own. It only hides its content on screen, so anything focusable inside stays in the Tab order: give such content `focusable`, so it shows while it has focus. ## Props | Prop | Type | Default | What it does | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `id` | string | none | Goes to the root ``. | | `focusable` | boolean | `false` | Shows it while it, or something inside it, has focus | | `as` | `'span'` \| `'div'` \| `'h1'`…`'h6'` \| `'p'` \| `'label'` \| `'legend'` | `'span'` | The element | `className`, `style`, `ref` and everything else go to the element, which has `data-component="visually-hidden"`. The `sr-only` utility class does the same in plain HTML. ## Component tokens None: it has nothing to see.

topics.name: Install and load
topics.text:
## Install and load

```sh
npm install github:dsgn-space/serupa-ds#v19.2.0
```

Pin a release tag, never `#main`. Then load the CSS once, in this order, before any of your own CSS:

```js
import '@diki-stwn/serupa-ds/tokens.css';   // every token, the themes, the fonts: always first
import '@diki-stwn/serupa-ds/base.css';     // page defaults; leave out when adding Serupa to an existing app
import '@diki-stwn/serupa-ds/bundle.css';   // components and utility classes (or components.css, plus utilities.css)
import { Button, Field, Input } from '@diki-stwn/serupa-ds';
```

The styles sit in cascade layers (`srp.tokens`, `srp.base`, `srp.components`, `srp.utilities`). The app's own unlayered CSS always wins over them, so an override never needs `!important`.

For production, trim the CSS in the build: `import { serupaPurge } from '@diki-stwn/serupa-ds/purge'` and add `serupaPurge()` to Vite's `plugins` (or `serupaPurgePostcss()` to `postcss.config.mjs` for Next.js and webpack). Without a bundler: `npx serupa-purge src -o public/bundle.min.css --components`. List any class the code builds at runtime with `keep: [...]` (or `--keep`).

topics.name: Theme
topics.text:
## Theme

Put the brand and mode on `<html>`, and load `theme.js` first in `<head>` (or paste its text in an inline script) so the page has no flash of the wrong theme:

```html
<html lang="en" data-brand="blue" data-mode="auto">   <!-- brand: blue, violet, emerald… any accent color; mode: auto | light | dark -->
```

Pick the brand by its color: `blue` (the default) or any other palette color (`red`, `orange`, `amber`, `yellow`, `lime`, `green`, `emerald`, `teal`, `cyan`, `sky`, `indigo`, `violet`, `purple`, `fuchsia`, `pink`, `rose`) and import its `brands/<brand>.css` after `tokens.css`. Tune the look on `<html>` or any section, never with your own CSS: `data-density="compact"`, `data-radius="sharp"` or `"round"`, `data-shadow="neutral"`, `data-contrast="more"`.

One theme on one element: `data-theme="violet-dark"`. For the app's own brand color, make a theme with `npx serupa-brand acme "#0f766e" -o src/acme-theme.css`, import it after `tokens.css` and use `data-brand="acme"` (plus `data-brands="acme"` on `<html>` for theme.js); never hand-pick shades for `primary`. For locale and the built-in words, wrap the app in `<SerupaProvider locale="id-ID" labels={idLabels}>`; its `size="sm"` (or `"lg"`) sets every form control's default size, so don't repeat `size` on each one. For router links, call `configure({ link: Link })` once at startup.

topics.name: Rules
topics.text:
## Rules

1. **Reuse before you build, in this order.** Stop at the first step that does the job:
   1. A ready-made screen or section: `npx serupa-add` lists the patterns (Dashboard, Sign in, Settings form, Team members, …) and blocks (Page header, Pricing, Stats row, …), and `npx serupa-add <Name>` writes one into `src/serupa/` as source to change. For a whole screen, start from one of these.
   2. A Serupa component from the list below. Don't rebuild a button, field, dialog, menu or table out of `div`s.
   3. Serupa components put together: a settings page is `Card`, `Field` and `Switch` in a column, not a new widget.
   4. A native element (`<details>`, `<progress>`, `<dl>`) styled with the utility classes and tokens.
   5. Only then your own code, on tokens, with keyboard use, focus and an accessible name kept. End the answer with one line, "Built by hand: <what>, because Serupa has no <component>.", so the gap gets seen.
2. **Tokens only.** Write no raw colors, pixel sizes, durations or shadows. Use the utility classes (`p-4`, `gap-2`, `bg-surface`, `text-text-muted`, `rounded-md`, `shadow-md`) or `var(--…)` tokens in your CSS (`var(--spacing-4)`, `var(--primary)`).
3. **Colors by role, not hue.** Use the alias tokens, which change per theme: `primary` (a fill), `on-primary`, `primary-text`, `surface`, `surface-muted`, `text`, `text-muted`, `border`, `danger`, `danger-text`, `success-text`, `warning-text`, `focus-ring`. A palette color like `blue-600` looks the same in every theme. Use one only when no alias fits. For brand or status text, use the `*-text` alias, never the fill.
4. **Restyle through component tokens.** Each component reads its own tokens (`--button-*`, `--input-*`), which default to the aliases. Override them on the page, a container or one instance, rather than overriding its `srp-*` classes. Use the components directly: no `ui/Button.tsx` that wraps Button to set its defaults, and no second component, icon, animation or CSS-in-JS library beside Serupa.
5. **Shared props.** `size` is `'sm' | 'md' | 'lg'`, at heights of 24, 32 and 44px. Form controls take `invalid` and `disabled`, and get their label, hint and error from `Field`.
6. **Pick feedback by how long it stays.** To confirm that something worked ("Saved", "Invite sent"), call `toast("Saved")`, and render one `<Toaster />` near the app's root. It goes away on its own and screen readers hear it. Use an `Alert` for a message that must stay on the page until it's dealt with, and `SaveStatus` for autosave.
7. **Words.** Every button starts with a verb that says what it does ("Save changes", "Send message"), never "OK", "Submit" or "Click here", and a dialog's title uses the same verb ("Delete project?" has a "Delete" button). Sentence case everywhere. No exclamation marks, emoji or "Oops". An error says what to do: "Enter your email", not "This field is required" or "Invalid input"; "We couldn't load your projects. Try again.", not "Something went wrong". An empty state says what goes here and offers to add the first one. The rest is in Content and voice: https://github.com/dsgn-space/serupa-ds/blob/main/docs/foundations.md#content-and-voice
8. **In an existing app, change only what the task needs.** Leave the other code, its formatting and its names as they are, even a hand-built button or a raw color next to your change. Use Serupa for what you add, and end the answer by naming the parts that could move to Serupa rather than moving them.
9. **Respect people's work.** Act at once and offer Undo with `toast.undo({ title, commit, onUndo })` rather than asking "Are you sure?"; confirm only what can't be undone. Progress and "Saved" show real work, never a timer. Ask only what the task needs. Leaving a flow keeps what was typed.

topics.name: Accessibility: what the app must do
topics.text:
## Accessibility: what the app must do

The components meet their part of WCAG 2.2 AA. The page meets the rest only if you also do these, in every answer, however short:

- **Page:** set `<html lang>` and a unique `<title>`. Use one `main` (`<main id="main">`, or `<Container as="main" id="main">`) and start it with `<SkipLink />`, the "Skip to content" link, which moves focus to the main content (`id="main"`).
- **Headings:** one `h1` per page and no skipped levels. Heading's `level` sets the element, and its look can differ.
- **Names:**
  - Wrap every form control in `<Field label="…">`. A placeholder is not a label.
  - Give every IconButton a `label` (its accessible name and tooltip). It takes no `aria-label`.
  - Give every meaningful Image `alt` text, and a decorative one `alt=""`.
  - Write link text that says where the link goes.
- **Errors:** say what's wrong and how to fix it, next to the field. On submit, move focus to the first error or to an ErrorSummary.
- **Color:** in your own content, color never carries meaning alone. Add text, an icon or a pattern.
- **Focus:** never use `outline: none` alone (use `outline-hidden` if you must). Keep targets at least 24px, and keep sticky headers off the focused element (`scroll-padding-top`).
- **Route changes:** call `announcePage()` after a client-side route change. Say status changes with `announce("Saved")`, not with a visual change alone. When markup must change with the screen width, use `useBreakpoint('md')` (the same widths as the `md:` utilities), not your own `matchMedia`; `useReducedMotion()` gates an animation you run from JavaScript, and an in-app "Reduce motion" setting is `data-motion="reduce"` on `<html>`; `useCopyToClipboard()` copies from a control that isn't a CopyButton, such as a menu item.
- **Motion:** use the motion tokens, and don't animate anything that `prefers-reduced-motion` would want still.

topics.name: Before you finish
topics.text:
## Before you finish

1. **Run the check and fix until it passes.** In an app `serupa-create` made, that's `npm run check`: the types, ESLint with jsx-a11y and `@diki-stwn/serupa-ds/eslint` (an Image with no `alt`, an IconButton with no `label`), and Stylelint with `@diki-stwn/serupa-ds/stylelint` (a raw color, spacing or radius). In another app, add `@diki-stwn/serupa-ds/eslint` after jsx-a11y in `eslint.config.js` and `extends: ['@diki-stwn/serupa-ds/stylelint']` to its Stylelint config, then run its lint.
2. **Tab through the page once.** Every control is reached in reading order, shows its focus ring, and works from the keyboard.
3. **Look at it in dark mode** (`data-mode="dark"` on `<html>`). Nothing you wrote should stay light.

tokens.name: --primary
tokens.description: Alias. Brand fill: primary buttons, checked boxes, the selected day, a Switch that's on, a Progress bar, with `on-primary` (white) on it. Light themes: brand 600 or 700, the lightest with 4.5:1 for white text. Dark themes: the same shade, lightened as far as 3:1 on a raised dark card asks and always a touch, 0.02 of OKLCH lightness, while white text keeps 4.5:1 (blue-600 #2563eb becomes #2b6af2), so a button is the same color in both modes. Yellow is the exception: yellow 500 in light and yellow 400 in dark, under yellow-950 text, since a yellow dark enough for white text reads as brown; Yellow Light's fill takes a `primary-edge`. Brand text, links, icons and lines are `primary-text`. More contrast: brand 800 with white text in light, brand 300 with brand-950 text in dark.

tokens.name: --primary-hover

tokens.name: --space-content

tokens.name: --space-row

tokens.name: --space-item

tokens.name: --space-surface

tokens.name: --space-section

tokens.name: --space-page

tokens.name: --motion-stagger
tokens.description: The gap between items of a group arriving one after another, for a group seen now and then (a page's cards, a first list of results), never one opened over and over (menu items, toasts). Each item waits its index times this.

tokens.name: --motion-stagger-limit
tokens.description: The longest any item of a staggered group waits, so a long list still arrives within a moment: items past the sixth arrive together.

tokens.name: --motion-sequence
tokens.description: The offset between the steps of one entrance, so they read as a sequence: a dialog or drawer’s backdrop starts, then its panel. Exits don’t sequence; everything leaves together.

tokens.name: --ease-enter
tokens.description: Something appearing: quick off the mark, then a long smooth landing.

tokens.name: --ease-exit
tokens.description: Something leaving: at full speed from the first frame, then easing off as it fades, so a closed surface is out of the way at once. An ease-in starts slowly, and the first frames after a close are the ones people watch.

tokens.name: --ease-move
tokens.description: Something that stays on screen and changes: a thumb sliding, a panel resizing, a color changing. A smooth start and finish.

tokens.name: --ease-settle
tokens.description: Something arriving at a new value or let go by the hand: a fill, a slide, a drawer dropped. Most of the travel at once, then a long glide to rest.

tokens.name: --ease-pop
tokens.description: Something small popping into place: a check mark, a count, a dot. Overshoots a touch, then settles.

tokens.name: --ease-spring
tokens.description: A press let go springing back, or a thumb or indicator landing: a real spring that overshoots and settles. Pair it with a duration about twice the motion it answers (a press of `motion-press` springs back over `motion-change-md`).

tokens.name: --ease-fling
tokens.description: Something the hand let go of mid-motion carrying on to rest: a drawer or carousel slide flicked. It starts at three times its average speed, so a settle timed as 3 × distance ÷ the hand’s speed starts exactly at that speed and slows from there (`settleTime()` in the components).

tokens.name: --ease-celebrate
tokens.description: A small, rare moment worth celebrating: a success check landing, a count bumping, an item snapping into its slot after a drag. Wobbles, then settles. Give it about three times the motion it answers (`motion-change-lg` or longer) so the wobble reads, and never use it for menus, dialogs, page moves or repeated actions. Off under reduced motion.
